Oh, that’s a good one. All shadowy and mysterious. You wouldn't get that now. Everything’s so…bright. And loud. He just looked blank. Said it sounded “depressing.” Apparently, everything needs a happy ending now. Depressing? Life is depressing sometimes! Films should reflect that! Not everything's sunshine and roses. Honestly, that seminar was… draining. Three hours on post-structuralism before five pm is just cruel and unusual punishment, don't you think? You and your students. Right, so, Mrs. Peterson said she absolutely  cannot  do Saturday night. Something about her book club having a crisis meeting – honestly, you’d think the world was ending! But… you promised I could have a sleepover with Lily on Saturday. I know, sweetie, and we’ll still  try  for Saturday. I’m just texting Sarah now. She mentioned she might be free. It’s just… finding someone reliable last minute is a nightmare. Mummy, look! The dinosaur has  massive  teeth! Bigger than my hand! Wow, that  is  a big dinosaur! Okay, one minute, let me finish this text. Okay, sent. Fingers crossed. Now, what were we saying about dinosaurs? I want to make cookies! Chocolate chip ones, with sprinkles! Okay, cookies sound good. But after we finish reading this dinosaur book, alright? We need to get dinner sorted too. I was thinking spaghetti bolognese? Yeah! And can I help stir? Of course you can help stir! You’re excellent stirrers. Although, maybe not with the hot sauce. Remember last time? You made a funny face! I did, didn't I? Right, Sarah just replied! She says she’s tentatively free, but she’s having her hair cut on Saturday afternoon, so it depends how long  that  takes. What’s ‘tentatively’? It means she might be able to do it, but it’s not definite yet. It’s a grown-up word, darling. Will Lily come then? We’re still working on it, love. Look, how about this? We’ll see what Sarah says, and if she can’t do it, we can have a really fun family night? We could build a fort, watch a movie, and  definitely  make those chocolate chip cookies. A fort?! A  big  fort? The biggest fort you’ve ever seen! We’ll use all the blankets and pillows. And can we take photos in the fort? Like a photoshoot? That’s a brilliant idea! We can dress up and everything. I have that silly feather boa somewhere… I want to be a dinosaur in the photoshoot! Rawr! You can absolutely be a dinosaur! Right, let's get this dinosaur book finished, then we’ll start prepping for dinner and maybe do a little cookie dough mixing. Does that sound like a plan? Speaker_2 & Yes! Good. Now, where were we? Ah yes… “Once upon a time, in a land filled with volcanoes…”

Honestly, this canteen food is…an experience. I think that’s the polite way to put it. It’s like they actively  try  to make beige food. You're not wrong! It's all shades of sad, isn’t it? I swear the pasta sauce is just watered-down tomato puree. I brought a sandwich today, thankfully. You should’ve done the same. I thought, “Oh, I’ll be a responsible student and support the university canteen.” Massive mistake. I’m regretting my life choices with every bite of this…chicken? Is that even chicken? It  looks  suspiciously like reformed poultry. Anyway, are you still up for that night out on Friday? Chloe was saying she’s managed to get a table at Pryzm. Pryzm?! Oh god, is that still a thing? Last time I was there, I think I lost a shoe. And my dignity. Classic you! Well, Chloe reckons they’ve done it up a bit. Apparently, it's less sticky floors and more…themed rooms now? Themed rooms doesn’t really reassure me. Still, I suppose it beats staying in and writing that essay on Post-Structuralism. My brain physically hurts just thinking about it. Tell me about it. I’m completely stuck on the Foucault section. It's just…words. Fancy words. All over the page. Right?! It’s like he’s deliberately trying to confuse everyone. My tutor said we need to “deconstruct the inherent power structures within the text.” I nearly choked on my coffee. Oh, those tutors! Always with the big words. My mum keeps asking me what I actually  do  at university. I tried to explain it to her, and she just started talking about proper jobs. Same! My nan asked me if I was learning to type. A  typewriter ! Honestly. She thinks university is just a fancy typing school. Bless her. Maybe we should just tell our families we’re training to be professional club-goers. Seems more relatable. That's a brilliant idea! “Yes, Gran, I’m mastering the art of responsible alcohol consumption and flawless dance moves.” Exactly! We could even get qualifications. “Level 3 Certificate in Social Fluidity.” What do you reckon? I'm in. Speaking of fluid, I need a drink. This canteen coffee is actively depressing me. Fancy grabbing a proper coffee after this? There's that little place on Eden Street... Oh, definitely. Their oat milk lattes are a lifesaver.

Right, so I was thinking, for next year, we should actually  do  a proper holiday. Like, not just a weekend in York or something. Somewhere hot. Hot sounds good. I’m so tired of grey. Though, honestly, anywhere that isn't actively raining feels like a holiday after this winter. Remember that trip to the Lake District last year? Pure, unadulterated drizzle. Oh god, don't remind me. I think I permanently smell of damp sheep after that one. Though, in fairness, the pub lunches were alright. Speaking of which, have you two tried that new Thai place near the station? It's lethal. No! Is it actually decent? I always read the reviews and they’re either raving or saying it gave someone food poisoning. There's no in-between. I went with a mate last week. Really good. Proper spicy, though. I ordered a 'medium' and nearly cried. I'm a pathetic excuse for a spice enthusiast, I know. You and me both. I’m a ‘mild’ kinda guy. Anything beyond that and my internal organs stage a full-scale rebellion. Anyway, back to holidays... what were you thinking, hot-wise? Spain? Greece? Somewhere a bit more adventurous? I’ve always fancied Croatia. I saw some pictures online and it looked stunning. Loads of little islands, crystal clear water… plus, it’s meant to be relatively affordable. Croatia’s a good shout. I was looking at Portugal last year, but everything was booked up. It's becoming the new Spain, apparently. Everyone and their nan is going there now. Portugal is lovely. My auntie and uncle went last year, spent ages in the Algarve. Said the golf was world class, if that's your thing. I’m more of a ‘lie on a beach and read a terrible book’ kinda holidaymaker. Sounds perfect to me. Speaking of terrible books, have you seen that new series everyone’s banging on about on Netflix? The one with all the dragons? Oh,  that  one. My sister's obsessed. She keeps trying to get me to watch it, but I’m not really a fantasy fan. Too much CGI, not enough actual story. I gave it a go. Got about three episodes in and realised I was actively bored. Plus, all the knights look suspiciously like they’ve wandered off the set of ‘Game of Thrones’. It's just…derivative. Fair enough. I’m hooked, though.

Right then, finished that crossword. Took me ages with 23 down, "Maritime vessel," six letters. Eventually twigged it was ‘yacht’. Good for you, Arthur. I’m still trying to decipher what Maureen said on the phone earlier. Something about a new fangled washing machine… honestly, these modern things! You and technology, Mum. It’s a never-ending battle. Speaking of battles, did you two see that football match last night? Absolutely brilliant! Villa were on fire. Football? Bah. All running about and shouting. Give me a good horse race any day. Saw Old Man Hemmings down the pub, reckons his mare is looking good for the Newmarket meeting. Oh, Arthur and his horses. Honestly, you’d think they were your children. Though I suppose they’re more reliable than some children! Remember young Timothy, the one I used to mind? Always getting into trouble, that one. I remember. He ended up going to that youth hostel in Cornwall, didn’t he? Said it changed his life. Though I suspect the surfing had more to do with it than any kind of self-discovery. Cornwall… Lovely place. We went there years ago, stayed in a little B&B near St. Ives. Prices have gone through the roof since then, I reckon. Everything’s so expensive now. Tell me about it! We’ve been looking at selling this house, you know. Prices are good, apparently. But where would we go? Everything's so small these days. Selling the house? Really? I thought you were happy here, Mum. It's got all your memories. We  are  happy here, dear, but it’s getting too much to manage. The garden, the stairs… It's a bit much for us now. We'd like something smaller, more manageable, perhaps closer to you. Closer to David? That’ll be the day! He’s always gallivanting about London. Remember when he tried to convince us to sell everything and buy a flat there? Madness, I tell you. Absolute madness. It was a bit ambitious, Dad. London’s not for everyone. Though I have to admit, I had a good weekend there. Went to a conference on new teaching methods. Interesting stuff, though tiring. Speaking of tiring, your father’s been on at me to list some his old bits and bobs on eBay. Apparently, he’s got a collection of commemorative spoons that are 'worth a fortune'. They  are  worth a fortune!

Honestly, I’m starting to feel like a dairy cow. Just… attached. It's relentless. Tell me about it! It's all everyone talks about, isn't it? "Is she feeding well?" "How long is she feeding for?" Honestly, I feel like people think my entire existence is now just providing milk. Exactly! And the judgement! If you bottle feed, you’re a bad mum. If you breastfeed for longer than six months, you're… also a bad mum, apparently? There’s no winning. Oh, absolutely. Auntie Carol had a little comment the other day about how ‘a good strong baby needs proper food, not just milk’. Honestly, the cheek! She didn’t even  have  children! Oof, Carol is the worst. She's always got an opinion, hasn't she? Remember when she tried to tell me how to decorate my flat? Oh god, yes! The beige curtains. Traumatic. But seriously, this feeding stuff... little Leo was cluster feeding all evening, and I felt like I was living on the sofa. Oh, Lyra did that last week. Just relentless. I barely moved from the armchair. Ben tried to be helpful, bringing me endless cups of tea, but honestly, I just wanted him to take the baby and  do  the feeding himself, just for five minutes! Oh, Ben. He's a good egg, but they never truly understand, do they? Mark just looks terrified whenever I detach. Like I’m some kind of dangerous, milk-producing machine. It's hilarious and pathetic all at once. And then there’s Mum. She keeps asking if I’m getting enough iron. As if the answer isn’t “No, Mum, because I'm constantly nourishing a tiny human being!”. Oh, mine’s worse. She keeps comparing Leo to your cousin Emily’s baby, like it’s a competition. “Oh, Emily’s baby slept through the night at six weeks, is Leo doing that?” Ugh, the comparison game! It's… it’s exhausting. Honestly, sometimes I just want to hide under the duvet. Me too. It’s wonderful, obviously, having him, but sometimes... it's just  a lot . Have you spoken to Sarah about how’s she coping? She had Elsie a week before us. I texted her yesterday. She said she’s struggling with the lack of sleep. Elsie apparently screams for three hours straight every night. Oh, poor Sarah. That sounds awful. Maybe we should go over next week and take her a casserole or something?

Honestly, did you  see  what’s happening with the water companies again? Absolutely outrageous, isn't it? Pumping raw sewage into the sea… It’s beyond belief, isn’t it? And they’re still awarding themselves massive bonuses. It makes my blood boil. It’s just… greed, isn’t it? Pure and simple. They clearly don't care about the environment or anyone else, just profit margins. It’s disgusting. I was reading about it on my lunch break yesterday. Makes you wonder what’s actually  in  the sea when you’re swimming, doesn’t it? Exactly! Anyway, enough doom and gloom first thing. What’s everyone got on today? I’m on a late shift, so I need to get preparations done for that. I’ve got that budget meeting at work. Should be a delightful two hours of explaining why everything costs more. I swear, the council’s coffers are bottomless. I’m finally cracking on with that website copy for Miller’s bakery. They want everything super-local and ‘rustic’ looking. It’s a fun brief, actually. Might pop in later for a sourdough loaf. I’m going to try and get the garden sorted. The roses desperately need pruning, and that patch of weeds is mocking me. Plus, I promised little Leo I’d build him a den. Oh, Leo will love that! You’re a wonder, love. Right, I need to empty the dishwasher and then wrestle with the washing machine. Apparently, someone… …left a bright red sock in with the whites. Oh, come on! It was an accident! Besides, a little pink never hurt anyone. It'll hurt your clean white shirts, that's who. Honestly, you’re a menace to laundry, you are. Speaking of messes, Winston’s been shedding like crazy. I vacuumed the living room last night, and it looks like it’s snowed already this morning. Oh, Winston. That fluffball. I swear he thinks he’s a polar bear. Have you managed to get him to stop eating the house plants? We’re still working on it. I’ve moved them all up higher, but he’s getting sneakier. I found him attempting a climb onto the windowsill yesterday. He’s a determined little chap. Maybe you need to get him some catnip plants, so he has something acceptable to destroy. Good idea, actually. He’s a terror, but we all love the little fella.

Honestly, this Geography test is going to be the death of me. I just… I can’t remember all the capital cities. It’s useless information! Tell me about it. Mr. Davies is  determined  to make us memorise everything. Did you finish the fieldwork report? I’m still on the bit about the river erosion. Almost. I’ve got the methods section done, just need to write the conclusion. Which is awful because I don’t actually  understand  what the data means. It’s all metres and percentages… bleurgh. Ugh, maths is just… no. At least art is good. Miss Peterson is letting us do anything we want for the Christmas card designs. I’m thinking snow scenes, maybe with little robins. Ooh, that’s nice! I was thinking maybe a really abstract, colourful thing. Something completely different. Though, knowing my luck, I’ll just end up gluing glitter everywhere. You always do! Remember last year's attempt at a paper snowflake? It looked like a glitter bomb exploded. Oh god, yes. Mum was  not  impressed. Speaking of Christmas… are you going to the Ed Sheeran concert in Cambridge over the holidays? My dad managed to get tickets. No way! Seriously? I tried and tried but they sold out instantly. Lucky you! Is it… is it the one at Parker’s Piece? Yeah, apparently. It's going to be freezing, but worth it, I think. Dad’s promised hot chocolate beforehand to keep us warm. He's gone all out with the Christmas stuff already. He’s got that neighbour, Mrs. Higgins, helping him with the garden lights. Mrs. Higgins is a gardening  legend . Her roses are incredible. I wish I had her patience. My mum tried to get me into gardening over lockdown, but I just kept killing the plants. You and me both. I managed to accidentally water a cactus to death. A  cactus ! It’s basically impossible. See? It's not just me! Have you thought about what you want for Christmas? I’m dropping hints about a new set of watercolour paints. Mine are completely dried up. I’ve been asking for stamps. Seriously. My nan collects them and she’s letting me have some of her duplicates. Apparently, some of them are really old and valuable. That’s… surprisingly cool. Stamps? I just assumed you’d want something more, you know, teenage-y. I do love a good stamp.

Honestly, Doreen, that rat puppet’s staring at me. It’s unsettling, even in the corner like that. Oh, don't be silly, Arthur. It’s just Reginald. He’s harmless. Little Timmy made him at school. He was very proud. Reginald, eh? A fitting name. Reminds me of a particularly troublesome client I had back in the day. Always trying to wriggle out of things. Well, this Reginald is wriggling into my nightmares, I tell you. You'd think after all these years I’d be used to the… eccentricities of the grandkids’ crafts. It’s a lovely thing to have, Arthur. A memento. Speaking of eyes, have  you  booked your eye test yet? You were saying your vision was a bit blurry last week. I keep meaning to. Mrs. Higgins at the bus stop was talking about a new optician in Diss. Said they’re very good, but getting to Diss… that’s the rub. Diss isn’t so bad. I can run you, Arthur, if you like. Bit of a detour, but it’s no trouble. Would you, George? That’d be awfully kind. The bus is a bit of a gamble these days, isn’t it? Always seems to be running late, and you get all sorts on them. All sorts? What sort? Oh, you know. Loud music, people eating greasy chips, teenagers taking up two seats with their bags… the usual. And the drivers! Some of ‘em drive like they’re in a Formula One race. You’re sounding like a proper old man, Arthur. Grumbling about the youth of today and the state of public transport. Well, it  is  the truth! I remember when the buses ran like clockwork. And everyone was polite. That was before my time, dear. Although, I do remember when handbell ringing was more popular. Old Mr. Peterson led the group at St. Mary’s. He was a lovely man. Handbell ringing… now there’s a pastime. Never tried it myself. Sounds rather… precise. Precise is an understatement. It requires dedication. Old Mr. Peterson used to practice for hours. Said it’s all about coordination. Not unlike driving a bus, I suppose. You have to be coordinated, and patient. And avoid the Reginald-like obstacles. Oh, Arthur! You and your rat puppet. Just promise me you won't start giving him a voice. No promises. He’s starting to whisper things already.

Right, so after this, wanna have a proper wander around? I’ve seen a few little shops down near the canal I wanna peek in. Aye, sounds lovely, lass. It's nice just to  be  in Venice, isn't it? Proper calming. Though it's a bit different to how I remember it. Different how? You’ve been before, haven’t you? Ages ago, though? Oh, years ago. When you were just a little nipper. Your Dad and I came for our anniversary. It was… quieter then. Less tourists, less… stuff. More actual Venetian life, y'know? There weren't as many of these little tourist shops everywhere. It felt more  real . Yeah, I can imagine. It's pretty rammed even now, considering it's not peak season. Still, it’s beautiful. And the coffee here is amazing. Fancy another slice of that Tiramisu? It’s proper good. Go on then, twist my arm. One more slice won’t hurt! It's definitely better than anything you get back home. Not like those awful pre-made ones they sell in the supermarkets. Remember old Mrs. Higgins used to make a Tiramisu for the Christmas bazaar? Dreadful stuff. Too much marsala wine, it tasted like cough syrup. Oh god, you're right! It was… an experience. Though everyone was too polite to say anything. So, you reckon we should try and find some cicchetti later? I read about those – little Venetian snacks. Cicchetti! Ooh, now  that’s  a good idea. They used to be a proper working class thing, cicchetti. Back in the old days, the dockworkers would pop into the bacari – that's the little wine bars – for a quick bite and a glass of wine before or after their shift. Sounds perfect. We could make a little tour of them. Sample a few different ones. What sort of things do they usually serve? Oh, everything and anything. Little sandwiches, fried polenta with mushrooms, marinated seafood… they're small, but full of flavour. And you have to try the  sarde in saor  - sardines marinated in onions and vinegar. It's a bit of an acquired taste, mind. Sardines, huh? Okay, maybe we’ll save that for last. After a few glasses of wine, I might be more adventurous. Speaking of wine, what should we drink with the cicchetti? Oh, definitely a spritz. Either an Aperol spritz or a Campari spritz. They're a Venetian institution!

Honestly, the gym was  packed  this morning. Like, shoulder-to-shoulder in the free weights section. I nearly gave up and went home for a lie-in. No way! It's usually pretty quiet before ten, isn't it? Maybe everyone's really motivated after the bank holiday? Or just, you know, feeling guilty about all the chocolate. Probably the chocolate. Definitely the chocolate. Speaking of which, this peri-peri chicken is a  necessary  evil after that. I feel like I need to replenish my protein, or something. That’s a good excuse. I went for the halloumi burger, trying to be… vaguely healthy. Not entirely succeeding, obviously, it’s Nando’s. How was your weekend, aside from battling gym bunnies? Did you do anything fun? Not a huge amount, actually. I was supposed to go to that retro night at the Fez with Chloe and Liam, but Chloe came down with a terrible cold. So, ended up just having a really chill night in, face masks and terrible reality TV. You? Any exciting adventures? Quiet one for me too, to be honest. My cousin was visiting from London, so we mostly just caught up. We tried to go to that new cocktail bar, 'The Alchemist', but the queue was insane. Apparently everyone and their mother wants a colour-changing cocktail. Ugh, The Alchemist. I’ve seen pictures. It looks… chaotic. Still, a colour-changing cocktail does sound mildly impressive. Have you heard anything from Ben, by the way? I bumped into his sister at Tesco last week and she said he’s still travelling. Oh, yeah! Last I heard he was in Thailand, learning to scuba dive. He sent me a picture of him with a massive, colourful fish. It was very… Ben. Still texting various girls though, apparently. Classic. Of course he is. Some people never change. Honestly, I'm glad we're past all that drama. Remember when he tried to convince me he was a ‘free spirit’ right before dumping me via text? Don’t remind me! That was awful. You deserve better. How’s work going, though? Still buried under project deadlines? You have  no  idea. We’re launching this new internal communication platform, and it’s a total disaster. Everyone’s getting confused, the IT guys are stressed, and my manager keeps breathing down my neck. It’s… not ideal. How’s Bupa treating you?

…and honestly, the sheer volume of paperwork is astonishing. They’ve completely re-done the tenancy agreements, haven’t they? And it’s all just…boilerplate. No consideration for the specific issues with this building. Old Mrs. Higgins’ leak, for instance. Still dripping. They sent someone round, declared it ‘cosmetic damp’ and closed the ticket. Cosmetic! Cosmetic damp. A particularly British euphemism, wouldn’t you say? They’ve always been masters of understatement. Reminds me of a story I stumbled upon while researching in the Spanish archives… it concerned Philip II and Mary Tudor, you know. The Spanish ambassador writing back to court about the ‘slightly inclement’ weather in England. Inclement! It was a hurricane! Oh, you and your archives. Still working on the book, then? You’ve been saying ‘nearly finished’ for… well, a very long time. Nearly is, as they say, the halfway point to done. It  is  progressing, though. The British Library has been invaluable, of course. Though their cataloguing system… lacking, shall we say. I needed a particular pamphlet from 1575, concerned with the provisioning of the Spanish Armada, and it took a librarian nearly an entire morning to locate it. Buried amongst pamphlets about… chrysanthemums. Chrysanthemums? Good heavens. Honestly, sometimes you’d think they deliberately try to make research difficult. Now, speaking of difficult, have you seen the state of the bollards on Kennington Park Road? Utter chaos! They’ve put them in completely haphazardly. Bollards? Is that still raging? I thought that was settled. Settled? No! Old man Hemmings tripped over one last week and nearly broke his hip. And they’re positioned so badly, you can barely get a pushchair past. It’s all down to this new housing management company, I tell you. No local knowledge, no common sense. It always comes down to a lack of local knowledge. You get these administrators…they don't understand the fabric of a place. It’s like trying to explain France to someone who’s never been. I spent a summer in Provence, you know, years ago. Completely different world. The way they view property, enterprise… even land itself. It’s so much more...rooted. I’ve always wanted to go to France. Honestly, it sounds idyllic. Though I've heard the bureaucracy is dreadful. Dreadful is an understatement. And they have a surprisingly robust anarchist movement, did you know? Not the bomb-throwing sort, thankfully, mostly philosophical.

This Sweet and Sour Chicken is… actually pretty good. Better than I expected from a place in Slough, to be honest. Told ya! My Nan raves about this place. She says it’s the best in Bucks. Though, knowing Nan, that’s not saying much. She thinks anything with a red sauce is amazing. Mmmph… these noodles are decent. Way better than the school dinners, that’s for sure. Honestly, Mrs. Higgins is trying to poison us with that grey stuff she calls ‘shepherd’s pie’. Seriously! I swear it’s got approximately zero flavour. And don’t even  mention  the broccoli. It’s like chewing on tiny trees. Speaking of school… Mr. Davies is on one again. He spent the entire history lesson ranting about TikTok. Apparently, it’s the downfall of Western Civilization. No way! Did he actually say that? Davies is so old-school. He probably still uses a flip phone. He does! I saw him struggling with it last week when he was trying to call your mum about that detention, Leo. It was… glorious. Oh god, the detention. Right. I completely forgot. I’m still not sure why I got detention for ‘disruptive questioning’. I was literally just asking about the Treaty of Versailles! Disruptive questioning is code for ‘you embarrassed him because he didn’t know the answer’, Ben. We’ve been over this. Yeah, you caught him out, didn’t you? He hates that. It’s like challenging his authority or something. So, anyone seen the new issue of ‘Cosmic Crusaders’? I finally picked it up. The artwork is insane! Dude, yes! I grabbed it this morning. Vector Prime is finally getting his own solo story arc. It’s about time! He’s the coolest character. I’m more of a Nova Blast guy myself. Her powers are just way more versatile. Plus, she’s got a killer costume. You’re all nerds. Seriously. But… in a good way. Speaking of which, anyone got plans for the weekend? My dad's trying to get me to help him with the garden. It's torture. Ugh, gardens. No thanks. I’m supposed to be helping my little sister with her science project. It involves a volcano and a truly terrifying amount of baking soda. I’m expecting an explosion. Mine's a family thing too - gotta go to my aunt’s birthday. It’ll be full of awkward small talk and relatives I haven’t seen in years asking about my grades.

Honestly, this house is brimming. Brimming, I tell you! It’s like living in a charity shop. Now, Mother, you say that every time we visit. It’s just… accumulated things. Years of accumulated things. We've been meaning to sort through it all, haven’t we, David? Meaning to is the operative word, love. Jonathan's birthday’s taking up all the bandwidth at the moment. Have we actually nailed down a venue? Can we please have it at that new bowling alley? It's got laser tag too! Please? All my mates are saying it’s the best. Bowling? Good heavens, lad. A bit loud for an old woman like me, isn’t it? I’d much prefer something… quieter. Perhaps a nice afternoon tea? Somewhere with a garden? Afternoon tea is lovely, Doris, but a bit… sedate for Jonathan, don’t you think? He’s always been a bit of a scamp. I was thinking a pub with a private room? Somewhere we can decorate, and not worry too much about him knocking something over. Remember that vase at Auntie Margaret’s? Don’t remind me. It took weeks to smooth things over with Margaret. A pub sounds good. But we need to book soon. They’re all filling up for July. Can we get a bouncy castle? Just… one small bouncy castle? For after the bowling? A bouncy castle in a pub? Oh, the things they come up with! Now, now, Margaret, don’t be so quick to dismiss it. The boy has a point. It'd be a laugh, wouldn’t it? Though I’d likely break a hip trying to get on it. We’ll stick to the pub for now, Liam. But we can see about a small cake, shaped like a bowling pin? Yes! With little jelly people on top! Right, cake and pub are good. I'll start ringing around tomorrow. Has anyone thought about presents? I’m completely drawing a blank. He’s got everything. He mentioned needing a new gardening trowel. Though knowing Jonathan, he’ll buy three before we even get round to it. He did say his tablet was getting a bit slow. Maybe an upgrade? He's always complaining about the online shopping experience being terrible. Tablets! Honestly! What did people do before all this technology? Just talk to each other, that's what. Grandma, you used to send letters!

Ugh, I’m seriously stressing about options choices. It’s due next week, isn’t it? Yeah, next Friday, I think. I’ve kinda sorted mine, but I still feel weird about it. Like, what if I pick the wrong things? Exactly! That’s what I’m worried about. Everyone’s saying you need to think about what you want to  do  with your life, but how am I supposed to know that now? I mean, I don’t even know what I’m having for dinner. Right? It’s so much pressure. I’m doing triple science, definitely. And then… history and English Lit. I’m kinda leaning towards Art, but Chloe’s trying to convince me to do Geography. She says it opens up loads of jobs. Ooh, what kind of jobs? Chloe always knows about that stuff. She watches all those “a day in the life” videos on YouTube. Loads! Like, environmental consulting, town planning… apparently, you can even go into marketing with Geography. She showed me this YouTuber, uh… “GeoWizard”, I think? He travels around and does all these cool location-based challenges. GeoWizard? Sounds…intense. I’m more into beauty vloggers, honestly. I’ve been watching this one, ‘Lily Bloom’, all week. She's got, like, the perfect winged eyeliner every single time. It’s ridiculous. Haha, fair enough. I wouldn’t even know where to start with that. My eyeliner always ends up looking like a raccoon. Speaking of perfect, Miss Harrison was going on about "perfect duty" in PE today. As if anyone  loves  netball at 8.30 in the morning! Oh god, don’t even get me started on PE. I’m avoiding it as much as possible. I’d rather be practicing my clarinet. You’re actually really good at clarinet! You should totally do music for GCSE. I thought about it, but Mr. Davies said it’s really demanding. And I already have so much homework. I’m thinking maybe… Drama? It seems a bit easier. Drama’s good! You're quite dramatic! Remember when you tripped over during the school play last year and just  carried on  pretending it was part of the scene? Don't remind me! It was mortifying. But yeah, maybe. Have you thought about what you want to be when you’re, like, a proper grown-up? Honestly? No idea. I keep thinking maybe a vet, because I love animals, but then I remember all the… the stuff vets have to  do  to animals.

Right then, lovely to have you, Amelia. Bit of a drive from Harrow, isn't it? Not at all, George. Lovely to see you both. Though, honestly, the A11 was a trial. Slow as molasses. Saw a kestrel hovering by Attleborough, though. Magnificent. Kestrels are good, aye. Used to see ‘em all the time round Costessey when I was a lad. Fewer now, though. All these modern farms... not much room for roughage, is there? Dad, you wouldn’t  believe  the traffic getting back from Cambridge today. Completely gridlocked. They’re doing roadworks on the A14 again. Honestly, you’d think they’d learn. Roadworks. Always roadworks. They started on that stretch of the A47 near Dereham nearly six months ago, and it’s barely changed. Waste of public money, if you ask me. Though, I suppose a lot of it ends up lining someone’s pockets. It’s the same everywhere, George. Reminds me of when they built the North Circular. Went on for years and years. Used to drive my husband Ronald absolutely mad. He was a builder, you see, always knew how things  should  be done. Ronald was a good lad. Proper craftsman, he was. Used to make anything. Remember that bird table he built for you, Amelia? Still got it, I reckon? Oh, I do. Still in the garden. Bit rickety now, but very sentimental. Talking of gardens, I’ve been trying to get this new gardening software to work. Absolute nightmare. It’s supposed to tell you when to prune and what seeds to sow, but it keeps crashing! Which software is it, Gran? Maybe I can take a look? I’m fairly handy with computers. It’s called ‘BloomBuddy’, dear. Sounds idyllic, doesn’t it? It’s anything but. Keeps asking me for a ‘driver update’ or something. Honestly, I just want to stick to a calendar and a bit of common sense. Computers. I’ve never trusted ‘em. Give me a good map and a bit of logic any day. Reminds me of a story… back in the sixties, we were doing a survey for a new bypass near Thetford. Had one of those early calculating machines, you know, the ones with the reels of tape. Thing broke down halfway through, and we had to do the whole bloody thing again by hand! Ha! I remember them! Massive things they were. Took up a whole room, practically.

…and young Timmy, bless ‘im, he came home from school the other day, lookin’ right downcast. I said, “What’s up, lad?” And he says, “Miss told me off for drawing dinosaurs in maths.” Dinosaurs! In  maths ! What’s wrong with a bit of imagination, eh? Oh, that’s awful. Teachers these days…they just want robots, don’t they? No room for creativity. When I had the little ones, their primary school was lovely. Always encouraging art and… well, just  being  children. It’s a mixed bag, isn’t it? My youngest is at secondary now, and it’s a whole different ballgame. Pressure, pressure, pressure all the time. It's all about grades and league tables. He's talking about dropping history, which breaks my heart. He loves the Tudors. Tudors, eh? Good, solid history. Not like this modern stuff. All… opinions. No facts. Speaking of solid, have you seen the state of my wardrobe? It's overflowing. I swear, clothes just breed in there when I’m not looking. You and me both, Arthur. I’ve been trying to have a clear-out for weeks. It’s like confronting a lifetime of bad decisions every time I open it. Though, I did get rid of that floral jumpsuit. That was a mistake. I saw a delivery driver nearly take out Mrs. Higgins’ garden gnome yesterday. He was going  flying . She came out shouting, waving her walking stick. It was a sight. Oh, I’d have paid to see that! They’re always in a rush, those delivery men. Zoomin’ around like they’re escaping something. I reckon they're all secretly spies. Spies! Oh, Arthur, you always did have a vivid imagination. Remember that time you were convinced the milkman was signalling to aliens with his bottles? Well, he was! The arrangement of the bottles was… peculiar. Anyway, what’s that show you were watchin’ the other night? The one with the detective?  Line of Duty ? It’s a police procedural, very tense. Keeps you guessing. I’ve seen all the series now though. It's a bit of a binge-watch, to be honest. Binge-watching is all anyone does these days. Though, I did try this new app where you can ‘tweet’ your thoughts as you watch. Seemed a bit pointless if you ask me. Who needs to know I thought that actor was miscast?

Right, honestly, this snow is ridiculous. I was hoping to get out in the garden this weekend, finish off pruning the roses, but… forget it now. Tell me about it. I was planning on getting the raised beds sorted. Everything’s frozen solid. Proper Siberian conditions out there. At least we’ve got a good view from the window. It’s pretty, I’ll give it that. Though I'm starting to worry about the bird feeders. They'll be struggling to get at anything. I filled them up this morning, before it got really bad. Used that fancy sunflower heart mix. Hopefully, that'll help. Speaking of struggling…did you catch last night’s  Come Dine With Me ? Absolute disaster. Oh, don't even! Brenda's profiterole tower. A profiterole  tower . It looked like the Leaning Tower of Pisa made of cream and pastry. And she blamed the wobble on the central heating! As if! It was structural instability, pure and simple. Honestly, the tension was palpable. It always is, isn’t it? Anyway, less culinary carnage. Have you made any progress on sorting out Liam’s stag do? It’s getting close now, isn’t it? It is. I've got a deposit down on a brewery tour in Nottingham. Thinking we can make a weekend of it. Need to firm up numbers, though. And figure out what Sarah wants for her hen do. She’s being infuriatingly vague. Sarah is always vague. Trust me, I know. She'll say “Oh, something low-key” and then want a weekend in Barcelona. Exactly! I’m trying to subtly probe, but she just bats it all away with a smile. Perhaps if we get a list of people going to Liam’s, we can multiply that by the cost per head and then present Sarah with a figure she absolutely  cannot  ignore for her own. Ruthless. I like it. I can help with the guest list. I've got most of Liam’s family contacts. Speaking of costs…we really need to nail down these holiday plans for the summer. August is creeping up. I know, I know. I was thinking…maybe Cornwall? We haven't been down there in ages. The beaches are lovely, and we could do some decent coastal walks. Cornwall sounds fantastic. Though it’ll be packed. Remember that time we tried to get a table at Rick Stein's?

Now, this is a good roast, isn’t it? Proper gravy too. Not like that watery stuff you get nowadays. It is lovely, dear. Your daughter’s really outdone herself. Though I still say a bit more pepper wouldn’t go amiss. Everything’s a bit… bland, these days. Thanks, Gran. I did try to make it how you both like it. Though I did sneak in a little smoked paprika into the gravy, just to give it a bit of a kick. That’s a really nice touch, actually. It’s subtle, but it adds something. Much better than just plain old pepper. Smoked paprika, eh? Is that one of those foreign things? Everything’s foreign now, isn’t it? Used to be able to get a good Norfolk turkey, decent potatoes… now it’s all flown in from somewhere or other. Don’t start, Arthur. It’s just the way things are. You can’t stop progress, even if you  want  to. Though I do agree, the flavour isn’t quite the same. Remember old Man Hemmings’ farm? Best potatoes in the county. I’ve heard stories about Hemmings’ farm! Mum always said his potatoes were legendary. I tried to source some locally grown ones for this, but it was surprisingly difficult to find a consistent supplier. Everyone seems to want to import. It’s a weird thing, isn't it? We’re surrounded by farmland, yet getting genuinely local produce can be a challenge. Supply chains and all that. Supply chains! Sounds like something out of a science fiction film. Back in my day, you knew where your food came from. Old Man Hemmings, Mrs. Gable’s eggs… simple. Now you need a degree in logistics just to work out where your dinner’s been. You wouldn’t trust a computer anyway, would you, dear? Still think they’re all a bit of a fad. Fads! They're the devil's work, those computers. Making people lazy. And reliant on things they don't understand. Now, pass me the Yorkshire pudding, would you? That’s the best part, anyway. Doesn't matter where the flour comes from, a good Yorkshire pudding is a good Yorkshire pudding. Coming right up, Grandad. Glad you're enjoying it. I was worried I’d overdone them a little. They’re perfect. Light and crispy. Honestly, this whole meal is fantastic. You’ve really set the bar high.

Honestly, Mum, this roast is incredible. You’ve really outdone yourself. The gravy is  chef’s kiss . Yeah, seriously. I’m already planning how to subtly ask for the recipe. Don't tell anyone, but I’m rubbish at roasting. Oh, you young’uns. Everything has to be instant these days. Takes time and patience, roasting does. Your grandma, God rest her soul, she could roast a chicken blindfolded and it’d be perfect. She used to say the secret was talking to it while it cooked. Said it needed encouragement. Talking to chickens… nonsense. Used to just whack it in the oven, good enough for us. Didn’t have all these fancy thermometers and timers back then. Grandpa! You always say that, but I remember you meticulously basting the turkey every half hour. Basting? That was your Grandma’s doing! I was…supervising. Making sure she didn’t burn it. Of course you were. So, Mum, are you and Dad still thinking about downsizing? You were talking about it last time I was here. We are, love. It’s just… this house holds so many memories, you know? Fifty years we’ve been here. Raised all of you lot in these rooms. It’s a good house. Solid. They don’t build them like this anymore. Though, the garden  is  getting a bit much for us. I know what you mean. It's a lot to keep up with. Have you looked at any properties yet? Just online, mostly. Nothing’s really catching our eye. We don’t want to go to a retirement village, not yet anyway. Just something a little smaller, easier to manage. Maybe a bungalow. A bungalow would be nice. Less stairs, definitely. Remember Auntie Brenda falling down the stairs last year? Don't remind me. Nearly gave us all a heart attack. She swore the cat tripped her, but I think she just lost her footing. Cats are no good. Mischief makers, the lot of them. Always getting under your feet. Had a ginger tomcat once… tried to steal my dinner. You and your stories, Grandpa. So, Dad, any luck finishing that shed you started building? It's…progressing. Slowly. The weather hasn't been helping. And I seem to have misplaced half the screws. Sounds about right. You’re not exactly known for your DIY skills, Dad. Now, now! He’s a very capable man. He just… gets distracted easily.

Right, so I was chatting with Ben from ‘InnovateEd’ this morning, and he's still banging on about micro-credentialing. Honestly, it feels like everyone’s chasing the shiny object, doesn’t it? Like it’s the solution to everything. It  could  be, though, couldn’t it? If done well. The problem with universities is the rigidity. Three years, set modules… it doesn’t cater to people who need to upskill quickly, or change career paths mid-stream. That woman at the pottery class yesterday – she’s a solicitor, wanting to retrain as a horticultural therapist. A full degree isn’t practical for her. True, true. And that's where these shorter, skills-focused bursts  could  be amazing. But the issue, as he admitted, is quality control. Everyone and their dog is offering a ‘digital marketing certificate’ now. How do you differentiate the genuinely useful ones from the, well, fluff? Accreditation, I suppose. But that just creates another layer of bureaucracy. It’s the classic dilemma. Remember that startup in Auckland, “SkillStack”? They tried to curate a modular learning platform, aiming for verified outcomes. They burnt through funding in about eighteen months. Oh, SkillStack! Now you’re talking. I remember reading about them. Very ambitious, awful execution. They didn’t understand the market. They were trying to  be  the university, instead of complementing it. What they needed was a strong partnership with an established institution. Leverage that existing reputation. Exactly! And their marketing was dreadful. All jargon, no emotional connection. I keep seeing these EdTech companies make the same mistake. They focus on the tech, not the learner. The human element is crucial. That video going viral this week, the one with the physics teacher doing demonstrations with household objects…  that’s  engagement. No fancy platforms needed. You mean the bloke with the spaghetti and the earthquake simulation? Brilliant. My niece showed me that. It’s all about making it relatable, isn't it? And using humour. People learn better when they're enjoying themselves. Absolutely. It reminded me of old Professor Davies at Uni. He’d explain complex biological processes using puppet shows. Ridiculous, but you remembered it! That’s what we need to build into these new programmes – a bit of playful chaos. Less PowerPoint, more…performance. So, you’re thinking less “online course” and more “immersive workshop”? Something like that. And personalized learning pathways. Artificial intelligence could help with that – map skills gaps, suggest tailored modules… But again, it needs a human touch to oversee it.

Right, I’m officially declaring dinner a disaster. This butternut squash risotto is… an experience. It tastes vaguely of sadness. Oh no! What happened? You usually smash risotto. Honestly, it smells okay from here, though. Smells are deceptive, my friend. It's just… grainy. And I think I added too much stock. It's like butternut squash soup with rice instead of cream. You’ve got to try it, purely for a laugh. I think I’ll pass on the sadness risotto, thanks. Long shift, need brain food, not… existential culinary crises. How was your week at work, though? Still battling the spreadsheet monster? Don’t even  start  me on the spreadsheets. Mr. Henderson decided, mid-week, that we needed a completely new reporting format. Meaning I spent two days re-doing everything. Two days! He just sprung it on us in the meeting. Honestly, I’m fantasizing about moving to Cornwall and opening a little bakery. Just me, scones, and no project deadlines. Cornwall, huh? That’s a big jump from central London. It’s beautiful though, isn’t it? I went to St Ives last year with Mum. Proper postcard stuff. Though, honestly, the traffic getting  to  St Ives was horrific. Like, rural gridlock. See, even the idyllic life has its downsides! Although, gridlock involving tractors is arguably more charming than gridlock involving black cabs. What about you? Hospital still… intense? Intense is an understatement. Had a really tricky case yesterday. Young lad, really struggling. It’s days like that where I question all my life choices. Honestly, sometimes I wish I’d just become a librarian. Quiet, books, maybe a cat… A librarian  and  a mental health nurse? You'd be the most well-rounded person ever! You could prescribe books as therapy. "I diagnose you with a severe case of… needing to read more Jane Austen!" That's brilliant! I’d totally do that. Speaking of needing things… have you thought any more about Halloween? Sarah’s throwing a massive party. Theme is ‘haunted manor’ apparently. Haunted manor? Ooh, I'm in! I've already been browsing costumes. I was thinking maybe a Victorian ghost? All pale makeup and flowing white dresses. What about you? I'm leaning towards something a bit more… ironic. I'm thinking a surprisingly cheerful zombie. Bright pink tutu, combat boots, and full undead makeup. Just to mess with people. That's amazing!

Honestly, the traffic was  awful  getting here. Absolutely gridlocked on the M11. Took me nearly two hours. Two hours?! From Essex? That’s… intense. Did you check the traffic reports beforehand? Of course I did! Said ‘slow moving’, ‘slow moving’ is a lie, darling. It was stationary, mostly. Hundreds of cars just…baked in the sun. I had the window down, thankfully. Nearly melted. Ugh, that sounds dreadful. I was lucky. Train was surprisingly empty. Managed to get a seat and even did some reading for work. Report’s due on Friday. Always working, aren’t you? You’ll burn yourself out. When are you taking a proper holiday, love? Not just a weekend here and there. I know, I know. It's just…it's a busy time at the studio. Everyone’s stressed, and if I don’t pull my weight, things fall apart. Thinking maybe October? Somewhere warm? October’s good. You deserve a good break. Somewhere with a beach. Not one of those pebbly ones, mind you. I hate pebbles. Give me sand any day. Speaking of things falling apart, have you seen the state of the garden? It’s a jungle out there. Oh, Mum. You always steer the conversation back to the garden. Dad’s meant to be tackling it this weekend, isn’t he? He says he is. But ‘meant to’ and ‘does’ are two very different things, you know. He'll sit in his shed with a cup of tea, reading the paper. That’s his idea of gardening. I could pop round on Sunday and give him a hand? Unless you’d rather he wrestled with it alone. It builds character. Oh, that would be lovely, dear. Really. He'd appreciate it, even if he pretends he doesn't. It's mostly the weeds, and the roses need pruning. He's terrified of the roses, actually. Says they bite. Roses biting? That’s a new one. Maybe he needs a better pair of gardening gloves. Anyway, how was your appointment with Dr. Davies? Everything alright? You seemed a bit quiet on the phone. Oh, it was fine, fine. Just the usual. Blood pressure’s a bit up, apparently. He wants me to cut down on salt. Cut down on salt! Where’s the joy in life without a bit of salt on your food? Maybe just a little less? He’s trying to look after you.

Right, so I’m properly stressing about this stats assignment. Honestly, I feel like I'm reading another language. Like, what  is  a p-value, really? Oh god, stats. I feel your pain. It's so… abstract, innit? It's like they deliberately try to make it confusing. Did you try looking at the online resources Professor Davies linked? Yeah, a bit. They just use even  more  complicated words to explain it! It’s like a translation gone wrong. You know when you put something into Google Translate and it comes out… vaguely resembling English, but not actually helping? Exactly! That’s a perfect analogy. I was looking at the lecture slides again last night and honestly, it might as well be hieroglyphics. What are you struggling with specifically? Maybe I can… attempt to explain it. Well, it's all the hypothesis testing, and whether to reject the null hypothesis. Like, what even  is  the null hypothesis? It feels so… artificial. Why are we trying to disprove something that probably isn't true anyway? Okay, okay, deep breaths. Think of it like this… it’s about proving something  is  happening, right? The null hypothesis is basically saying 'nothing's going on'. So you're trying to gather enough evidence to say 'actually, something  is  going on, and it's not just random chance.' Hmm… that makes a bit more sense. But then it's all about confidence intervals and significance levels and… Ugh. It’s just so different from anything I’ve done before. It is. It's really methodical, which is good in a way, because it forces you to be precise. It’s all about applying a very specific scientific method. Like, you have to define your variables and your methods  before  you even look at the data, otherwise it’s all a bit dodgy. Dodgy. That's a good word for it. Speaking of dodgy, did you see the football last night? Man United were… well, they were Man United, weren't they? Oh, don't even  start  me. It was painful to watch. They had, like, one good five-minute spell and then just went back to aimlessly passing the ball around. Honestly, I’m starting to think Erik ten Hag is completely out of his depth. I know, right? I'm starting to wonder if we’ll ever get back to the glory days. It feels like a lifetime ago now.

Honestly, I nearly jumped out of my skin this morning. I was getting ready for work, and there was this  huge  spider, right in the shower. Oh, don't I know that feeling! They just appear out of nowhere, don't they? I had one in the kitchen last week, clinging to the lightshade. Gave me a fright, that did. A lightshade! That's even worse. I can deal with them on the floor, you know, you can carefully guide them into a jar. But up high… impossible. My husband had to deal with it. He’s much braver than I am. My Derek wouldn't go near one. He screams! Honestly, a big, grown man. He gets me to get rid of 'em. Though I'm not exactly thrilled about it, mind. Especially the big hairy ones. Oh, the hairy ones are the worst! Though, you know, I read somewhere that they’re actually quite good to have around. They eat other insects. That's what they say, but I'd rather have a few flies than a spider the size of my hand, thank you very much. Speaking of unwanted guests, we’ve had a bit of a problem with mice lately. Oh no, really? That sounds awful. We haven’t had any, thankfully. Though we did have a bird fly into the kitchen window last week. Scared the life out of both of us! Oh dear! Was it alright? It just stunned itself. Flapped around for a bit, then seemed to recover and flew off. But it was a right thump. I thought something had broken! It was a robin, a little beauty. Lovely. We get a lot of birds in the garden. Blue tits mostly. And a cheeky little robin too, comes right up to the window sill. It’s nice, but they make such a mess with the birdseed, don’t they? They do. But it’s worth it, isn't it? To see them. I always feel guilty if I run out of seed. It is nice. Although, the mess attracts the mice, I reckon. It's a vicious circle, really. I've got traps down, but they're clever little things. They are. It’s awful, isn’t it? Living alongside all these creatures, some of them welcome, some decidedly not. I suppose it’s just part of living in the countryside. That's true.

It’s lovely to finally put a face to the name, isn’t it? I mean, we’ve spoken on the phone a few times arranging this, but actually  meeting … it’s nice. Especially after all the family tree digging. Honestly, I feel like I know your great-grandmother better than some of my own relatives now! Oh, don't I know the feeling! It’s a strange thing, isn’t it? Getting so invested in people you never knew. Though, your information on the Hughes side was invaluable. I'd always  heard  stories about Old Man Hughes being a bit of a rogue, but you actually found a record of him being fined for… was it sheep stealing? It was! And apparently, not just sheep. A pig, a goose, and a rather fetching cream separator. He was a character, clearly. It explains a lot about my grandfather, actually. That rebellious streak runs strong. Though thankfully, he channeled his into… well, a slightly less illegal profession. That's often the way, isn't it? A bit of mischief gets refined into something more acceptable as the generations pass. It’s a comforting thought. Though, it’s funny how you can trace habits like that. It makes you wonder what bits of  me  will show up in the grandchildren. Speaking of family, I’m so sorry to hear about your mother, you know. I saw the notice… Thank you. It was… a long process. She had Vascular Dementia. It started subtly, little memory lapses mostly, but it progressed so quickly. The last year was particularly difficult. It feels strange, even now. Losing someone piece by piece before they’re actually gone. That sounds absolutely heartbreaking. I had a colleague, lovely woman, went through something similar with her husband. She said it was like watching a favourite book slowly have its pages ripped out. A brutal image, but a truthful one, I think. That’s… that’s exactly it. Every lost memory felt like losing a part of  her . It’s terrible seeing someone so vibrant… reduced. She was a headmistress, you know. A very formidable woman. Always pushing me to excel. A headmistress! No wonder you became a teacher. It must be in your blood. Though, I suspect you had a natural aptitude for it too. Were you always drawn to the profession? Not immediately, actually. I tried marketing for a year after university.

Honestly, seeing those hot air balloons drift over the fields just… makes everything feel alright, doesn't it? It’s utterly ridiculous, really, giant fabric bubbles, but so peaceful. It is lovely. Bit of a contrast to marking essays about post-structuralism, that’s for sure. Did you see how low that one came? You could almost wave at the pilot. I did! I wonder if they get used to people waving. Probably just see a blur of waving arms. Oh, look, Maisie’s gone rabbit-hunting again. She’s a menace, that dog. A fluffy, adorable menace. She’ll probably come back covered in mud. Honestly, she thinks every field is her personal obstacle course. It’s good for her, though. She needs it. City life was…limiting. Remember trying to take her to Regent’s Park and she just wanted to chase pigeons into traffic? Vaguely trying to block that memory out, actually. This is so much better. Look, a kestrel! Hovering. Brilliant. I haven't seen one of those in ages. They're fantastic aren't they? It's amazing how they can just hang in the air like that. Shame about those power lines, though. Completely ruin the view in that direction. They do. Necessary evil, I suppose. Though, you'd think they could bury them these days. It’s not like it’s a particularly challenging landscape. Thinking about it, they probably cost a fortune to maintain, too. Probably. Everything does. Speaking of fortunes…did you see the price of camping gear lately? We’re going to need new tent pegs, at least, and a repair kit for the airbed. Don’t even mention it. It’s daylight robbery. Why is everything so expensive? We're basically paying for the privilege of being slightly uncomfortable in a field. Exactly! And then there’s the food. “Glamping” is the answer. Someone else to set everything up, and cook… and potentially fend off Maisie if she decides the glamping tent is now her castle. You're awful. But you're right. Maybe next year. Although, the money… I need to have a serious look at the budgeting spreadsheet. That conference funding application didn’t come through, so… Oh, that’s a shame. That would've been really helpful. We can manage, though. We always do. Maybe less… gourmet marshmallows around the campfire? Sacrilege! You’re suggesting cuts to the marshmallow budget?

Honestly, this weather is just… relentless, isn’t it? Still grey, even for October. I was hoping for a bit of autumnal sunshine, you know, golden leaves and all that. Aye, it’s a damp one, alright. Proper Yorkshire weather, this. Though even up north we get a bit of brightness, usually. You don't get much sun in Solihull, do ya? Always seems a bit… muted. You’re not wrong. It’s quite a change from where I grew up. Hitchin gets its fair share of gloom, but it's a different  kind  of gloom. Less… persistent. How are things at the gyms? Still battling to get everyone motivated as the nights draw in? Tell ya what, it  is  harder. Summer’s easy – everyone wants to look good for holidays. October… it’s a slog. I had one fella this morning saying he was thinking of giving it a miss ‘til January. January! Like he’ll just magically be fit then. Oh, the January rush! We get that with language classes too. Everyone full of good intentions after Christmas, aiming for fluency by Easter. It rarely happens. Ha! Sounds about right. It’s all about consistent effort, isn’t it? I try and tell ‘em that. Proper coaching, small goals, building it up. Sometimes they listen, sometimes they just want a quick fix. Exactly. It’s the same with languages. People want to be fluent after three lessons. I always say, think of it like building a house – you need foundations first! Speaking of which, I’m trying to read this book on language acquisition, all about the subconscious processes and how we internalise grammar. It’s… dense. Oh yeah? What’s it called? I do a bit of reading myself, mostly thrillers. Something to switch off from all the gym talk. Though, I did try and learn a bit of Spanish once, for a holiday. Didn't get far, I’ll be honest. It's called  The Architecture of Language . It's fascinating, but it feels like I need a degree in linguistics just to  understand  the footnotes. I’m teaching a group of business professionals Spanish at the moment. It’s fun, but they mostly just need phrases for meetings and negotiating. Less concerned with subjunctive moods, thankfully. Negotiating, eh? I used to be terrible at that. Years of letting people walk all over me. Had to learn the hard way.

Right, now then, have you managed to get the washing line sorted, love? It's lookin' a bit worse for wear after that wind we had last week. Nearly, Grandma. Just need to tighten up one of the posts. Found the spanner in the shed, but it was covered in… stuff. “Stuff” is a polite word for muck, lad. Your Grandad always said the shed was a repository for all the world’s lost socks and discarded bits of string. Aye, and rusty tools. You could build a whole new shed out of the rusty tools in that shed. Don't bother with a new line though, lass. They don’t make ‘em like they used to. Remember when washing lines were made of proper rope, not this flimsy plastic stuff? I remember. You could hang a horse off those lines, they were so strong. This one’s alright for sheets and towels, but anything heavy and it’ll give way. Speaking of heavy, did you remember to take the bins out, Ethan? Oh! Crikey, nearly forgot. The recycling one’s full to the brim. Loads of cardboard from all the Amazon parcels. Amazon! Hmph. In my day, we didn’t need Amazon. We went to Woolworths! Everything you could possibly want, all under one roof. And a pick ‘n’ mix! And proper service, lass. You asked for something, they  found  it for you. Not like now, you spend half an hour lookin’ for someone to help. True enough. Though I do appreciate having things delivered, saves my back. Now, have you lot decided what you want for tea? I was thinking a shepherd’s pie. Ooh, yeah, that sounds good! Can I have extra gravy? Gravy's always good, lad. Though your Grandma makes a gravy that could cure all ills, wouldn’t you agree, Arthur? Best gravy in Yorkshire, I'll tell you that for nowt. Though I reckon I could give her a run for her money… Oh, go on, Arthur, don't start. You and your gravy. It's always too watery! He's got a point, Grandma. Sometimes it's a bit… soup-like. Cheeky boy! It's not soup-like, it’s  rich ! You youngsters don't appreciate a properly made gravy anymore. Alright, alright, settle down. No need for a gravy war. I’ll make the shepherd’s pie, and Arthur can make his “soup-like” gravy if he insists.

Honestly, this satnav is driving me round the bend. It insists we go through that tiny village again. The one with the bridge that looks like it’ll collapse if a pigeon lands on it? Aye, Old Brampton. It’s a scenic route, if you like scenic and terrifying in equal measure. Are you sure you haven’t accidentally set it to ‘most challenging’? I’ve checked three times! It’s on fastest route. Honestly, I used to be able to navigate by map reading. Proper map reading, with an OS map and a compass. Remember those days? Vaguely. Mostly I remember getting lost and you getting cross. This is definitely preferable. Besides, it gives us time to listen to that new album. Have you given the new Lankum record a proper listen? A bit. It's… intense. Very intense. I prefer something a bit lighter on a drive, to be honest. Something with a bit of a beat. Like The Unthanks. Have you heard their latest poetry settings? I have! Beautiful. Reminded me of that ceilidh we went to in Penrith last year. Do you remember old Mr. Henderson trying to teach everyone the Gay Gordons? He was a disaster. A delightful disaster! He had the enthusiasm, if nothing else. Though, I suspect he’d had a wee dram or two beforehand. Speaking of which, did you remember to pack that flask of ginger wine? Naturally. Wouldn’t dream of embarking on a journey like this without it. Though, knowing our luck, we’ll arrive at the gig and it’ll be teeming with police. Remember that time in Keswick when… Don’t even start! I’m still mortified about Keswick. And my ankle! It’s still not quite right, you know. That cobblestone was lethal. It was a rogue cobblestone. A menace to society, that stone. It’s a wonder we get anywhere at all. Speaking of getting anywhere, the weather forecast isn't brilliant for tomorrow. Looks like more rain. Perfect weather for pottering about in the wool shop, then. I need to get started on that jumper I promised Elsie for her birthday. She’s been hinting for months! She’s a canny one, that Elsie. Always knows how to get what she wants. Like you with that new loom. One minute you're saying you don't need it, the next… It was on offer! And it’s a Dobcross loom.

Right, so I’m officially operating on caffeine and a pain au chocolat. This site visit this morning really took it out of me. Did you see the state of that plumbing? Honestly, it was…a choice. A bold architectural statement in corroded copper, perhaps? No, seriously, it was appalling. I’m going for the full English. Need something substantial after witnessing  that . And how was your morning commute? Mine involved a man having a very loud phone conversation about his cat’s dietary requirements. Oh, classic. Mine was mostly avoiding eye contact. Though I did overhear two girls dissecting last night’s Love Island. Brutal. Apparently, Liam is “playing a game.” You’d think people would have better things to worry about. The modern condition. Anyway, speaking of things to worry about, have you spoken to Ben recently? He sounded utterly miserable on the phone yesterday. Said he’s completely overwhelmed with the Henderson project. No, not since Friday. Poor Ben. He always takes on too much. He’s brilliant, genuinely, but he doesn’t know how to say no. I told him he needed to delegate, but he just sighed and said “easier said than done.” He's probably pulling all-nighters again. Typical. Someone needs to stage an intervention. Or at least hide his laptop. So, back to slightly less depressing topics… what are your initial thoughts on the university brief? I’m still wrapping my head around the “communal living” aspect. It’s…ambitious, isn't it? Designing a complex that facilitates both privacy and community. It feels like a real challenge to get the balance right. I’m leaning towards emphasizing shared outdoor space, like courtyards and rooftop gardens. Creates opportunities for accidental interaction. I like that. I was thinking about modular designs – something adaptable. Allowing residents to customize their spaces but still maintain a cohesive aesthetic. It's less about grand statements and more about functionality, I think. Which is kind of…us, isn’t it? Point taken. We’re not exactly known for excessive ornamentation. Remember old Professor Davies critiquing my dissertation? Said it lacked “soul.” Oh god, Davies. He was brutal. "Technically proficient, but emotionally vacant," wasn't it? I think he just hated anyone who dared to prioritize practicality over pretension. Honestly, the man’s designs looked like they were actively trying to trip people. Precisely! Though, maybe there’s a certain…irony in that?

Right, milk, sugar? You know I’ve started having mine with a tiny splash of vanilla extract. It’s lovely. Just milk, thanks Mum. Vanilla sounds… posh. How was your day? Still battling the A1 traffic? Posh but simple, honestly. And the A1 was, shall we say, ‘spirited’. Someone decided merging onto the roundabout was optional. Nearly caused a pile-up. Honestly, the driving standards these days… Ugh, tell me about it. I was behind someone on the B6403 this morning who thought their indicators were purely decorative. Just drifted into my lane. I had to brake. Honestly! It’s not hard, is it? It’s basic courtesy. I swear, people think their cars are some sort of personal fortress. Did you hear from Chloe about Saturday? She was supposed to confirm if she could make it for dinner. Oh, yes, she messaged. She can’t, unfortunately. Something’s come up with Liam. Apparently his nan is poorly. She sends her love, though. Oh dear, that’s a shame. Poor Liam’s nan. And a shame about Saturday, I was looking forward to us all catching up. It feels like ages since we’ve all been together. I know, it does. Everyone’s so busy. Sarah’s doing that extra course, isn't she? And Ben’s still working ridiculous hours. He is. It’s a good job, but it’s consuming him. I think he needs a proper holiday. Speaking of holidays, have you thought about what you’re doing with your leave this year? Not really. I was thinking maybe a weekend somewhere… Brighton maybe? It’s easy enough to get to. Or maybe a city break? Brighton’s lovely. We went there for our anniversary a few years ago. Though it can get  packed . A city break sounds nice. Rome? Barcelona? We could even look at Paris, and I could dust off my schoolgirl French. Oh, please no! I’d rather not witness that. Maybe Barcelona. I’ve always wanted to go. We could look at some deals. I’m quite good at finding little bargains. Anyway, enough about travelling. How’s work going? Are you still enjoying being a civil servant? It’s… fine. It’s stable, which is good. It's not exactly exhilarating, but it pays the bills. I'm mostly doing data entry at the moment. Very thrilling. Well, stability is important. And at least it gives you time to pursue your hobbies.

Right, so I’ve been looking at the job description again, and it’s… a lot. More than I initially thought. The Media Coordinator role at the Arts Council? Yeah, it looked pretty full-on. But a good full-on, y’know? Proper responsibility. That’s what worries me. Responsibility is good, obviously, but I’m not sure I have  all  the things they’re asking for. They want someone with experience in social media marketing, event management, press release writing… and grant applications! Grant applications! Blimey. Okay, breathe. You’ve done press releases for the school, haven’t you? And you’re a natural at social media, you’ve built up a decent following for your language learning stuff. That’s different! That’s me talking about verb conjugations. This is about promoting… performance art. And reaching a wider audience. It’s not the same skillset. It’s transferable, love. You’re a communicator, you understand how to reach people. And event management… remember that school trip to France? You organised the whole thing! The hotels, the itinerary, the emergency contact list… you were amazing. That was seven years ago! And it was stressful. I swore I’d never organize another group of teenagers again. They lost three passports. Okay, fair enough. But the point is, you  can  do it. Look, they’re asking for a lot, that’s true. But they’re also probably expecting candidates to tick, like, 90% of the boxes. Don’t self-reject before you’ve even applied. You’re right. It’s just… the thought of an interview. I’m terrible at interviews. I either ramble on for too long or freeze completely. You don't ramble! You’re enthusiastic. And freezing… well, practice is key. We can do mock interviews. I’m pretty good at the grilling technique. Years of radio, you know. I can ask the tough questions. That sounds terrifying. But maybe… helpful. What kind of questions do you think they’ll ask? Besides the obvious ‘tell me about a time you failed’ stuff. They’ll want to know about your understanding of the arts sector. So brush up on what the Arts Council does, their current projects, that kind of thing. And they'll definitely ask about your experience with different media platforms. Be prepared to talk about analytics, engagement metrics… the jargon. Jargon. Always the jargon. I’ll have to do some serious Googling.

Right, so, genuinely, I’ve been thinking… this house-sitting thing is amazing, right? But it’s just… amplifying it, isn’t it? How much I just  don’t  want to go back to the grind. The constant pitching, the fundraising… it's exhausting. It is, isn't it? You seemed so burnt out before we even left. And honestly, watching you properly relax for the first time in ages has been… good. It makes the idea of you doing something completely different feel less like a pipe dream. But what  is  the something different? You've mentioned a few things. Okay, well. Remember that pottery course we did in Devon, ages ago? Before everything got… hectic? I really enjoyed that. The physicality of it, the focus… it was almost meditative. And I was actually… decent. You  were  good! I remember being jealous of your wonky but charming vases. But turning that into a business? That feels like a huge leap. Australia's expensive, even house-sitting doesn't negate that. I know, I know. It’s not about quitting everything tomorrow. It's about building something  alongside  things, initially. I’ve been sketching out an idea for small-batch, handmade ceramic planters. Unique designs, good quality clay… Instagram, local markets, maybe even a small Etsy shop. Less pressure than a tech startup demanding venture capital, you know? That actually sounds… really nice. It plays to your creative side, it’s tactile, and it’s less dependent on constant growth. But you'd need a space. Somewhere to work, a kiln… that’s a considerable investment. I've been looking. There’s a little industrial unit just outside of Byron Bay. Rent’s reasonable, has power, water, and apparently, the local council are surprisingly supportive of small arts businesses. It’s about an hour’s drive from here, but… manageable. Byron Bay… that’s moving pretty quickly, isn’t it? We haven’t even discussed what that would mean for  us . I like my job, I'm secure… bringing that stability. I'm not necessarily itching to uproot everything. I know, and I wouldn't ask you to. That's why I haven't mentioned it properly until now. But if I started small, just building up the business gradually, you could keep teaching. We could look at moving part-time, maybe finding a school closer to Byron? Or even renting a smaller place here for a few months while I get things started?

Honestly, Leo, you've got peas  all  over your chin. Look at you, a little green sprout! Peas good! Peas yummy! He's a messy one, isn't he? Reminds me of wee Jamie MacIntyre, used to paint himself blue with mashed potatoes. Absolute terror, but a sweetie at heart. Blue with potatoes, you say? The things children get up to. I remember my granddaughter, Penelope, deciding the living room carpet needed redecorating with beetroot juice. A financial disaster, that was. Oh, don’t even  start  on decorating. We're still waiting for a quote for a new kitchen. Honestly, the housing situation around here is appalling. Finding builders is like pulling teeth, and then they want a king's ransom for the job. And the school places! Dreadful, absolutely dreadful. My neighbour’s granddaughter didn’t get into any of the local primaries. They’re talking about sending her miles away. It's not right, is it? A consequence of…well, many things, really. A growing population, insufficient forward planning. And, of course, the influx of…shall we say, new communities. You mean the Polish families? Dad, seriously? Now, now, dear, I’m not being prejudiced. Simply observing. There's been a significant influx, hasn’t there? And it puts a strain on resources. There’s always been migration, Arthur. Always. Glasgow was full of Irish folk when I was a girl. Had to learn to understand the accent! And they all contributed. Exactly! And it’s not just them. Everyone deserves a good school for their children. It’s a basic right. Speaking of rights... Uncle George is still going on about his physiotherapy. Apparently, the NHS won’t cover a full course. Grampa George grumpy? A little bit grumpy, yes. He says his knee is acting up again. Honestly, the NHS is a wonderful thing, but it’s stretched to breaking point. And the paperwork! Don't even get me started on the paperwork. It's enough to give anyone a headache. Speaking of things needing fixing... have you seen young Timothy’s beard? It's…ambitious, to say the least. Looks like a squirrel is nesting in it. Oh, don't! He's very proud of it. He's trying to achieve a “lumberjack chic” look, apparently. Lumberjack chic! Goodness me. When I was a teacher, the boys just wanted to look like footballers. Though, I remember one boy who grew a very impressive moustache for a school play…he was playing a villain, you see.

…and honestly, the whole referendum thing just felt so… divisive, didn’t it? Everyone at it in the pub, shouting. It's calmed down a bit now, thankfully. Though I still get a shiver thinking about it. Oh, you’re telling  me . It was awful. My sister and brother-in-law were practically not speaking for months. Still a bit frosty, actually. And the misinformation… it was relentless. I spent ages trying to explain things to my Mum, and honestly, it felt like talking to a brick wall. Exactly! It's like people just refused to listen to anything that didn’t confirm their own beliefs. Speaking of things that require patience… have you heard anything more from Sarah about piano lessons for Lily? She’s been asking again. Oh, not yet. She's been so busy with preparations for the fete. Apparently, they’re hoping for a record turnout this year. They've got that bouncy castle booked, and she’s organising the face painting. It’s a mammoth task, honestly. Still, good for her, getting involved. It is lovely she does that. Remember when  we  were organising events at sixth form? The stress! All those bake sales and charity washes... God, don’t remind me! I swore I’d never look at another sponge cake again. Although, I was quite good at the face painting, if I say so myself. Remember that time I painted little Kevin Thompson as a tiger? He was thrilled. Poor Kevin. What’s he up to these days? Last I heard, he was an accountant somewhere in London. Married, two kids. A far cry from the tiger-faced teenager. Anyway, did you manage to get those car park passes sorted for the sports centre? I’m taking Mum on Tuesday for her aquafit class. Oh, nearly forgot! Yes, they’re in the post. Should arrive tomorrow. It’s ridiculous how much they cost, isn’t it? Like they’re penalising people for trying to keep fit. Though, speaking of fitness, I’m really struggling to get back into my walking routine after that awful cold. Oh, you were poorly, weren’t you? It’s going around. Mum had it last week. Felt like she’d been run over. It knocked me for six. Even thinking about it now makes me feel a bit tired. I’m supposed to be going on that walking holiday with Brenda next month.

Right, so I was explaining to old man Hemmings from marketing this morning…the absolute  state  of his Twitter game. Oh, Hemmings. Is he still tweeting about golf and vaguely political things? Worse. He'd retweeted a meme about… honestly, I can’t even repeat it. It was something about Nicola Sturgeon and a shortbread tin. I had to have a quiet word. It's bad enough he doesn’t understand hashtags, but that was just…a disaster waiting to happen. You're a saint, really. Dealing with that. I've been trying to get the postgrad students to actually  use  Twitter for academic discussion, rather than just looking at cat videos. It’s a losing battle. Academic Twitter is a whole other beast, isn’t it? It's just people arguing about philosophy and citing incredibly long threads. I dip in occasionally, mainly to see who's falling out with who. Exactly! It’s like a particularly aggressive pub debate, but in 280 characters. I tried to get them to follow a few key academics in their field, build a network… they just looked at me blankly. They’re too young, probably. They’ve grown up with TikTok and Instagram. Twitter feels… ancient history to them. They want visuals. Quick hits. Reels. Aye, exactly. Though I’ve ironically found Instagram helpful for promoting the department. Pictures of the farm, students working on projects… gets more engagement than anything I post on the uni website. See?
