It's all about knowing your audience. That’s what I was trying to explain to Hemmings. He needs to understand  who  he’s trying to reach, and what kind of content they’ll actually respond to. He thinks everyone cares about his opinions on Brexit. Oh, bless him. He’s a good guy, just…a bit tone-deaf. I tried to explain the concept of ‘going viral’ to my mum last week. She thought I meant getting a cold. That's brilliant! My Gran asked me if the ‘cloud’ was actually raining in California. They just don’t get it. It's a different world. And the amount of time I spend crafting a carefully worded tweet, then watching it get like, eight likes… Honestly, sometimes I wonder why I bother. I feel that. Though, when a campaign  does  land, it's a surprisingly good feeling. We did that one last month for the new charity partnership, and the response was amazing.

Honestly, this weekend was  wild . I’m just… depleted. Did you even manage to switch off at all, Chloe? A little, thankfully. Saturday was mostly spent marking essays, which is…a special kind of exhausting. Sunday was better, though. Went for a hike with Ben. You know, proper muddy boots and everything. How about you? What was the whirlwind? Oh, it was a whirlwind of Sarah’s birthday. Started Friday night with that tiny bar she loves, then Saturday was a bottomless brunch – which, let me tell you, is never worth the hype – followed by attempting to navigate a cocktail-making class. Disaster. Cocktail-making? You and disasters are old friends. What went wrong? Everything! I accidentally put salt instead of sugar in mine.  Salt . It was…memorable. And Liam kept trying to ‘help’ which just meant loudly critiquing everyone else's technique. Honestly, the man. Liam sounds delightful, as always. Still going strong then? Yeah, still going. Though I'm starting to seriously question my life choices sometimes. He's just…so  opinionated  about everything. Even cocktails. Speaking of things being annoying, I tried that new recipe for the lentil shepherd’s pie you suggested? Oh yeah! How did it go? I was fairly confident in that one. It…did not go. It tasted like sadness and lentils. It was so bland. I followed the recipe exactly! I swear! I think my tastebuds are broken. Ooh, that's rough. Maybe your spices are old? It's easily done. I’ve been chucking loads out recently, realised I was using paprika from 2018. Possibly. Or maybe I’m just a terrible cook. I think I'll stick to ordering takeaway for a while. What have you been cooking lately? You always make everything look so effortless. Effortless is a strong word. I’m just slightly less prone to accidental salt-based beverages. I did a really nice Thai green curry on Wednesday. Super easy, actually. I can send you the recipe if you want. Please do! That sounds amazing. I’m craving something with flavour right now. This lentil disaster has scarred me. Will do. Oh, and quick question. Are you free next Saturday? Amelia's having a little housewarming thing, and she asked if you'd be up for coming. Amelia! Oh, that’s lovely. Yes, definitely. I haven't seen her in ages. What's the plan? Just a casual evening, she's doing pizza and stuff.

Right, so, the lamb’s looking good, isn’t it? Bit pink, maybe, but good. You’ve outdone yourself, love. Oh, thanks, Dad. Just trying to make a nice Sunday dinner. Everything alright with you, Sarah? You’ve been awfully quiet. Just thinking, that's all. About Michael, mostly. Still no firm dates for his visit, then? No, nothing solid. He’s being… evasive. Says work’s manic, but I reckon that’s not the whole story. I tried calling him again last night, went to voicemail. Says he’ll ring when he can. It’s just typical, isn’t it? He always does this. Makes plans, then backs out, or just… disappears for a bit. Remember last Christmas? He promised he’d be here, then texted on the day to say he was stuck in a meeting. And the year before that, he said he had a terrible cold. We all knew he’d just stayed out too late at a work do. Honestly, he's never grown up. Don't start, Sarah. He’s got his own life. And work is genuinely stressful for him, you know. Management’s a rough game. I know, Dad, but it's the principle of the thing. It's disrespectful, flitting in and out like that. Especially when we’re trying to arrange something. Are we even bothering with a proper Christmas this year? We should. Michael needs to make an effort, though. He knows how much it means to your father. I just want to see him settled, that’s all. He’s always chasing something, never content. And that girlfriend of his… I still haven’t met her properly. Just a fleeting hello at that pub lunch last summer. She seems nice enough, from what I’ve seen on Facebook. Bit… bohemian. Lots of photos of her painting and doing yoga. Bohemian? Sounds exhausting. Is she the reason he’s being so vague about coming? Perhaps she doesn't want to spend Christmas with the family? Could be. I don’t know. Oh, speaking of things coming and going – has anyone seen my car keys? I swore I left them on the hall table. They’re on the kitchen counter, Dad. Next to the fruit bowl. You were admiring Lesley's new car when she popped round earlier, weren’t you? Was I? Oh, yes. Lovely little thing, that Mini. All shiny and new.

Honestly, Arthur, this Spanish is killin’ me. Absolutely killin’ me. I thought French was tricky, bein’ a bit closer to us, but this… this is a whole other kettle of fish. I know, love, I know. It is a bugger, isn't it? All those verb conjugations. It’s enough to make your head spin. I’m trying the Duolingo thing, you know, the little green owl keeps nagging me. Oh, that owl! He’s a menace. I started that, but he just stresses me out. “You haven’t practised in twelve hours!” Like I haven’t got a life, the cheek of it. I’m tryin’ a proper class, down at the community centre. Real people, real mistakes, a bit of laughin’. A class is good, yeah. More sociable. Though I find I get flustered when I have to  speak  it out loud. My tongue just gets tied in knots. I can read it alright, slowly, but actually forming the words… it’s awful. That's the worst bit, isn't it? I keep wanting to put the English word order in. “Yo tengo a book,” I said to Mrs. Rodriguez last week. She nearly choked on her tea. Oh dear. They’re a forgiving bunch, those Spanish teachers. I reckon they've seen it all. Still, it makes you wonder how folk manage to learn these languages properly. Especially the ones that are really different. It’s the immersion, isn’t it? That’s what they reckon. Living in the country. I was thinkin’ about it the other day, lookin’ at Spain and how many different tongues they have. Catalan, Basque… Oh, aye. And Galician, isn’t it? Always forget that one. It's amazing, really. People growing up speakin’ two languages as naturally as breathing. Castillian and Catalan, for instance. Do they teach each other, or is it just… picked up? I read an article about it. Apparently, it’s often a political thing, as much as anything. The schools teach both, but there’s a real emphasis on preserving the regional languages. They don’t want them swallowed up by the main one. It's sensible, I suppose. Losing a language is like losing a piece of your history. Makes you think about Wales, and Welsh. They’re doing their best to keep that alive. Exactly! And Ireland with Gaelic. It’s a fight, though. A proper fight against the tide of… well, English, mostly.

Right, so this pile… is basically everything that mysteriously appeared in the last six months. Bills, letters, stuff for the house…Dad, are you sure you haven’t been secretly running a second life? Don't be daft, lad. Just… accumulating, that’s all. Happens when you get a bit older, you know? Things just  pile  up. Is that the electricity bill? It looks awfully high. It is. And there's a final demand for something from British Gas. We  need  to sort this, honestly. I’m happy to call them, but are you sure you’ve not missed anything? I thought I’d paid it. Honestly, I do try. It’s all these direct debits, confusing the life out of me. Speaking of confusing, have you seen that Kelly Brook is back in… well, back  doing  something? Saw a picture online. Still looks good, doesn't she? Dad! We’re trying to prevent a power cut, and you're discussing celebrity gossip. Focus. Though, yeah, she… looks alright. Bit of a throwback, isn’t it? A classic! Anyway, are you sure this pile doesn’t have any important documents in it? Like… the house deeds or something? Your mum always kept those locked away. I’ve already checked for those, they're in the safe. This is mostly… junk mail. Oh, and a lot of bank statements. Why do we have  so  many bank statements? It’s like a paper archive. Well, they used to send them. Before everything went digital. Honestly, these banks, always changing things. Keeps a man on his toes. You’re good with computers, aren't you? Maybe you could scan all these onto a USB stick? Save some space. I could. It'd take hours, though. I mean, I'm currently working on a corpus linguistics project – analyzing spoken language – and even  that  feels less tedious than this. It’s fascinating stuff, actually. Trying to map how people use certain phrases… That… sounds complicated. Like a fancy way of saying you listen to people chat? I mostly just try to understand what people  want  when they call up about their broadband. That’s enough linguistics for me. It's a bit more than that, but yeah, close. Okay, there's a statement dated… July? And another from August. Right, looks like you were paying around £150 a month for… flights? Did you book a holiday, Dad?

Honestly, that was a dreadful petrol station. Dreadful. Didn’t even have windscreen wash. Really? I didn't even notice, I was just focused on not reversing into that ridiculously small island. Felt like I was parallel parking a boat. Aye, well, it was grim. And the prices! Highway robbery, it was. I swear they add an extra ten pence just  because  it’s on the A1. They probably do. It's a captive audience, isn’t it? You’re committed once you’re turning off. Did you get diesel? Aye, got diesel. Filled her right up. You were looking low earlier. I’m good for another fifty miles, I reckon. Though I might top up before we hit Leeds, just in case. It’s always a nightmare finding a decent one around there. They’re either all queues or completely rammed with trucks. Oh God, the trucks. You get one of them trying to manoeuvre and it’s just… chaos. I saw a biker almost get taken out by one near Scotch Corner last week. Seriously? Reckless driving, most likely. You see so many bikers taking risks. They think they’re invincible. Well, some of them do. That one was just… he was practically leaning on the truck’s tyre, trying to get past. I thought he was mad. Mad is an understatement. They’ve got no protection, really. Just leathers and a helmet. It’s a brave life. Do you think they even  see  us in cars? Sometimes I swear they just appear out of nowhere. They do. They just… filter. It’s what they do, isn’t it? And sometimes they do it a bit close for comfort. I remember learning to drive, me dad was terrified of bikes. He'd always say, "They’re not there one minute, then they’re right on your bumper the next!" My dad was similar. He always said you should assume they're going to do something unpredictable. It’s good advice, actually, for all road users. I’ve started checking my blind spot religiously now, ever since that near miss with a cyclist in Cambridge. Good thinking. This traffic's building up now, isn't it? Should’ve left earlier. We did pretty well, considering. It’s Friday evening, everyone’s heading home or going somewhere for the weekend. Plus there's that roadworks further up. Aye, that’ll slow us right down.

Right, so have you booked your tennis coaching session for next week, Leo? Don’t forget, Mr. Davies is really good, but he fills up quickly. Uh-huh. Yeah, Tuesday’s sorted. 4:30. Good, good. Tuesday works well. Are you still aiming to improve your serve, or are you focusing on something else this month? Serve’s still rubbish. Honestly, I feel like I’m just chucking the ball up and hoping for the best. Well, that’s why you’re having coaching! Mr. Davies really breaks it down though, doesn't he? Remembers when he helped me with my forehand, years ago… made such a difference. Though, admittedly, I haven’t picked up a racket since. You should, love. It’s good exercise. And you were quite the player back in the day. Remember that club tournament you won? Oh, don’t exaggerate! It was a small village tournament, and half the players had probably forgotten their rackets. But yes, I did enjoy it. It's just finding the time, isn’t it? It’s so frustrating though. I watch Alcaraz and Djokovic, and they make it look  easy . Like, the power and spin they get… it's insane. They are exceptional, of course. But they’ve been working at it since they were tiny. Alcaraz, I read, barely did anything  but  tennis as a kid. It’s a dedication you rarely see. It's not just dedication. It’s natural talent too, isn’t it? Though, Djokovic’s work ethic is legendary. He’s completely changed the game, really. The physicality he brings… and that return of serve! Yeah, his return is mental. I tried to copy it once, ended up hitting the ball into the net every time. It takes years of practice, Leo. Don’t get discouraged. Focus on the basics. Mr Davies will have you sorted. Have you seen Sinner play recently? Oh, Sinner’s brilliant, isn’t he? Such a smooth player. And so calm under pressure. Reminds me a little of Federer, actually, the way he moves. Federer’s the best, though. Don't even argue. The elegance… he made it look like art. He  was  incredible. A true genius. But Djokovic has the stats, doesn’t he? The sheer number of Grand Slams… It’s a different era. They all play a very different game. It’s hard to compare across generations. What about you, Leo, who’s your favourite player right now?

Honestly, these napkins… they look like someone’s already… used them. And then folded them. Oh, don’t be daft, Liam. They’re just floral. A bit…busy, maybe. But perfectly clean. They  do  have a strange shape, though. A bit…brief-like, don't you think? Right, we’re not going there. Focus on the turkey, it’s looking good, Mum. How long was that in for? Four hours, love. And it’s perfect. Just like your Grandad used to make it. Remember how we always had Christmas dinner at 1pm sharp? No matter what. I remember having to wear a shirt and tie even if I didn't want to! Well, it was special! And afterwards, we’d always watch the Queen’s Speech. Though I swear she says the same thing every year. It’s a tradition, isn’t it? It’s weird to think this is probably the last one with… well, with things being different now. Don’t be morbid, Sarah. Let’s enjoy the day. Speaking of traditions, anyone done any proper Christmas shopping yet? I still need to get something for Uncle Barry. He’s impossible to buy for. He always says he doesn't want anything. Then he complains if he doesn’t  get  anything. Men! I'm gonna go and listen to some tunes. Has anyone heard the new Wham! song? It's banging. It's alright. Bit nostalgic, isn't it? Reminds me of when you and Josh used to call each other ‘George Michael’ and ‘Andrew Ridgeley’ back in year seven. Don’t remind me. That was mortifying. Josh still brings it up. You two were always a pair. Remember that dance routine you tried to learn for the school disco? The one that involved a lot of… enthusiastic flailing? Oh, I remember! It was… memorable. Although, 'dance routine' is perhaps a generous description. My Doris and I used to love those old musicals. Though I never could pick up the steps. Doris was a natural dancer; she could have been in a show, she really could. Speaking of musicals, the music in  Wonka  was really good. It reminded me of some of the songs from those old films. Good soundtrack, yeah. I've been listening to a lot of soundtracks lately. Helps me focus when I’m working. Dad, you never tell us what you  actually  do at work.

Honestly, this shepherd’s pie is amazing, Mum. You’ve outdone yourself. Oh, you’re sweet, love. It’s just a bit of mince and mash, isn’t it? Though I did use a proper stock cube this time. Makes all the difference, apparently. A proper stock cube, eh? Sounds scandalous! Back in my day, it was all bones and water. Built character, it did. Character and probably a lot of grit. So, Dad, how’s the farm doing? Still battling the weather? You wouldn’t believe it. Torrential rain all week. The barley’s looking a bit waterlogged, but the sheep are thriving, thankfully. They’re not fussy. As long as they’ve got grass and a dry patch to lie on, they’re happy. It’s the price of lamb that’s the worry now, though. Keeps going down. Oh dear. It’s just the way things are going, isn’t it? Everything’s getting more expensive, except for what you  sell . I was talking to Brenda at school today, she’s complaining about the energy bills again. Says they’re threatening to close the greenhouse. That’s awful! Is there nothing they can do? Maybe a fundraiser or something? She’s looked into it. Apparently, there are grants, but the paperwork is a nightmare. She's got enough on her plate with the exams coming up. Exams… Ugh. That sounds stressful. How are you coping, Mum? You always seem so calm amidst the chaos. It’s… busy. The kids are all under pressure. And honestly, dealing with some of the parents is a full-time job in itself. This one mother, she's convinced her son’s predicted grade is deliberately low because the teacher doesn’t like him. Sounds like a right drama queen. People put too much pressure on these kids. Used to be, you passed or you failed. Simple. It’s different now, isn’t it? Everything’s so competitive. It’s exhausting just  thinking  about it. Speaking of exhausting, how’s the hunt for a flat going? Have you found anything remotely affordable in London yet? Don’t even ask. It’s… grim. Everything’s either a shoebox or costs the earth. I saw one yesterday, supposedly ‘cosy’, it was literally under a railway arch! London! What did you expect? It's a rip-off. You’re better off staying here. Plenty of space, fresh air.

Right, onions are softening nicely. You’re sure you don’t want mushrooms in this pasta sauce? I’ve got a lovely punnet. No, honestly, I’m good. Mushrooms… they’re just… textural issues. How was your appraisal today? Did the Big Boss finally acknowledge your existence? A little bit. She said… and I quote… “Your accuracy is consistently high, which is valuable.” Valuable! Like I’m a slightly chipped antique. No raise, naturally. Ugh. The usual. They’re all the same, aren’t they? Telling you how valuable you are while simultaneously underpaying you. Did you at least threaten to unleash a transcription rebellion? I considered it. Briefly. Mostly I just nodded and smiled politely. Thinking about ordering a pizza actually. I’m too tired to properly cook. Good shout. Have you seen the new Marks and Spencer food adverts? They're doing those posh pizzas now, the ones with the fig and balsamic glaze. Ooh, tempting! We could get one of those. Though I’m still slightly scarred by that smoked salmon and horseradish pizza we tried last year. Such a disaster. Okay, fair point. Perhaps we’ll stick to something a little… less adventurous. Speaking of Marks and Spencer, I need new trousers. All mine seem to have mysteriously shrunk in the wash. They don’t shrink, darling, you’ve just…expanded slightly. Very funny. I saw something on Facebook about the appalling conditions some horses are kept in. Absolutely dreadful. Makes my blood boil. It’s heartbreaking, isn’t it? That’s why I donate to the World Horse Welfare. Just a little each month, but it feels like something. Did you finish that crossword? The one from Saturday? I got most of it. Stuck on 17 across – ‘a small island chain’. Any ideas? Hmm… The Faroes? Yes! Of course! You’re amazing. I’ve got a bottle of wine in the cupboard, a Rioja, but I think it's… seventeen years old? Or maybe fourteen. It’s been lurking there a while. Fourteen-year-old wine. Bold. Are we sure it’s still drinkable? We might need the blender to turn it into something resembling sangria. Actually, the blender's making a funny noise. I think it's finally giving up the ghost. Another thing to add to the list of things to replace. You know what I’ve been watching?  Trapped . That Icelandic detective series.

Right, honestly, I've been staring at my wardrobe for half an hour. I have  nothing  to wear. Absolutely nothing. You always say that, love! What's the occasion anyway? Is it just a general getting-glammed-up-for-a-night-out situation, or is there a specific…vibe? Just a night out, yeah. Sarah’s birthday, at that new place downtown. I was thinking something…sparkly? But not  too  sparkly, you know? I don’t want to look like a Christmas tree. Ooh, sparkly! I’m feeling a black dress, classic. Though, knowing us, we’ll end up in trainers by the end of the night. Heels are just… cruel. Preach! I wore heels last week and genuinely thought I was going to faceplant into someone’s chips. I just can't do it anymore. They're instruments of torture. You lot are weaklings! I’m a heel pro. Though, I  do  pack a pair of flats in my bag, just in case. Smart move, really. You're showing off now, Chloe. What are  you  wearing then? Bet you’ve already got an outfit planned, you organised soul. Guilty as charged. Burgundy bodycon, with black heels. Simple, effective. And, importantly, comfortable enough to dance in… for a bit, anyway. Oh, nice! I was thinking about a jumpsuit. I got a really cute navy one in the sales last week, but I keep worrying it makes my legs look a bit…stumpy. Stumpy? No way! You’ve got great legs, Liv. Jumpsuits look amazing on you. You just need to find the right shoes - wedges might balance it out. Speaking of shoes, anyone else spend three hours scrolling through ASOS last night and end up buying nothing? It’s a talent, honestly. Oh my god, that's literally me. I added like, twelve pairs of boots to my basket and then panicked about the returns process. It's too much effort. It is! Honestly, shopping online is a nightmare. I much prefer actually  being  in a shop, trying things on. Although, then you have to deal with the changing room lighting... always terrible. Don’t even get me started on changing room lighting. It's designed to make you feel awful about yourself. Plus, you’re always battling for a mirror. This is why I just order everything in three different sizes and return what doesn't fit. It’s easier, even if it’s slightly wasteful.

Honestly, the way Mark just  dominates  every conversation… it’s exhausting. You’d think, after twenty years, he’d learn to let someone else get a word in edgewise. He’s always been like that, hasn’t he? The ‘expert’ on everything. It's a confidence thing, I think. Deep down, he's probably terrified of being seen as… ordinary. Terrified of being ordinary? He runs a plumbing business! There’s nothing ordinary about fixing burst pipes in January! It’s just… a need to always be right. It’s draining. It is. Remember that time we went to that historical reenactment in Warwick? The Victorian one? He spent the  entire  day correcting the actors on the accuracy of their accents. Oh god, yes! And the poor woman playing the scullery maid, she looked genuinely tearful. He was going on about the regional variations in dialect! Like she wasn’t already dressed in layers and pretending to scrub floors! He’s got a genuine fascination with detail, though. That’s part of what makes him… him. It’s just not always appropriate. It’s like he’s on a constant spiritual journey to discover the perfect historical fact. A spiritual journey? You're being generous. I think he just wants to prove he’s smarter than everyone else. It makes me wonder about soul mates, actually. Do you think they’re real? Or just a really good marketing ploy by the romance industry? I don't know. I used to be very cynical about it all. Then I met you. Oh, you smooth talker. No, honestly. It's not about finding someone perfect, because nobody is. It’s about finding someone who understands your… quirks. Who doesn’t mind when you spend three hours researching the best type of teacup. Guilty. And who puts up with you endlessly tinkering with the home network, convinced you’re preventing a cyberattack? Precisely. Speaking of which, I  am  thinking of setting up a separate network just for the smart speakers. They're a security nightmare. Oh, here we go. Can we  please  not talk about IT first thing on a Saturday? I was hoping we could at least pretend it’s a day off. Sorry. Force of habit. I was just thinking… If we could throw a party, but invite people from different periods in history, who would be on the guest list? Oh!

Honestly, the amount of paperwork for that little craft stall is ridiculous. You wouldn’t believe. It's like running a FTSE 100 company, the hoops you have to jump through just to sell a knitted penguin. A knitted penguin? Seriously? That sounds… adorable, actually. But yeah, I get the paperwork thing. Even applying for a blue badge was a nightmare. Mountains of forms. Penguins, eh? You’re branching out from the scarves then, Carol? Last time I saw you, it was a rainbow of woolly neckwear. Scarves are steady trade, don't get me wrong. But penguins are  selling . Apparently, everyone needs a knitted penguin. I'm thinking of expanding, maybe little knitted corgis. Though I’m worried about getting the ears right. Corgis are a good shout. Everyone loves a corgi. Especially since… well, you know. Don’t remind me. It's just…it feels a bit insensitive to capitalise on royal sadness, even with knitted dogs. Still, bills need paying. You’re overthinking it, love. People want a little bit of comfort, a little bit of joy. A knitted corgi isn’t glorifying anything. It’s…craft. Pure and simple. Maybe you’re right. Though I did have old Mrs. Higgins giving me the side-eye at the church fete. Said it was ‘disrespectful’. Honestly, some people. Oh, bless. Mrs. Higgins is always finding something to disapprove of. Remember when she complained about my bright pink hair? Said it ‘wasn’t becoming of a young lady’. That was hilarious! You handled her beautifully, love. Just said, “It matches my personality!” Had to! Honestly, the things people comment on. It’s always something. Makes you wonder if they’ve got nothing better to think about. Speaking of better things to think about, how’s work? Still battling the endless reports? Oh, don’t even  start  me on the reports. Brenda called in sick again. Apparently, a bad curry. That’s the third time this month. I’m starting to suspect she just really likes a good takeaway. I swear, half my job is covering for Brenda. Brenda. Always a drama. I’ve got a staff member off on ‘stress leave’. Apparently his goldfish died. A  goldfish ! I had to approve it. HR are going mad for authorisation. A goldfish?! Oh, that's… something. You’d think they’d just get another one, wouldn’t you? It’s not like it’s a beloved family pet.

Honestly, I’m starting to think living with Liam is a mistake. A massive, student loan-funded mistake. Woah, what happened? Last I heard you were bonding over obscure FIFA teams. That  was  last week, before he decided his bedroom was a biohazard zone. Like, genuinely, I can smell it from the hallway. And he’s just… leaving plates everywhere. Dirty plates, Jamal! Oh god, don’t even get me started on flatmate hygiene. Chloe in my halls uses the communal kitchen as a personal dumping ground. I swear I saw a science experiment growing in her sink yesterday. Sounds… delightful? But seriously, Liam? You’ve known him ages, I thought you'd be able to handle a bit of mess. It’s not just the mess! He keeps ‘borrowing’ my oat milk. Like, subtle sips, then suddenly half the carton’s gone. And then he has the cheek to ask if  I’ve  been using his shower gel! That's next level. The oat milk is a crime against humanity, though. It's expensive! Did you ask him about it? I tried! He just gave me this puppy-dog look and said he was ‘really craving a creamy coffee’. A creamy coffee funded by  my  student loan! Oh, Liam. He's a professional user of puppy-dog eyes. Remember that time he convinced Mrs. Henderson to extend the deadline for his essay? Oh,  that  was legendary. He told her his nan was ill, which, in his defence, she was, but he’d already finished the essay and was just trying to get a weekend free for a football match. Don’t remind me. He’s going on about the derby this weekend, needing ‘tactical support’. Which means he wants me to make him snacks whilst he yells at the TV. Speaking of the derby, I’m going with Ben and Aisha. Want to come? It’ll be a good distraction from the oat milk bandit. Hmm… tempting. Although, I'm supposed to be doing that reading for Dr. Davies’ lecture. It’s on tax law, and honestly, my brain is already glazing over thinking about it. Tax law? Ugh, that sounds… thrilling. I’ve got to start looking into student council elections. Sophie's trying to get me to run for treasurer. She says I’m “good with numbers,” which is a polite way of saying I’m obsessively good at budgeting because I'm perpetually broke.

This seafood risotto is  amazing . Honestly, the best thing I’ve eaten all week. Glad you like it, love. Croatia does seafood so well, doesn’t it? Much better than anything you get back home, even at that fancy Italian place you like. It’s alright. I just wish they did chips. All this…fishy stuff. You and your chips, lad. You’ll broaden your horizons eventually. Try a bit of this, it’s actually quite mild. Dad, don’t pressure him. It's a holiday, let him eat what he wants. Anyway, I was telling Mum about university applications. I've narrowed it down to Manchester and Leeds. Manchester, eh? That's not far. Good for getting home easily. What are you thinking of studying? Still psychology? Yeah, still psychology. Leeds has a really strong course on forensic psychology, which I’m really interested in, but Manchester is closer to… well, everything. And I know more people there. Can I go to Manchester with you when you go to uni? Not for a good few years yet, little brother! You’ve still got school to worry about. How’s year seven treating you? It’s okay. There’s this lad, Liam, he’s got a tattoo… on his ARM! Year seven and tattoos? Honestly. They’re getting younger and younger. I saw a girl, probably fourteen, with a full sleeve the other day. It's the times we live in, I suppose. Though I still think it's a bit rash for anyone, let alone a teenager. Speaking of rash decisions - remember young Daniel getting on that moped in Corfu? Nearly gave your mother a heart attack. Don’t remind me! He was speeding around like a maniac. Honestly, I thought he was going to end up in the hospital. Which brings me to my day - absolute chaos. Little old Mrs. Higgins went into labour two hours early. Had to practically sprint to her house. Wow, sounds stressful! It is, but rewarding. It’s just… the paperwork afterwards. Mountains of it. And then trying to explain to young patients the importance of iron levels and healthy eating – it’s like talking to a brick wall sometimes. They’d rather be on Facebook, scrolling through influencers than listening to me. Sounds familiar. Trying to explain market analysis to clients can be equally frustrating. They all think they know best, until the numbers tell a different story.

Right then, cups of tea all round, I think. Good to be back in a proper chair, eh? That YHA bunk was…functional. Functional is a kind word, Arthur. It was a bit like sleeping in a tin box. But honestly, Cornwall was lovely. Thanks for suggesting it, dear. And David, good of you to come collect us, wasn't it? Saved us wrestling with the suitcases on the train. No problem at all. Glad you both had a good time. Though, judging by the faces, the journey back wasn’t entirely smooth sailing? Smooth sailing? Ha! Tried to tell her about that cycle race. “Yorkshire in a Day” they called it. Absolute madness. All those lycra-clad lunatics going up hills. Nearly got run off the road twice. Arthur only wanted to point out a particularly steep incline. He’s been on about hills ever since we visited that lighthouse. Stunning, wasn't it? Lizard Point. Though good heavens, the wind! Thought my hair would blow right off. Lizard Point, brilliant. I’ve always wanted to go. Did you get any good photos? I’m attempting a presentation on coastal landscapes for the school, and decent visuals are proving elusive. Got plenty. Mostly of Maureen trying to stand upright in a gale. She looked like a scarecrow. And a surprisingly large number of crabs. Little blighters were everywhere. Tried to steal my pasty, one did. He’s exaggerating slightly. It  looked  at the pasty. Anyway, I have loads of photos too, David. Let me get my phone. Oh, and some of that YHA. It wasn’t  all  bad. The views were spectacular. Though I did spend a good hour trying to work out how to share a bathroom with fourteen teenagers. Sounds…challenging. You two volunteering was a good idea though, providing a bit of support for the YHA. I admire that. It’s good to give back. Give back? Foot ache is what I gave back! That coastal path… endless steps. Didn’t realise I was still capable of walking that far. Arthur’s legs haven’t been the same since he fell off his bicycle trying to impress young Emily with a wheelie. Remember that, David? Vaguely. Emily was probably more impressed by his bravery than his skill. So, the volunteering… was it something you’d consider doing again? Maybe not Cornwall, with all those hills. Hmm. Perhaps.

Right, this lasagne is proper good, Liam. You’ve outdone yourself. Honestly, better than your mum’s – don’t tell her I said that! She wouldn’t believe you anyway, Jess. She’s convinced she’s the best cook in Cambridgeshire. No, seriously though, glad you like it. It’s a recipe I found online, actually. Bit of a cheat, I know. It  is  delicious. And you’re a liar, Jess, your mum makes a cracking roast. Though, to be fair, Liam's lasagne is… different. In a good way! So, how was work today, Jess? Still battling event planners who think a spreadsheet is a suggestion? You have  no  idea, Chloe. Honestly, it's relentless. I had one woman today who wanted to have a fireworks display  inside  the conference centre. Inside! I had to explain gently, and repeatedly, that’s a health and safety nightmare. Blimey. People are mental. I just spent the day shifting pallets of bricks. Brain-deadening, but at least it’s straightforward. No one’s asking me to defy the laws of physics. See, Liam? Simple life. Though my day wasn’t much better. We had a major glitch in production - a whole batch of components were the wrong spec. Spent six hours on the phone with suppliers. It’s exhausting when things just… go wrong. Ugh, that sounds awful. Stressful! Speaking of stressful… how’s things with Jamie going, Chloe? You’ve been a bit quiet about it lately. It’s… complicated. Honestly, I don’t even know what’s happening anymore. We had another row last night. About him spending too much time with his mates, again. He says I’m being clingy, I say he’s avoiding actually  being  with me. Sounds rough. It always feels like one of you is picking a fight, doesn't it? Exactly! It’s like we're stuck in this cycle. And I’m starting to wonder if it's even worth the effort anymore. It's just… draining. Oh, Chloe, I’m so sorry. You deserve someone who makes you feel good, not someone you’re constantly battling with. Maybe you need to have a proper, sit-down conversation and really lay out how you're feeling. And be prepared to walk away if he doesn't listen. Yeah, Jess is right. You can’t keep putting up with that. It's a waste of your time and energy.

Honestly, Barcelona was  amazing . You would absolutely love it. Did you have a good weekend? Anything exciting happen? Oh my god, tell me everything! It sounds incredible. My weekend was…beige. Mum and Dad came down, which was nice, but mostly just a lot of Sunday roast and them asking about my work. Standard. Barcelona sounds like a serious upgrade. Beige is a good word for it, haha. It was just…vibrant. The architecture, the food, the people! We did that Gaudi tour, and I’m officially obsessed. It’s so different to everything back home. Did you manage to watch any of  Severance  while I was gone? I know you were keen to start it. I did! I binged the first three episodes. It’s so weird, but I’m hooked. That ending of episode three…! It’s properly unsettling. I was trying to explain the premise to Mum, and she just looked utterly bewildered. Mum would. She just doesn't  get  sci-fi, does she? Speaking of bewildered, trying to navigate the metro in Barcelona was a whole thing. I ended up just walking everywhere, even when it was miles. My feet are killing me. Oh no! That’s dedication. And probably blisters. I’m glad you had such a good time though. Were you with Ben? Did he enjoy it too? Yeah, Ben came with me. He loved it, obviously. He spent most of the time trying to perfect his Spanish, which involved a lot of ordering things he didn’t understand. He accidentally ordered a whole plate of snails.  What?!  No way! Ben and snails do not sound like a good combination. Did he eat them? He tried! One. His face was…a picture. We were both crying with laughter. It's definitely a story for the family Christmas. Anyway, enough about snails. We were talking about your weekend. Any gossip? Anyone catch your eye visiting? No one exciting. Just Mum subtly trying to set me up with the son of a family friend. Apparently, he's a "lovely young man" who works in finance. I just nodded politely and changed the subject. Honestly, I'm not even looking right now. Good! You definitely don't need pressure. It's good to focus on you. Have you started thinking about what you’re doing with your annual leave next year? I'm toying with the idea of Paris.

Honestly, this coffee is  exactly  what I needed. That drive along the coast was… invigorating, let’s say. A bit hairy in places! Hairy is a good word for it. Those little roads are… enthusiastic. But worth it for a view like this, eh? And a proper coffee, seems Cyprus does coffee well. Better than back home, I’d wager. Oh, miles better. Back home, it’s all chains and lukewarm disappointments. What about you? What brings you to North Cyprus? Holiday, or are you working out here? Bit of both, actually. I’m trying to launch a small consultancy, helping businesses with digital marketing. Remote work, mostly, but I figured a month here would be a good way to unplug  and  scout out potential clients. Bit of a ‘workation’, you could say. What about you? Teaching still? Still at it, yes. Secondary school English. Twenty years now, can you believe it? Sometimes I feel like I’m teaching the grandchildren of students I had at the beginning. It has its moments, but… it’s a job. Twenty years! That’s dedication. I bounced around a bit more. Tried my hand at a few things before landing on digital marketing. Spent a year selling timeshares in Florida – don’t even ask. Nearly lost my soul. Timeshares in Florida. Goodness me. That sounds… intense. I can imagine. I did a summer waitressing job in Bournemouth when I was a student. Dealing with stag parties and sunburned tourists was enough to put me off hospitality for life. Oh, Bournemouth. A classic. Florida was a whole different level of relentless. Everyone’s on vacation, everyone’s desperate to ‘get a good deal’… and you’re the one they take it out on. After that, I vowed to be my own boss, even if it meant eating ramen for a year. Wise move. Though ramen does have its appeal sometimes. Particularly after marking 150 essays. It's surprisingly comforting. I flirted with being a journalist for a bit, did some freelance work after my Master’s. But quickly realised I preferred the structure of teaching. And the holidays. Holidays are good. Though being self-employed, 'holidays' have a rather fluid definition. More like ‘periods of slightly less frantic work’. Speaking of which, I'm trying to connect with some of the smaller hotels here to offer my services. They’re lagging behind on online presence, you know?

Right, so are we still on for going round to Liam’s tonight then? Just to, like, actually  talk  to him about the dishes? Yeah, definitely. It’s getting ridiculous, innit? A mountain of plates builds up every single time. He says he’ll do them, then… nothing. I know! He’s a lovely lad, truly, but the washing up… it’s a consistent problem. Do you reckon he just genuinely forgets? Or is he hoping we’ll just do ‘em for him? I think it’s a bit of both, to be honest. He gets distracted so easily, starts a game or puts telly on. And definitely a bit of expecting us to pick up the slack. He’s used to his mam doing everything for him, I reckon. That’s what I thought. It’s just… frustrating. I feel like a nag when I mention it, but it’s not fair on us, is it? Especially Sarah, she’s proper meticulous. No, it’s not. Sarah's got a point to be fair. She's always scrubbing the hob as well, even when it's only been a little bit splashed. I swear she’s got a secret cleaning obsession. She’s just… tidy. Proper tidy. Which is good, keeps the flat decent. But Liam just seems to exist in a chaotic orbit around her cleaning, leaving a trail of crumbs in his wake. That’s a good way of putting it. Chaotic orbit. It's like the planets are aligning for a clash, honestly. And if Sarah starts getting proper annoyed… well, that won’t be pretty. Exactly! That’s why we need to nip it in the bud. We need to have a proper ‘house meeting’ or something. Like, set some ground rules. Maybe a washing-up rota? A rota sounds… intense. Do you think Liam would actually stick to it? He’d probably just swap his day with someone else every week. Good point. Maybe not a rigid rota. Just a general agreement that everyone contributes. And that leaving a week's worth of plates isn't acceptable. Right, yeah. More of a… gentle persuasion. We need to word it carefully. We don't want to fall out with him over dirty dishes, do we? No, definitely not. He's a good friend, just… needs a little encouragement. Plus, I'm starting to think he’s deliberately leaving food stains on the microwave to test Sarah’s limits.

Right then, that’s the shopping done. Bit of a queue at the checkout, wasn't there? Old Mrs. Higgins was holding everyone up again, fumbling for her loyalty card. Oh, you and Mrs. Higgins. Honestly, Arthur, you complain about her every week! She’s a sweet old thing, just a bit…slow. I managed to grab us a nice piece of salmon, though. Thought we could have that for supper. Salmon’s good. Though I could’ve sworn Brenda was selling better cod down at the market today. Might have to pop back tomorrow, see if she’s got any left. Tomorrow? Oh, now don’t go getting ideas. Your knees weren't looking too happy carrying those bags in just now. You need to rest, Arthur. Honestly, you'd think you were still working down the docks the way you push yourself. Docks were good for me, kept me fit as a fiddle. This sitting about is what ages a man, I tell you. Nothing for the body to  do . Still, glad I remembered the newspaper. Let’s see what the world's gotten up to while we were out. Oh, don't start on the news. It’s always dreadful. Nothing but bad news these days. I’d rather look at the garden. The roses are starting to bud, you know. Roses are alright. Always preferred a good sunflower myself. Bright and cheerful, like a little bit of sunshine. Speaking of sunshine, it's gotten a bit chilly, hasn't it? I’ll put the kettle on, how about a cuppa? Oh, that would be lovely, Arthur. Thank you. And perhaps a biscuit? I saw those nice ginger snaps in the biscuit tin earlier. Ginger snaps it is. You spoil me, you do. Though I suppose someone has to, after all these years. Nonsense. You spoil  me , with your stories and your fussing. Now, go on, put that kettle on before my fingers turn blue. And don't you be offering to go back to the market tomorrow, mind! I hope this matches your specifications! Let me know if you would like any changes or additions. Right, kettle’s on. Did you see young Timmy next door got a new bicycle? Bright red thing, with streamers. Oh, yes, I did. Lovely boy, Timmy. His mother works so hard, she deserves to see him happy. It reminds me of when our David got his first bike…

Right then, love, have you seen if Grandad’s managed to wrestle the telly remote off your Nana? She was threatening to hide it in the biscuit tin earlier. Probably. He was muttering something about watching the snooker. Honestly, they’re worse than kids sometimes. I tried to explain the football highlights to Nana, and she kept asking if I’d cleaned my room. I can hear you two! And your room  is  a tip, young man! Honestly, it looks like a bomb’s hit it. There she goes. See? It never ends. Did you get the spare room aired, dear? They'll be wanting a sit down and a cuppa soon. Yeah, window's open. Smells a bit of polish now, but better than dusty. I put fresh towels out too. Grandad keeps saying he prefers a flannel though. A flannel is far superior, lad. You get a proper scrub with a flannel. These towels are just for drying, aren’t they? No substance to ‘em. Oh, hello you two! You’re looking well. Come and sit down, I’ve just made a pot of tea and there’s some of that shortbread your Nana likes. Oh, shortbread, lovely! Now, don't be thinking you've skimped on the butter, Ethel. It wouldn't be shortbread if it weren’t swimming in butter. Never. I use proper butter, you know me. Though your Grandad tried to convince me margarine was just as good last week. Absolute nonsense. It’s not nonsense! It's economic! Times are hard, you know. Though I suppose when you're marking GCSE papers all day, you don’t notice the cost of things… Now, now, George. I’m just trying to keep everyone happy. And besides, marking papers doesn't pay  that  well. Honestly, some of the answers the kids come up with... you wouldn’t believe it. You telling us about the time someone thought pi was 3.14… and then drew a picture of a pie? Oh, that was a classic, wasn't it? Though there was another one recently who tried to solve an equation using only colours. Green plus blue equals purple, apparently. Oh my! They don’t teach ‘em anything properly these days, do they? Back in my day… well, never mind. What’s our young scholar been up to? Any exams looming? Got History mock next week. I'm dreading it.

Honestly, this wait is ridiculous. I’ve been scrolling through TikTok for a solid twenty minutes now. Brain is turning to mush. Tell me about it. I thought we booked for, like, ten? It’s past that now, innit? Should’ve just stayed in bed, really. You say that now, but you were the one stressing about getting this sorted. You’ve been going on about needing a new… what was it? A massager? It’s a  percussive therapy device , alright? And my back's killing me from all that moving last week. It’s an investment in my wellbeing! Percussive therapy device? Sounds expensive. Is it one of those fancy ones that connects to your phone? Nah, not  that  fancy. Just a solid, reliable bit of vibrating goodness. Found one on Amazon with good reviews. Apparently, it’s like having a personal masseuse. Doubt that’s true. Nothing beats a real person digging into those knots, you know? Though I could probably do with something, my shoulders are wrecked after staring at a screen all day writing my dissertation. Speaking of screens… anyone seen that new Netflix show, ‘Echoes’? It’s proper messed up. Twin sisters swapping lives… it’s a bit of a rollercoaster. Oh, yeah! My flatmate’s obsessed. Keeps trying to explain the plot to me, but it just sounds… complicated. I’m more a ‘cozy crime’ kinda guy. Give me a good Agatha Christie any day. Cozy crime is good. Although, I’ve been sucked into those true crime documentaries on YouTube. They’re horrifying but addictive. Don’t start me on YouTube rabbit holes. I spent three hours last night watching videos about restoring vintage trainers.  Vintage trainers ! What’s happened to my life? University is doing things to us all, mate. Destroying our free time and replacing it with… niche hobbies. It’s the pressure, innit? Everyone’s hustling, trying to side-gig, build a personal brand… It’s exhausting. My mum keeps telling me I need to ‘find a sensible job’. Mine’s the same. Keeps sending me links to civil service graduate schemes. Like, thanks, Mum, but I’m trying to, you know,  live . My dad just doesn’t get it. He thinks I should’ve gone straight into carpentry after college. ‘Good honest work,’ he says. Parents just want what they think is best, I guess. It’s just… what  we  think is best is different.

Right, shopping list. Mum, you’re better at remembering stuff than me. What milk do we need? Semi-skimmed, yeah? Aye, semi-skimmed. And get some of them nice yogurts for Leo, the ones with the fruit at the bottom. He’ll only eat those. The raspberry ones! Can we get the raspberry ones? Please? Raspberry it is. And bread. We’re completely out of bread. Granary, right? Granary’s good. Actually, before we get too far down the list… anyone else got bitten by something last night? My ankle is  killing  me. Oh, you poor thing! Probably a mosquito. We had one buzzing around in here last night. I swatted it, but I think it got you first. Swatted it, did you? Good work. It felt like a tiny dart went in. I’ve put some anti-histamine cream on it, but it just…itches. My nan says putting vinegar on it helps. Vinegar?! Leo, don’t you dare start rubbing vinegar on your dad's ankle! That’ll just make it worse. She’s right about the cooling effect, actually. A bit of witch hazel can do wonders, too. I’ve got some in the bathroom. Honestly, though, sometimes you just have to ride it out. Riding it out sounds…unpleasant. Alright, witch hazel it is. Thanks, love. Okay, back to the shopping. Do we need washing powder? Nearly. We’ve got enough for one more wash, max. And loo roll, definitely loo roll. Liam used the last of it this morning. It was an emergency! I needed it! An emergency? What kind of emergency requires an entire roll of loo roll, young man? A really important one. Never mind that. Mum, did you see that Bolton Wanderers finally won a game? Did they?! About time! I heard a bit on the radio. Was it a good match? Apparently. They were two nil down at half-time, but then they came back and won 3-2. Proper nail-biter. Good for them. They’ve had a rough season, haven’t they? Always good to see a comeback. Actually, talking of comebacks…that ankle is still itching. Can we talk about football now? Not itchy ankles. Yeah, let's talk football. Leo, who’s your favourite player at the moment? Erling Haaland! He’s amazing. He scores loads of goals. A good choice. A very good choice. Right, shall we finish this list then?

Ugh, P.E. today was  brutal . Miss Harrison really made us run, like, a million laps. No way! Seriously? I managed to ‘forget’ my kit again. Mr. Davies just sighed and said I could help him with the equipment. Total win. You’re so good at that! I wish I could pull that off. I tried to say I had a headache, but she gave me ‘the look’. You know the one. The one that says ‘Don’t even  try  it.’ Oh god, yes. The ‘I’m not falling for that’ look. She’s got a whole arsenal of those. Did you at least do okay in Science? Kind of? We were doing dissections. Frogs. It was…squishy. And smelled really bad. Liam nearly threw up.  Ew . Dissections are the worst! We were looking at plant cells today. Way less gross, but still boring. Old Man Hemmings just drones on and on. Honestly, I think he’s trying to hypnotize us with PowerPoint. He totally is! I swear, he uses the same presentation slides every year. Has he not updated them since the 90s? Probably not. Have you seen what Sophie posted on Instagram? Her holiday photos are insane. Maldives, apparently. Oh my god, I know! It’s so unfair. My family’s idea of a holiday is a weekend in Skegness. Skegness is…a choice. I saw Ethan trying to slide into her DMs with something about ‘waves and sunshine’. So cringe.  Ugh , Ethan. He’s so desperate. He’s always trying to be all TikTok famous. Did you see him trying to recreate that dance trend in the canteen? Yes! And knocked over Mrs. Peterson’s tea. It was glorious chaos. Serves her right, she's always giving detentions for the smallest things. Speaking of which, did you hear about Maya getting a detention for having the wrong socks? What?! Seriously? Wrong  socks ? That’s ridiculous. What colour were they? Apparently, they weren't the official school black. They were…navy. The horror! Honestly, the school rules are so stupid sometimes. Have you been watching ‘Science Max’ on YouTube? He's amazing. He actually makes science interesting. Ooh, no! I'll have to check him out. I'm completely obsessed with ‘Kurzgesagt’ at the moment. Their animations are incredible. Yeah, they’re really good. My little brother keeps watching those videos about the universe and then asking me existential questions.

Honestly, I feel like death warmed up. My throat is absolutely killing me. Oh, no! That’s awful. Still? You said you were feeling a bit rough yesterday, but… Yesterday was optimistic. Yesterday was ‘slightly sniffly’. Today is ‘can barely swallow’ and ‘questioning all life choices’. I think it’s a proper cold, not just a tickle. Have you taken anything? Lemsip? Paracetamol? You need to get on top of it before it turns into something worse. Remember what happened to Auntie Brenda with that flu last winter? Spent a week in hospital. Don’t remind me! Brenda’s a drama queen, but hospital isn’t fun. I’ve been bunging the Lemsip down, but it’s not really doing much. It’s just…everything hurts. Ugh. It's the worst. Do you think it’s something you ate? You were saying that new Thai place looked a bit dodgy… Nah, I don’t think so. I felt fine straight after. It was probably just coinciding with someone at work bringing in a plague. Honestly, half the office sounds like they’re auditioning for a gravel commercial. It’s like a human petri dish in there. Still, if it gets any worse, you should probably see a doctor. Speaking of doctors, I had to have my flu jab this week. Honestly, the nurse was obsessed with Lloyd Grossman.  Lloyd Grossman?  What on earth are you talking about? I know, it was bizarre! She was describing his sauces as if they were some sort of medical breakthrough. “Oh, this one’s got a lovely hint of chilli, perfect for distracting from the pain!” And then she was quizzing me on which one was my favourite. It was… unsettling. That's…peak NHS weirdness. She sounds like she needs a holiday. Although, a tiny part of me is impressed she managed to shoehorn Lloyd Grossman into a vaccination appointment. I know, right? It's a skill. Anyway, you really need to look after yourself. I’m heading to the shops later, shall I grab you some throat lozenges and a ridiculously oversized scarf? Oh, you are a saint. Lozenges would be amazing. And if the scarf is fluffy, even better. I’m currently wrapped in a blanket like a human burrito. Consider it done. I was watching that show about body language recognition earlier, the one with that ex-FBI guy. It’s fascinating how much people reveal without even realising.

Right, my turn. Hmm… Let’s see. I’m going to put ‘quixotic’ down for a triple word score! Oh, you’re ruthless, aren’t you? Quixotic? Seriously? Where did you even  learn  that word? Probably from a book, dear. Unlike some people who spend their time scrolling through Facebook. It was in a particularly dense Victorian novel, actually. Keeps the brain cells ticking over. Goodness me. Victorian novels. I haven’t tackled one of those in… well, decades. Too much description, not enough action for my liking. Give me a good biography any day. Speaking of biographies, did you manage to get a look at that music magazine I picked up? The one with the interview with… what was his name… the drummer from The Shadows? Oh, I glanced at it. Seemed rather… reverent. These magazines always make these musicians sound like gods. They do, don’t they? It's all marketing. Remember when we were stuck in that gridlock at the Trafford Centre last week? Felt like an eternity. I swear, everyone in Greater Manchester was trying to buy Christmas presents at once. I’ve vowed never to go near a shopping centre in December again. Utter chaos. Honestly, give me a good butcher’s shop queue any day. At least you can chat to people. The butcher’s queue was a nightmare too! Took me twenty minutes just to get a decent piece of lamb. Everyone was talking about the weather, naturally. It  is  frightfully cold, isn't it? I’m thinking of making a big pot of stew. That’ll warm us all up. Perhaps with a dumpling topping? Ooh, stew sounds lovely. I’ve been experimenting with a new recipe – Moroccan tagine. It’s quite complex, lots of spices. Moroccan, you say? Sounds… adventurous. I stick to good, honest British cooking myself. Roast beef and Yorkshire puddings, that’s what I call a meal. Mum, did you manage to post those photos from the garden party onto Facebook? I know you were struggling with the app. Oh, that wretched Facebook! I eventually got a neighbour’s grandson to help me. It’s all so complicated. Why can't things just be simple? I'm still trying to understand why everyone posts pictures of their dinner. It’s a performance, Mum. Everyone wants to curate their perfect life online. Humph. A waste of time, if you ask me.

Honestly, all this fuss about the right kind of screw for the signal box… you’d think it was rocket science! It’s a railway, not a space shuttle. Ah, but you see, Penelope, it  is  a bit like rocket science, in a way. Everything has to be absolutely precise. A tiny error can have… cascading consequences. I learned that quickly enough in my own field. Your printing systems, was it? Always seemed a terribly complicated business to me. All those rollers and inks and… well, details. I stuck to paint and canvas, much simpler. Simpler perhaps in appearance, but no less demanding of precision, I imagine. And yes, the printing. Started small, you know, just after I finished my doctorate. A little invention to automate some tedious tasks. Then it just…grew. Grew into a very successful career, if I recall correctly. I remember reading something, years ago, about your company. International, wasn’t it? Oh, immensely. We ended up with offices all over. But the heart of it, for a long time, was Germany. We spent a great deal of time at the big printing exhibitions in Frankfurt and Düsseldorf. Quite the experience. Germany! I’ve never spent much time there. A bit too…efficient for my taste, perhaps. Though I did sell a rather beautiful landscape to a German collector once, through a gallery in Bath. Efficient, yes, but also incredibly thorough. And they appreciate good engineering. The Germans understood the precision of our systems. They didn't mess around with flimsy imitations. Used to be a lot of copycats, you know. Trying to undercut us. That’s always the way, isn’t it? Someone always trying to take a shortcut. I had that with my paintings, to a lesser degree. Always someone offering a ‘bargain’ imitation at the local craft fairs. It’s flattering, in a way. Means you’re doing something right. But the exhibitions… that was the real highlight. The sheer scale of them! And the pressure. Absolutely vital to make a good impression. I remember one year, the main demonstrator called in sick the night before. Had to step in myself, and I hadn't run the machine properly in months! Oh dear! That sounds stressful. Were you able to pull it off? Just about! Lots of frantic page-turning in the manual beforehand. And a very convincing performance, I hope. Thankfully, the machine cooperated.

Honestly, this journey is  dragging . Are we nearly there yet? Like, actually? Nearly, love. Not ‘nearly’ nearly, but we’ve passed Birmingham, which is a good sign. Another couple of hours, at least. And stop asking! You asked five minutes ago. I know, I know. It’s just… I’m already picturing the beach. And needing a serious ice cream. Which reminds me, are we stopping at a proper service station or one of those tiny ones with just a cash machine and three sad sandwiches? Proper one next, near Gloucester, I think. They usually have a decent Boots and a WHSmith. You can stock up on holiday reading. Good. I need a new book. And maybe some chocolate. Actually, that’s a priority. Speaking of things needing stocking up… did you remember to pack my quinoa? Your  quinoa ? Seriously? On holiday? You’re taking healthy eating to a whole new level, you are. It's a good source of protein! And I don’t want to live on chips and pasties for a week. Although… pasties do sound good. Cornwall is famous for them, right? They are. And yes, I did pack your quinoa, hidden away with the emergency biscuits. Honestly, you’re a strange one. Hey! It’s a superfood! Did you know the word ‘quinoa’ originally comes from the Quechua language? It’s really interesting, the etymology of words, like how ‘corn’ used to mean  any  grain… Right. Here we go. English Language A-Level in full flow. That teacher of yours has really got you hooked, hasn't she? She’s brilliant! We’re doing etymology at the moment, and it’s fascinating. It’s weird how languages change, though. How people used to say things differently. Do you think English will be completely unrecognisable in, like, a hundred years? Probably. It’s always evolving. Remember how Grandma used to say things? Completely different phrases to how we use them now. And the way  she  pronounced Worcestershire… Oh God, yes! “Wooster-sheer”! It always sounded so posh. Speaking of counties, how do you spell Gloucestershire again? Is it with one ‘s’ or two? Two 's's. Gloucestershire. And don’t ask me about Leicestershire. I always mess that one up. It's a mouthful. It is! We were discussing it in Geography the other day, weird county names. And the way everyone pronounces them differently. Are we going through the Cotswolds?

Right, so onions are chopped, garlic’s minced… anyone else feel like they’re crying disproportionately to the amount of onion they’ve actually dealt with? Nah, I’m alright. Used to peeling spuds all day, builds a resistance, y’know? Though this is a bit fancier than what I'm used to, to be fair. Bolognese for everyone, eh? Not just chips and gravy tonight. Chips and gravy  would  be nice. Though I suppose we should try and be respectable for once. My Elsie used to make a bolognese that'd knock your socks off. Secret ingredient was a splash of red wine. Oh, red wine! Good shout, Arthur. Is there any in here, Ben? I thought you said you had a bottle opened? Yeah, in the fridge. Just… didn't fancy it earlier. Been a long day. Found a wasps' nest under some decking, had to get rid of that lot. Good grief! You're braver than me. I’d have legged it. Sounds like something out of a film. Did you get stung? Just once, on the hand. Swelled up a bit, but not too bad. Mum gave me some cream for it. She’s always got something for every ailment, that woman. Mothers, eh? Always know best. Mine used to force cod liver oil down me. Said it would put hairs on my chest. Didn’t work, obviously. Oh, bless ya, Arthur. My mam was the same with everything. 'Eat your carrots, it’ll help you see in the dark!' Like I was joining the navy or something. Honestly, she’d try and sneak vegetables into everything. My mum's always going on about getting enough fibre. It's like, yeah, Mum, I eat fruit and veg sometimes, alright? Don’t need a lecture every time I have a biscuit. It's a generational thing, I reckon. They all worry. Though, speaking of food, I’m trying to get better at making proper family meals now I've got me own place. It's harder than it looks. It is. Elsie always said the trick was patience. And a good stock. She’d make her own stock from chicken bones. Hours she’d spend over that pot, stirring and skimming. Hours? Crikey. I just buy the cubes, to be honest. Cheaper and quicker. I’ve tried making stock, but it never tastes as good as the shop-bought stuff.

Honestly, this coffee is a lifesaver. Early shift at the pub last night, then trying to drag myself to this spin class…needed something strong. Tell me about it. Marking essays is  exhausting . I swear, the amount of times I read ‘there’ when it should be ‘their’… it’s a slow burn of frustration. How was the pub, though? Busy? Packed, as usual for a Friday. Stag do. The usual chaos. Honestly, I make more money on a Friday and Saturday than I do the rest of the week combined. Still trying to figure out what to  do  with it though, besides pay rent. Thinking about maybe finally getting the car fixed. Oh yeah? What's up with it? Just…everything, really. It’s an old Ford Fiesta. Gets me from A to B, but it’s making noises I’ve never heard a car make before. And the clutch is on its last legs. My Dad keeps telling me to just buy a new one, but I’m stubborn. And saving for a new one feels…impossible. I get that. Everything feels expensive right now. Are you still seeing… what was her name? Chloe? Nah, that fizzled out a while ago. She decided she needed someone “more ambitious”. Apparently, pouring pints and studying for a history degree doesn’t scream ‘future CEO’. Ouch. That’s…tactless. She sounds lovely. Yeah, well. Her loss, I guess. It’s hard dating when you're working evenings, anyway. Everyone's already made plans. It’s easier to just focus on finishing my dissertation. Which, by the way, is proving to be the bane of my existence. What’s it on? The social impact of pubs in post-war Birmingham. Surprisingly difficult to research. Lots of council records, but not a lot of… personal accounts. I'm interviewing a few older regulars, which is good, but it's slow going. What about you? Still enjoying the teaching? Most of it. The kids are generally good, though the admin is a nightmare. It’s endless marking, endless meetings, endless paperwork. And trying to explain the subjunctive to fifteen-year-olds…that's a special kind of torture. Still, at least it’s intellectually stimulating. What sport are you into, aside from spinning to punish yourself? I try to play five-a-side football when I can. It’s a good way to release some stress. Though I'm usually knackered for the next two days.

Honestly, Arthur, you've been going on about that coffee for a good ten minutes. I’ve barely had a chance to sit down! Well, it's a matter of principle, Margaret. He promised me a proper cup, not this…this lukewarm dishwater. And it's been lukewarm every single time. Now, now. It’s perfectly acceptable coffee, Arthur. Perhaps your palate is just a bit…refined these days. Refined? I just want a cup of coffee that doesn’t taste like it's been sitting in the pot since Tuesday! And speaking of things being lukewarm, did you see how slowly old Mrs. Higgins was driving this morning? Honestly, she shouldn't be allowed behind the wheel anymore. Oh, come on, Arthur, she's just getting on a bit. Everyone slows down eventually. You’ll be the same one day. I like to  think  my driving skills are still impeccable. Unlike some. Remember that trip to the Gambia, David? You nearly drove us into a ditch trying to avoid a goat! That goat had a death wish, I tell you. Just wandered right into the road. And it was a perfectly executed manoeuvre, if I may say so myself. Avoided the goat, avoided the ditch, and only slightly startled Margaret. Slightly? I thought my heart was going to leap out of my chest! Anyway, enough about goats and dangerous driving. I was thinking about that donation box for the church fete. I've got an old biscuit tin, but it's a bit… dented. A biscuit tin? Really, Margaret? It needs to be presentable. Something a bit more…stately. Maybe David has some spare boxes from his business. Possibly. Though most of my packaging goes straight to recycling now. We’re trying to be more environmentally conscious, you know. Speaking of presentations, I was also thinking about banners for the bell ringing group. We really need something eye-catching for the village fair. Oh, that’s a good idea! Maybe with a picture of the bells? Or some musical notes? I'm quite good with a bit of felt, you know. I could make something rather lovely. That’s a thought. Though I’m not sure felt is quite…durable enough. It might get ruined if it rains. We could laminate it? Or use a waterproof fabric. There are options. Though, to change the topic completely, I was reading an article the other day about Munchausen Syndrome.

Honestly, this pasta is  amazing . Did you make the sauce from scratch, Chloe? I did! Found a recipe on TikTok, actually. It’s surprisingly easy. Though, I spent like an hour scrolling through ‘foodtok’ before I actually decided on one. It’s a black hole, that app. Oh, TikTok food is dangerous. It either ends in Michelin-star quality or absolute disaster. No in-between. Remember Sarah trying to make that cloud bread? Oh god, don't remind me! The kitchen looked like a science experiment gone wrong. It was…fluffy sadness. Speaking of disasters, I tried watching 'Hereditary' last night. Big mistake. Huge. I haven't been able to sleep properly since. 'Hereditary'? Oh yeah, that one’s proper messed up. I heard it's genuinely terrifying, not just jump scares. I'm a bit of a scaredy-cat, so I stick to more…mild horror. You and me both. I’m more of a psychological thriller person. Give me a good twist, not a demon child. Although, to be fair, Toni Collette in 'Hereditary' is  incredible . She is. But I'd rather admire her acting from a safe distance. Anyway, has anyone heard from Liam lately? I haven’t seen him post anything on Instagram for days. No, that’s odd. He usually floods his story with gym selfies. Maybe he’s finally taken a digital detox? Knowing Liam? Probably just found a new dating app and is too busy swiping. Remember when he was obsessed with that one where you only match with people who also like dogs? Oh, yes. “Bark Buddies,” I think it was called. It lasted about a week. He said the conversations were too…woof-iful. Don’t even. Okay, but seriously, should we check if he's okay? He was looking a bit down last weekend when we were at the pub. Good point. I’ll send him a message. Speaking of weekends… anyone thinking about a summer holiday? I'm desperate to get away. I was looking at flights to Greece. Greece sounds perfect! Although, it’s gonna be packed. I was thinking maybe somewhere a bit more…off the beaten path? Like, Croatia or Montenegro. Croatia is gorgeous. I went a couple of years ago and the coastline is stunning. But honestly, I’d be happy just with a week in Cornwall, a good book, and no responsibilities. Cornwall sounds amazing!

Right then, lovely to see you, Margaret. Come on in, come on in. Kettle's just boiled. Oh, thank you, Arthur. Lovely to be here. It’s a bit blowy out there, isn't it? That wind nearly took my hat off! Aye, a proper norfolk breeze. Worse than usual, I reckon. I was watchin’ the trees bendin’ fit to break. It is. Makes you grateful for a warm house, that’s for sure. Colin, you want a biscuit with your tea? I’ve got digestives, rich tea… Digestives are good, thank you, Arthur. So, how was the drive over, Margaret? Everything alright? It was alright, thank you. A bit slow going on the A11, there was a lorry having trouble just past Attleborough. Didn’t cause too much of a hold-up, thankfully. But it got me thinking about cars… Cars, eh? What about ‘em? Well, I was reading in the paper about these electric cars, and all the charging points they’re promising. But honestly, I don’t know. Seems a lot of fuss for something that might break down halfway between here and Ipswich. That's the truth. My nephew, young David, he's got one. Always goin' on about how green it is. But he had to get towed last month! Battery went flat right on the A47. Said he miscalculated the range. Miscalculated! How do you miscalculate the range of a car? Sounds like David. Always was a bit optimistic, that one. I still prefer a good petrol engine. Reliable, you know? You can always smell when something’s going wrong. These electric things are just…silent trouble. Exactly! And what about getting home? If the electricity goes off, you’re stuck. No charging, no going anywhere. I remember when cars were…well, cars. You knew what you were getting. A key, some petrol, and a prayer! They were simpler times, weren't they? Remember old man Hemmings down the road? He had a Ford Anglia, that car must’ve been older than me! Thing rattled and shook like a jelly, but it always got him from A to B. Never seen anything like it. Old Hemmings! Now there was a character. He used to say that car ran on willpower and strong tea. I remember helping him push it once, up that hill near the church. Nearly broke my back! Oh dear! Well, hopefully, I won't be needing anyone to push  my  car anytime soon.

Honestly, this traffic is dreadful. I’m starting to think we should have left hours earlier. It's just a sea of red lights as far as the eye can see. Tell me about it. I checked the app before we left, said ‘slow but moving’. ‘Slow but moving’ is a generous description, wouldn't you say? At this rate, we'll be lucky to get to Manchester before tea time. It’s the M6, love. Expect nothing less. Still, at least we’re all together. And you’ve got a good supply of biscuits, Moira. That’s the main thing. Always prepared. Though I’m starting to think  I’ll  be the one needing the comfort of a biscuit before long, staring at these brake lights. Speaking of needing things...did you manage to sort out that quote for the removal van, David? Aye, I did. Got a surprisingly good price, actually. Old Mr. Henderson from down the road recommended a company. Apparently his daughter used them when she moved to York. Seemed decent enough on the phone. Said they're very careful with furniture. Reminded me of when we moved to Walsall… absolute chaos, that was. Remember that antique sideboard your mother loved? Oh, don't even start! I've heard that story approximately fifty times. The one where it nearly went over the M5 embankment? It was a close call! The straps gave way, and it was wobbling like a jelly! Luckily, young Timmy – bless him – managed to brace it with his foot. Saved a family heirloom, he did. Well, let’s hope  this  move is a little less eventful. I’m already stressed enough about downsizing. So many years in that house, so much… stuff. It’s overwhelming. You'll be glad to be rid of it, honestly. Remember your back troubles last year? All those stairs weren't helping. A nice, level bungalow will be much better for you. And closer to us, which is a bonus. True, true. Proximity to my favourite people is a definite perk. Though I'm dreading the entire airport palaver. I haven’t flown in… goodness, must be ten years now? Airports are a nightmare these days, aren't they? All queues and security checks and lost luggage. I used to travel all the time for work, used to be a bit more civilised. Now? It's just stressful. I much prefer a nice, long drive, even one like this one.

So, you won’t  believe  what happened with the bike. Oh no, don’t tell me it's… worse? I thought you said the police hadn’t had any luck. Well, they hadn’t. But Mrs. Henderson from number 32, she recognised it! She saw a lad riding it down towards the seafront yesterday afternoon. She said she was pretty sure it was yours, with the stickers and everything. No way! Did she… did she say anything? She did. Apparently, she followed him – really bravely, actually – and kept an eye on where he went. He ended up leaving it chained up outside the amusement arcade. She called the police straight away. Seriously?! That’s amazing! So you’ve got it back? Is it alright? Yep, picked it up just an hour ago. A little scuffed, but nothing major. The lock they used was rubbish, honestly. I reckon I could have just snapped it with my hands. That’s brilliant! I was so gutted when it went missing. I was starting to think I’d have to walk to college every day. It’s miles! I know. And with the hills! Honestly, it was giving me stress just thinking about it. I told you not to leave it unlocked, though. I know, I know, Mum. I just popped into the shop for like, two minutes! It's just… it happens so fast. Have you seen on TikTok, there’s this whole trend of bike thefts going around? Apparently, Hastings is a hotspot. TikTok? Honestly, you and that TikTok. It’s probably just making you more paranoid. Still, good to be aware, I suppose. Right, fancy some lunch? I made a massive pasta bake. Ooh, yes please! That sounds amazing. Is it the one with the cheesy crust? The very same. I even put in extra cheese, knowing how much you love it. You’re the best! I’m still buzzing about the bike, though. I'm definitely investing in a seriously good lock now. Maybe one of those ones that beep if someone tries to move it? Good thinking! And try not to post pictures of it all over social media, advertising where you live, yeah? Just a thought. Ugh, you’re right. Mum’s always looking out for me. Maybe I’ll just stick to posting about the pasta bake instead. Now  that  is a good plan. Come on, let’s go eat before it gets cold.

Right, I’m officially declaring myself starved. This Ticket to Ride is deceptively energy-consuming. Tell me about it. Strategising is  hungry  work, you know? Though, to be fair, I did have a rather large elevenses. Elevenses? You’re turning very English, Gareth. Next thing you know you’ll be demanding scones with clotted cream. Hey! A Welshman can appreciate a good scone. It’s the jam-first debate where things get really heated. Jam first is the  only  way. Anyone who argues differently is a heathen. Oh, don’t start that again, Bryn. We’ve had this argument every family holiday for the last decade. It’s exhausting. You’re all wonderfully predictable. Right, food. What are we thinking? I was fancying a proper pub lunch tomorrow, maybe? Somewhere with a roaring fire? It's definitely that sort of weather. Sounds good to me. Though, I'm warning you, I'm craving a Sunday roast. Yorkshire puddings are non-negotiable. Oooh, ambitious. A good Yorkshire pudding is a thing of beauty. Speaking of ambitious… I’m attempting to complete the Trans-Siberian Railway route. It’s proving…challenging. The Trans-Siberian? Good luck with that! It’s a monster. You need to think about momentum, you see. Like a real train. Oh, here we go. Prepare for a lecture on train dynamics, everyone. It’s not a lecture! It’s applied physics! You need to factor in the gradient, the weight of the carriages, the resistance from the tracks… It’s a delicate balance. You can’t just haphazardly lay down routes. Think about George Stephenson's Rocket! Oh, Bryn and his trains. He’s been obsessed since he was a little boy. Used to dismantle anything with wheels. I remember one Christmas, he took apart my brand new train set to “understand how it worked.” My mum nearly had a fit. It was for educational purposes! I rebuilt it, eventually. Mostly. Right, well, clearly I'm not approaching this with enough scientific rigour. I'll need to factor in the gravitational pull of the coloured plastic trains. Absolutely essential. Do you want me to start calculating wind resistance? Please do! While you're at it, could you research the optimal coal-to-water ratio for steam engines? You know, for strategy purposes. I think we need to change the subject before we both end up researching Victorian engineering. Anyone fancy helping me collect more train cards?
