Right, your go. Honestly, this game is taking  forever . I thought ‘Ticket to Ride’ would be a quick evening activity after your mum’s roast, not a three-hour strategic battle for railway dominance. It  is  taking a while, isn’t it? Though, I’m thoroughly enjoying it. It’s a good change from marking essays. And besides, Mum’s roast deserves a lengthy wind-down. She puts so much effort in. True, true. She did outdo herself with the Yorkshire puddings. Still, I’m starting to feel like I need a map just to figure out where everyone is trying to go. You’re awfully quiet, what nefarious plan are you hatching? No plan. Just…considering my options. Strategizing. It's funny, isn’t it, how seriously people take board games? I was reading an article the other day about the German  Spiel des Jahres  award – apparently, it’s a massive deal. Like, national news level. Really? That’s…intense. I always assumed board games were just a bit of fun, a rainy-day activity. Germans seem to take everything very seriously though, don’t they? Even their leisure time? It’s a whole culture, apparently. They have these huge board game conventions, and it’s considered a perfectly acceptable adult hobby. A lot more sophisticated than Monopoly and Cluedo, though. They’re all about intricate mechanics and long-term strategy. Hmm. Sounds exhausting. I prefer something a bit lighter, honestly. We should dig out 'Carcassonne' next time we’re here. It’s a lot more… pastoral. Less about resource management and more about building little medieval landscapes. Good shout. You know, it’s a weird contrast to the drinking culture here, isn’t it? In Germany, it's all about the games being the  focus . Here, a ‘games night’ often feels like a thinly veiled excuse to get progressively more tipsy. Oh, you’re spot on. Especially with Uncle David involved. It starts innocently enough with a bit of Scrabble, then someone suggests cards, then it’s ‘never have I ever’ fuelled by gin and tonics. It escalates quickly. Precisely! And don't even get me started on family charades. It’s less about acting out clues and more about deliberately obtuse interpretations to wind everyone up. Oh God, yes. And Dad  always  chooses incredibly obscure historical figures. No one has a clue what he's doing. It's purely designed to frustrate us.

Honestly, this shepherd’s pie is amazing, Kerrie. You’ve outdone yourself. It's even better than last time. It really is fantastic. What’s the secret this time? More Worcester sauce? Just a good pinch of nutmeg, boys. That’s all. My grandmother always said a pinch of nutmeg makes all the difference. And proper lamb mince, never beef. Nutmeg! That’s clever. I always forget the little things like that. I tried making a stew last week and it was… well, it was edible. But not  this  good. I’m still trying to get my head around moving all the white goods. It’s a nightmare. The washing machine alone feels impossible. Oh, that’s a headache, isn’t it? Did you get quotes for removal firms? They’re expensive, but worth it if you’ve got a lot to move. I did, and horrifyingly so! I was hoping to just bribe a couple of strong friends with beer and pizza, but I think I might actually need professionals. The staircase in the new place is  narrow . You really should get professionals. It’s not worth risking injury, or damaging your stuff. Remember what happened to Sarah when she tried to move her sofa herself? Oh, don't remind me. A trip to A&E and a very expensive sofa repair! She learned her lesson, that one. Speaking of which, how’s Sarah’s back? Last I heard, she was still having trouble. She’s a lot better, thankfully. Physiotherapy seems to be doing the trick. She’s back to doing her pottery, which has really cheered her up. She’s making some beautiful little planters now. That’s good to hear. She puts so much effort into it. It’s always nice to see people doing things they enjoy. I’m just… stressed about all this moving stuff. And the bins! Apparently, the collection schedule is completely different in the new area. Oh, bins are  always  a source of contention. Honestly, I spend half my life trying to figure out which bin is for what. It changes every year! And don’t even get me started on the council’s website… It’s designed to be purposefully confusing, I swear. I’ve spent ages trying to find out what day our recycling gets collected. It feels like a conspiracy. It does! And the new place… it’s got a tiny kitchen.

Honestly, Mum, this traffic is mental. Feels like we’ve barely moved in the last ten minutes. It always does around here, darling. Especially heading towards the North Circular. Remember when your father used to get absolutely  furious ? Full-on road rage. Oh yeah, the horn was his second voice. He’d be laying into people left, right, and centre. I try to just… zen out. It’s not worth the stress. Wise lad. Though a little assertive honking never hurt anyone, within reason. Are you still enjoying the car, by the way? Your Grandad would be chuffed to see you driving it. Yeah, it’s good. Properly comfy, actually. Still getting used to the parking, though. It’s a beast. Though I think it’s more the London drivers I need to get used to. They’re a special breed, aren’t they? So, how was that meeting with your supervisor yesterday? Still feeling good about the dissertation? Yeah, it’s going alright. He gave me a couple of pointers on the methodology, which was helpful. It’s just… enormous. Feels like I’m drowning in research sometimes. Well, you’re a clever boy, you’ll get there. You always do. Speaking of enormous, I had the most dreadful email from a prospective author this morning. Thought he was submitting a manuscript to the  TLS  – completely missed that we only do reviews. Oh, bless him. People don’t read the submission guidelines, do they? Apparently not! It’s a constant battle, that. And then the debate about digital versus print. Everyone’s convinced print is dead, but we still get a surprising number of subscriptions. I get that. I still prefer proper books. The  feel  of them, you know? Though, I confess, my Kindle does get a fair bit of use. Especially on the commute. It’s convenient, I’ll give it that. But there’s just something about holding a beautifully bound volume… Although, shipping costs are killing us. It’s getting ridiculous. Right? Everything’s getting more expensive. You’d think they were sending the books by private jet. Practically! Oh, speaking of expense, I need to pick up a birthday present for your Aunt Sarah. Any ideas? She's impossible to buy for. Hmm… she mentioned wanting to go back to France, didn’t she? Maybe a nice French cookbook? Or a voucher for a French wine tasting?

Right, so then the seagull  actually  swooped down and tried to steal the chips right out of her hand! Honestly, I’ve never seen anything like it. Old Mrs. Higgins nearly had a heart attack. No way! Classic Blackpool. They’re proper aggressive them seagulls, aren’t they? They’ve no shame. It’s true! My little cousin lost a whole sausage roll to one last year. She was devastated. The seagull didn’t even look sorry. Just perched on the tower, smug as anything. You get that in Scarborough too, honestly. One tried to take my ice cream. I had to physically wrestle it off him. Nearly ended up with a beak mark! Wrestling a seagull? You’re braver than you look, love. I was fuelled by raspberry ripple, alright? It was a matter of principle! Speaking of risking life and limb for snacks, remember that time Liam tried to climb the lamppost at Southport Pleasure Beach to get a better view of the fireworks? Oh god, don’t remind me. My dad nearly killed him. He was absolutely furious. He thought he was Spider-Man! He was shouting “With great power comes great responsibility!” as he was halfway up. He’s always been a bit dramatic, our Liam. I remember when he convinced himself he was a pirate for a whole month after that trip to Alton Towers. He wouldn't answer to anything but "Captain Blackheart." Oh, I'd forgotten about Captain Blackheart! He made us all walk the plank – which was just a piece of wood across the garden, but still. And he insisted on wearing an eye patch, even to school. Mrs. Davies had to have a word. Poor Mrs. Davies. She's seen it all, hasn’t she? Remember when I tried to convince everyone I could speak fluent Welsh after that school trip to Snowdonia? Oh my god, yes! You just kept saying “Shwmae” and hoping for the best! The look on the sheep farmer’s face was priceless. He clearly had no idea what you were on about. It was the sheer confidence that made it so good. You totally committed to the bit. I think we were all a bit… experimental at school, weren’t we? Trying to figure out who we were. Definitely. I went through a goth phase, remember? All black clothes, pale makeup, the whole nine yards. Oh yeah, the one where you insisted on calling everyone “darling”?

Honestly, the best thing about a proper winter camp, you know, when it’s  really  cold… is the silence. Utter, absolute silence. Sounds… bracing. I’m quite happy with central heating and a good book, thank you very much. Though I suppose I can appreciate the appeal, in a purely theoretical sort of way. Dad’s right, it’s incredible. It’s a different kind of quiet than you get anywhere else. People just… don’t  go  out when it’s like that. You've got the whole landscape to yourself. It's a bit like feeling like the first person to ever see the place. Exactly! Last February, up in the Cairngorms… snow was coming down sideways, wind howling like a banshee, and not a soul for miles. You build your snow shelter, get the stove going… and then just  listen . It's incredibly grounding. A snow shelter? You build a snow shelter? Good heavens, Arthur, you’re a brave man. Or possibly slightly mad. I’m imagining something out of an Arctic survival manual. Not quite as dramatic as that, Moira. It’s a quinzee. You pile up a huge mound of snow, let it sinter for a couple of hours, then hollow it out. Keeps you remarkably warm. It’s about the physics, really, the way the snow insulates. Fascinating stuff. He’s a bit obsessed with the physics of it all, Mum. But it really works. I've been doing it with him since I was a kid. You wouldn’t believe how warm it gets inside. And it forces you to be… efficient. You can’t take unnecessary things. Every ounce counts. That sounds… challenging. I'd be worrying about everything freezing – toes, fingers, vital organs… Proper kit, Moira, proper kit. Merino wool base layers, down sleeping bag rated for -20… it's an investment. But it's an investment in your well-being, truly. It’s about stripping things back to basics, reconnecting with… well, with yourself and the natural world. It's a good mental reset, too. Being completely self-reliant for a few days, solving problems as they come... it's a good antidote to the constant stimulation of modern life. Plus, you see wildlife you’d never normally see. Tracks in the snow, ptarmigan blending into the landscape… Ptarmigan? Are those the ones that change colour? Aye, they do. White in the winter, mottled brown in the summer.

Honestly, I’m still reeling from that film last night. “Everything Everywhere All at Once”. What  was  that? Right? A complete sensory overload. Brilliant, though. Utterly brilliant. I haven't thought about hot dog fingers since…well, since last night. Hot dog fingers! Don't even. It’s just…so much. My brain feels like it needs a lie-down. Did you actually  follow  all the universes? Because I was losing track after the raccoon chef. No way. I just went with it. Tried to appreciate the sheer creativity, you know? It’s one of those films where trying to understand it logically detracts from the enjoyment. It’s more about the  feeling  it gives you. That's fair. It definitely evoked  a feeling . Mostly, bewilderedness. Though I did love Ke Huy Quan. He was amazing. Proper comeback story. Totally. And Michelle Yeoh just absolutely carried it. She’s incredible. Reminded me a bit of…have you ever read any Ursula K. Le Guin? Vaguely. Something about Earthsea, wasn’t it? Ages ago in uni. Why? There’s a similar kind of… philosophical depth, I think. Le Guin explores these vast, complicated worlds, but the heart of the story is always very human. Like with “Everything Everywhere”, it’s all these crazy sci-fi concepts, but ultimately it’s about a mother-daughter relationship. Ooh, I see what you mean. That makes sense. I might have to revisit Le Guin then. I remember liking the writing, just being a bit… lost in the world-building at the time. Speaking of needing comfort after a confusing experience, fancy grabbing some Thai tonight? There’s that new place on the High Street everyone’s raving about. Thai sounds perfect. I’m craving a proper Pad See Ew. It’s been too long. Did you manage to get any of that mango sticky rice last week when we went to that other place? Oh, disappointingly not! They'd sold out. I was gutted. Honestly, it’s borderline obsession at this point. I need to hunt down some decent mango sticky rice. It's a mission. We will find some. We  must . It’s a fundamental human right, surely? Absolutely. Right up there with free healthcare and decent public transport. Speaking of missions, I’ve got that site visit tomorrow morning. Dreadful journey, all the way out to… well, somewhere near Melton Mowbray. Oh, dear.

Right, so then the giant… he didn’t actually  eat  the little boy, you know. That’s what I thought when I first read it, but he just… tickled him until he couldn’t breathe from laughing! Tickled him? Like, really, really tickly? Oh,  incredibly  tickly. Apparently, giants have really rough hands. Like sandpaper. Can you imagine? Sandpaper hands would hurt! Could you build a giant with Lego, do you think? A really, really big one? Mmm, that’s a good question. It would need a  lot  of Lego, wouldn’t it? And you’d need to reinforce it, because all those blocks would make it wobbly. I could make the head! I have lots of grey bricks. You could definitely make the head! And maybe you, Leo, could do the feet? They’d have to be huge. Like, bigger than this bedroom! I could! But then it wouldn't fit in the room. Would it? No, it definitely wouldn’t. It’d be a garden giant! Speaking of big things… remember Mrs. Higgins at Brownies last night? She was going on about the Brownie Promise, and how important it is to do a ‘good turn’ every day. I said I helped tidy up my toys! Does that count? That absolutely counts, sweetheart. That's a brilliant good turn. Leo, did you do a good turn? I shared my PlayStation time with Finn. He wanted to play the racing car game. Oh, that was very kind of you. See? Good turns don't have to be huge things. It's just being helpful and thoughtful. You know what  isn't  very helpful or thoughtful? My computer at work. It's been playing up all day. What’s wrong with it? It just keeps freezing. I was trying to make a spreadsheet in Excel – you wouldn’t believe how many numbers I have to put in! – and it just… stopped. I had to start all over again. It makes me want to throw it out the window. Can’t you just get a new one? Like a really fast one? We'll see. They’re quite expensive. It reminds me of Grandpa's old typewriter. Remember that? The clicky one? The clicky one! It was so loud, but he loved it. He said it made a satisfying sound. He wouldn’t have understood computers, I don’t think. He was a very practical man.

Honestly, Arthur, you look like you’ve slept in your clothes. Not that it matters here, of course, but still… a bit of effort never hurt anyone. Oh, come off it, Margaret. Comfy is the aim of the game at my age. Besides, you’ve barely fared much better with that… is that a gravy stain? It is  not  gravy! It’s… a remnant of the rhubarb crumble from last night. And it's perfectly respectable. More coffee? I made a fresh pot. Don't mind if I do. Speaking of rhubarb, I was driving past that old farm near Skipton yesterday - the one we used to get our rhubarb from, remember? It’s all gone to seed. Or rather, to weeds. Sad to see. Used to be a thriving place. Oh, that’s a shame. They had beautiful fruit. It's the same with so many places around here. You start looking into the history, and you realise half of West Yorkshire is built on or around deserted medieval villages. Incredible, isn't it? All those lives, just… vanished. Vanished and replaced with roadworks, apparently. I spent a good hour yesterday crawling along the A650, thanks to some essential repairs. Essential to whom, I wonder? Certainly not to me and my blood pressure. Don’t start on the roadworks. I had to navigate a minefield of cones just to get to the shops yesterday. And then they had the cheek to send me a leaflet advertising their services! Junk mail, the bane of my existence. Tell me about it. It’s a constant stream of offers for things I neither need nor want. And the phone! Constant calls about PPI, or extending my car warranty on a car I sold five years ago! It’s driving me round the bend. I just put the phone down on them now. Rude, perhaps, but effective. Though sometimes they ring back on a withheld number. It's a conspiracy, I tell you. A conspiracy! Are you enjoying your toast? I made the damson jam last week. Lovely jam, Margaret, truly. You’ve got a gift for it. Far better than anything you can buy in the shops. You should think about selling it. Oh, don’t be daft. I just enjoy making it. Like my herbs, you know? I’ve got basil, rosemary, thyme, mint… all thriving on the windowsill. It's therapeutic.

Honestly, this new hand cream is a lifesaver. My skin was getting  so  cracked with all the handwashing at work. It's lavender and chamomile, smells divine. Lavender and chamomile, eh? Sounds… calming. Though I still reckon a good dollop of Vaseline does the trick. More economical, at least. You've gone all fancy on me, haven’t you, love? Oh, don’t be such a scrooge! It was on offer at Boots. And it’s not just about the smell, it actually  works . You’ve still got that redness on your knuckles, haven’t you? Just a touch. It’s character building. More importantly, did you manage to get those new blood pressure tablets sorted? The chemist said they were waiting for a delivery. Yes, picked them up this morning. Though they tried to push me towards the ‘own brand’ again. Honestly, I told them I’d rather walk to Spain than take a cheaper version of my medication. Walk to Spain? Mum, you’re dramatic. Well, I am a nurse! I know what I need. Besides, I’m planning something a little more exciting than walking to Spain. I was looking at holidays… maybe Greece next year? Greece? Nice. Always fancied Santorini. Though getting around those islands… nightmare. All those winding roads. Remember that time we got lost in Cornwall? Oh god, yes! Dad tried to navigate using Facebook directions. It led us down a farmer’s track barely wide enough for the car! It did! And I’m pretty sure we ended up in someone’s greenhouse. Honestly, these phones are supposed to make life easier, but… Speaking of phones, have you seen what Auntie Maureen’s been posting on Facebook? Another one of those chain letters about changing your profile picture to a landmark. Honestly, she believes everything she reads. Oh, bless her. She still thinks emojis are ‘hieroglyphics’. Exactly! It’s endearing, but… frustrating. I tried to explain to her that it’s just a silly fad, but she said it was ‘showing support’ for… something. I honestly didn’t listen after that. It's a distraction tactic, that's all. Keeps her busy. Did you get anything good for Christmas? Apart from luxury hand cream, obviously. Oh, you know… the usual. Socks, chocolates… you got me that lovely scarf, which is perfect. What about you? I got a new gadget for the garden. Apparently, it automatically waters the plants.

Honestly, this week has been  wild  at work. New client, total nightmare. They want everything to sound like a motivational Instagram post, even for… industrial plumbing supplies. Oh my god, seriously? That sounds awful. What’s the brief, like, “Reach for the pipes!”? Don't even joke! Something equally cringe. It’s exhausting trying to inject enthusiasm into…fittings. I spent three hours yesterday crafting copy about ‘robust drainage solutions’. Robust! Oh, the joys of copywriting. I’m starting to think my PhD is less stressful. Although, honestly, the data sets are making my brain melt. I'm programming a survey about public trust in the media right now, and everyone just seems incredibly cynical. No surprise there, is there? Have you seen what’s been happening with… well, everything? The whole thing with the water company dumping sewage? It's beyond belief. It’s horrific. And then the Tories just… deflect. My mum was going on about it at dinner last weekend, saying it's just blatant corruption. Honestly, trying to have a sensible conversation with her is impossible. She goes straight to conspiracy theories. Oh, mums. Mine’s obsessed with that show, ‘Escape to the Country’. Keeps trying to convince me I need to buy a cottage in the Cotswolds and ‘find myself’. Like, I’m currently trying to ‘find’ a decent salary in London, Mum. Bless her. My parents are convinced I’m having a crisis because I haven't secured a ‘proper’ job after finishing my Masters. They keep subtly suggesting I apply for teaching. Ugh, the pressure. Are you still seeing Ben, by the way? I haven’t properly caught up since… well, since everything with Chloe happened. We’re… on a break. A very long, uncomfortable break. He’s still processing, I think. It was all a bit messy. Turns out Chloe and my flatmate were secretly besties. The betrayal! Oh, wow. That’s… a whole other level of awkward. I'm so sorry. That’s awful. Honestly, people can be so awful. Tell me about it. It's just... draining. Anyway, enough of my drama. How are  you  doing, actually? Anything exciting happening, aside from the plumbing copy? Not much. I’m trying to save up for a deposit on a place, which feels impossible. London rent is ridiculous. I’ve started meal prepping to try and cut down on costs, but I keep accidentally burning things.

Honestly, I’m absolutely shattered. Did absolutely nothing all day except transcribe that dreadful interview about pigeons. Pigeons, honestly! Pigeons? That  is  a niche topic. Could be worse, though. Could be tax law. You’re both lucky you can relax at home. I’ve been staring at this blank page all afternoon. Writer’s block is a genuine physical ailment, you know. Feels like my brain’s turned to concrete. Oh, I know the feeling. Though mine’s more likely turned to pigeon facts. Did you manage to get a walk in today, David? You were talking about trying to get back into running. Not today, no. Rain came on just as I was about to head out. And honestly, after dealing with spreadsheets all day, the thought of pushing myself physically… it just didn't appeal. Maybe tomorrow. What about you, Sarah? Any venturing out? Just to the shops. Needed milk. And avoided eye contact with Mrs. Higgins, she cornered me last time to talk about her grandson's GCSE results for half an hour. Oh, the neighbourhood watchdogs! They mean well, but…a captive audience is never pleasant. Speaking of neighbourhoods, have you seen what that house on Elm Street sold for? The one with the awful garden gnomes? No, really? Don’t tell me it went for over asking. Over asking, and by a  significant  amount. Apparently, it was a bidding war. Nearly half a million. Honestly, it’s ridiculous. Half a million for  that  house? They must be mad. It needs a complete gutting. Honestly, the market is completely bonkers. I sometimes wonder if we should just move somewhere rural. Rural? You'd miss your shops, Sarah. You and your Mrs. Higgins avoidance tactics. True. Though a little peace and quiet does sound appealing. But then you look at house prices  outside  the city…it’s just as bad. It’s a terrible position to be in. I'm thinking I should just build an extension and stay put. Though last time I attempted anything DIY, it involved a trip to A&E. I can imagine. You have... a certain enthusiasm for projects, don't you, Margaret? Enthusiasm is one word for it. Chaos is another. Right, I think I need to make a cuppa. And possibly contemplate the meaning of life while I do. Or, you know, just think about what to make for dinner. Good idea.

Right, so basically the whole department’s in a bit of a flap because of this new budgeting thing. Apparently, they’re expecting us to cut… well, everything. Oof, sounds cheerful. Is that across the whole Uni, or just your little corner of it? Seems pretty widespread, yeah. Apparently, fewer students are applying, or something, and funding’s been cut. Means no new software, delayed maintenance on the archives… the usual. It’s stressful. I spend half my day just cataloguing ancient documents, the other half arguing why we  need  a new scanner. Classic. Bureaucracy at its finest. I’m getting the same sort of vibes at work, although it's more about justifying project costs. Every single item needs three quotes now, and a full risk assessment. It's slowing everything down. Especially infuriating when a bolt costs, like, three quid. Three quid! Honestly. You’d think they’d trust you lot to build things that don’t immediately fall down without needing to micromanage the bolt budget. You’d think. Though, to be fair, I did hear about Old Man Hemmings’ bridge design last year… apparently, didn’t quite account for the river’s tendency to  flood . Oh, no! Hemmings? He’s the one who always wears the tweed and smells faintly of pipe tobacco, isn’t he? The very same. Still, it makes it easier to understand why they’re being so cautious. Anyway, enough about work. You were telling me you went to see a musical? Oh aye! Went to see “Six” at the Cambridge Theatre. Honestly? Brilliant. I didn’t really know much about it before, just that it’s about the six wives of Henry VIII, but it’s done like a pop concert. Each queen gets her own song, and they're all belting out these amazing tunes. Sounds… intense. A bit different from the sort of things I usually go to. I was considering seeing “Hamilton” when it comes to London, but it’s so expensive. It  is  pricey, but “Six” is much more affordable and honestly, really fun. It’s not highbrow theatre, it’s just… good. Loads of energy. You’d enjoy it. Did you see anything good lately? Not really. Been mostly heads-down with work, unfortunately. Though I did catch a documentary about trainspotting the other night. Surprisingly gripping. Trainspotting? Really? That’s a… niche interest. I know, I know.

Right, that’s the fence posts sorted, more or less. Just need a good coat of paint and they’ll look as good as new, eh? Though, honestly, looking at the state of next door’s garden… it’s a losing battle. Tell me about it. Old Man Hemmings, isn't it? Let it go completely, he has. I drove a bloke past there last week, potential buyer, fancy house up the road, and he nearly choked when he saw it. Said it brought the whole street down. It's a shame. I heard he's got a bad hip, though. Can't get about like he used to. Still, shouldn’t let it become a jungle. All those developers sniffing around, you know? They’ll be wanting to flatten everything and build flats. You’re not wrong there. They’re already building those monstrosities down by the docks. Looks like concrete boxes stacked on top of each other. No character at all. Used to be a thriving market, that place. It’s horrifying, isn't it? The relentless march of…progress. Speaking of relentless, did you see that new film, “The Lighthouse”? The one with Willem Dafoe and Robert Pattinson? Can’t say I did. I was working all weekend. Picked up a bloke from the airport, then a hen party. Honestly, the things I hear in this job. Oh, it’s brilliant. Properly unsettling. Two lighthouse keepers going slowly mad. Dafoe is incredible, just completely loses himself in the role. It reminded me a bit of that Beckett play we saw,  Waiting for Godot , but with more seagulls and… existential dread. Sounds a bit heavy, that. I prefer a good action film, something to switch the brain off. Like that  John Wick  one. Bang, bang, bang. Job done. Different strokes, I suppose. I’ve been trying to get back into painting, you know. Haven’t touched a brush in ages. Found a really cheap easel in that charity shop on Smithdown Road last week. Absolute bargain. You always were a good artist. Remember that portrait you did of me, years ago? My mum still has it up on her wall. Oh, God, that was awful! I was still learning. It made you look like a right villain. Speaking of charity shops, I was wondering… would you mind if I borrowed your ladder for a couple of days? These gutters need a proper clean before winter, and mine's missing a couple of rungs.

Honestly, this scenery is just… relentless, isn’t it? Fields and fields. Beautiful, of course, but after a while, it all blends into one green blur. Are we sure we didn’t miss a turning for something a bit more… dramatic? Dramatic? Auntie Carol, relax! We're in rural Poland, not filming a blockbuster. It’s  meant  to be peaceful. Besides, it’s nice to just… be. No deadlines, no parent-teacher meetings, just the open road. And look, that little church steeple. See? Not entirely devoid of interest. Easy for you to say, you’re the one driving! I’m just observing the endless expanse of… crops. Though, a little detour wouldn’t kill us. Remember that medieval castle we saw advertised near Krakow? We’ve got Tarnow booked, remember? And we agreed to stick to the plan. Though, speaking of plans… have you worked out exactly how much this trip is costing us? I’m trying to keep a record for budgeting, and the campsite fees are adding up. Oh, dear. Not another financial reckoning. Honestly, I’m trying not to think about it too much. All this ‘freedom’ comes at a price, doesn’t it? I did transfer you some money yesterday, though. Was it enough? Yeah, that was brilliant, thank you. It covers the fuel for a good chunk of the journey, I think. We’re doing okay, but I’m worried about food costs. Polish supermarkets are… interesting. Trying to navigate the sausage aisle is a whole adventure in itself. Oh, I can imagine! I’m happy to stick to bread and cheese, if that helps. Less linguistic challenge involved. And are you still in touch with Sarah and Liam? I was thinking about them the other day. Haven’t heard from them properly since… well, ages. Yeah, I messaged Sarah just last week. Liam's still working crazy hours at the hospital. They’re talking about trying to get away for a weekend in the Lake District in October. I told them about the van – they were a bit jealous, naturally. Good. They deserve a break. Though, honestly, this van is a bit of a revelation. I’ve been meaning to declutter the spare room for years, and this is the impetus I needed. Anything not absolutely essential has been donated or sold. It’s quite liberating, actually. See? Travelling does good things for the soul.

Right, just off the M55 now, onto the A6. Should be alright, shouldn’t it, love? You’ve got the Sat Nav, haven’t you? Yes, Dad, I’ve got it. It's telling me to exit at the next junction. Honestly, you worry like a new mother. He just doesn’t like getting lost, do you Dad? Remember that time in the Lake District? We ended up on a farm track. Don't remind me! Thought we were going to need a tractor to get us out. Your mother… she wasn’t best pleased. Still, a nice view though, weren’t it? Beautiful, but a bit stressful at the time. Speaking of stressful, how are those revision notes coming along, Elsie? Exams getting close now. Ugh, don’t even mention it. History is just… a lot. So many dates. I keep mixing up Henry VIII’s wives. Six wives, wasn’t it? A right messy business. Your grandma used to be brilliant at history. She could rattle off monarchs for fun. Used to tell us stories about ’em too, not just dates. She did have a gift for storytelling. I remember her telling me about the Queen when I was first learning English. Made it so much easier to understand the whole monarchy thing. It’s weird thinking about the new King now, isn't it? Feels like it was only yesterday we were all glued to the telly. Aye, it does. Seventy years she reigned. A lifetime. They don’t make ‘em like that anymore. No, they don’t. Oh look, there’s a Waterstones coming up. Do we need anything from there? I was thinking of getting something for my mum, she's been talking about the Hay Festival. Ooh, Hay Festival sounds amazing! I saw something on TikTok about it. Loads of authors and book stalls. I wish I was going. It’s good, that festival. A bit pricey though, isn't it? Your Auntie Brenda went a couple of years ago. Spent a fortune on books she ended up giving away. Sounds like Brenda! She's got a good heart. I saw a really good biography of Marie Curie, might grab that. Elsie, are you reading anything good at the moment? Aside from history textbooks, of course. I’m trying to get through ‘Circe’ by Madeline Miller. It's really well-written, but quite slow. It's a bit… dense, you know?

Well, I never! Honestly, you two, keeping a whole visitor a secret? I thought I’d lost my hearing, not my ability to detect a conspiracy! Oh, Mother, you’d have found out eventually. We wanted it to be a surprise. You haven’t been to Thirsk in ages. And Leo’s been wanting to see you properly. Hi Gran! It’s good to see you. Did you have a nice journey? Lovely journey, thank you, Leo. Though that sat nav tried to take me through a farmyard at one point! Honestly, these modern gadgets… they’re clever, but they lack common sense. Remind me to tell you about the time a computer told me a perfectly good recipe involved beetroot in a trifle. Beetroot! Oh, don’t start on the technology again, Mum. Leo’s quite the whiz with it himself, you know. He’s building some sort of…what was it, Leo? A gaming computer? It’s a PC, yeah. I’m trying to get it built for next month’s LAN party. It's complicated, but really fun. A “LAN party”? Sounds like something out of a science fiction programme. Still, as long as it’s keeping you occupied. Though I do worry about young people spending too much time staring at screens. It can’t be good for the head, can it? It's a balance, isn’t it? We try to encourage him to get out and about. He plays rugby, thankfully. Keeps him fit. Rugby! That’s proper exercise, that is. Not like… tapping away at buttons. So, what have you two been up to? This house looks…different. You’ve been clearing out, I see. We have. Trying to declutter. It’s a never-ending task. Your visit was actually a good excuse to tackle the attic. Found some…interesting things. A whole box of your old hats, for starters. My hats! Oh, good Lord. I'd forgotten all about those. Some of them were rather stylish, you know. Before everyone started wearing baseball caps. Mum says there's a really weird one with feathers and...stuff. Ah, yes. That was for the races, years ago. Your Grandfather insisted. Thought I needed to make a statement. He was a good man, your Grandfather. Though a bit oblivious sometimes. He was. Listen, Mum, how are  you  doing? You seem…pale. Are you feeling alright? Oh, I’m fine, dear.

Right, so, what do you reckon? Feels pretty snappy, doesn’t it? Bit weird having a 17-inch screen again, been on smaller ones for ages. Yeah, it’s a beast! Seriously, the screen is… immersive. What did you end up going for, RAM wise? 32 gig. Figured future-proof it a bit. I’m still getting used to the keyboard, feels a little… mushy. Not as satisfying as my old one. Though that one was ancient, honestly. Thirty-two? Blimey. I still run everything off eight. Eight gig. Gets the job done for gardening blogs and YouTube, thankfully. What are you planning on doing with it, besides watching cat videos? Fair point. I’m hoping to actually get back into some digital painting. Been meaning to for ages. And I’ve got a couple of animation projects floating around in my head. Plus, rendering times on the old thing were… glacial. You should. Remember that weird short you started back in college? The one with the sentient toaster? Oh god, don’t remind me. That was… ambitious. And technically awful. Speaking of terrible tech, did you guys see old man Hemmings struggling with his new smart TV the other day? He was practically in tears. Hemmings? The one who still uses a flip phone? Yeah, saw it. His daughter was trying to explain streaming to him, it was a disaster. He kept asking if he needed a cable for Netflix. A cable! Honestly. It's like trying to explain the internet to my nan. It's all "where does it  go ?". It's generational, isn't it? I’ve been trying to explain TikTok to my Korean pen pal, and she’s like, “Why would anyone watch 15-second videos of people dancing?” I told her it’s a cultural thing. A very bizarre cultural thing. Speaking of Korea… you still planning that hiking trip? Yeah, hopefully next spring. I'm trying to learn a bit more of the language, but it’s  hard . So different from anything I’ve tackled before. You’ll be alright. You picked up bits of Greek pretty quick when we visited Cyprus, didn’t you? Plus, you’re the language instructor. That’s literally your job. True. Maybe he needs you to give Hemmings a crash course in 21st-century technology. He'd probably pay good money for that. Although he’d likely complain it’s a waste of his TV license fee.

Honestly, this place is  lovely . They’ve really done a good job with it, haven’t they? All that exposed brick… very ‘Shoreditch’. Feels a bit odd finding Shoreditch in Tarnow, though. It is nice, yeah. And the pierogi I had were… proper. Not like some of the stuff you get, all gloopy and filled with too much potato. This was, like, grandma-level pierogi. Which is the highest praise, obviously. Absolutely. Grandma-level. I’m glad you got the pierogi. I went for the soup… bit of a risk, ordering soup in Poland. It’s usually  so  heavy. But it was actually really light and lemony. Good to hear. I’m still trying to work out what I want for dessert. That cheesecake in the window is calling my name, but I had a rather large breakfast. Polish breakfasts are… substantial, to say the least. Substantial is putting it mildly! Mrs. Kowalski practically force-fed me a mountain of scrambled eggs and sausages. I think she genuinely thought I was wasting away. Speaking of substantial… how’s the running going? Still managing to drag yourself out there in the mornings? Ugh. It’s… a struggle. I’ve been awful this week, honestly. Trying to cut down on the booze a bit, and it's making me feel even more sluggish. It’s ridiculous, isn’t it? Like, I know it makes me feel rubbish, but the urge is just… there. It is, isn't it? I mean, I’ve never been much of a drinker myself, but I understand the pull of just… needing something. It’s funny, isn’t it? How we all have these little crutches. I used to spend hours online, just… scrolling. Filling the void with nonsense. Oh, yeah, I get that. My phone is basically an extension of my hand. It's terrifying. I was reading something the other day about dopamine hits and how addictive social media is. Made me feel marginally less pathetic, knowing it’s scientifically engineered to keep you hooked. Marginally being the key word, I presume? It’s that feeling of… not quite being enough, isn’t it? Like something's missing. It's strange. I always thought when I got older, I’d have it all figured out, know who I am and what I want. Oh, bless. That’s adorable. You think  anyone  has it figured out? I’m twenty-six and I still feel like I’m wandering around in the dark wearing mismatched socks.

Right, so Dorset Steam Fair is definitely on then? You’re both up for it? Absolutely! Haven’t been for… goodness, must be five years now. Used to love it when the kids were little. Though getting a decent spot to watch the arena events was always a battle. Five years? More like ten, Arthur! And yes, I’m in. It’ll be a nice day out. Though, I’m a bit worried about your mobility this year, love. Is it going to be too much for you? Nonsense, Maureen. I'm not  completely  falling apart yet! They’ve improved the access, haven't they? I remember reading something about better facilities for wheelchairs and the like. Yeah, I checked the website. They’ve got designated viewing areas, accessible toilets, and you can hire mobility scooters if needed. I can book one for you, Arthur, if you think it'd help. No need to be a hero. Appreciate it, love, but let’s see how I feel on the day. Don't want to be stuck on a scooter if I can manage with the stick. Bit undignified, isn’t it? Dignity’s overrated when your knees are screaming at you, Arthur. Honestly. It's more dignified to enjoy yourself than to grit your teeth and suffer. Okay, okay, we'll play it by ear. Right, tickets. They’re pricey, aren't they? It’s nearly a hundred quid for the three of us. Worth it for a good day out. Though speaking of pricey… did you see that little cottage that went up for sale near the beach? Absolutely gorgeous. But… £450,000! Seriously? In Bournemouth? That's… optimistic. Even for a small place. I was looking at flats further inland, but even those are ridiculous. Everything’s gone up so much. Bournemouth property is always a rip-off. Always has been. Remember old Mrs. Higgins selling her tiny house for a fortune when the university expanded? Made her retirement, she did. It just feels impossible to get on the property ladder these days. It's depressing. Oh, look, a ginger cat just wandered across the garden! It's beautiful. Just like Marmalade used to be. Aw, it  is  lovely. It looks a bit scruffy though, could do with a good brushing. You miss Marmalade, don’t you? Terribly. She was such a character. Always getting into mischief. Remember when she climbed into the airing cupboard and knocked all the towels down?

Honestly, this weather is dreadful, isn’t it? Rain, rain, rain. Reminds me of Kendal, though – always a bit drizzly up there. Feels like I’ve brought the Lake District with me. It's a bit bleak, isn’t it? Good for the garden, I suppose. Though, with the wind, I doubt much will stay put. You’ve timed your visit badly, love. We had a lovely little spell of sunshine just last week. Can I just… this guy on Twitter is arguing that Shakespeare didn’t  actually  write Shakespeare. Like, seriously? Oh, the internet. Full of geniuses. Probably a bot, anyway. Don’t waste your energy, lad. What are you even looking at? Just… stuff. This drama club is putting on  Hamlet  and I’m thinking of auditioning for Horatio. Oh, that’s lovely, dear! You always were a good actor. Remember that Christmas play at primary school? You were a brilliant shepherd. Though I do recall your father had to sew a button back on your costume halfway through. A classic mishap. And yes, he was an excellent shepherd. Very dignified for a seven-year-old. So, Horatio, is it? A good part. Lots of sensible talking. Speaking of sensible, have you thought about what you want for supper, Margaret? I was thinking a shepherd’s pie? Rather fitting, given the shepherd discussion. That sounds delightful, dear. Though, don't go overboard with the potato topping. Remember last time? It was rather… substantial. Mom, you always say that, and it’s always delicious. You make the best shepherd’s pie in Yorkshire. Actually, there’s this new artisan bakery opened in Thirsk. They do amazing sourdough. We could get some bread to go with it? Oh, I’ve heard about that place! “The Flour Child,” isn’t it? Apparently, their pain au chocolat is to die for. We could pop in later. Oh, I do love a good pain au chocolat. Though I always worry about supporting these… newfangled businesses. Old Mr. Henderson at the village shop has been serving us for fifty years! Times change, Mom. It's good to support local enterprise, wherever it comes from. And Mr. Henderson will be alright. He's a shrewd businessman. Speaking of changes, did you hear about Reverend Davies leaving the church? Apparently, he's taking up pottery. Pottery! Honestly! What will the congregation say? He was always a bit… unorthodox, wasn’t he?

Right, so dentist appointments. Cindy, you’re first on Tuesday, aren’t you? And Aaron, yours is Thursday this week. Don’t forget to brush properly, both of you. But I  do  brush properly! I know you do, darling. Just a reminder. And Aaron, no complaining this time, okay? Remember what happened last time? It was scary. The spinning brush thing. It's just to make sure your teeth are sparkly clean. Speaking of checks, did you get the letter about the hearing tests at school? For everyone in Year 3? Oh yeah! Miss Davies told us about it. It’s a little booth you go in. It's a quiet booth. That's right. Good to get those checked regularly. Anyway, have you two been talking to Ashaad lately? Yeah! We built a fort with her at playtime. A really big one! With loads of blankets and cushions. And a secret entrance. Sounds amazing. It’s lovely you have such a good friend at school. It feels like only yesterday you were both tiny, and now you’re building forts and having secret entrances! It’s so weird, isn't it, how quickly they grow up? Sometimes I wish I wasn't growing up. Oh? Why’s that? Because then birthdays aren't so close together. Ah, you mean because you both have birthdays so close? It's rather special having sibling birthdays so near to each other though, isn’t it? A double celebration. It means more cake. It does indeed mean more cake! Though, remember last year and the Monet themed party? That was a bit much, even for me. I liked the Monet cake! It had those little water lily flowers on it. It was… ambitious. I spent hours trying to pipe those tiny flowers on. Right, what about dinner? I was thinking pasta bake…or we could do something with those radishes I got from the market? No radishes! They’re spicy! I like radishes with butter. See, Aaron, Cindy appreciates a good radish. Honestly, you two. One minute complaining about the dentist, the next debating radishes. Speaking of things you're good at, how's the maths going? Hard. Times tables are really hard. They take practice, sweetie. But you’re getting there. Have you started thinking about what you want for your birthdays? I want a new art set. A  really  big one with everything.

Honestly, I’m still recovering from that roast yesterday. Your mum really outdid herself, didn’t she? I think I gained half a stone just looking at it. Oh, she always goes overboard. It's her love language, isn’t it? Feeding people until they physically can’t move. Though, to be fair, it  was  delicious. Did you manage to sneak any leftovers home? I tried! But your dad intercepted me with a Tupperware box and filled it to the brim. I’m pretty sure it’s mostly parsnips. Which, don’t get me wrong, are nice, but… parsnip overload. Dad and his parsnips, a classic pairing. How’s the flat looking after the weekend mayhem? Did you attempt to tackle the mountain of dishes? Ugh, don’t even. I did a quick sweep, got the worst of it, but it still feels… looming. I’m seriously considering just buying paper plates from now on. It’s more sustainable to just replace everything, honestly. Luna wasn’t helping, either. She decided the discarded gravy boat was a personal swimming pool. Typical Luna. That cat has zero shame. Barnaby’s been a bit of a terror too, demanding attention every five minutes. I practically tripped over him three times trying to get ready for work this morning. Being a SLT is exhausting, and then you come home to a furry dictator. Story of our lives. Speaking of work, how was your first week back? Still battling the vocal cords of the elderly? You make it sound so grim! It’s actually really rewarding. But yeah, lots of swallowing difficulties, a couple of strokes, and one man who was convinced his dentures were trying to escape. It’s… varied. What’s been happening in the world of copywriting? Still churning out ad copy for beige paint? Pretty much. Though, I did get assigned a campaign for a dog walking app. Slightly more exciting. I spent two hours researching the optimal length of a dog lead. My life is glamorous. I'm seriously starting to wonder if I should’ve just followed through with the Masters. Oh, don’t say that! You're good at what you do. And remember how stressed you were during the application process? It wasn’t for you, you said. I know, I know. It’s just… seeing your patient success stories, it feels like you’re actually  helping  people.

…and honestly, the sheer freedom of it! We’d cycle all the way to Bristol, maybe twenty miles, just on a whim. No helmets, of course, nobody bothered with those then. Just a packed lunch and off we’d go. It feels… astonishing now, looking back. Twenty miles on a bike? Good heavens, Margaret! You were a brave one. I remember being terrified of going down hills. Even now, the thought of it makes my stomach flip. It wasn’t so different up North, though the terrain was… less forgiving. More hills, generally. Though, admittedly, we weren’t cycling to Bristol. More like from one side of Manchester to the other, dodging trams. Trams! Now  there’s  a thing of the past. Speaking of past things… the NHS perks, eh? When I first qualified, you could practically live on them. Remember those sailing courses? Absolute madness, really. Oh, the sailing! I’d almost forgotten! And the 'lectures at sea' as you used to call them, Arthur? Honestly, I pictured you giving oral surgery on the deck of a yacht. Not quite! But there were a few… interesting incidents. A very seasick patient and a rather damp impression tray, I recall. Nowadays, you're lucky to get a free coffee. Though, I was looking at Prague the other day. Some unbelievable deals. Prague? Oh, I’ve always wanted to go. Is it as beautiful as they say? Stunning. Absolutely stunning. Charles Bridge, the Astronomical Clock… and the beer is cheap as chips. They do these little walking tours, all hidden courtyards and secret gardens. And bizarrely, if you know the right people, you can get into pretty much anything, even fully booked theatres or exhibitions. A friend of mine, a journalist, seems to have a key to the city. Sounds intriguing. Better than sitting around moaning about the solar farm. Did you all hear about that? Approved, apparently. Blight on the landscape, I say. I was disappointed. It’s prime agricultural land. Though, I suppose it’s the price of progress. Speaking of progress…have we finalised anything for the jive? That barn, Old Man Hemlock's place, is looking lovely now they've done it up. Old Man Hemlock’s barn? Yes, it's a good space. Bit rustic, but that suits the jive. They're putting in a proper sprung floor, which is essential. And apparently, they're hoping to get a license for live music.

Right, so we’re agreed – the Aussie sun is definitely impacting my brain cells. I’ve been staring at this whiteboard for an hour and all I’ve written is ‘EdTech’ in massive letters. It’s the jet lag, darling. And the novelty of house-sitting a place with a pool. Don't worry, brain cells recover. EdTech  is  broad though. We need to niche down. I was thinking about what’s missing, what I struggle with as a teacher… and it keeps coming back to engaging resources for visual learners. Visual learners, huh? Okay, I can get behind that. Loads of potential there. The problem I see is everyone’s doing video now. YouTube is flooded. How do we stand out? Just… better quality? Better quality is a baseline, isn’t it? It needs to be  different . I’ve been toying with the idea of curated case studies. Think historical events, literature, even scientific concepts… broken down and explained using moving image – not just documentaries, but animation, short films, even carefully selected clips from feature films. Interesting. So, like… a ‘71’ but used to explain the Troubles to a history class? We talked about that film the other night, actually. A really gritty, realistic portrayal. Could be powerful, if handled correctly. Exactly! ‘71’ is a fantastic example. Or, for a literature class, using scenes from a film adaptation of ‘Frankenstein’ to dissect the themes of creation and responsibility. It’s taking existing content and repurposing it with a very specific pedagogical angle. I like the repurposing angle. It avoids the massive cost of original production. The legal side would be a headache, though. Fair use, licensing… all that jazz. We’d need to be very careful. Absolutely. That's where my expertise comes in. I'm pretty familiar with copyright law in an educational context. And we’d focus on short clips, transformative use… building analysis  around  the footage, not just showing the footage. It's about providing a framework for critical thinking. Okay, so case studies… curated moving images… aimed at visual learners. What about the platform? YouTube feels… limiting. And the algorithm can bury good content. I was thinking a subscription model. A dedicated website. Maybe tiered access – free taster content, then paid subscriptions for full access to the library of case studies, plus accompanying teaching materials. Worksheets, discussion prompts, assessment ideas. The whole package. A membership site.

It’s funny, isn’t it? How different the sea is depending on where you are. I mean, North Norfolk – that’s bracing. It slaps you in the face, all grey and wild. Completely different to anything down South. Absolutely. Proper wild. I remember that trip to Cromer with your parents, the wind was… biblical. Salt spray everywhere, trying to hold onto your hat. My face felt like it was being sandblasted. Oh, God, yes! Mum was convinced she’d lost her dentures in a wave. Nearly caused a full-scale search operation. And then the South Coast… it’s almost… polite. All pastel shades and gentle lapping. Like a paddling pool for adults. Exactly! And warmer, obviously. Remember visiting Sarah and Ben in Brighton last summer? The sea was actually  pleasant . I even went for a swim. You and a swim? That’s news. You usually regard the ocean with deep suspicion. Well, it wasn’t  cold . And Ben was being particularly enthusiastic about paddleboarding, so I felt pressured. Honestly, felt like I was in a Jane Austen novel, all bathing machines and disapproving glances. Ben and his… hobbies. He's always got a new passion. Remember when he was obsessed with competitive cheese rolling? Oh, don’t even. The stories! He ended up with a sprained ankle and a profound respect for Gloucestershire hillsides. Poor Sarah had to nurse him for weeks. And the homemade cheese he was trying to perfect? Let's not forget the smell. It permeated their entire flat. It was… pungent. I swear, the postman started leaving parcels on the doorstep rather than risking a conversation. It's a good job Sarah is so patient. She is, isn’t she? They’re a good team, even when Ben is enthusiastically ruining his body for a slightly silly pursuit. Do you think they’ll ever move back up North? I don’t know. She misses her family, but he… he thrives in the bustle of the city. He needs the energy, I think. And the specialist cheese shops. Fair enough. Although, I suspect he could find specialist cheese shops anywhere if he really put his mind to it. That man has a nose for artisanal dairy products. You're not wrong. It's terrifying. Speaking of terrifying, did you hear from David recently? I haven't seen any of his Instagram posts in ages. No, not for a couple of weeks.

Oh my god, look at what she’s wearing! That dress is… a choice. What? The red one? It's a bit much for daytime TV, isn’t it? Like, you'd need to  be  the daytime TV show to pull that off. It's…bold. I think she’s trying for retro, but it's landing somewhere closer to ‘slightly terrifying auntie’ territory. The pattern clash is criminal. Criminal is right! Florals with stripes? Who even  thinks  of that? It’s like they just threw everything in a bag and said “make me a dress!” She's probably got a stylist. And the stylist is currently hiding under a desk somewhere, desperately rewriting their CV. You know, I saw a really cute skirt in the shops today. A-line, corduroy, mustard yellow. I was thinking about getting it for autumn. Ooh, mustard yellow is a good shout. Very on trend, isn’t it? You’d look lovely in that. What about tops with it? Definitely a cream or white roll neck. Or a dark green if you're feeling brave. Mustard and green are surprisingly good together. I was thinking cream, yeah. Or maybe a little black turtleneck? I've got one that's really versatile. Black would work, but cream feels more… autumnal, you know? Like pumpkin spice latte vibes. Speaking of autumnal vibes, are we still doing the shopping trip next weekend? I need to start thinking about layering pieces. I’m determined to finally master the art of the stylish scarf. Yes! Definitely. Saturday good for you both? We could hit up the vintage shops on Mill Road? I’ve been meaning to go for ages. Saturday's perfect. And YES to Mill Road. You always find the best bits there. I'm hoping for a good leather jacket. Mine’s looking a bit sad. Oh, Mill Road is dangerous for my bank account. I always end up buying something I definitely don’t need. But it’s  so  worth it. Same. I always go in with a list, and leave with a completely different pile of clothes. It’s a curse. Look! She’s changed outfits! Honestly, it's even worse now. What  is  that fringe jacket? No. Just… no. Someone please save us from this fashion disaster. It's like a costume party reject. I think I need a strong cup of tea after witnessing that.

Mum, look at this photo I took in art today. It’s supposed to be abstract, but Mr. Davies said it looks like a splattered raspberry. Oh, darling. It’s… vibrant. Very, very vibrant. What were you  going  for? I was trying to capture the feeling of being overwhelmed, you know? Like, all the pressure with the mock exams coming up. Oh, sweetie. That  does  sound overwhelming. Are you revising okay? Are you actually  doing  any revision, or just swirling paint around? Mum! I am! It’s just…history is awful. All those dates. It’s just memorising stuff, isn’t it? I don’t actually  understand  it. It’s about understanding the context, love. The ‘why’ behind the dates. But I get it. It's tough. What’s your biggest fear about the exams? Besides failing, obviously. Um… I think just… disappointing you. And Dad. You both want me to do well. Oh, honey, we just want you to  try  your best. That’s all we ask. Truly. Honestly. How was work today? Same old complaints from Mr. Henderson about the coffee machine? Probably. He complains about  everything . Speaking of complaints, Mrs. Peterson tried to tell me off today for having my headphones in. Said I looked ‘unapproachable’. Oh, Mrs. Peterson. She’s a character, isn't she? Thinks the world revolves around her geraniums. Honestly, some people. I had a right nightmare with a delivery driver. He insisted he’d delivered something to reception, but no one had signed for it. Went on for half an hour! Sounds stressful. You need a holiday. Have you booked anything yet? We're still looking. Dad keeps changing his mind. One minute he wants to go to Scotland, the next he's talking about a cruise. Honestly, I'd rather stay home and read. I’ve started this new book – it’s a historical fiction, set in the Tudor period. Really gripping. Ooh, interesting. I’m trying to get into reading more. I saw some TikToks about this book called ‘The Seven Husbands of Evelyn Hugo’. Have you heard of it? I have, actually! A friend recommended it to me. Said it's brilliantly written. Have you seen Ricky Gervais’ new special? No, is it good? He's so controversial, though. Some of his jokes… He  is  boundary pushing, definitely. But he’s also incredibly funny. I was crying with laughter. Although, admittedly, some of it did make me feel slightly uncomfortable.

Right then, lovely to see you both. Cup of tea? I’ve just put the kettle on. Oh, that’d be lovely, Arthur. Thank you. Bit of a trek from Harrow, mind you! Though the traffic wasn’t too bad, surprisingly. Yeah, wasn’t bad at all coming from Brum. Though, honestly, watching the state of that M6…makes you wonder who signed off on the roadworks. Nightmare. Roadworks are always a mess. Always. Remember old man Hemmings down the lane? Tried to re-tarmac his drive himself. Looked like a badger had been at it when he finished. Shabby workmanship, that was. Oh, Arthur! You always have a story. So, how are you keeping? Still wrestling with that application form for the bowling club membership? Wrestling is putting it mildly. It’s a blasted thing! Asking for my mother’s maiden name, for goodness sake. What’s that got to do with bowls? And then there's the bit about ‘digital literacy’. What even  is  that? It’s basically how comfortable you are using computers, Dad. I could take a look for you if you like? I’ve got a bit of experience filling in forms, what with being a teacher…and dealing with parents. Would you mind, lad? That’d be a godsend. Honestly, it's enough to keep a man up all night. And I  have  been up all night, actually. That cockerel next door. Cock-a-doodle-doo at 4 AM! Drives me mad. Oh, that cockerel. I heard it when I walked past yesterday. Dreadful! Poor thing probably thinks it’s doing a good job. Still, doesn’t make it any easier to sleep. You'd think someone would do something about it. Speaking of noisy things, little Tom Wilkins in Year 3… honestly. He's a handful. Currently fixated on building a fort out of chairs during maths. Problem children, eh? They've always been around. Remember young Derek Plunkett? Used to steal plums from Mrs. Higgins’ orchard. Little terror. Oh, Derek! He ended up a dentist, didn't he? Imagine that! Funny how things turn out. Look, while we’re on the subject of things turning out… have you seen those baby birds in the nest in your apple tree, Arthur? I have! Little cheepers they are. Mum and Dad are working hard bringing them worms. It’s a miracle, really, when you think about it.

Honestly, Arthur, the thought of it all is quite exhausting. Just… the sheer logistics. You’re overthinking it, Margaret. You always do. It’ll be wonderful, having Isla here. Truly. Wonderful for  whom , Arthur? Wonderful for me, shuffling around trying to make space, dealing with the inevitable culture shock, and, frankly, the added expense? She’s been in Australia for fifteen years! Fifteen! She’s built a life there. She  wanted  to come here. She said so, quite clearly. And she’s not a child anymore, Margaret. She’s a capable woman. She's not expecting you to run everything for her. But she's my daughter, aren’t you listening? And she’s…adjusting. She's leaving a sunny climate, friends, a job she enjoys…for rainy Brighton and… well, us. And the National Health Service, bless its heart. Oh, here we go. Don't start on the NHS again. It served you well enough. And Brighton isn't  that  bad. The pier is lovely, you know. The pier is full of seagulls and sticky toffee apples, Arthur. Not exactly a sophisticated welcome to Britain. And she’s used to…space. Houses in Perth are enormous. Here, we’re crammed in. I’ve already started shifting things around, trying to clear the spare room and… it’s just depressing. We've managed perfectly well in this house for thirty years, Margaret. A bit of shifting won't kill us. We can always get rid of some of your…collections. My ‘collections’ are memories, Arthur! Each one represents something! And it’s not just the space. It’s… I’m worried she’ll be unhappy. What if she regrets this? What if she quickly realises she’s made a mistake? She wouldn’t have come if she thought that. She said she misses family, she wants to be closer. She wants… well, you, Margaret. She’s missed  you . She calls. We video chat. It’s not the same. And what about finding work? She’s a graphic designer. The market is flooded here! She might end up flipping burgers. Now you’re being dramatic. She’s brilliant at what she does. She’ll find something. And even if it takes a while, we'll help. That’s what family does. I suppose. It’s just… it feels like such a big upheaval. After all these years of quiet, of just us… it’s a shock to the system.

So, did you catch much of the Scottish referendum coverage yesterday? Absolute nail-biter, wasn't it? Nail-biter is putting it mildly! I was glued to the television, frankly. Thought for a good while there it was going to be a ‘yes’. Quite a relief, I think, for a lot of people, though I can understand the disappointment north of the border. It’s a messy situation, all round. It really is. And the fallout… the political manoeuvring already begun is exhausting just to watch. Makes you wonder what the next few years will hold. Anyway, enough about politics depressing us both. How did your interview go on Friday? You were a bit cagey about it afterwards. Oh, the interview. Right. Well… it was… an experience. It wasn't terrible, not terrible at all, but I don’t think I shone, if I’m honest. They were very keen on someone with more experience leading large, funded research projects. Which, as you know, isn’t exactly my forte. Ah, bugger. That’s a shame. You’ve got plenty of experience, just not  that  kind of experience. Who was interviewing you, anyway? Was it old Professor Davies? He’s a bit of a stickler. It was Davies, and his deputy, Dr. Albright. Albright was the more… probing, shall we say. Kept asking about quantifiable outcomes. I felt like I was back in undergraduate statistics. Davies was mostly nodding and making encouraging noises, which didn't exactly fill me with confidence. He’s utterly hopeless at reading a room, that man. Sounds about right. He’s a brilliant academic, no doubt, but people skills… not his strong suit. Look, don’t beat yourself up about it. There’ll be other opportunities. Besides, you’re a valuable asset to the department as you are. You’re very kind, old boy. I appreciate that. Although, truthfully, I’m beginning to wonder if I should just stick it out until retirement and avoid the whole job-hunting circus. It's rather draining. Speaking of draining… how's your daughter? Still loving university? She is! Absolutely thriving, actually. She's joined the debating society, apparently. Can you believe it? Little Emily, the shrinking violet, now arguing the toss about… well, everything. She was telling me all about her latest debate – something about the ethics of AI. It went on for hours. Good for her. It's wonderful when they find something they're passionate about.

Right, so the spoon goes…no, absolutely not, Leo! It needs to be balanced, not hanging off the edge. Honestly, you'd think a chef would understand balance! It’s harder than it looks! And it’s a  mousetrap game , not a physics lesson, Mum. He’s got a point, darling. Though, admittedly, this elaborate Rube Goldberg machine you’re designing is…ambitious. Are we aiming for a Nobel Prize or just to get a biscuit to fall into a cup? It's very clever, actually. The potential energy transfer is quite beautiful. Though I do worry about the cat getting involved. Jasper has a…history. Jasper deserves a Nobel Prize, honestly. The sheer audacity of his naps is inspiring. Speaking of audacious, remember Uncle George trying to build one of these in Florida? With coconuts? Oh,  don't  remind me. That was a disaster. He nearly took out Mrs. Henderson's prize-winning hibiscus. And the sheer number of ants… He was convinced it would be a huge success. So American, that whole “bigger is better” mentality. He always wanted everything to be a spectacle. He did love a performance. He used to tell us stories about American kids, didn’t he? How obsessed they were with…what was it? Competitive hotdog eating? Yeah! And state fairs. He described them as terrifying but amazing. Apparently, everything is deep-fried. Even the butter. Deep-fried butter?! Seriously? I’ve never understood the attraction. The portion sizes alone…it’s quite shocking. I spent a summer working at a library near Philadelphia. The children’s reading groups were enormous. And so…loud. Loud? Compared to Leo dismantling the kitchen? A different kind of loud. More…enthusiastic. And aggressively patriotic. Everything was about America being the best. It was charming, initially, but after a while… It must have been a culture shock. You’re used to British understatement. I always found the American healthcare system a bit baffling, from what George described. The expense, the insurance…it all seemed so complicated. It’s a constant worry for people over there, isn't it? I had to deal with a colleague who nearly bankrupted herself trying to cover her son's medical bills. I briefly considered applying for a position with the embassy in Washington a few years back. Good money, but ultimately… You wouldn’t have lasted a week. Too much enthusiasm required.

Right, okay, so… operation ‘wardrobe refresh’ was largely successful. Oh really? Did you bankrupt us entirely? I heard the rustling of carrier bags from the hallway. Don’t be dramatic. It wasn't  that  bad. Mostly things on sale. And I really needed some… well, you know. New things. New things? Last time I checked, your wardrobe was threatening to explode. What prompted this sudden urge for retail therapy? It’s not retail therapy! It’s… sensible acquisition. The conference next month, remember? And I realised I have absolutely nothing appropriate to wear. Everything feels… stale. Or covered in cat hair. Or both. The conference in Shanghai? You have a perfectly good navy suit. Navy is so… predictable. And it wrinkles. Immediately. I got a really lovely teal dress. It’s silk, so it drapes nicely. And a cream blouse, really soft. Teal and cream. Sounds… bright. You usually go for more muted tones. I’m branching out! Trying to be a bit more adventurous. I also got a really nice pair of trousers – wide-legged, black, incredibly comfortable. They practically feel like pyjamas. Practical  and  stylish. Excellent. Did you manage to resist the lure of shoes? Because that’s usually where things get dicey. Maybe… a small pair. They were on sale! And they’re incredibly versatile. Black block heels. You can wear them with everything. "Small pair"? That sounds suspiciously like code for "at least three pairs". Okay, fine. Two pairs. One is a little more… sparkly. For evenings. Sparkly? You’re going to blind the entire academic delegation. Don't be ridiculous. It’s subtle sparkle. It’s… sophisticated sparkle. And I needed something for dinner, didn't I? We're going to that nice restaurant near the Bund, remember? Oh, right. That  is  a bit more of an occasion. Still, let's have a look at this haul, shall we? Before our credit card statement arrives. Alright, alright. Don't judge. They're much nicer in person, honestly. And they were a  bargain . I'm not judging, darling. Just curious. And slightly apprehensive. Now, where's my coffee? This requires serious evaluation. Coming right up! Then prepare to be amazed by my impeccable fashion choices. I highly doubt that, but I’m willing to be entertained. Just you wait. I always do. I'll get the coffee started. Perfect. Do you have anything planned this evening? The old admin for tomorrow, but I'm sure I can get it done tomorrow before lunchtime.

Ah, that was a match and a half, wasn’t it? Jesus, the last ten minutes… I thought we were done for. It was brilliant! That try by Mack Hansen was  amazing . He just flew past everyone. It was a bit stressful watching, I have to admit. My heart was going a mile a minute. Though, honestly, anything with a lot of shouting and running around keeps me awake these days. Aye, it was a good show. Reminded me of the days when my young’uns used to be glued to the rugby. Your wee lad's getting quite the taste for it, isn't he? Yeah, I love it. We had a rugby taster session at school today, actually. I got to try tackling—it’s harder than it looks! Harder than it looks alright! It’s a proper man’s game. Though, you wouldn’t know it looking at some of the fellas playing these days. More about speed than brute force now, I think. Speaking of young lads and games… Oisin, darling, you need to finish your peas. And then, cards. Auntie Moira brought a lovely card for your birthday. We need to get everyone to sign it. Okay, okay, peas coming. Is it the one with the dinosaur on the front? The very one. Your grandmother chose it. She’s terribly proud of you, you know. Especially now that you’re getting into sports. It’s good to see you active. It is. Better than staring at those screens all day. Though, I suppose even rugby gets shown on the telly these days. When I was teaching, sports day was the highlight of the year! Rounders, egg and spoon races… simple joys. Right, right. Simple joys. We should do something like that with Oisin, more often. Maybe a picnic in the park this weekend? That sounds lovely. But first, cards. And then, bedtime. He’s yawning already. It's getting late. Can I have five more minutes? Please? Five minutes, then straight to bed. And no arguing. Once he's tucked up, maybe we could go outside and have a look at the stars? It's a beautiful clear night. I always loved showing the children the constellations. Oh, that's a wonderful idea, Moira! I've been meaning to get a telescope. Maybe we could look for planets? Absolutely. After the cards and Oisin's bedtime, we can all head outside.

Honestly, I’m starting to feel like all I talk about is nappies and sleep schedules now. It’s… consuming. Oh, you’ve joined the club! It's lovely to hear little Leo's doing well though, isn’t it? He sounds like a little cherub. He is, when he’s not screaming for a feed. My mum keeps saying it flies by, but at 3am when he’s decided sleep is for the weak, it feels eternal. How’s your sister, by the way? Still loving London? She is! Though she’s actually starting to look at places a bit further out. Apparently, the flat hunt is… brutal. She wants something a bit bigger, maybe with a garden. Says she’s realised she needs space for… well, future possibilities. You know how she is. Oh, definitely. She always did have a five-year plan mapped out. Makes me feel a bit chaotic, to be honest. Have you heard anything about that new development near Grandchester Meadows? I saw a leaflet and it looked… nice. Oh, the one with the riverside views? I think my aunt mentioned it. She said it's seriously expensive though. London prices creeping outwards, I suppose. Are you and Tom thinking about moving anytime soon? Not yet. We’re quite happy where we are for now, small as it is. Although… I’m starting to realise Leo is going to need his own dedicated space eventually. Tom keeps joking about converting the shed! We were having a clear out in the loft yesterday, though, and I unearthed a bunch of clothes I haven't worn in ages. Proper vintage stuff. Ooh, send them my way! Seriously. I'm trying to avoid buying loads of new stuff and just reusing what I have. And your taste is always brilliant. Remember that floral dress you wore to Sarah’s wedding? I was so jealous. Oh, that one! It’s probably lurking somewhere… I’ll definitely have a sort and send anything that fits. You've got a much better eye for styling things than I do anyway. Although, I'm definitely dressing for comfort these days. Tracksuits are my friend. Tell me about it! Comfort is key. It’s so strange, though, isn't it? We were talking about learning Italian just a few years ago, planning that trip to Rome, and now… it’s all baby talk and house hunting.

Right, so then old man Hemmings, he’s going on about how “proper Bedfordshire folk” don’t pronounce the ‘h’ in ‘house’. Proper ridiculous, innit? Like, who cares? Oh, Hemmings. He’s a lost cause, that one. Still banging on about the old ways. It’s just dialect, man. Natural evolution. My nan used to drop her ‘h’s all the time. My yiayia, she didn’t even  have  an ‘h’ to drop. Everything was just…different. Proper Cyprus stuff. Though she picked up a bit of Luton slang over the years, bless her. Used to call everything "chuffed". Chuffed? That’s northern, isn’t it? I thought that was Yorkshire. Nah, it’s spread. Luton’s a melting pot. You get a bit of everything, especially with the airport. You hear accents here you wouldn't believe. Remember that Finnish guy who used to come into the pub? Oh god, yeah! The one who tried to order a pint of…what was it… “sadness”? Thought he was asking for a dark beer. Sadness! That’s brilliant. Speaking of pints, I’m thinking of getting back into learning guitar. Dust off the old six-string. Good on ya! I always admired people who can play. My attempts ended with a lot of frustration and stringed fingers. You still doing artwork? Saw some of your stuff online, looked wicked. Yeah, still plugging away. Freelance stuff mostly. Keeps me busy. Pays the bills, sort of. It’s just…finding the clients is the killer. And then dealing with the ones who think graphic design is just ‘messing about on the computer’. Tell me about it. Gardening’s the same. People think it’s just mowing a lawn. It’s a science, man! Soil composition, pruning techniques… and the sheer physical graft. I'm considering a bit of MMA training actually, for self-defence, you know? Seen a few… questionable characters about lately. MMA? Serious? That’s a bit intense, isn’t it? Though I get it. Confidence and all that. I've been trying to learn some basic self-defense techniques just from YouTube. It feels a bit pathetic. YouTube is alright for a start, I guess. Though nothing beats proper training. My cousin did a course, says it’s changed his whole outlook. He used to be a right pushover. Now he's…calm, but you wouldn’t want to cross him. Speaking of crossing people, anyone fancy a game of Monopoly later?

Right, onions are sizzling. You okay to chop the peppers while I do this? Yeah, no problem. Though honestly, this kitchen is freezing. Feels like winter again. It is a bit nippy, isn't it? Should we put the heating on? Nah, let's not. Trying to save a bit, remember? Especially with… well, everything. Speaking of saving, have you thought any more about getting a smaller car? We’ve been over this, haven’t we? I  like  the Mini. It’s fun to drive. I know, I know. It is a nice little car. But the insurance is killing us, and the petrol… Honestly, the commute is costing a fortune. I'm spending almost £200 a month just getting to and from Peterborough. Okay, £200 is a lot. But you  could  cycle a couple of days a week? You always said the cycle path is pretty good. It is, when it's not pouring with rain. And when I don’t have to carry a load of project documents with me! Seriously though, a more economical car would make a huge difference. Something like a… a Toyota Yaris? A Yaris? That sounds… sensible. A bit  too  sensible, perhaps? Sensible is good! We’re trying to be responsible adults, remember? Think of the holiday we could afford if we weren’t throwing money at a car. You are relentless. I suppose you’re right. It's just… I feel like I’ve only just paid it off. Getting rid of it feels like a waste. It's not a waste if it saves us money long term. We could look at selling it privately, get a bit more for it than going through a dealership. My mate, Liam, sold his old Ford like that. Got a really good price. Hmm, okay. That's a thought. Maybe we could browse AutoTrader tonight, just to get an idea of prices? No commitment. Deal! And while we’re being responsible, I’ve been looking at energy providers. Think we could switch and save a bit on the bills? You're on a roll! Okay, okay. Let’s have dinner first. All this talk of saving is making me hungry.
