Actually, remember that time your old Fiesta broke down on the A1? Don't remind me! That was a disaster. I had to call the AA at like midnight. And then wait two hours in the freezing cold.

Right, now then, love, you’ve had a good brew, haven’t you? Grandad, more biscuits? You look like you’re rationing yourself again. Never rationing, lass. Just savouring. These ginger nuts are proper good, they are. Not like them factory ones, all crumbly and tasteless. He says that about  everything  factory made, doesn’t he? Says the butter doesn’t taste the same. Honestly, Arthur, you’d think they put sawdust in it. Well, they practically do! It’s all additives and… stuff. Yorkshire butter, that’s what you want. From a proper farm. Can I just quickly ask about the Wi-Fi password? Mr. Henderson wants us to upload the history project tonight. Oh, bless you. It’s the usual, love. “YorkshireRose2023”, all one word. Though, honestly, I’m thinking of changing it. Everyone seems to know it now! Changing it to what, then? “Arthur’sGingerNuts”? Now you’re talking! That’s a secure password. Nobody’d guess that. Don’t encourage him, Doris. Honestly. Anyway, are you sure you’ve got everything for your rugby training, lad? Warm coat, gloves… it’s turning nippy out there. Yeah, Mum, all good. Got my kitbag packed. I’m meeting Tom at the bus stop. Good. And text me when you get there, won’t you? Just so I know you’re safe. This traffic has been awful lately. It’s always awful around here. Used to be lovely and quiet, used to be. Before they built that bypass. Bypass didn’t solve anything, did it? Just moved the traffic further down the road. That’s progress for you, eh? Speaking of progress, I’m trying to work out the heating schedule. It’s costing a fortune. I think I need to lower the temperature overnight. You’re always freezing, though, aren’t you, love? You have to be warm. Old bones need warmth. I’ve got me thermal vest! And a hot water bottle. I’m set. The main thing is to try and be sensible. Those electricity bills are frightening. I was marking GCSE papers today, and honestly, some of them couldn't work out percentages! You’d think they’d at least know how to figure out a discount on a jumper… Don’t tell me you had another one trying to divide by zero? Oh, you know it! At least two this year. They just… don’t  think . It’s a lost art.

Right, so Captain Blackheart’s ship has just run aground on a coral reef, and… oh, for goodness sake, Leo, are you trying to eat your pirate eye patch? But it smells like…chocolate! It  looks  like black liquorice, darling, and absolutely does not taste like chocolate. Honestly! Elsie, are you drawing a map? A treasure map? Mmm-hmm! It’s to find the sparkly jewels! They’re hidden on… erm… Rainbow Island! Rainbow Island! Excellent. Very creative. Now, after we rescue Captain Blackheart from the reef, we need to think about Shakespeare week. It’s starting Monday, isn’t it? Shakespeare? Is that the man with the frilly collar? That’s the one! He wrote lots of plays, very famous ones. We might even try and go to Stratford-upon-Avon if the weather’s good. Wouldn’t that be exciting? Is there a pirate ship in Stratford? Probably not a pirate ship, sweetheart. But there’s Shakespeare’s house, and the Royal Shakespeare Theatre… we could see a play! Maybe  A Midsummer Night’s Dream ? It has fairies and magic in it. Ooh, fairies! Can we wear fairy wings? Absolutely. We can dress up! And speaking of exciting things, remember the circus workshop we booked? The one in the real circus tent? YES! I want to be a trapeze artist! I’m going to swing really high! That’s wonderful. Elsie, what will  you  be at the circus? I want to ride an elephant! A sparkly pink elephant! A sparkly pink elephant. That sounds… spectacular. Right, who wants some pineapple? It’s looking a bit like pirate treasure, all golden and chunked up. Pineapple! Yes! Are we doing the Easter pictures tomorrow? We are! We're going to decorate eggs and then I’ll take photos of you two looking all Easter-y. Remember the little bunny ears? I want glitter on my egg! Lots and lots of glitter! Lots and lots of glitter it is. Honestly, this house will be covered in glitter for weeks. Elsie, did you finish that stop-motion animation you were working on? The one with the Lego pirates? Almost! Captain Bluebeard needs to find the treasure, but he keeps losing his sword. I can help him find it! I’m good at finding lost things. That’s very kind of you, Leo. Maybe you can be Captain Bluebeard’s first mate. Now, eat your pineapple before it sails away like a pirate ship!

Honestly, Roger, you wouldn’t  believe  the fuss. Jeddah to Cyprus, I tell you. Perfectly sensible plan, clear skies… or so we thought. Sensible? Dorothy, attempting to sail the Red Sea in a… what was it, a thirty-foot yacht? With Bernard at the helm, no less? Ah, but it’s the  story  that matters, isn’t it? Bernard always did have a talent for attracting trouble. Remind me again, what was the official charge? Attempting to leave port without proper clearance, as I recall. And, crucially, ignoring repeated requests from the harbourmaster to… well, stay put. Something about unseasonal winds. Though the real issue, I suspect, was Bernard’s insistence on a full English breakfast  on  the deck just moments before setting off. It wasn’t just the breakfast! It was the fact they didn’t understand we had provisions! They thought we were trying to smuggle something. Goodness knows what. I tried to explain, in my best Arabic, that we simply wanted to sail to Cyprus. And they responded with…armed guards? I heard you ended up in a cell. Not a cell, precisely. More of a holding room. Very clean, surprisingly. But filled with bewildered-looking fishermen and a rather insistent camel. The camel kept trying to eat my handbag. A camel! Only you, Dorothy. You manage to get arrested with a camel involved. This is prime material for your next book. You  are  writing another one, aren't you? I’m toying with the idea. It’s rather difficult, you see. Getting the tone right. It wasn't frightening, exactly, just… extraordinarily inconvenient. And hot. Terribly hot. Saudi Arabia and its peculiar charms. I remember you telling me about the difficulty obtaining even a thimbleful of sherry while teaching there. Ah yes, the restrictions. Completely different to my stint in Spain. Wine flowed like water, practically. One had to be careful not to get carried away, naturally. Though a little Rioja with tapas never hurt anyone. It's all relative, isn’t it? My sister-in-law spent a year in Iran during the seventies. She told me they used to distill alcohol from dates. Apparently it was potent, and strictly forbidden, so naturally everyone made it. Dates, you say? That actually sounds rather appealing. Better than some of the… concoctions I was offered in Jeddah. They had this local drink made from fermented milk. Honestly, it tasted like sour socks.

Honestly, the state of that bathroom this morning… I don’t know what goes on in there. It looked like a bomb had hit it. Oh, tell me about it. Remember when Liam was that age? Exactly the same. Everything ends up… everywhere. It’s a teenage boy thing, I reckon. No spatial awareness, no concept of ‘putting things back.’ I  did  put the empty shower gel bottle in the bin! Yes, dear, well done. But the clothes on the floor, the wet towel draped over the… everything else. It's just relentless. It is a phase. They eventually learn. Mostly. Though Liam’s bathroom still needs a good scrub when he comes home from uni. Speaking of which, have you started looking at holiday options for August yet? A little. I was thinking maybe somewhere in Cornwall? Nice beaches, relatively easy to get to. Though honestly, part of me just wants to stay here and avoid the stress of travelling with a teenager. Cornwall would be… okay. Can we take the bodyboards? Possibly. We’ll see. It depends on your behaviour between now and then. And whether you promise to at least  attempt  to tidy your room occasionally. You’ve got to offer incentives, you know. Remember when I used to bribe Liam with extra pocket money if he helped with the gardening? Worked a treat. Hmm, tempting. Though I’m trying to instill a sense of responsibility, not just rewarding him for basic chores. He needs to start thinking about work experience, doesn't he? It's looming. Ugh. Work experience. Ms. Davies said we need to start thinking about it. It’s so boring trying to find stuff. Everything’s either stacking shelves or helping in a charity shop. Now, that’s not true. Liam did work experience at a garage once. Got covered head-to-toe in grease. He hated it, of course, but it was  something . I was hoping he might find something a bit more…creative. He’s quite good with computers, could maybe volunteer somewhere helping with IT. I’ve been having a look online. It's finding something suitable and within travelling distance that's the tricky part. Actually…Emily’s dad works with computers. He builds websites and stuff. Maybe I could ask him? That’s a brilliant idea! See? Sometimes things just fall into place. Speaking of Emily… how are things going with her?

Honestly, this scenery is unreal. Like, absolutely stunning. Didn’t realise Croatia was  this  green. It is lovely, isn’t it? Much nicer than the motorway back home. And the air smells… clean. Not like Bolton sometimes, you know? Everything smells of diesel and chips. Can we stop for ice cream soon? I'm starving. We had a massive breakfast, Liam. Though, yes, we can look for a gelateria in the next town. This whole truffle thing is making me hungry again, actually. Oh, speaking of truffles, did I tell you about that chef I follow on Instagram? He does a truffle mac and cheese.  Truffle mac and cheese . It’s obscene. Obscene is right. Truffles are wasted on mac and cheese, love. They need something… elegant. A proper risotto, maybe. Or shaved over pasta. My client, David, he’s a bit of a foodie. Went on and on about a truffle hunt he did in Italy last year. Said it was life-changing. Cost him a fortune, naturally. Sounds like something Mark would be into. Remember Mark and his… everything being artisanal? Oh, Mark. Honestly, he'd have a nervous breakdown if he saw me having a cigarette. Though, to be fair, I’m trying to cut down. It’s just… holidays and having a smoke. It goes hand-in-hand. Gran, you told me they were really bad for you! I  am  trying to stop, darling! One a day isn’t going to kill me. It’s stress relief, okay? Dealing with expectant mothers all day is…a lot. You’re a saint, honestly. Dealing with all that. Reminds me, saw something fascinating on TV the other night about stem cell research. Apparently, they’re making huge breakthroughs with treating complications in pregnancy. Oh yeah? That’s amazing! It's mad how quickly science is moving. Feels like yesterday we were all freaking out about Dolly the sheep. Who’s Dolly the sheep? Oh, you wouldn't remember. It was a big thing when we were kids – the first mammal cloned from an adult cell. It's all a bit scary when you think about it, isn’t it? Still, good to see advancements that can help people. Speaking of helping people, did you hear old Mr. Henderson’s grandson is off to university in America on a football scholarship? Really? Good for him. That’s fantastic. Shame about the state of English football at the moment though.

Honestly, this canteen food is…an experience, isn’t it? I think I’ve identified at least four different shades of beige on my plate. You’re being kind. It’s functional, I suppose. Fuel for the afternoon. Though I’m starting to suspect the ‘chicken’ is actually tofu in disguise. Definitely tofu. I tried to spear a piece with my fork and it just…slid off. Like trying to catch smoke. Oh god, yes! Exactly. I’m clinging to the hope that the salad bar will offer some redemption. Although, judging by the wilted lettuce, that's a long shot. So, how's the dialect data coming along, Amelia? Still drowning in recordings of Norfolk vowels? Pretty much. It's fascinating, genuinely, but transcription is…slow. Especially when people decide to just trail off mid-sentence, or slur everything into one long sound. You wouldn’t believe the number of “hmmms” and “ahhs” I’ve had to code for. Sounds intense. I’m still mostly just making spreadsheets and chasing people for updates on the Peterson project. Less intellectually stimulating, let's say. Though, I did manage to convince Malcolm to finally approve the budget for the new server. Small victories. Nice one, Ben! That’s a proper win. Malcolm’s notoriously tight-fisted with the funds. I’m currently battling the algorithm on the new ad campaign. It keeps trying to target 70-year-olds with gaming laptops. It's… challenging. Oh, that’s brilliant! The algorithm clearly hasn’t grasped target demographics. Sounds about right. The AI revolution is clearly still a work in progress. Are you two heading to the Arts Festival this weekend? I saw they’ve got a photography exhibition on, thought it might be good. I was thinking about it. I’ve been meaning to get out more. Uni life gets a bit…claustrophobic sometimes, you know? Just bouncing between the office and my flat. I'm definitely up for it! I need a break from phonemes and spectrograms. A bit of visual stimulus sounds perfect. Plus, I heard there's a decent gin bar nearby. Excellent! Gin is always a good plan. We could grab tickets for that film screening too, the one about the Cambridge punting history? Oh, that sounds… incredibly Cambridge. I'm in. Anything to lean into the stereotype, right? Absolutely. Embrace the punting. It's practically a requirement for living here.

Right, so are you absolutely sure about the directions, love? It all looks a bit… uniform out here. Fields and fields and more fields. Positive, Auntie Carol. Google Maps says another five kilometres, then a left turn onto a little side road. Apparently, Kasia’s place is practically hidden. She says everyone gets lost the first time. Hidden is one thing, driving into a ditch is another! Honestly, this campervan is lovely, but it’s not exactly built for navigating Polish farm tracks. Are you sure we’ve got enough clearance? Relax, it’ll be fine. I checked the reviews of the campsite Kasia recommended, and someone specifically mentioned getting a larger vehicle down that road. Plus, I’m a pretty good driver now, remember? Been doing this for a couple of years, trekking around Europe with students. Trekking around Europe with students is very different to a Polish backroad in a borrowed campervan, dear. Though, good for you, being so adventurous. It just…it feels a long way from Cambridge, doesn’t it? It is a long way! Which is the point, isn’t it? Kasia’s been going on about this for months, wanting us to come and see her new garden. And honestly, after the last year, a bit of Polish countryside is exactly what we need. Yes, well, the countryside is nice. I’m more concerned about this ‘little side road’. Is it… paved? I think so? The satellite view wasn’t super clear. But Kasia said it's generally okay, just bumpy in places. We'll take it slow. And if we  do  end up in a ditch, at least it’ll be a scenic ditch. Always the optimist. Right, well, let's just hope it’s not a particularly muddy ditch. This borrowed campervan’s owner would have my hide. He’s a lovely man, but very particular about his vehicle. Don't worry, we'll be careful. Did you remember to pack the Polish phrasebook? Kasia said her English isn't brilliant when she's explaining complicated things about fertiliser and… beetroot. Oh, yes, it’s in the little bag beside you. Though I suspect 'Where is the nearest shop?’ and ‘Do you accept card?’ will be the extent of my Polish vocabulary this trip. That’ll probably cover most emergencies! Actually, she mentioned there’s a little market in Tarnow on Saturday. We could stock up on pierogi.

Honestly, that was a dodgy call. They’ve been letting Villa play far too easily, haven’t they? You’d think with all the money they’ve splashed, they’d be… more dominant. Aye, a bit. But listen, speaking of money splashing, did you see the new Liverpool kit? Absolutely dreadful. That colour… it’s like someone spilled a pint of Guinness on a white shirt. No way! Really? I haven’t even looked. I avoid looking at football strips these days. It's just…corporate greed on nylon, isn’t it? They churn them out every year, make a fortune, and half the time they’re objectively awful. Objectively is a strong word, but… yeah. This one’s pushing it. And the sponsor. Another betting company. Honestly, it's relentless. When did football just become one giant advert? It's been a slow creep, hasn't it? Remember when it was breweries on the shirts? At least that felt a bit… local. Now it's all global gambling conglomerates and vaguely defined 'financial services'. Exactly! And they pay these players millions to  wear  the logos. It’s just… baffling. Makes you wonder what’s actually driving the sport these days. Is it passion, or just revenue? Probably revenue, if we’re being realistic. Though, I reckon there's a tipping point. People are getting fed up with it. They  will  switch off. Maybe. Though, people seem to switch off and then switch back on for the big tournaments. It's a weird cycle. Speaking of things people shouldn't be able to have too much of… I'm craving a McDonald’s. Oh, don’t even! We literally just had a proper dinner. You're always craving McDonald’s! I know, I know. It’s a weakness. A terrible, French fry-filled weakness. I was thinking a McChicken meal, and maybe some… onion rings. Don't judge. I'm judging, but lightly. It's…comfort food, isn’t it? Something reliably awful. Like some of those football strips. Precisely! It's the reliably awful things in life that really hit the spot sometimes. Though, if Liverpool are going to keep playing in Guinness-coloured shirts, I might have to take up a different hobby altogether. Maybe take up decoupage with me? We could decoupage footballs… onto cardboard. And then cover them in betting company logos. A meta-commentary on the state of the game.

Honestly, it’s just… draining, you know? Another day, another rejection. And then having to explain  again  to the Jobcentre why I haven’t magically secured employment. They just don’t get it, do they? It’s not like jobs are falling out of the sky. Did you tell ‘em about the online course you started? Yeah, of course. They said it “doesn’t count as actively seeking work.” Seriously? It’s boosting my skills! They just want tick boxes filled, innit? I swear, sometimes I think they enjoy making it difficult. They do. Pure bureaucracy. Makes you wonder where all the money goes, though, doesn’t it? When they’re making life a misery for people genuinely trying. It's infuriating. It is. And then Liam was on about how Uncle Barry spent his inheritance already. The whole lot. Just… gone. What?! All of it? He only got that when Gran died, didn't he? That was a decent bit of money. Apparently. Liam said he blew it on… well, a combination of stuff. A new car, “investments” which are probably just a scam, and… expensive takeaways. Typical Barry. Always had his head in the clouds. Still, his money, I suppose. But honestly, it’s just… irresponsible. I know, right? It's just… it feels like some people get handed things on a plate and squander them, while others are fighting just to get by. I'm even looking at reducing the gas and electric. Don’t do that, love. You need to keep warm. We’ll figure something out. Speaking of figuring things out, I was thinking about taking the kids on a little day trip soon. Maybe Brighton. Oh, that sounds nice. They’d love that. Bit pricey getting the train though, wouldn’t it? Especially with all of us. Yeah, it’s a killer. I was looking at deals online, trying to find some off-peak returns. It’s just… getting them all organised is a nightmare. Remember when I tried to take Maisie to London and completely misread the platform numbers? Oh god, yes! And you were convinced you were on the right train until you saw a bloke with a totally different destination on his newspaper! I swear his face was priceless. Actually, I think I may have accidentally stared at him for too long. He looked a bit… well, a bit offended. I thought he was one race, and then he started talking and… oh never mind.

Honestly, Doreen, you wouldn’t believe the traffic getting here this morning. Satnav took me the scenic route… through two villages and a farm! Oh, you and your sat nav, Annie. They’re a blessing and a curse, aren’t they? Mine tries to send me down footpaths sometimes, bless it. Footpaths! Honestly. Back in my day, we  knew  the roads. Didn't need any fancy machines telling us where to go. Peterborough wasn't half as busy then, mind you. You could get anywhere in ten minutes. Ten minutes? You’re having a laugh, Mum! Even now, it takes me that long to get across town during rush hour. It's ridiculous. Did you see that news report about the plane crash yesterday? Oh, awful, wasn't it? Poor souls. Makes you think, doesn't it? All that technology… and still these things happen. Horrible. Absolutely horrible. Reminds me of when… oh, never mind. Too long ago. Sad times, sad times. Are you having a good lunch, Annie? I noticed you didn’t touch your quiche. It was lovely, Mum, honestly. Just not terribly hungry, I think. Long morning at work. Trying to get Mr. Henderson to understand why he needs to update his accounts… it’s like talking to a brick wall sometimes. Men and technology. A dangerous combination! My Barry can barely work the telly. Though, he’s clever with his hands. Fixed my washing machine last week, he did. Saved me a fortune. That’s good. Mine just complains if I ask him to change a lightbulb. Says it’s ‘women’s work’. Honestly! Men! They’re all the same. My George… he’d rather complain than lift a finger. Though, he was a good provider, I’ll give him that. Remember that time he brought home that enormous salmon? Oh, yes! And you said it looked like a… well, you said it looked a bit like a prehistoric creature. Mum! You always did have a way with words. She's got one of those warts as well, hasn't she? Right on her hand, you can see it clear as day. It's alright, Annie, They aren't catching. I've had 'em for years, right on me thumb. Never bothered me none. Just part of being old, I suppose. You wouldn’t get them much these days, everyone’s so clean. Speaking of clean, Doreen, everything looks lovely.

Honestly, I think Mr. Davies is actively trying to make us all fail his Physics tests. It’s just… cruel. You are  not  kidding. That last one was brutal. I thought I’d done okay, and I got a D. A D, Lily! I got a C-! A C  minus ! I actually cried a little bit in the library after. Not my finest moment. No shame. I nearly had a meltdown in Art. Mrs. Henderson keeps saying we need to “explore our inner selves” through pottery. Like, I just want to make a mug, not analyze my childhood trauma. Oh my god, that sounds…intense. She’s one of the trainee teachers, isn't she? Yeah, the one who always looks faintly panicked. Honestly, she’s sweet, but I feel like she’s winging it half the time. Remember when she accidentally called Mr. Peterson “Dad”? Oh,  please ! I was trying so hard not to snort. He went bright red! And then she tried to recover by saying something about him being a “father figure” to the students? Exactly! It was the most awkward thing ever. Anyway, Physics is just… ugh. I genuinely don’t understand any of it. Honestly, I'd rather write ten essays for Miss Ashton. Miss Ashton is brutal, but at least she’s predictable. You know what she wants. With Physics, it’s like Mr. Davies is speaking a different language. Plus, he  loves  to call on people who clearly have no idea what’s going on. He does, doesn’t he? It’s like he thrives on our suffering. Yesterday he asked Ben to explain the Doppler effect and Ben just froze. He just stood there, staring into space. Poor Ben. He’s so lovely, but science is definitely not his thing. Did you hear Chloe’s managed to get into the advanced art class? No way! That’s amazing! She’s so talented. All those detailed sketches she does… I can barely draw a stick figure. I know, right? She’s a proper artist. I'm just trying to survive the mandatory sculpture project. I’m seriously considering making a giant potato. A giant potato? That's brilliant. You should! Mr. Williams would love that. He’s secretly a bit eccentric. Maybe I will. It’s less stressful than trying to create something meaningful. Oh, speaking of stressful, did you finish the English homework?

Honestly, the things Mrs. O’Malley used to say… she was a nun, you know, proper old-school. “The devil works in mysterious ways,” she’d say after little Timmy spilled his milk. As if  milk  was a demonic influence. Sounds intense. Like, genuinely scary intense, or just… old-fashioned strict? A bit of both, I think. She  believed . Absolutely, fundamentally believed. It makes you wonder, doesn’t it? About people who are that certain. Ba-ba! More peas! Alright, sweetheart, more peas coming right up. See? A much simpler faith. Peas are good. Peas are life. Yeah, Liam’s a pragmatist. Though, thinking about it… all this certainty. It's kinda like, what if everything  is  a simulation? Like…  The Matrix ? Oh, here we go. You’ve been watching too many sci-fi films. No, but seriously! If we're living in a computer program, then religion could just be code programmed in by the… architects or whatever. Architects? Right. So, God is a programmer? That’s a new one. Well, not necessarily  God , but… someone. Something. And it explains why people need it, right? The program needs us to  think  there’s meaning, so it builds in the religion aspect. I suppose. But it feels… awfully cynical. I used to have a friend, Sarah, who got  really  into Scientology. That was… a whole other level of believing, let me tell you. Scientology? Isn’t that the one with the aliens and the auditing? That’s the one. She gave me a pamphlet once, explaining all about engrams and clear levels. I tried to be polite, but honestly, it just sounded… bonkers. She ended up moving to America to join one of their facilities. Haven’t heard from her in years. Wow. That’s… dedicated. Or maybe… brainwashed? It's hard to say. She was looking for something, I think. A sense of belonging, a purpose. We all are, aren’t we? Whether we find it in a nun’s pronouncements, a sci-fi movie theory, or… well, somewhere else. Pea! Pea! See, Liam’s found his purpose. It’s peas. Now, eat your dinner, love. And you, young man, stop trying to philosophize with a mouthful of mashed potato. Okay, okay. But seriously, though… what  do  you think? About all of it? I honestly don’t know. I think people need to believe in  something . Whether that’s a higher power, a better future, or just the goodness in their friends.

Right, so if we go this way, it avoids that awful roundabout near the Tesco. Honestly, it's chaos there at this time. Yeah, good shout. Though I still maintain that people just don’t  understand  roundabouts. It’s not hard, is it? Give way to the right. Simple. You’d think, wouldn’t you? It’s like they never had driving lessons. Speaking of lessons… how’s the salsa going? Still two left feet? Less so, actually. I mean, I’m still not going to be challenging anyone on Strictly, but I can sort of…follow. And I haven't stepped on anyone's toes  too  badly this week. It’s more coordination than anything, I think. You should come along! Me? Oh, no chance. I’d just embarrass us both. I have the grace of a baby giraffe. Remember that time I tried to do that line dancing thing at Sarah’s hen do? Oh god, yes! You nearly took out old Mrs. Henderson. That was legendary. Speaking of Sarah, how’s the planning for the Cornwall trip going? You were supposed to be looking at cottages. I am! It’s… overwhelming. So many cottages. So many pasties. Trying to find somewhere that takes a dog and isn't completely falling apart, and isn’t costing a fortune. It’s a struggle. I saw one that was advertised as having “Olde Worlde Charm.” Turned out to mean damp and wonky floors. "Olde Worlde Charm" is code for needing a full renovation. Always. Did you see that documentary about the history of the English language? The bit about how “Old English” sounded? It was completely unrecognisable! Like they were gargling pebbles. No, I missed that. I’ve been stuck in a hole re-reading all this corpus linguistics stuff for work. It’s fascinating, honestly, but it feels like my brain is going to explode. The patterns…the statistics… Sounds…fun. I'm glad I opted for engineering. Much more concrete. Although, trying to explain stress calculations to clients can feel like speaking Old English sometimes. Do you think they ever actually listen? Probably not. People switch off as soon as you start talking technical jargon. Like when Dr. Sharma was on that medical drama last night. He was explaining some procedure, and I just zoned out. I'm pretty sure he said something about “nanobots” or something equally sci-fi.

Right, so I was reading about Grožnjan, apparently it’s this whole town full of artists. Like,  full  of them. Studios everywhere, galleries… sounds right up my street. Ooh, that does sound lovely, doesn’t it? We could definitely spend a day there. Though, honestly, after navigating these roads… I need a strong coffee, and maybe a lie-down. These Croatian drivers are… spirited, to say the least. Spirited? They’re mental, Mum! That little Fiat nearly took us out back there. Boys will be boys, and drivers will be drivers, eh? It’s all part of the adventure. Although, I have to agree, the driving is… enthusiastic. Still, the scenery is stunning. Look at those olive groves! Seriously. And the smell! It's amazing. I saw a little sign for an olive oil tasting near Motovun, we should definitely stop. I need to stock up. Thinking Christmas gifts already, you know? Good thinking. And wine! We need to find some local wine. I read Istrian Malvazija is really good. Bit dry, apparently, but very refreshing. Can we go to Pula? I saw pictures of the Roman amphitheatre, it looks awesome. Like something out of  Sons of Anarchy . Honestly, Ethan,  again  with  Sons of Anarchy ? You've watched that series like, six times. It’s a classic! And everything looks cooler in  Sons of Anarchy . Even Roman ruins. A classic for you, perhaps. I find it a bit… gritty. Although, I have to admit, the scenery  was  rather good. Reminded me a bit of… well, a slightly wilder Center Parcs, actually. Don’t even mention Center Parcs, Richard. After last summer, I need a holiday that doesn't involve queuing for a swimming pool. Although, the kids did enjoy that pottery painting… Okay, pottery painting is good. But Grožnjan sounds much more… adult. We could get some unique pieces. I could actually  make  something for once, instead of just admiring other people’s work! Can we have ice cream in Pula if we go? A really big one. We can have ice cream anywhere, darling. What about that market in Rovinj? I was hoping we could go there tomorrow. Apparently, it's amazing for fresh produce and local crafts. Rovinj sounds good. I saw a few restaurants with sea views advertised. I’m fancying some fresh seafood tonight. I’m getting rather bored of motorway service station sandwiches. Me too! Oh, and I saw someone mention a little Konoba – that's a traditional Croatian tavern, right?

Right, so then Chloe was proper taking the mick, wasn’t she? About us trying to learn that card game. Honestly, I felt like a right mug. She’s just like that, innit? Always needs to be the smartest one in the room. Though, to be fair, it  is  a complicated game. I still don't fully grasp all the rules. Complicated? It’s just a load of cards, love. You’re overthinking it. Though, I was too busy trying to stop Liam from accidentally revealing his entire life story every time he won a hand. Oh god, Liam. He's an open book. Speaking of revealing things…did anyone ever figure out why Sarah was so weirdly quiet all night? She barely touched her drink. She looked proper stressed, didn’t she? I thought maybe something was up with Ben. They were having a right hushed conversation in the kitchen. I overheard a snippet, actually. Something about... a video? And someone being really upset about it. Didn’t catch who. Oh,  now  you've got my attention. A video of what? Don’t tell me someone was secretly filming everyone again? Remember what happened at Jess’ birthday? Ugh, don’t remind me. That was mortifying. Someone put a clip of me attempting to do the Macarena on TikTok. The shame! But this sounded different. Sarah sounded genuinely distressed. I’m guessing someone was being a bit of a creep. It wouldn’t surprise me, honestly. There's always one. It got me thinking though... remember that conversation we had last week, about... you know... exploring things? Oh,  hell . Don’t go there now, not in front of Chloe’s little sister! I wasn’t going to go into detail! Just, it made me wonder… do people ever film…  that  sort of thing? Like, just for themselves, or… Oh, absolutely. There's a whole world of that online, love. Don’t pretend you haven't seen it. Though, filming it? That feels… weird. I agree with Chloe. Massive invasion of privacy, even if it’s just for yourself. It feels like… setting yourself up for trouble, doesn't it? Plus, imagine if it got out. Nightmare fuel. Seriously. And that’s why you don't even go there. I mean, me and Ben were talking about…games, like board games. Not…  that . Although, he did mention some very complicated role-playing stuff.

Right, I’m officially flagging. This course on cybersecurity is  draining . Need caffeine, desperately. And something… substantial. Tell me about it. I swear, half these students are actively trying to confuse me with their questions. Honestly, they think they're hackers already. You grabbing a coffee then, Dave? Aye, coffee's a must. Though, honestly, coffee and a biscuit never cut it anymore, not after a morning of explaining firewalls. I’m thinking something savoury. What about that new place down the street? “Spice Delight”? Heard it's decent. Spice Delight? Is that the Indian one? I walked past it yesterday, the smells were amazing. Though, I’m trying to be good. Hence, the banana. Attempting ‘healthy’ for at least one day this week. Healthy? At lunchtime? You're a braver man than I, Mark. I need carbs. And spice. Give me a good vindaloo and I’m a happy man. Ooh, vindaloo sounds good actually. Though my stomach hasn’t forgiven me for the last one I had. Remember that curry night after the conference in Blackpool? How could I forget? You were green for a good hour afterwards. Proper suffering. Blackpool… that was a weekend. I think I still have photos somewhere of you attempting karaoke, Dave. Don’t you  dare . Those are classified! Anyway, back to food. Spice Delight it is, then? Unless anyone's got a burning desire for a panini or something equally… bland. No, vindaloo is calling my name. Though, maybe I’ll ask for a mild one this time. Learned my lesson. What are you thinking of getting, Mark? You sticking with the banana? Tempted, very tempted. But a good biryani… that’s hard to resist. I reckon I can cope with a medium. Maybe. I'll just have a large glass of mango lassi on standby, just in case. Sensible. Right, I’ll go and scout out Spice Delight. See how long the queue is. Don’t want to be sat here starving all afternoon. You two want anything specific? Just the vindaloo. And maybe some garlic naan, if they have it. Biryani, and definitely that mango lassi. Actually, two lassis. Just to be safe. Two lassis. Got it. Right, adventure awaits. Back in five, hopefully with tales of culinary delights…and minimal queueing. Good luck! Don't let them upsell you on anything too spicy. And remember, no karaoke photos! No promises on either count… He’ll be back with a story, you watch.

Right, so I was explaining to me mam, bless her, what TikTok is. Oh, good luck with that. My dad still thinks Instagram is just for filters. Oh, you're telling me? Trying to explain algorithms to my sister-in-law is a lost cause. She thinks Facebook  decides  what she likes. Exactly! I said, “It’s just short videos, Mam, people dancing, doing challenges…” and she goes, “Like those talent shows? Is Simon Cowell involved?” Oh, brilliant! See, that’s the generation gap in a nutshell. They see anything visual and immediately think of TV. It’s fascinating, isn’t it? How quickly these platforms come and go. Remember Vine? Gone in a puff of smoke. Vine! Oh, I was proper addicted to Vine. Those six-second loops were genius. I tried to make a few myself, utterly embarrassing looking back, of course. I vaguely remember. I was more of a Tumblr person back then. All those slightly angsty quotes over blurry photographs. So very 2012. Speaking of angsty, I’ve been looking at how students are using social media for research. Mostly it’s… questionable sources, shall we say. Lots of ‘influencers’ presenting themselves as experts. Oh, God, yeah. I saw a post the other day claiming that the Library of Alexandria was destroyed by a rogue hamster. No! Seriously? Swear on it. Had like, fifty thousand likes. The comments were full of people saying, “OMG, that hamster was a menace!” It's terrifying, frankly. We're fighting a constant battle against misinformation. And these algorithms just amplify the craziest stuff. It feels like we’re librarians trying to build sandcastles against the tide. You point out the proper academic databases, and they’re all scrolling through TikTok looking for answers. I tried to explain Boolean searches to a student last week. Her face just glazed over. I might as well have been speaking Klingon. You know what I read recently? There’s a whole subculture of people on TikTok pretending to be librarians. No way! What are they  doing ? Mostly just aesthetic videos. Cozy libraries, books stacked in artistic piles, lots of candlelight. It’s… not exactly promoting information literacy. Sounds like Instagram with more bookshelves. I think I need to go lie down. All this talk of social media is giving me a headache. Maybe I’ll just go back to cataloguing… with actual cards. Now  there's  a thought.

Right, so we’ve got the broad strokes of the business case down, haven’t we? The projected patient numbers, the staffing model… it all seems fairly robust. It's this 'what to do for the tape' bit that’s really bothering me. How do we present all this – the ethical considerations, the patient pathways, the community need – in a way that doesn’t feel… reductive? I agree. It’s not just numbers, is it? It’s about dignity and quality of life. We need to highlight the preventative work, the support for families. That's where the narrative really strengthens. Perhaps a series of patient stories, anonymised of course, woven through the presentation? Demonstrates the  need  without exploiting vulnerability. That’s a good idea. And we  must  emphasise the consultation process. We’ve held those meetings with the local GPs, the community nurses, even the chap from the church. It shows we’re not just descending from on high with a pre-ordained plan. Absolutely. That’s crucial for buy-in. And it also informs the final design. I had a lengthy conversation with Dr. Davies yesterday - a surprisingly insightful man, despite his gruff exterior. He flagged up the fragmented nature of end-of-life care in this area. People slipping through the cracks, inadequate coordination between hospital discharge and home nursing. Which feeds directly into the rationale for  this  location, doesn't it? Tunbridge Wells and the surrounding villages have an aging population, relatively affluent, but demonstrably underserved in terms of specialist palliative care. And frankly, the current facilities are… underwhelming. Exactly. The nearest dedicated hospice is a good forty-minute drive, and that presumes there’s an ambulance available. What about those reliant on public transport? The business case makes a clear argument for accessibility. Though, getting the land rights sorted is proving…challenging. I saw the initial designs from the architects. Using that old estate agent’s office plot is…a bold choice. It's small. Footprint is limited, yes, but we can go vertical. Three stories, sensitively designed. Lots of natural light, garden terraces… We aim for it feeling less ‘institution’ and more ‘home’. I want it palatable to the local residents, you know? No-one wants a hospice looming over their garden. Thinking about the demographics, there's a surprisingly high number of ex-pats around here. Lots of retired professionals. They’ll have expectations regarding the level of care.

Oh, look at this one! Us at Sarah’s wedding. God, that feels like a lifetime ago. Everyone was so… optimistic. Optimistic and slightly tipsy, if I remember correctly. Old Man Hemmings nearly took a tumble trying to do the Macarena. Haha! I vaguely remember that. Was that the one where Aunt Carol tried to convince everyone she was distantly related to royalty? That was  another  wedding, darling. Though Carol does try and claim royal connections at every family gathering. Remember Ascot last year? She was absolutely convinced the Duchess of Cornwall gave her a knowing wink. She did! She spent the entire afternoon regaling anyone who'd listen with the story. Speaking of which, are we still going this year? I need to book tickets. Yes, we are. Though I’m already bracing myself for the Carol show. I’m thinking we need a decoy strategy. Distract her with a particularly flamboyant hat. I'm in. I can work on a backstory for a fictional distant cousin who’s a lady-in-waiting. We could really sell it. You’re wicked. Right, this potato needs a bit more attention. How’s the job hunt going, by the way, Chloe? Any interviews lined up? Actually, yes. I have one on Friday, for a content creator role at that digital marketing agency in Canterbury. It sounds pretty good, the work seems really creative. Oh, wonderful! That’s brilliant, love. Are you nervous? A bit. It's the first real interview I’ve had since graduating. I keep worrying I’ll say something completely stupid. You won’t. You’re articulate, intelligent, and you've got a brilliant portfolio. Just be yourself, and remember to ask them about the team dynamic. That always shows you’re thinking long-term. He's right. And remember what I always say – breathe! It helps with the nerves. Oh, look at this photo – Grandma and Grandad on their honeymoon! They look so young… and Grandad’s hair! Wow! I’ve never seen him with that much hair. It’s so different. I always thought of him as the bald, grumpy one. He was a dashing young man in his day, apparently. Your grandmother always said he was quite the charmer. Though she also said he was terrible at cooking. Terrible is an understatement. He once tried to make shepherd’s pie with peas instead of carrots. The less said about it, the better.

Right, so are we actually gonna watch this, or are we just gonna sit ‘ere talkin’ about how scared we are? 'Cause I’m gettin’ a right neck ache lookin’ up at the telly. I’m building the suspense! You can’t just  launch  into a horror film, you gotta… prepare. Like, preemptively regret all your life choices. Preemptively regret...? You sound like yer mum readin’ a book review. It’s a film, Liv. It's made up. Mostly. Mostly? That’s reassuring. No, but seriously, this one’s supposed to be properly creepy. Apparently, the director used actual binaural recordings for the sound design. Binaural what now? Sounds fancy. And terrifying. Is it one o' them found footage things? 'Cause I hate found footage. Always shaky cam and voices breathin' down yer neck. Makes me feel sick. No, thankfully not. It’s more… psychological. Apparently, it plays on yer primal fears. Like, darkness and isolation and… clowns. Oh,  don’t  mention clowns. Seriously. I had a bad experience with a clown at a birthday party when I were little. Ended with me hidin’ under a table and cryin’. Still get shivers thinkin’ about it. Honestly? You're terrified of everything. Remember when you wouldn’t go near the garden shed because you thought there was a spider in it? It was a  massive  spider, I swear! Like, the size of me hand. And it was lookin’ at me. Judgementally. Right. A judgemental spider. Okay, look. This film isn’t about spiders or birthday parties. It’s about a remote lighthouse keeper who starts seein’ things. And hearin’ things. Seein’ and hearin’ things? That’s just Tuesday for my grandad. No, honestly, I’m just worried it'll be all jump scares. I hate jump scares. Makes me jump. Obvious, innit? It’s supposed to be slow burn. Atmospheric. That’s why I picked it. And, I’ve made popcorn. Extra butter. That should help with the fear. Extra butter, you say? Now you’re talkin’. Right, okay. I'll suffer for the extra butter. But if I scream, you’re holdin’ me hand. And not laughin’. Deal. But no promises if the judgmental spider makes an appearance. You are a menace, you are. Just… press play, will ya? Before I change me mind and we watch Bake Off instead. Okay, okay. Here we go… Prepare to be spooked.

Right, well, almost bedtime for me I think. Just finishing this cup of tea. You alright, Grandad? Oh, aye, fine, fine. Just been flicking through the channels. Nothing but rubbish on these days, you know. All shouting and flashing lights. Give me a good old book any day. I know what you mean. Though, I did order a new book  online  last night. From that website you showed me, Amazon. Are you getting the hang of that whole online shopping thing? Getting there, getting there. Still feels a bit… strange, doesn’t it? Ordering things from a picture. Back in my day, you went to the shops, you  saw  what you were buying. Felt the material, that sort of thing. It's convenient though, isn’t it? Especially for things like books. Though I was looking at Airbnb too, thinking about a little weekend away somewhere. Have you ever considered that? Airbnb? What’s that then? Sounds like a fancy biscuit. No, no! It’s where people rent out their homes, or rooms in their homes, to holidaymakers. Like a bed and breakfast, but through an app. Hmm. Sounds a bit… precarious, doesn't it? Letting strangers into your house. I’ve always believed in a good, reliable hotel. Though, hotels aren’t what they used to be, are they? They've changed a bit. Actually, speaking of food, I ordered a pizza earlier. I could bring you a slice if you're peckish? Oh, that’s kind of you, dear. But no, I’m alright. Had a nice bit of cheese and a biscuit earlier. You enjoy. Reminds me, your cousin Emily rang today. Said she’s coming down next week. Oh, lovely! I’d forgotten she was planning a visit. How long is she staying? A few days, I think. Said she wanted to see the garden. She’s always liked your garden, hasn’t she? She has. I'm trying to rearrange the living room a bit. I was thinking of selling that old armchair. It's just taking up space. Have you seen anyone looking for furniture recently? Not that I’ve noticed. Old Mrs. Higgins down the road mentioned needing a new sofa, but she’s more of a floral print type of woman, and your armchair is…well, it’s quite masculine, isn’t it? It is, isn't it? Right. Well, I think I’ll take a picture and put it on that selling website you showed me, Gumtree.

Aye, honestly, that Kerouac’s been sittin’ on my shelf for months now.  On the Road . Everyone raves about it, says it changed their life, but I just… can't get into it. Feels a bit boyish, doesn’t it? All that romanticising of hitchhiking and bein’ a beatnik. Boyish? Coming from  you , Alistair? The man who once spent three weeks backpacking through the Highlands with nothing but a rucksack and a copy of poetry by Burns? That was different! That was… a spiritual journey! Kerouac just feels like a well-meaning lad trying to be profound. Besides, the Highlands are a bit more forgiving than some dusty American highway. I reckon I lost a good stone just fighting the midges. You always exaggerate. Still, I see your point. It  is  a bit… performative, isn’t it? Though I did enjoy the sheer energy of it. It made me want to just hop on a train and disappear. Which, ironically, is exactly what I  didn't  do. Had essays to mark, remember? Ah, the glamorous life of a Director of Studies. Chained to your desk while the rest of us are out exploring the world. Speaking of exploring, you still heading to Japan next year? Aye, all being well. Planning on going in cherry blossom season. Supposedly breathtaking. I've been reading a lot about Kyoto, trying to get a feel for the place. It sounds… refined. A bit less chaotic than somewhere like Tokyo, eh? I've heard the same. I was in Tokyo for a conference a few years back and it was… overwhelming. Brilliant, but overwhelming. The sheer density of people, the noise… it was incredible. Though I did manage to find a tiny little ramen shop down an alleyway that was heaven on earth. Those are the best finds, aren't they? The bits you stumble upon. I'm hoping to spend a couple of weeks just wandering, getting lost, seeing what happens. Though I’m trying to learn a few basic phrases, just to avoid completely embarrassing myself. My Japanese extends to…  konnichiwa  and a rather enthusiastic ‘arigato’. That’ll get you far! I remember trying to order coffee in Italy once. Ended up with a plate of prosciutto. The waiter was very confused. That’s brilliant! You really do find trouble, don’t you? I’m more worried about the etiquette. Apparently, there's a whole world of unspoken rules about how to behave, how to present yourself… Don't overthink it.

Honestly, Mum, the interview felt…weird. Not bad weird, just…off. Off how, love? Was it the people? The building? You were saying it’s a really prestigious firm, wasn’t it? Foster & Partners? Yeah, Foster & Partners. The building was incredible, obviously. All glass and steel, very minimalist. But the interviewers… they kept asking about my ‘passion’ for sustainable architecture. Like, I understand it’s important, and I  am  interested, but it felt like they wanted me to weep dramatically about saving the planet. Oh, architects. Always a bit dramatic. It’s the artistic temperament, I suppose. But seriously, you  are  passionate about it, aren’t you? You chose your dissertation on passive house design, didn't you? I am! But I explained my interest in the practical application, the problem-solving, the efficiency, and they seemed…disappointed. They wanted poetry, not blueprints. And one of them, this senior partner, kept referring to the ‘emotional connection’ to materials. I nearly choked. Emotional connection to concrete? Right. Well, some people are like that. They get a bit carried away with the philosophy of it all. Did they ask about the portfolio? That’s usually the bit that counts, isn’t it? They want to see what you can  do . They did. They spent a good twenty minutes on it. They asked about my design choices for the community centre project, wanted to know my rationale behind everything. That part felt good. It was the fluffy stuff that threw me. Well, that’s good then, that the work speaks for itself. Listen, don’t beat yourself up about it. These things happen. Sometimes you just don’t click with a company’s vibe. It’s not necessarily a reflection on your skills. I know, I know. It’s just…this was a really competitive position. And I've been applying for jobs for months now. It's starting to feel a bit disheartening. I can imagine. Have you heard anything back from that smaller firm, the one in Shoreditch? The one doing the eco-housing project? Not yet. I sent a follow-up email last week, but nothing. I'm starting to think they've gone with someone else. They’re a lot smaller, so maybe they just didn't have the budget to hire. Actually, I completely forgot to tell you - I also applied for that role at the National Trust, doing conservation work.

Right then, settle yerselves. Cup of tea, Doris? Arthur, you’ll have your usual, I expect? Aye, please, Bernard. A nice strong brew. Been a long drive, even just coming from Costessey. Traffic was somethin' awful around the roundabout. Oh, don't even  mention  the traffic, Arthur. I came round earlier and it was nose-to-tail all the way from Harrow. Honestly, you’d think everyone decided to go shopping at the same time. They probably did. Everything's gotten busier, hasn’t it? Used to be able to get anywhere quick as you like. Remember that, Arthur? When you could drive into Norwich and find a parkin’ space without a palaver? Aye, those were the days. Before all these fancy one-way systems and cycle lanes. Makes a fella dizzy just tryin' to navigate the city now. Though, I must say, that new supermarket on the edge of town is handy. Good prices, too. I went there last week. It's alright, but they seem to move everything around every time you go. You spend half an hour just lookin' for the biscuits! They do that on purpose, Doris. It’s a tactic to get you to buy things you don’t need. They call it ‘consumer journey optimisation’ or some such nonsense. Consumer what-now? Sounds like a load of balderdash to me. They just want yer money, that’s all. Speaking of money, did you see what they’re sayin’ about house prices now? Still goin' up, apparently. Absolutely ridiculous. Young folks haven't a chance these days. I remember when you could buy a perfectly decent semi for a few thousand pound. Now they’re payin' half a million for a shoebox. It’s criminal, it is. My granddaughter’s savin’ up, but she says it'll take her a lifetime to afford anything. And even then, it'll be somethin' tiny. They should build more council houses, that's what they should do. Like they used to. Good quality, affordable homes. Not these flimsy things they stick up now. They won't do that though, will they? It's all about profit these days. Speaking of buildin' things, I was readin’ about that new road they’re plannin' to build through the countryside. Says it’ll cut journey times, but I reckon it’ll just ruin the landscape. Oh, I heard about that. It's a shame.

Right, so I was chatting with Old Man Hemmings from the community garden this morning, and he's really keen on utilising that little nook by the fire escape on the ground floor. The one we were thinking of for storage? Honestly, I was hoping to get some shelving in there, we’re bursting at the seams with all the event kit. He wants to do a little… seed swap and propagation station. Apparently, there’s a real appetite for it in the local gardening groups. He’s offering to manage it entirely himself, bless him. A seed swap… that’s… nice. But is it  income generating ? That’s the big question, isn’t it? We need to be thinking about how we maximise every inch of this building. That’s what I said to him! Gently, of course. I suggested he could maybe run little workshops, seed-starting sessions, things like that. A small fee, you know? Workshops… now you’re talking. We could market those really well on social media. ‘Grow Your Own!’ – very Brixton. Have you checked the fire regulations for that space though? It’s right next to the escape route. We don’t want plant pots obstructing anything. I already flagged it with Barry, the fire safety bloke. He said as long as there’s clear access and the plants aren’t flammable, we should be okay. He did remind me, for the tenth time, about the boxes blocking the corridor near the kitchen. Oh,  that . Right. I’ll get onto that after the meeting with the new yoga teacher. Apparently, she’s wanting to book the hall every Tuesday evening. Excellent! That’s a good consistent income stream. Is she paying the going rate? I don’t want us getting undercut again. Remember what happened with the pottery class? I’ve already negotiated with her, she’s aware of our rates. She’s offering to run a free taster session for some of the families we work with too. Good PR. That’s brilliant, actually. Good thinking. Although… free sessions eat into profit, don’t they? We need to track those accurately. I am, I am. I’ve built it into the spreadsheet. Speaking of which, have you sorted holiday cover for the front desk? I’m off for two weeks in August. I’ve asked young Maya if she's available. She’s finishing her A-Levels and said she’d be keen.

Honestly, Ben, you  have  to try this chutney. It’s ridiculous. Mrs. Davies from the village made it - apparently, it’s a family recipe. Plum and something… fiery. Oh.  Woah . Right. Fiery is…an understatement. It’s like a tiny dragon just breathed on my tongue. Delicious, though. Seriously good. Told you she was a wizard with preserves. Old Mrs. Davies could pickle a brick and it’d taste amazing. This lamb is…exceptional. Did you get it from that butcher in Ross-on-Wye, Dad? The one you raved about last time? Best butcher for miles, I tell you. Proper Welsh lamb, even down here in England. Though, I suspect even  I  couldn’t ruin a leg of lamb, to be fair. You’ve really outdone yourself with the potatoes, Sarah. So fluffy. What’s your secret? Oh, it's embarrassingly simple. Just a knob of butter and a splash of milk. My grandmother swore by it. She said it's all about treating them gently. They’re sensitive little things. Sensitive potatoes, eh? I’ll remember that when I’m back in the kitchen. Though, I suspect my potatoes are usually subjected to a bit of harsh treatment. I’m more of a ‘throw everything at it and hope for the best’ kind of chef. That explains the occasional culinary masterpieces. And the…other things. Remember that paella incident, Ben? Don't even  mention  the paella. It looked like something dredged from the bottom of the sea. And tasted… vaguely of sadness. It was memorable, at least! Margaret, are you enjoying? You haven't said much. Oh, I am! Lovely meal. It's just…nice to be  away . Away from work, away from everything. It’s been a stressful few months. That's exactly what this is for. A complete escape. No marking, no reports…just countryside and chutney. Speaking of escapes, have we finalised the plan for tomorrow? I was thinking we could walk up to Symonds Yat. Apparently, the views are incredible. Sounds good to me! As long as it doesn't involve a climb that requires ropes and carabiners. I’m on holiday, after all. I'm in. I need to burn off all this delicious lamb and chutney somehow. Maybe I can convince Mrs. Davies to give me the chutney recipe. I’ll try and recreate the dragon breath back home. Don't bother, son.

Honestly, the traffic was  mental  getting out of Leeds. I thought I was going to be stuck there forever. Oh, yeah? I thought the M1 was pretty smooth, actually. Maybe you hit it at a bad time. Still, better than trying to navigate Manchester, isn’t it? That city is a labyrinth. Manchester's not  that  bad. It's got character! Leeds is just...grey. All grey buildings and grey people. No offence. None taken. I’m more of a countryside person anyway. Though, I do like a good weekend in London now and then. The museums are brilliant. Remember that Hockney exhibition we went to? Oh aye! That was class. Though I’m still convinced half the art world just pretends to understand it. You know, nods sagely and says things like, “The deconstruction of the patriarchal gaze…” You're terrible. But probably right. Speaking of pretending, have you seen that new advert for the… what is it, the sparkly water? The one with the incredibly earnest voiceover about ‘hydration’? Ugh,  that  one! It's so irritating. It’s just water, love, calm down. It’s not curing cancer. I saw one for a car the other day that was equally ridiculous. Some bloke ‘conquering’ a muddy hill. Like, good for you and your 4x4. They’re all the same. Overblown and full of nonsense. Remember when adverts used to just…tell you what the thing did? Simpler times. So, are we still on for that Thai on Friday? I'm craving a good Pad See Ew. Definitely. Should I book? I tried to last night but kept getting put on hold. Their phone system is a nightmare. Go for it. If you can get through. I'll check in with me mam later. She's been on at me to visit. Said she's making that crumble she knows I like. Your mam's crumble  is  exceptional. Honestly. I think I’ve gained a stone just thinking about it. How's your brother getting on, by the way? I haven’t spoken to him in ages. He’s good, yeah. Still obsessed with those vintage synthesizers. He’s trying to get a band together, apparently. Said his flatmate's a drummer. Doubt it’ll go anywhere, but he's enjoying himself. That sounds like him. Total commitment to slightly niche hobbies. Have you been watching anything good lately? I started “Severance” on Apple TV, and it’s properly weird.

Honestly, the hospital… it’s just a conveyor belt, isn’t it? In, examined, out. Barely a human touch. I had my follow-up appointment after the hysteroscopy yesterday, and it was all “next!” and “sign here.” Oh, you poor thing. That sounds awful. Is everything alright, though? With… you know… everything? Physically, yes. Apparently, all clear, which is a relief. It’s just… the whole process is so dehumanising. And it brought everything back, you know? Thinking about Mum. Oh, Alison. It hasn’t even been six months, has it? It still feels so raw. I saw John at the shops the other day, he’s shrunk, honestly. Just… lost. He has. Poor man. It’s hard to watch. He's trying to be strong for the kids, which makes it worse, I think. He won't  let  himself grieve properly. Said he has to be ‘the rock’. Men, eh? Bottling it all up. My Brian, same after his dad died. Wouldn’t say a word, just threw himself into work. Ended up with a stomach ulcer. Speaking of things bottling up… I’m trying to do this new diet, you see. This ‘soup diet’. A soup diet? Seriously? I know, sounds grim, doesn't it? But Doreen at the school – you know, the dinner lady – swore by it. Lost two stone. I just… I’ve put a bit on, haven't I? Lockdown did me no favours. And my knees are playing up something fierce. Need to shed some weight. You look fine, honestly. And a soup diet sounds… miserable. I’m trying to just eat a bit more consciously, you know? More vegetables, less biscuits. Though the biscuit tin is calling my name as we speak. It’s always the biscuits, isn’t it? My sister, Brenda, she’s gone full keto. Says it’s changed her life. Apparently, she’s practically glowing. She was always the chubby one, though. Always sensitive about her weight. Brenda? Oh, I remember her. Always so bubbly, even when she was self-conscious. It’s funny, isn't it? How we all have our things. Mum always worried about her weight, too. Always on some diet or other. Though, towards the end… she just didn’t care anymore. Which, in a way, was almost a relief. It is, isn’t it? When it just… doesn’t matter anymore. It’s just… being.

Right, well that was a lovely dinner. Honestly, that dauphinoise potatoes were  almost  worth the effort. Almost. They were good! Can I have some more pudding? Later, young man. Let your mother finish her sentence. You’ve already had a generous portion of both. So, Sarah, how was your day wrestling with rogue semicolons and marketing mayhem? Don’t even  start . Ms. Henderson decided, at 4pm, that she wanted a completely different tone for the website copy. Apparently, ‘professional’ now equals ‘slightly whimsical’… Honestly, the briefs I get! It’s like people haven’t read a style guide in their lives. What’s a semicolon? It sounds scary. It’s like… a comma, but stronger? That’s… a surprisingly good description, actually. It’s used to join two related sentences. But never mind that. Daniel, how was school? Any exciting scientific breakthroughs today? We dissected a frog. It was… slimy. Oh, joy. A childhood staple. I remember mine. Not fondly. You’d think they’d at least let you wear gloves. Honestly. Speaking of unpleasant experiences, work was… interesting. Massive supply chain issues. Apparently, a key component for the new machinery is stuck in a port because of… well, everything going on in the world. It’s a headache. Everything going on? You mean the, the…situation? That. And the escalating cost of everything. It’s making forecasting incredibly difficult. I spent half the day on calls trying to mitigate the damage. Right, can we talk about something else? Like skiing? Are we still going skiing this winter? Of course we are! We’ve already booked the chalet, remember? In Val d'Isère. Although… I am slightly worried about the snow. The reports aren't great. I’m getting better at skiing! I nearly managed a black run last time. 'Nearly' being the operative word. Don’t get ahead of yourself. It’s not a race. It will be good to get away though. A proper break. I need to switch off. Honestly, sometimes I dream of spreadsheets. Can I choose the music for the drive? Negotiable. But no death metal before 10am. What about work experience? Mr. Harrison said we need to start thinking about it. Oh, right. That. Well, I was thinking maybe… something with the local newspaper? They always need help with proofreading, and it would give you some real-world experience. That’s a good idea.

Right, okay, this one… this is absolutely dreadful quality, isn’t it? Taken on that little disposable camera we had on the Japan trip. Oh my god, is that me trying to feed a deer in Nara Park? I look… enthusiastic. And slightly terrified. Enthusiastically terrified is a good way to put it. They  are  surprisingly assertive for deer, aren’t they? Especially when they’ve clocked you’ve got those little crackers. They headbutt you for them! I remember. One actually nibbled my jacket. I was convinced it was going to eat my entire sleeve. It probably wanted the fabric softener. You always used a very floral one. No, seriously though, look at the background. The temple is beautiful, even blurry as it is. Remember how humid it was there? Sweltering. I think I lived in a permanent state of dampness for two weeks. But it was incredible. Do you remember that tiny ramen shop we found in Kyoto? Vaguely. Is that the one where the chef didn't speak a word of English and just pointed at pictures on the menu? I think I accidentally ordered a bowl of something vaguely fishy. You did! And you pretended to love it. I was trying so hard not to laugh. You were making these exaggerated ‘mmm’ sounds. Strategic politeness, darling. Strategic politeness. Okay, next photo… oh, hold on. This isn't Japan. This is… the badger incident! Oh,  no . Not the badger. It’s a classic! Look at that expression on your face. Pure horror. I was genuinely scared! It was right on our doorstep, huge and… and sniffing around. And you were filming it, completely unfazed! Well, someone had to document it for posterity. It was a remarkably bold badger. It just waddled up like it owned the place. It probably did. It's Norfolk. They  do  own the place. Did it actually try to get into the house? It hovered. It definitely hovered. I think it was assessing our biscuit supply. You screamed and slammed the door. I did not scream! I emitted a… startled yelp. A perfectly reasonable reaction to a wild animal attempting a home invasion. A startled yelp that could be heard in the next village. This photo is gold. Seriously, I should get these printed. Maybe some, but definitely not the badger one. I’ve got enough embarrassing photos floating around already, thank you very much.

…and honestly, the pub quizzes in Galway were  intense . Like, people were taking this seriously. Proper serious. Someone almost came to blows over the capital of Burkina Faso. Burkina Faso! Oh my god. Irish people and their geography. It’s a potent combination. I swear, they’ve all memorised every county border. I’ve always wanted to go to Ireland. It just looks… wild. All those cliffs and green fields. Did you guys do any skinny dipping? Don’t tell me you  didn’t  do any skinny dipping. We absolutely did. Down in Dingle. It was freezing, obviously, but exhilarating. The Atlantic has a certain bite to it. Though, I think I lost a bet and had to go in first… You did! And Liam filmed the whole thing. It’s a truly unflattering video. I’ve forbidden its release. Good call. My pale English skin doesn’t handle the cold well. It turns a truly alarming shade of blue. Speaking of pale, has anyone been keeping up with the news? Apparently, there’s this new zombie virus… Oh, don't even  start  with the zombie apocalypse talk, Chloe. I’ve stocked the cafe with tinned goods, but that’s purely for the winter rush, alright? Strictly business. Nah, she's prepping. I saw her buying those ridiculous machetes online. They’re for… opening coconuts! Yes, coconuts. I’m diversifying the menu. Trust me. Anyway, back to less terrifying topics. How’s the bakery going, Rosie? Still churning out those amazing rugelach? It’s manic, honestly. Especially with the Jewish holidays coming up. Everyone wants babka and challah. It’s lovely, but exhausting. I was up until 2 am braiding challah last night. Then Martin started  snoring . You could hear it through the walls. Martin’s snoring is legendary. It’s like a freight train. Though, honestly, I’m starting to think he does it on purpose to annoy you. Does he? That’s cold. I've got to say, you make the best babka. It's seriously good. My Nan down in Melbourne would be impressed. She’s a bit of a baking fiend. Thank you! I’ve been experimenting with different fillings. I’m trying to recreate this apricot and almond one my grandmother used to make. It’s proving tricky. I keep consulting Claudia Roden, but it’s just not the same. Claudia Roden is the queen. I’ve got her book on Jewish food.

Honestly, I’m convinced you’ve got a sixth sense for finding the  worst  peanuts in any pub. These are… dusty. Dusty? No, they’ve got character. A bit of…earthiness. You’re too used to those fancy roasted salted ones, you are. This is proper pub peanut experience. Earthiness is a polite word for stale, Mark. Anyway, how’s the dissertation going? Still battling with the Bayesian statistics? Don’t even. I swear that software is actively trying to sabotage me. Spent three hours debugging last night, only to realise I’d put a semi-colon in the wrong place. A  semi-colon , Sarah! It’s the digital equivalent of tripping over air. Oh, you poor thing. Sounds…fun. I’ve been mostly wrangling data all week. Though I did discover a brilliant new game – “Stardew Valley”. You’d hate it. It’s all farming and relationship building. Farming? You know I peak at ‘Call of Duty’. Anything involving nurturing virtual crops sends me into a cold sweat. Speaking of virtual worlds, have you seen the new trailer for that VR theme park simulator? Looks insane. The one where you build your own rollercoasters and then… ride them? Yeah, it looks terrifyingly good. I’m a bit of a theme park wuss though, to be honest. I prefer the  idea  of big drops to actually experiencing them. You wouldn’t last five seconds on Nemesis at Alton Towers. You’d be screaming before it even started climbing. Harmlessly enjoying the atmosphere! And it’s not just rollercoasters. I also have a healthy fear of water rides. I always end up soaked and miserable. Right. So, everything fun is inherently terrifying. Got it. We should probably stick to films then. Have you seen anything good lately? Actually, I watched that documentary about border security at Heathrow. It was… intense. Oh god, those are bleak. All that scanning and questioning. It’s a total downer. I prefer something a bit lighter, you know? Superheroes, explosions, stuff no actual airport would ever allow. It's just... fascinating how much goes on behind the scenes. The amount of fake passports they find! And the lengths people go to, trying to smuggle things through. Apparently, they found someone attempting to bring in live finches in their underwear last year.  What?!  Live finches in… You're kidding. I wish I was! Apparently, they’re quite a delicacy in some parts of Asia.

Honestly, this haddock is  perfect . Just how I like it – crispy batter, flaky fish. You haven’t had this one before, have you, Carol? No, I usually go for cod, but I thought I’d branch out. It is good, though. Really good. Though, you know, queuing for twenty minutes for chips… it does test your patience. I’ve been thinking about taking up rowing, actually. Rowing? Seriously? That’s a bit of a leap from book club, isn’t it? I know, I know. It’s Fiona at the gym. She's really into it, and she said the club is lovely, very welcoming. They're doing a beginner’s course. It sounds… peaceful, actually. And good exercise, obviously. Though, I imagine it’s very wet. Oh, it  is . You’ll need some proper gear. I tried kayaking last summer, and I was soaked through from head to toe, even with a waterproof jacket. You want to invest in those really good, breathable waterproofs, and definitely a hat. You lose so much heat from your head. Good to know. I was already bracing myself for the gear situation. It always ends up expensive, these hobbies. Remember when I took up pottery? The cost of the clay alone... Don’t remind me! You had clay everywhere for months. Speaking of expensive… I’m still trying to figure out what to get my cousin, David, for his birthday. It’s next month and I only met him properly last year, at Aunt Margaret’s funeral. Apparently, we’d been to family dos as kids, but I genuinely don’t remember. Oh, David. Yes, a bit of a mystery, isn’t he? Aunt Margaret always kept everyone at arm’s length. It’s strange, thinking about her now. It still feels so recent, even though it's been nearly two years. I miss her terrible jokes. Me too. She was… unique. It was good to finally connect with David though. He lives in Australia, so it was unlikely we'd have met otherwise. We talked for hours at the wake. Said he'd always wondered about his English cousins. It's funny how grief brings people together. It can also drive them apart, sadly. Have you heard anything more about Uncle George? Not good, I’m afraid. Mum spoke to Aunt Sylvia yesterday. They've confirmed it's Parkinson’s. She said he's… struggling.

Dad, seriously, you wouldn’t believe what Mrs. Davies was going on about in History today. It was all about Morse code! Like, who even  uses  Morse code anymore? Ah, Morse code. Now there's a skill. Used to be proper important, you know. Back in the day, ships, wartime… saved a lot of lives, that did. Yeah, yeah, she told us. It just seems… pointless now. When we can just text each other instantly. Honestly, I sent Liam like, fifty texts this morning. Fifty! Blimey. That’s… a lot of thumbs working. Are you alright for results day next week? You seem a bit distracted. Sort of. I mean, I’m trying not to think about it. What if I mess it all up? Then I won’t get into uni, and… Now, now. Don’t you start that. You’ve worked your socks off. You’ll be just fine. Whatever happens, happens. We’ll sort it. Easy for you to say. You’re not the one needing A-levels to get student finance. True enough. Though dealing with Vodafone sometimes feels like needing an A-level in frustration management. Speaking of phones, mine’s playing up again. Keeps dropping calls. They said they’d send a new SIM, but knowing them… Probably stuck on an Amazon delivery van somewhere in Milton Keynes. Remember that garden gnome you ordered? Took three weeks! Don’t remind me. It was a gift for your Auntie Brenda. She loved it, though. Says it keeps the slugs off her petunias. Anyway, back to your results. Have you mapped out a route to the uni campus yet, just in case? You know, to scope it out? Not yet. I was thinking of doing it on Saturday. Maybe we could go? And then grab some food afterwards? I’m craving that new pasta place near Piccadilly. Sounds good. We can. I'll check the traffic. Getting around Manchester on a Saturday is…an experience. Actually, did you see those shoes you were looking at on eBay? They’ve gone down in price. Really?! Oh my gosh. Send me the link! I thought they were way too expensive before. Maybe if I do well on my results, they can be a treat. There you go. Positive reinforcement. That’s the ticket. Though maybe we should stick to food shopping first. We’re almost out of vegetables. Your mum’s been hinting about needing more greens in our diet.

Man, it’s good to actually  be  here, innit? Feels like ages since I’ve seen this place – and you! How’s uni treating you, seriously? Last I heard you were drowning in coursework. Tell me about it. It's been… intense. Just finished my dissertation, thank God. Handed that monster in last week, feel like a weight’s been lifted. Properly knackered though. What about you? Still battling with the coding? Battles is an understatement. I swear, my computer actively  resists  me. I'm trying to get this AI to actually, you know,  do  something interesting, but it’s just spitting out gibberish. The internet has become my enemy, honestly. Endless debugging. Yeah, I get that. The struggle is real. Speaking of the internet, you remember how we were talking about Japan last year? I was proper down a rabbit hole looking at flights. Japan? Serious? You actually started looking? I thought that was just a “one day…” kinda thing. Nah, I got fully invested. Tokyo looks insane, right? All those lights, the food… I was looking at these little ramen places tucked away in alleyways. I found a blog written by this guy who lived there for a year, he had a whole list. Sounds incredible. Though, realistically, when are we talking? Post-graduation? Because right now, funds are… limited. Ramen over here is instant noodles, let’s be real. Definitely post-grad. I’m thinking maybe next summer? If I can get a decent internship sorted, I reckon I could save up enough. I’ve started looking at TEFL courses too, you know, teach English over there. Long-term plan, yeah? That’s ambitious, man. Good ambitious. I’m still trying to figure out what I'm doing  after  I hand in my thesis. Thinking about trying to get into a game development company, maybe. Pretty cutthroat industry though. It is. But you're good, you've always been good with that stuff. Remember that game you made when we were like, fifteen? The one with the dodgy graphics but the surprisingly complex storyline? Oh god, don't remind me! That was a disaster. But yeah, I enjoyed it. I think I just need a push, someone to tell me I’m not wasting my time. Easier said than done, innit? Nah, you’re not wasting your time. You got skills. Look, we’ve both got this looming exam stress thing hanging over us still.

Honestly, Dad, you've got to get a smartphone. It’s not the devil's work, you know. I was showing Mum how to video call just yesterday, and she was delighted to see little Leo making faces. Oh, she was, was she? She didn’t mention a word to me. Though, knowing her, she probably did, and I was too busy pruning the roses to listen. Still, I’m perfectly happy with my little Nokia. Does the job. Calls. Texts. What more do I need? You're both daft as brushes, the pair of you. Back in my day, a phone was chained to the wall! And we were grateful for it! Though I admit, all this Facebook business… seems a bit pointless showing everyone what you had for breakfast. It’s not just about breakfast, Grandad! It’s keeping in touch. Seeing photos. I saw Sarah’s photos from Buckfast Abbey last week. Looked lovely, didn’t it? It  is  lovely. We went a few years ago. The gardens are breathtaking, and the stained glass… truly remarkable. Though all that incense gave me a dreadful headache. Buckfast Abbey? Now  there’s  a place. Used to go there with your grandmother. They made a tonic wine, you know. Powerful stuff.
