Cured all sorts of ailments. Or so she claimed. Probably just enjoyed a little tipple! Speaking of trips, what are we thinking for next year? We talked about Cornwall, but maybe somewhere a bit further afield? I was looking at cruises. Cruises? Oh, I don’t know about cruises. All that enforced merriment. And the sea can be so unpredictable. Remember that time on the ferry to France, Arthur? Nearly lost my lunch over the side. Lost more than your lunch, old girl! You were as green as a gherkin! No, cruises aren't for you, Beatrice. Too much fuss and bother. A nice, quiet cottage in the Cotswolds, that’s what you need. Hmm, the Cotswolds  are  lovely. But a cruise could be good. They do Caribbean ones, Mediterranean ones… and you don’t have to worry about packing and unpacking. Packing is half the fun! And you need good travel insurance, you know. Especially now with everything going on. I read an article about a woman who spent a fortune on medical bills in Spain because her insurance didn't cover pre-existing conditions. Insurance… Bah! A racket, the whole lot of it.

Honestly, you two look so relaxed! Belgium clearly did you good. How was it overall? Oh, Brighton’s a bit… brisk, after Bruges, I tell you. It was lovely, really lovely. Though driving… that was an experience. An experience is putting it mildly, Harold. An absolute nightmare! That sat nav of yours, honestly, it tried to send us down roads narrower than my Mini Cooper! It was cutting-edge technology, Daphne! It  said  it was the fastest route. Faster to a demolition derby, maybe. Oh Dad! You and technology… never a good mix. Did you at least manage to see some sights? Mum, you were saying something about the markets? The markets were  amazing , darling. Bruges had a lovely market square, all cobbled stones and beautiful flowers. And the lace! I got you a little something, actually. It's in my bag, don't peek. Oh, Mum, you shouldn’t have! You really didn’t have to. And the chocolate! Don't even get me started on the chocolate. I swear, I came back two stone heavier. Daphne kept buying me pralines… supposedly for ‘medicinal purposes’. They were fueling your sightseeing, Harold! You needed the energy after complaining about the sat nav. Honestly, that thing. It wasn't even picking up road signs properly. We ended up in a farmyard at one point! A farmyard?! Seriously? Serious as a heart attack. A cow looked at me like  I  was the one who was lost. And then trying to reverse out... the road was covered in, well, you can imagine. Oh, Dad! That sounds… chaotic. You should’ve just stopped and asked for directions. Asked for directions? From  Europeans ? They’d have given me a ten-minute lecture on the history of the road before even pointing me in the right direction! No thank you. That's a bit harsh, Harold. Most people were very helpful, actually. Except for that waiter… the one who brought me the mussels. What about the mussels? Were they bad? Not bad, darling, just… small. And they didn't serve them with enough chips! It's just not the same with a handful of frites. And the service was so slow! I was practically waving my arms to get his attention. Your father was asleep by the time they arrived. I was resting my eyes! It had been a stressful drive, thanks to the aforementioned technological marvel.

Right, onions are softening nicely. Honestly, I think this ragu is going to be  good . Maybe even worthy of a second helping. Which, let’s be realistic, happens rarely with my cooking. Don’t be so self-deprecating! You make a cracking shepherd’s pie. And remember that lemon drizzle? People were practically fighting over the last slice. That was a fluke. Pure luck. Speaking of fighting, have you seen what Carol posted on Facebook? Another holiday photo. Maldives this time. Honestly, the woman’s permanently on vacation. Carol’s always been a bit… flamboyant. Though, a bit of sun sounds rather appealing right now. Especially with the weather turning. Is the wood delivered for the fireplace yet? Not yet, no. I chased them up this morning. Apparently, “logistical difficulties”. Honestly, what even  are  logistical difficulties when it comes to wood? They just chop it down and deliver it, don’t they? Probably a fancy term for ‘we’re too busy’. They always use those terms. Still, it’ll be lovely to get a fire going. Makes the whole room cosy. Reminds me of Scotland, actually. My gran always had a roaring fire going, even in summer. Oh, and the smell. It’s so… comforting. Though, it does bring back memories of having to lug buckets of coal up the stairs. Not so comforting then! Oh, speaking of smells – have you noticed Mrs. Henderson’s been wearing that awful perfume again? The one that smells like someone emptied a bottle of cheap air freshener into a bag of mothballs? Oh,  that  one. It assaults the nostrils, doesn’t it? It lingers for hours. You can smell it down the street. It's a shame, she's lovely, but the perfume… It’s a crime against fragrance. Honestly, a simple rose scent would be preferable. Did you remember to order those lilies for Mum? Her birthday’s next week. I did! They’re being delivered on Tuesday morning. White lilies, her favourite. And I’ve booked a table at The Ivy for us all. Oh, that’s lovely! She’ll adore that. You are a star. Right, need to add the tomatoes. Have you got the wine open? I’m feeling like we’ve earned a glass while this is simmering. Already on it. A nice Merlot, as requested. And I've been thinking...we should invite Ben and Sarah over for dinner soon.

…and honestly, the heat in Queensland was just relentless. I’d been used to a Bristol summer, you see, a bit of warmth, a bit of drizzle, and suddenly it was just… furnace-like. Queensland, eh? My son spent a year out there, near Brisbane. Said it was a good life, but the flies! He’s a bit of a stickler, mind you. Used to complaining about things. Always was. Brisbane’s lovely. I lectured at a university there for a semester. The students were brilliant, very enthusiastic. Though, trying to explain the nuances of the Sheffield dialect to them… that was a challenge. Oh, the Sheffield dialect! I’ve always admired it, so robust. Very different from the… gentler tones of the West Country. Though, I have to say, some of those Northern expressions completely flew over my head when I first encountered them. Robust is one word for it, love. My wife used to say it sounded like everyone was perpetually arguing! It’s a very direct way of speaking, you see. No beating around the bush. I spent half my working life dealing with businessmen, you wouldn’t catch  them  speaking like that – always suits and trying to soften everything. Dreadful! That’s interesting. I’ve always found a bit of directness refreshing, actually. Trying to decipher what someone  really  means when they’re being overly polite can be exhausting. I had a colleague, down in London, who was the master of it. All smiles and subtlety, and a complete shark underneath. Oh, the Southerners! Don't get me started. All that ‘lovely’ and ‘darling’… it feels so insincere. I taught English as a Foreign Language for years, and honestly, the hardest students to understand weren’t the Japanese or the Koreans, it was moving to London to train the teachers! You’ve hit the nail on the head there. I used to joke that you needed a translator to understand a Londoner. Though, the business world is full of it. Trying to get a bank loan, for instance… hours of polite conversation, endless paperwork, and ultimately, a ‘no’ delivered with the utmost regret. It's a performance, isn’t it? Everything's a performance. I remember trying to explain to a class of students why we say ‘it’s raining cats and dogs.’ They were utterly baffled. Honestly, sometimes I’m baffled by it too. It's the poetry of language, I suppose.

Honestly, this pierogi is… unexpected. I mean, good unexpected, but not what I anticipated in a vegan restaurant. It’s… beetroot and horseradish? Yeah, Polish food is full of surprises. They  love  their beetroot. And horseradish, you’re right. It’s a flavour combo, isn't it? I saw a place advertising vegan golabki earlier – stuffed cabbage rolls. Apparently they use mushroom and rice filling. Oh, that sounds… substantial. I’m trying to avoid substantial. I’m on a mission to reduce my screen time, and substantial meals feel… conducive to inertia. It’s pathetic, I know. No, it's relatable! I'm constantly battling it. Though my problem is less inertia and more endlessly scrolling through Instagram. It's a total time suck. Have you seen what’s happening with TikTok at the moment? All the US politicians trying to ban it. Oh, I skimmed something about that. Is it actually going to happen? I barely even  look  at TikTok. Too many teenagers doing… whatever it is they do. I'm mostly on Facebook, keeping an eye on family, and occasionally getting sucked into conspiracy theories via my brother. It’s a dark hole. It’s chaos. Apparently, they're worried about data security and Chinese influence. Though honestly, the algorithms on  all  these platforms are manipulating us. I’ve started unfollowing a bunch of accounts just to see what happens to my feed. It’s terrifying how quickly it changes. You sound like you're doing a sociological experiment! That's rather clever, actually. I've been trying to find something good to listen to instead of watching things. Podcasts, you know? But everything feels either true crime – which depresses me – or self-help, which feels… condescending. Oh, I get that. I’ve been into a few history podcasts actually. Dan Carlin’s ‘Hardcore History’ is amazing, though it’s  long . Like, six-hour episodes. But they're captivating. He does really in-depth dives into historical events. Six hours?! Good heavens. I barely have the concentration for a thirty-minute program. I tried watching a drama series the other night. “The Crown,” everyone raves about it. But I kept checking my phone! It's awful. That’s the problem, isn’t it? Everything’s competing for our attention. Have you tried anything on BBC Sounds? They’ve got some decent radio dramas and documentaries. I listened to a really good one about the suffragettes last week.

Right, so swimming is definitely on for Saturday morning, agreed? Unless someone has a sudden aversion to chlorine. Can I take Finley? And can we get those little armbands shaped like sharks? I don't  need  armbands. I’m a good swimmer! Finley can come, sweetheart. And we’ll see about the shark armbands. Though you  are  getting quite confident, Leo. Remember last time you were pretending to be a submarine and kept dunking Finley’s head? It was an accident! He kept splashing me! Right, an accident. And then after swimming, Pippy's mum said she’s happy to have you both for a couple of hours while I sort out… well, everything. Yay! Pippy’s fun! We built a castle! A really, really big castle! And we pretended it was a dragon’s lair! And Pippy was the dragon! That sounds wonderful. Now, I was thinking… Remember how Pippy wants a Blue Peter badge? Yeah! She’s been telling me all about it! Well, she already sent off her entry about building the castle, but she needs a photograph of us all with it. Do we have a good photo? I look really silly in all the photos! You never look silly. Let’s have a look on my phone. Oh, here's one... Hmm, a bit blurry. And another... You're both pulling faces. This one's better! Right. Sorted. Can we see Pippy’s Travelling Circus again? It was so good! We might be able to arrange something next week. Her mum said she's doing a little show for the neighbours soon. It’s amazing what she can do with puppets and scarves. She made the puppets talk! It was creepy! But cool. It's meant to be a bit creepy! Right… now. Slightly more grown-up topic. I was looking at passports. Yours are both… well, let’s just say they need renewing before we even  think  about a holiday. Holidays are fun! Can we go to the beach? I want to go to a castle! A  real  castle! We'll see. Passports first. And then... oh, did you know Auntie Carol told me something completely bizarre? She said she read online that in some parts of China, they eat  very  old eggs? Like, months old! Ewwww! That’s disgusting! I know, right? Apparently, it’s a delicacy! She said the yolk turns all… green.

Right, so then she was saying, like, he just… doesn’t anymore. And she’s proper stressed, yeah? Like, really upset about it. Oh, no. That sounds awful. How old are they both? Early thirties, I think. Him maybe a bit older. She’s been with him for, like, eight years, so you’d think… you know? It's just, she's worried it's something  she’s  doing, but her mate was saying it’s probably just… you know. Erectile dysfunction? Is that what she thinks? She didn’t say the words exactly, but that’s definitely what she meant. She was all roundabout, like "it just doesn’t happen how it used to" and “he seems… distant”. It was a bit awkward, to be honest. I didn’t really know what to say. God, that  is  awkward. Especially if it’s something medical. It's not exactly something you can just… fix with a pep talk, is it? Exactly! I just said, “Well, maybe he’s stressed with work?” trying to deflect, but she didn’t look convinced. She said his work’s been quiet lately. Ugh. It's a tricky one. They really should talk to a doctor about it, shouldn't they? There's stuff they can do. All those adverts on telly… She said she tried to suggest it, but he just brushes it off. Says he's “just tired”. Men, honestly. Always pretending everything’s fine when it clearly isn’t. It’s like, just  go  and get it checked out! It's a pride thing, I reckon. A lot of them are embarrassed to even talk about it. Which makes it worse, obviously. It’s not like breaking a leg, it feels… personal, I suppose. Yeah, that makes sense. But it's affecting their relationship! She was saying they've barely been intimate for months. It’s causing a proper rift between them. Months? That’s a long time. It’s understandable she’s upset. I mean, sex is a big part of a relationship, isn't it? She thinks so. She was saying she feels rejected and unloved. It’s just… sad, innit? You want your friends to be happy. It is. And it’s really hard to offer advice when you don't know all the details. It's like, you don’t want to say the wrong thing and make it worse.

Right, so I was thinking, for tonight, we could do the chilli with the rice, but I'm really trying to keep the Healthy Extra B choice down, you know? And rice doesn’t  quite  cut it. Ooh, good point. Maybe swap the rice for sweet potato? It's free, obviously, and fills you up so much more. Although, I did see someone on the Slimming World Facebook group saying sweet potato counts as a tiny bit of speed food, so… tiny bit of syn potential. Oh, well, a  tiny  bit isn't the end of the world, is it? I’m just trying to be super strict this week. I weighed myself this morning and it was… frustrating. The scales are a liar, honestly. They jumped up half a pound. Half a pound! Scales are evil. Honestly, I swear they’re conspiring against us. I had the same thing last week. I think it’s something to do with the battery being low or… I don’t know, witchcraft. Anyway, chilli is good. Have you got that spice mix I got from Sainsbury's? The one with the smoky paprika? Oh yeah, the one you said was "life-changing”? It’s in the cupboard. It  is  good, actually. Makes it feel less… bleak. Are you worried about syns in the tomatoes? I always feel like they're secretly full of sugar. Nah, chopped tomatoes are free. It’s the passata you need to watch. And pre-made sauces. That’s where the sneaky syns hide. I'm thinking we can have a massive portion of broccoli with it too. Bulk it out, you know? And maybe some of those double peas you got from Iceland? Brilliant! Double peas are a lifesaver. I’m glad I impulse-bought them. They’re frozen solid though, might take ages to defrost. Oh, and I’ve got a new zero-calorie syrup - mint chocolate chip. For my tea later. Don’t judge. Mint chocolate chip? Okay, that  is  a bit decadent. But you deserve it! I’ve been eyeing up some of those flavored syrups for ages. Are they actually any good or do they taste artificial? I haven’t tried it yet, but it smells amazing. It's one of those Skinny Syrups ones. Apparently, they’re surprisingly good. Speaking of treats, are we still on for treat day on Saturday? I'm thinking maybe a small portion of cauliflower cheese with the roast.

Honestly, I’m starting to think Italy’s a disaster waiting to happen. Just…the logistics of getting around, the crowds… Disaster is a strong word, love. We’ve managed worse than Italian train schedules. Remember that camping trip in the Lake District? The tent pole snapped, it poured, and you were convinced a badger was trying to get in. That was  different . That was an act of God, and possibly a very determined badger. Italy is…organised chaos. And I just want a relaxing holiday. Somewhere we can actually switch off. Right. Relaxing. So, no hiking through the Dolomites then? Definitely no Dolomites. I was thinking… Cornwall. Honestly. A little cottage, the sea air, cream teas… Cornwall? That’s…surprisingly sensible. I was bracing myself for Iceland. Iceland is for adventurous couples who  enjoy  being cold and damp. We are, predominantly, a ‘sun lounger and a good book’ kind of couple. Fair enough. Though I did always fancy seeing the Northern Lights… Still, Cornwall sounds…nice. We could finally get around to visiting that pottery place you’ve been talking about for years. Oh, the one near St Ives? Yes! And we could walk the coastal path. And maybe…just maybe…I could finally finish that short story I started about the lighthouse keeper's daughter. The one with the mysterious ship? Still going with that? It’s evolving. Now it involves a smuggled parrot and a surprisingly complex blackmail plot. I’m thinking of entering it into that local writing competition. Go for it! You’ve got a real knack for that sort of thing. Though, perhaps tone down the parrot. It sounds a bit…fluffy. It’s symbolic! The parrot represents…freedom! And a bit of squawking chaos, admittedly. Speaking of chaos, have you been following this latest political debacle? Honestly, they’re all at it. Briefly. I try to avoid the news. Gives me a headache. It's all just shouting and pointing fingers. Exactly! And then they wonder why no one trusts politicians anymore. It’s a self-fulfilling prophecy. It's making me rethink everything. Maybe I should just give up being a PA and become a full-time novelist and live in that Cornish cottage writing about parrots. Now  there's  a career change. Though, who would manage me then? I’d need a PA. Good point. It's a vicious circle. Oh, and something else I’ve been thinking about.

Right, so, the 18th is definitely free then? For your mother’s birthday lunch? Aye, completely. Cleared it with the boss months ago, truth be told. She knows how much family means to me. Though she did give me a look when I said it was for a lunch, not a full-blown party. Well, your mother isn't one for fuss, is she? A nice roast, good company, that’s all she wants. I’ve booked The Black Swan, remember? They do a lovely shoulder of lamb. Oh, brilliant. Good choice. She’ll be chuffed. Did you see the postcard I sent from Skye? Of the Old Man of Storr? It was lovely, actually. Very atmospheric. You and Margaret really did have good weather for it, judging by the picture. Though I did think…it looked a bit bleak, even for Scotland. Bleak? Nah, dramatic! It  is  dramatic scenery. It wasn’t always sunny, mind. We had a couple of days of proper drizzle. But mostly, we got away with it. Margaret’s already talking about going back next year. She always does. You’d think she’d be craving sun after a Nottinghamshire winter. Speaking of which, what are your plans for next weekend? Anything exciting? Not particularly, no. Bit of gardening, maybe. The roses need pruning. And I promised young Thomas I’d help him with his physics homework. He’s struggling with momentum, apparently. Ah, the bane of every teenager’s existence. Momentum. I remember tutoring students on that for years. It’s all about understanding the concepts, not just the equations. That’s what I keep telling him! He just wants a formula he can plug numbers into. You wouldn't believe the argument we had. It reminded me of debates we used to have about…well, everything, really. Indeed. We were always argumentative, weren't we? Though I suspect it was usually me starting it. Have you been following the latest polling on Scottish independence? It’s…unsettling. Aye. It’s getting a bit hairy, isn't it? You'd think people would have learned something from the last referendum, but no. Seems everyone’s dug their heels in even further. Honestly, I don’t envy Humza Yousaf his position. It's a complex situation, isn’t it? So much history, so much emotion tied up in it. I worry about the ramifications, especially for the UK as a whole.

Right, so we’re all agreed then? We’re going to draw pictures to send to the families coming from Syria? Yes! Can I use the glitter pens? Please? I want to draw a really good chair. A comfy one. Glitter pens are a  maybe , sweetheart. We don’t want to get glitter  everywhere , do we? And that’s a wonderful idea, darling. A comfy chair is exactly what someone might need. But it'll make the picture pretty! They'll be happy! It will, yes. But maybe we save the glitter for a little border, okay? More manageable. Now, what kind of chair are you thinking of, Leo? A big one. With arms. And cushions. They look tired, Mummy. On the news. You’re very thoughtful, Leo. You’re right, they’ve had a very long and difficult journey. A comfy chair would be lovely. Is it like the armchair in the living room? Not  exactly . More… squishy. Like Gran’s chair. I'm drawing a chair too! It's going to be pink and sparkly! And have wings! Wings? That’s a very imaginative chair, Lily! That sounds fantastic. It sounds like a princess chair! What are you both thinking of drawing around the chairs? Flowers! Lots and lots of flowers! And a sunshine! I’m going to draw a house. A safe house. And maybe… a garden. With apples. Oh, that’s beautiful, Leo. A safe house and a garden with apples. That’s exactly what they need, isn’t it? Somewhere to feel safe and grow things. It’s lovely that you’re thinking about that. Mummy, are they scared? They  were  scared, Lily. They had to leave their homes very quickly because it wasn’t safe there anymore. But they’re coming here now, to a place where they  will  be safe. And your pictures will help them to know that people here care about them. Will they get our pictures before they get to their house? We’re going to send them to the organisation helping the families, and they'll make sure they get there soon after they've settled in. It's a little gift to say 'welcome'. Will they understand my sparkly chair? Absolutely! A sparkly chair is a universal sign of happiness, I think. It doesn’t matter what language you speak, everyone understands sparkles! Mummy, we had a test at school today.

Honestly, I’m still reeling from Sarah’s announcement. Twins! Can you believe it? Twins! Wow. That  is  a lot. She always did do things in a big way, didn’t she? Remember her wedding? Full-on Bollywood extravaganza. Oh, absolutely. It was incredible. But twins… it's different, isn't it? Especially after she’s been trying for so long. I’m so happy for her, genuinely, but… a little overwhelmed just  thinking  about it. It's a huge shift. And poor Ben. He seemed a bit shell-shocked when he told me this morning. I think he was expecting the one, maybe, but definitely not two. Exactly! I bet. He's usually so cool and collected. Perhaps he is excited, just in shock. We need to make sure we offer to help properly. Not just the usual “let me know if you need anything”, you know? Like, actual practical help. Agreed. I was thinking maybe we could organise a meal roster once they're settled. Or offer to do some shopping for them. They're going to be so busy. Brilliant idea. And maybe check in on her teaching schedule? She was already stressing about maternity cover and now it’s doubled the complexity. Good point. Speaking of teaching, I had a nightmare with the Year 2s today. Little Leo decided to dismantle the entire Lego castle during story time. Just… piece by piece. Oh, Leo. He's a character, isn't he? Remember when he tried to trade his packed lunch for my earrings? How could I forget? Absolute chaos. It took me twenty minutes to rebuild that castle. It’s moments like that you question your career choices. Tell me about it! But then you get the little breakthroughs, right? Like when Maya finally understood fractions? True. That was a good moment. She beamed. You could see the penny drop. It's the good days that keep you going, I suppose. Have you heard from Chloe lately? She's been a bit quiet. No, not for a couple of weeks. She mentioned she was going through a rough patch with her mum, but she didn’t go into detail. I messaged her a few days ago but haven’t had a reply. Oh dear. That doesn't sound good. Maybe we should give her a call? Not push, just check she’s alright. Good idea. I'll try tomorrow.

Honestly, this is exactly what I needed. Fresh air, no students emailing… bliss. Tell me about it. Though I’m starting to suspect all this peace and quiet is a cunning plan to lure us into a false sense of security before term starts again. Like a tranquilizer before the storm. You’re probably right. Speaking of storms, did you hear about Old Man Hemmings? Swears he saw a hare running across the field yesterday, right before Mrs. Peterson’s prize-winning roses got completely flattened. You’re kidding! He still believes in all that stuff? A hare predicting disaster? Apparently! He told me he’s been warning people for weeks, saying a black cat crossing the path was a bad omen. It’s quite endearing, actually. Though I wouldn't want to be on the receiving end of his prophecies if something  did  go wrong. He’s a character, that’s for sure. Reminds me a bit of my grandad. He used to insist you shouldn’t walk under ladders and always touch wood. I think he genuinely believed a policeman would materialize out of thin air if you broke those rules. Oh, lovely. A superstitious policeman! Imagine. Though, thinking about policemen… did you see that article about Professor Davies getting a write-up in the paper? The one about the historical reenactment gone wrong? Yes! Apparently, his portrayal of a medieval tax collector was…a little too convincing. A  little ? He apparently confiscated a student’s phone and demanded payment in “livestock.” Apparently, the police had to be called. It's all over the university intranet. Incredible! He’s always been a bit eccentric, but that’s a whole new level. Good publicity for the history department though, I suppose. “Professor stages realistic medieval tax revolt!” That’s what the Dean’s saying, anyway. Trying to spin it as ‘immersive learning’. I think the students are just amused. It’ll be a legend for years. Guaranteed. It’s the kind of story they’ll be telling freshers during orientation week for decades. Honestly, university life is never dull. Makes you wonder what fresh chaos awaits us this term. Don’t even start. I’m trying to enjoy this moment of peace. Speaking of enjoying things… have you started thinking about holiday plans at all? Anywhere you fancy escaping to when we finally get a break? I’ve been idly browsing, yes.

Dad, honestly, you won’t believe the state of my phone battery. It’s practically non-existent. I’m charging it everywhere I go now. These newfangled things. Always needing a plug. Back in my day, a phone was for making calls, and it lasted a week on a single charge. Simpler times, eh? You say that about  everything , Dad! But seriously, I need a new one. Maybe when I finish this degree, I’ll treat myself. Speaking of treating myself, have you booked those fishing trips yet? You promised to take me before I go back to uni. Nearly. Just need to check the tides. Old Man Hemmings reckons there’s a good run of bass coming up. Though, getting the gear sorted… that’s another matter. It’s all packed away in the garage, covered in dust. And then there's the van… What about the van? You said you were going to hire one to clear out Mum’s old stuff from the shed. Going to, yes. But they’re all booked up for weeks! Apparently, everyone’s moving house at once. And the ones that  are  available want a fortune. It’s daylight robbery, I tell you. Should’ve just done it months ago. Well, maybe we can look online together later? There might be some last-minute cancellations. Oh! Did you manage to get tickets for the Great Dorset Steam Fair? I know how much you love it. Got ‘em! Got ‘em! Friday and Saturday. Roy’s coming with me this year. Said he wants to see the Fowler engines. They’re his favourite. That’s nice. It’ll be good for you both to get out. Are Uncle George and Auntie Maureen going to try and make it? Maureen’s knee is playing up again, so I doubt it. George might come down on Saturday. He's always saying he wants to, but then he always finds something. Honestly, getting the family together is like herding cats. Tell me about it. Hey, have you seen that little antique shop opened up in the High Street? I walked past it yesterday, and it had some really interesting bits and bobs. I thought of you straight away. Really? What sort of things? I used to be quite good at spotting a bargain. Always had an eye for quality, you know. Though, recently, everything seems overpriced. Just because it’s old doesn't mean it’s valuable.

Honestly, the thought of them knocking down the library… it just feels wrong, doesn’t it? It’s been there forever. It is a bit shocking, isn’t it? I saw the plans online. A multi-storey car park. Seriously? Do we  really  need another one? Exactly! We already have two within a ten-minute walk. It feels like they just want to concrete over everything, don't they? The council seems determined to erase any sense of history. It's that short-sightedness. They never think about the long-term impact. It's not just a building, it's a community hub. Old Mrs. Higgins goes every Tuesday for the book club, and the kids use it for after-school homework. And the architecture! That Victorian façade is beautiful. They spend money on awful modern developments that look hideous after five years, but can't maintain a lovely old building like that? It makes my blood boil. It’s the same with that old pub on High Street, remember? They let it fall into disrepair, then said it was unsafe and had to be demolished. Now it's a block of flats no one can afford. Oh, don’t even get me started on that. It’s all about maximizing profit, isn’t it? They don’t care about preserving the character of the town. Speaking of preserving things, have you had a chance to look at those fabric samples for the sofa? I did, briefly. A bit overwhelming, weren't there? So many choices. I liked that sort of muted teal, I think. What about you? I was leaning towards the grey. It’s more practical, I think, with the dog. He sheds  everywhere . Though the teal is lovely… maybe as cushions? Good idea. Practicality wins, I suppose. Although, I was reading an article online about how people are moving away from greys, saying they look a bit… sad. Sad? A sofa can look sad? That's a new one. Where did you read that? In… it was one of those online design magazines. 'House & Habitat' or something. I was just scrolling through news while I had my coffee. Honestly, half the stuff on the internet is nonsense. You’re not wrong. They’re always trying to convince you that you need to completely redecorate every six months. Did you see anything in the actual newspapers this morning? Not just online fluff?

Oh, this is a good one. Bit cheesy, but good. Do you two recognise this? Hmm? Oh, vaguely. Is it… Erasure? Sounds like it. Belting out the eighties, are we, David? You haven't changed a bit. Still stuck in your youth. Hey! There's nothing wrong with a bit of nostalgia. It's good music! And it reminds me of… well, never mind. So, Chloe, how’s the hair salon? Busy, I presume? Absolutely rammed. It’s been manic since… well, since everything opened up again, really. Everyone wants a new look, apparently. It's exhausting but good. I’m saving for a holiday, finally. That’s brilliant! Where are you thinking of going? I’m leaning towards Greece. Or maybe Italy. Somewhere hot and with good food. I need a proper break. All that standing on my feet... Greece is lovely. We went to Crete a few years back. Beautiful beaches, incredible food. You wouldn’t regret it. Speaking of presents, I’ve been trying to think of something to get Emily for her birthday. She’s so difficult to buy for. She says she doesn’t  need  anything. Ugh, the worst kind of person to buy for! Does she have any hobbies? Anything she's really into at the moment? She's got back into painting, apparently. Watercolours. She used to be really good at art, back in school. But she’s always saying she doesn’t have the time. Perhaps some really good quality watercolour paper? Or a set of professional brushes? That might encourage her to pick it up more. Ooh, or a voucher for an online painting class? Loads of those around now. That’s a good idea! I hadn’t thought of that. Thanks, Chloe. I’m rubbish at this sort of thing. I usually end up getting her a gift card. Don't feel bad. It's the thought that counts. Though a thoughtful present  is  nice. I’ve been trying to get back into reading. I’ve got this huge stack of books, but I just can't seem to focus. That’s the problem with modern life. Too much distraction. I’ve turned the TV off most evenings. It’s amazing how much more you get done. I’ve been binge-watching that detective series, “Shetland.” It’s very bleak, but compelling. The scenery is stunning. Oh, I’ve heard of that!

Right then, lad. So, you’re starting to properly look at cars now, are you? Beyond just posters on your wall, I mean. Yeah, Mum. Properly looking. I’ve been on Autotrader every night this week. Found a few that…aren’t completely awful. “Not completely awful” is a good start, I suppose. What kind of things are you looking at? Don’t tell me it’s one of those souped-up hatchbacks that’ll bankrupt us both in insurance. No! Not souped up. I was looking at…a Ford Fiesta. A few different ones. Or maybe a Vauxhall Corsa. Something small, reliable…sensible. Sensible is good. Very good. Though a Fiesta…insurance on those can be surprisingly hefty. You know, it’s not just the car itself, it’s  who  is driving it. I figured. That’s what I wanted to ask you about, actually. How does insurance even  work ? It seems really complicated. All those different groups and no-claims bonuses… It is complicated, designed to be, if you ask me. Basically, they assess the risk. The car itself is part of that. A sports car, naturally, is higher risk than a…well, a sensible Fiesta. But your age is the biggest factor at the moment. And where you live. Malton’s not too bad, thankfully. York centre would be pricey. So, being sixteen makes it worse? That’s rubbish. I’m a perfectly safe driver! …On the Playstation. I’m sure you are. But insurance companies don’t care about PlayStation skills, love. They look at statistics. Young drivers have more accidents. Plain and simple. Hence the astronomical quotes you’re likely to get. Then there’s the car’s engine size. Smaller is cheaper. And what they call ‘modifications’. Absolutely no modifications. Right. No spoilers. Got it. What about adding  me  as a named driver on your policy? Would that bring it down? It might, but it’s a bit of a double-edged sword. It depends on my no-claims bonus and, honestly, on  your  driving record - even though you have one. If you were to have an accident, it could affect my premium. We’d have to get a quote and see. It is worth looking into. Okay. And what about black boxes? I've seen ads for those. Black boxes…they can be a good option, yes. They monitor your driving – speed, braking, time of day – and reward safer driving with lower premiums.

Honestly, this day… it’s been one of  those  days at work. Just endless meetings about meetings, all leading to absolutely nothing. Sounds rough, Dad. What happened? Did old Mr. Henderson try to take credit for your code again? Worse, actually. New project, looming deadlines, and the boss breathing down everyone’s neck. I swear, the man thinks stress is a motivator. It’s just… debilitating. You really need to start taking those mindfulness breaks, love. Remember that app I showed you? Headspace? Headspace? Oh, right. The one that tells me to focus on my breathing while my inbox is exploding? Doesn't quite cut it, does it? I tried a stress test online yesterday, you know, one of those 'how stressed are you?' quizzes. Said I was operating at 'critical levels'. Critical levels, eh? Sounds serious. Is there anything you can  do  about the workload? Easier said than done. It’s just… the culture, you know? Everyone’s terrified of admitting they’re overwhelmed. It's all 'Yes Man' this and ‘Go the extra mile’ that. Remember the fuss when Ireland legalized gay marriage? It felt like a genuine, national step forward. This… this feels like a step backwards for people’s well-being. It was a good day, wasn’t it? When that vote passed. Such relief. I remember watching the results come in. So, uh… did you guys hear about that new podcast everyone’s talking about? The one about unsolved mysteries? A podcast? No, not really keeping up with those. Though your mother listens to about five different true crime ones. Drives me mad, she does. All that…grim stuff. Is this one grim? It's interesting, actually. Helps me switch off. Speaking of switching off, maybe you should consider talking to someone, love. About work. A therapist? Now you're talking. Look, I appreciate the suggestion, but… It’s not a bad idea, Dad. It's good to talk. And look, maybe we could order a Chinese takeaway tonight? Distract you a bit? A Chinese? Now you’re talking sense. Though I have to say, the quality of the chicken in the curry has really gone downhill lately. It’s like rubber. Oh, don't start on the chicken, dear. It's always a culinary gamble with those places. It’s the words they use on the menus, too. “Succulent.” What  does  that even mean? It means they're trying to convince you it's not old, I suspect.

Honestly, that was a proper near miss with that seagull. Thought it was going to come right through the windscreen. You and your dramatics, love. It was miles away. Though, they  are  getting bolder, aren’t they? Like they own the sky. Reminds me of when your grandad used to say the same about pigeons in Bolton town centre. Grandad said pigeons were flying rats! He did, didn’t he? Always had a strong opinion, our Grandad. Speaking of opinions, anyone fancy debating the merits of driving versus the train again? Because I’m still saying cars are superior. Here we go. Look, darling, you know my position. Trains are more efficient, less stressful, and far better for the environment. Especially considering the traffic we’re about to hit getting closer to the hills. Efficient? We spent three hours waiting for a train to get to Manchester last month! And then it was delayed! At least in a car, we’re in control. These hilltop villages are lovely though, aren't they? Proper postcard material. Makes you think of all those little Italian towns. Always dreamed of visiting Tuscany. Tuscany? Is that where they make pasta? Amongst other things, yes. They also have very steep hills. Look at that view though, Dad's right, it's beautiful. Still, I reckon you could fly over all that quicker, you know, like Bear Grylls. Bear Grylls isn’t known for his punctuality, is he? More for eating bugs and surviving in the wilderness. And speaking of surviving, how’s the Law conversion course going, Sarah? Are you still thinking it was a good idea after the EU referendum fallout? It’s all got so much more complicated. It’s...intensive. And yes, Brexit has thrown a spanner in the works with a lot of things. It’s all very ‘what does European Law even  mean  now?’ But I’m getting there. Just trying to remember all the cases. It’s a lot of kilograms of brainpower needed, not pounds…or is it the other way round? Kilograms, love. Kilograms are weight. Miles are distance. You'd think after all those science lessons… Why do we have miles  and  kilometers? It’s so confusing! It's a legacy of empires, basically. Different systems. Honestly, you’d think we’d have unified everything by now. It’s like the whole debate about metric versus imperial. It's ridiculous.

Honestly, this lentil shepherd’s pie is hitting the spot. I was  craving  something proper comforting. It is good! Though, honestly, I still think you put too much rosemary in everything. It overpowers everything else. Never! Rosemary is a gift from the gods. It elevates everything. Besides, you ate, like, three helpings. I’m with El on the rosemary front. It’s… assertive. But good pie, genuinely. Really filling after a twelve-hour shift. Fair enough. Anyone else thinking about that documentary we watched last night? About the cultured meat? “Shmeat”, as they called it. Ugh, don’t even. I’m still processing. It’s… unsettling. Like, meat without the animal, which is the whole point, but… it feels  wrong , somehow. I thought it was pretty fascinating. And logically, it makes a lot of sense. Way less environmental impact, no animal cruelty... It solves a lot of problems. Exactly! I mean, I'm vegetarian, obviously, but even if I wasn’t, I’d seriously consider it. All this talk about animal welfare… it’s just horrific. Seeing the conditions in most abattoirs… Yeah, but is it really  that  different? You’re still essentially… growing meat. It’s not like suddenly everyone's going to stop wanting burgers. It’s still satisfying that same primal urge, just in a lab. Doesn’t feel like progress if we’re just replacing one form of exploitation with another. That's a good point, actually. It kind of sidesteps the issue of why we eat meat in the first place. It doesn’t challenge the idea that animals are just resources for us. True. But think about the hunting argument. People romanticise hunting, say it’s “natural”, but a quick, clean kill in the wild is probably less suffering than most factory farming. And this is… even cleaner. No suffering at all. Hunting is still terrible though! Taking a life for sport? It's just…oppressive. And it’s often not quick or clean, let’s be real. My uncle used to hunt, and the stories he told… Speaking of unpleasant things, anyone seen the new series of  Curb Your Enthusiasm ? It's absolute gold. Larry David is a horrific human being but I can’t stop watching. Oh my god, yes! The one with the coffee shop and the muffin top? I was cringing so hard. He  always  manages to make the most mundane situations into epic conflicts.

Right, that was a proper rubbish ending, wasn't it? Honestly, all that build-up for  that ? Tell me about it. I knew something was gonna happen with the dog, didn’t I? They always kill off the dog. It's a cinematic rule or summat. Oh, don't! You ruined it for me! I was hoping it would be okay. You’ve got a sixth sense for tragic pet deaths, Liam. Nah, it's just experience. Too many tear-jerkers watched with Nana. She  loved  a sad film. Though, speaking of tragic… did you see that deal on the new Playstation online? Playstation? You're already thinking about Christmas presents in October? It's a bit early, isn't it? Never too early! Especially when it’s a good deal. It was on that site, ShopTo, like, £350 for a bundle. I reckon I could swing that, if I don't go too mental on takeaways this month. You’ll be ‘swinging’ when your student loan lands, won't you? Don’t pretend you’re budgeting, Ben. Hey! I am a responsible young adult! Mostly. Anyway, I’ve been meaning to ask, Daniel, have you applied for any jobs yet? Proper ones, not just…you know. A few. Got another rejection email yesterday. "Highly competitive applicant pool." Translation: someone with a bit more experience. It's brutal out there, init? You've got a good degree though! A First! They can’t just ignore that. Apparently, they can. Keeps saying I lack “relevant experience”. What relevant experience am I supposed to have at 23, living in Whitehaven? Been to Uni, worked at the chippy, that’s about it. You could put down your…er… extreme Minecraft skills? Oh aye, that'll impress 'em. “Proficient in block building and virtual resource management.” I can see it now. Honestly, you're underselling yourself. You're smart, you're capable… it’s just finding something. Maybe you need to broaden the search? Like, look further afield? Further afield? Where? London? I'd need to win the lottery to afford a shoebox apartment there. I was thinking maybe Newcastle, or even Manchester. Not  that  far, and more opportunities. Manchester's alright. Went to a gig there last year, decent night. Though getting the train back was a nightmare. Remember that? Stuck at Preston for three hours. Don't remind me. That was a disaster.

Honestly, this free buffet is a lifesaver. After that panel on legal tech, my brain was properly fried. Did you manage to catch any of it? A little bit. I drifted in and out, mostly during the bit about blockchain. It all felt… a bit much, if I’m honest. More interesting to see who everyone ended up becoming, though, right? Did you spot Amelia Finch? Last I heard she was defending human rights cases in Geneva. No way! I didn’t. Geneva! That’s amazing. I mostly spotted people who’d gone into corporate law, predictably. Loads of grey suits. It makes you wonder if all those all-nighters were  really  worth it for… mergers and acquisitions. Tell me about it. Remember old Mr. Henderson saying “Think of the salary!”? Perhaps he had a point. Though, personally, I’m much happier with the research side of things. Still using my brain, but in a less… cutthroat way. Exactly! I feel the same. Though, I won’t lie, sometimes I fantasize about winning the lottery and just travelling the world. Speaking of which, how was your trip to Italy last month? You were raving about Tuscany before you went. Oh, Tuscany was incredible. Truly. The food, the wine, the countryside… it was just perfect. We stayed in this tiny little agriturismo, ran by a family for generations. I’m trying to convince Ben we need to go back next year. He’s more of a ‘beach holiday’ kind of guy, though. Ah, the classic holiday debate. I'm firmly team ‘culture and history’. I’m thinking Portugal next. I’ve been reading about Lisbon, and it sounds amazing. Plus, it’s relatively cheap, which is always a bonus. My aunt went a couple of years ago and said it was transformative. Portugal’s on my list! My cousin lives near Porto, so I keep meaning to visit. Family gatherings are… an experience, though. My grandma still asks me every single time when I'm going to "settle down and find a nice doctor". Oh, the pressure! Mine's a bit different. Whenever I mention my job, my Uncle Barry inevitably launches into a monologue about how I should have gone into teaching like his wife. “So stable,” he says. “So rewarding.” Sounds familiar. They just don't  get  it, do they? They think anything academic is just… procrastinating with books. Precisely!

Right, honestly, that lecture this mornin’…absolute state it was. Dr. Ainsworth just droned on and on about…well, I don’t even  know  what he was on about, to be fair. Just endless dates and names. Sounds about right for Ainsworth, does it? He's a lovely bloke, but captivating, he is not. What was it on again? The Tudors? Aye, the Tudors. But it wasn’t about the juicy bits, like Henry VIII and all his wives. It was about…parliamentary acts. Parliamentary  acts , Liam! I’m tryin' to get a degree in English Literature, not become a politician. Harsh. Did you take notes at least? You're a champion note-taker, you are. I  tried . But he speaks so monotone, I kept losin’ my place. Ended up drawin' little doodles of corgis instead. Honestly, I reckon I know more about the royal canine family than I do about sixteenth-century law right now. Oh, brilliant. You'll be an expert on corgis by Christmas, then. Seriously though, is it all the lectures that are gettin' you down, or just Ainsworth? It's...buildin' up, innit? Like, the seminar yesterday was good, but then I had that awful one. And I’ve got two more tomorrow. I’m startin’ to feel like all I do is sit in stuffy rooms listenin’ to people talk  at  me. You need a break, love. You’ve been workin’ so hard since term started. I know, I know. But there's so much to do! Essays, readings… it's relentless. Look, I was thinkin'...remember how you were sayin’ your shoulders have been a bit achy? Yeah, a bit. From all the bendin’ over books, I reckon. Well, I saw a flyer for that new place in Headingley, "Zen Den" or somethin'. They do proper massages. Like, proper deep tissue stuff. Oh, really? That actually sounds…amazing. I could really use one of those. I thought so. I was thinkin’ maybe we could go on Saturday? After you’ve finished that essay on Brontë sisters? Reward for finally tackling that monster. You’re readin' my mind. Oh, that sounds absolutely perfect. A proper relaxing afternoon. That's just what I need. Sorted then. It'll do you good. And listen, if Ainsworth’s drone is gettin’  too  much, skip a lecture. Seriously. Your mental health is more important than knowin’ the intricacies of the Statute of Uses, or whatever it was he was rabbitin’ on about.

Right good roast, this. Honestly, Mary, you’ve outdone yourself. Yorkshire puddings are almost… perfect. Almost. Oh, Dad, you always say that. I aim for ‘almost perfect’. Keeps me striving. And you’re just being polite, you always say the roast is good. It  is  good, Arthur. Don't be so cynical, love. It's lovely to have a proper family lunch like this, isn’t it? So rare these days. Rare indeed. Everyone rushing about. Speaking of rushing, has young Thomas sorted out that holiday with his girlfriend? He mentioned something about Spain? I think so. He was on the phone last night arranging it. Something about cheap flights to Malaga. He’s very keen on finding a bargain, that one. Good for him. He deserves a break. Teaching is exhausting. Though, honestly, I'm starting to wonder if  I  deserve a break. The workload is just… relentless. You’ve been saying that for ten years, Brenda. You enjoy it, deep down. Don't pretend you don't. Remember Mrs. Higgins? She retired and lasted a week before she started volunteering at the library. Drove her husband mad. That’s true. Mum does thrive on being busy. Still, it’s good she’s considering slowing down a bit. Though, what  would  she do with herself? Honestly? I think she’d garden. She talks about it constantly. A proper vegetable garden, she says, to ‘be self-sufficient’. Self-sufficient? At our age? Honestly. Though I suppose it beats watching the news. Did you see what’s happening in Calais again? Dreadful. More boats. It’s awful, isn’t it? I read something online about the conditions they’re living in. It’s just… heartbreaking. Makes you feel so helpless. It does. And the politicians just bicker. No one’s actually  doing  anything constructive. It’s all posturing. That's politics for you. Always has been. Always will be. Now, about future plans… I've been thinking. We should look into that cruise we talked about. The Mediterranean one. The one in October? Oh, that sounds lovely, Dad. But isn’t that awfully close to Thomas's wedding? We should probably wait and see when they're finally setting a date. She’s right, Arthur. We don’t want to miss that for a cruise. Though, a bit of sun would be nice. It’s been a damp summer. Fair point. Fair point.

Right, another Monday. Honestly, I’m fuelled entirely by caffeine at this point. How was your weekend, Gareth? Anything exciting happen beyond marking essays? Exciting? Not exactly. Utterly consumed by domestic chaos, more like. We finally started the bathroom renovation. Good Lord. Oh dear. Renovations. A Pandora’s Box of stress, aren’t they? I remember when we did the kitchen… it was a nightmare. Dust  everywhere . Dust is the least of it, Idris. The plumber turned up two hours late, looking like he’d slept in his van. And then he tried to convince me we needed to move the entire soil stack! Move the  soil stack ? Good heavens. What did you say? I nearly choked on my tea, I can tell you. Apparently, it wasn’t ‘up to code’. Which, as far as I could gather, meant he hadn’t bothered to read the plans properly. I had to get his supervisor involved. Honestly, finding reliable tradespeople is like searching for unicorns these days. Tell me about it. We’re thinking of redoing the downstairs loo, just a cosmetic job really, new tiles, that sort of thing. But already the thought fills me with dread. Do you know a decent tiler? Actually, yes. Old Dai Evans. He did a fantastic job for Bronwen Lloyd – you remember Bronwen, History department? – completely transformed her hallway. Bit of a character, mind you. Always talking about rugby. Bronwen, yes, of course! Good egg, Bronwen. Rugby… that’s a small price to pay for a well-tiled floor. I’ll have to get her number from someone and ask about Dai. He’s worth a call. Though, be warned, he only works on Tuesdays and Thursdays. Says it’s lucky days for grouting. Only on Tuesdays and Thursdays? That’s… dedicated. Or possibly eccentric. Either way, I'll bear it in mind. This bathroom of yours – are you gutting the whole thing? Pretty much. New suite, new flooring, the whole shebang. My wife, Carys, has been pinning ideas on Pinterest for months. I swear she’s single-handedly keeping the bathroom tile industry afloat. It’s going to look lovely, eventually. Though I suspect our savings account will be weeping. Pinterest is a dangerous place. My daughter got us into it. Suddenly, our living room needed a ‘feature wall’ and ‘mood lighting’. It’s a slippery slope, I tell you. Exactly! And then there’s the kitchen.

Right, so who wants more curry? This is a good one, isn’t it? A proper vindaloo. Yeah, it’s good! Not  too  spicy, though. It’s lovely, actually. A bit much with the rice, though, I think. My stomach’s already rumbling. Ah, you’re a delicate flower, so you are. Now, Liam, you’re polishing off your plate, good man. Don’t be shy about asking for more. You’re growing like a weed. Dad, you always say that! Well, it’s true! Feels like only yesterday you were trying to eat… what was it? A key? Oh, don’t remind me! He was convinced he could eat metal and gain superpowers. He actually swallowed a small screw! It wasn’t a  small  screw! It was a fairly big one. And I didn’t swallow it! I got it stuck on the roof of my mouth and panicked. Panicked is putting it mildly. You were screaming the place down. I thought you were choking! We had to drag you to the doctor. And they said it would pass. Just…pass. Can you imagine? Baa! Me eat! No, little man,  you  are not eating metal. You stick to the puree. Speaking of which, is Leo behaving himself tonight? He’s finally asleep. Took ages. He’s been obsessed with night deposit boxes all week. Apparently, they're "secret treasure holes". A night deposit box? Where did he even hear about those? Honestly, no idea. Probably some YouTube video. He saw me using one the other day and went wild. He kept trying to put his toy cars in the slot. Kids are peculiar, aren’t they? Right. Liam, your birthday is coming up fast. Any thoughts on what you’d like to do? I’m thinking maybe that big park event in Fitzgerald’s Park? The one with the bouncy castles and the face painting? That sounds good. We can invite a few of your friends. And what about afterwards? A few slices of cake? Yeah, that'd be great! Maybe we could get that horrible history science book you were looking at? The one about, what was it, Victorian surgery? Ugh, Mum! That sounds… gross. But yeah, actually, I kind of want it. It's funny. Strange lad, you are. Alright, a park event and a gruesome history book it is. Now, speaking of gruesome… I was reading an article about the human body the other day and the sheer complexity of it.

So, Elsie, how's the little’un doing with school? Still enjoying it, are she? Oh, she’s a good girl, Amy is. Bit quiet, mind you. But she’s doing well enough. Just started a new project on… well, what  was  it, now? Something about volcanoes, I think. Volcanoes, eh? That sounds exciting. We’re doing the Stone Age at the moment with my Year 5s. Always a hit, that. Lots of cave painting and pretending to hunt mammoths. Ugh, the Stone Age is  so  boring. We just did that last year in Year 4. It's all just rocks and furs. Now, now, young lady. Don't be disrespectful. History's important. Especially learning about where you come from. You wouldn’t want to live in a cave, would ya? No! Definitely not. But it's just… repetitive, you know? She’s right, Arthur. It does get a bit repetitive. Though I suppose it’s good they’re learning something. Bit different to when  I  was at school, wasn’t it? More about sums and sewing, if you ask me. It's always a balancing act, isn't it? Trying to cover everything. Speaking of which, did Amy ever go back to those horse-riding lessons she was doing? She seemed to really enjoy that. Oh, she did! She absolutely loved it. But it got a bit expensive, to be honest. And then the weather turned, and… well, you know Norfolk winters. It’s a bit bleak for riding. Aye, bleak it is. I remember when I was a lad, winter meant staying indoors and playing dominoes. No fancy horse riding for us! Though I always fancied a good gallop, I did. Never had the money for it though. My friend Chloe goes horse riding every week. She got a new pony for her birthday. It's called Sparkle. Sparkle! That’s a good name. I bet that’s a treat. Do you ever go with her? Nah, it’s kinda girly. And I'm not really into ponies. Oh, Amy would have loved a pony! She was always talking about them. We even visited a farm a few times to just… look at them. Remember that place near Attleborough, Elsie? The one with all the animals? Used to take the kids there years ago. Had a lovely little tea room, too. Oh, yes! Farmer Giles’ place! We went there with the grandchildren.

Honestly, this traffic is ridiculous. I thought we’d be there by now. It's just… stationary. It always is, love. Steam Fair always brings it to a standstill. Everyone and their mother decides to come. Remember when we first came, what, twenty years ago? Wasn’t half this bad. Twenty five, Dad. And it  was  bad then! We were practically crawling along the A31. Though, it’s not just the fair, is it? It's everything. All the new builds they're putting up around here. Where are all these people  going  to park? Exactly! And it’s not just parking at the fair, it’s… everywhere. Trying to get a parking space in Gillingham these days is a nightmare. They're building flats on every scrap of land. Flats, flats, flats. That's all they build now. No houses for families. And they’re tiny. Boxes, that’s what they are. You can barely swing a cat. My mate, Arthur, he’s been on the council list for years. He needs somewhere smaller, you know, now the kids have flown the nest. It’s the council housing that’s the problem, isn’t it? There just isn't enough of it. They keep saying they’re building more, but it's never enough to meet the demand. And what about older people, like Arthur? Somewhere safe, with a little garden… It shouldn't be so hard to find. It's awful, isn't it? I was reading about assisted living places, and they’re so expensive. Mum would never be able to afford that. Assisted living… robbery, that is. Charging a fortune for a bit of help. And half the time, the staff are rushed off their feet. No time for a proper chat. It’s true. I see it all the time at work. They try their best, the staff do, bless 'em. But they're so short-staffed. It’s heartbreaking. And then you get families complaining… but it's not the carers’ fault. Speaking of heartbreaking… look at that space over there. Is that… disabled parking? Right at the front? And look how many spaces are empty! Why even bother having them if people just park there anyway? Typical. Always the same. People think the rules don't apply to them. Honestly, you’d think they’d have someone patrolling, handing out tickets. They  should . It’s ridiculous.

Honestly, I’ve been spending hours online looking at allotment layouts. It’s a rabbit hole, isn’t it? You start with ‘easy vegetables for beginners’ and suddenly you’re reading about companion planting and soil pH levels. Oh, I know the feeling. I did the same when I first started trying to keep houseplants alive. It’s amazing how much detail there is. Have you actually  got  the plot confirmed yet? Yeah, finally! I got the email yesterday. Plot 23b, down the back near the compost heap. Not ideal, but beggars can’t be choosers, right? Apparently, it’s a bit overgrown, which is…an understatement, according to the lady on the phone. Oh dear. A bit of a challenge then. But good! Overgrown just means potential. Loads of potential. So, what’s the initial plan? Are you going full-on veggie patch, or a bit of flowers too? Veggies, definitely the priority. I'd love to grow my own salad stuff, you know? Proper, fresh stuff. I'm thinking raised beds for most of it. Makes it a bit easier on the back, and the soil is…well, it’s something. I’ve seen pictures of the allotment, and it’s definitely seen better days. Raised beds are a good shout. And definitely worth it for your back. I helped a friend build some last year, and it made a huge difference. Did you think about what you’re going to grow? Beyond salad, I mean. Broad beans, definitely. I love broad beans. And I was thinking maybe some courgettes, though I’ve heard they’re a bit…prolific. I don’t want to be giving courgettes away to everyone for months on end! Oh, you will be! Everyone gets courgettes. It’s the law. You could try growing a bush variety, apparently they take up less space and are a bit more manageable. And what about potatoes? They do pretty well in this climate. Potatoes are a good idea, I hadn’t really thought about it. I was thinking about doing a little section for herbs, too. Rosemary, thyme, basil…the usual suspects. It’d be nice to just be able to snip off what you need when you’re cooking. Definitely. That’s the dream, isn’t it? Fresh herbs on tap. You’ll need to think about pest control too. Things like netting to keep the pigeons off, and maybe some companion planting to deter unwanted bugs.

Right, so I’m officially breaking up with the idea of trying to make friends with anyone on my course. It’s a lost cause, honestly. Oh no, why? I thought you were getting on alright with Chloe? The one who always steals your pens. Chloe’s a menace, a delightful menace, but… no. It’s just everyone’s already in their little cliques, innit? They all knew each other from sixth form or something. It’s like trying to barge into a pre-existing party. Yeah, I get that. It’s brutal sometimes. Uni friendships are… different. It felt so easy making friends in school, didn’t it? Everyone was just thrown together. Massively. Now it’s like an interview process every time you attempt conversation. “Oh, where did you go to school? What A-Levels did you do?” Like, chill out! I just want someone to share a chip butty with. Exactly! It’s exhausting. I’m clinging onto our friendship for dear life, honestly. You’re my Doncaster lifeline. Oh, don't say that! You’ve got loads of friends at uni, though. You’re always out doing stuff. It’s not the same, is it? They’re good, genuinely, but we’ve known each other since we were practically babies. It’s… different. Plus, they don’t understand half my slag. I tried explaining what a ‘mardy’ face was the other day and got blank stares. Oh, the horror! You have to protect the Yorkshire slang at all costs. It’s a cultural treasure. Anyway, back to my loneliness… I’m thinking of joining the hiking society. Ooh, that’s a good shout! Get yourself out in the Peak District. Distract yourself with scenic views and the possibility of falling in a bog. Falling in a bog isn’t part of my master plan, thank you very much. But yeah, fresh air and exercise. Could be good. What about you? Any luck on the romance front? I feel like it’s been ages since you mentioned  anyone . Don’t even start. I had a disaster date last week. He spent the entire evening talking about his Warhammer collection. Oh, no way! Seriously? Seriously! I tried to steer the conversation towards, like, world events or his favourite film, but he’d always loop it back to miniature figurines and dice rolls. It was… intense. Oh, bless. That’s a  very  specific hobby.

Right, honestly, that last raid was a disaster. Absolute shambles. Liam, you just kept running into walls! He was a bit… distracted, wasn’t he? I think he was admiring the scenery. Honestly, the detail in ‘Eldoria Online’ is stunning, but you gotta focus, mate. Distracted? He was trying to pet a digital badger! A  badger , man! We were supposed to be taking down the Shadow Lord. Priorities, Liam, priorities. Badger did look fluffy though. In his defence. I’m still convinced that Shadow Lord was over-levelled. No way a group of our level should’ve struggled that much. Over-levelled or not, we wiped three times. Three! My resurrection potions are looking mighty low. Did anyone remember to grab more from the market in Oakhaven? I did, actually. Got a stack of ten, and some decent healing salves. They were on offer, couldn’t resist. Should be in my bag. You’re a lifesaver, Chloe. Literally. I used like, half my supply just keeping everyone alive long enough for Liam to… commune with wildlife. Speaking of Oakhaven, anyone fancy grabbing a takeaway later? I’m starving after that. “Spice Palace” is doing their two-for-one deal on the Vindaloo. Vindaloo? You’re a brave soul, Raj. My stomach can barely handle a Madras. I'll stick to a Korma, thank you very much. It's a uni student staple, innit? Cheap and cheerful. Korma’s good. Comfort food. I was thinking of hitting up the campus library later, got a history essay due Friday. Feeling completely overwhelmed by the Tudors. So. Much. Politics. Ah, the Tudors. Henry VIII was basically a walking drama. Though, honestly, I’m struggling more with this coding assignment. Python is actively trying to make me question my life choices. Tell me about it. I’m trying to build a simple game, and it just keeps crashing. I think I’ve introduced a paradox somewhere in the code. It's no Eldoria Online, that’s for sure. I saw Sarah wearing that new jacket today. The one she was talking about, the leather one? It’s proper nice. A bit pricey though, she said. Oh yeah, I saw it on her Insta. Looks amazing. I'm still rocking the same old hoodie I've had since first year. Fashion isn't exactly a priority when you're living off instant noodles. I’ve been meaning to get a new pair of trainers.

Honestly, Doreen next door, you wouldn’t believe. She’s started one of her ‘detox’ diets again. All juice and…well, I didn’t quite catch what else, but it smelled of spirulina. The whole hallway did! Oh, Doreen. She’s a character, isn’t she? Still going on with those things then? I thought she gave up after the cabbage soup debacle of ‘21. You’d think! But no. Apparently, this one’s “life-changing.” She was telling me it’s going to realign her chakras. I just nodded. Honestly, I just wanted her to stop talking about her insides. Sounds…intense. I’m glad I just stick to trying to eat my greens. Did you hear back from Brenda about the cinema? We were thinking of seeing that new Wes Anderson film. Oh, yes, Brenda messaged. She can’t make Friday. Said something about a bridge night commitment. Honestly, bridge! What is it with her and bridge? She’s obsessed. Right? It feels like every time you suggest something, it’s “Oh, I’ve got bridge.” I swear she’s building a fortress of card tables in her living room. Exactly! So, Friday’s no good. How about Saturday afternoon? It's supposed to be raining, anyway. Perfect cinema weather. Saturday’s good for me. I’ve got that deadline looming at work, but I can sneak out for a few hours. Is it the one with Timothée Chalamet? That’s the one! I’ve heard good things. Apparently, it’s very…pink. All the sets are pink. Oh, brilliant. Wes Anderson being Wes Anderson. I love his films. They’re so meticulously crafted, aren’t they? Like little worlds. They are. Reminds me of that one we saw, what was it…  The Grand Budapest Hotel ? That was a good one. Funny, and beautifully done. Oh, loved that one! Ralph Fiennes was  amazing . Have you seen anything good lately? Besides Doreen’s internal struggles, of course. I finally got around to watching that documentary about Bowie,  Moonage Daydream . Honestly, it was breathtaking. Just a wonderful tribute. I was a right Bowie fan back in the day, you know. Oh, I’ve heard about that! I need to add it to my list. I’m currently slogging through a really bleak Scandinavian crime drama. It's good, but…it’s a lot. It requires serious concentration and a strong cup of tea.

…and then she just  launched  into a detailed explanation of the rules for ‘Wingspan’. Like, a twenty-minute rules explanation for a bird-collecting board game. It was intense. Oh, bless her. She does love a good, complex board game, doesn’t she? Is she still going on about getting everyone to play ‘Gloomhaven’ next month? You know it. She's already making a spreadsheet. Honestly, it’s like preparing for a military campaign. I said I might be busy, and she looked genuinely hurt. I think she's trying to fill the void since… well, you know. Since Liam moved to Manchester? Yeah, poor thing. She's always been someone who needs a project, hasn't she? It's good she's got hobbies, at least. Did you manage to avoid actually  playing  Wingspan? I pleaded a headache. A very convincing headache, I might add. I used the excuse that I had that awful interview this morning. Oh, how did that go? The one for the research position at the university? It was…fine. A lot of behavioural questions. "Tell me about a time you failed." "Describe a situation where you had to work in a team." You know the drill. It was a panel of three, and one of them looked like she hadn't smiled since 1987. Oh, those are the worst! It's like they're actively looking for reasons to reject you. Speaking of things that are stressful, I finally booked us that spa day for next Saturday! Oh my god, amazing! I need that so badly. I’ve been running on fumes lately. What did you book? It’s at that place in Shoreditch, the one with the thermal suite. Massages, facials, the whole shebang. We can just lie there and moan about everything. Perfect. I'm already mentally preparing my moan list. It's extensive. Did you see ‘The Undateables’ last night? I did! Oh my gosh, the gentleman who collected garden gnomes! That was…something. I know! Bless him. It’s just lovely to see people being so open and hopeful. Although, his expectations were… ambitious, considering. A little. I was rooting for him, though. It reminded me I really need to catch up with Sarah. I haven’t seen her since Christmas. She’s been really busy with work. Oh, how is she? Last I heard she was editing that cycling magazine?

Right, I’m officially declaring war on this washing machine. It’s eating socks again. It's a black hole for single socks, I swear. Oh, not again. Is it the same one as last week, the blue striped one? No, this is a black one. A perfectly good, perfectly reasonable black sock. Vanished. I've checked inside the drum, behind it, even inside other washing loads. Gone. It's a conspiracy. Maybe it’s clinging to something else? Sometimes they get stuck inside duvet covers, that sort of thing. I’ve turned the duvet cover inside out like a forensic investigator! Nothing. Honestly, I’m starting to suspect a tiny sock-gnome lives inside it. A sock-gnome? Now  that  explains a lot. Here, drink your tea. You’re getting worked up over a sock. It’s the principle of the thing! And it’s a perfectly good sock! Plus, I’m starving. Did you manage to grab anything from the shop earlier? I was up to my elbows in laundry detergent and existential dread. Yeah, got some pasta and that pesto you like. I was thinking we could do a quick carbonara? Unless you fancy ordering something? Carbonara sounds perfect. Though, quick is good. I need to at least  attempt  to make a dent in these research papers tonight. Dr. Evans is having a field day with my methodology. Ouch. Still, you’re brilliant at what you do. He’s just being a… well, you know Dr. Evans. Pedantic. That’s putting it mildly. He once spent twenty minutes critiquing my use of the Oxford comma. Twenty minutes! It's a comma, James! Oh, God. Sounds about right. How are your mam and dad doing, by the way? I haven’t spoken to them in ages. They’re good, actually. Mam’s taken up pottery. Apparently, the kitchen table is now permanently covered in clay. Dad's trying to learn the guitar, which, according to my sister, is torturing the neighbours. Sounds like them. They’re good at finding new hobbies, your parents. What about your sister? How is little Leo? They’re both fine. Leo is currently obsessed with dinosaurs. Apparently, he roars at the postman. Oh, bless him. Sounds adorable. We should really try and get up to Sunderland soon. It's been too long. Definitely. Although prepare for an extended pottery demonstration and a lot of enthusiastic, but probably off-key, guitar playing.

Honestly, the price of houses these days… it’s beyond belief. We were looking at something in Penrith, just a little cottage, you’d think it was a palace with the asking price. It’s the same down south, Mum. Absolutely bonkers. I was helping a friend look in Guildford, and everything's inflated. It's all London money flooding outwards. You’d get a decent semi here for what a garden shed costs them. It’s the ‘premium’ isn’t it? Everything south of… well, Birmingham, really, carries a premium just  because  of where it is. Doesn’t matter if it's structurally unsound or built on a landfill. It’s the postcode. Exactly! And all this talk about leveling up… absolute nonsense. They’re not leveling anything up, they’re just shifting the inequality around. It’s just… frustrating. We thought maybe a little bungalow near the lake, you know, for retirement. Now? Forget about it. Did you see that article about the VW scandal again? It popped up on my newsfeed this morning. Something about further compensation claims? Oh, that’s been rumbling on for years, hasn’t it? The sheer scale of it… deliberately cheating on emissions tests. Incredible. And they still get away with it, more or less. It’s the arrogance of these big companies. Thinking they can just do whatever they want and get away with it. It’s the same with the housing developers. Building cheaply, squeezing every last penny out of everything. I read somewhere that VW were actively trying to delay payouts as long as possible. It’s not necessarily the initial fine, it’s the long-term compensation to people who were misled. The impact on resale values etc. It's a pattern, isn’t it? Accountability seems to be optional for large corporations. It's all lawyers and loopholes and kicking the can down the road. Makes you wonder what else they're getting away with. Speaking of getting away with things…have you seen what they’re charging for petrol now? Don’t even start me on petrol! It’s daylight robbery. And then everyone complains about the price of avocados. Priorities, people, priorities! This whole country is becoming unaffordable. I remember when you could buy a perfectly lovely house in Penrith for under fifty thousand. That sounds like a different lifetime. My parents told me stories about buying their first house in Birkenhead.

Honestly, Doreen, you wouldn’t believe the fuss old Man Hemmings is kicking up now. About the bins again. Not the bins! What's he on about  this  time? He’s a right misery, that one. Always has been. Honestly, you two. Always moaning about someone. It's exhausting just listening to you. It’s true though, isn't it? He went round Ms. Periwinkle, complaining that her recycling bin was overflowing. Overflowing! The poor woman's just got a bad hip, can’t get out there every week. Serves her right for getting one of those fancy blue ones. Should've stuck with the grey. Less noticeable. Frank, honestly! That's dreadful. She's entitled to a blue bin if she wants one. You’re encouraging him, you are. It's just upsetting people for the sake of it. I’m just saying, it’s causing a right palaver. And it’s all because he's got nothing better to do since his pension started. Too much time on his hands, that’s what it is. Speaking of pensions… mine’s landed, thankfully. Though it’s not nearly as much as they said it would be. Inflation, they say. Always inflation. Mine's the same, Geoffrey. It’s a disgrace. Barely enough to cover the heating these days, never mind anything else. They say we’re all supposed to be grateful we even  have  a pension. I heard young Tim down the pub telling his wife she’ll be lucky to get anything. Tim’s just started that new job in IT, hasn’t he? All computers and clever stuff. I wouldn't trust a computer to tell me the time, let alone manage my pension. You say that, Geoffrey, but you were asking me just last week how to set up that online banking. That was… different. I just wanted to see if it  could  be done. Didn't mean I was going to start relying on it. It’s all a bit frightening, isn’t it? Everything online now. It is. Reminds me of that holiday we took to Cornwall. Remember that little B&B we stayed in? The one run by that lovely couple? Oh, yes! The one with the wonky stairs and the full English breakfast? Lovely place. They were wishing they hadn’t started letting their place out to strangers after some builders moved in. Apparently, they were up all hours, playing loud music, and tracking mud everywhere.

Honestly, this Biology essay is killing me. “Explain the evolutionary advantages of altruism.” Like, what even  is  altruism, beyond being a fancy word for being nice? Dude, it’s basically doing stuff for others even if it doesn’t benefit you. Like, risking your life to save someone. Evolutionarily, it doesn’t make sense, right? Shouldn’t it be survival of the fittest,  me  first? That’s what I thought! Mr. Davies was going on about kin selection. Apparently, you’re more likely to be altruistic towards family because they share your genes. So it’s still selfish, just…indirectly. Ugh, Davies. He loves a good complicated explanation. He spent like twenty minutes last lesson explaining how peacock feathers evolved. Twenty minutes! Seriously? It’s just… shiny feathers. Birds like shiny things. End of. Nah, apparently it’s about demonstrating genetic fitness. Like, “Look how healthy I am, I can afford to grow these massive, impractical feathers!” It’s all about attracting a mate. Sounds exhausting. All that posturing. Humans aren't much better, are they? All the flexing on Instagram. Speaking of Instagram… did you guys see that video of old Mr. Henderson falling over in the fruit aisle? It’s gone viral. No way! Mr. Henderson? The one who always yells at us for blocking the biscuit aisle? Yeah! Someone filmed it and put it on TikTok with that sped-up music. It’s hilarious. He was trying to grab a pineapple and completely lost his balance. Oh my god, send me the link. That’s amazing. Though, kinda feel bad for the guy… a little bit. Don’t feel too bad. He’s earned it.
