He gave me grief for accidentally knocking over a display of avocados last week. Said I was a menace to society. Menace to society! Over avocados? That’s ridiculous. It's always the older generation judging us. It's like they think everything was better in their day. Honestly, they probably didn't even  have  avocados when they were our age. You know what I hate though? When people start going on about how ‘woke’ everyone is now. Like, calling out sexism or racism is suddenly a bad thing? Tell me about it. My aunt tried to explain to me why feminism isn’t “necessary” anymore. Said women have “equal rights”. Oh, here we go. The classic ‘but women can vote now!’ argument.

Honestly, the whole thing was a blur. Woke up in recovery, feeling… well, not exactly  right . They said the operation went well, thankfully. No complications, they kept repeating. But it’s just… unsettling, isn’t it? Unsettling is an understatement, love. Having anything poked and prodded inside you… I wouldn't wish it on my worst enemy. How’s the pain now? Are you keeping up with the tablets? The pain's manageable, thankfully. Still a little tender, obviously. And yes, religiously taking the antibiotics and the painkillers. Though they make me feel a bit spaced out, if I'm honest. I nearly put salt in my tea this morning. Salt in your tea! Oh, you  are  feeling it then, eh? Remember when your grandad tried that? Said it brought out the flavour. Nearly gave your nan a heart attack. He was a stubborn old fool, your grandad. Always had to have his own way. Still, a good man. Though I never understood the salt in the tea. Times have changed, Grandad wouldn’t last five minutes these days. Anyway, the consultant said the infection markers are coming down, which is the main thing. He wants to see me again next week, just for a check-up. Good, good. Regular check-ups are key. You need to look after yourself. You’re always rushing around, doing things for everyone else, you forget about number one. Easier said than done, isn’t it? Especially with Mum needing so much help these days. Speaking of which, did you manage to sort out that appointment with the acupuncturist for her back? I did, yeah. Tuesday afternoon. She’s a bit skeptical, bless her, but I told her to give it a go. Anything's worth a try, eh? It can’t hurt. Acupuncture? Hmph. Poppycock. Give her a hot water bottle and a bit of liniment, that’s what she needs. That's what  we  used to do. Your mother always was one for a good liniment rub. Remember how strong she used to make it? Nearly knocked you off your feet, Maggie. I remember! It smelled like turpentine. Anyway, how are  you  two doing? Anything exciting happening in your world? Not much excitement here, just work, work, work. Mrs. Henderson's house was a right state this week. Dust everywhere. Honestly, people live like pigs sometimes. You don’t say. Still, honest work is honest work.

Right, so we were talking about why learning about difficult things, like slavery, is important, even though it’s really upsetting. Do you two understand a little bit about what slavery was? It was…when people weren’t free? And they had to work for other people? That’s a good way to put it, sweetheart. They weren’t free, and they were forced to work for others, often in terrible conditions, without getting paid. It happened a long, long time ago, mostly, but it’s important to remember it so it  doesn’t  happen again. But why did people  do  that? That’s mean! It is very mean, isn’t it? It’s a really complex question, and there isn’t one simple answer. Some people thought they were better than others, which is completely wrong, of course. Others wanted to make money, and they didn’t care how much suffering they caused. Like… bad guys in a story? In a way, yes. But these were real people, doing real, awful things. And it wasn’t just a long time ago. Even more recently, people fought wars over whether slavery should be allowed. Wars? Like with guns and bombs? Yes, sometimes. Wars are also about different ideas and beliefs. America had a big war, called the Civil War, partly about whether people could own other people as slaves. It was a really brutal war, with lots of people getting hurt. Did the good guys win? Eventually, yes. Slavery was made illegal in America. But even after that, people still faced a lot of unfairness and discrimination. It takes a long time to fix things when something has been wrong for so long. Discrimination? What's that? That’s when people aren’t treated fairly because of who they are – their skin colour, where they come from, what they believe. It's still a problem today, sadly. That’s why it’s important to learn about history, so we understand how things got to be the way they are and how we can make them better. So… learning about all these sad things can help people not be mean anymore? Exactly! It can help us understand other people's feelings and learn to be kinder and more respectful. It also shows us how brave people have been in fighting for what's right, even when it was really difficult and dangerous.

Honestly, I’m still reeling from that  Great British Bake Off  final. Poor Rahul! He looked like he was about to faint the whole time. He’s a lovely lad, Rahul. A bit… flustered, perhaps. But a very good baker. I thought Kim-Joy had it in the bag though. Her gingerbread scenes were phenomenal. They  were  amazing! I saw pictures of them online. Did you see the article about Prue Leith’s new cookbook? Apparently, she’s put a recipe in for a Victorian sponge that uses mayonnaise. Mayonnaise?! In a cake? Good Lord. That sounds… questionable. Mayonnaise! That’s what they used to do back in the war, you know. When eggs were rationed. My mum used to make cakes with it. Didn’t taste of mayonnaise, apparently. Just made it nice and moist. Still, sounds a bit odd to be deliberately doing it now. Speaking of odd, did you hear about old Mrs. Higgins next door? Apparently, she’s convinced the foxes are holding meetings in her garden. Oh, not again! She told me last week they were planning a revolution. Said they were tired of being underestimated. She’s a character, isn't she? Though, they  are  getting bolder. I saw one strolling down the high street the other day as if it owned the place. They’re a menace. Honestly. Digging up the lawn, leaving… presents. I’ve been trying to fox-proof the garden, but it's a losing battle. You need a good terrier. That’s what you need. They’ll sort them out quick as a flash. Remember Buster? He’d chase ‘em up a tree without a second thought. Oh, Buster! Good times. He was a proper little scamp. We really miss him, don’t we? We do. Though, I’m secretly relieved not to be scooping up dog poo at 6 am anymore. Remember that time he… well, never mind. Oh please, tell the story! No, no, it's too embarrassing. Let's talk about holiday plans. Are you two still thinking of going to Italy this year? We are, yes. Tuscany, hopefully. We've booked flights, but haven't nailed down the accommodation yet. It’s proving surprisingly difficult to find somewhere that takes dogs. Oh, that  is  tricky. Italy is beautiful though. Have you ever been to Lake Como? It’s stunning. Beautiful? It's full of posh birds and fancy cars!

Right, okay, dishwasher duty team. Poppy, you’re on plates, Leo, you’re tackling the cutlery. And please,  gentle  with the glasses, remember what happened last time? But plates are  boring . Can I do the forks instead? They’re pointy! No pointy forks, Poppy. Plates. I’ll help you with the big ones. Leo, are you managing? Yep! Found a spoon! It’s a  really  big spoon! That’s… good, Leo. Just make sure it goes in the right section. Oh, and no playing with the knives, please. Mummy, did you read me a Harry Potter chapter last night? The one with the… the whatchamacallit… the scary forest? The Forbidden Forest? Yes, I did. And you were very brave listening, weren’t you? Even when Voldemort was… well, being Voldemort. Voldemort’s silly. He has a funny nose. He  does  have a rather distinctive nose, doesn’t he? You two are surprisingly critical literary analysts. Is Harry Potter real? That’s a good question. He’s real in the stories, of course. But he's a character someone  wrote  about. Like… like George Stephenson. Who’s George Stephenson? Oh! He was a very clever man. He lived a long, long time ago, before cars and planes. He invented… well, he really improved steam locomotives! Trains! Trains? Like the one we took to London? Exactly like that one! But the first trains were very different. They puffed a lot of smoke and were quite slow. He was called the ‘Father of Railways’ because he made travelling much easier for everyone. Did he drive the train himself? He did sometimes! And he spent years building the railways, figuring out how to make them strong enough and safe enough. It was really hard work. Imagine trying to build a track all the way from here to… I don’t know, to Norwich! That’s a looong way! It  is  a very long way! He was a proper inventor, though. Very determined. Not at all like… well, not like Draco Malfoy. Draco Malfoy is a bad guy! He is a bad guy. George Stephenson was a good guy. Now, how’s the cutlery coming along, Leo? And Poppy, have you rescued any plates yet? We need to get this done before dinner! I hope this meets your requirements! Let me know if you'd like any adjustments or further conversation. Is there anything else I can help you with?

Right, so I’m officially losing to Amelia on Words With Friends. It’s ridiculous. She just throws down a ‘quixotry’ for triple word score. Who  knows  those words?! Oh, she's a menace. Honestly, Amelia could win Scrabble with a dictionary tied behind her back. You need to start strategically using those blank tiles, Leo. That’s the key. Speaking of strategic, anyone else think old Mr. Henderson is getting seriously dodgy with his supper club? He’s been advertising on that new website, ‘Eat Local London’, and I heard he didn’t have the correct food hygiene certificate last time. Dodgy as in… not declaring income dodgy, or actual food poisoning dodgy, Bex? Because that’s a very different level of dodgy. Both, actually. Apparently, someone complained to the council about him not paying his taxes, and now he's trying to fly under the radar with the supper club. It’s a bit of a mess. Oh god. That’s… a lot. I always thought he was a bit eccentric, but not a tax evader. He always offered me extra cake. Is that a bribe? I don’t know anymore. Don’t overthink it, Leo. He probably just likes cake. Although, Bex has a point. It's important to be legit, especially with food. Remember when I was looking into getting a food hygiene qualification? It was a nightmare wading through all the legal stuff. Yeah, I had to do that for the café. Honestly, the forms were designed by someone who actively hates people. Took me a week, and I’m fairly sure I’m still technically breaking some obscure regulation. Speaking of jobs… anything new on the front with that publishing internship, Clara? Still waiting to hear back? They said they’re swamped with applications. Apparently, everyone wants to work in publishing. Which, fair enough. It’s… a thing. I’m just trying to distract myself by perfecting my sourdough. Honestly, the hydration levels are  crucial . You need 78% hydration, no less. I swear, you talk about sourdough like it’s a newborn baby. It’s practically is! It needs nurturing! It needs love! And precise temperature control. Actually, can someone check the oven? I think it’s supposed to be at 220, fan assisted. On it. 218. Close enough. Smells amazing in here, by the way. Seriously, you’re a wizard, Clara. You should bottle that smell and sell it.

Honestly, this canteen food is…an experience, isn’t it? I swear the gravy has a life of its own. It’s…robust. It’s certainly filling. My babushka would say it needs more dill, though. Everything needs more dill, according to her. Your grandmother sounds like a woman after my own heart! I’m Sarah, by the way. We’ve worked together a few months now, haven’t we? I feel terrible, I’m rubbish with names. Anna. It’s nice to properly meet you, Sarah. And yes, a few months. I’m still getting used to the British school system, it’s very different from anything I experienced growing up. It  is  a bit of a beast, isn't it? Especially covering for so many different teachers. How are you finding it? And how’s the IT admin side going? The IT side is fine, quite logical. I enjoy fixing the printers, honestly. It’s… satisfying. The covering is… unpredictable. Today’s Year 7s were particularly energetic. One tried to convince me that rubber ducks were a legitimate form of currency. Oh, bless them! They’re brilliant at that age. Always testing the boundaries. My youngest, Liam, he’s eight, and he’s currently obsessed with building miniature castles out of cardboard boxes. The living room is a hazard zone. Cardboard castles are good! My little cousin, back in Tomsk, he built an entire city. It took up the whole living room. My aunt was not pleased. Do you have other children? Just Liam. My eldest, Emily, is at university studying history. Keeps me on my toes, that one. Always debating something. What about you, Anna? Any family back home? I have a younger brother, Dmitri, studying engineering. And my parents, of course. We video call often, but it’s not the same. I miss my mother’s cooking terribly. She makes the best pelmeni - little meat dumplings. Oh, that sounds amazing! I love trying new foods. I’m a bit of a disaster in the kitchen myself, though. I can burn water, honestly. My husband does most of the cooking. He makes a fantastic roast dinner. Roast dinner is very British! I have tried it – Yorkshire pudding is… interesting. I’m getting better at cooking though. I’ve started to make sourdough bread. It's a slow process, but very rewarding. Sourdough! That sounds impressive. I've attempted it once, it ended up looking like a hockey puck.

Right, so are we definitely going the right way? Because this doesn’t look like… Mothercare way. It looks like we’re heading towards the docks. Trust me, darling. I know Preston better than you think. We need to go past the docks, then take a left at the next roundabout. It's a bit of a detour, but avoids all the city centre traffic. Honestly, it's chaos around there right now. Aye, she's right, love. That city centre’s a nightmare. Especially on a Saturday. Still, it’s good to get out, isn’t it? Been cooped up all week with that surveyor poking around the house like we’ve got something to hide. Tell me about it. It was so awkward. He kept asking about damp patches, like, excuse me sir, this house is perfectly fine! Except for maybe the… well, the bit in the bathroom. The ‘bit’ in the bathroom that requires a full renovation? That’s why we’re doing the survey, isn't it? To find all the ‘bits’. Yeah, okay, fair point. But honestly, he was really focusing on this tiny stain on the ceiling. Like it’s a massive structural issue. They always do that, lass. Gotta justify their fees somehow. Did he say anything about the garden? I’m worried about the fence. Old Man Hemmings next door’s always complaining it’s leaning into his garden. He mentioned it. Said it needs… securing. Which I think is code for “replacing the whole thing”. It does need doing. We’ve been putting it off. Right, turn left here, and we’re golden. Oh! Did you see that blanket in that shop we passed? The really fluffy cream one? That would be  perfect  for the baby’s room. Ooh, yeah! It was really nice. But probably ridiculously expensive. Everything in Mothercare is ridiculously expensive. Remember when I was little and you used to get me blankets from… what was that shop? The one near the market? Woolworths! Aye, Woolworths. You could get anything there. Pick ‘n’ Mix, stationery, blankets… a proper institution. She used to have the best little knitted cardigans, your mum did. It’s a shame they’re all gone. But we want the best for this little one, right? Safety and comfort. Speaking of which, are you drinking enough water? You look a bit pale. I’m fine, honestly.

Ugh, I’m so stuck on this level of ‘Astral Ascent’. It’s  impossible . Astral… what now? Sounds stressful, love. Are you sure you shouldn't be doing your homework? Mum! It  is  homework, kind of. Mr. Davies wants us to analyse game design, and I chose this one. But seriously, the boss is just… unfair. He one-shots me every time. One-shotting? Dramatic. What class are you playing? Maybe you need to adjust your build? I’m Zale, the spirit-walker. And I  have  tried different builds! It's not the build, it's the timing. It's like the game is actively trying to mess with my head. Mess with your head? Oh, don’t start down that rabbit hole. It’s just a game, sweetheart. No, but it’s designed to keep you hooked, right? All the colours and the sounds… and the frustration. I read an article saying game developers use psychology to make you addicted. Yeah, there’s definitely a lot of behavioural science baked into game design. Reward systems, variable schedules… It’s all designed to trigger dopamine release. It’s clever, actually. See! It's evil! I feel terrible after playing it and yet I keep going back. It’s… exhausting. Well, maybe a break is in order. Have you thought about Christmas yet? Are you making a list? Your auntie Maureen keeps asking. Ugh, Christmas. Everyone asks what I want, and I have no idea. I don’t  need  anything. Except maybe a strategy guide for ‘Astral Ascent’… You know, we could actually  go  somewhere for Christmas this year. Not just stay here. Remember that hiking trip Dad was talking about in the Lake District? Oh, that sounds lovely! Though your father would need to book it soon, everything gets snapped up. And the weather… it could be freezing. The Lakes? That sounds… cold. And probably no Wi-Fi. That’s the point! Disconnect a little. Remember what fresh air smells like. He's got a point. You’re always glued to that screen. Though, I suppose I spend enough time online too, chatting with my sister. She's trying to get me to understand TikTok. Honestly, it’s all just people dancing, isn’t it? Mostly. Although there’s a lot of science stuff on there too, actually. Like little experiments and explainers. Speaking of science, how’s university going? Found any research opportunities yet?

Right, so, copper is pretty easy to find in Minecraft, isn’t it? Loads of it just…underground. But it’s not  that  useful on its own, is it? Unless you’re making…lightning rods. Lightning rods are SO cool! I made a whole tower just for lightning! It zapped all the time! But diamonds are the best! You need diamonds for everything good. Swords, pickaxes… Yes, diamonds are amazing. But they’re  hard  to find. You have to go really, really deep down. It took me ages to find enough for a full set. It’s way harder than finding copper. I found a diamond once! But a zombie took it. It was  so  unfair! Oh no! That is unfair. You need to build better defenses against the zombies then. Maybe a wall made of…hmm…what’s a strong material in Minecraft? Obsidian! Obsidian is super strong! You need a diamond pickaxe to even break it! Exactly! See, you two are Minecraft experts. Now, thinking about real materials…what’s stronger, steel or bronze? Steel! Definitely steel! It’s shiny and you can make really good swords and armour with it. That’s a good answer. Steel  is  stronger, because it has carbon added to the iron. Bronze is iron and tin mixed together. It was important a long time ago but it's not as strong. What about velvet? Is velvet strong? Velvet isn’t about strength, darling. It’s about being soft and fancy. It’s made of silk, or sometimes cotton, and it’s really nice to touch. Like…a really posh cushion. Grandma has a velvet dress! It’s purple! Oh, yes! That’s a beautiful dress. Right, so while we’re talking about inventing things…I’ve been thinking about a new legend. A legend? Like…with dragons? Possibly dragons. But this one’s about a magical forest, and a girl who can talk to trees. She has to protect the trees from… a grumpy gnome who wants to turn them all into furniture. A grumpy gnome! That’s silly! He’s very grumpy. And he has a tiny axe. She needs to find a special berry…the glowberry…to make the trees invisible. Ooh, glowberries! Can you make glowberries in Minecraft? You can make glow berries in Minecraft, yes! Which is probably why my brain decided to include them. Are you both taking your vitamins?

Right, so then she just… vanished. Like, completely. Didn’t reply to a single message. No way! After all that talk about being best mates forever? What happened? Dunno! That's the frustrating bit. I tried calling, texted, even messaged her on Insta, nothing. It's proper weird. Makes you question everything, doesn’t it? Like, what did I do wrong? People are strange, aren’t they? Honestly, sometimes I think I prefer my own company. Less drama. You know, less chance of getting left hanging. Tell me about it. It’s just… we’d been friends since primary school. Years! It's not like a boyfriend going all silent, this is a  friend . Yeah, that's different. Did anyone else hear anything? Maybe she just needed space? I asked around. No one’s seen or heard from her. It’s like she just…poofed. It’s just… creepy, innit? You hear stories about people disappearing, and you think 'that'll never happen to me'. Makes you think about all those weirdos online too. Don’t go down that rabbit hole, aye. You’ll end up thinking everyone’s a paedophile. Seriously, it’s not helpful. I know, I know. It’s just…seeing stories on the news, it just makes you wary. Anyway, speaking of weirdos… did you see old man Hemmings trying to chat up Sarah at the bus stop yesterday? Ugh,  him . Always lurking. I swear he thinks anyone under 30 is fair game. Sarah dealt with him, though, didn't she? She told him she had a boyfriend who was a boxer. He scarpered proper quick. Good on her. Right, enough about creepy people. What's been happening with you? Still messing about with that guitar? Yeah! I finally managed to learn the intro to 'Wonderwall'. It’s still a bit clunky, but getting there. Proper! Oasis are legends. I tried learning guitar once, but my fingers just wouldn't cooperate. I'm more of a lyrics kinda guy. You always were good at writing. Remember that terrible poem you wrote about our PE teacher? Oh god, don't remind me. Mrs. Peterson was terrifying. It was a masterpiece of passive aggression, though. Absolutely. So, what bands are you into at the moment then? Anything new? Been listening to a lot of Idles lately. They're proper shouty, but good. And Fontaines D.C. You’d probably like them.

Honestly, this weather is  mint . Proper sunshine. Makes a change from Slough drizzle, eh? Seriously! I was dreading being stuck inside all half-term, but this is perfect. You still on for that exhibition in London on Friday, Kai? The one with the street photography? Oh yeah, the one Leo was banging on about? I’m in. Though knowing Leo, he'll probably want to spend three hours analyzing one picture of a bin. That sounds about right. He  is  a bit… intense about art. Did you guys finish that history assignment? Mrs. Davies is gonna murder us if we haven’t. Nearly. Just the conclusion left. It’s a slog though, isn’t it? All that research on the Industrial Revolution… feels a bit pointless. Tell me about it. I’m way more stressed about my EPQ. Trying to get interviews for my research is proving impossible. Everyone ignores my emails. I’m doing it on the ethics of fast fashion, you know? It’s a big topic. That sounds… ambitious. I went for something a bit simpler. Building a gaming PC. Less reliant on people actually replying to me. Smart move. Speaking of ambitious, did you see Maya’s Insta story? She’s practically living in Montenegro. Beaches, mountains, fancy restaurants… it's ridiculous. Ugh, don’t even. It’s just…flaunting. Her dad owns half of Wembley, it’s hardly a relatable holiday. Fair point. Still, looks nice. Thinking about uni applications… have you guys got any ideas beyond “somewhere with a decent student union”? I’m leaning towards Bristol, maybe. Good music scene, not  too  far from home. Thinking about doing Economics. You? I’m torn. I really like the idea of studying Anthropology at York, but… it feels a bit… impractical? Like, what jobs do you even  get  with an Anthropology degree? My mum keeps suggesting teaching. Teaching’s alright, I guess. My uncle does it. Says the kids are the worst part. Honestly, I haven't got a clue. Probably just pick whatever has the lowest entry requirements. Harsh! You're capable of more than that, Kai. Remember when you made that amazing paella for Sarah's birthday? You're practically a chef! That was one time! And I nearly set the kitchen on fire. Plus, my mum did half the chopping. You’re just humble. You should totally do something food-related. Maybe culinary school?

Honestly, this kitchen is a disaster zone. I walked in earlier and someone had left a half-eaten pot noodle on the counter… for  days . It was actively growing something. Tell me about it. I swear, living here is a breeding ground for germs. And the passive-aggressive notes? Don't even get me started. "Please clean up after yourselves!" Like we’re five years old. It’s uni life, innit? A bit of chaos is par for the course. My mum would have a heart attack if she saw this place. She's obsessed with cleanliness. Literally has a cleaning schedule for everything. My nan is the same. She'd inspect every surface with a white glove. She keeps asking when I'm going to 'settle down' and get a proper job. Like being a student isn't a proper job! Oh, the “settle down” question. My auntie Maureen brought that up at Christmas. Said I should be thinking about a 'sensible career' and 'finding a nice young man'. As if those two things are mutually exclusive. Ugh, relatives. Always with the unsolicited life advice. Mine are obsessed with how much everything costs at uni. Constantly asking how much my rent is, how much books are... They think I'm rolling in it just because I moved away for university. It's expensive, though, isn’t it? I'm already dreading the overdraft at the end of term. My dad keeps sending me articles about budgeting, like I haven’t heard it all before. “Cut back on takeaways!” he says. Easy for him to say, he's got a fully stocked fridge. Rent is insane. I’m working part-time at the campus bar just to keep my head above water. It's not glamorous, but it pays the bills. And the tips aren't bad, especially on student nights. I’m considering getting a second job. But then I’d have no social life. It’s a vicious cycle. I'm trying to save up for a trip to see my family back in Cornwall over Easter, but it feels impossible. Train tickets are daylight robbery. Cornwall? Lucky you! Mine are up in the Lake District. It's a trek, and mum always makes me feel guilty for not visiting enough. Says I only call when I need money. Which…is sometimes true. Mothers, eh? Always know how to make you feel small.

Honestly, Mum, the kids are already driving me round the bend about Christmas. Leo’s decided he  needs  a drone this year. A drone! Oh, boys and their gadgets. Your father would have been the same, always wanting the latest bit of technology. Remember that video camera he saved up for, the one that weighed a ton? Vaguely. I mostly remember him fiddling with it and filming us all looking miserable. But a drone is a different league. They’re expensive, and potentially dangerous. I’ve told him he can ask Santa, which feels like a polite fob-off, but what else can I do? Santa’s a good buffer. Distances you from the ‘no’ a little bit. Though, knowing your brother, Richard, he’ll probably promise Leo one anyway. He’s always the indulgent uncle. Oh, don’t even get me started on Richard. He rang last week boasting about taking the kids to Lapland. Lapland! I’m trying to get through December without completely losing my mind and he’s whisking them off to the North Pole. Oh, he does love to show off, doesn’t he? But he means well. Remember when he tried to build that treehouse for them in your garden? Nearly gave your Dad a heart attack. Oh, God, yes! It was a death trap. Entirely unstable and leaning precariously over the shed. Dad spent a week dismantling it while Richard kept suggesting “structural improvements”. Speaking of things needing improvement, how’s the teaching going? Still battling with teenagers who think grammar is optional? It’s…a challenge. I’ve got a new group of beginners, mostly Spanish and Italian, and it’s lovely seeing them learn, but getting them to understand prepositions is like pulling teeth. Then there’s Signor Rossi, who insists on correcting  my  pronunciation. He thinks he’s a linguistic genius. Oh, the audacity! You’re the teacher! Exactly! Though, honestly, some days I feel like I'm learning more from them than they are from me. It’s good though, keeps me on my toes. It's just… tiring. I'm starting to think that holiday in Portugal next spring is going to be absolutely essential. It sounds wonderful. We should try and go with you. I’d love to spend some proper time with the grandchildren. Actually, Mrs. Peterson from my yoga class was telling me about a lovely little villa she rented near Lagos last year.

It’s just… good to actually  see  you, Dad. Feels like ages. Two years is a long time, isn’t it? Feels like a lifetime, lad. A lifetime. Good to see you too, honestly. Thought the M25 would swallow me whole getting here, though. Absolutely rammed. Still, better than relying on trains these days, eh? Did you have a nightmare getting here? Nah, not too bad. Actually, I was messing with a new phone app that analyses driving – tells you if you’re braking harshly, accelerating too fast… all that. Quite addictive, actually. It felt like being back in driving lessons! Sounds like one of those things that'll just stress you out, doesn’t it? Everything's a data point these days. Speaking of driving… they've put another speed camera up near the old library, you know. Absolute racket. And apparently, they're thinking of lowering the limit  again . Seriously? They just did that! It's like they  want  people to lose their licenses. Remember Uncle Barry? Got done doing 33 in a 30 zone and lost his for a month. Nearly had a heart attack. Aye, that was a mess. He was fuming. Speaking of messes...how’s work going? Still teaching the… what are they, the Japanese businessmen? Yeah, mostly. It’s alright. Keeps me busy. Though it’s…interesting, trying to explain the nuances of English idioms to people who've already mastered everything else. Trying to explain ‘raining cats and dogs’ is always a highlight. What about you? Still dealing with angry customers all day? You wouldn’t believe it. Had a bloke yelling at me for a solid ten minutes about a delayed parcel. Said I’d personally ruined his birthday. Honestly, some people. I’ve been feeling a bit under the weather lately, too. Just a nasty cough that won’t shift. Doctor said it’s probably just a bug, but it's dragging me down. Oh, that’s rough. You need to look after yourself, Dad. Really. Remember what happened to old Mr. Henderson? Worked himself into the ground and then… well. Don’t remind me. Awful business. I’ve been thinking… maybe Brighton isn’t such a bad idea, actually. Mum always liked the sea air. Maybe a little flat, a bit of a change of scenery. Brighton would be nice. A bit more going on than Crayford, that’s for sure.

Honestly, the supermarket was  mental  today. I swear everyone decided to do their weekly shop at exactly 2pm on a Tuesday. Oh, don’t even. I popped in on my lunch break, thinking I’d be quick, and it was the same. Packed. People abandoning trolleys everywhere. It’s chaos. Did you at least manage to get everything? Mostly. I had to swap brands of pasta three times before I found one they hadn’t completely decimated. And they were out of oat milk.  Out  of oat milk! It’s a national crisis, I tell you. A crisis indeed. I'm switching to almond, myself. Not as good for a latte, but at least they seem to keep it in stock. Speaking of stock… did you see the PR fallout from that band, ‘Static Bloom’? Ugh, disaster. Oh, the ones who had that awful tweet about… well, everything? Yes. It’s fascinating, isn’t it? How quickly things can unravel. My media ethics students are having a field day dissecting it. Apparently, the PR team is scrambling, trying to issue a non-apology apology. A non-apology apology! Brilliant phrasing. That’s exactly what it is. It's always the same, isn't it? Trying to walk the line between acknowledging wrongdoing and not actually admitting fault. Precisely. It's exhausting just  watching  it unfold, let alone  being  the PR person in that situation. I feel for them, honestly. Though, a little foresight could have prevented this mess. True. Although, I’m starting to think foresight is a rare commodity these days. Did you hear anything more about the funding bid for the new music tech lab? I did. It’s looking… optimistic. We should hear something definitive by the end of the week, apparently. Professor Davies is pretty confident. He's been schmoozing all the right people. Good. That lab would be transformative for the department. We could finally get students hands-on experience with some proper kit. Are you going to that gig on Friday? The Jazz Collective at The Waterfront? Oh, I’d forgotten about that! I completely meant to get tickets. I’ve been so swamped with marking. Is it a good line-up? Apparently, pretty good. Liam’s been raving about the saxophonist. Said she's phenomenal. I’ve already got a ticket. Fancy coming along? I can grab you one if they haven’t sold out.

Right, onions are sizzling nicely. You’re sure you want chorizo  and  chicken in this paella? It feels… ambitious. Ambitious is good! It’s Saturday night, we deserve ambitious. And honestly, the chorizo will give it a lovely smoky flavour. Trust me. How’s the beanbag coming along? Still attacking it with those needles? Attacking is a strong word. Gently… persuading it to become a beanbag. It’s slow going. I’m on the fifth panel. This chunky yarn is lovely and soft, but it’s a beast to work with. I’m seriously considering using the smaller needles next time. Fifth panel, that’s progress! You'll have a massive, cosy beanbag in no time. It'll look brilliant in the living room, especially when it's finally finished. Did you manage to sort out the shower curtain? I noticed the old one was looking a bit… tragic. Oh, don’t even. I ordered a new one online. A lovely teal one. It should arrive tomorrow. But then I started looking at bathroom mats, and suddenly the whole bathroom wants redecorating. The ripple effect of a new shower curtain. It’s a dangerous game. What’s wrong with the current bathroom, anyway? It’s perfectly functional. Functional, yes. Inspiring? Not so much. It’s just…beige. Everything is beige. I saw this gorgeous wallpaper online, with little birds on it. And I’m thinking pale grey tiles. Maybe even a new mirror. Birds, huh? That's a bit…bold for you. I always thought you were more of a geometric pattern kind of person. I am! But I’m feeling adventurous. And beige is just… depressing. Don’t get me wrong, I love a neutral, but this is just… flat. It needs life. Speaking of life, are you adding peppers to this paella? Already done. Red and yellow, for colour. And a pinch of saffron, naturally. It wouldn't be paella without saffron. You know, while you're redecorating the bathroom, maybe we could finally tackle that wonky shelf in the hallway? Oh, please no! One disaster at a time. I have enough on my plate with the beanbag and the potential bathroom overhaul. We’ll leave the wonky shelf for another day, shall we? It’s been wonky for years, it's practically a feature now. A very… structurally questionable feature. Right, I think this needs another splash of wine.

Right then, finished that crossword. Took me ages, though. Seven across… “A small, flightless bird…” Had me stumped for a good ten minutes. Oh, you and your crosswords, George. Always got your nose in one. What was the answer? Kiwi. Of course, it was Kiwi! Should’ve twigged sooner. You’d have had it straight away, wouldn’t you, David? Probably. I used to enjoy a good crossword in my younger days. Though I’m more likely to be poring over the financial news these days, sadly. Bit more… pressing. Financial news? You’re still worrying about the markets, even in retirement? Honestly, David, you need to relax. It’s not so much  worrying  as… keeping an eye on things. One has responsibilities, you know. The portfolio needs tending to, even if I’m not actively working. Well, I’m glad somebody’s keeping an eye on things. I couldn't tell a share from a shillelagh. Not my cup of tea, that. Give me a good mystery novel any day. Speaking of mysteries, have you heard from Sarah lately? She said she was going to call after her holiday, but it’s been nearly a week. No, I haven’t. I assumed she was just settling back in. Busy unpacking, doing laundry… the usual post-holiday rigmarole. She usually rings straight away. She knows we like to hear how she’s getting on. That young man of hers… always asking about me, that’s good. He’s a lovely boy, isn’t he? Very polite. Reminds me a bit of his grandfather, actually. Though a bit more…trendy, perhaps. He’s a sensible lad. A good match for Sarah. Although, I still harbour a slight reservation about their decision to move so far north. North? It's not  that  far north. It’s only York! It's a long drive for us, George. A very long drive. And I worry about Sarah being so far from us, should anything happen. She's a grown woman, David. She’s perfectly capable of looking after herself. Plus, she’s got him, and they’ve got a lovely little house there. She's happy. That's the main thing. Exactly. If she’s happy, we should be happy for her. Though a phone call wouldn’t go amiss, mind. I’ll give her a ring tomorrow, then. Just to check everything’s alright.

Honestly, I’m absolutely shattered. That shift was  brutal . Old Mrs. Henderson decided today was the day to try and escape again. Oh, not again! She’s a character, isn’t she? Still, you’d think after the third time they’d increase her meds or something. Sounds… eventful. Anything interesting happen on your commute home, Dad? Besides narrowly avoiding death on the M25, obviously. Surprisingly peaceful, actually. Though I did see young Timmy from number 47 attempting to parallel park. It was a masterclass in… not being able to parallel park. Took him a good ten minutes and a lot of reversing. Oh, Timmy! He’s hopeless. Remember when he tried to build that birdhouse? It looked like a wonky shed. Oh god, yes. It leaned so far, I was convinced it was going to topple over in a light breeze. Speaking of building things, have we finalised the Christmas dinner menu? I was thinking goose this year, instead of turkey. Goose sounds amazing! A bit more… festive, somehow. Though, can we please have Brussels sprouts banished forever? They are the enemy. Brussels sprouts are a tradition, darling. A slightly unpleasant tradition, but a tradition nonetheless. I’m with Lily. No sprouts! We had them last year, and I swear, they haunted my dreams. Alright, alright, no sprouts. Happy? We can have honey-glazed carrots instead. What about desserts? I was thinking Yule log, but I'm open to suggestions. Ooh, a Yule log would be lovely. Maybe Mum could make her chocolate orange cheesecake too? That’s always a winner. Yes! And we  have  to have mince pies. I’ve already been eyeing up the Fortnum & Mason ones. They’re extortionate, but so worth it. Fortnum & Mason? Really? You and your fancy mince pies. I'm happy with the Sainsbury's basics, thank you very much. Although… I did see they had some nice Stollen. Perhaps a Stollen is in order. Don’t start you two. It’ll be a full-blown shopping rivalry before you know it. We still need to figure out presents, too. I’ve got most of your gifts sorted, but I’m struggling to find something for Uncle George. He already  has  everything. He loves those ridiculously expensive socks, doesn’t he? The cashmere ones? Another pair might be a safe bet. Or a really good bottle of whisky? He’s always moaning about the price of a decent single malt.

This coffee is lovely, isn’t it? Much stronger than what I’m used to back home. Aye, it’s good stuff. They don't mess about with it here. Real Turkish coffee. I’ve been coming here for… oh, must be fifteen years now, winter months mostly. Gets you through the grey. Fifteen years! Wow. You must know the place like the back of your hand. I'm only just getting my bearings. It’s beautiful, of course, but… different. Different is a good word. It takes some getting used to. Did you manage to get out and about much yesterday? Beyond the pool, that is. Not a tremendous amount, no. Just a little wander around the harbour. It was  packed  with people. Mostly British, it seemed. And a lot of stag dos, actually. It felt a bit… Blackpool, to be honest. Blackpool with sunshine, you mean. That’s Kyrenia for you. Saturday is always busy. All the day-trippers from the south come up. They get a good exchange rate, you see. Oh, I didn’t realise that. Is it easy enough to cross the border? I was reading something about needing to show your passport and… well, I’m a bit cautious, I suppose. Perfectly safe. A bit of a faff, admittedly. You just show your passport, they stamp it, and you’re through. It's mainly a formality. I’ve done it dozens of times. You can get a bus right into Nicosia – it’s a fascinating city, very divided, of course. Worth a visit, if you’re feeling adventurous. That sounds intriguing, actually. I’d like to see a bit more of the ‘real’ Cyprus, not just the tourist areas. What about eating? Any recommendations? I had a kebab last night, but it wasn’t particularly… inspiring. Kebab’s are hit and miss. Best bet is to get away from the harbour front. Go up into the old town, look for somewhere filled with locals. Ask for “meze”. That's a selection of small dishes. You’ll get everything from hummus and olives to grilled halloumi and lamb. It’s a feast. Meze... right, I'll remember that. Any particular restaurants spring to mind? There's a place called ‘The Lodge’ up near the castle. It's run by a lovely family, really authentic. And not overpriced, which is a bonus. Though, honestly, you can’t go far wrong stumbling into a little taverna.

Honestly, the students were dreadful today. Just absolutely dreadful. Didn’t read the assigned chapters, kept asking questions already covered in the lecture… it was relentless. Oh, no. Really? Was it a specific class or just… a general bad day? I think it was mostly the second years. They're starting to get that end-of-term ‘I can’t be bothered’ attitude already, and it’s only November! It makes me wonder if I’m doing something wrong, you know? Am I not engaging them enough? Don’t beat yourself up about it, El. You’re a brilliant lecturer. They’re probably just overwhelmed with everything else going on. Exams looming, socials… the usual chaos. Remember how  we  were? True, true. We were masters of procrastination. Still, it’s frustrating. I spent ages prepping that lecture, and to have them just… blankly stare back at me. It feels a bit pointless. I had a similar thing with my postgrads, actually. One of them, Ben, was convinced his dissertation topic was brilliant, but when I probed him on the methodology… it just wasn’t there. Had to gently suggest he rethink things. Awkward. Oh, those dissertation supervisions. The bane of our existence. Still, at least you were being constructive. I just wanted to yell at my second years. Controlled outbursts are sometimes necessary. Though perhaps not in front of undergraduates. Speaking of controlled… look at that smog! It's getting worse, isn't it? It's awful. You can actually  taste  it. It was bad yesterday, but today it’s like breathing through wool. I saw Old Man Zhang coughing his lungs out by the market. It's terrifying, to be honest. We should really invest in those air purifiers for the flat. I keep putting it off, thinking it'll improve, but it clearly isn't. Definitely. And maybe start wearing masks again when we walk to work. Though it feels so… dystopian, doesn't it? It does. But what choice do we have? It’s affecting our health. Speaking of health, did you hear back from Sarah about next weekend? She said she might be able to join us for that hike. No, not yet. I texted her this morning, but she’s probably busy. She’s always busy with her kids and her pottery. Though she did mention something about a particularly disastrous kiln firing last time we spoke.

Right, so, anyone fancy a chilli tonight? I've got loads of peppers that need using up. Chilli sounds lovely, actually. A bit spicy? My stomach's been a bit…sensitive lately. Oh yes, please make it spicy! I’m craving something with a kick. Look at this photo, though. Remember Auntie Maureen’s 60th? The hat she was wearing… Oh, heavens. That felt like a lifetime ago. She really does love a flamboyant hat. Did you manage to get hold of her about the weekend? She didn’t reply to my text. I spoke to her yesterday. She's off on a coach trip to Skegness. Said she’s taking Brenda and Doreen. Apparently, it's a 'singing and dancing extravaganza'. Skegness! Classic Auntie Maureen. She’ll be bringing back stories for days. Right, I'm starving. What time are we aiming for lunch tomorrow? I was thinking maybe that little Italian place near the market? Oh, that sounds nice! They do a lovely pasta salad. Around oneish? Gives me time to finish this report for work. It’s dragging on forever. Honestly, spreadsheets are the bane of my life. One’s good. I need to chase up a few things with the contractors tomorrow morning. They're still having issues with the new ventilation system. It’s like talking to a brick wall sometimes. Ugh, sounds stressful. I spent most of today battling with a client who wanted to completely change the tone of voice  after  we’d already signed off the copy. It’s infuriating when they don’t trust your expertise. You’d think they’d hire someone if they weren't happy with your work, wouldn't you? Anyway, back to more important things… chilli. I’m thinking rice and some crusty bread on the side? Perfect. Actually, did you see that new documentary about the Amazon rainforest on Channel 4 last night? It was absolutely heartbreaking. I missed that! Was it the one with the indigenous tribes? I read an article about it, sounded really powerful. I’ve been hooked on ‘The Great British Bake Off’ though, it's just so wholesome. Oh, I'm not a massive baking fan, but it  is  nice, isn’t it? A bit of light relief. Mmm, needs a bit more chilli powder, I think. How was your day, love? Apart from the ventilation system woes. It was okay.

Honestly, this new bus route is a joke. It’s supposed to make getting to the science park easier, but it takes longer now! Really? I hadn't even noticed a change. I cycle, mostly. Though I did see a bit of a kerfuffle at the bus stop on Trumpington Road yesterday. Oh? What happened? Some student was giving it large about… well, everything, really. Something about university fees and exploitative practices. Had a whole placard and everything. Blocked the bus for a good ten minutes. Sounds about right for Cambridge. Everyone's got an opinion and a placard. Did anyone try and actually  talk  to him? A couple of people, but he was pretty entrenched. Very passionate, I’ll give him that. It reminded me a little of some of the stuff at Imperial, actually. More direct action though, usually. Imperial? Right, that’s where you did your Masters, yeah? How did it compare to Cambridge, overall? I mean, beyond the protest styles. Hugely different. Imperial was…focused. All engineering, all the time. Cambridge feels… broader. More historical, obviously. And a lot more emphasis on tradition. Tradition meaning pointless formal dinners and having to wear a gown? Amongst other things. At Imperial, if you needed a lab, you booked it and got on with it. Here, you have to apply for access, write a risk assessment, and possibly present it to a committee. Oh,  brilliant . Sounds utterly exhausting. It can be. But it’s also… charming, in a frustrating way. It forces you to think through things, I suppose. It’s just… slower. And more expensive, when you factor in the gown hire. Speaking of expensive, have you been to the Cambridge University Press bookshop lately? They’re charging an arm and a leg for everything. I needed a specific linguistics textbook for a project and nearly had a heart attack. Yeah, it's ridiculous. I've started ordering everything online. It’s cheaper, even with the postage. They're relying on the tourist trade, I think. Everyone assumes anything with the Cambridge name on it must be gold-plated. Exactly! It’s just… frustrating. You’d think a university town would have reasonably priced books. It feels like they’re actively trying to price students out of learning. Well, they’re certainly not making it easy. Maybe this student protester had a point, even if his methods were a bit… disruptive.

Honestly, this cheese board is ridiculous. They’ve just… dumped a load of different things on it. Do you even  like  goat's cheese, Mary? Oh, I do, actually. Not the really strong stuff, mind you. A little goes a long way. Though, I’m more interested in these olives. Are they stuffed? They are, Mum. With pimento, I think. Honestly, this place is lovely though. A good find, Sarah. It's nice to get out of Birkenhead for a change. Glad you think so, Chloe. I stumbled across it online. Needed somewhere halfway between our places, and Hunsonby seemed perfect. Beautiful countryside. It is pretty. Reminds me a bit of County Clare, actually, though nothing quite matches Ireland, does it? Though I suppose you wouldn't remember County Clare, being a little babe when we last went. I have vague memories, Mum. Mostly rain and sheep. And Grandma telling me horrifying stories about selkies. Oh, brilliant! Your Grandma was a character. Speaking of characters, how’s Liam? Still causing mayhem? He's a handful, that boy. Absolutely a handful. He tried to convince me the other day that square roots were a conspiracy theory. A conspiracy theory! Imagine, after thirty years teaching the blessed things. Honestly, where do they get it from? Sounds like my nephew, Alfie. He’s currently convinced dinosaurs aren't real and the museums are all part of a massive hoax. Oh, kids! They're amazing, aren’t they? Little sponges for nonsense. How is Daniel, by the way, Sarah? Are things... going well? And are you still seeing him? Oh, Daniel’s grand. He’s coming up next weekend, you know. Finally. Been ages. He’s bringing that friend of his, Mark, too. Apparently, Mark's a history buff. Hoping he doesn’t corner me with talk of the Wars of the Roses. I’ve enough trouble remembering fractions as it is. Oh, good! That’s lovely, Mum. It’s good to have someone around. Do you think they'd mind if we all tagged along to that little market in Penrith on Saturday? Oh, I don’t know, darling. I didn’t want to impose. Daniel and Mark have been looking forward to a quiet weekend. I'm not sure I'd call a weekend with your mother quiet, honestly. But yes, you can tag along. As long as I get a chance to browse the vintage clothes.

Honestly, it’s just… relentless, isn’t it? All this concrete. You wouldn’t think, would you, being right next to the river, that you’d see so much grey. It is a bit grim, this stretch. Though, it does improve as you get closer to Greenwich. More greenery. And you can actually  see  across the river properly then. It’s just… Woolwich feels very… functional. Functional is a polite word. It feels like someone just dumped a load of buildings here. And look at the O2. Still can’t believe they built that monstrosity. Think of the cost. It’s alright, isn’t it? Not to my taste, but it’s become a landmark. The kids quite like going there for concerts. Though getting  to  it is a nightmare. We really need a car, don’t we? Don’t even start. We’ve had this conversation a hundred times. Where would we  park ? And the cost! Insurance, petrol… it’s just not worth it. We manage perfectly well with public transport. It's just inconvenient sometimes, especially when we're all lugging stuff for a family holiday. True. Remember that trip to Cornwall last year? Getting all the beach gear and the kids' stuff onto the train was… an experience. Though, at least we didn’t have to worry about traffic. Exactly. And honestly, thinking about driving all that way, sitting in jams… it gives me anxiety just thinking about it. It’s less stressful, even if it takes a bit longer, to get the train. I suppose. It's just... I was reading a recipe online the other day, an American one, and all the measurements were in cups! Cups! What is a cup? Is it a mug? Is it smaller? It’s infuriating. Oh, don’t even get me started on American measurements. It’s all so imprecise. We have perfectly good metric system. It’s baffling why they haven’t adopted it. It’s a whole different philosophy, isn’t it? Everything over there is… bigger. More dramatic. More…  cup-shaped . It makes you wonder, doesn’t it, what’s the point of all this striving? All this building? All this… volume? You’re getting philosophical on me now. It’s a lovely day for it, I suppose. Though I think it’s more about distracting ourselves from the fact we’re walking past a sewage works.

Honestly, this weather is  depressing . It’s been raining non-stop for three days. I tried to go for a run this morning, but I was soaked through within five minutes. Tell me about it! I'm already damp just thinking about my shift later. At least the residents at the home don’t mind the rain so much, keeps them reminiscing about summer holidays, bless 'em. Though it does mean more laundry, of course. Speaking of which, have you seen my phone? I swear I left it on the kitchen counter. Probably under a mountain of stuff, Mum. It’s always the way. I think Leo was building a fort there earlier. Oh, and about the sports day… it’s next week, and the forecast is looking grim. Real grim. Oh no! That's awful. Leo was so excited. He's been practicing his running like a little Olympian. All that effort for a soggy field. I know! And Maisie’s been going on about the egg and spoon race for weeks. I’m thinking of getting them some waterproofs, but they'll just complain about being too hot and sweaty. Honestly, kids. Remember when you two were little? We used to have that little inflatable pool in the garden, even in the rain. Your dad said we were mad, but you didn’t care! Gillingham summer rain is practically a rite of passage. Oh God, yes! And we’d fill it with bubbles, even though it was freezing. Mum, you always let us get away with murder. You were always braver than me, honestly. I’d be shivering, and you’d be splashing. Anyway, did you see what Emily got Lily for her birthday? Another build-a-bear. Seriously? That girl has a whole army of them. Oh, Emily. Always overdoing it. Lily’s room is practically a teddy bear convention. I'm trying to get Leo interested in, like, building Lego or something. More practical. It’s nice they have something to cuddle though, isn’t it? Little comfort blankets. Speaking of comfort, how’s Finn doing with the potty training? Still a work in progress? Oh, don't even ask. It's a battlefield. One step forward, two steps back. We had a minor victory this morning, but then there was… an incident… this afternoon. I’m starting to think he’s deliberately doing it just to wind me up.

Right, so, genuinely, what’s the big picture looking like for you? Beyond just surviving term three. Term three  is  the big picture right now, to be honest. But… you're right to ask. I’ve been doing a lot of thinking. The Head of Department keeps hinting about a potential Lead Practitioner role next year. It’s… tempting. More responsibility, more pay, but honestly, more paperwork. Paperwork is the enemy of all good things. But Lead Practitioner could be good for your CV, right? Long game. You’ve always talked about wanting to potentially move into educational consultancy, eventually. Exactly. It's that 'eventually' that feels so… distant. And frankly, after twenty years in the classroom, the thought of  more  meetings feels exhausting. Though, maybe it’s just the Australian sun frying my brain. Could be the sun. Or the sheer volume of spiders. But seriously, think about what would genuinely  fulfil  you. Not just what looks good. We’ve finally got the freedom to be a bit selfish with our aspirations, haven’t we? No mortgages, no kids demanding everything... Don't remind me about the kid thing. My sister just sent me pictures of little Leo. It's adorable, meltingly so… and simultaneously makes me feel slightly guilty. Guilt is unproductive. We’ve had this conversation a million times. We made a conscious decision, remember? To focus on experiences, travel, build something  ours . Speaking of which, have you heard back from Sarah and Mark about joining us in Thailand next year? Mark emailed. He's cautiously optimistic. Sarah’s still juggling work commitments, apparently. She’s angling for a sabbatical. Said she’s finally brave enough to ask. Good for her! Thailand with them would be amazing. We could rent a little villa, do some diving, actually learn to cook Thai food properly… Mmm, that sounds idyllic. I’ve been looking at some online TEFL courses, actually. Just… playing with the idea. If we were spending extended periods overseas, I could potentially pick up some freelance tutoring work. Keep the skills sharp, earn a bit of pocket money. Now  that’s  a smart idea. You'd be brilliant at that. And it means we don’t solely rely on my fluctuating tech investments. Building a diversified income is key. I've been pitching that app idea to a couple of venture capitalists. Still early stages, but the feedback’s been positive.

Honestly, I still can't believe you’ve never played Pokémon. Not even a little bit? Nah, never got it. All that catching and battling… seemed a bit much, innit? Always preferred a good RPG with a story. You're missing out, seriously. Pokémon was  life  growing up. Remember trading cards at primary school? Absolute chaos. Oh god, the playground Pokémon card economy. It was wild. People were practically bartering their lunch money for a holographic Charizard. My little brother was obsessed. Used to try and ‘evolve’ his actual pet hamster. Poor thing. No way! What? Yeah, he thought if he fed it enough weird stuff, it’d turn into something stronger. Mum nearly lost it. Kids are mental. Speaking of mental, did you see old Mrs. Higgins at the bus stop earlier? Giving me proper side-eye 'cause I didn't hold the door open for her. Oh, she’s a nightmare. Thinks everyone's out to get her. And she has a face like a slapped arse, doesn't she? Rude but true. Manners are just…gone. No one has them anymore. Especially not on the roads. Tell me about it. Someone nearly ran me off the road on the way here. I gave them a bit of a beep, though. Felt good. You didn't, did you? You and your road rage. You’re like a coiled spring, ready to fight over a parking space. It's not road  rage , it’s assertive driving! And it’s just… sometimes you feel like you’re in fight or flight, you know? Everything’s just a bit  much . I get that. Everything's stressful at the uni library right now. It’s all deadlines and stressed-out faces. I just want to hide under a blanket with a box of After Eights. After Eights are the ultimate comfort food. Remind me to get some for our camping trip next month. Camping? Are we still doing that? Thought that was off after… well, after last year with the midges. I swear they tried to carry me away. We are! We’re going to a different site this time. Hopefully, fewer bloodsucking insects. Plus, I've got a fancy new mosquito net. It's got fairy lights. Fairy lights? What is this, a festival? It makes it cosy! Anyway, right, someone needs to pop to the shop. I’m out of Malteasers.

That gravy’s good, Elsie. Proper good. Not like that watery stuff you get at the pub these days. Oh, thank you, Arthur. It’s just a bit of beef stock, thickened with flour, nothing fancy. Years of practice, that’s all. It  is  lovely, Elsie. Seriously. And the roast potatoes are perfect – crispy on the outside, fluffy inside. You’ve outdone yourself. Absolutely. I think I’ve officially eaten my weight in potatoes. Though, to be fair, I was pretty hungry after that lecture this afternoon. Student essays… honestly, some of them. Essays, eh? What are they writing about now? Everything’s all ‘woke’ and political, isn’t it? Saw it on the telly last night. Blimey. It depends on the module, Grandad. I had one today on the socio-political impact of… well, it’s rather complicated. Let’s just say it involved a lot of critical race theory. Critical what-now? Sounds dreadful. Give me a good gardening programme any day. Gardener’s World is a lifeline this time of year. He’s got a point, Elsie. I’ve been binge-watching that football documentary on Netflix. About the 90s Premier League. Proper nostalgia. Football! Now  there's  something I understand. Norwich were rubbish again, weren’t they? Saw the score online. Honestly, they’ll be relegated if they carry on like this. They did put up a bit of a fight against Liverpool last weekend, though. A bit of a fight? They got thrashed! Three-nil, wasn't it? It's a disgrace. Used to be a time when Norwich could hold their own. Well, things change, Arthur. You can’t live in the past. Speaking of changes, are we still on for the garden party next month? I've started thinking about the decorations. Sounds good to me! I can help with… um… logistical things. Making playlists, maybe? I can do the cake! I've been experimenting with a new lemon drizzle recipe. It's rather impressive, if I do say so myself. A lemon drizzle? Now you're talking. Elsie used to make a good lemon drizzle. Not as good as your mother’s, mind you. Beatrice could bake a cake that would raise the dead. Oh, Beatrice. She had a talent. And a mischievous streak. Remember that time she put salt instead of sugar in Uncle George’s tea? No way! I’ve heard stories!

Honestly, I’m starting to think this wasn’t the right move, y’know? Lancaster. Uni in general, maybe. What d’ya mean? You were buzzing about coming here back in… July was it? All ‘fresh start,’ ‘independence,’ ‘best years of my life’… sound familiar? Don’t remind me. It  sounded  good. But it’s just… a lot. The work’s harder than I expected, and I miss home. Proper miss it. More than I thought I would. Well, everyone feels a bit homesick at first. It’s completely normal. Remember when I was convinced the catering hall tried to poison me with lukewarm beans in the first week? Oh god, you were  convinced . You wouldn’t eat anything from there for a month. This is different, though. It's not just missing a good Cornish pasty. I'm seriously considering dropping out. Woah, hold up. Dropping out? That’s… massive. Have you spoken to anyone about this? Like, a tutor, or the student support people? Not yet. I feel a bit silly, to be honest. Everyone else seems to be thriving. And my parents… well, they’ve sacrificed a lot to get me here. They’d be gutted. Your mum always did have big plans for you. But hey, their happiness isn’t worth  your  unhappiness, is it? You need to do what's right for  you . What did you even want to study again? Was it… art history? It was. It  sounded  good. Lots of pretty things. Turns out, writing essays about pretty things is… less pretty. It’s just… not clicking. What about you? How are things going with law? Still thinking of being a barrister? Exhausting, to be honest. Honestly, though, I wouldn’t trade it. It's a struggle, but it feels…worth it. Look, don't make any rash decisions. Just… talk to someone. And maybe, just maybe, clean your shoes? They’re absolutely  filthy . Oh, these? I walked across the quad after it rained. It was a mudbath. A mudbath you actively walked  into ? You’re a menace. Seriously, they look like you’ve been digging for gold. They're attracting flies. They're comfortable! Speaking of weird things, did you ever find out where your name, Saoirse, actually comes from? My mum always said it was ridiculously complicated to pronounce. Oh, aye. It's Irish, see. My nan was proper obsessed with Irish culture. Saoirse means ‘freedom’ or ‘liberty’ or something.

Honestly, this place is  lovely . I’ve walked past so many times and always meant to come in. It’s a bit…fancy for a Tuesday, though, isn't it? It is a bit, isn’t it? But you said you needed a treat after that project finished. And I figured we hadn't seen each other in  ages , we deserve a nice setting. How  was  it, anyway? The whole ‘Operation Streamline’ thing? Stressful. Utterly stressful. The client kept changing their mind, the deadlines were impossible… Honestly, I think I aged about five years in three weeks. But it’s done now. Completely handed over. I’m officially on ‘do nothing’ duty for a week. Which is terrifying, actually. I don’t  do  nothing. You’ll cope. You always do. Though I can see why you needed the celebratory wine. Speaking of, what are you having? I’m eyeing up the sea bass. Ooh, that sounds good. I think I'll go for the pasta. Something comforting. And yes, definitely wine. A large one. Work has just been… draining. How are things at Pearson? Still battling the endless world of educational publishing? You have no idea. It’s… a lot. They’re restructuring again. Which means everyone's walking on eggshells, wondering if their job is safe. It's exhausting. I'm trying to be proactive and volunteer for extra projects, you know, make myself indispensable. Ugh, that sounds awful. Seriously, the constant uncertainty must be draining. I thought marketing was supposed to be creative and fun, not… politically charged. It has its moments! And my team are brilliant, which helps. But corporate life, you know? It’s always something. Still, at least it pays the bills. Which brings me to… have you started looking at houses yet? You mentioned wanting to get on the property ladder. Briefly. I had a look on Rightmove, but it just felt… daunting. Everything is so overpriced! And I keep getting distracted by thinking I should be saving for, like, a round-the-world trip. It’s a dilemma. Secure future versus spontaneous adventure. I get that. I'm torn between both too, honestly. I’ve been squirreling away money, but then I see flights to Iceland and think… just go! Maybe we should both just quit our jobs and backpack around Southeast Asia? Now  that’s  a plan! Although, I suspect my boss would be less than thrilled.

Right, have you seen this jacket on eBay? I thought of you straight away. It's that sort of colour you like – that dark navy. Ooh, let me see.  leans closer to the laptop screen  Is it a good one? Not one of those dodgy fakes, is it? No, it looks proper. It’s from a seller with good feedback, see? Hundreds of ratings. And it says it’s genuine North Face. Though you always have to be careful, don't you? Yeah, Dad got done once with some supposed Adidas trainers. Turned out to be… well, rubbish. He was fuming. Exactly! That’s why I'm being cautious. It's £45 plus postage. Do you think that's reasonable? Hmm. For North Face, yeah, that sounds alright. Amazon have similar ones but they're always like, sixty quid or more. See, that's why I look on eBay first. You can find some proper bargains if you’re patient. Although sometimes the postage is ridiculous. Some people charge more for postage than the item itself! It’s a rip-off, that is. I was looking at some new headphones on Amazon the other day. They were about thirty pound, but the postage was nearly ten! Oh, that's awful. You've got to factor that in. Sometimes it’s worth just paying a bit more upfront to get free delivery. Especially if you're a Prime member, isn't it? I don't have Prime. Mum and Dad do, though. I just…borrow their account sometimes. Don’t tell them I said that.  chuckles  Your secret’s safe with me. Speaking of Amazon, I've been meaning to order some new maths textbooks. The new syllabus is a nightmare – so much new stuff. Sounds…fun. Don't start! It's a lot of extra work marking the papers. At least with Amazon, I can get them next day. eBay's good for clothes and bits and bobs, but for textbooks, I prefer the reliability of Amazon. So you trust Amazon more than eBay, then? Even though they're a bit pricier? It's not so much about trust, it's more about convenience. And returns. If something’s wrong with an Amazon order, it’s usually pretty straightforward to send it back. eBay can be a faff sometimes, dealing with individual sellers. Good point. I bought a game on eBay once, and it didn't even work.

So, how was your commute this morning? Still a nightmare on the train? Honestly, Dad, it was…an experience. Signal failure just outside of Bishops Stortford. We were stuck for nearly an hour. Everyone was crammed in, shoulder to shoulder. It was a bit much. An hour? Blimey. They never did fix those lines properly, did they? Always seemed a temporary fix back in my day, and look at it now. Still causing chaos. You’d think with all the money they spend… You’d think, wouldn’t you? I ended up just working from my phone for a bit. At least I could get  some  work done. But honestly, it’s draining. Makes you question why we all bother going into the office. Well, someone's gotta keep the wheels turning, eh? Though I never understood this obsession with offices anyway. Always seemed a waste of good space to me. Back when I was… well, not working, mind you, but just pottering about, a fella could just  be . No need to rush around and sit in a box. You and your “pottering about”. It sounds idyllic. But seriously, the company keeps pushing for more office days. Says it’s for ‘collaboration’ and ‘team building’. Collaboration? Team building? Sounds like management speak to me. Fancy words for getting you lot to work harder for less. Maybe. It feels that way sometimes. Anyway, enough about my awful commute. How are things here? Mum keeping you busy? Oh, she's alright. Constantly rearranging things, as usual. Found some old photos yesterday. From when you were little. Honestly, you were a terror! Climbing all over the furniture, covered in mud… Oh, come on! I was a perfectly reasonable child! Maybe a  little  adventurous. Adventurous? You nearly took down the entire Christmas tree! Remember that? Your mother was beside herself. Okay, okay, you win. I was a handful. But I turned out alright, didn’t I? Got the fancy degree, the fancy job… You did, you did. Makes a fella proud. Though I still think a good trade is more useful. Something you can  do , y’know? Well, I’m doing alright with project management, Dad. It’s not exactly plumbing, but it pays the bills. Speaking of which, are you still going to that book club next week? Oh yes. Agatha Christie this time. 'And Then There Were None’. Bit morbid, if you ask me, but apparently Margaret insisted.

Right, so genuinely, is anyone actually considering flying on Christmas Day? Because I’m still picturing it and it feels… chaotic. Absolutely not. Even  thinking  about Gatwick on Christmas Day gives me anxiety. Plus, Nana would have a fit. It's against all her Christmas principles. Oh god, don't even mention Nana and principles. It’s a whole lecture. I'm firmly staying put. Though, I did have a customer today trying to pre-order a Christmas Day cake. I had to politely explain that, no, the café will be closed. People are wild. I'm staying put too. Honestly, the thought of being stuck in an airport on Christmas… nah. I’d rather wrestle a kangaroo. Kangaroos I can handle. Airports on Christmas, less so. Okay, so we’re all at least vaguely committed to  being  here. Which leads to the inevitable food discussion. What’s everyone doing this year? I volunteered to do starters, but I’m open to suggestions. I'm on dessert, obviously. I’ve been experimenting with a gingerbread and white chocolate cheesecake. It's dangerously good. Ooh, that sounds amazing! I’m doing the main course. Thinking a proper, huge roast. Turkey, all the trimmings, Yorkshire puddings the size of your head… the whole shebang. Sounds epic. Can I offer to bring the booze? I’ve got a mate who works at a distributor, can get some good deals. Yes, please! You are a lifesaver. And maybe some non-alcoholic options for Nana, lest she start lamenting the state of modern morality. Speaking of things you don’t want to encounter on Christmas… I nearly hit a deer on the way home last night. A full-on, bounding-out-of-nowhere deer. Oh no! Are you alright? And was the car okay? Yeah, I’m fine. Car's fine too, thankfully. It just… leaped. I swerved, heart nearly jumped out of my chest. It’s getting ridiculous around here, honestly. They’re everywhere. That’s rough. We get that a bit in the outer suburbs where I grew up. Often it's kangaroos, but same energy. Roadkill is never a good Christmas omen. It is grim. Though, arguably less grim than finding a fox in your bin on Boxing Day. Happened to me last year. Oh, you and your wildlife encounters! It's like you actively attract them. It’s a gift, apparently. They probably just want a bit of leftover turkey.

Honestly, this satnav voice is killing me. It’s like… aggressively polite. Aggressively polite? What does that even  mean ? You know? Like it’s judging your life choices while telling you to turn left. “In 200 metres, make a sharp left turn…  if you dare .” It’s just a voice, man. Don't overthink it. Though, I did once get one that sounded genuinely sarcastic. Oh, really? Which one? TomTom, I think. Kept sighing after every instruction. Like, “Recalculating…  again .” See! It's a thing! They're developing personality into these things. It's unsettling. You know what  is  unsettling though? The way this car smells. Smells? What smells? It smells…car-ish. No, it smells like…old biscuits and regret. Seriously, ANON needs to give this thing a good airing. It's a classic car, Liam. It’s supposed to smell of things. Character. Character? It smells like a forgotten picnic. And it’s a bit rattly, isn’t it? I swear the dashboard is vibrating with every bump. It’s fine. It’s doing its job, getting us to Norwich. It wouldn't be an adventure if everything went smoothly. Adventure? We are going to your Aunt Mildred’s for Sunday lunch. It's hardly Shackleton. Don’t underestimate Aunt Mildred, Liam. She’s a force of nature. Last time I was there, she cornered me for an hour about the ethical implications of non-playable characters in video games. She’s…passionate. So, are we still sticking to the plan with the driving? I’m happy to take a stint after Cambridge. Yeah, I’ll do the Cambridge to… Peterborough bit, then you take it from there? That’ll split it nicely. I’m just a bit tired after that project at work, honestly. Feels like I’ve been staring at blueprints for weeks. You and me both. Debugging is basically staring at lines of code until your brain melts. It's less glamorous than people think. Well, you both get paid good money to stare at things. I’m stuck wrestling with semicolons and passive voice. Sounds… thrilling. Right, satnav is telling me to take the next junction. Aggressively politely, of course. Just ignore it if it judges you, Liam. Just focus on the road, you two. We don’t want to add ‘accident’ to the car's scent profile. Fine, fine. Aggressively polite satnav, brace yourself for a smooth, regret-free left turn.

Right, so new Arctic Monkeys album dropped. Have you guys listened yet? Nah, not yet. Been stuck doing physics homework all evening. Honestly, Mr. Davies is  determined  to make our lives miserable. What’s it like? Is it any good? I gave it a quick listen on Spotify, but I was kinda… underwhelmed, to be honest. It's not bad, but it’s not  Tranquility Base Hotel & Casino . It feels a bit… back to basics? Like they’re trying to recapture the old vibe. Yeah, that’s kinda what I thought. It’s alright, definitely listenable, but it doesn’t really  grab  you, y’know? It’s missing something. I was expecting something a bit more experimental after the last one. You reckon? I kinda liked  Tranquility Base . It was weird, but in a good way. All those lounge-singer vibes. Makes a change from screaming guitars. It definitely took a few listens to get into, I’ll give you that. Reminded me of Bowie a bit, actually. Speaking of Bowie, did you guys see that new documentary about him?  Moonage Daydream ? Oh yeah! It was amazing. The visuals were insane. I watched it at the Everyman, the sound was incredible. Seriously tripped me out. I wanted to go, but my mum said it was too expensive. Ended up having to watch it on… well, let’s just say a less-than-legal streaming site. It was still pretty good though, the concert footage was unreal. It’s just… the way he commanded the stage. And the costumes! He was such a chameleon. Completely reinvented himself like five times. Seriously. Makes most modern artists look a bit… boring. All the same haircuts and clothes. It's like they’re afraid to take risks. Exactly! And the music videos these days. All just… phone footage and filters. Remember when music videos were actual  productions ? Like, Michael Jackson’s 'Thriller’? Or even something more recent like… I dunno… Gorillaz stuff? Oh man, Gorillaz. They were genius. Phase One was the peak, though. Damon Albarn at his finest. Have you seen the new episode of  Severance ? Dude,  Severance  is mind-blowing. I'm completely hooked. The cliffhanger at the end of last week's episode was brutal. Seriously, I need to know what's going on with the goats. The goats?! You're focusing on the goats? I'm more worried about what Helly R. is up to.

Right, so how was Balanceability today, you two? Leo, you went first, didn't you? It was GOOD! I did it! I actually balanced! For ages! You did? That’s brilliant! How long? Like… almost all the way to the cone! And then I wobbled. But almost! It was okay. I fell over a lot. Oh, sweetie. Falling over  is  part of learning, though, isn’t it? It’s how you get better. Did your instructor say that? She said I needed to look where I was going, not at my feet. But it’s hard! It is hard! It's really clever what they teach you, getting your balance like that. It’s a really good skill. Leo, you looked where you were going? Yep! Straight ahead! Like Miss Davies says in school - focus on your target! Excellent! See, you're using all your skills! And what about school generally? Anything interesting happen today? Lily got a gold star in maths! Oh, wow! That’s fantastic, Lily! What did you get a gold star for? For doing all the sums right! Even the tricky ones! That's brilliant! I bet you were really proud of yourself. It's such a good feeling when you finally succeed at something tricky, isn't it? Reminds me of when I finally finished my Masters dissertation… What's a disser…tation? Oh, it’s a very long piece of writing you do at university. It's a bit like writing a super-long school report! Anyway, back to you two. Was there anything else interesting happening at school? Any gossip? Mr. Henderson was talking about his house. He’s getting it renovated. Oh, is he? I heard they're putting in a swimming pool! A swimming pool? Wow! Does it have a waterfall? I think he said something about a little manmade waterfall! Apparently, it's going to be amazing.
