But he also said we have to remember to be really careful around water, especially diving. Because you can bump your head? Exactly. You can get seriously hurt. It's much safer to go in feet first. My friend, Charlie, nearly fell in the pond at the park yesterday. Oh dear! Was he okay? Yeah, his dad grabbed him. It was scary! Glad to hear he’s alright. Right, who's hungry? I was thinking pizza tonight. What do you think? Pizza! Yes! With pineapple?

Honestly, I’m shattered. That commute absolutely murdered me this morning. Three trains, each one delayed. Honestly, it’s a miracle I made it to the office before eleven. Oh, no way! That sounds awful. Cambridge is… charming, but getting  into  Cambridge can be a nightmare. Mine was alright, just the usual rush hour chaos, but nothing like three delayed trains. You need to move closer, seriously. Tell me about it. Easier said than done, though, isn’t it? Rent here is criminal. I’m saving, I’m saving, but it feels like a lifetime away. Speaking of saving, I’m trying to get back into running. You were saying you’ve been doing that 5k thing? Yeah, Parkrun on Saturdays. It’s… surprisingly addictive. And brilliant for clearing your head after a week of spreadsheets. Though my legs screamed at me yesterday. I think I pushed a little too hard last week. Ooh, good to know! I’m thinking of starting slow. Just a couple of short runs a week and building up. I used to be really into it at uni, but then… life happened. Conferences, events, trying to keep everything afloat at work… didn’t leave much time for lycra. I get it. It's easy to let things slide. Trying to balance everything is the worst. Speaking of balance, how are things going with… Liam? You seemed a bit down last time we talked. Oh, Liam. It’s… complicated. He’s lovely, genuinely, but he’s just… so  needy . It’s exhausting. Like, I can’t breathe without him wanting to know where I am, what I’m doing, who I’m talking to. It’s suffocating. Oh, honey, that sounds really draining. You deserve someone who trusts you, y’know? And gives you space. Don’t let someone make you feel guilty for needing your own life. I know, I  know . I just… I feel bad. He’s really good to me, in a lot of ways. He’s just… intense. And he keeps hinting about moving in together. It makes my skin crawl a little bit, honestly. Whoa, hold your horses! You’ve only been seeing him a few months, haven’t you? Moving in together that quickly is a recipe for disaster. You need to set some boundaries, clearly and firmly. Tell him you need more space. I’ve tried, subtly. He tends to… reinterpret everything as me not caring about him.

Right, another Dominoes drive done and dusted. You creamed Old Man Hemmings again, didn't you? He was lookin' proper glum. Aye, he didn’t stand a chance, Gran. I was on fire tonight. He kept muttering about beginners’ luck, but it's been three weeks now. Beginners’ luck? Lad, you’ve got a head for figures, that’s what it is. Always had. Reminds me of your granddad, Arthur. He could count cards faster than a whippet could run. Your Granddad Arthur was a card shark, Stan, let’s be honest. Though he did share his winnings… sometimes. Now, finish your pizza, you two. You'll need your strength for football practice tomorrow, Liam. It’s alright, Gran, I'm nearly done. This pepperoni's wicked. You always get the best. Aye, your Gran makes a fine pizza, even if she does insist on putting pineapple on some of ‘em. It's an abomination, I tell ya. Oh, don't start, Stan! A little sweetness balances the savoury. Besides, Liam likes it. Don’t you, Liam? Yeah, it's good. Different. Sometimes. Different and wrong, I say! Anyway, speaking of different, did you get that haircut sorted, Liam? You were lookin' a bit like a haystack last week. Mr. Thompson did it on Friday. Short back and sides, like I asked. Good, good. Can’t have you lookin’ like some city boy, eh? Gotta maintain a respectable Yorkshire trim. It’s important. Your Uncle Stan’s obsessed with haircuts. He used to get his done every week, even when he was just hauling cattle all day. Said it helped him think. It did! A tidy head, a tidy mind. That’s my motto. Though, honestly, some of those barbers in Northallerton…they think they're artists. Charge a fortune for a bit of snipping. Did you see Marcus’s new trainers? They cost more than a month’s wages, apparently. Don’t even get me started on these youngsters and their trainers. They’re like works of art, aren't they? They don't even  play  football in 'em, just wear 'em to school. Waste of money, if you ask me. Speaking of money, you remember Mrs. Higgins from the Dominoes? She was on about Easter presents for her grandkids. Asked if I had any ideas. Honestly, the pressure! Oh, she always asks  you . Thinks you’re some kind of expert on children’s toys because you take your granddaughter, Maisie, to the zoo.

Right, so milk first, or tea bag first? Honestly, it’s a fundamental life decision. Tea bag first, always. Milk after. You wouldn’t want to scald the milk, would you? It ruins the whole flavour profile. You know, makes it… sad. Scald the milk? Dramatic much? It's just tea, love. Though, I suppose you’d say that about everything, being a PhD student. Everything’s got a ‘flavour profile’ and a potential for existential sadness. Hey! It’s a valid concern. And it bleeds into all aspects of life. Like… pubs. Have you noticed Cambridge pubs are remarkably underwhelming? Underwhelming? Compared to what, The Shipwright in Sunderland? That's a high bar, you know. Proper pub grub, proper atmosphere. These Cambridge ones feel… curated. Like someone’s decided what a “pub experience” should be. Exactly! Curated! They're trying too hard. And overpriced. I swear I paid seven quid for a pint of something vaguely resembling ale last week. Seven quid! Back home, you’d get two pints and a packet of crisps for that. It’s the same with the food here. Everything’s “seasonal” and “locally sourced”. Which is lovely, in theory, but sometimes you just want a proper chip butty. Not artisan potato wedges with aioli. Aioli on chips? Honestly. It’s an abomination. Speaking of abominations, did you see that photo of Chris Pratt looking… different? Oh, don’t even. I saw it. What  was  that? He looked like a waxwork that had been left in the sun. All puffed up. People are losing their minds. It’s terrifying. And he’s supposed to be, like, this action hero. Although, I wouldn’t trust any action hero who willingly goes through that much cosmetic… enhancement. Exactly. It's all a bit suspect. It's like, just…be normal. Eat your greens. Which, by the way, I haven't done nearly enough of lately. I need to start being less reliant on biscuits. You and me both. I haven’t seen a vegetable in approximately three days. All research, all the time. I did attempt to make a soup last week, but it ended up resembling wallpaper paste. Wallpaper paste? Oh, dear. Maybe stick to the theoretical flavour profiles, then. And leave the actual cooking to me. I might even attempt a chip butty sometime this week, just for old times’ sake. You are a lifesaver.

Right, okay, my turn! Ugh, this is a tough one… “Astronaut.” Oh dear. No describing sounds, no saying ‘space’… oh, this is going to be awful. You’ve got this, Cariad! Think…think what they  do . Not where they  go . Don't say 'rocket'! You always go for rocket. She's right, you always lead with ‘rocket’. It's your go-to. I  know  I always say rocket! That’s why I’m preemptively banning myself! Okay… um… someone who… floats? No, too vague. Someone who… wears a very bulky suit? Bulky suit sounds like a deep-sea diver, love. Oh god, you’re right! This is a disaster. I’m going to have to pass. No way! You’ve had ages. Five seconds left! Think of the training! Training… rigorous…  sweat … hmm… someone who undergoes… intense physical… preparation? Intense physical preparation sounds like an athlete! Oh, she’s really stretching now. This is getting good. No, no, no! It’s not an athlete! It’s… it's someone… who… goes… really… HIGH! Oh, Cariad, you’re hopeless! High! What does that even mean? Time’s up! It's Astronaut! You failed spectacularly. My turn! Okay… “Marmalade.” Right. This is easier. Ooh, tricky one. Sticky? No! No helping, Rhys! It’s too early! … Um… a spread? But not butter? Sounds like something your Nan would make. Nana always made the best marmalade! Okay, think… orange… peel… bitter-sweet… Fruit preserve? Getting warmer! Really warmer! Think… breakfast. Breakfast...toast...oh! Is it… is it marmalade? YES! Finally! You saved me, Eira! Honestly, I was starting to panic. I was about to just describe the jar. You’d have been disqualified for that! The rules are clear - no describing the  object  itself. Reminds me of a holiday we took to Seville. The orange groves were incredible. They had marmalade everywhere. Literally everywhere. Seville, lovely! Right, my turn again. Oh please, something easy.  Reads card  “Giraffe.” At least it’s an animal… Long neck! No! Too easy! And you’re Rhys’s partner, you can’t just blurt it out! It's a good shout, though. Very descriptive. Spots! NO! We are not allowed to say spots! Think…habitat! Africa? Getting warmer! Tallest… land animal? Oh, this is a good one! You’re leading them nicely. This is impossible! It feels like we’re playing 20 Questions! That's the point, silly. It’s a test of your descriptive abilities, not your knowledge of giraffes!

Right, okay, so I  think  I understand this scoring system now. It’s utterly ridiculous, isn’t it? Like, why do you get bonus points for having five cards of the same suit? It makes no logical sense! Oh, come on, Elana. It's a bit of fun! Don’t overthink it. It’s Rummy, not rocket science. Besides, it’s the only way I stand a chance against your intensely strategic brain. He's right, you know. You treat everything like a lesson plan. Relax! Honestly, I’m just trying to avoid getting utterly trounced by the both of you. Oh, leave her be, boys! She’s just competitive, that’s all. Though, I have to agree, this game is a bit… convoluted. Reminds me of my Auntie Blodwen and her obsession with complicated knitting patterns. You'd start one, and six months later, you’d still be on the ribbing. It’s not that I  want  to be strategic, it’s just… ingrained. Years of teaching primary school, you know? You’re always analyzing, adapting, predicting… it's a habit. See! Predicting! She's already planning her next move. I’m telling you, she’s got a flowchart in her head for every possible hand. Alright, alright, enough analysis. Anyone got a red eight? I'm desperately needing a red eight. Sorry, love. Nothing for you here. Just a lot of black nines and a hopeful seven. Though, speaking of desperate, did anyone bring enough biscuits? I think we’re going to need reinforcements to get through this evening. I brought a couple of packs of digestives, they’re in the kitchen. And some ginger snaps, if anyone's feeling fancy. Though honestly, after all this driving yesterday, I just want to sit and… do nothing. This cottage is lovely though, isn’t it? So peaceful. It’s perfect. Miles from anywhere. Good job we got Bronwen to navigate, though. I swear she found that shortcut through a sheep field. Oh, she always does! Bronwen’s got a sixth sense for the most direct, if slightly unconventional, routes. Remember that time she tried to take us across the Brecon Beacons on a motorbike? Don't remind me. I thought I was going to end up tumbling down a mountainside. My knuckles are  still  white thinking about it. Right, okay, enough reminiscing about near-death experiences, let’s get back to the game.

Honestly, I’m already stressing about uni applications. It feels so… monumental. Like, one wrong sentence in my personal statement and my entire future is ruined. Dramatic much, Chloe? It’s not  that  bad. I mean, I didn't even bother with uni, and I’m alright. The care work is… tiring, yeah, but I’m learning stuff, and it’s actually rewarding. It’s good you’re enjoying it, Liv. I’m constantly second-guessing choosing the apprenticeship. It’s good money, and I’m actually  doing  accounting, not just learning about it, but everyone keeps banging on about how a degree is ‘essential’. Depends what you want to do, doesn’t it, Sarah? I mean, with engineering, a degree is pretty much a given. Though even  I  questioned it during second year. All those equations… felt like my brain was going to explode. Tell me about it! I'm trying to balance A-Levels  and  a Saturday job at Boots. My brain feels permanently fried. Honestly, sometimes I just want to binge-watch another series instead of revising. Have any of you seen ‘Severance’ on Apple TV? It’s completely messed with my head. Ooh, I've heard about that! Is it good? I'm currently obsessed with 'The Crown'. Elizabeth Debicki as Diana is just… breathtaking. I tried ‘Severance’ but it was a bit too slow for me. I need something a bit more… escapist after work, you know? I was glued to ‘Love Island’ all summer, don’t judge me. No judgement here! Sarah and I were both secretly watching 'Married at First Sight UK'. It’s terrible, but you can’t look away. Right? It's like a car crash – you know it’s awful, but you just have to see what happens. Speaking of awful, Mum's been a bit under the weather again. Just a bad cold, she thinks, but you know how she is… always downplaying things. Oh no, I hope she’s okay! Tell her I said to rest up. It’s awful when anyone’s poorly, especially around Christmas. Yeah, Grandma was complaining about her hip again last week. She's determined to host Christmas dinner, though. Honestly, it's a miracle she's still doing it. My nan’s trying to get me to help her with the wrapping this year. Said she ‘needs a young pair of eyes’ to make everything look pretty.

Honestly, this programme is dreadful. Absolute rubbish. I don’t know why we bother sometimes. Pass the peas, love. It's alright, isn’t it? A bit slow, maybe. But it's good background noise while we eat. Background noise is generous, Sal. It's actively lowering the IQ of the room. Don’t be silly, Arthur. It's just a bit of fluff. Though I do miss proper dramas. Remember ‘Upstairs, Downstairs’?  That  was a series. Grandma, you mention ‘Upstairs, Downstairs’ about five times a week. Well, it's a good one! And it reminds me of when your grandad— Oh, here we go… Let her reminisce, Liv. It’s better than listening to this drivel on the telly. Speaking of which, I was thinking of trying to cycle into town tomorrow, if the weather holds. Cycle? Into Cambridge? Arthur, you haven’t been on a bike in… decades! I know, I know. But I’m feeling a bit stir-crazy. And honestly, trying to park in Cambridge is a nightmare. Remember last time, Sal? We walked half a mile from the car park. Don’t remind me! My feet were killing me. And it was raining! Honestly, it’s easier to get a taxi. I cycle in most days for work. It’s the quickest way, honestly, especially during term time. Though you do have to be careful with the students. They have absolutely no road awareness. That’s what I’m worried about. I’m a bit wobbly, to be honest. It'd be a disaster. Might just stick to walking. Walking’s good. We could all go for a walk down by the river tomorrow afternoon. Lovely and flat. That sounds nice, actually. I finished work pretty early tomorrow. I’d be up for that. Although… I really need to sort out getting my driving test booked. Oh, don’t even  start  on that, Arthur. After all these years? I thought you’d given up. No, I’m serious! I’m feeling more confident now. I’ve been doing a few lessons with Mrs. Higgins down the road. She's very patient. Mrs. Higgins? The one with the bright pink scooter? The very same! She’s a good instructor, a bit eccentric, but good. It’s just… the parallel parking. That’s my downfall. Well, good luck with that. Honestly, though, I think you’re better off sticking to the bus.

Honestly, this is a lovely turnout for an Alumni Day, isn’t it? I wasn't sure what to expect. It is, yeah. I think the free wine helps! Though it’s nice to see so many people still connected to the Faculty after all this time. Are you an alumnus yourself? Just recently. Finished my Masters in Applied Linguistics last year. Currently working as a research coordinator – pretty good fun, actually. You? Same cohort as you, I think! I’m an administrator for one of the research projects. Bit less glamorous, but keeps me busy. I’m Olivia, by the way. Hi Olivia, I’m Chloe. And that’s… Professor Davies, isn’t it? Over by the window. It is! He was terrifying during my dissertation. Absolutely brilliant, though. He always pushed you to really  think . Dreadfully rude eavesdropping, I suppose, but I couldn’t help hearing you mention dissertations. Still a fresh wound, I imagine? Not anymore, thankfully! Chloe, by the way. And this is Olivia. Professor Davies. A pleasure to meet you both. So, Applied Linguistics, you say? Fascinating field. I spent a year in Spain, you know, teaching English back in the… oh, goodness, the seventies. Wonderful country. Particularly the Basque country - such a unique language. Utterly unlike anything else in Europe. I’ve always wanted to go. I know very little about the Basque language, actually. I did a tiny bit of Spanish at school but I’m dreadful at it. It’s notoriously difficult! Completely isolated language family. Reminds me a bit of the challenges linguists face with some of the minority languages in China. I was lecturing there briefly a few years ago. The sheer scale of linguistic diversity is astonishing. That sounds incredible. It’s amazing how much language can tell you about a culture, and history. Are you still involved with any research, Professor? Oh, dabbling, dabbling. Mostly mentoring students now. Though I still try to keep my hand in with sociolinguistics. Spent a good portion of my career looking at dialectal variations across the country. My wife and I are Londoners originally, but we’ve lived in Cambridge for… well, too long to count. London's changed so much! I haven't been back properly in ages. My family’s still there, though. It has. Though some changes are positive, I suppose. Although I can't say I understand a word the youngsters are saying these days!

Honestly, it’s so weird being back here. Feels like ages since I’ve properly seen you both. Two years is… a long time, isn’t it? It  is  a long time, Liam. Life just gets…away from you, doesn’t it? Especially with work. How are things going with the teaching? Still battling teenagers who think grammar is optional? You know it. Though this term’s group is… mostly alright. I’ve got one kid who spends the entire lesson drawing anime, but honestly, he’s pretty good. And at least he’s quiet. What about you, Chloe? Still wrestling with angry patients and dodgy teeth? You have  no  idea. Mrs. Higgins decided to argue with me about the price of a scale and polish yesterday. Like I make up the prices! Honestly, some people. And Sarah, how’s the recruitment game treating you? Still finding people to fill jobs nobody wants? Pretty much. It’s the same old story. Everyone wants a high salary for minimal effort. Though I did finally place someone in that warehouse manager role, the one I was moaning about for months. Bit of a relief, honestly. Remember Auntie Carol used to work in a warehouse? Vaguely. Isn’t she still going on about the ice bucket challenge? She did like three videos. Don't even. She’s still sharing things on Facebook about how it ‘changed the world’. It was a moment, Carol, a moment! She forwarded me one yesterday, with a picture of her looking really proud. Oh god, the Facebook. I had to unfriend Uncle David last month. He started posting conspiracy theories. It was exhausting. Seriously, what  is  it with our family and Facebook? It’s a slippery slope. Remember when Grandma got addicted to FarmVille? She wouldn't talk about anything else at Christmas. Speaking of family, how are the kids, Chloe? Are they still driving you mad? Constantly. Leo’s at that age where everything is a negotiation. Absolutely  everything . And Maisie's started asking about adoption. She had a project at school about different families. It was sweet, but a bit…heavy. Oh, wow. That's... mature of her to ask, isn't it? Did you explain everything okay? We did our best. It opened up a really good conversation, actually. It's made me think we should maybe look into fostering at some point. That’s amazing, Chloe.

Honestly, this coffee machine is driving me round the bend. It makes a lovely cup, when it  works , but half the time it just gurgles and spits, and then refuses to froth the milk. It’s possessed, I tell you. Sounds familiar. Everything seems to break down at once, doesn’t it? Luckily, mine's a simple French press. No fancy tech to go wrong. Have you looked at getting it serviced, or is it just…old age? Old age, I suspect. They don't  make  things like they used to. Planned obsolescence, that’s what it is. Designed to fall apart after a year. It’s infuriating. Speaking of falling apart, have you two given any more thought to the storage costs? The removal people quoted me a fortune for keeping everything while we sort out the house. A fortune is right. I nearly choked on my tea when I saw the estimate. Apparently, needing space for "sentimental items" incurs a premium. Sentimental items! It's just a load of boxes filled with old photographs and my grandmother’s china. I did a bit of digging online, and there's a self-storage facility just outside Penrith that’s marginally cheaper. Not by much, but every little helps. Though even then, it's going to eat into the renovations budget, isn’t it? It is. It's all eating into the renovations budget. Honestly, I'm starting to wonder if we should just sell everything and move into a bungalow. Less to worry about. Less to store. Don't be ridiculous, Arthur. You spent years building up your collection of antique maps! You can’t just abandon that. I know, I know. It’s just… frustrating. It’s not just the money, it’s the whole mess of everything. Then you turn on the news and it’s just…well, you know. Politics. Don’t get me started. I was reading an article about the Labour leadership race this morning. It's all so…predictable. More infighting. More empty promises. I’m losing faith in  all  of them, to be honest. It feels like no one is listening to the ordinary person anymore. They're all too busy jostling for position. Remember when people actually went into politics to  make a difference ? Idealism. A dangerous thing, idealism. It gets crushed pretty quickly in that world. I used to be quite idealistic, you know.

Honestly, Mum, the thought of Christmas already fills me with dread. Not the  day  itself, necessarily, but the build-up. The frantic shopping, the endless cooking… It's just… a lot. Oh, now, darling, don’t say that. Christmas is magical! Though, I do agree about the shopping. It's become so commercialised, hasn’t it? Remember when it was about making things, not  buying  things? Vaguely. I was quite little. I remember Mum trying to get me to make paper chains, which ended up looking like mangled worms. It felt less magical and more… sticky. Oh, you always were a creative one! No patience for neatness. So, have you started thinking about what to get anyone yet? Your father's birthday's barely been and gone. No, not really. I was thinking maybe a weekend away for you and Dad? Somewhere quiet. You both deserve a break. You’re always working, aren't you? Still doing consultancy? Still plugging away, yes. It keeps me busy, keeps the brain ticking over. It’s mostly online now, thankfully. Less travelling. Although, this last project… a company in Birmingham… honestly, the bureaucracy! It took me three days just to get access to their systems. Oh, bless you. Sounds exhausting. Are you enjoying it though, generally? Is it fulfilling? Because you seemed a bit down last time we spoke. It’s… alright. It pays the bills. I miss the teaching, I have to admit. The direct interaction with people, the feeling of actually  helping  someone learn. Consultancy is a bit… detached. You were such a brilliant lecturer. You should go back to it. There’s a lot of demand for experienced people. Maybe a part-time position? I’ve considered it. But the universities… they’re all so focused on research now, aren't they? Teaching is almost secondary. And the pension… I’m not sure I could afford to give up the security of my consultancy earnings. That's fair. It’s a tricky one. What about the grandkids? Are you seeing them much? Leo's getting so big! Not as much as I’d like. Sarah's always so busy with work and little Leo and everything’s so far away now you’re in Devon. We had him for a night last week, though. He absolutely adores building dens. We turned the entire living room into a fortress! It was chaotic, but wonderful.

Honestly, I thought Gran was gonna kill Grandad last night. The snoring! It was like a foghorn. You’re telling me! I was half-expecting the ceiling to come down. He wasn't letting  anyone  get a wink of sleep. Did you hear that little snort he does right before a proper rumble starts? Oh god, the snort. It's a warning sign. Like a tiny, congested trumpet. I actually shoved my pillow over my head, it was that bad. I swear, he practices it. My dad snores a bit, but it’s nothing like that. It’s more of a gentle purr. Your Grandad sounds…intense. Intense is an understatement. It’s a full-on orchestra. Remember when we stayed at their house for that football match and he kept waking himself up with it, then just…rolled over and started again? Oh, brilliant memory! He didn't even register it happened! Completely oblivious. Speaking of oblivious, have you seen Sarah lately? She’s gone all quiet. Quiet? Nah, I saw her in Waterfields yesterday. She was having a right good natter with Brenda behind the counter. She was moaning about her coursework, naturally. Oh, Waterfields. I went this morning. Got a couple of those little sausage rolls. Honestly, they’re addictive. And Brenda slipped me an extra éclair. She’s a legend. I need to go to Waterfields! I’ve been craving one of their jam doughnuts all week. And they do the best Richmond sausages, don’t they? Proper meaty. Richmond sausages  are  top tier. Although, me Nan swears by the ones from the market. Says they’ve got more flavour. She's a bit of a sausage connoisseur. Your Nan’s a woman after my own heart. My Grandad used to carry a handkerchief  specifically  for wiping his sausage roll fingers. A proper linen one! That's… dedication. I’ve lost count of how many times I’ve wiped my hands on my jeans after a sausage roll. You animal! You can’t just use your jeans! It’s a sacred food item! It requires respect. And a linen handkerchief, clearly. You’re all mad! But I’m totally getting a linen handkerchief now. For sausage roll emergencies. So, back to Sarah…Did she mention if she’s seeing Ben anytime soon? Haven’t heard anything about them for ages. No, she just said she was focusing on her dissertation.

Honestly, that was the busiest weekend  ever . I feel like I haven’t stopped moving since Friday afternoon. Oh yeah? What were you up to? Aside from, you know, generally being brilliantly busy? Well, Friday was Sarah’s birthday, which was lovely, but involved a  lot  of coordinating with everyone to get to the restaurant on time. Then Saturday was the volunteer day at the animal shelter – which was rewarding, don’t get me wrong, but covered in…well, everything. And then Sunday was supposed to be a chilled-out recovery day, but Mum decided it was the perfect time to redecorate the spare room. Oh, bless her. Always finding a project. Sounds exhausting though. Did the redecorating at least  look  nice? It will, eventually. Right now it just looks like a bomb’s hit it. She’s gone for a very…bold shade of teal. It’s like, staring into the ocean. Or a slightly aggressive swimming pool. Teal, eh? A bit much, maybe. My Margaret would never. She’s all creams and beige these days. Says it’s calming. Calming is good. I needed calming this weekend. How was yours? Did you manage to get out on the bike at all? A little bit. Saturday was alright, did a decent run around the lanes. But Sunday… rained. Solid. Proper Midlands drizzle, you know? The kind that gets  inside  you. So I ended up spending the afternoon sorting through old invoices. Thrilling. Oh, the glamour! Sounds…productive. At least you weren’t covered in animal by-products. True enough. Though dealing with dodgy invoices can feel a bit like that sometimes. Listen, about next weekend… Margaret and I were thinking of driving over to Stratford. Might catch a performance at the RSC. Fancy joining us? Oh, that sounds  really  nice, actually. Stratford is lovely. What are they doing at the moment? Midsummer Night’s Dream. Thought you might enjoy that. It’s a bit of light relief after your hectic weekend. That  does  sound perfect. I’d love to. Let me just check my work schedule tomorrow, but I'm pretty sure I'm free. Excellent! Margaret will be pleased. She keeps saying you’re too busy to have any fun. Tell her I'm making a concerted effort. Though she’s probably right. It's just…work’s been a bit crazy lately with the new project launching. It's all go, go, go.

Honestly, the Year 10s are  exhausting  this year. They’ve got zero motivation. It’s like pulling teeth to get them to conjugate a simple verb. Oh, tell me about it! My lot are the same. I think it’s the post-lockdown thing, isn’t it? They’ve just… lost the habit of learning. It’s a real struggle. What languages are you teaching at the moment? French and a bit of German. Though, the German class is tiny. Five students, and honestly, two of them are only there because their parents made them. It's a bit demoralising, really. You? Spanish and a very reluctant bunch of Year 7s attempting French. Spanish is alright, I enjoy it, but trying to get them excited about the past participle...it’s a battle. It makes me question everything, you know? Like, am I even doing a good job? Oh, absolutely. I have those moments too. Especially when they ask, “When are we ever going to  use  this?” and you're scrambling for a relevant response beyond “university applications.” Exactly! It’s hard to make subjunctive mood sound appealing in the real world. Though, I did take a group to Barcelona a few years ago and seeing them actually  use  the language… that was magical. Oh, I'd love to do a language exchange trip. It's just getting the budget sorted that's the killer. Speaking of things that are killers… how are you coping with everything now Elsie’s here? Coping is a strong word! It’s… chaotic, lovely, utterly exhausting. She’s seven months now, and just starting to crawl, which is a whole new level of vigilance required. You realize how many things are actually within reach when you’re constantly retrieving them from her tiny hands. Oh, I can imagine! My sister keeps sending me videos of her nephew, and it's just a constant stream of near-disasters. It’s terrifying and adorable all at once. Are you thinking about going back to work full-time? That’s the million-dollar question, isn't it? I’m currently on maternity leave, and the thought of leaving her is… heartbreaking, honestly. But financially, we need to. My husband’s been amazing, taking on more childcare, but it’s not sustainable long-term. I'm thinking of going back three days a week to start. That sounds sensible.

Right then, lovely bit of Victoria sponge, wouldn’t you say, Margaret? Just the ticket with a cuppa this afternoon. It is nice, Arthur. Though a bit sweet, even for me. You know I can’t have too much sugar these days. The doctor’s warnings and all that. Oh, don't be silly, George, just enjoy it. A little bit of what you fancy does you good. Besides, Arthur makes a cracking sponge. Doesn’t he, Arthur? Well, I do try. It’s all about the beating, really. Gotta get the air in there. Look at that robin, though. Building a nest again in the pyracantha. Bold as brass, that one. They are, aren't they? Always the first to spot the new feeders, too. Filled them up this morning, did I. Seed and those little fat balls. Keeps ‘em going through the colder spells, even though it's getting milder. Have you seen Mrs. Higgins’ garden? It’s completely overrun. Vines everywhere and weeds taller than I am. I swear, she’s given up entirely. Poor soul. Getting on a bit now, isn’t she? It’s hard work, gardening. Especially when your knees aren’t what they used to be. She always was a bit… eccentric. Remember those puppets she used to make? Horrible things. All felt and button eyes. Gave me the shivers, they did. Oh, I remember! She used to put on shows for the grandchildren. They loved them, though, didn’t they? Little Timmy used to be fascinated. He was a quiet lad, Timmy. Used to follow me around the garden when he was little, asking about the birds. Shame about his diabetes, though. Started so young. It’s awful, isn't it? Seems to be more and more of it about these days. All that processed food, I reckon. And sugar in everything! You've got a point there, George. Everything seems to be full of sugar. Even things you wouldn’t expect. It's a wonder any of us are still standing. Speaking of standing, look at old Mr. Peterson trying to prune those roses. He's wobbling all over the place! He’s a stubborn one, that. Refuses to admit he needs a bit of help. It's all very well being independent, but there's a limit. You don’t want to end up falling and breaking a hip. They don’t make ‘em like they used to, do they?

Right, I think I'm going to go for the grilled halloumi with the salad. It smells amazing. Are you having the kebab again, David? You know me too well, Sarah. Can't resist a good kebab when in Cyprus. Though, I might try the sheftalia, if they have any left. Old Man Yiannis always sells out quickly. Speaking of Yiannis, did you see him having a right go at Mrs. Papadopoulos earlier? Oh, no! What happened? She’s usually so meek. Apparently, she tried to order the lamb chops and told him she wanted them well-done. Yiannis nearly exploded! Said it was a crime against lamb, a sacrilege! She just shrunk back, poor woman. He's got a passion for his cooking, that one. A bit loud sometimes, but a good heart. Oh, Yiannis. He  is  a character. It reminds me of my Uncle George, utterly uncompromising about his roast potatoes. Must be crispy, must be Maris Pipers, no argument! He drove my Aunt mad. Reminds me of my sister, actually. Remember how obsessed she was with her Persian cat, Mr. Bigglesworth? She’d practically serve him salmon on a silver platter. She always said he had a sensitive palate. Oh, goodness, yes! The cat who thought he was royalty. How is she, by the way? It feels like ages since I’ve seen her. I know she wasn't doing well with her arthritis. She's…managing. It's gotten worse, sadly. She's started seeing a specialist, trying these new injections. Says they help, but she’s still in a lot of pain. It’s heartbreaking, really. She’s always been so vibrant. It’s a harsh reminder, isn’t it? About how quickly things can change. My brother, as you know, he had that scare last year. I remember. That was awful. You must have been so worried. Terrified. Absolutely terrified. Made me think a lot about…well, everything. About what really matters. It's why I’m trying to enjoy these little things, you know? This sunshine, this food, a good chat with a friend. Absolutely. We need to grab these moments when we can. It's wonderful being here in Northern Cyprus, isn't it? So peaceful. I've been trying to learn a bit of Turkish from Ali, the waiter. He’s very patient. Good for you! I tried a few years ago, but it didn't stick.

Honestly, Mum, the commute is killing me. An hour and a half each way. It's just… draining. I keep meaning to look at places closer to London, but everything is so tiny and expensive. Oh, darling, I know. It’s dreadful. We were talking about that just yesterday, your Dad and I. It’s no life, spending all that time travelling. Have you seen that little development near Wimbledon? Might be worth a look. Though knowing London prices… Wimbledon? You’ll need a lottery win for Wimbledon. Still, good on her for looking. When  I  started commuting into Birmingham, it was a good forty-five minutes, and I thought  that  was bad. Nowadays, you young’uns are expected to live like this. It's not just the time, Dad, it’s the cost! Trains are ridiculous. And then I feel guilty about using the car because of the environment. It's a whole thing. Well, you’re doing a good job, love. Project Co-ordinator sounds very important. Are they giving you any real responsibility yet, or is it still mostly admin? It’s getting there. I’m shadowing Sarah on the new campaign launch next week, which is exciting. Lots of meetings, lots of spreadsheets… but it’s a step up. Good, good. You need to be getting your teeth into something. Sarah, is she still with that fella, the architect? Yes, they're still going strong. They went to Italy last month, apparently. Sent us a lovely postcard. Speaking of which, are we doing a Secret Santa again this year? I’ve been trying to think of something for Sarah. Oh, yes! I think Auntie Brenda suggested it. I’ve already got a few ideas. Maybe something for the house? You two keep talking about renovations. We are, aren’t we? That downstairs bathroom… It’s been on the ‘to do’ list for five years now. Your Dad wants to rip the whole thing out, start from scratch. It’s a disaster area! I’m telling you, it needs a complete overhaul. Plus, the plumbing is ancient. One day it’s going to burst and flood the whole house. You two need to get organised! Maybe as a Christmas present to yourselves, you could book a consultation with a builder? That’s not a bad idea, actually. We could. Your Grandad would have loved helping with that, you know.

Honestly, I was scrolling through TikTok last night, and you won’t BELIEVE the catfish I found. Proper wild. Ooh, go on then! I love a good catfish story. Is it one of them where they've stolen photos off a model or somethin'? Worse, I think. This one was pretending to be…an army veteran. Like, massively decorated, hero status. But then someone did a reverse image search and all the photos were of this bloke who runs a landscaping business in Florida! No way! That's dedication to a lie, isn't it? What was the catfish trying to get out of it? Money? A date? Both, apparently. Been chatting to this woman for months, all romantic, building her up…then started hinting at needing help with ‘medical bills’. It was a whole production. She nearly sent him a grand! A grand?! Bless her. People are mental. It's like, how do you even  think  you can get away with that stuff? It’s the confidence, innit? The sheer audacity. Reminds me of some of the people on Jeremy Kyle, honestly. Oh god, don't even get me started on Jeremy Kyle. I was flicking through channels the other day and it came on. I forgot how…intense it was. Intense is an understatement! It was a societal study in chaos, wasn't it? All the screaming and the lie detectors… And the storylines! Every episode was like, "My fiancé is my brother!" or "She stole my best mate!" It was ridiculous, but I was hooked. I know, right? So trashy, but you couldn't look away. I think it was the sheer desperation of some of the people on there. It was…sad, actually. Yeah, you’re right. It wasn't just entertainment. There were some proper broken people on that show. But then they'd all be shouting at each other and I'd lose the thread of the actual sadness. Remember that one with the bloke who thought his girlfriend was having an affair with his mum? Oh my god, YES! And his mum was just sat there, completely unfazed! She was the coolest person on the whole show. That was a legendary episode. Honestly, they should bring Jeremy Kyle back just for the drama, but like…with a therapist on stage to actually help people. Now  that's  an idea. "Jeremy Kyle: Healing Edition." I'd watch that.

Right, so I was thinking… Paris next summer? Properly thinking about it, not just dropping hints. Paris. That’s… ambitious, darling. Ambitious and lovely. What sparked this sudden burst of Parisian longing? It isn’t the pastries, is it? Though, admittedly, they  are  exceptional. No, it’s… well, it’s a few things. Professor Dubois was talking about the Sorbonne’s library today, and it sounded incredible. All those original texts, metres and metres of Classics. And honestly, I just need a break from… everything here. Uni’s stressing me out, the city’s buzzing, I just want to  breathe  somewhere different. I understand perfectly. London can be suffocating, even for those of us who’ve lived here decades. And the Sorbonne… ah, memories. I spent a very happy year there, after Vienna, before settling here, really. Though my French was… shall we say… enthusiastic rather than accurate. Enthusiastic? That’s a polite way of putting it, knowing you. Didn’t you once accidentally order a plate of snails thinking they were mushrooms? Don’t remind me! The waiter’s face! And my poor Father, he was mortified. He spoke fluent German and Italian, you know. Expecting a certain standard of continental sophistication. Being raised in Italy definitely gave him expectations. Speaking of languages, I’m struggling with German. It’s just… so structured. All those cases. It feels completely alien compared to Latin, even. And I thought I was good at languages! It  is  difficult. The declensions can be a nightmare. But think of it as a puzzle. A complex, infuriating puzzle. And it's a beautiful language, truly. My grandmother used to sing Lieder to me when I was little – Schubert, Schumann… Such emotion. Perhaps I could help you with it? Seriously? That would be amazing! You're way better at it than anyone I've asked so far. Of course, darling. Anything. Though, first… this computer. It’s being utterly obstinate again. I was trying to upload some photos from Tuscany – the bee pictures, remember? – and it just keeps freezing. It’s infuriating. It used to be so simple, just point and click. Computers. Always the bane of your existence. Okay, let me have a look. Did you try restarting it? The usual first step. Naturally! Do you think I’m a complete novice? I restarted it three times! It’s probably a driver issue. Honestly, these modern contraptions.

Honestly, Dad, you were practically tailgating that lorry! It’s making me nervous. Tailgating? I was maintaining a safe following distance. You young people exaggerate everything. Besides, they were going far too slow. He does have a point, love. They  were  crawling. Though, a bit of space is always good, isn't it? Especially on a motorway. Crawling is better than causing an accident! And you nearly swerved into the next lane when that car pulled out. I reacted! That’s what drivers  do . I’ve been driving for fifty years, I think I know what I’m doing. Fifty years… goodness me. Remember that awful little Ford Anglia you learned in? The one that smelled of damp dog? Ah, Bessie. Now  that  was a car. None of this modern nonsense with all the electronic… whatchamacallits. Speaking of modern nonsense, have you sorted out the MOT for the Rover yet, Dad? It’s due next week, isn’t it? It is. I’m taking it to Old Man Hemmings. He’s a bit of a rogue, but he’ll always look after me. Won’t charge me the earth, unlike those big garages. Hemmings… isn’t he the one who failed my Darren’s car because of a slightly dim brake light? He’s thorough, is Hemmings. Safety first, eh? Anyway, this traffic's building up. Should’ve left earlier. Seems everyone’s heading to Dorset. Tell me about it! I’ve got an essay to write on post-structuralism, and I was hoping to get some reading done in the car. Now I’m just watching the brake lights of the car in front. Post-structuralism… sounds dreadful. What even  is  that? Something to do with buildings and… structures? Not exactly. It’s a philosophy thing. It’s really complicated… it questions everything. Honestly, sometimes I think my lecturer just makes it up as he goes along. Reminds me of trying to explain Windows 8 to Mum. She never got it. Windows 8 was awful. Couldn’t find anything! Gave me a headache just looking at it. I stick to what I know. Though I recently got one of those… Mantiques things. You know, for the garage. Oh, the wireless speaker? Darren got one. He loves it. Says he can listen to the radio while he’s working. Speaking of work, how are things going, Mum? Still having to cover all those shifts?

Right then, love. Kettle’s just boiled. You want a cuppa? Earl Grey alright? I remember you saying you liked a bit of bergamot. Oh, that’d be lovely, George. Thank you. Bergamot’s a treat, isn’t it? Makes it feel a bit…special. Though anything tastes good when you’ve been pottering about in the garden all afternoon. My back’s aching something dreadful. Garden’s a right beast this time of year, isn’t it? Everything growing at once, weeds taking over before you can blink. I tried to deadhead the roses earlier, and nearly poked my eye out. You and those roses! You’ve been battling them for years. Honestly, you’d think they were plotting against you. Milk and sugar for you, George? Just a dash of milk, please. Don’t want to ruin a perfectly good brew. Been thinking, you know… about young Michael. Michael? Your grandson? What about him? Is everything alright? He didn't mention anything when he called last week. Seemed cheerful enough. Oh, he sounded fine on the phone. But I was reading an article in that magazine –  Practical Retirement , you know the one – about apprenticeships. Seems a good way to get a trade, doesn’t it? He was always good with his hands, taking things apart and putting them back together. Though usually not quite  how  they were before… That's Michael, alright. Always tinkering. It's a good idea, an apprenticeship. Better than messing about with… well, you know. All these fancy degrees and whatnot. Doesn’t guarantee you a job these days, does it? Exactly! A proper skill is what’s needed. Plumbing, carpentry… something solid. I should mention it to him. But he’s always been a bit stubborn, that one. Thinks he knows best. They all do at that age, George. It's part of growing up. Just plant the seed, love. Let him come to it himself. Don't want to nag. It’ll just make him dig his heels in. You’re right, of course. You always are. You’ve got a knack for knowing how to handle those youngsters. All those years minding children…you learned a thing or two. You pick things up. Mostly patience, I think. And a healthy supply of biscuits. Speaking of which, are there any of those ginger snaps left? I could do with a little something sweet with my tea.

This pasta’s lovely, honestly. You’ve really outdone yourself, Liam. Is that basil from the garden? It smells amazing. Aye, it is! Finally getting a decent yield. Though the slugs are having a field day, little blighters. I might need to invest in some copper tape, you reckon? Copper tape sounds sensible, yeah. Or maybe one of those beer traps? Grandad used to swear by them. Though, knowing our luck, the slugs would throw a party in it. They probably would. Speaking of parties, did you manage to get ahold of Chloe? I haven't seen her post anything about coming down for the weekend. I did, earlier. She’s stuck in London with a conference. Said it’s absolutely rammed, and the weather’s been dreadful. Apparently, it's been pouring down all week – typical London. Oh, that’s a shame. I was looking forward to catching up. It feels like ages since we all properly hung out. Remember that awful indie night we went to with them last year? Oh god,  do  I. The sticky floors, the questionable music… and Mark trying to dance! It was glorious, and utterly mortifying, all at once. What was that band even called? ‘The Static Feedback’ or something? Something like that. Honestly, they sounded like someone was strangling a cat. But hey, at least it made for a good story. Did you hear that new album by Florence + the Machine? I did! I listened to it on my commute yesterday. It's… different. I’m not entirely sure what to make of it yet. It’s less anthemic, a bit more stripped back, yeah? Right? It’s a grower, I think. I’ve had it on repeat all day. It’s good to see her experimenting, though. Can't keep making ‘Lungs’ forever. True. Speaking of experimenting, how’s the PhD going? Are you any closer to cracking this coding problem that's been driving you mad? Slowly but surely. I think I’ve finally debugged the core program, which is a minor miracle. Now I’m wrestling with the visualisation aspect. It needs to be... elegant. Which is proving surprisingly challenging. Elegant coding – sounds like an oxymoron. You're always so precise though, I'm sure you'll get there. You know, I was thinking about getting some hanging baskets for the garden. What do you think? Petunias, maybe? Petunias are a good shout.

Liam Anya Honestly, this flat is a disaster zone. I swear, the research data multiplies when I’m not looking at it. Sounds familiar. My thesis feels like it’s breeding while I sleep. How’s the unemployment stuff going, by the way? Still wading through applications? Wading is… generous. It’s more like being repeatedly slapped in the face with rejection emails. It’s just… demoralising, you know? Seeing all these entry-level jobs requiring five years’ experience. Five! I’ve barely had five years  with  a degree. It’s ridiculous, isn’t it? The whole system is rigged. Remember when we were stressing about university fees? At least we  knew  we’d be in debt. This is just… a constant, low-level anxiety about finding something, anything, that pays the bills. Exactly! And then you see people who left uni with… less, honestly, less focused degrees, already climbing the ladder. It's infuriating. What about you? How's the PhD treating the bank account? Slowly bleeding it dry. Thankfully, the stipend covers the basics, but ‘basics’ in Cambridge are… optimistic. I’m seriously considering taking on tutoring just to be able to occasionally afford a takeaway that isn’t beans on toast. Oh god, the beans on toast life. I remember that well. I tutored for a year after my Masters, it was… exhausting. Especially the GCSE kids. Honestly, the drama. You’d think they were prepping for Hamlet, not a maths exam. It's the same with undergrads, honestly. The existential crises over essay deadlines. It's often more about emotional support than actual academic guidance. Speaking of drama, did you see that  Wicked  is playing in London?  Wicked ? Oh my god, I love  Wicked ! I saw it years ago with Mum, it was amazing. I’d absolutely go again. Though, funds are…tight, as we’ve established. I was thinking… maybe as a little pick-me-up? Once you land something, a celebratory  Wicked  trip? Or even just a cheaper matinee? That... actually sounds really good. A proper occasion, not just a ‘I haven’t cried today’ treat. Exactly! And we can belt out ‘Defying Gravity’ on the train home. Just annoy everyone. You know me too well. Oh, this reminds me, I had a private student once who insisted on singing show tunes  during  the lesson. It was a disaster. A complete and utter disaster. No way!

Honestly, the illustrations are lovely, aren’t they? Really capture that… wistful feeling. But the story itself… it feels a bit…flat. Flat? What do you mean, Mum? It’s about a little badger who loses his favourite button. Sounds good to me. It  sounds  good, darling, but it doesn’t  feel  good. There’s no… conflict. No real emotion. Think about the books Gran used to read to you. Remember ‘The Velveteen Rabbit’? That had real heart. Oh, ‘The Velveteen Rabbit’… that brought a tear to my eye every time. Such a beautiful story about becoming real through love. Your grandfather used to read it to your mother, you know. Yes, Mum. We’ve heard the story. Several times. And it’s a good comparison, actually. This badger, he needs a proper quest. He needs to overcome something. Maybe the button rolls into Old Man Hemlock’s garden, and everyone says Hemlock is a grumpy recluse… Ooh, that’s a good idea! A grumpy recluse! Maybe he secretly loves badgers? Maybe! See? That’s adding layers. Listen, I was thinking… we’ve all got so many stories about our family. What if we tried writing a children's book  about  our family? About us? What kind of story? Well, I was looking at this family tree I started – it's a mess, admittedly – and it got me thinking about how… complicated families can be. You’ve got me, and your Dad, and then Leo and Finn, and then your brother, and… well, it’s a lot. Complicated is an understatement, dear. Your father and his brothers… always a bit of a whirlwind, that lot. And then there was your Uncle Alistair, always chasing rainbows. What about my step-brothers? Would we include them? Of course! It’s about  all  of us. We could tell a story… about how families aren’t always perfect, how they change, and how no matter what, you can always find love and acceptance. It might be a bit ambitious for a kids’ book. Maybe we could make it about a family of squirrels? Squirrels have complicated family trees too, right? Lots of hiding nuts and forgetting where they put them. That's a good analogy for life, that is. Though my family wasn't known for hiding nuts, more for… airing grievances. Do you remember your Aunt Morag and her constant complaints about the price of tea?

Right, so I was talking to Debs at the library today, yeah? And she was going on about her new job at that Italian place, Bella Italia. Seems alright, loads of hours though. She’s proper stressed already. Oh, no way? Bella Italia? That’s… a choice. Loads of carbs if you work there, definitely. Bet she’s already put on weight just  smelling  the pasta. She said she’s living off salad this week to counteract it. Honestly, it sounds exhausting. I’m still glad I stuck with the bookshop. Slow pace, quiet… mostly. Though Mrs. Higgins did spend half an hour today complaining about the lack of Mills & Boon novels. Oh,  Mrs. Higgins . She's a legend. You should write a book about her. "The Romantics of Rotherham Road." It’d be a bestseller. Ha! Maybe. Though, honestly, I'm starting to feel like I need  a  job, you know? Like, a proper one. This student assistant stuff is alright, but it’s not exactly building a career. Tell me about it. I’m dreading the summer. Mum keeps hinting about me getting a ‘sensible’ placement. Like I haven’t spent the last two years studying history. “Useful skills,” she says. As if knowing the entire lineage of the Tudors is useless. Exactly! It's  cultural capital . They just don’t understand. Speaking of… did you shave your legs today? Oh, here we go. Seriously, Liv? We’re having a deep philosophical discussion about career prospects and you’re asking about my leg hair? Just making conversation! And yeah, seriously. It’s October, but they're looking a bit… wild. You know? Well, I’ve been busy. And frankly, I'm embracing my inner cavewoman. It's warmer. Think of it as insulation. Insulation? You're going to attract moths! I swear, I'm starting to grow a moustache if I don't keep on top of it. Not a full-on one, thankfully, just… fuzz. You and your fuzz! You're so dramatic. You're not growing a moustache. Honestly, it's liberating not shaving. Less faff. Plus, think of all the water we're saving. Okay, okay, you’ve made your point. Environmental warrior. But if you come near me with those hairy legs, I'm deploying the emergency tweezers. Oh, you wouldn’t dare! Besides, they're not  that  hairy. They’re… gloriously natural. Gloriously natural and potentially causing a national crisis.

Right, so ‘V’ is for… vehemently disagreeing with anyone who thinks alcopops are a good idea. Honestly, a sugary mess. Harsh. Though, I get it. They’re a gateway drug, aren't they? Proper student fodder. Speaking of which, remember that time Liam tried to make his own… well, let’s just call it ‘hooch’? Oh, God, no. Don’t. The smell alone was a biohazard. The whole hall reeked of fermented apples and regret for a week. He nearly poisoned half the floor. He swore it was perfectly safe! Said his grandad used to make it all the time. Turns out grandad was a master of plausible deniability and a terrible brewer. And then he tried to say it was basically cider. Liam always did have a… flexible relationship with the truth. What’s ‘W’ then? ‘W’… wrestling. Or, more specifically, boxing. Saw a decent fight last weekend - local lad, did really well. Proper grit. Reminded me of that time your cousin, Mark, thought he was Muhammad Ali after too many pints. Oh, don’t even. The pub brawl that wasn’t? He spent most of it apologizing and trying to explain he was ‘just practicing his footwork’. The landlord wasn't buying it. The landlord nearly threw him out! It was brilliant. He was swinging wildly, missing everything. It was less boxing and more… flailing. Okay, ‘X’ is tricky. Xenophobia. Sadly rather relevant, especially with the football. I was reading an article about the racist abuse aimed at some of the England players at the Euros. Disgusting. It is. You wouldn’t think in this day and age… It's always simmering under the surface, isn't it? I mean, I remember being at a match years ago, and hearing some really vile stuff. It just… chills you. It does. And the fact that it’s still happening, still being downplayed by some… it’s infuriating. Makes you wonder what it takes to actually make a difference. It’s a systemic problem, I think. Starts with the tabloid press, fosters a climate of… othering. Which conveniently leads us to ‘Y’ for yelling racist abuse. Horrible, but true. Ugh. Yeah. Let's not dwell. One more. ‘Z’… zzz's. Because honestly, after talking about all that, I need a nap. Or another pint. I second that pint. To avoiding homemade hooch, flailing relatives, and hoping for a future where football fans can just… enjoy the game.

…and honestly, the estate agent was  so  optimistic. “A little TLC,” he called it. TLC! The entire west wing is practically breathing damp. You could grow mushrooms in the drawing-room, I swear. Oh, estate agents. They’re masters of understatement. I had one once describe a collapsed roof as “having character.” Did you get a proper structural survey done before you even considered putting in an offer? Of course, of course. Though I suspect even the surveyor was being polite. The timbers are… well, let's just say they've seen better centuries. But the potential! It’s a Grade II listed manor house, Doreen, built in 1680. The original panelling is exquisite. 1680… Lovely. And what’s the client hoping to achieve with it? A hotel? Holiday lets? They’re toying with the idea of a small, boutique hotel. Ten rooms, maybe. But the budget is, shall we say,  ambitious  for the scale of the work required. They’ve clearly watched too much of ‘Escape to the Country’. Ah, the ‘Escape to the Country’ effect. It invariably leads to tears. Boutique hotels in historic buildings rarely end well unless there's a substantial pot of money behind them. Have you looked at the potential for Heritage Lottery funding? That’s what I wanted to pick your brain about, actually. I've done a preliminary search, and it  might  be eligible, but the criteria are so convoluted. I’m worried we’ll spend weeks on a bid and then be told it’s not applicable because of some obscure clause about maintaining the ‘historic fabric’ whilst simultaneously installing underfloor heating. The eternal struggle! Yes, the HLF can be a nightmare. The key is to frame it as more than just a commercial venture. Focus on the community benefit. Will it create jobs? Will it offer educational opportunities? Will it preserve a vital piece of local heritage? Emphasise the latter, of course, but weave in the other elements. They  love  a good community engagement strategy. That’s a good point. They want to host local art exhibitions and things like that. I hadn’t specifically highlighted it as a benefit in the initial draft of the proposal. It was more about ‘luxury weekend getaways’. Luxury weekend getaways are all well and good, but they don’t shout “nationally important heritage asset!” You also need a really robust business plan. Show them you’ve thought through the long-term sustainability of the project.

Right, so three sugars for you then? Honestly, you’re going to be bouncing off the walls by lunchtime. You’d think a PhD student would have more self-discipline than that. Hey, research is exhausting! Brain food, I tell you. Brain food. And you know I need the energy to decipher whatever Professor Davies is rambling on about this week. It’s like he  wants  to be incomprehensible. Sounds about right. Honestly, I sometimes think academics deliberately build walls of jargon just to feel superior. Speaking of jargon, how's the data looking for your thesis? Still wrestling with those statistical anomalies? It’s…progressing. Slowly. I’ve managed to refine the model a bit, but honestly, I’m starting to suspect a fundamental flaw in my initial assumptions. It's all about the pragmatics of politeness strategies, remember? And it turns out, people are just…messy. They don't follow neat little rules. Tell me about it. I deal with survey data all day. People will lie to your face, or just not remember what they did five minutes ago. Humans are terrible data points. Seriously. Is it the politeness strategies differing depending on social grouping you're looking at? Exactly! I was hoping for a neat correlation between socio-economic background and the types of indirectness people use, but there's so much overlap and variability. It's making it really hard to draw any firm conclusions. It’s fascinating, but frustrating. It feels like linguistics is less a science and more… interpretive dance sometimes. Interpretive dance. I like that. It’s a bit like my job, actually. I’m supposed to be finding statistically significant patterns in customer behaviour, but half the time it feels like I'm just telling a story with numbers. See? We’re basically professional storytellers. With slightly fancier qualifications. Anyway, enough about my research woes. What about you? Any exciting developments at work? Besides the usual data-wrangling. Not really. Just prepping for the next round of focus groups. We're looking at perceptions of sustainable packaging. Apparently, everyone  says  they care about the environment, but their purchasing habits tell a completely different story. The hypocrisy of humankind. A classic. So, distraction tactic needed then? Have you properly started planning that trip to Greece? You were on about Santorini last time we spoke. I have! I've actually booked the flights. We're going for ten days, end of July.

Right, so, school dinners. How were they today? Lily, you go first. Okay. It was… beige. Beige? That’s… descriptive. What  was  beige? Everything. The chicken, the potatoes, the… stuff. It all looked the same colour. Mine had green bits! Broccoli! I don't  like  broccoli. Oh dear. Did you eat around it, Leo? I tried to hide it under my chicken, but Mrs. Davies saw. She said I had to eat  some . Oh, that's a shame. Well, at least you tried. Did anyone have pudding? Chocolate concrete. It was a bit hard. Chocolate concrete? Is that a new flavour? It’s just… really firm chocolate pudding. Right. Well, that doesn’t sound terrible. We should probably talk about money for the tennis tournament next week. It’s £10, isn’t it? Ten pounds?! That’s  loads  of money! Can I win a trophy? You might be able to, Leo! If you play well. But £10 covers the cost of the court hire and the little prizes. It's going to go quickly. I’ll transfer it over tonight. Mummy, remember when we went to Granny’s? She gave us loads of biscuits. Way better than school dinners. Granny  does  spoil you both. And her biscuits are legendary. Though perhaps not a balanced diet. Granny said she used to run away to join the circus! Did she? Your Granny was a bit of a rebel, wasn't she? She said she wanted to be a clown! But Grandad found her and brought her home. A clown? Granny? That's… silly. It is a little silly, isn't it? Although I can imagine her being a very dramatic clown. All bright colours and big shoes. She said she could ride a horse and juggle! I believe she  did  ride a horse when she was younger. Juggling… well, that might have been an exaggeration. I want to be in the circus! Can I be a trapeze artist? A trapeze artist? That takes a lot of practice, sweetie. And courage! I want to tame lions! Oh dear. Perhaps we should stick to the tennis tournament for now. Lions are a little too ambitious, don’t you think? Right, who wants an apple? It’s a slightly less beige option than school dinner chicken. Speaker_2 & Speaker_3 : Me! Okay, okay, one each. And then we need to think about what you’re wearing for the tournament.

Honestly, the special effects were incredible, but the plot…thin as a wafer. All flash and no substance, really. Hmm. That sounds about right for most of these blockbusters these days, doesn't it? Give 'em something shiny to look at and they won't notice the story’s missing a few chapters. Reminds me of Parliament, actually. Dad, you always find a way to bring it back to politics. But you’re not wrong. It  was  very… visually arresting. I was thinking about that debate at Cambridge last week, actually, the one about historical teaching. Oh, the one about narratives? I read a bit about it. A lot of contention, wasn’t there? Seems people are really divided on how much focus should be on, well, perspectives. Exactly. It felt a bit performative, to be honest. A load of academics shouting at each other about ‘decolonising the curriculum’ while ignoring the practicalities of getting kids to actually  learn  dates and key events. Decolonising… fancy word. When I was at school, history was about Kings and Queens, battles and empires. Simple. And we learned it all by rote. Probably did us more good than all this… nuanced approach. But wasn’t that part of the problem, Dad? A very… specific narrative? I mean, my history teachers were brilliant, but it was very focused on British achievements. Very little about, say, the impact of colonialism on other cultures. That’s the point, isn’t it? It’s not about erasing history, it’s about presenting a more complete picture. But it’s incredibly difficult to balance that with the constraints of the national curriculum. It’s already crammed full. It is. And revised constantly! Honestly, the poor teachers are running to keep up. Remember when they changed the way they taught Maths? Utter chaos. Oh God, yes. I remember my mum trying to help me with ‘new maths’ and ending up more confused than I was. She’d been taught completely differently. I never understood all that new maths business. Numbers are numbers, aren’t they? Straightforward. When  I  was at school—which, admittedly, was a long time ago—we had a proper grounding. Latin, Greek… it taught you discipline. It sounds… intense. I did Latin for a year, hated it. I was much more focused on English Lit. And Drama. See, that’s the thing. The system needs to be more flexible.

Right proper chilly this morning, innit? Feels like October already, not August. It does, doesn’t it? Lovely and sunny now, though. Makes a difference. I put the washing out. Hopefully it’ll dry. Everything’s been so damp lately. Damp is an understatement, Margaret. We had a proper downpour yesterday afternoon. Nearly flooded the patio. Had to send young Thomas out with a mop. Sounds like you've got him working hard for his keep. Reminds me of when I was a lad. My old man always had me doing jobs around the house. Said it built character. Character and blisters, more like. My dad weren't one for making me graft, no. He was always more interested in his pigeons. Spent his whole life with them birds. Daft, really, when you think about it. Your father was a lovely man, Albert. He always had a kind word. And he did build that magnificent pigeon coop, didn’t he? A real craftsman. He was. Reminds me… I was sorting through some old photos the other day, and came across one of your mum, Eileen, Albert. She was a beauty. And she always remembered everyone’s name. A proper lady. Aye, she was. Always worried about everyone else. Always baking. Couldn’t get her to sit still, she couldn’t. Always on the go. Wonder what she’d make of all this, eh? All the trouble in the world. She’d be heartbroken, I reckon. Reminds me of my grandmother. Lived through the war, she did. Lost her brother at Dunkirk. Never really spoke about it, but you could see it haunted her. These conflicts…they ripple down the generations, don’t they? They do. It’s awful what’s happening over in Ukraine. Makes you feel so helpless. Brings it all back, doesn’t it? The stories you heard growing up… Absolutely. And the way the police are dealing with these protests now. Seems a bit heavy-handed to me. Blocking roads, arresting people… Freedom of speech is going out the window. It's a tricky one, isn't it? Striking a balance between allowing people to protest and maintaining order. But some of those tactics do seem a bit draconian. Still, better than what you see in some other countries. Speaking of order, Doreen, remember that awful mahogany sideboard your parents had? The one that smelled of beeswax? Oh, how could I forget?

Right, so just to be clear, you’ve got the keys to the flat, Mum has a box of stuff for you – mostly photos, I suspect – and I’m just…processing the whole ‘last drive’ thing. Feels weird, doesn’t it? Weird is an understatement, son. Absolutely strange. Thirty-odd years, dropping you kids off at school, picking you up, driving you to uni… and now it’s the last run from your mum’s. Feels like a chapter’s closed, that’s for sure. Though, to be honest, a lot of chapters feel closed recently. Tell me about it. This whole house move feels like a massive upheaval. You sure you’re alright with all this, Dad? Really? Of course I am. It’s… sensible. Downsizing. Makes perfect financial sense. Though, a part of me wishes your mother was still around to argue about it. She’d have a whole list of reasons  not  to move, you know. "Too much history," she'd say. "Where will I put the china?" God, she would. Speaking of financial sense, how’s the mortgage looking on the new place? Everything sorted? Nearly. The solicitor’s being a bit slow, to be honest. Keeps asking for the same documents again and again. Drives me mad. Standard, I suppose. But yes, the finances are… manageable. Though, don't mention the word 'interest rates' to me, I might have a little fit. I hear you. They're scary. Listen, are you still feeling a bit rough? You sounded a bit congested on the phone yesterday. Just a bit of a cold, I think. Old age creeping up on me, that’s all. Shouldn't have been outside helping your sister load the van on Saturday. Damp air did for me. Probably. Though Brenda from work swears it’s going around. She’s been brewing ginger and lemon tea all week. You should get some of that. Mum always swore by ginger and lemon. Speaking of Brenda, how's work? Still dealing with complaints about broadband speed? Oh, you have  no  idea. It's relentless. People yelling down the phone, blaming  me  for their internet not working. Honestly, some of them… you’d think I personally built the infrastructure. They’re lucky I'm relatively patient. It's good money, though. Keeps me ticking over. You deserve a medal. Seriously. So, Auntie Carol, did you manage to speak to her about Christmas?

Right, so we’re agreed – roast beef then? Your Nan always loved a good roast, and it feels…fitting, doesn’t it? Yeah, roast beef’s good. Though she did say last week she wasn’t keen on gravy anymore. Something about it being “too sludgy,” which, honestly, sounded a bit like her. Oh, she always had a way with words, didn’t she? Alright, no gravy. We can do horseradish sauce, and maybe a nice minted jelly. Now, the table. I was thinking I’d put Uncle George next to you. He’s been asking after you, and he’ll keep you entertained with his stories. Oh, no. Please not George. He’ll spend the entire meal talking about his fishing trips and how he almost caught a cod the size of a small child. Can I maybe have Auntie Brenda instead? She’s much kinder. Hmm. Alright, Auntie Brenda it is. But you owe me one. George will be devastated. And then…let’s see. Your cousin Liam is coming with his girlfriend, right? They can go on the end, near the window. Yep, that sounds good. He said she’s really looking forward to meeting everyone. She’s a bit shy, apparently. Oh, bless. We’ll make her feel welcome. Right, food mostly sorted. I’m going to pop down to Billingsgate tomorrow morning for the beef. They have the best quality, and I want it to be perfect. Billingsgate? Wow, that’s a trek! Are you sure? Old Man Hemmings does a lovely bit of beef down at the market. Hemmings is alright, but it’s not  Billingsgate  alright? It's her birthday, and I want everything to be special. Plus, I need to get some salmon for myself. Been craving it all week. Speaking of craving… didn’t you say you were rearranging the kitchen cupboards? Are you still on for finding space for all those candles you bought? Oh, don't even remind me. It's a disaster! I thought I had a brilliant system, but then I ended up with a mountain of Tupperware and nowhere to put the decorative things. And have you seen how many tins of tomatoes we have? It’s ridiculous. You do love a bargain tin of tomatoes. I'll help you when I come round on Saturday. We can sort it all out. That would be amazing, thank you.

Honestly, this pain is ridiculous. I’ve been popping paracetamol like sweets all day. Still your wisdom teeth then? Are they actually  coming  through, or just… being generally awful? A bit of both, I think. One's definitely poking, feels like it’s trying to bore a hole straight through my cheek. And the other… well, it just feels like someone’s constantly prodding it with a fork. It’s vile. Oh god, that sounds grim. Have you managed to get an appointment with a dentist? Is it even possible here in France? I’ve tried! They’re saying the earliest they can see me is…next Tuesday. Which feels like a lifetime away. Mum keeps saying I should’ve gone to a dentist before we came, but honestly, who thinks to plan dental work around a holiday? Mum, always the planner. Mine would have just said, “Oh, you’ll be fine, a bit of pain never hurt anyone.” Remember when I broke my wrist and she tried to convince me it was just a sprain? Oh, your mum! Honestly. They're all the same aren't they? Just… dismissive of actual discomfort. Though, to be fair, yours  is  a bit of a tough cookie. She is. Still, it’s nice being away from it all, even if you're suffering. Just… peaceful. Are you dreading going back to uni? Oh, massively. I'm gonna have to start properly thinking about dissertations and everything, and I just haven't got the headspace for it right now. I’ve been deliberately avoiding it. And then there's the whole house move thing. Oh yeah, your folks are still moving, aren’t they? Is it all going okay? Doncaster to…where again? Lincoln. It’s taking forever. Apparently, the people buying our house are being really difficult. Mum's on the phone constantly, getting stressed. It's a nightmare. She's convinced they're trying to haggle the price down at the last minute because they found a… a hole in the garden shed. A hole? In a shed? Really? That’s… pettiness on a whole new level. She needs to tell them to sort it themselves if it bothers them so much. That’s what I said! But she's worried it'll fall through. Honestly, she's a nervous wreck. I’m trying to be supportive, but it's hard when it’s all just…shed-related drama.

Right, so, Operation Random Acts of Kindness is a go. Any initial thoughts? Apart from leaving glitter bombs everywhere, which is absolutely off the table, Leo. But it would be  funny ! No. Absolutely not. We're aiming for nice, thoughtful, not sparkly chaos. Elsie, you first. What wonderful thing could you do for someone? Hmm… I could make Mrs. Peterson a card. She always gives me stickers. That’s lovely, Elsie! A really thoughtful idea. And you, Leo? Something beyond attempting to bedazzle the postman? I could…help Dad wash the car? A valiant offer. Though I suspect he might suspect ulterior motives involving a favour later. But yes, good! It counts. We could also bake something. I was looking at lactose-free cake and cookie recipes. Your tummy hasn’t been entirely happy with dairy lately, Elsie. Ooh, cookies! Chocolate chip? Possibly. Or maybe something with orange… It's nearly Chinese New Year, isn’t it? We could make mooncakes, although those are…a bit more involved. Speaking of which, did you two know it’s the Year of the Dragon? Dragons are cool! They breathe fire! Can we decorate the house with dragons? We can definitely decorate. I’ve got some red paper and gold glitter –  responsible  glitter, not the bombing variety – and we can make paper chains. Maybe even try our hand at calligraphy, though my Chinese writing skills are…non-existent. Mummy, can we have a Chinese takeaway? We can  discuss  a Chinese takeaway. After acts of kindness, mind you. We don’t want bribery involved. Right, back to ideas. I was thinking about leaving little notes of encouragement in library books. Or we could use the chess pieces as money! Like, if someone needs a pound, they can have a rook! That’s…creative. And slightly illogical, but creative. Though I foresee arguments over the relative value of a knight versus a bishop. No, we're sticking to actual money for charitable donations, I think. I've been trying to think of things we can do that don't  cost  a lot. We could give Grandma flowers! That’s a brilliant idea, Elsie! We could pick some from the garden, or maybe buy a small bunch. Speaking of Grandma, did you know Auntie Carol is thinking about dying her hair purple? Purple?! That’s awesome! I know! She said she wants to “rebel against the grey.” I think she’s having a mid-life crisis, but a colourful one.

Mum, did you  see  Mrs. Henderson’s car this morning? It was… well, it wasn’t really a car anymore, was it? Oh dear. No, I missed that. What happened? Another seagull incident? They're getting bolder, you know. Saw one try to steal a chip right out of old Mr. Davies’ hand yesterday. No, way worse! Apparently, someone ran a red light on Queens Road and smashed right into her. She wasn’t in it, thank goodness, but the car… it was awful. All crunched up. Oh, that’s terrible. Poor woman. Glad she wasn’t hurt. It makes you think, doesn’t it? How quickly things can change. It's a bit like Alice falling down the rabbit hole, isn’t it? One minute you're pottering along, the next… chaos. Kind of, yeah. Though Alice’s chaos was a lot more… whimsical. Have you read  Alice in Wonderland  to Leo yet? Not yet, darling. I keep meaning to. He’s been obsessed with dinosaurs lately. Roaring all day long! Such a little terror. Speaking of little terrors, did you notice that new scratch on your knee? How did  that  happen? Oh, that? Just tripped over the cat in the garden. Felix was being a menace, weaving between my legs. It stings a bit. I think I'll have a scar. You always were a bit clumsy, my love. It'll fade, don't worry. I have a  fantastic  scar story, actually. When I was about your age, I tried to build a stage for a puppet show in the garden… needless to say, it collapsed, and I ended up with a massive splinter in my hand. Had to go to A&E! Ouch! Was it painful? Oh, it was dreadful. But it was worth it for the puppet show! Speaking of shows, are you still practicing your song for the school play? Yeah, I think so.
