It’s really hard… it’s that high note in the chorus. And Miss Davies wants me to  really  embody the character. She said I need to find the character’s inner life. Sounds intense. What song is it again? It’s from  Wicked . “Defying Gravity.” It's so good, but hard to sing. I've been looking at tutorials online, on YouTube, to get the high note right. Good for you! Using the internet for good. Leo, on the other hand, just uses it to watch videos of people opening presents.

Honestly, after last night, I feel utterly drained. Giving that advice to the solar panel lot… it's just reliving it all again, isn't it? Feels like Groundhog Day with pylons and turbines. It  is  exhausting, isn’t it? You put so much into fighting the wind farm, then another one pops up, or now, fields covered in solar. It's relentless. Did they seem receptive to what you said? The solar group, I mean. Receptive? Aye, they were. Colin, bless him, was scribbling notes faster than I’ve ever seen. They’re a bit…naive, though. Thinking a strongly worded letter to the council will do the trick. They haven't grasped the scale of it yet. Exactly! It's not about convincing the Development Control Committee. It’s about understanding who  really  pulls the strings. And the money. Oh, the money involved. They need to dig, find out who’s funding the applications, who stands to benefit. You were right about the planning appeal, though. That's where they nearly tripped themselves up. Not having a proper barrister, relying on a local solicitor who hadn't dealt with anything like it before… a complete disaster waiting to happen. We were lucky to get away with it, honestly. Lucky and determined. Don’t undersell your work, Margaret. You practically lived in the library for months, chasing down precedents. And you were brilliant at getting the local press onside. That’s crucial. Public opinion can sway things, even with a biased council. The press helped, certainly. Though I still think they sensationalized it a bit. ‘Save Our Skyline!’ rather dramatic, wouldn’t you say? Still, it got people talking. But honestly, it’s the council itself…they’re just so easily swayed. A few promises of ‘green jobs’ and they’re putty in the hands of these energy companies. It’s not all their fault. They're under pressure from central government. Foot-dragging on truly sustainable energy solutions puts them in a difficult position. They’re supposed to meet these climate targets, and frankly, wind and solar are the easy answers, regardless of whether they're suitable for the local environment. Easy and profitable for someone. That's the crux of it. And all this talk of ‘renewable energy’… where’s the investment in  storage ? We can generate all the power in the world, but if we can't store it when the wind isn't blowing or the sun isn’t shining… it’s pointless.

So, how’s the driving going, love? Any closer to passing that test? It’s…progressing. Slowly. Had another lesson yesterday, and Mr. Henderson, bless him, is still saying my junctions are “ambitious.” Ambitious, is it? That's a polite way of saying you’re still shooting the gap! Your father was the same when he first learned, you know. Nearly took out Old Man Hemmings’ hedge on Woburn Road. Now, Margaret, don't embellish! I didn’t  nearly  take it out. I just…misjudged the width of my father’s Austin A30. It was a narrow escape, admittedly. But it taught me a valuable lesson about spatial awareness. Right. So, basically, I’m following in your footsteps, Dad. Except with a slightly more modern vehicle and hopefully fewer near-hedge experiences. The parallel parking is the worst. I just get flustered. You just need to visualise it, dear. Think of it like… threading a needle. Slow and steady. And don’t look in the mirror  too  much – that’s what Derek always says. He gets right stressed watching people park. Derek’s a backseat driver even when he’s not  in  the car. Speaking of cars, have you looked into insurance quotes yet? That can be a shock, you know. Especially for new drivers. I’ve had a look, yeah. It's… eye-watering. Trying to add me as a named driver on Mum’s policy is the cheapest option, but even then it’s not exactly budget-friendly. Well, it’s peace of mind, isn’t it? And you’ll be able to visit more often. Speaking of visits, are you still thinking about that little tour of France this summer? I am! I’ve been looking at gites in Normandy. Nothing fancy, just a little cottage with a garden. I thought maybe a week or so, just to practice my French and…you know, relax. Normandy’s lovely. We went there years ago, Margaret and I. The food was excellent. Though I must say, trying to order a simple cup of coffee was an ordeal. My schoolboy French wasn't up to much. Oh, you’d manage, Arthur. You always charm your way through. What about you, love? Still on for dinner with Bethany and her husband on Wednesday? Yes, definitely. I promised them ages ago. It’ll be good to catch up. She’s been really busy with a new project at work.

Honestly, Dad, the parking around here is a nightmare. I nearly got a ticket trying to pop into the shops earlier. It's worse than Brighton, and that's saying something! Brighton? Don't talk to me about Brighton. Full of students and… well,  people . And you can't park anywhere, ever. Used to be a decent seaside town, you know. Back in the fifties, you could park right on the promenade. None of this fancy double yellow nonsense. You and your fifties stories. Though, honestly, a bit of promenade parking wouldn’t go amiss now. Did you see that article online about the council proposing even more restrictions? It’s infuriating. Online, eh? You and that phone… constantly glued to it. Always getting those… notifications. Beep beep beep all day long. Drives me mad. What is it this time? Facebook telling you Brenda down the road bought a new hat? It’s not  just  Facebook, Dad! It's useful, honestly. I’m organising a flat viewing for when I finally move. Found a couple of places that look alright near the station. Moving? Still going on about Brighton, then? You’ll miss your mother’s cooking, you know. Though even  she’s  complaining about the price of everything these days. Nearly had a fit over the cost of sprouts at the market. I’ll still come home for Sunday roast! And I can learn to cook, can’t I? I’m slowly getting there. Attempted a shepherd’s pie last week. It was… edible. Edible? That's a low bar, love. Your mother could feed a family of ten on what she could get out of a tin of beans and a bit of ingenuity. These days… everyone wants avocado and quinoa. When I was a lad, if you were lucky, you got a bit of dripping on your bread. And we survived. It’s a bit different now, Dad. People need proper nutrition and… I don't know. It’s just sad seeing how many people are relying on food banks, even while politicians argue about… well, everything. Politicians. Don’t get me started. Bunch of… anyway. You enjoying your tea? Biscuits alright? I got those nice shortbread ones you like. They’re lovely, thanks. Makes a change from those ginger snaps you’re so fond of. Though to be fair, I'll eat anything dunked in tea. Speaking of which, are you still having a little bet on the horses?

Honestly, this coffee is…adequate. It’s doing a job, I suppose. Reminds me of university cafeteria coffee. You know, the stuff you drink because you  need  to stay awake for another Shakespeare lecture. Oh God, Shakespeare. Professor Armitage, right? The one who could deliver a soliloquy with more drama than Olivier? And then sigh dramatically when no one “understood the subtext.” The very one. He once marked down a student for being “too enthusiastic” in their interpretation of Hamlet. Too enthusiastic! The man thrived on misery. He probably secretly enjoyed crushing our souls. Sounds about right. He probably went home and practiced his disappointed professor face in the mirror. Speaking of soul-crushing, how’s the job at the bookshop going? Still enduring endless requests for Dan Brown? Don't even  start . It’s a constant stream. And the people who ask for “that book with the code”… honestly. I’ve started just directing them to the children’s section. More intellectually stimulating, frankly. You’d think being surrounded by books would be idyllic, but it mostly involves explaining to people where the toilets are. Classic. My temporary gig at the golf club is… interesting. Mostly it’s listening to incredibly specific complaints about swing technique and trying not to look like I have absolutely no idea what they’re talking about. You and golf. A truly baffling combination. I always pictured you as more of a… competitive thumb-wrestling champion. Hey! I  am  a competitive thumb-wrestling champion. Relatively speaking. I once beat Old Man Hemmings down the street. Legend has it he was a fearsome opponent in his youth. It was a glorious victory. I truly  won  that day. Right, and you’ve been bragging about it for approximately three years. It’s almost impressive. Speaking of family legends, did your Auntie Maureen ever tell you the story about why your surname is actually a slightly altered version of ‘Nightingale’? Oh, here we go. She’s been digging that up again? It involves a… questionable ancestor who changed his name to avoid debtors, apparently. And a fondness for singing off-key. That’s where the Nightingale bit comes in. I swear, she finds these things out just to embarrass me. Everyone calls me ‘Nige’ for a reason – it’s vastly preferable. She’s a character, that one. My grandmother’s obsessed with tracing our family tree. She’s discovered we had a distant relative who was a sheep thief.

Honestly, this week at work has been  mental . Like, genuinely questioning all my life choices mental. Tell me about it. I spent all Tuesday shifting bricks in the rain. Rain, right? November rain is a different beast altogether. Just…seeps into your bones. Oh, you poor thing! I thought my week was bad. We had a last-minute change of speakers for the conference, and it’s thrown the whole schedule. I’ve basically been running around like a headless chicken trying to re-organize everything. And  everyone  is blaming me, naturally. Classic. It's always the event coordinator's fault when things go wrong, isn’t it? Even if it’s completely outside your control. I swear, people think we just  wave a magic wand  and everything falls into place. Yeah, nobody appreciates the graft, do they? Especially when it involves physical graft. My back is killing me. Speaking of killing you…are we still on for that Thai green curry thing on Saturday? I need a proper treat after this week. And possibly a lie-down. Absolutely! I’m already planning what spring rolls to get from that place near the market. They do the best. Though, I  should  be trying to be good. I started a new diet, you know. A diet? In November? You’re a braver woman than me. I’m leaning into winter comfort food. Stews, roast dinners, that sort of thing. It’s a survival mechanism, honestly. I know, right? But I keep seeing these fitness influencers online and feeling bad about myself. It's just…an attempt to counteract. It’s one of those “eat clean, feel clean” things. It lasts about a day. Those influencers are the worst. All perfectly filtered lives and avocado toast. I used to follow one, she was all about ‘intuitive eating’ and then posted a picture of a huge chocolate cake. Like, make up your mind! Exactly! It’s so disingenuous. Anyway, I’m trying to cut out carbs, which is already a disaster. I’m living on salads and sadness. Sounds grim. You need to move out of Cambridge, honestly. Too many healthy eating places here. Back in Doncaster, it's all about value for money and a good chip butty. Oh, I miss a good chip butty! Actually, talking about moving… have you two heard anything about Leo finding a place? He’s been sofa surfing for weeks now.

Right, well, you can just about see the whole garden from here, can’t you? Bit of a mess, mind you. Haven't had a chance to get out there properly since…well, since everything. Looks alright to me, Arthur. A bit overgrown, maybe. Good to see some green, though. Everything seems so grey these days. Hello, Margaret, you still there? Bit laggy today, this Skype business. Yes, I’m here, George. It  is  a bit patchy. Arthur, it's lovely to see your garden! You always did have a knack with things growing. Are those your tomatoes coming along nicely? Not bad, not bad. Though the slugs are having a field day. Need to get out there with some beer traps, I reckon. Speaking of which, you remember old Mrs. Higgins next door? She’s started replacing all her fencing. Right up to the boundary, the cheek! Cheeky cow, that woman! Always has been. Boundary disputes, that’s all it is. Probably thinks she’s gaining a few inches. Exactly! And she's put up a right ugly fence too. Dark brown, clashes with everything. Makes our little bit look scruffy. Oh dear. That doesn't sound pleasant, Arthur. Trying to be neighbourly is hard enough as it is. Did you speak to her about it? Tried. She just gave me a look that could curdle milk. Said it’s her land, she can do what she likes. Honestly. Sounds like a right battle brewing there. Don't let it get you down, Arthur. It’s not worth the stress. What about that owl box you were building? Did you ever get that up? It's up, yeah. Put it on that old oak tree over there. Haven’t seen any owls take up residence yet, though. Maybe they don’t like the neighbourhood. Give it time, George. They're shy creatures. I've got a lovely little herb garden going, filled with rosemary and thyme. Helps with the cooking, you know. Trying to eat a bit better now, old age creeping up. You and me both, Margaret. Though I’m still partial to a bit of pie and mash. Speaking of which, did you see that painting programme on last night? The one with the chap who paints landscapes? Can't say I did. I was watching a documentary about black holes. Fascinating stuff. Black holes? Oh, Arthur, you and your cosmos!

Honestly, this traffic is mental. I didn’t realise getting to Durham for a Sunday roast could be so…an ordeal. Tell me about it. Should've just taken the train. Though, admittedly, the train station's a bit of a trek from where your aunt lives, isn't it? Aye, it is. And then you're relying on buses. Those Durham buses are…an experience. Remember that one time with Old Man Hemmings? Oh god, how could I forget? He was convinced the bus was actively trying to avoid his stop. Spent the entire journey shouting directions at the driver. He did! And the driver just kept ignoring him. Proper Geordie grit, that man had. Speaking of grit, have you ever actually  been  inside Durham Cathedral? It's spectacular. I’ve seen it from the outside. It looks…imposing. Proper, you know? But no, never been in. Always seemed a bit too touristy. Touristy, maybe. But the architecture…it's breathtaking. And the cloisters! They filmed bits of Harry Potter there, did you know? Really? Which bit? I’m always slightly skeptical of those claims. Seems like every old building in Britain’s ‘been in Harry Potter’. Honestly, I can’t remember which film, but my cousin, she’s a proper Potterhead, swears it’s there. Anyway, speaking of impressive buildings… did you see that house in Hexham we drove past earlier? The one with the huge garden? The grey stone one? Yeah, it was lovely. A bit secluded though, wasn’t it? Aye, right up on the hill. Wonder what it costs. Probably a fortune. You'd need a whole team of gardeners just to keep that lawn tidy. Easily half a million, I’d guess. Maybe more. It’s all relative, I suppose. What's a fortune in Northumberland is just…normal in Surrey. True enough. Still, dreaming's free, eh? I'd settle for a little cottage with a decent garden. Something where I could keep a couple of chickens. Chickens? You? I thought you were a city girl. I can be both! Plus, fresh eggs. You can't argue with that. What about you? Dream house? No mention of glass and steel modernist monstrosities, please. No, no. Probably something a bit more…traditional. Stone cottage, like you said, but maybe a bit closer to civilisation. Somewhere with a good pub within walking distance. Now you’re talking.

Honestly, that robin this morning… sounded like it was right  in  the room. Woke me up good and proper. Not a bad thing, mind, but a bit startling at half past five. Oh, I know the feeling. Though mine’s usually a blackbird, all showy and loud. More of a performance than a song, really. You’d think they were auditioning for the Royal Opera House! Are you still getting through all that birdseed? Oh, buckets of it! The long-tailed tits are relentless. They come in little squadrons, you know? And the great spotted woodpecker… he’s a right character. He clings to the feeder like a little acrobat. It’s a right mess though, all the husks everywhere. It is a bit of a palaver, isn't it? Still, better than listening to that dreadful beeping on my alarm clock. I swear, it gets more aggressive with each passing year. I keep meaning to get a gentler one. Maybe one with birdsong, ironically. That  would  be ironic! I've just switched to my phone, actually. A gradual sunrise simulation. Much kinder. Though I did have a bit of a scare last week. Woke up with a nosebleed. A proper gusher. Oh dear! That sounds alarming. Were you alright? Honestly, it frightened the life out of me. Thought I was losing a pint! Managed to stop it eventually, but it left me feeling quite shaky. I’m going to mention it to Dr. Davies next time I’m in, just to be on the safe side. You having any worries health-wise? Well, old Mrs. Higgins down the road… she’s not been looking herself at all. Very pale. Apparently, it's her throat. They suspect something… not good. You know, she was always such a vibrant woman, always puttering about in her garden. Oh, that’s dreadful. Poor woman. I remember her from the village fêtes – always had the best tomatoes. It's terrifying, isn't it? You read so much about it…throat cancer is on the rise. It is. And she’s a smoker, you see. Always has been. I tried to gently suggest she give up years ago, but she just wouldn't listen. Stubborn as a mule, she is. They often are. It's difficult to tell someone what to do with their own life. Though you can see the consequences, can't you? Speaking of gardens, mine is a complete disaster.

Honestly, it’s just  lovely  to see you. It feels like ages. Last time was… Sarah’s hen do, wasn't it? It was! Goodness, that feels a lifetime ago now. Cambridge is a good shout though, neutral ground. And this café is really nice, isn’t it? Much better than that crowded place near the market. Definitely. I remember thinking I’d get elbowed in the face trying to get a scone. So, how  are  you? Really? Last I heard… you were still navigating the world of IVF? Oh, God. That. It’s… well. It didn't work, in the end. Not after the third round, anyway. We decided to stop. The emotional toll was just… too much. Oh, darling. I am  so  sorry. That must have been devastating. I always admired your determination. It was. And then… it just felt like enough was enough. And, ironically, shortly after, I just… embraced the idea of doing it alone. Single parenthood, via donor. Wow. That’s… a big decision. A really big decision. Is everything alright now? Are you… are you expecting? I am! Due in February. It's... surreal, honestly. Completely different from what I imagined, but good. Honestly, good. A lot of paperwork, a lot of appointments, but good. That’s wonderful! Truly. I'm so thrilled for you. It’s amazing what science can do these days, isn't it? Though, honestly, sometimes I worry about how obsessed everyone is with announcing everything on social media. Oh, don’t even  start  me on social media. My niece is glued to TikTok. Just endless videos of people dancing. It's exhausting even watching  her  watch it. I keep saying, “Go outside! Read a book!” But what do I know, right? Exactly! And the pressure! Everyone presenting this perfect, curated version of their lives. It’s… damaging, I think. I’ve actually been trying to limit my time on it lately. Joined a yoga class instead. Yoga! That’s brilliant. I've been meaning to try that. I get so stressed with work. Social work is… relentless. So much heartbreak. Tell me about it. Teaching has its moments, but it’s nothing like dealing with the things you deal with every day. Speaking of stressful, I’ve actually been using my weekends to write. Write? What are you writing? A novel? Kind of! It’s… well, it started as a memoir, about leaving my marriage and deciding to completely change my life.

Honestly, the kids are driving me round the bend with the subjunctive these days. They just… don’t  get  it. It’s like trying to explain colour to someone who’s only ever seen grey. Ah, language teaching. A noble profession, but a frustrating one, I imagine. Used to be the same with grammar in my day, though it was prepositions giving  me  the grey hairs. Still, simpler times, eh? No internet distraction. Simpler, maybe. Though I’m not sure ‘better’ is the word. They’re so glued to their phones, half of them are learning slang from TikTok that I don’t even recognise. It's a whole other language! How  are  your grandkids, by the way? Last I heard, Emily was off to university? She is! Started in September. Doing History, can you believe it? Says she wants to be an archaeologist. Always had her head in a book, that one. Little Thomas is keeping me busy though. He’s just discovered football, naturally. My garden is currently resembling a warzone. Oh, lovely! History is a good choice, though. A proper subject. My brother’s son wanted to do ‘Influencer Marketing’. Influencer Marketing! I nearly choked on my tea. Goodness me. The world’s gone mad, hasn’t it? Still, at least it’s providing employment for someone. Speaking of mad things… did you hear about old Mr. Henderson’s shed being broken into last week? No! Really? Poor man. What did they take? He’s got a lovely garden, always pottering about. Apparently, just his tools. Nothing valuable, but the principle of it. It’s getting worse around here, you know? Little bits of vandalism, car break-ins… it's unsettling. Never used to be like this. It is, isn’t it? I read something about police numbers being cut again. Feels like they’re just… reacting, not preventing. It's worrying. I've started locking the back gate now, even during the day. Sensible. You can't be too careful. Makes you feel like a prisoner in your own home though, doesn't it? Anyway, enough doom and gloom. How’s your health been? You were looking a bit peaky last time I saw you. Oh, it’s just this perpetual tiredness, you know? Working full-time and trying to keep on top of everything. My doctor says it’s stress. Easier said than done, cutting down on stress, isn’t it?

Right, so who’s bringing what for the takeaway tonight? I’m happy to grab some poppadoms and chutney if no one's got it covered. Ooh, good shout with the chutney, Liam. I can do the naan bread, easy peasy. And maybe some onion bhajis? I’ll sort the dips, raita and mango chutney covered. I’m heading to the shops after this anyway. Anyone fancy anything specific from there? Mango chutney already? Excellent. I can do drinks then – beers, soft drinks, the works. Though, if anyone’s wanting anything fancy like that ginger beer stuff Anya likes… Nah, I’m good with a standard lager, cheers Ben. Anya’s still stuck at that conference in London, right? Yeah, she texted earlier. Said the keynote speaker was… well, let’s just say ‘enthusiastic’ about medieval Icelandic sagas. Apparently, he went on for a good hour about the symbolism of cod in them. Cod symbolism? Seriously? That sounds… riveting. I had a lecturer like that once, obsessed with the architectural significance of Victorian lamp posts. Sounds like a joy. Speaking of joy, anyone seen that new Wes Anderson film? Heard it’s visually stunning but a bit… quirky, even for him. I’ve been meaning to, but I’ve been stuck on a bit of a retro kick. Been listening to The Smiths all week. Makes me feel about 16 again, miserable and angst-ridden. Ah, The Smiths. Classic. I've been obsessed with Khruangbin lately. It’s instrumental, really chilled, perfect for concentrating. Good for work, good for… lying on the sofa, basically. I’m more of a film score kinda guy, myself. Hans Zimmer is a genius. Listening to the  Interstellar  soundtrack right now, actually. Gets you thinking about…well, everything. Zimmer  is  brilliant. He could make a washing machine sound epic. You guys ever go to those cinema-with-a-meal deals? Saw a bloke bringing a full roast dinner into the Odeon last week. A  full  roast? Bless him. That’s dedication. Or just madness. Probably both. That’s amazing! It’s a new level of cinema snacking. I just usually smuggle in some Maltesers. Low risk, high reward. I tried to bring in a home-made lasagne once. Got stopped at the door. Apparently, “outside food” is a no-no. Can you believe it? They’re clamping down on the lasagne front, are they? Times are tough.

Honestly, this Cambridge traffic is ridiculous. Took me nearly an hour to get from the A14 to here. Tell me about it! I thought I’d left enough time, but I’m already stressing about being late to pick up Lily from her camp. Which camp is she at this week? The sports one? No, the art one. She’s obsessed with painting at the moment, covering everything in glitter and… well, everything. The house is a disaster zone. Haha, sounds about right. My little cousin went to a Lego camp last summer. My sister was finding bricks in the vacuum cleaner for weeks. Speaking of finding things in unexpected places, I nearly lost my gym bag in the boot of my car last week. It was wedged behind the spare tyre. You finally joined a gym then? Good for you! I keep meaning to, but the thought of all the grunting and lycra… It’s not  that  bad. It’s just… motivating myself to go is the hard part. I signed up for classes though, that helps. Boxing, actually. Boxing? Wow, that’s a change from spreadsheets and engineering diagrams! Yeah, well, needed something to release some of this Cambridge traffic frustration. It’s good, genuinely. Though I’m pretty sure I’m perpetually bruised. I’ve been trying to get back into running. It's just…the weather’s been so unpredictable. One minute it's sunshine, the next it's torrential rain. Seriously! I was thinking of going for a run this morning, but then it started hailing. Hail in July! It’s mad. It is, isn’t it? We were saying at work that it feels more like October than summer. Still, makes a change from last year’s heatwave, I suppose. Remember how everyone was complaining then? Oh god, yes. Couldn't sleep, couldn't concentrate… it was awful. At least this is…tolerable. Although, I could really do with a holiday. Somewhere hot. You and me both. I was looking at flights to Greece earlier. Nothing too crazy, just a week of sun and sea. Ooh, Greece sounds lovely. We went to Crete a few years ago, it was amazing. Honestly, the food alone was worth the trip. I've been trying to convince Ben we need to go somewhere. He's dead set on Scotland, though. Says he wants to “embrace the rugged landscape”.

Honestly, that was a dodgy call. Dodgy, man. What? Oh, the offside? Yeah, a bit tight. Though, to be fair, he  was  leaning. Leaning doesn't make it not offside! It's millimeters, love. Millimeters! They've ruined it, VAR has completely ruined the flow. Come on, it adds to the drama. You know you love a bit of drama. Though I do agree, they spend far too long looking at replay lines. Feels like half the game is spent squinting at a screen. It’s not ‘drama’, it’s frustrating! I just want to watch a football match, not a forensic investigation. Speaking of frustrating, have you seen anything good on film lately? I'm desperate for something to watch over Easter. Oh, I finally got around to watching ‘Everything Everywhere All at Once’ last week. Oh aye, I’ve heard good things! Mental, isn’t it? All the timelines and stuff. Absolutely bonkers, but brilliant. Michelle Yeoh is incredible. Bit of a commitment though, it’s a long one. Speaking of Easter, are your mam and dad coming down? Aye, they are. Arriving Friday, leaving Monday. They’re bringing the usual Easter eggs, and my dad’s already threatening to ‘help’ with the garden. Oh dear. The garden’s seen better days, hasn’t it? Maybe having a professional do it next year would be a good shout. Save everyone a lot of stress. And potential back pain. You're probably right. It's just…expensive. Plus, my Dad genuinely  likes  pottering about. It’s his ‘thing’. Though he does have a tendency to over-enthusiastically prune things into oblivion. Sounds about right. Right, look at that! Good tackle. Finally, some proper football. About time. Though, honestly, they're all just running about like headless chickens. No finesse, no artistry. It's just brute force these days. Remember when Bergkamp used to play?  That  was football. I’m too young to properly remember Bergkamp, you’re showing your age! Though, I've seen the highlights. He was class, no denying that. What are you planning for Easter besides dodging gardening duties? Probably just chill, loads of chocolate, maybe a walk if the weather plays ball. We could go punting if it’s nice. You fancy that? Punting sounds good. And essential chocolate consumption is definitely a priority. It wouldn’t  be  Easter without it. Couldn’t agree more. Honestly, the ref needs glasses.

Ah, look at this one. Young Master Leo, barely able to walk, covered head to toe in chocolate. Must have been… what, three years old? Wow! He looks… intense. Like a tiny, chocolate-covered warrior. Intense is a good word for it. He hadn’t quite mastered the concept of ‘sharing’ back then. Remember the birthday party, Margaret? The cake incident? Ach, how could I forget? Poor wee Sophie was devastated. Leo decided her entire slice was rightfully his. A greedy little monkey, he was. But a lovely one. He’s grown into a lovely one, hasn’t he? It's hard to believe he’s nearly sixteen now. This photo book is a treasure. It reminds me of all the silly things, the little moments you forget. He hasn’t changed  that  much, really. Still has that mischievous glint in his eye. Seen some of his TikToks, pretty funny stuff. TikToks? Oh dear. I don’t understand any of this new technology. Is that the one with all the dancing? It’s a bit more than dancing, love. But he’s a good lad. Honestly, I'm very proud. He’s doing well in school, too. Did you hear he's trying out for the cross-country team? Cross-country? That's a good, healthy thing. Reminds me of the London Marathon. I watched it every year for decades when I lived in London. The atmosphere was electric. Oh, yes! I remember you telling stories about volunteering at the water stations. Standing there cheering everyone on. You were always so enthusiastic. Well, someone had to keep their spirits up! It's a gruelling race, that. Though nothing like… well, nothing like a proper hike in Iceland. Have you seen the pictures from your trip, Sean? I showed them to Leo actually. He was fascinated by the glaciers. Said it looked like another planet. We are hoping to go back soon. Iceland looks awesome. You said it was freezing though? It was crisp, let's say. But the scenery more than makes up for it. The Northern Lights, the waterfalls… incredible. Much more exciting than being cooped up watching films. Though we did go to the cinema last week, didn’t we, Eleanor? We did. Saw that new superhero one. It was… loud. A bit much for me, to be honest. I preferred it when we went to the funfair a couple of weeks ago.

Honestly, Mum, that crumble was incredible. Seriously, you’ve not lost your touch. It tasted exactly like the ones you used to make when I was little. Oh, it's just a simple recipe, dear. Apples, a bit of butter, flour, sugar… nothing fancy. Though, finding good cooking apples these days is a challenge. They just don’t  taste  like they used to. They don't. Everything tastes… engineered, doesn’t it? Like it’s been bred for appearance rather than flavour. Remember those Cox’s Orange Pippins you used to grow in the garden, Mum? They were the best. Oh, yes! Beautiful apples. We used to have a glut, didn’t we? We’d be giving them away to all the neighbours. Old Mr. Henderson next door lived for those apples. Used to say they cured his rheumatism! I remember him! Always with a Werther’s Original stuck to his cardigan. He used to call me “Little Blossom”. Honestly, the things I forgot until you start talking, Mum. It  is  a small world, isn't it? I was talking to Sarah at work yesterday, and her son’s just started at the same primary school as Ben. Apparently, they’ve been having a massive row over who gets to be ‘it’ in tag. Little dramas! Oh, the politics of the playground! It never changes. I remember being utterly devastated if I was ‘it’ first. It felt like an eternal punishment. What games did you play, Mum? Was tag popular back then? Oh, we played everything! Hopscotch, skipping ropes… we used to make up games with pebbles. And marbles! Hours and hours spent with marbles. We’d spend our pocket money on ‘aggies’ – those glass marbles – trying to win each other’s best ones. I remember marbles! I was terrible at them. Always losing mine. I was better at building things. I had a massive box of Lego. Remember Lego, Kath? You always built elaborate castles. I did! Hours I spent. I was obsessed. It’s funny, isn’t it, what sticks with you? Speaking of obsession, I’ve completely fallen down a rabbit hole with eBooks. I finally got a Kindle, and I’m reading two books at once. It’s awful and wonderful. eBooks? What are those? Is that one of those things with a glowing screen? I much prefer a proper book. The smell of the paper, the feel of it in your hands… It's different, Mum.

Right then, lovely bit of cheddar this, isn't it? Not like that plastic stuff you get nowadays. Proper matured. Mm, very nice. Though I do favour a Red Leicester, personally. A bit of sweetness to it. You wouldn't catch me with a bit of Edam though. Always a bit…bland, don’t you think? Bland’s a good word for it, Eileen. Like drinking water with a hint of cheese. Remember old Mrs. Higgins used to swear by Edam? Said it agreed with her tummy. Oh, bless her. She did have a delicate constitution, didn’t she? Always complaining about a draft. Even in July! I swear she thought the sun was trying to give her a cold. She was a dear, though. Always a kind word. She was. Used to bring us a pot of her plum jam every year. A bit tart, mind you. Always needed a good dollop of cream with it. But you couldn’t refuse, could you? Of course not. It was the thought that counted. Though I always felt a bit guilty, secretly adding the cream. She’d have had my hide if she knew! Still, a good bit of jam is a good bit of jam. Have you seen young Timothy next door lately? He’s grown another foot, I swear. Can’t say I have. Haven't been out much this week. Knees are playing up again. Damp weather, I reckon. It'll be raining cats and dogs before you know it. Oh, dear. You should get those knee pads I saw advertised on the telly. The ones the footballers wear, but for everyday use. Apparently, they’re marvellous. Knee pads? Me? I’d look a right fool, wouldn’t I? Walking around like RoboCop. No, thank you very much. A bit of liniment will have to do. And avoiding the garden, mostly. Suit yourself. Though you do miss out on the roses. They're coming on beautifully this year. That new variety I got… the ‘Peace’ one… it’s just spectacular. Roses are all well and good, but give me a nice vegetable patch any day. Something you can  eat  at the end of it. That's proper satisfaction. Remember your dad's tomatoes? Best you ever tasted. Oh, Harold's tomatoes  were  good. He used to fuss over them something dreadful. Spent more time talking to them than he did to me sometimes, I swear!

Honestly, this latte is  saving  my life. Week six of Year Two is hitting different, you know? Little Timmy decided to paint himself with glitter glue today. Glitter. Glue. Everywhere. Oh, bless him. Sounds… festive. I had a similar situation with Leo and the Play-Doh. Luckily, it wasn't glitter, just a vaguely alarming shade of purple stuck in his hair. How’s your mum doing, by the way? I haven’t spoken to her in ages. She’s well, thanks. Still obsessed with cross-stitch. Last time I spoke to her she was going on about a new pattern involving badgers. Badgers! Apparently, it’s very intricate. She was also subtly enquiring about when I’m going to give her grandchildren. The usual. Oh, the badger obsession sounds… very Mum. Mine’s currently convinced she can renovate an entire Victorian house single-handedly. She found a “bargain” on Rightmove. It needs, like,  everything  done. Oh god, that's ambitious. My dad tried a similar thing. He ended up with a shed that leaned at a forty-five-degree angle and a very strained relationship with a bricklayer. Speaking of bargains, anyone got any gift ideas for Ben’s birthday? I'm completely stumped. He says he doesn’t  want  anything. Ugh, the worst! Men are so difficult. What about an experience? Like, that axe-throwing place we talked about? Or maybe a brewery tour? He loves a good craft beer. Ooh, brewery tour is good! Or… and hear me out… a language course? He’s always saying he wants to learn Italian. Imagine him trying to order a cappuccino in fluent Italian! That  would  be amazing. Although, knowing Ben, he'd probably end up accidentally ordering a live octopus. He’s got that effect on people, apparently. Remember that time he tried to explain cricket to a group of Americans and just… confused everyone into silence? Oh my god, YES! They were just staring at him, completely baffled. He was using all these terms like silly mid-on and leg before wicket… it was glorious. He’s hopeless. He genuinely thinks everyone understands cricket. It's adorable. How’s work, actually? Still battling with the endless copy edits? It's relentless. This week it's all about organic dog biscuits. Apparently, there’s a huge market for artisanal treats for pampered pooches. Honestly, the lengths people go to for their pets.

Right, so I was chatting to Old Man Hemmings over the fence this morning, you know, the one who’s always complaining about the bins? Oh, God, yeah. What was he on about  this  time? Honestly, that man could find fault with sunshine. Apparently, young Jamie next door reversed his mum’s car a bit too enthusiastically and nudged his rose bush. A  single  rose bush. He was making it sound like a national tragedy. Sounds about right for around here. It’s always something with him. Though, a rose bush…bit dramatic, innit? Dad, can we talk about Harry Potter later? I’m right at the good bit. In a minute, lad. It’s just…it's the constant negativity, you know? I try to be friendly, but it drains you. Reminds me a bit of some of the students, always looking for something to dissect and complain about. Well, you’re a lecturer, you’re used to complaints! Though, I get my fair share at the school. Little terrors, some of them. But at least they're usually about something legitimate, like the dinner lady giving them too much gravy. Speaking of school, I had a right nightmare with a customer at reception today. Kept going on about how the council is letting the area go to rack and ruin. Said it’s attracting…well, let’s just say people with bad intentions. Oh, don’t even start me on that. I saw something on the news last night. Horrific stuff, that ISIS business. It makes you feel helpless, doesn’t it? And then you worry about bringing that closer to home, even if it's just through scaremongering. It’s frightening. My sister’s husband’s cousin, bless him, he’s out in Iraq with the army. I try not to ask too many questions, but it’s always at the back of your mind. Is ISIS like Voldemort? Really evil? That’s…a complicated question, son. Let’s just say they're people who do terrible things, and try to scare other people. Much,  much  worse than anything Voldemort did. Honestly, sometimes I just want to escape all of it. That’s why I love reading. Getting lost in a good story. I've been rereading 'Pride and Prejudice' actually. So relaxing. Austen is a good shout. I’m more of a thriller person myself. Something to take my mind off cleaning toilets and dealing with sticky fingerprints!

Honestly, the thought of all the paperwork for Nepal is giving me a headache already. Visas, vaccinations… it’s not like popping to France anymore, is it? No, it's a whole operation. I remember when we went to Thailand, you needed a yellow fever certificate if you’d even  looked  at Africa. It was ridiculous. Still, Nepal… magnificent. I’ve always wanted to trek there. Are you thinking of the Everest region? Oh, Everest is a bit… ambitious for me, I think. More the foothills, gentle hiking. Though Geoffrey keeps saying he wants to ‘conquer’ something. Honestly, at our age! Geoffrey! He barely conquers the garden these days. Speaking of conquering, did you see that bike race went right through the village yesterday? The Tour of Britain? Utter chaos, but quite a spectacle. I did! Absolutely rammed. Old Mrs. Higgins nearly got taken out by a cyclist trying to get a good view. She was waving a Union Jack and everything. My daughter, Sarah, she’s training for an Iron Man. Can you imagine? Swimming, cycling, then a marathon! She’s incredibly dedicated. She was out on her bike all morning, probably training for it. It’s inspiring, really. Good for her! Though, all that lycra... I don’t think I could manage it. It's a far cry from my cycling days when I was a girl, just a sensible skirt and sensible shoes. We used to cycle all the way to Bristol, you know, for a treat. Sensible skirts! That's the spirit. Speaking of treats, I popped into the Village Shop yesterday. They’ve finally got decent sausages. Not those watery things they used to sell. Oh, good. The Village Shop is a lifeline, isn’t it? Though, I still prefer the Farm Shop for fruit and veg. Everything’s so much fresher. And they do a fabulous gluten-free bread. Gluten-free, there’s always someone needing gluten-free these days. Though, honestly, when I was a teacher, dealing with allergies was a nightmare. One little boy couldn’t even  look  at peanuts. It’s all changed with the free school meals now, hasn't it? It has. Apparently, it's all very strict about what constitutes a packed lunch now, too. No sweets, no chocolate biscuits. My colleague's daughter is furious, she's a bit of a lunchbox queen. It's a good thing, really, isn’t it?

Honestly, this week at work has been  mental . You wouldn’t believe the requests I’ve had. Like, someone wanted a falconry display…  inside  the conference hall. No way! A falconry display? Seriously? Cambridge isn’t exactly lacking in green space, is it? That’s… ambitious. Did you manage to politely explain why that wasn't feasible? Politeness went out the window after the third phone call demanding I source ethically sourced, miniature Shetland ponies for a themed team-building exercise. Miniature! Shetland! Ponies! I just… I said it wasn’t possible due to health and safety. Oof. Sounds stressful. My job's thankfully a bit more grounded, but the deadlines are brutal at the moment. We’re launching the new production line next month and everything feels a bit last minute. Tell me about it. I’m drowning in admin at the moment. Old Mr. Henderson decided he needs  everything  in triplicate, handwritten, and delivered to his office by 3pm. Every. Single. Day. Oh my god, that sounds like a nightmare. Is he… okay? Seriously. Is he a bit of a dinosaur? A dinosaur is being generous. He’s actively resisting all attempts at digitalising anything. He thinks email is ‘a fad’. Some people. It’s good to vent though, isn’t it? It's just... It feels like everyone expects you to just  manage , you know? Like, manage the impossible, manage the ridiculous, and still manage to smile. Exactly! And then when things inevitably go wrong, it’s  always  your fault. I had a delegate complain the coffee wasn’t hot enough. Apparently, that ruined their entire conference experience. Oh, dear god. The coffee! It's always the coffee. Remember Sarah at uni? She had a meltdown because the uni canteen ran out of oat milk. Oh, Sarah! She was… a lot. I miss those days though, don’t you? Less responsibility, more questionable life choices. Definitely. Though, even then, we managed to create chaos. Remember the time we tried to ‘borrow’ those traffic cones for a themed party? Oh, don’t remind me! We almost got arrested! And the party was… underwhelming to say the least. It was truly awful. But fun! We need to do something fun soon, properly. Not just complaining about work over tea . Are you both free next Saturday? There’s that new jazz club opened in town, I was thinking we could check it out?

Honestly, the council are unbelievable. Demolishing the library? It’s just… short-sighted. Tell me about it. I saw the plans online - luxury flats, naturally. They’ve got no interest in community spaces, do they? Just maximising profit. Exactly! And they call it ‘regeneration’. It's destroying everything that  makes  Plumstead, Plumstead. I'm properly fuming. I was thinking we should start a petition. A petition is a good shout. We could get it going online, change.org or something? Easy enough for people to sign. I’d definitely sign it. I was thinking that. And we should get the local paper involved, see if they’ll run a story. It feels like nobody’s listening otherwise. Good plan. Though, knowing the  Plumstead Penny Pincher , they’ll probably just run a tiny piece buried on page seven. Still, it’s better than nothing. How’s the transcription work going, by the way? Still loads of legal stuff? Ugh, yes. Endless depositions about car accidents and neighbour disputes. It’s soul-destroying, honestly. I’m starting to feel like I know more about fender benders than anyone should. It’s good money, though. And flexible, which is essential with everything else going on. That's the main thing, isn’t it? Flexibility. My shifts are a nightmare at the moment. They've put me on late turns three times this week. It completely messes with my sleep. Oh, that's rubbish! You need your sleep. Are you at least getting extra for working lates? A measly twenty quid a shift. It’s not worth the exhaustion. And then Brenda, you know Brenda from accounts, keeps complaining about how  she’s  the one doing all the work while I’m at home ‘having a lie-in’. Brenda sounds… delightful. Honestly, people. Speaking of brains and exhaustion, I was reading about these brain training apps. Apparently, they can help stave off cognitive decline. Oh yeah? I’ve seen ads for those. Lumosity, isn't it? Do they actually work? Or are they just another way to part people from their money? That's what I'm wondering. Apparently, you have to do it consistently for it to have any effect. I was trying to come up with a mnemonic to remember to do it every day. Something suitably embarrassing. Ooh, good idea. What did you come up with? Okay, don't laugh. “Lazy Lions Don’t Eat Pickles.”

Right, well, that was a lovely bit of quiche, wasn’t it? Marjorie, you really do make a good quiche. Aye, it were good. Though a bit rich for me, these days. Gets right to me, it does. Still, can’t complain, can you? Oh, don't be silly, George. A little richness never hurt anyone. You had a good portion, didn’t you? More than either of us, actually. Had to keep me strength up! Been dealing with them Jehovah’s Witnesses again this morning. They’re persistent, I’ll give ‘em that. Oh, not again? They’ve been round here a couple of times themselves. Always polite enough, but… persistent is the word, yes. What did you tell ‘em this time, George? Told ‘em what I tell ‘em every time. “Not interested, thank you very much.” Though this young lad, he kept going on about the end of the world. Said it’s just around the corner. Oh, they always say that, don't they? Been saying that for decades. Bit of a sales tactic, I reckon. Gets people worried. Speaking of worried, did young Daniel ever sort out that parking ticket he got at Cromer? I believe so. He mentioned it at the weekend. Apparently, it wasn't too bad, a reduced rate because he’d parked on a yellow line briefly. He was trying to drop the children off quickly, you see. Dreadful parking situation down there, isn't it? Especially in the summer. You try finding a spot near the pier! It’s a nightmare. Used to take us half an hour just to drive around and around. Back in the day, of course. It's always been bad. Though it’s even worse now with all the holiday lets. Every house is a car, it feels like. Makes a person not want to bother, honestly. Reminds me, did you two see old Mrs. Higgins down at the village fete last week? She was trying to win that coconut shy. Swung so hard, nearly took out poor Mr. Peterson! Oh, I did see that! Nearly sent him flying. Mrs. Higgins is a character, she is. Always stirring something up. She’s got spirit, that's for sure. Though I'm still trying to figure out why she's so fiercely opposed to the new bins the council's putting in. Says they're an eyesore. She's probably just got a lot of stuff she needs to…store, shall we say?

Honestly, Mum, the logs are just… pathetic. Honestly, you’d think for the price they charge now, they’d be decent seasoned wood. It’s all damp and smoky, just awful for the burner. You’d think so, wouldn’t you? Though I suppose demand is up. Everyone’s at it with the log burners these days, trying to save on the heating bill. Saving on the heating bill. A quaint notion. Though I do remember a time when a good fire was the only heat you  had . Not this central heating nonsense. Do you recall old Mr. Henderson, next door in Edinburgh? He'd boast about never putting the heating on, even in January. Just layer upon layer of woollens. Henderson, yes. Stubborn man. His wife, poor soul, was permanently chilled. Though he did have a lovely cat. A ginger tom, very independent. Much like himself. Speaking of animals, have you seen Mrs. Higgins’ new poodle? It’s… a creature. All fluff and no substance. And she dresses it in little outfits! Oh dear. Sounds about right for Mrs. Higgins. She’s always been a bit… eccentric. Did you hear about that new Italian restaurant opening on the High Street? Apparently, it’s rather good. Is it? We tried that dreadful tapas place last week. Overpriced and underwhelming. The patatas bravas were… an insult to potatoes. The standards these days. It’s all style over substance. Much like the state of education, to be frank. These academy schools… utterly dreadful. It's all about the budget, isn't it? Cutting corners everywhere. I was transcribing some interviews the other day about outsourcing customer service to India. Apparently, it's saving companies a fortune, but the quality... well, it's not great. It’s the same everywhere, isn’t it? Chasing the cheapest option. I had a meeting today about streamlining processes at work. Which basically means doing more with less. It’s exhausting. Exhausting for you, perhaps. Imagine what it’s like being a headmistress dealing with all of  that . The paperwork alone! Though I always said a good mashed potato could solve most problems. Your mashed potato  was  legendary, my dear. Smooth as silk. No lumps whatsoever. Unlike some I’ve encountered. Remember young Timothy, at the school fête? Insisted on adding gravy to his mashed potato  and  custard. Oh, don't even get me started on school fetes!

Honestly, the council tax this year… it’s gone up again. Seems they think we’re all suddenly rolling in it. Tell me about it, Arthur. Mine’s crept up too. Not as much as yours, I expect, living in that nice little bungalow. More room means more rateable value, they say. It's daylight robbery, the lot of it. They promise improvements, better services, but what do we actually get? More potholes and bin collections that seem to miss a week more often than not. Exactly, Margaret! And they wonder why people get so fed up with politics. Speaking of which, did you see that interview with that chap from the Labour party? Sounded like he hadn't a clue about the real world. Oh, don't get me started on politics. They're all the same, aren't they? Promises promises… I remember when they were talking about building more affordable houses. Still waiting. Affordable for who, Norman? Certainly not for young people starting out these days. My granddaughter, Sarah, she’s been looking for a place in Norwich. The prices are scandalous. It's the same everywhere, apparently. My nephew in Bristol is having the same trouble. He says it’s all down to investors buying up properties and leaving them empty. That’s right. Driving up the prices for everyone else. I was reading in the paper about a bloke who bought a place just to rent it out as an Airbnb. Absolute madness. Honestly. It used to be you bought a house to  live  in, not to make a quick buck. I remember when Old Man Hemmings sold up and moved to Spain. Said he couldn't stand the changes to the village anymore. Hemmings was a good sort. Used to help me with the garden when my back was playing up. Still, Spain… that sounds nice. I did a bit of travelling in my younger days, mostly for work, but saw some lovely remote places. Up in Scotland, particularly. Proper wilderness. Remote places, eh? I’m not one for all that. Give me a nice cup of tea and the telly any day. Speaking of which, have you managed to get one of those smart TVs, Arthur? I have, Norman. My daughter set it up for me. It's… complicated. All these streaming services and apps. Makes my head spin. I mostly just watch the news and the gardening programmes.

Right, so the lad from Dell was absolutely useless, wasn’t he? Said the warranty was up. Up! It’s barely a year old. Mmmhmm. Coulda just fixed it, though, couldn't he? Sounds like a simple graphics card thing. Honestly, tech support these days… they read from a script. It's infuriating. Didn't  you  used to fix computers for a living, darling? You could probably do it blindfolded. I could, alright. But time, you see? Time's the killer. Between work and… …keeping this one from dismantling the dining room, there’s not much left. Tower! Higher! Oh, for goodness sake, Leo. No throwing the vegetables. Honestly, you're a miniature hurricane. He's just excited, Mum. It’s dinner. And Dad’s complaining about computers again. I’m not complaining, I’m stating a fact. It's a perfectly good machine! And it's a pain not having it for streaming the rugby on Saturday. Speaking of Saturday, has anyone finalised plans? Are we still going to Ciaran’s for the match, or are we having people here? Ciaran's is good. More space for… you know… enthusiastic shouts when Ireland scores. Agreed. Less chance of breaking anything  here . Though, I'm making the fajitas, so someone needs to run to the shops for extra sauce. We always run out. That medium one just doesn't cut it. I can go after Leo’s bath. Don’t want him covered in sauce and running wild. He'd look like a tiny, spicy monster. Monster! Roar! A very accurate description. And while you're at the shops, could you see if they have those ear-plugs for swimming? I said I'd take young Master Leo to the pool on Sunday, but I'm dreading the water in his ears. Those little ears stick  right  out! He's got cute ears, Dad. He does. But they’re prime targets for water retention. It’s a personal trauma from my own childhood, I tell you. Spent half my life shaking my head like a dog. You did have a talent for waterlogged ears, yes. Alright, sauce, ear-plugs, and then I’ll try to wrestle Leo into the bath. What about after the rugby on Saturday? Fancy a quiet night in, or shall we brave the town? Town, definitely. Haven’t been out in ages. Maybe catch a film? Rest my feet after a hard-fought afternoon cheering on the boys.

Right, pizza’s almost ready! Who’s excited? Me! Pizza! With pineapple? No pineapple! Pineapple doesn’t  belong  on pizza! It’s…it's wrong! We’ll have a bit with and a bit without, okay? Everyone gets a happy pizza. Now, while it’s cooking, let's talk about something else. I was trying to explain to Grandma on the phone how you two communicate with each other... it’s a secret language, isn’t it? It’s not a secret! It’s just… faster. Yeah! And grown-ups don't  get  it. It's all about faces. Faces? Like, pulling funny faces? And wiggles! And knowing what the other one is thinking before they say it! Wow, that  is  impressive. Almost telepathic. Speaking of things people don’t believe in…did anyone want to talk about the Loch Ness Monster? Nessie IS real! I saw a picture! Oh really? What did the picture show? A long neck! And a bumpy back! And it was swimming in the water! My friend Leo says Nessie is just a really long eel. A really long eel, huh? That’s a good theory. Maybe. So, back to pizza. If I have three slices, and you have two, and then I have another one... how many slices do I have? Er… four! Good job! See, maths  is  useful. Especially when it comes to pizza allocation. Now, after pizza, what are we doing? Still thinking about that fairy garden? Yes! We need sparkly things! And tiny houses! And a little pond! With a frog! A pond and a frog it is. Oh, and remember we need to pick out outfits for Auntie Carol’s party on Saturday? Any ideas what you want to wear? I want to wear my princess dress! The sparkly one! I want to be a superhero! With a cape! Sparkly princess and superhero… excellent choices. We’ll have to see if we can find capes. Honestly, sometimes I wish I could just do a handstand whenever things get too complicated. That always seems to clear my head. It's hard! I can almost do a handstand! But I need to practice! You both need cushions! And maybe we can practice  after  the pizza, okay? Speaking of which… it’s ready! Let's eat! If I had five pizzas...and we ate two...how many pizzas would we have left? Three! You’re brilliant!

Honestly, this Peka is incredible. I’ve never tasted lamb so tender. It's completely falling off the bone. Told you! Croatian cooking is something special. It’s all about slow cooking and fresh ingredients. This region, Istria, they call it the ‘Tuscany of Croatia’ for a reason. Everything just  tastes  better here. Can I have another slice of that bread? It’s really good dipped in the sauce. Of course, lad. Help yourself. Though you might want to save some room for dessert, I hear the  fritule  are divine. Little fried dough balls, apparently. Ooh, definitely. I'm already planning the dessert strategy. This wine’s lovely too. What  is  it, Mum? Malvazija. A local white, very dry and crisp. Goes beautifully with the lamb. Better than anything you get in Bolton, eh? Way better. Though I miss chips. A man of simple pleasures. Speaking of places, we should definitely explore Rovinj tomorrow. I read it’s a stunning little town, built on a peninsula. Apparently, the sunsets are something else. Yes! I already looked at pictures. It looks gorgeous. We should get some proper photos, although my phone camera isn't great. Maybe we can convince someone to bring a proper camera. Your Dad has his fancy one, hasn’t he? Always taking pictures of everything. Honestly, sometimes it's a bit much. He took a photo of a lizard by the pool today. A really close-up one. It looked kinda scary. Lizards are harmless, son. Actually, they’re rather beneficial, keeping down the insect population. Reminds me of a story… back in Nigeria, we had geckos in the house – tiny things, chirping away all night. Thought they were annoying at first, then found out they were eating all the mosquitoes. Nigeria? Wow. You’ve been everywhere, haven't you? It’s a bit of a jump from Croatia! It is! A long story for another time. Although, no place feels quite as…relaxed as this. It’s nice to get away from everything. Even the news. Remember all that fuss about Ebola a few years back? Crazy times. Don't remind me! I was working in the city then, all the airports were on high alert. Those immigration officers were particularly prickly. Always felt like they were looking for something. Speaking of travelling, where do you want to go next, Dad? You always have a list. Oh, a long list!

Right, well that was a good lunch, wasn’t it? Always a good spread when you lot come round. Though I swear, Margaret, you’re getting better at making that potato salad every time. Oh, shush now, Arthur. Just enjoying myself. Though I did find a slightly better recipe online, used a bit of crème fraîche instead of mayo, makes all the difference. Speaking of online… I had another phone call today. Debt collectors. Honestly, it’s relentless. Keeps being about PPI, something I never even  had . They say it’s a reclaiming thing, but really? At my age? Happens to everyone, doesn’t it, David? They just buy the lists, hoping someone will bite. Just tell them you’ve already dealt with it, or hang up. Don’t give them any information. Exactly! My cousin Bertie, bless him, fell for that a few years back. Gave ‘em his bank details. Nearly lost everything. Had to get his grandson to sort it out with a computer and all that. Still won’t touch one, Bertie. Says they're the devil's work. He’s not wrong, is he? Though I do rely on mine for recipes, and keeping up with the grandchildren. Little Emily sent me a picture of her sunflower today, practically taller than her! Speaking of, I was looking at seed catalogues this morning. Thinking about getting some sweet peas. Good idea, Margaret. Though you'll need to get them in pretty soon. The weather's been so changeable. I saw a programme on the telly last night about a rather spectacular display at Abbey Gardens, Bury St Edmunds. They’ve got a whole section dedicated to climbing sweet peas. Oh, yes, I remember that garden. Wonderful place. Though I’m not a huge fan of all the fuss they make over gardens on TV these days. It’s all so… staged. Give me a bit of wild countryside any day. Now, you two are always on about gardens and flowers! I was watching that documentary on the war last night. Fascinating. Reminded me of old man Hemmings down the road. He used to sing hymns in the church  and  the abbey, he had a voice like an angel, he did. Though couldn't hold a tune when he was having a pint at the pub, mind. Oh, Arthur! You always have a story to tell. Though I prefer a bit of music on the radio, or even a good drama.

Honestly, that was a  day . Three domestic disputes, a shoplifting, and then that lad with the… well, let’s just say a very creative explanation for being caught with a suspiciously large quantity of fireworks. Och, aye, they're always a handful, aren’t they? You get used to it, eventually. Though I don't think I  ever  get used to the excuses. Fireworks in February? What was he planning, a personal display for Valentine’s Day? Something like that, apparently. He claimed he was “testing them for safety.” The magistrate didn’t look convinced. It's just… draining, you know? Seeing people’s lives unravel like that. It’s not the grand drama of TV, it's just… sad. Aye, it is. It's the everyday sadness that gets to you. I mostly just show people where to sit, confirm their names, that sort of thing, but even  I  can feel the weight of it all. It's just people making bad choices, or having really rotten luck. Still, keeps things interesting, doesn’t it? Better than sorting socks, as my late husband used to say. Definitely more interesting than socks. I sometimes wonder about the whole system, though. Does it actually  help  anyone, or are we just… processing people? I mean, short sentences, fines they can’t pay… does it really change anything? That's a question for the clever folk, dear. I just keep the peace. But you’ve got a point. Seems to me, a lot of it comes down to money, doesn't it? And a lack of it. If folk had a bit more to go around, maybe they wouldn’t be driven to… well, to shoplifting or whatever else they’re up to. Exactly! And it’s not even about being  rich , just having enough to feel secure. Speaking of money, did you see the price of petrol this morning? Absolutely ridiculous. I’m starting to consider cycling everywhere. Don’t go doing that! Solihull’s hills will have you regretting it before you reach the first one. I take the bus, myself. It’s slow, but it's better than the stress of driving and the cost of everything. You teaching the little ones today? Yep, Year 5. We’re doing French, and it’s… a struggle. They’re fantastic kids, but getting them to grasp the gendered nouns is like banging my head against a brick wall.

Right, so we were talking about what makes people happy, weren’t we? What makes  you  happy, Lily? Um… ponies! And chocolate! And… and when you read me stories! Lovely! Those are all brilliant things. And what about you, Leo? What makes  you  feel happy? Dinosaurs! Roar! And building really tall Lego towers that don’t fall down. Oh, excellent choices. Very important things. It's good to have things you enjoy, isn’t it? Sometimes people think happiness comes from having lots of money… Lots and lots of money? Like a million pounds? Even more than a million! Imagine a huge pile of money. Would that make you happy, do you think? I could buy ALL the dinosaurs! Every single one! Even the really, really big ones. You could, couldn't you? But would having all the dinosaurs  make  you happy, or would it just be… nice to have them? I’d buy a pony! A sparkly pink pony! And a chocolate fountain! A chocolate fountain sounds amazing! But think about it – if you had all that money and no one to share the pony or the chocolate with… would it feel as good? I’d share with you! And Lily! We could have a dinosaur park and a pony riding club! That’s a very kind thought, Leo. See, that’s part of happiness too, sharing things with people you love. It’s lovely to have nice things, but feeling good inside, that’s the most important thing. Like when Grandma gives us big cuddles? Exactly like that! Or when we all pile on the sofa for a movie night. Things that make you  feel  good. Can we make up a rhyme about happiness? Ooh, good idea! Let's try. I’ll start: “Happiness is sunshine bright…” “…and playing games with all my might!” That’s brilliant, Lily! Your turn, Leo. "...and dinosaurs that stomp and fight!" Perfect! See? We don’t need lots of money to make a happy rhyme, do we? We just need each other and a little bit of imagination. Can we have chocolate now? And build a Lego dinosaur? Maybe later. But for now, let’s keep thinking about all the things that make us happy, even  without  a million pounds or a sparkly pink pony. Okay! Happy! Roar! Happy dinosaur! Yes, a very happy dinosaur indeed. Can we read the dinosaur book? Yes please!

Honestly, Mr. Davies is banging on about careers  again . Like we all know exactly what we want to do at sixteen. It’s ridiculous. Tell me about it. He was going on about actuarial science. Actuarial science! Who even  chooses  that? It sounds… depressing. Exactly! It's like, calculating risk for insurance companies. Peak excitement. I swear he just reads articles from the Financial Times and thinks we should all aspire to be… that. He probably thinks it's secure. My dad's always going on about secure jobs. Apparently, being a… a professional dog walker isn’t ‘secure’. Ha! Your dad’s the best. Seriously, though, I was reading about this guy, like, a proper inventor. He patented this self-folding laundry system. A what now? Seriously? Yeah! It's like, you dump your clothes in, and it folds everything automatically. Apparently, he sold the patent for, like, millions. Millions? That’s insane. I’ve got a prototype for a self-filling water bottle. So far, it mostly just leaks. That’s… ambitious. But hey, every inventor has to start somewhere. He probably had a lot of leaky prototypes before he got to self-folding laundry. True. It’s the funding, isn’t it? That’s the killer. I need, like, a miniature pump and a sensor and a… well, a lot of things. Maybe you could pitch it to Mr. Davies? Tell him it’s a ‘disruptive innovation’ and he’ll probably give you the school’s entire budget. Don’t tempt me. Actually, thinking about funding… my uncle's been going on about investing in China. China? Isn’t that… risky? I mean, everything is made there already. What can you even  invest  in? He reckons it's all about the tech companies. Apparently they're massively undervalued, and the middle class is exploding. He’s talking about electric vehicle infrastructure, AI… all that stuff. That sounds… complicated. And a bit scary. I read an article about how they're building entire cities, like, from scratch. It’s like, what happens when a country gets  that  ambitious? Yeah, it's huge. He said it's the biggest economic shift in history. Apparently, everything is shifting east. Like, the whole world's centre of gravity is changing. Wow. That’s… a lot to take in. It makes actuarial science seem pretty trivial, actually. Definitely. I mean, calculating the risk of a washing machine breaking down is hardly world-changing stuff.

Honestly, this soup is  exactly  what I needed. My legs are screaming at me. I thought I was fitter than this, after all those walks last autumn. Tell me about it! I thought I’d be flying down those slopes, channeling my inner Lindsey Vonn. More like stumbling Lindsey Vonn. And David’s knee… poor man. He's being so stoic, but I know it’s hurting. He wouldn’t admit it if it wasn’t practically falling off! He’s just like Dad, always trying to be the strong one. Did you see him trying to subtly stretch it after that black run? It was… not subtle. Ha! I did. Emily was filming it, naturally. She’ll have that on repeat for years. Speaking of Emily, how did her lesson go this morning? She was so nervous. Much better than expected, actually. She started off really wobbly, clinging onto the instructor like a limpet, but by the end she was actually doing controlled turns on the blue slope. She was beaming. Said the instructor, Stefan, was brilliant. Really patient. Oh, that’s lovely to hear. She needs a win, she’s been so stressed with university applications. It’s all anyone talks about at the moment, isn’t it? Pressure, pressure, pressure. Absolutely. And then there's Leo. Still talking about wanting to defer a year and ‘find himself’ backpacking around Southeast Asia. Honestly, I don’t know where he gets it from… not  you  certainly. Definitely not me! Though a year backpacking does sound rather… appealing right now. Without the teenagers, obviously. Listen, about tomorrow… do you fancy trying that new ski school they told us about? The one that does off-piste guiding? Oh, I don’t know. Off-piste sounds a bit… adventurous for me. Especially after today. I’m happy sticking to the marked runs, thank you very much. I was thinking we could. It might be nice to push ourselves a little. David’s definitely out, with his knee, and Emily and Leo are planning on going with their instructor group. It’d just be us. Hmmm. Is it terribly expensive? Because I’m trying to be sensible with the spending this trip. The exchange rate is a killer. Not too bad, I looked into it. It's about £75 each for a half-day. And they provide all the safety equipment. Think of the views!

Honestly, Arthur, you're wobbling something awful. Hold still! I’m trying for a nice even trim, not a Picasso. I  am  holding still! It’s just… thinking about these racket strings, you see. The sheer volume we could potentially deal with. Is ‘fleet’ too grandiose a word, do you think? A ‘fleet’ of rackets needing repair? A fleet? Arthur, you sound like a naval commander. It's badminton rackets, not battleships. And stop fiddling with your ear. You'll end up looking like a pug. Well, it’s about scale, isn't it? If we target all the schools in Bristol, and the clubs… it could be a significant workload. And the stringing itself… I’m still convinced cable ties are a viable short-term solution. Cable ties? Arthur, you’re having a laugh. That’s not  repair , that’s a makeshift bodge. Think of the tension! They’d snap immediately. And potentially take an eye out. But think of the cost difference! Proper stringing is extortionate. Cable ties are pennies. We could undercut everyone. We'd be the budget racket repair kings! And known as the kings of disastrous badminton matches. No, no, we need proper string. Nylon, I suppose. What’s the gauge most people use? 0.65mm? And how much is a spool these days? We need a proper costing sheet. I was having a look online. A decent spool is about thirty quid. But the tricky bit is the threading. It has to be even, consistent tension... have you ever tried it? I watched a YouTube video. Seemed… fiddly. Perhaps we could offer different tiers of service. ‘Basic Cable Tie Emergency’ for five pounds. ‘Professional Nylon Restringing’ for fifteen. Now you’re talking! And we could differentiate based on school level. Primary schools… they’re less fussed about perfect tension. A bit of cable tie reinforcement wouldn't hurt for Reception class rackets. They're mostly just hitting balloons anyway. Arthur! I've nicked your ear! Oh, dear. I am so sorry. Ouch! It’s alright… just a little prickle. Though, actually, while you’re at it… could you just tidy up the sideburns a bit? They're getting a bit unruly. Always wanting something else. Right, sideburns. But this business plan… we need to think about marketing. "Racket Rescue"? "String Things"? "The Badminton Boutique"? Too pretentious? We could even pitch it on Dragons’ Den. Imagine!

Lovely cuppa, Maureen. Always a good brew you make. Oh, thank you, Arthur. Just a bit of Tetley’s, nothing fancy. Though I did get some new biscuits – ginger snaps. Anyone want one? Ooh, yes please! Ginger snaps are the best with tea. So, Dad, how did your painting session go yesterday? Did you manage to get any further with the seascape? Slowly, slowly. It’s… it’s proving tricky, this one. Getting the water right, you see. It looks a bit flat. Like a millpond, not the North Sea crashing about. Water is notoriously difficult, isn’t it? It reflects everything, and seemingly has no solid form. What medium are you working in again, Arthur? Oils. Always oils. Been using them for… oh, sixty years now, at least. I tried acrylics once. Didn't like 'em. Too quick drying. No blending. You could try layering glazes, Dad. Building up the colours slowly. That can give a really nice depth to water. It takes patience, but it can look amazing. I saw a fantastic exhibition at the Sainsbury Centre last month, lots of Turner inspired work… Glazes, you say? Hmm. Sounds… fiddly. I'm more of a slap-it-on-and-hope-for-the-best kind of painter, I confess. He’s always been a bit that way, our Arthur. Never one for a lot of fuss! But he does have a good eye, even if he doesn't give himself credit. Remember that portrait he did of young David when he was a boy? It was lovely. I’ve seen some of his landscapes, they’re really quite atmospheric. Perhaps a different brush might help? A wider, flatter one for the initial washes? Might give it a more expansive feel? I’ve got a whole box full of brushes, you know. Old man Willowby – bless his soul – he sold me a job lot when he was packing up his shop. All sorts of shapes and sizes. I suppose I could rummage around… it’s just… finding the right one. Maybe you could take a photo of the painting and we could look at it together? I could offer some suggestions. Sometimes a fresh pair of eyes is all you need. That’s a good idea. We could look at some reference photos too, of the North Sea. See how professional artists tackle those kinds of scenes. Oh, I don’t know about “professional.”

Honestly, I spent the entire afternoon ‘tidying’ my desk at work, which mostly involved moving piles of paper from one side to the other. Productive, right? Oh, the classic office re-arrangement. Sounds about par for the course. I spent most of my shift today trying to explain to a patient why, no, they couldn’t have a pet badger in the ward. A badger?! Seriously? What on earth… Apparently, it’s his emotional support animal. He’d named it Winston. Honestly, some days I question my life choices. And then I remember the paycheque. Fair enough. Speaking of questionable choices, have you seen Chloe’s Instagram lately? The photos from her weekend away are…a lot. Filtered to within an inch of her life. It's exhausting just  looking  at it. Oh, Chloe. She’s committed to the aesthetic, isn’t she? It’s like she’s auditioning for a reality TV show about influencers. Honestly, the lengths some people go to. It's completely performative. It's genuinely weird. And then she was subtly bragging about this expensive spa treatment she had. Like, we get it, you have money. Must you shove it in everyone’s faces? Some people just thrive on validation, I suppose. It's a sad little cycle. God, I’m starving. Is that pasta I smell? Yep! Carbonara, if you’re interested. I promised myself I’d actually cook something proper this weekend. Although, knowing me, I’ll probably end up ordering a takeaway on Sunday. Tempting… but carbonara wins. You’re a lifesaver. I’ve been surviving on hospital sandwiches all week. They’re somehow simultaneously dry and greasy. It's a culinary paradox. Sounds horrific. Honestly, the English language is just…dying. People are butchering it left, right and centre. I saw someone write “irregardless” the other day.  Irregardless ! Oh, the humanity! It’s a plague, I tell you. A plague of grammatically incorrect sentences. And don't even get me started on the overuse of 'literally'. It's just… inaccurate! Like, literally, everything’s not  literally  everything. Ugh. Right, I’m going to grab a glass of wine. This conversation is stressing me out. Good idea. I'll finish stirring this pasta. And then, maybe, just maybe, we can actually start planning something fun for the weekend,  before  procrastination swallows us whole. Agreement. Fun is good. Though, honestly, cleaning the bathroom is starting to feel like a herculean task.

Honestly, the commute was  brutal  this morning. Accident on the M4, apparently. Took me nearly an hour and a half to get to Reading. An hour and a half? Blimey. You know, sometimes I think about just… chucking it all in. Becoming a shepherd. Less stress, fresher air, and fewer people trying to merge without indicating. A shepherd? You? You’d last five minutes. You’d be trying to install Wi-Fi in the sheep pen. Hey! Don’t underestimate my adaptability. Besides, a shepherd needs to be organized. Project management skills are transferrable, you know. Just adapting them to a woollier clientele. Right. And what about the…  necessities ? You’d be giving up your cigarettes and gin and tonics for a life of… dandelion tea? Okay, that’s a fair point. The vices are a sticking point. Though, imagine the opportunity to grow my own juniper berries. A truly artisanal G&T. You're irredeemable. Seriously though, you need to cut down on those fags. It’s not healthy, and it smells awful. I know, I know. I’m working on it. It's just… stress, isn’t it? And that commute doesn't exactly  reduce  the stress levels. It’s a vicious cycle. It is. But you know, sometimes I think people confuse intelligence with common sense. My boss is incredibly clever, academically brilliant, but utterly lacking in the ability to just… think things through practically. Oh, that’s spot on. I see it all the time at work. People with all the qualifications in the world, but can’t troubleshoot a simple network issue without needing a flowchart. Exactly!
