He was asking me this morning how to forward an email on his phone.  Forward  an email! It’s basic. It’s the same with cultural understanding, isn't it? You can read all the books you like about different societies, about feminism, about equality… but until you actually  experience  those things, truly listen to someone else’s perspective… it’s just theoretical knowledge. You're right. I was reading something the other day about how expectations of women are so different in various parts of the world. It’s easy to be a feminist in a relatively privileged environment like ours, where we can openly discuss these things. But what about women who don't have that freedom? Precisely. It's easy to sit here and judge, but it's far more valuable to try and  understand .

Right, so, who wants to tell Grandma all about the farm? Leo, did you have a favourite part? The tractors! Big tractors! And I drove one! Well, pretended to. I liked the baby goats! They were SO fluffy and they ate out of my hand! They did, didn’t they? You were very brave letting them nibble your fingers. Did you wash your hands extra well afterwards? Yes! Lots and lots of soap! I wanted a piglet. A tiny pink one. But Daddy said we couldn’t bring one home. Well, a piglet might make a bit of a mess of the house, wouldn’t it? And who would look after it? I would! I'd feed it and everything! That's very kind of you to offer. Right, before we get carried away with farm animals, how was school today, you two? Lily, you first. It was… okay. Maisie kept copying my drawing of a unicorn. Oh dear. Did you tell your teacher? Yes. Miss Davies said Maisie just admires your unicorns. But it’s  my  unicorn! I understand why that would be frustrating. It's good you told Miss Davies, though. Now, Leo, how about you? Any trouble today? Well… I… I accidentally threw a building block at Thomas. Oh, Leo. What happened? He took my blue one! The really good blue one for the castle! And I got cross and… and it just sort of flew. Did it hurt Thomas? Not really. He just cried for a bit. Miss Jones gave me ‘time out’. Okay. Well, throwing things isn’t a good idea, even when you’re cross. It can hurt people, even if it’s not meant to. You need to use your words, remember? Tell Thomas you were cross that he took your block. I know, I know. It's hard. It is hard. But practice makes perfect. Now, speaking of practice, I was thinking we could have a movie night later? I rented that new animal DVD you both wanted. Ooh, the one with the penguins?! The very same. Can we have popcorn? With extra butter? We can definitely have popcorn. But only a  reasonable  amount of butter, okay? We don't want greasy fingers all over the sofa. Deal! Yeah, deal! Penguins and popcorn! Best night ever! Sounds like a plan. Now, who’s for a biscuit? Speaker_2 & Me! Alright then, let’s go find the biscuit tin.

Right, so milk first, or tea first? Honestly, it’s a hill I’m willing to die on – tea first, always. Prevents cracking, you see. You and your tea rituals, Elara. Milk first is perfectly acceptable. Besides, you’re the one with the postgraduate degree, shouldn't you be able to handle a potentially cracked mug? It’s not about handling it, Ben! It’s about  preventing  it! It’s preventative maintenance. Like, I've been perfecting my knitting tension, right? It’s all about being proactive, avoiding future problems. This jumper for my niece needs to be flawless. Speaking of flawless…did you see that interview with Timothée Chalamet? He was trying to explain modern art and just…completely floundered. It was glorious. Oh god, no. I try to avoid the celebrity trainwreck news cycles. Makes me feel vaguely depressed about the state of the world. Though, I did see a picture of Florence Pugh at the Olympics opening ceremony. Stunning dress. Really pulled off the British aesthetic. She did, didn't she? Bit much patriotism for my liking, all that flag waving, but she looked fantastic. Are they showing much knitting at the Olympics, do you think? A new sport, maybe? Extreme needlework? Don't be ridiculous. Although, competitive cable knitting  would  be a spectacle. Imagine the tension! No, they’re mostly doing the usual sports. Have you seen any of the gymnastics? It's terrifying and amazing all at once. A little bit. I’ve been rather glued to trying to finish this chapter on post-structuralism. It’s drier than a biscuit left out in the Sahara. Honestly, sometimes I wish I'd gone into something practical, like…knitting. Practical? It's an art form! And a deeply satisfying one. It’s meditative. It's…architectural, in a way. You’re constructing something from nothing. Though, you'd probably overthink the deconstruction of the pattern, wouldn't you? Almost certainly. Probably write a whole thesis on the inherent instability of knitted structures. You'd definitely get a first. So, are you planning on doing anything for Easter? Mum keeps asking if we’re coming up to Sunderland. I'm not thrilled about the thought of a six-hour drive each way, to be honest. Perhaps a quiet weekend in Cambridge? We could visit the Fitzwilliam Museum. They've got that new exhibit on Pre-Raphaelite paintings. Ooh, that sounds lovely!

Right, so we’re agreed then? London on Sunday? Aye, sounds good to me, love. Though I still reckon the train is a right palaver. All that queuing, and then fighting for a seat… Oh, don’t start, Arthur! It’s easier than driving, isn't it? You know how the traffic gets, especially on a Sunday. We’d be stuck on the M25 for hours. And parking… forget about it! Aye, well, I suppose. Still, I’d rather be in control of where I’m going, you know? Not relying on timetables and announcements I can barely hear. You’re just a grumpy old man, that’s all! We’ll get the 9:30 from Euston, that gives us plenty of time. I’ve already checked the National Rail website. Checked the website, have you? You and your technology. I still prefer a good old-fashioned guidebook. A guidebook?! Arthur, it’s 2024! Anyway, I was thinking we could go to the Science Museum first. They’ve got that new exhibition on space exploration, the one I was telling you about. Space exploration? Sounds a bit…much, doesn’t it? All those flashing lights and complicated diagrams. I’m more of a history man, myself. Something a bit more grounded. Grounded? You mean dusty and boring? Come on, Arthur, it’ll be fascinating! And afterwards, we could go to the Imax. They’re showing that documentary about the Amazon rainforest. Imax, eh? Is that the one with the enormous screen? Makes me feel a bit dizzy, those things. And all that 3D stuff… I always end up with a headache. Oh, you always complain about something! It's a treat, Arthur. And it's a good excuse to get out of the house. We haven’t had a proper day out in ages. That's true enough. It’s just… my back hasn't been brilliant lately. Sitting in those cinema seats for two hours isn’t exactly ideal. We can ask for aisle seats, then? You can stretch your legs whenever you need to. And we can take the bus around London, instead of walking everywhere. They’ve got those new electric buses, very comfy apparently. Electric buses, eh? They're always breaking down, from what I hear. Still, a bus is better than walking, I suppose. I remember when you could hop on a tram…  those  were the days.

Right, so Christmas dinner. Operation Festive Feast, as it were. We need a plan, eh? Last year was… chaotic. Mostly because of Aunt Carol and the gravy. Chaotic is putting it mildly. I think I’m  still  finding cranberry sauce in unexpected places. And yes, the gravy incident. Good lord. We need a designated gravy monitor this year, I reckon. I volunteer… to  not  be it. Fair enough. No, seriously, we need to divide and conquer. I’m happy to do the turkey, I think. I’ve perfected my roasting technique since last year’s slightly… pale attempt. You have? That’s good. Because the pallor of last year’s bird was a major talking point. I can handle the stuffing, no problem. And maybe the roast potatoes? I’ve been experimenting with goose fat. Goose fat? You’re a dangerous man, you are. That sounds incredible. Okay, stuffing and potatoes are yours. I’ll tackle the vegetables - Brussels sprouts, obviously, to appease Mum. Although I’m still petitioning for them to be banned. Never going to happen. Brussels sprouts are a Christmas tradition. Like arguing with relatives and terrible Christmas cracker jokes. Speaking of which, have you seen what’s on at the cinema around Christmas? Any contenders for a pre-dinner movie? I was looking, actually. There's that new sci-fi thing, “Echo Bloom”, getting good reviews. Or we could go for something more festive? There's always a terrible rom-com somewhere. Let’s avoid the terrible rom-com. They’re a national embarrassment. “Echo Bloom” sounds good. Slightly escapist. What about everyone else? Have you spoken to Sarah and Mark? Are they coming up from Shanghai? I texted Sarah this morning. They’re tentatively in. Mark’s got a conference, but he’s trying to reschedule. They said to say hello, by the way. They’re missing proper English pubs. Apparently, the ‘Irish Pub’ in Shanghai isn’t quite the same. An Irish pub in Shanghai… that’s the definition of irony, isn’t it? It probably serves Tsingtao with a shamrock on top. Bless them. We should try and get Ben and Chloe over too. Haven't seen them in ages. Good idea. They’re usually pretty reliable. I’ll give Ben a call tomorrow. He’s probably busy prepping for his exams. How’s his Mandarin coming along? It’s improving. He’s starting to get cheeky with the taxi drivers, apparently.

Honestly, Twitter is a cesspit tonight. Just… endless takes on absolutely nothing. I swear, people  need  drama. Tell me about it. I was scrolling earlier and saw someone having a full-blown meltdown because their oat latte wasn’t frothy enough. Like, seriously? Oh, the oat latte brigade are the worst. I had a woman yesterday practically accuse me of personal sabotage because we’d run out of oat milk at 2pm. Two. PM. Like I  planned  that. Right? The entitlement is… something else. It's the same people who leave one-star reviews saying “staff were rude because they asked me to wear a mask.” Ugh, the reviews. Don't even get me started. I got one today saying my sourdough was “too chewy.” Too chewy! It’s  sourdough , it’s supposed to be chewy! You get those, I get them. Someone left a review saying my cafe was "pretentious" because I had actual artwork on the walls, not just prints from IKEA. Pretentious! It's a local artist, supporting the community! People just want to be outraged. It’s a hobby now. Speaking of outrage, have you seen that new bistro that opened up on Deptford High Street? Vaguely. The one with the… aggressively minimalist décor? Aggressively is a good word. It's like they designed it to actively repel humans. Just concrete and uncomfortable looking chairs. Sounds charming. They charging, like, twenty-five quid for a plate of three olives? Worse. Twenty-eight. And it’s described on the menu as “deconstructed Mediterranean vibrancy.”  Deconstructed . Like what, they just threw the olives at the plate? Oh, dear god. Honestly, some of these places. I’m trying to figure out a new colour scheme for the bakery, though. Thinking maybe a slightly warmer tone, less… sterile. That's a good shout. Yours is lovely and bright, but maybe something a bit cosier for autumn? I’ve been sketching some ideas for a little revamp of the café too. Thinking about getting a new coffee machine. The current one's starting to sound like a dying walrus. A dying walrus? That’s… vivid. You’re braver than me, starting a whole business revamp. I'm just trying to finish this dissertation. It's on the semiotics of internet memes, unsurprisingly. Oh my god, that sounds… niche. It is. It really,  really  is. But it pays the bills, sort of.

Honestly, the state of that garden is appalling. I really must get out there tomorrow. It's just completely overrun. Can I have more peas, please? Of course, darling. Just don't fill your mouth so much, it's not very polite. Oisin, are you eating your carrots? They’re alright, Mum. Not as good as chips, though. Well, we can’t have chips every night, can we? Carrots are good for your eyes. You want to be able to see when you’re biking with your friends, don't you? Speaking of biking, I saw Mrs. Henderson out on her new electric bike today. She was going  fast ! Nearly took out poor Mr. Davies’ geraniums. Serves him right, he’s always complaining about kids playing football near his house. Now, now, let’s not encourage negativity. He just loves his flowers. Did anyone see those blue tits building a nest in the apple tree? I saw! They were carrying bits of fluff and string. Lovely! I wonder if they'll lay eggs. We’ll have to keep a close watch. It’s so exciting. It is nice, isn’t it? Though I’m slightly terrified of getting dive-bombed. Remember last year with those swallows? Oh, don’t remind me! They were relentless. Anyway, Oisin, are you finished? You barely touched your roast chicken. I'm not  that  hungry. Can I have some raspberries for dessert? Of course, you can. But you need to eat some more of your dinner first. It's important to eat your vegetables. You’ve got that history exam coming up, don't you? You need all your brainpower! I know, I know… It's just… dates and kings. It’s so boring. Oh, history’s fascinating! It’s just about finding a way to make it interesting. Perhaps think of it like a story? A really, really long and dull story. Nonsense! Now, have a few more mouthfuls of chicken, and  then  we’ll discuss raspberries and perhaps even a small scoop of chocolate ice cream. Ice cream! YAY! Chocolate! You’re easily pleased, aren't you? Oh, I remember when Leo was this age. Everything revolved around food, and chocolate. He used to hide chocolate biscuits under his bed. Children! They are little hoarders. Remember when Amelia tried to keep a gerbil in her doll’s house? She named it Mr. Bigglesworth, didn't she?

Honestly, Mum, the supermarket was a nightmare this morning. Absolute chaos. Everyone seemed to be panic buying again. Oh, really? What were they grabbing this time? Toilet roll, like last time? Worse. Pickles. Seriously, pickles. The pickle aisle was completely cleared out. I needed gherkins for the potato salad, and there wasn't a single jar left. Pickles? Well, I never! What’s the world coming to? I used to make my own pickles, you know. Lovely and crisp, they were. None of this vinegary nonsense you get now. I bet they were, Gran. You were always brilliant in the kitchen. I just ended up getting some capers instead. Hopefully, they’ll do. Capers are nice. A bit different. You alright for bread, though? I know you were saying you wanted to make sandwiches for your lunch next week. I got bread, thankfully. And cheese. Everything else just seemed… frantic. It’s like people are preparing for the apocalypse, one jar of pickles at a time. It's this television, you know. Scaremongering. They put it all in your head. Speaking of heads, did you manage to get an appointment with Sharon for your eyebrows, dear? They were looking a bit… wild last time I saw you. Oh, Mum! They’re not  that  wild. But yes, I booked in for next Tuesday. She’s fully booked for weeks after that, so I feel lucky. Good thinking. It makes such a difference, having your eyebrows done. Makes you look so much more… put together. I keep meaning to go, but I just haven’t got around to it. You should, love. Treat yourself. And speaking of treatments, you need a haircut! It’s getting a bit long, isn’t it? I know, I know. It’s just… finding the time. And honestly, I don’t really like going to the hairdressers. They always try to upsell me something I don’t need. I used to go to Mrs. Higgins down the road. Lovely woman. She’d always have a good gossip while she cut your hair. Those were the days. Though she did have a terrible habit of smoking while she was doing it! The smell would cling to your hair for days. Oh, goodness! That's awful. They're not allowed to do that now, are they? Definitely not! It’s been years since you could smoke indoors, thankfully. Gran, you really shouldn’t have had that cigarette earlier.

Honestly, this weaning thing is… a performance. He just looks at the spoon like I’ve offered him something deeply offensive. Oh, they all do that at first, Mum. It's a texture thing, mostly. He's used to smooth milk, and suddenly you’re presenting him with… mashed carrot. It's a shock to the system. A shock is an understatement. It’s like a tiny, silent protest. And the mess! I spent twenty minutes cleaning carrot puree off the highchair  and  his eyelashes. Oh, the eyelashes are the worst. My class were learning about facial features this week and I was telling them about babies, and even  they  all knew about the eyelash puree situation. Right? It's a universal truth of motherhood. So, what’s happening this week then? Anything exciting planned with school? Not particularly exciting, lesson planning mostly. Year Two are still horrifyingly obsessed with dinosaurs. I’ve lost count of how many ‘T-Rex facts’ I’ve had to listen to. Though, I’m starting a new block on communication next week, so we’re going to look at different ways of expressing ourselves. Oh, that sounds lovely. Are you going to do any sign language with them? That’s the plan! I've been doing a little online course, just a basic introduction. It's amazing how even simple signs can help them express what they need before they can really verbalise it. I thought it would be especially good for the quieter ones. That’s a brilliant idea! Remember how frustrated little Leo used to get when he was tiny, before he could talk? Sign language would have been a lifesaver. Exactly! And it's supposed to help with language development generally too. I'm a bit nervous about teaching it, though. I don't want to mess it up and give them all the wrong signs. You’ll be fine. You're a natural teacher. What about catching up with family this week? Are you still going to your Auntie Maureen’s on Wednesday? Yes, I promised. Although, Auntie Maureen’s definition of ‘a quick cup of tea’ is usually a three-hour interrogation about my life choices. Oh, she’s a force of nature, isn’t she? You’ll need to take reinforcements. Perhaps your cousin, Sarah? Good thinking! I'll give her a ring. And what about you? Are you and Dad meeting anyone?

It’s funny isn't it? How even a tiny incline feels like a proper hill after being in London for so long. Everything’s so…flat there. You get used to it. Although, I do think Londoners overestimate what counts as a hill. A slightly raised pavement is practically Mont Blanc to some of them. Exactly! And look at this view though. You can actually  see  for miles. Not just across the road to another Pret. It’s lovely. Proper Norfolk countryside. It's amazing how quickly you feel calmer just being amongst it all. Though, I’m still slightly nervous about getting completely lost. This network of footpaths is…extensive. Don't worry, I’ve got the map on my phone. And honestly, even if we did get a bit lost, it wouldn’t be the worst thing. We’d stumble across a quaint little village, probably with a pub. You’re always optimistic about finding a pub. Well, it's a reasonable assumption in Norfolk, isn’t it? Every village seems to have at least one. Look, there's Wighton ahead – do you fancy heading that way? It’s supposed to be really pretty. Wighton sounds good. Is it one of those villages where all the houses are made of flint? Some of them, yes. A lot of them round here are. It gives them a really unique look, doesn't it? It’s amazing how they managed to build everything with that stuff. Must have been back-breaking work. It is impressive. And it blends in so well with the landscape. It’s a world away from the brick and glass of the city. Do people actually  live  in these villages full time, or are they mostly second homes now? A bit of both, I think. It’s changing, sadly. More and more places are becoming weekend retreats for people from London and Cambridge. Still a good community spirit in most of them though, thankfully. It's good to see. That’s good to hear. It would be a shame if they just became ghost towns out of season. It’s the people that make a place, really. Definitely. And the pubs, let's not forget the pubs! Come on then, Wighton awaits. It's not a huge climb, I promise. Only a metaphorical mountain compared to London. Alright, alright. Lead the way, mountain guide. Just don’t complain when my calves are aching tomorrow.

…and honestly, the CGI was just  awful . Like, genuinely distracting. It ruined the whole thing. Really? I thought it looked alright. Not groundbreaking, but passable for a superhero flick. What film were you on about again? ‘Chronos’! The new one. Everyone was raving about it, saying it was the best one yet, and I was just…underwhelmed. Especially after the trailer. The trailer made it look amazing. Oh yeah, that one. I haven’t seen it yet. I’m more looking forward to the new Nolan film. Apparently it’s properly mind-bending. Ooh, that sounds good. I like Nolan. Not always  understand  him, mind, but I like him. Speaking of mind-bending, how’s Liam’s new job going? Still completely lost in jargon? Oh, spectacularly. He tried to explain it to me last night. Something about ‘dynamic load modelling’ and ‘finite element analysis’. I just nodded and pretended to understand. Honestly, it sounded like he was making it up as he went along. Classic Liam. So, still happy though? Is he actually enjoying it, or is it just a good paycheque? He seems genuinely challenged, which is good. He was getting bored in his old role, said it was all a bit…routine. This is definitely pushing him, though. He’s working late most nights. That’s a shame. He needs to have a life, the poor lad. You need to drag him out for a proper night, remind him what fun is. I keep trying! He’s just…focused at the moment. And stressed. Which brings me to another point… the cyclists. Oh, don't even get me started on the cyclists. Honestly! I was driving into town earlier, and this bloke just swerved right out in front of me, no signaling, nothing. I had to slam the brakes on. They're mental. Absolutely mental. They think they own the road. I swear they actively try to annoy drivers. It’s like they’re invisible until they’re directly in your path. And they never look! I’m all for cycling, good for the environment and all that, but they need to be more aware. Exactly! It’s not a personal challenge to see how close you can get to a car before they brake. It’s just…dangerous. I nearly took one out last week, purely by accident, thankfully. See! It's only a matter of time before someone gets seriously hurt.

Honestly, this is exactly what I needed. Fresh air, no emails… just fields. And look at those poppies! They’re everywhere. They  are  stunning, aren’t they? Makes you wonder about the economics of it, though. All this land… what’s the most profitable thing to grow around here these days? It can't all be barley, can it? Barley, oilseed rape, sugar beet mostly, I think. Old Man Hemmings down the lane does a roaring trade in lavender. Apparently, essential oils are huge. He’s got a whole distillery set up. Lavender, huh? Sounds… less brutal than a monoculture of beet. I was reading a paper the other day, actually, about the long-term economic impact of prioritising short-term cash crops. Depletes the soil, reduces biodiversity… it’s a real issue. Sounds like something you’d be writing yourself, to be fair. You and your sustainable development papers. Though, I imagine convincing a farmer to switch to a less profitable, but more sustainable, approach is… challenging. Very. It’s about incentivising them, showing them the long-term benefits. And honestly, getting consumers to pay a little bit more for ethically sourced produce. It’s a whole systems thing. It's frustrating, though, when you see the data so clearly. Tell me about it. Trying to get undergrads to understand basic economic principles is a similar struggle. It’s like talking to a wall sometimes. Did you hear about Sarah’s proposal finally getting approved? No! Really? The one on language acquisition in bilingual children? That’s brilliant. I knew she’d get there. She’s so dedicated. She is. She was practically bouncing when she told me this morning. Said the funding’s secured for three years. It means she can actually hire a research assistant. Fantastic. She deserves it. It reminds me I need to chase up my own grant application. It’s just…finding the time. Feels like every spare minute is spent marking essays. It does, doesn’t it? It’s ridiculous. I’m seriously considering just banning personal pronouns from essays. It would save me hours of correcting “I think” and “in my opinion”. You wouldn't! Though, honestly, the temptation is strong. Speaking of distractions, did you see the football last night? Chelsea absolutely demolished Spurs. Oh, please don't. I'm trying to enjoy the peace and quiet. You know I support Arsenal.

Right, so if we're leaving here now, we'll get to Durham about… half past? Assuming the A1 doesn’t decide to be a car park again. Yeah, sounds about right. It was horrendous last weekend, wasn't it? Proper stop-start all the way past Scotch Corner. I swear, people forget how to merge. Honestly! It's like everyone suddenly forgets they passed their driving test. Speaking of driving, yours is looking extra shiny today. New wash? Haha, yeah. Gave it a proper clean yesterday. Felt it needed it after that M62 debacle. Bit of bird poo, bit of…everything, really. It’s a magnet for grime, this car. You say that like it’s a personality trait. Mine just collects dust and old takeaway wrappers, basically. Are you excited for the football tonight? I am, actually! Bit nervous though, considering their form lately. They need to pull something out of the bag. You watching? Definitely. My dad’s already booked the living room. It's a sacred space on match nights. He has all his rituals and everything. Bit mad, really. Sounds familiar. My grandad was the same with cricket. He’d have the radio on, even if the TV was showing it, just in case the commentator said something important the TV coverage missed. Oh, bless him. It’s good to have those little traditions, isn't it? So, back to Durham, are we meeting Liam and Sarah at that new Italian place? Yeah, "Bella Notte", I think it’s called. I had a look at the menu online. Seems decent. Parking’s supposed to be a nightmare though, apparently. Fantastic. That’s just what we need. Another parking saga. Reminds me of trying to get into that tennis tournament in London last year. Ended up parking about a mile away and walking. Oh, the Queen’s Club? I've heard stories. It’s always chaos around those events. Absolute chaos. Anyway, Durham shouldn't be  that  bad. We just need a plan. Maybe drive around a few times, stalk people leaving… Stalking is a strong word. "Observing parking opportunities" is much more polite. Fine, observing. Honestly, it's a good job places like the Angel of the North exist, just to give us something pretty to look at while we're stuck in traffic. That’s true. It's quite a landmark, isn’t it? Always surprises people when they see it for the first time.

Honestly, this Rebekah Vardy trial… it’s just  fascinating , isn’t it? I mean, the things that come out. It’s all so… petty, really, isn't it? Oh, I’ve seen a bit of it on the news. Sounds a right mess, that. All over a story in the paper, is it? Seems a lot of fuss. Fuss is what young people  make , dear. Back in my day, we didn’t have all this… celebrity nonsense. Though, I do enjoy a good scandal now and then. Keeps things interesting. It does, doesn’t it? It’s just the level of detail, the screenshots… it feels a bit intrusive, somehow. Anyway, enough about that. Have you noticed how many geese are around lately, Doreen? They're gathering in fields near my office. Oh,  loads  of them! Down by the river, it’s absolutely covered. They’re proper noisy, aren’t they? Honking all day long. My Colin says they're getting ready to head off soon. They know when it’s time, those birds. Been doing it for centuries. Used to watch them fly over Peterborough in massive V-shapes. Always gave me a feeling of… well, of something bigger, you know? Something moving with the seasons. Yes, it’s incredible when you think about their migration. Thousands of miles, guided by instinct. It’s amazing. I read an article about how they navigate using the earth’s magnetic field. Magnetic field? Blimey! That’s clever. I just thought they followed the sun, or something. They were always said to follow the lead goose. A strong one, knows the way. And the others just… follow. Simple as that. Though, sometimes a young one would get left behind, poor thing. Always a sad sight. I saw a heron down by the pond in the village yesterday. A really big one. It just stood there, absolutely motionless, then  swoop  – caught a fish! It was so quick. Herons are lovely. We had one visit our garden once. Scared the life out of my cat! It thought it was a monster. They’re beautiful, but they can be a bit of a nuisance, you know. They’ll take the goldfish right out of your pond if you're not careful. Mrs. Higgins lost a whole school of them that way, years ago. Oh dear! That’s awful. It’s a delicate balance, isn't it?

Honestly, this quiche is amazing. Did you make it? Thanks! Yeah, it’s a Jamie Oliver recipe. Ridiculously easy, honestly. Though I did nearly set the kitchen on fire trying to blind-bake the pastry. Oh no! You and blind-baking. It seems a universal struggle. I always end up with soggy bottoms. Me too! It’s the bane of my life. Anyway, how’s the job hunt going? Last I heard you had that interview at the sixth form college. Ugh. Don’t even ask. It was…an experience. They kept asking me about differentiation, and I just felt like they wanted me to say all the buzzwords. Like, yes, I differentiate, obviously, but I want to tailor lessons to the students, not just tick boxes. Oh, the joys of education bureaucracy. They often forget the actual  people  involved, don't they? Was it a terrible panel then? One of them kept interrupting me, and another just had this… intense stare. It was unnerving. And then they asked me about my experience with ‘challenging behaviour’ and I accidentally launched into a story about a Year 7 who tried to eat his pencil. Oh, bless him! No! I know, right? It just  came  out! It wasn’t even a relevant example! I think it pretty much sealed my fate. I haven’t heard back, so I’m assuming it was a disaster. Oh, no, that’s rotten. Don’t give up though. Something will come up. You’re a brilliant teacher. Remember that observation last year? They were raving about your rapport with the students. Thanks, that’s kind of you to say. It just feels a bit hopeless at the moment. Especially seeing everyone else settling into their new roles. How’s work been for you? Still wrangling teenagers? Still wrangling! It's…fine. A bit hectic, but fine. We’ve got a new head of department, though. Very enthusiastic. Possibly  too  enthusiastic. She wants us all to embrace ‘dynamic learning spaces’ which translates to moving desks around every five minutes. Oh, God. No. The chaos. Exactly! And she keeps talking about ‘growth mindset’ like it's a religion. It is important, but honestly, sometimes I just want to teach Shakespeare without having to justify it with six bullet points about resilience. Speaking of things that require a lot of patience… how's little Leo? Is he sleeping through the night yet?

Honestly, I’m starting to freak out a little bit about… everything. Like, the future. It feels really… amorphous, doesn’t it? Amorphous? That’s a good word for it. I’ve been feeling it too. It’s not like when we finished our masters and it was, ‘right, get a grad scheme, climb the ladder.’ It’s… what  is  the ladder now? Exactly! Like, I’m happy enough at work, don’t get me wrong. Production Controller isn’t exactly glamorous, but it pays the bills. But is this  it ? Fifteen years of spreadsheets and chasing suppliers? God, no. And that's the thing, isn't it? I thought I wanted to be a PA, a really efficient, organized PA. And I am! But it feels…limiting. Like I’m facilitating  other  people’s dreams. Oh, I know that feeling. My mum keeps saying I should just be grateful I have a job, especially after… you know, everything. And I  am  grateful, truly. But grateful and content aren’t the same thing. No, they really aren't. Remember Sarah from uni? The one who always knew she was going to be a documentary filmmaker? Vaguely… didn’t she end up working in marketing for a toilet roll company? That's the one! She was so heartbroken, but then she said… she said it freed her up. She started making little films in her spare time, completely independently. Said the pressure was off. That’s… actually quite inspiring. I’ve been thinking about taking that pottery class at the community centre, purely for fun. Just to do  something  that isn't work or adulting. Do it! Honestly, we need more ‘just for fun’ things. I’ve been looking into volunteering at the animal shelter. It’s a massive commitment, I know, but the thought of cuddly puppies… Ooh, puppies! See, that's good. Although, my flatmate's cat is already trying to adopt me. She follows me everywhere. You're a cat magnet. Seriously though, maybe we should have a proper 'future planning' session? Like, actually sit down with a glass of wine and brainstorm? Not pressure, just… think out loud. Actually, that’s a brilliant idea. We could do it next week? I’m free on Wednesday evening. We could order a takeaway and completely fail to come up with a five-year plan. Perfect! Wednesday it is. And we can definitely fail.

Honestly, I’m starting to think Liam’s just… a bit of a knob, you know? Oh, go on then. What’s he done  this  time? It was bad enough last week with the whole forgetting our cinema plans thing. It's not one big thing, it's just… everything. He keeps texting Sarah, like, constantly. And it’s never anything important! Just, "Haha, that's funny" or "How was work?". It's so pathetic. Sarah from uni? The one with the bright pink hair? Yeah, that’s the one. I asked him about it casually and he just went all defensive, saying they're just being friendly. But  why  is he being so friendly with her when he's supposed to be with me? Ugh, boys. Always something. I swear, they thrive on the drama. Is it like, proper flirting though? Or just… attention seeking on his part? I honestly don’t know. That’s what’s driving me mad! It feels like he  wants  me to be jealous. Like he's fishing for compliments or something. That is a bit manipulative, isn’t it? My ex, Tom, used to do that. He'd mention chatting to other girls just to see if I'd get all clingy. It was exhausting. See! It's a tactic! You’re not imagining things. It's really annoying when they play games. Speaking of annoying, have you heard from Chloe lately? She's been so distant since we told her about Ben and I getting more serious. Oh God, yeah. It’s awful. She hasn’t replied to any of my texts. I tried to call her yesterday, went straight to voicemail. I'm genuinely worried she's properly upset. She always did have a bit of a thing for Ben, didn’t she? Even before you two officially got together. Yeah, but I thought she was over it. We’ve all been friends for ages! I just don't understand why she can’t be happy for us. It's not like we stole him from her. It’s that whole feeling of being left out, I reckon. Like, everyone else is pairing off and she’s still single. It's rubbish, but it explains her moodiness. She’s always been a bit sensitive. It's hard, though. You don’t want to tiptoe around her forever. But you also don’t want to lose a friend.

Right, this shepherd’s pie is  exactly  what I needed after the day I’ve had. Honestly, proofreading legal documents all day… it’s enough to make your eyes cross. It's good, Mum. Really good. Can I have some more gravy? Of course, darling. Just a little though, you've already had a generous portion. So, Leo, how was hockey practice? Did you manage to score? It was alright. Mr. Davies was being really strict today, making us do loads of drills. I didn’t score, but I did a good assist to Finn. He’s getting really confident now. That’s good to hear. It's important to have those supportive teammates, isn't it? You learn just as much from them as you do from the coaches. Yeah, Finn's a good player. He nearly scored a hat-trick last week. Oh, that’s fantastic! You two seem to be really enjoying hockey this season. It's lovely to see you both so enthusiastic about something. Remember when you both insisted on learning the ukulele? That lasted all of five minutes! Don’t remind me! My fingers hurt just thinking about it. It was… a valiant attempt. So, Sarah, any progress on figuring out that trip to Cornwall? The kids have been asking about it non-stop. I’ve been looking at cottages, actually. Found a few that are reasonably priced and close to the beach. It's just working out the dates with work. I’ve got that big marketing campaign launching in July, so it’ll have to be August, I think. August is good! That’s after my geography fieldwork. Can we go to Newquay? I want to try surfing again. I was terrible last time, but it was still fun. We can definitely go to Newquay. We could even take a surfing lesson this time, get you both properly taught. I’m less keen on  me  attempting it, though. I'm more of a sandcastle builder, frankly. I'm happy to supervise the sandcastle construction, if needed. It sounds like a lovely plan, that. We could explore some of the coastal paths too. Have you looked at Tintagel Castle? They say it’s spectacular. I have! It’s on the list. Also, Mrs. Henderson at school mentioned a really good wildlife centre nearby. She said they rescue seals. Leo would  love  that. Seals?! Seriously?

Honestly, the scale of these trees is just… humbling, isn’t it? Makes you feel incredibly small. And a bit silly worrying about things like… what Brenda said at the party. Oh, Brenda. She's a menace, that one. What did she say  this  time? Was it about Mark’s beard again? Worse, actually. She cornered poor Aunt Carol and started giving her ‘advice’ on her gardening. Apparently, Carol’s roses are “tragically uninspired.” Can you  believe  the cheek? Carol’s roses are legendary! No way! Brenda doesn't even  have  a garden! She lives in a flat with a balcony the size of a postage stamp. She’s all talk. It's just… a need to feel superior, I reckon. Exactly! And Aunt Carol, bless her, just stood there taking it. She's too polite to tell Brenda to shove her ‘advice’ where the sun doesn’t shine. I wanted to intervene, honestly. I would have! You're better at that sort of thing than me. I just clam up. Reminds me of what happened with Sarah and Liam at Christmas. Oh god, don’t start. What fresh hell did they unleash? I thought things were finally calming down after the… incident with the cranberry sauce. It's Liam's mother. She’s been subtly - and not so subtly - hinting to Sarah that she’s not “ambitious enough.” Apparently, being a primary school teacher isn’t a ‘proper’ career. Oh,  wow . That's… spectacularly rude. And so unfair. Sarah is brilliant with those kids. She’s making a real difference. Tell me about it. Sarah was properly upset. Liam tried to defend her, but his mum just steamrollered him with all this talk about "potential" and “wasted talent.” It was awful. It took Sarah weeks to get over it. Honestly, some people! They just don't understand that happiness isn’t measured in paychecks or prestige. It's just… exhausting dealing with that sort of negativity. Sometimes I think I need a permanent holiday just to recover from family gatherings. Me too. Although a holiday in a redwood forest is a pretty good start, wouldn't you say? It puts everything into perspective. Brenda and Liam’s mum feel a million miles away here. Absolutely. These trees have seen everything, haven't they? They've probably witnessed far worse family dramas than ours. Makes you think, doesn't it? It does.

Right, so the Kievs are in. Nearly burnt my fingers getting them out of the freezer, they're  solid . Honestly, you'd think they were designed to withstand a nuclear blast. Cool! Are they the really cheesy ones? 'Cause the cheesy ones are the best. They’re the ones with the garlic butter, dear, not just cheese. Though honestly, I’m still not convinced they’re as good as they used to be. They seem… smaller. And less garlicky. Smaller, definitely. It's shrinkage, I tell ya. Everything’s shrinking. Speaking of shrinkage, did you see that England game yesterday? Utter collapse. Wales were brilliant! Proper smashed ‘em. I was shouting at the TV the whole time. Mum didn’t like it. She said I was being a bit… loud. Loud is a diplomatic way of putting it, darling. You were practically conducting the orchestra with your yelling. And calling the England players…  wallies . Well, they  were  wallies! Missing tackles, dropping the ball… it was embarrassing. Ah, you’ve got your Grandad’s vocabulary already, haven’t ye? Wallies. He’d be proud. Though he’d probably have a more… colorful description. Please, let’s not delve into your father’s colorful descriptions. Anyway, are we still on for Granny next weekend? She was asking about you, Leo. Yeah, I guess. Can I bring my game console? There's nothing to do at Granny's except look at old photos. You can bring it, but you’re not glued to it all weekend, understood? Granny wants to  talk  to you, not watch you stare at a screen. And no backchat, young man. I don’t  always  give backchat. Oh, really? Remind me of last Tuesday when I asked you to put your shoes away… See? This is what I mean. Alright, alright. Enough family history. I was meaning to ask, have you managed to upload those photos from the holiday to Dropbox? I can’t seem to find them. I thought I did. Or maybe Flickr? I always get confused. I started a whole album, but I can’t remember which platform. Honestly, it's all so complicated. Flickr.Definitely Flickr. You said you liked the filters better there. Look, I’ll have a poke around later. My head’s pounding, though. Probably need a biscuit. Biscuits would be good! Can I have one? You can have one  after  your dinner, Leo.

Right, so I’ve chopped all the onions, you can start on the peppers if you like? It’ll just save a bit of time. Sounds good. Though honestly, I'm still full from that ridiculous cheese and pickle sandwich I had at lunch. Proper doorstep it was. Oh, you and your sandwiches! You'd eat a sandwich for breakfast if you could get away with it. Speaking of getting things, have those cups arrived yet? The ones I won on eBay? Oh, the vintage ones? Yes! They arrived this morning. Parcel was left by the back door. I’ve put them in the display cabinet in the dining room. They're  gorgeous , honestly. Really delicate. You’ve got a good eye for these things. Oh good! I was worried they'd be chipped or something. Sometimes the pictures are…optimistic, shall we say? I’m hoping to use them when my sister comes down next week. That’s a lovely idea. She’ll appreciate that. Are you making that lemon drizzle cake again? She’s obsessed with it. Naturally! It’s practically a requirement for her visits now. Although… I’m thinking of trying a new recipe. I saw one with poppy seeds. Ooh, poppy seeds sound nice. You’re very domestic all of a sudden. Speaking of domestic, I got some of that buckwheat bread from the market today. Oh lovely! Is it the one from that new baker? The Polish lady? That’s the one! It smelled amazing. Apparently, she only does it on Saturdays, so I had to get there early. She had a queue already forming. That market is getting really popular, isn’t it? It's good to see. Better than another betting shop, anyway. Absolutely. It's bringing a bit of life back to the area. So, about Friday…are we still going to The Black Swan for my leaving do? Of course! Wouldn’t miss it. Though I still think it’s ridiculous you’re leaving after ten years. Tell me about it. It’s just…time for a change. And frankly, I need less paperwork in my life! I’m hoping some of my colleagues will actually turn up. Old man Hemmings swore he would, but knowing him… He’s all bluster, Hemmings. He'll be there. And even if he isn’t, we'll make sure you have a good time.

Honestly, the paperwork is just… relentless. I’m drowning in it for this placement. It’s not even  interesting  paperwork, it’s just compliance stuff. Compliance is the bane of everyone’s existence, isn't it? Especially now. Everything’s under scrutiny. You know, dealing with smaller businesses, you see how easily things can… slip through the net. It’s scary. Slip through the net? You mean like, people not declaring everything? Oh, lad, you have  no  idea. I was talking to a bloke down the pub last week – runs a little building firm – and he was moaning about a client wanting to pay half in cash. Said it was “easier”. I nearly choked on my pint. Oh, God. That's… blatant. Did he take it? He said he politely declined. Said he’d rather deal with traceable transactions. Good for him. But it happens. A lot. It's tempting, especially when you’re starting out. Tempting, yes. But the fines now are eye-watering. Not even worth the risk, even for a small amount. I had a client a while back who thought he could just… shuffle some money around accounts. Thought he was being clever. HMRC caught him within a month. Nearly lost his business. Sounds stressful. I wouldn’t know where to even begin with all that. I'm still figuring out what I’m doing with me life, let alone dodgy accounting! Tell me about it. Uni’s clever and all, but it doesn’t exactly prepare you for real-world… stuff. Like working out your taxes, or understanding why everything needs to be documented three ways to Sunday. Well, you’re lucky to have us, aren't you? I can always give you a crash course. Honestly, it's not as scary as it seems. Understanding the basic principles is key. It’s all about the paper trail. No trail, big trouble. That's right. And it’s not just the fines either, it's the reputation. Word gets around in Doncaster, you know. A dodgy reputation can ruin you. Speaking of reputations… how are the little ‘uns doing? Are they behaving themselves? They are… a handful. Little Jack is convinced he can fly. Keeps jumping off things. Honestly, it's terrifying. And Lily is currently obsessed with glitter.  Everything  is covered in glitter. Oh, glitter. The herpes of the craft world. It gets  everywhere . You’ll be finding it for years.

Honestly, this weather is doing my head in. One minute it’s sunshine, the next it’s threatening to pour down. Makes planning anything impossible. Tell me about it. I had a garden fete to organise for the hospice, and I was sweating buckets all day, stressing about whether everyone would get soaked. Thankfully, it held off, but it was a close call. Did alright though, raised nearly £800. That’s brilliant, Dad! You’re amazing at those things. I’m just trying to survive a week of Year 6s hyped up on sugar and impending freedom. Honestly, the energy is…something else. Sounds chaotic! I had a woman trying to return a dress yesterday, saying it didn’t fit anymore. It was clearly worn, tag was off, everything. Some people, honestly! You just can’t win. Oh, the joys of retail! Still, at least you're not wrangling thirty nine seven-year-olds. How’s the sign language class going, love? Are you still enjoying it? I am, actually. It’s harder than I thought, remembering all the different signs, but really rewarding. I’ve been practicing with some of the kids at school who have hearing impairments, and they absolutely love it. It’s lovely to be able to communicate with them on their level. That’s fantastic, sweetheart. Always good to learn a new skill, especially one so helpful. It sounds really worthwhile. I wouldn't have a clue where to start, though. My brain just doesn’t work like that. We were thinking… well, I had a scan appointment today. Oh? And…? Don’t leave us hanging! Everything looks good. We’re having a little girl!    Oh my gosh, that’s amazing! Congratulations! I’m so happy for you both! A little niece! That’s wonderful news! I'm already picturing all the cute outfits. Seriously, I might have to start saving now. Brilliant! Absolutely brilliant! A granddaughter! I’m over the moon. We’ll have to start planning a little shopping trip, won’t we? Though, your mother will probably have a list as long as my arm already. You have no idea. She’s already sent me links to twenty different prams. Twenty! I told her it's only the first scan! Oh, grandmothers. They’re a force of nature. But it's lovely she’s so excited. Definitely. It’s nice to know you’ve got that support.

Honestly, this canteen food is…consistent. Consistently bland. But it’s quick, I suppose. Tell me about it. I swear they season everything with the same grey powder. At least the salad bar is okay. Did anyone actually manage to get a decent coffee out of that machine though? Mine tasted vaguely of metal. No, mine was awful. I think I’ll just stick to tea for the rest of the week. So, how’s everyone’s week been? Aside from canteen-related grievances, of course. I feel like I’ve just been drowning in proofs. Honestly, the amount of commas people misuse… Oh, don’t even  start  on the commas. I think my brain is actively rejecting the sight of them after formatting that manuscript yesterday. It was a historical fiction, which is lovely, but the author had a… unique approach to punctuation. It felt like a personal challenge. Right? I’m currently looking at transcriptions for a dialect study, and sometimes I just stare at the page and wonder what language people are even speaking. It’s fascinating, but also incredibly exhausting trying to decode everything. Oh, that sounds  intense . What dialect are you researching? I’m focusing on variations in East Anglian English, specifically around Aylesbury. It's surprisingly diverse, even within a relatively small area. Lots of subtle shifts in pronunciation and vocabulary. That’s really cool! I mean, terrifying for transcription, probably, but cool. It's amazing how much regional variation there still is. Publishing can kind of iron all that out, though, doesn't it? Everything has to be ‘standard’ English. It does. It's a bit sad, actually. You lose so much flavour. I grew up in Sweden, and we have a lot more acceptance of different linguistic variations. It feels much more… natural. That's a really good point. I’ve been doing some proofreading for a children’s book and the author deliberately included some colloquialisms, and the editor was  obsessed  with trying to remove them. Said they weren’t “accessible” to a national audience. Accessible… it’s such a buzzword. Sometimes I wonder if it just means ‘sanitized’. I had a supervisor once who insisted I remove any slang from my interview recordings. Said it wasn’t ‘academic’. Like, people actually  talk  like that! Exactly! It feels like we’re constantly being told to erase the way people truly speak. It’s… frustrating.

Right, so the visa application… absolute state, innit? They want a  photocopy  of the original photocopy of my passport. Who even  does  that anymore? Seriously! It’s like they’re deliberately trying to make it difficult. I spent ages last night filling out the forms, and then realised I needed a different pen colour for section four. A different  colour , mate. You’re joking! What colour did they want? Lilac? Nah, blue, but I’d already done it in black. Had to start again. It’s a nightmare. And the passport photos… mine look like I’ve been mugged. I know! I went to that booth in the market, thinking it’d be quick. It just… highlighted every single flaw. I look like a criminal. We need to re-do them, definitely. Yeah, we do. Think your mum’s got that decent camera she used for your graduation? We could try and get a passable shot in her garden. Better than those booth things. Good shout. I'll ask her. We need to get this sorted, though. Deadline’s looming. Speaking of sorting, how’s the donations looking? Have you had much on the JustGiving page? Slow, to be honest. A few quid from family, a couple from mates… not exactly setting the world alight. I was thinking… what about Gumtree? We could put an ad on there, explaining what we’re doing and asking for sponsorship. Gumtree? That’s… clever actually. Bit random, but it could reach a different audience. I’ll knock something up tonight. “Two lads, one ridiculous car, driving to Mongolia for charity! Sponsor us!” Keep it simple. Perfect! And we need to sort out the car stuff proper. Have you booked that mechanic to give it a once-over? Yeah, booked him for Saturday morning. He said he'll check the fluids, tyres, brakes… the usual. He reckons with a bit of luck, she’ll hold out. She's a brave little Fiesta. Brave indeed. Remember that time you tried to drive her through that field after the festival? Don't remind me. She was stuck for hours. Had to get Farmer Giles and his tractor to pull us out. That was a low point. Hopefully, Mongolia won't involve any fields. Let's hope not. We’re going to need all the car’s strength for the actual roads, never mind any impromptu off-roading adventures.

Honestly, I still feel dreadful. Like, absolutely knackered. Did  anyone  actually sleep last night? Sleep? Girl, I barely blinked. Sat with you in A&E for hours, then had to walk all the way back up here. My feet are killin’ me. How’s the arm, actually? Still throbbing? It’s a miracle I’m functioning at all. I had a lecture at nine.  Nine . After all that. And yes, arm, still looks like a balloon. Honestly, you scared the life out of us crashing into that table, Liv. I know, I know. I keep replaying it. One minute I’m reaching for a biscuit, the next…snap! And the pain! It was awful. They said it’s just badly sprained, thankfully, no break. But the doctor kept going on about needing to rule things out. Ruled out what?! I felt like a science experiment. They always say that, don't they? "Rule things out." It's just their way of covering themselves. Still, good they checked it out. Did they give you anything stronger than paracetamol? Just paracetamol. And a sling. A very fashionable sling. I look like I’m auditioning for a period drama. You do, actually. Very ‘damsel in distress’. Speaking of distress, did you see Ben texting you last night while we were at the hospital? Ben? Oh god. I didn’t even look at my phone. Was he being…Ben? Understatement of the century. Basically, he was super concerned but simultaneously managing to make it all about how  he  was worried. Like, “I was so scared for  you , it’s been a really hard week for  me …” Honestly, the man’s a walking drama fest. Ugh. He’s exhausting. I really thought…well, never mind. I need coffee. Strong coffee. Anyone with me? Lead the way. I think I’ve still got remnants of sleep clinging to my brain. Maybe a biscuit too. You know, for medicinal purposes. So, are you gonna tell me about this ‘thought’ you had about Ben? C’mon, spill. We're your flatmates, we're built for this. It's nothing. Just…I was thinking maybe he’s not actually serious about wanting a future. He keeps talking about ‘taking things slow’ and I’m starting to think ‘slow’ means ‘never’. Ooh, red flag city. My cousin went through that with her boyfriend. "Slow" turned into "radio silence." Exactly! It just feels like I’m putting in all the effort.

So, lad, did you have a good time at Auntie Brenda’s anniversary do on Saturday? Honestly, it was a bit of a whirlwind, wasn’t it? Yeah, it was alright. A bit crowded though, wasn't it? Couldn't really move without bumping into someone. And loads of people I didn't even know. Oh, aye, Brenda always invites everyone and their dog! She’s got a huge family, you know. Cousin Margaret brought three of her husband’s sisters this time, and I swear I’d never clapped eyes on them before. Did you manage to speak to young Thomas? He's grown a foot since I last saw him! Not really. He was just messing about with his phone the whole time. I said 'Hi' but he didn't really look up. It was more interesting watching Grandad try and work the photo booth. Oh, bless him! He’s hopeless with technology, isn’t he? He kept asking me how to get his picture ‘on the telly’. Took me a good ten minutes to explain it just went to a screen! Did you see him nearly knock over the cake? Yeah! That was funny. Mum had to grab it just in time. He was going on about wanting a bigger slice afterwards too, even though he’d already had two! He’s always been a greedy one, your Grandad. Remember when he ate all the Quality Streets at Christmas when you were little, and then blamed it on the dog? Oh yeah! I remember that! He said Buster had a secret sweet tooth. He did! And your Auntie Carol was on form, wasn’t she? Telling everyone about her new pottery class. For a good hour, solid. She's always got a hobby, hasn't she? Last time it was bird watching. She made us go out with her at dawn, even though it was freezing. Aye, she's enthusiastic, I'll give her that. But honestly, all those floral dresses… she looks like a walking garden! Did anyone ask about your exams? I felt like I was being grilled by everyone about your A-levels. Yeah, a few people. Mostly Grandma. She kept saying I need to get good grades so I can ‘get a proper job’. Like being a game designer isn't a proper job. Oh, don't pay her any mind. She's from a different generation.

Honestly, Dad, are you  sure  you packed enough water? I’ve already finished half mine and we’ve barely left Manchester. Drama queen. Yes, I packed plenty. There’s a whole case in the boot, remember? Along with about seven different types of biscuit. And relax, we're not crossing the Sahara. It’s just… I get really thirsty. And I need a pen. I wanted to start that holiday journal Gran got me, but I can’t find one anywhere. Check under your seat. I think I saw one rolling around earlier. Honestly, you lose more pens than I do money. Speaking of which… how are your A-Levels looking now that results are out? Are you still firm on York? Yeah, York’s still the one. I’m terrified, obviously. Everyone says Latin’s a killer exam. Mrs. Davies warned us the examiners are  brutal . Latin, eh? Fancy that. I barely scraped through French. Still, you’re a bright spark. You’ll be fine. What about lunch? Fancy stopping somewhere around Birmingham? I saw a decent-looking services on the motorway map. They might even have a Holland & Barrett if you’re craving one of those vitamin gummy things. Ugh, don’t remind me about vitamins. They taste like sadness. And Birmingham’s ages away! Can’t we just skip lunch and aim for a proper dinner in Cornwall? I’m craving a pasty. A pasty it is, then. But we'll need petrol soon, and I wouldn't mind a cuppa. My IBS has been acting up a bit, so maybe a peppermint tea. Oh, not the IBS talk again. You and your stomach. It’s like a whole other person. It feels like it sometimes. Speaking of feeling unsettled, I still can’t believe how much hassle it was moving all our stuff. All those boxes… it took me a week just to unpack the DVDs. Did I ever tell you about the time I tried to assemble that flat-pack furniture? Disaster. Only about a million times. You ended up using duct tape and swearing a lot. A slight exaggeration. But it got the job done. Though now the washing machine’s making a funny noise... I suspect another delivery and another afternoon battling IKEA instructions. Sounds… fun. Are we going through Gloucestershire? I always forget which counties we go through. It's such a long drive.

Honestly, the state of the garden is appalling. I keep meaning to get out there, but… well, you know. Life just gets in the way. Tell me about it. I spent the weekend battling spreadsheets. Thought I'd finally get on top of things, ended up further behind. At least you  have  a garden to neglect. My balcony is currently sporting a single, rather sad-looking geranium. Neglect is a strong word, dear. It simply requires…strategic management. A garden, like a school, demands consistent attention. You can’t just leave things to run wild, expecting a pleasing outcome. Aye, that's true enough. It’s a bit like wood, innit? Leave it untreated and it’ll rot. Needs a bit of oil, a bit of care. Though I’m more used to dealing with oak than roses, mind you. Strategic management sounds lovely, but I’m picturing a small jungle out there. It's just overgrown. I really need to tackle the rose bushes, they’re getting completely swallowed by bindweed. Bindweed is the devil’s work. It’s insidious. You pull it, it just comes back stronger. Like a particularly persistent office memo. It’s about getting to the root of the problem, isn’t it? With both the bindweed  and  the memos, Archibald. You must be firm and unrelenting. Don't allow it to gain a foothold. Firm and unrelenting, eh? Good advice for life in general, that. Reminds me o’ me old boss. Relentless he was. Drove us all mad, but got the job done. I wish I could be relentless with the garden, but I’m more of a ‘procrastinate until it’s almost too late’ kind of person. It's embarrassing, really. I used to have such a lovely garden. Don’t beat yourself up about it. We all have our priorities. Besides, a bit of wildness is good for the bees, isn’t it? While I appreciate the sentiment, it’s essential to maintain a sense of order. A neglected space reflects a neglected mind, I always say. Now hold on a minute, Eilidh. Just 'cause someone's garden's a bit wild doesn't mean their mind's away with the fairies. Sometimes folk just got other things on their plate. I've got three kitchens to finish this month, that takes some attention, you know? Oh, three kitchens! That sounds…busy. What sort of kitchens are they?

Right, Operation Mother’s Day is a go! What do you two think? We need a plan. Gran’s expecting a visit, of course, but what else can we do to make it special? Can we make her a card? With glitter? And draw a picture of a dinosaur! A really,  really  big one! Gran likes dinosaurs, doesn’t she? She does! A glittery dinosaur card sounds amazing. Excellent ideas, both of you. We can definitely do that. I was also thinking, maybe we could bake her something? Cookies? Brownies? Cookies! With sprinkles! Pink sprinkles! No, chocolate sprinkles! They're better. Chocolate is the best. Okay, okay, we can compromise. Half pink, half chocolate sprinkles. Deal? Both Speakers 2 & 3: Deal! Good. Now, I was also wondering if Gran would like to come to Forest School with us next week? It’s a bit muddy, but you two  love  it. Forest School is awesome! I found a really cool stick last time. It’s a magic wand! I made a fairy house! It was covered in leaves and moss. See? Gran would love that. Although, she might need wellies. And maybe a change of clothes. She’s a bit like a stick in the mud sometimes, isn't she? Oh, are you now? Where did  you  hear that? Daddy said it! Right. Well, it’s an idiom, darling. It means she can be a bit stubborn. It doesn’t mean she  is  a stick! What’s an idiom? Oh, good question. It’s like… a saying that doesn’t mean exactly what it says. Like if I said “it’s raining cats and dogs,” it doesn't  actually  mean cats and dogs are falling from the sky, does it? No! That would be silly! Exactly. It just means it’s raining very hard. So if I said you’re “pulling my leg” you’re not actually pulling my leg? No, you’re not! You're surprisingly quick on the uptake for someone who just learned what an idiom is. Can we go back to the cookies now? I want to start planning the sprinkles! Yes, absolutely. Sprinkles are very important. But first, let’s write Gran a little note and tell her about our Mother’s Day plans, and ask her about Forest School. What do you say? Okay! And we can write “Happy Mother’s Day, best Gran ever!” And lots of hearts!

Honestly, I’m still reeling from Auntie Maureen’s funeral. It just…doesn't feel real, you know? She was always  there . I know, it’s awful. I keep expecting her to ring, complaining about the price of tomatoes or something. She was a force of nature, wasn’t she? A total force. And she fought that cancer for so long. Years, didn’t she? It feels almost… selfish to be relieved it’s over, but the pain she was in towards the end… You're not being selfish at all. It’s natural to feel a sense of peace when someone you love is finally at rest. It’s the watching them suffer that’s the truly unbearable part. My Nan was the same. Held on for so long, but the last few months… just watching her fade. It’s horrible. And it makes you think, doesn’t it? About your own mortality, your family. I’ve been feeling so anxious lately, constantly checking myself for lumps and bumps. Ridiculous, I know. Not ridiculous at all. It’s a completely normal reaction. It’s fear, pure and simple. Are you talking to anyone about it? You’ve always been so good at bottling things up. I’m trying to be better about that. I booked a session with that counsellor, Sarah, you recommended. Haven’t had it yet, but just booking it felt…lighter. And I’m trying to talk to Ben more, but he just keeps saying "You’re fine, you're worrying too much.” Men, honestly. They mean well, but they just don’t  get  it, do they? Honestly, Sarah’s brilliant. She really helped me when I was struggling after my mum’s diagnosis. Just having someone to vent to, without judgement, made such a difference. That’s what I’m hoping for. It’s just… everything feels so fragile all of a sudden. And then Leo's been having such a tough time at school. Oh no, what’s happening with him? Is it still that bullying situation? It's… evolved. It started with the teasing, but now it’s more subtle. Exclusion. He’s saying they won’t let him play football at breaktime, that they whisper when he walks past. He’s so quiet about it, which worries me even more. He’s normally so boisterous. That’s awful. He's such a sweet boy.

Right, so I think I’ve finally cracked the code with this week’s lesson plan. It's all about conditional sentences, which… honestly, feels like teaching a particularly frustrating magic trick. Oh god, conditionals. They’re the bane of every language learner’s existence, aren’t they? Especially the mixed ones. I remember struggling with those for ages when I was learning French. Exactly! It’s like, “If I  had  studied, I  would  be…” and their brains just short-circuit. Speaking of brains short-circuiting, how did your linguistics seminar go yesterday? Anything interesting? It was alright. Professor Davies went on a tangent about the history of the definite article in Old English. Fascinating, obviously, but a bit…much for a Tuesday morning. I basically spent the hour doodling little speech bubbles. Sounds about right. Davies  does  have a tendency to get lost in the weeds. Did he mention his trip to South Korea again? He’s obsessed with it. Oh, you know he did. Apparently, he wants to do a comparative study on honorifics in English and Korean. He was saying how incredibly different the roles of men and women are, linguistically, over there. It’s all about showing respect, but it’s so gendered. Yeah, he's mentioned that before. It's a tricky topic, isn't it? I read an article once that pointed out how much subconscious politeness structures our language here, even if it’s not explicitly gendered like in Korean. True. Thinking about politeness… I’m starving. And I completely forgot to pack a lunch. Seriously? You, the queen of meal prep? What happened? I was rushing this morning, trying to finish that essay on Chomsky's theories – which, by the way, still feel utterly incomprehensible – and just…forgot. Okay, okay. Don't worry. I was thinking we could order something. Fancy a veggie Thai? There’s that place on St. George's Road that does a decent Pad See Ew. Ooh, yes! That sounds amazing. Although… maybe we should actually  cook  something at some point? We've been living off takeaway for a week. You’re right. We should. I was thinking of trying that lentil shepherd’s pie recipe I found. It's pretty simple, even for me. That sounds… healthier, at least. Though honestly, I'm always a bit skeptical of vegetarian shepherd's pie. Feels a bit blasphemous, doesn’t it?

Honestly, this pizza is saving my life. I swear, that physics problem set nearly broke me. It was genuinely offensive. Tell me about it. I’m still reeling from the module assessment feedback. Mr. Davies just…eviscerated my essay. Said it “lacked intellectual rigour.” Intellectual  rigour ? It was a 2000-word analysis of TikTok trends! Davies is just a wind-up merchant. Remember when he tried to convince us that Schrödinger’s cat was a metaphor for Brexit? Oh my god, yes! And then he got genuinely offended when someone pointed out the logical flaws. Speaking of flaws, has anyone seen my sports kit top? I swear I left it in the living room. Didn't you wear it to Sugarhouse last week? You were doing that weird dance with Ben to Charlie Simpson. Oh,  that  dance. I have photographic evidence somewhere. It’s horrifying. You looked like a malfunctioning robot, honestly. Though, Sugarhouse was good. Remember when we all tried to sneak in flavoured vodka? And Liam got caught by security? Classic. He acted like he’d committed a federal crime. Honestly, Liam's dramatic flair is a gift. Reminds me of Jack Whitehall. Speaking of, is anyone watching  The Big Fat Quiz  on Boxing Day? We  have  to. Definitely. It's tradition! Though, last year was a bit ropey. They kept referencing stuff I hadn't even been born when it happened. I’m more of a  University Challenge  person, to be fair. I love feeling smugly superior about random facts. You  always  feel smugly superior, love. Anyway, anyone playing Articulate tonight? I've been practicing my describing skills. Ooh, yes! We need to put a ban on anyone using overly complicated descriptions again, though. Remember when you tried to explain ‘Vampire Diaries’ last time? It took ten minutes and involved explaining the entire mythology of supernatural creatures. In my defence, it  is  a complicated show. And it’s vastly underrated, might I add. It has more emotional depth than  Twilight , definitely. Don’t even mention  Twilight . Honestly, it's a cultural stain. I still have nightmares about Edward Sparkles. Ok, ok, no  Twilight  talk. Has anyone read anything good lately? I’m in the mood for a thriller. Preferably one with a ridiculously convoluted plot. I just finished  Cloud Atlas . It's a bit of a mind-bender, but worth it. Or if you want something lighter, the  Chaos Walking  trilogy is good fun, despite being a bit… cheesy.

Aye, honestly, the traffic’s been mental since we left Durham. I thought getting out of the city would be the worst of it, but it's just…constant. Yeah, it’s pretty grim. I wasn't expecting this on a Tuesday afternoon. Thought everyone would be at work. Maybe there’s something on down the A1? Dunno. Maybe. Though, it’s not just the A1, even the little back roads were packed. I was thinking, right, someone’s probably had a right shunt somewhere, causing a knock-on. That’s always a possibility. Makes you wonder if it’s worth the hassle sometimes, doesn’t it? Just to visit your mam for a couple of hours. Don’t say that! She’ll be gutted if I only stay for a couple of hours. She’s been making a massive effort with the garden, she wants to show it off. Says she's got a new rose bush that smells "divine." Divine, eh? Sounds like your mam. Still, it's good of you to go. I barely see my folks, and they live closer than yours. Guilt, mostly. I get that. It’s easy to let weeks slip by. I was telling Sarah about this lass at work, she booked a holiday to Turkey and then her cat got ill and now she's cancelling and losing all the money. Oh, no! That’s awful. Poor lass. Cats are expensive enough without having to cancel a whole holiday because of them. Tell me about it. They're little fluffy money pits. She was saying she feels awful about leaving him with someone else, but also, she's proper stressed about the financial side of it. Ended up having a right cry during lunch. That's rough. You'd think travel insurance would cover something like that, wouldn't you? You'd think! But apparently, it's a pre-existing condition. The cat's always been a bit… delicate, she said. Apparently, it's a clause in the small print. It's always the small print, isn’t it? Always. Reminds me of when I tried to claim on my car insurance after that little scrape last year. The list of things  not  covered was longer than the list of things that were. Oh god, what happened with that? I remember you mentioning something... Some idiot pulled out on me at a roundabout.

This weather, eh? Proper miserable. Feels like November already. It does, doesn’t it? I swear my joints are aching more with this damp. It gets right into your bones. Gran, you said you had a doctor’s appointment yesterday? How did it go? Oh, it was the usual. He poked and prodded, told me to lose weight, and prescribed more of those pills. Honestly, I think I’m rattling with the amount of medication I take now. That’s frustrating. Do you feel they’re actually  helping  though, with the pain? A little, maybe. Hard to tell. It’s just… everything feels a bit achy these days. And I’m tired. Always tired. Tired’s right. Can’t even face watching the football properly. Norwich were dreadful again last night. Absolutely dreadful. Oh dear. Dad, you get so worked up about their games! It can’t be good for your blood pressure. What else is there to get worked up about, eh? The weather? My knees? It’s the football, keeps me going. Though I tell you what, the commentator was a right pain. Kept going on about tactics, nobody cares about tactics when they're losing 3-0! Sounds about right. I tried to explain blockchain to my students today. Similar level of glazed expressions, I think. Mum, have you managed to get that new telly set up? The one you ordered online? Oh, don't even  start  me on that telly. That’s been a disaster! First, the delivery man left it in the garden in the rain. Then, trying to connect it to the internet… honestly, it might as well be written in ancient Egyptian for all the sense it makes. You need young Alex to come round. He's good with all that techy stuff. He sorted out my tablet when I couldn't even find the on switch. I did ask him, but he's so busy with work. Said he'd try to pop over next week. Honestly, it’s just a waste of money. I might as well have stuck with my old one. At least I understood that! It’ll be worth it once it's set up, Mum. You’ll have all those streaming services, and you can finally watch ‘Great British Bake Off’ in proper HD. Hmm. That is tempting. But honestly, the stress of getting it working… it's giving me a headache.

Honestly, the wedding planning is… consuming my life. I spent three hours last night comparing ribbon colours.  Ribbon  colours! Oh, you’re already lost in the details! It’s good though, right? Means you’re excited. How’s Mark coping? He doesn’t seem the ribbon-choosing type. He’s mostly just nodding and saying “Sounds lovely, babe.” I think he’s secretly terrified. He did try to suggest brown tape once. Brown  tape  for wedding decorations. The audacity! Did you… did you veto that immediately? Vetoed is an understatement. I think I may have shrieked. He quickly backtracked saying it was a joke. A  very  bad joke. Men. Honestly. Speaking of men… how’s Liam? Still refusing to discuss anything remotely resembling the future? Ugh, don’t even get me started. He just avoids the topic. Like, if I even mention the word ‘commitment’ he suddenly remembers he needs to… check the football scores. Or feed the goldfish. The goldfish?! Does he even  have  a goldfish? It’s a metaphor, obviously! It’s just... frustrating. I want to know if we’re on the same page. I’m not asking for a ring, just a conversation! I feel you. It’s awful when they shut down like that. It makes you question everything. Well, maybe you need to stage an intervention. Get all the girls together, corner him with a nice dinner and a carefully worded list of questions. Ooh, I’m in! We could make it a themed intervention. Like, ‘Operation: Future Talk.’ We'd need code names. This is getting out of hand. But honestly, it’s tempting. Although, I’m trying to avoid inflicting my wedding stress on everyone else. Speaking of dinner… I was thinking we could all go to that new Italian place on Friday? I need a night away from swatches and seating plans. Yes! Absolutely. That sounds amazing. I haven't had proper pasta in weeks. Count me in. I need carbs and gossip. And maybe we can brainstorm Operation: Future Talk while we’re there. For, you know, research purposes. Perfect. It's a date then. Though, honestly, sometimes I think I’d rather spend a quiet night in. Sarah keeps going on about how she and Ben are ‘thinking about’ kids. No way! Sarah? The one who swore she’d never change a nappy? The very same. She’s completely gone off the deep end with baby names.

Honestly, this new telly… it’s got more buttons than a blasted spaceship. And half of 'em I haven’t a clue what they  do . Doreen, you were saying your grandson, young Thomas, is good with these things? Oh, he is, Arthur. A whizz, that boy. Spends all his time on that computer, mind you, but he understands all this streaming and on-demand malarkey. He sorted my tablet out when it froze last month. Said I was trying to run too many things at once. Honestly, I was just looking at pictures of the great-grandchildren! It’s the same at school, honestly. Trying to get the little ones to focus when they’ve all got a phone in their pockets. It’s a constant battle. Though, I have to say, some of the educational apps are brilliant. We're using one at the moment for phonics that's genuinely engaging. Phonics, eh? Funny how things change. Back in my day, it was just chalk and talk, and a good whack on the knuckles if you weren’t paying attention. Times were different, I suppose. Not necessarily better, mind you. Oh, definitely not better, Arthur. We’ve come a long way. Though it does worry me, all this screen time. I used to take the children out riding, you know? Old Maggie, the pony, she was a saint. Little Emily practically lived in the saddle. That sounds lovely, Doreen. My daughter’s been talking about getting the kids into horse riding. Says it's good for discipline and builds confidence. I'm a bit wary, though – it's an expensive hobby, isn’t it? That it is, lad. That it is. Everything’s getting more expensive. I’m dreading the winter, I am. Heating bills are going through the roof. And my pension…well, let's just say it doesn't stretch as far as it used to. Tell me about it, Arthur. I’m just thankful I managed to save a little something when I was working. Though it dwindles, doesn't it? Seems like it just disappears. Still, we manage. A cup of tea and a good chat always makes things feel a bit better. Absolutely. And look, Arthur, if you're really struggling with the heating bills, there are schemes available. I was reading about one the other day, a warm home discount. I can send you the link if you like?

…and honestly, the teenagers I’m teaching at the moment, their grammar is appalling. Absolutely appalling. You wouldn’t believe it, coming out of secondary school. Ah, well, things change, don’t they? When I left school, we were all expected to write properly, beautifully even. Penmanship was a thing! Now it’s all thumbs and screens. Exactly! It’s the screens.
