They’re texting each other in abbreviations, and then they try to write an essay…it’s a disaster. Still, it keeps me employed, I suppose. Though sometimes I wonder if I’m just fighting a losing battle. Don't say that! You're a good teacher, I know you are. It’s a valuable skill, knowing another language. Makes you see the world differently, doesn’t it? Remember that trip we took to Italy, a few years back? You were ordering for us in fluent Italian, and I felt like a right buffoon! Oh, don’t be silly! You managed perfectly well. Though I do enjoy being able to use it. So, how was your weekend? Did Margaret enjoy the garden centre? Oh, she absolutely loved it. Spent a small fortune, naturally. Hydrangeas mostly. She's convinced she can get them to bloom blue, despite the soil being resolutely pink. It's a running battle, really. I just help carry things. Sounds…domestic. It’s good she has a hobby though. Keeps her busy. I think I’ll finally tackle the garden this weekend. It’s become completely overgrown. Though I’m not nearly as green-fingered as your Margaret. You’ll be alright. Just a bit of weeding and hacking, that’s all. Speaking of keeping busy, how’s your brother, David? Haven't seen him in ages. He's good, actually. He’s finally started that pottery course he was talking about. He’s really into it, apparently. Making all sorts of…interesting creations. He sent me a photo of a rather wonky-looking vase. Good for him. Always good to have something to occupy you in retirement, isn’t it? I’ve been tinkering with my stamp collection. Found a rather rare Penny Black the other day. Oh, really? That's impressive! You've had that collection for years, haven't you? Your father started it, didn’t he? That's right. Passed it down to me. It's a good link to him, I suppose.

Honestly, that was the most… underwhelming Valentine’s Day ever. Like, seriously. Oh no! What happened? Don’t tell me Liam didn’t even  attempt  romantic gestures? Attempt is a strong word. He remembered it was Valentine’s Day, which is a start, I guess. But it was… a Tesco meal deal and watching football. Oh, bless him. He’s… practical. Practical bordering on completely oblivious! I mean, I didn’t expect roses and a fancy restaurant, but a  little  effort? I saw Chloe’s boyfriend got her a weekend away to Brighton! Brighton! Ooh, fancy! Is Brighton nice? I’ve never actually been. My mum always said it was full of stag dos and… well, just a bit much. It can be, yeah. But it's cute! They went to this little cinema on the pier, apparently. Old-school vibes. We should go sometime, proper girls’ trip. Ooh, I'd be up for that. Anything’s better than another night in watching terrible reality TV. Speaking of which, I spent my evening trying to decipher what my flatmate was ordering in this new Vietnamese place. Oh, the one near the library? I’ve walked past, it smells amazing. It  is  amazing! But the menu… it’s all in Vietnamese, mostly. And she was speaking to the waiter in Vietnamese, and I just sat there looking bewildered while trying to point at a picture of noodles. Haha! That’s hilarious. You need a translator! I’m going to try and learn some basic Italian before my trip to Rome next year, just so I don’t end up in a similar situation. Good idea. Though, honestly, even ordering a coffee can be stressful when you're trying to remember all the phrases. I went to that fancy Italian place near the market last week and completely butchered my pronunciation. The waiter definitely judged me. They always do! It’s like they're actively listening for you to mess up. I’m terrible with accents anyway. I can never tell the difference between someone from Birmingham and someone from… well, anywhere else in the Midlands! Oh, you're so London! We get that all the time. People always lump everyone from the Midlands into one big accent. It’s frustrating! My cousin gets so annoyed. She’s from Nottingham, and people just assume she’s from… I don't know, somewhere near Manchester.

Honestly, the sheer audacity of him to say that on Question Time… it wasn’t even a  dog whistle , it was a full-blown foghorn of racism. Mmhmm. Classic. Honestly, I switched off after the first ten minutes. It’s just exhausting, you know? Constantly having to dissect every syllable for coded bigotry. This Dan Dan noodles are  incredible  though, seriously. You have to try some of mine. I will, I will. I just… it feels like we’re going backwards. Like all the progress everyone fought for is just… eroding. And he’s got a platform to say that stuff! It’s because the platforms are broken, isn’t it? Algorithmically amplified outrage. And the media loves a good controversy. Keeps the clicks coming. It’s all just… a game to them. Though, realistically, it affects real people. Speaking of affecting people, Mrs. Henderson from the office is at it again. Oh,  not  her. What is it this time? Is she still trying to take credit for my designs? Worse. She spent the entire morning complaining about “woke” housing policies. Apparently, building affordable flats near her leafy suburban paradise is a personal affront. Said it would “ruin the character of the area.” Oh, for goodness sake. The ‘character’ being exclusively for people who already own property and can afford extortionate council tax? Exactly! It’s amazing how quickly ‘community spirit’ evaporates when it’s threatened by, you know,  people . I tried to gently point out the housing crisis and systemic inequalities, but she just glazed over. Honestly, sometimes I wonder why I bother. It’s the same argument all the time, isn’t it? ‘Protecting property values’ is just a euphemism for ‘keeping out anyone who isn’t already privileged.’ It’s all tied together, isn’t it? The racism, the classism, the whole system. Totally. It's all branches of the same rotten tree. Capitalism incentivises that kind of thinking. Competition for limited resources. Scarcity mindset. Makes people… unpleasant. And the housing situation just  fuels  it. It's designed to be a system where owning property is the ultimate goal, the ultimate marker of success. And then they’re outraged when someone suggests maybe, just maybe, everyone deserves a safe and decent place to live. It’s mad. I've been looking again, you know, trying to figure out if I can actually get on the ladder, or even just a slightly less precarious rental.

Honestly, I’m dreading Tuesday. Just…dreading it. Nursery drop-off? It’ll be alright, Mum. He’ll probably be fine, and you’ll feel awful for the first hour then better. Honestly. That's what everyone says. It's not  him  I’m worried about, you know? He’s a little social butterfly, always wanting to be with other kids. It’s  me . It’s the thought of leaving him, that’s all. Suddenly I’m back at work and… well, it feels selfish really. It’s not selfish! You need to work, you want to work. And little Leo will have a brilliant time, learning and playing. Think of all the new things he’ll experience. I know, I know. It’s just… it’s a big change. And then trying to balance everything. Work, picking him up, dinner, bedtime… I feel like I’m already exhausted just thinking about it. You’ll get into a routine. It’ll be hectic for a bit, but you will. And Dad’s helping, right? He is, he is. Though he keeps suggesting we watch that awful police procedural on Tuesday nights. Says it’ll ‘take my mind off things’. Honestly, half the time I’m too tired to even  see  the television. Ugh, no way. That show is so predictable. We should have a proper girls’ night when you’re settled back in. Maybe a film? Or we could finally try that new Italian place. Oh, that sounds lovely. It feels like ages since we’ve just… hung out. What are you thinking for your summer holiday then? Any plans? Still up in the air, to be honest. I was thinking maybe Interrail again? Last time was amazing, but a bit rushed. Or maybe something a bit more… chilled? Somewhere with a beach. A beach sounds wonderful. Maybe Spain? We could all go. Leo would love building sandcastles. Although, realistically, it might be a bit ambitious for this year… We could look into it. No promises, but no harm in browsing, is there? Speaking of Leo, how's the weaning going? He’s been having purees for ages, hasn't he? That’s the other thing stressing me out! He is, and he’s getting a bit bored of it now. I tried him with some mashed sweet potato yesterday, and he just… spat it out. Made such a mess. Oh dear.

Honestly, the day just… vanished. I feel like I achieved absolutely nothing. Just endless emails and pointless meetings. How was your day, David? Much the same, actually. Spent most of it on the phone, chasing donations. It's getting harder and harder, you know? People are tightening their belts. Though, I did manage to get a commitment from old Mr. Henderson for the garden revamp. Small victory. Mine was… eventful. Had a right nightmare with a delivery driver refusing to bring a stock order all the way to the back of the shop. Said it wasn’t his job. Honestly! Spent a good half hour arguing with him. Sounds stressful, Chloe. I had a relatively quiet one. A lot of prep work for the new campaign launch next month. It’s going to be huge, if we pull it off. Spent a lot of time in meetings, too, naturally. Oh, that reminds me, David, did you get that statement sorted for the police about… well, you know. Yeah, finally. It took ages to get my head around everything that happened. Had to go down to the station this afternoon. They were very thorough. It’s just… unsettling, re-living it all. Sounds awful. Hopefully it’ll get resolved quickly. Definitely. Glad you got it done though, Dad. The sooner it's off your plate, the better. Absolutely. Speaking of things off my plate, has anyone else had a ridiculously high phone bill this month? I just got mine from EE and it's nearly double what it usually is. I haven’t even  done  anything different. Oh, don’t even get me started on EE! I swear they just make up charges. I had a battle with them last year over something similar. It took hours on the phone and eventually threatening to switch providers to get it sorted. Seriously? I’m with Vodafone, thankfully, haven’t had any issues. I’m on Three. It’s usually pretty reasonable. Maybe it’s a glitch, Mum? Have you checked the itemised bill? I have, and there are a few charges for premium rate calls to numbers I don’t recognise. It’s so frustrating! I’m calling them tomorrow, but I’m bracing myself for a lengthy argument. Good luck with that. You’ll need it. Right, what are we all doing for the rest of the week? Any plans? I’m working every day, unfortunately.

Honestly, man, the wedding was brilliant. Seriously brilliant. Your mum absolutely smashed it with the buffet, though. I think I ate my weight in spanakopita. Tell me about it! She was proper proud, she'd been making it for days. She's got that recipe handed down, apparently, from… well, a woman in Cyprus, generations back. It's a family thing. You alright with it, being a proper Englishman and all? Mate, I’m always up for good food. And that wasn’t just good, it was  exceptional . It was a welcome change from my usual diet of beans on toast, let me tell you. Speaking of changes... how are you finding married life? Still feels real? It's...different. Good different, mostly. Still figuring out the whole 'shared remote' situation, that's the biggest hurdle so far. But yeah, it's good. Feels like, you know, proper settled. What about you? Still churning through historical documentaries? Saw you posting something about Rome on Insta. Oh, always. I got properly sucked into a series about the late Republic, the whole Caesar versus Pompey thing. It’s wild the amount of backstabbing and political maneuvering that went on. It’s practically  Game of Thrones  but, you know, real. Have you ever dipped into any Roman history? Not really, no. Always preferred the Greek stuff, to be honest. All that mythology. Spartacus, mainly. I watched that series a few years back, the one on Netflix. Proper violent. Ah, yeah! Good show. A bit…  stylized  for real history, but good entertainment. Makes you think though, doesn’t it? All those lives cut short, all that brutal stuff. Makes our little problems seem pretty insignificant. Like, I was stressing about a student’s essay all week, and then I think about someone dying in an arena... Exactly! Puts things into perspective. Speaking of dying young… did you see that documentary about Amy Winehouse? Proper heartbreaking. Such a talent, gone way too soon. Yeah, it was awful. It's just so sad to watch someone self-destruct like that. Makes you appreciate…well, just being around, I suppose. Fancy a tea? I’ve got a whole collection now, thanks to my aunt. She’s convinced I need to expand my palate. Tea sounds good, yeah. What kind have you got? Anything exotic? Loads. Earl Grey, obviously. A couple of fruit infusions. Oh, and a proper smoky Lapsang Souchong.

Ugh, seriously, that English test was  brutal . Did you understand any of the poetry questions? Brutal is an understatement! I completely blanked on the Tennyson one. I knew it was about, like, charge of the light brigade…but the actual analysis? Gone. You? Same! I think I just wrote whatever came into my head, hoping for a few marks. Mrs. Davies is so intense about poetry, isn’t she? It’s like it has to mean  everything . She’s the worst. She always looks at you like you’ve personally offended her if you don’t have a deeply insightful response. I much prefer Mr. Harrison. He just wants us to enjoy Shakespeare. Definitely! He’s actually funny. Anyway, what did you think of the art project? The still life with the fruit? Oh, that was alright. A bit boring, honestly. I wish we could do something more…I don’t know, exciting? Like abstract painting or sculpture. All I did was just copy the apples and oranges. I felt the same. I tried to get my shading right but it just looked muddy. Miss Peterson kept saying “think about light and shadow,” but it’s hard when it’s just…fruit. Speaking of hard, I’m so behind in French. Oh, don't even  start  on French! Madame Dubois is terrifying. She speaks so fast, and if you get one verb tense wrong, it’s like the end of the world. I know! And the homework is endless. Did you manage to finish the writing exercise about your weekend? Barely. I ended up just making something up. I wrote about going to a really exciting music festival, even though I spent the weekend doing laundry. Smooth! I wrote about going to the cinema, which is also a lie, but less extravagant. So, are you still in wind band? How’s practice going? Yeah, still going! It’s…okay. We're trying to learn this really complicated piece for the winter concert. It's got loads of fast bits for the flutes, and honestly, I’m struggling to keep up. Oh no! That's the one Mr. Allen was talking about, isn’t it? The really dramatic one? That’s the one. It’s making me seriously question my flute-playing abilities. Have you seen Leo in the corridors lately? He keeps giving me really weird looks. Leo? Oh,  him . Yeah, he’s been staring at everyone, I think.

Honestly, Brenda, you wouldn't  believe  the price of a scone in this place. Three pound fifty! Three pound fifty for a scone and a tiny pot of jam. Daylight robbery, I tell you. Mmm? Oh, aye, sounds steep. Did you get the fruit one or…? Just a plain one. Didn’t fancy the fruit, thought it might be mostly sultanas. Though, honestly, even for a plain one… it’s scandalous. Your Grandad would have had a fit. Remember how he used to complain about a loaf of bread costing… what was it, sixpence? Sixpence and a ha’penny, more like! He’d rant all afternoon. Though, mind, sixpence was worth something  then . It's all relative, isn't it? Though, three fifty  is  a bit much. They're probably charging extra ‘cos it’s a fancy café. Look at the bunting, proper posh. Bunting doesn’t make a scone taste better, pet. Speaking of posh, did you hear about young Amelia Henderson? She's off to study… what was it? Marine Biology… in Australia. No way! Australia? That's miles away. Is she getting a scholarship or something? They must be loaded. Apparently, her dad works for one of those big tech companies down south. Something to do with… algorithms, I think. Honestly, all that computer stuff goes right over my head. I preferred a good textbook and a classroom, thank you very much. It’s a different world now, Brenda. They’re all glued to those phones. Look at Ethan here. What are you even looking at, love? Just… stats for the match tomorrow. Newcastle are playing away against Leeds. Trying to figure out if Shelvey's likely to start. Football, football, football. Honestly. It's all anyone talks about. Your father was the same. Ruined a perfectly good Sunday afternoon watching men kick a ball about. Now, now, Elsie. Don’t be disparaging. It's a good hobby. Gets them out of the house. Reminds me of when we went to that match in Rome, remember? The flags... the noise... It was fantastic! Even  I  enjoyed it, and I'm not a football fan. Rome! That was… goodness, how long ago was that? Just before your health started to go, wasn’t it? We had such a lovely time. Though the food… I don’t think I ever quite got used to all the pasta. It’s alright, pasta.

Honestly, Dad, you wouldn’t  believe  the traffic getting up here. It was utter chaos on the A11. Took me nearly three hours. Three hours? Blimey. Should've taken the back roads, love. Know 'em like the back of me hand, I do. Though, mind you, even they’re gettin’ busier these days. Everyone seems to be on the move. It’s all these tourists, isn’t it? Flooding Norfolk. Can’t move for ‘em. Still, good for the local economy, I suppose. It’s a bit frustrating, though, isn’t it? Especially trying to get anywhere on a Saturday. Though I suspect a lot of it is people just… well, getting bigger, and needing bigger cars to fit in. Oh, don’t start on that again, darling. You and your observations about societal waistlines. I’m just saying! It’s true! You see it everywhere. My students are practically glued to their screens and living on takeaways. It's a ticking time bomb for health issues. Now, now, don’t be so harsh. Everyone enjoys a bit of a treat. And it’s not always about the size of the car, it's about the number of 'em. Kids everywhere. Your Cousin Margaret, now  she's  put on weight. Says it's her thyroid. But I reckon it’s all the cream she puts in her tea. She’s convinced it’s a medical condition, the clever thing. It's more complicated than that, Mum. There’s genetics involved. Predisposition. It’s not just willpower. And sometimes it  is  medical. Exactly. Though, I was reading an article about how epigenetic factors are more significant than we previously thought. It’s not just what your parents gave you, it’s what  their  parents experienced. Epigen…whatsit? Sounds like somethin’ you’d find in a science fiction film. I just know a bloke who used to be rail thin, suddenly piled on the pounds last year. Turns out he had a tumor pressin’ on his pituitary gland. Oh, poor man! Still, that’s rare, isn't it? Most people just… enjoy themselves a little too much. Remember Old Mr. Henderson? He said he put on weight deliberately, to keep warm in the winter. Said it was like havin’ a built-in duvet. Oh, Mr. Henderson. Always a character. Speaking of characters, are you still working on that enormous jigsaw, Mum? The one of the cathedral?

Honestly, Moodle is driving me up the wall. I spent three hours last night trying to get the Turnitin integration to  actually  work for the essay submissions. Three hours? Ugh. What was the issue this time? Is it still the plagiarism detection settings? No, not this time. It seems to be…communicating with the student list? It’s like half the students aren’t showing up in Turnitin at all, even though they’re all enrolled on Moodle. I checked and re-synced everything, and still nothing. That’s bizarre. Did you check the enrolment method? Sometimes if they've manually enrolled or something it messes with the sync. Yeah, everything’s set to automatic enrolment via the course. It’s just…random. Like, Sarah and David are showing up, but Emily and Ben aren’t. There’s no logic to it! Hmm. Have you tried exporting the Moodle enrolment list as a CSV and just manually uploading it to Turnitin as a last resort? It’s a pain, but might get it sorted for this deadline. Oh god, that sounds…time-consuming. But you’re right, if it avoids a load of late submissions because they can’t actually hand it in… I suppose I’ll have to. I just wish the system would work seamlessly. It’s supposed to  save  us time, not create more work! Tell me about it. Remember last semester with the quiz function? The whole thing glitched and reset all the students’ attempts halfway through the exam. Don't remind me! The emails I got were…intense. I felt terrible. Honestly, sometimes I wonder why they even bother updating Moodle, it just introduces new ways for things to break. I think it’s the university’s commitment to “digital transformation” or some buzzword like that. They want to appear progressive, even if it means making our lives significantly harder. Right? It feels like they focus on the  idea  of technology being helpful, rather than actually considering how it functions in practice, or if it's even… useful. Have you started prepping the feedback rubric for those essays yet? I’m thinking of trying a slightly different approach this time. I’ve sketched something out. Thinking about incorporating more specific criteria for the argument development section. I’ve noticed a lot of students are struggling to, well, actually  make  an argument rather than just describing things.

Honestly, I feel like I’ve aged a decade in the last three days. This jet lag is brutal. Tell me about it. I thought I’d be fine, just a little off. But it’s like my body thinks it's permanently 3 am. Did you manage any decent sleep last night? A couple of patchy hours. Mostly spent staring at the ceiling wondering if I'd accidentally fallen asleep in a seminar. Which, honestly, wouldn’t be the first time after a conference. How was little Leo? Was he up all night again? Surprisingly… relatively good. He did wake up once, around 5, but a quick feed and cuddle and he went straight back down. I think he senses you’re back, actually. He’s been unusually quiet today, just observing everything. Oh, that’s sweet. I miss being his default entertainment centre. I feel terrible leaving him, even for a few days, but the conference was really important. It absolutely was. And you were brilliant presenting, from what everyone said. Worth battling the time difference for. Speaking of important things… did you manage to get those meeting notes sorted? Professor Davies is chasing me for them. Ugh, yes. I finished them just before I collapsed into bed last night. They’re on the shared drive, under ‘Conference - Davies Meeting’. Urgent formatting required, naturally. Honestly, he's such a stickler. He is. But a brilliant academic, so we suffer his quirks. Right, okay, good. That’s one thing off my plate. Listen, are you free on Saturday? The Little Theatre Company are doing a production of ‘A Midsummer Night’s Dream’. I managed to snag some tickets. Oh, really? That sounds lovely! We haven’t been to the theatre in ages. Is it the outdoor one, by the river? It is! It’s supposed to be amazing, they’ve built a whole set amongst the trees. It's a bit of a trek, we’d need to leave around six to get a decent parking space. Six sounds good. Although… six might be prime Leo meltdown time. We might need to coordinate strategically. We can ask my mum if she's free to babysit. She adores him and is usually up for an evening of Leo-wrangling. I can text her now. That would be fantastic, thank you. It would be so nice to just… be adults for a few hours.

…so, anyway, Omar’s cousin, Fatima, she’s still stuck trying to get a visa to come over. Honestly, it's a nightmare. She's got the job offer at the hospital, all lined up, but the paperwork… it’s just endless. Ah, the joys of immigration, eh? Takes a special kind of bureaucratic skill to make things intentionally difficult. Is it the UK visa she’s needing? Yeah, standard skilled worker visa. Apparently, they’re being extra cautious with anyone coming from the region – you know, the political climate and all that. It’s a bit… frustrating. She’s a qualified nurse, for goodness sake! I understand. It's always the innocent people who suffer the most. It's the same story with my brother’s wife's family trying to get out of Iraq. So much depends on which box you tick, and a bit of luck. Though, to be fair, sometimes it's just a lot of money. Have you heard? The price of oil’s climbing again. Oh, don't even get me started on oil. It feels like everything comes back to that doesn’t it? All this… instability, a lot of it is fuelled by that black gold, and who controls it. It’s a mess. A mess is an understatement. And the influence of Wahabi ideology doesn't help either, spreading across North Africa and beyond. I was speaking to a friend who was in Libya a few years back, and he said the rise in extremism was directly linked to the oil wealth and the corruption that came with it. Libya… god, that’s a whole other can of worms. It’s heartbreaking what’s happened there. Seems like a constant cycle of conflict. And it’s the young people who end up getting caught in the middle, isn’t it? No opportunities, just… drawn into things they shouldn’t be. Exactly. My cousin, Khalil, he’s trying to get his kids out of Basra. He wants them to have a better life, you know? Education, some semblance of stability. But it’s expensive. Really expensive. I’m trying to help him with the paperwork, but I’m not a visa expert like you, dealing with students from all over the world. Well, I can certainly take a look at Fatima's application for her, maybe spot something that’s missing. Happy to help, truly.

Honestly, that was a lovely roast. Lamb’s always such a treat, isn’t it? Though I feel a bit…sluggish now. It was excellent, your cooking’s still top-notch, even under pressure. Though watching  Escape to the Country  whilst eating felt a bit odd, having the TV on in the dining room. Nonsense. It’s perfectly civilised. A bit of background noise. Though they always pick the most dreadfully beige houses, don't they? And the people always want a ‘project’. Honestly, who  wants  a project at their age? I do quite like seeing what they do with the places, though. It’s escapism. More escapism than the cruise you’re all planning, actually. Oh, don’t start. Mum’s already got the outfits planned. Apparently, formal night requires a ‘statement necklace’. One must be prepared! It’s the Mediterranean, darling. You can’t just turn up in your gardening clothes. Besides, I deserve a bit of luxury. I've earned it after years of dealing with unruly teenagers. Speaking of earning things… how’s the flat sale going? Any progress with the landlord? He’s been dragging his heels for months. It's… frustrating. He keeps finding new things ‘wrong’ with it. Apparently, the shower head needs replacing, and the paint’s ‘slightly off-white’. It’s utter nonsense, trying to get extra money. Landlords! The bane of my existence. Honestly, they think they're doing you a favour by letting you live in their damp, crumbling properties. I had terrible trouble when I was Headmistress, renting a little cottage near the school. The man kept popping round unannounced. It was infuriating! It’s the money we need, though, isn't it? Everything's so expensive. And Mum needs a good care home, one where she’ll actually get some stimulation. Not just watched by someone scrolling on their phone. Exactly. We need to find somewhere decent, and that costs. I saw a place in Guildford, looked lovely but… the price! Guildford’s awfully fashionable. Pricey. You’d be better off looking a bit further afield. Perhaps somewhere in Surrey, but not  too  close to the town centre. I did bring some Scottish tablet, by the way. Thought it might be a nice wee treat after dinner. It's from that little shop in Edinburgh you like, Dad. Oh, brilliant! You remembered. That shop does the best tablet.

Right, I’m tellin’ ya, I’m proper fed up with beans on toast. It’s been a staple for… well, too long, innit? Oh, come on, Liam. You say that every week. It’s cheap and cheerful. Besides, you could, like,  spice  it up a bit. Add some cheese. Maybe some hot sauce? Honestly, the things you complain about. I’m livin’ off instant noodles most of the time. At least you’ve got beans. You’re still on the noodles, Anna? Thought you were trying to get a bit more… adventurous in the kitchen? Adventurous requires money, Mark. And time. Both of which are in short supply. Uni life, eh? It’s just… feels a bit pathetic, doesn’t it? A graduate livin’ at home, eatin’ beans on toast. Makes me feel like I’m goin’ nowhere. Don’t beat yourself up about it, love. The job market’s brutal. Remember what Sarah said? Her boyfriend’s got a degree and he's still deliverin’ pizzas. True. And plenty of people are stuck at home for longer than they’d like. It's not a sign of failure, Liam. More a sign of… the times. I know, I know. It's just...Mum keeps askin’ about applications. And Dad keeps makin’ subtle digs about "contributin’" more. Oh, parents. Mine ring up to ask if I’m "meeting nice boys". It’s infuriating. Like my entire worth is based on my relationship status. Mine are just obsessed with my coursework. "Are you studyin’ hard enough, love?" "Have you finished that essay yet?" Honestly, it's constant pressure. Least they’re interested, eh? My mam barely knows what course I did at college. She thinks I’m still just… helpin’ out at the primary school. It's not that I don’t appreciate them bein’ concerned. It's just… I feel like a disappointment. I was supposed to be off travelin’ the world, not stuck here. You will be, Liam! Once you get somethin’ sorted. And honestly, travelin’ the world costs a fortune. You’re better off savin’ up a bit first. Speaking of savin’ up, has anyone heard from Ben? He said he was lookin’ at flatshares in Newcastle. I messaged him yesterday. Said he’s viewin’ a couple of places this week. Seemed pretty optimistic. Apparently, there’s this one place with a massive kitchen. Which, knowing Ben, is his top priority.

Right, so I need to actually  make  the biscuits tomorrow, not just talk about it. Honestly, sometimes I think I spend more time planning lessons than actually  doing  the lessons. Can I help decorate? With the sprinkles? Lots and lots of sprinkles! And the icing! I want to put blue icing on mine. It'll be a monster biscuit! You absolutely can both help decorate. But first, we need to actually  have  biscuits to decorate. It’s for the Year 3s, remember? We're learning about following instructions, and then they get to eat the results. It’s genius, really. What are you doing in the lesson, Mummy? Are they being good? Well, usually. There's always one or two who decide the instructions are…suggestions. Last week, little Leo tried to build a tower out of the playdough  while  I was explaining how to make a simple shape. Leo’s silly! He is a bit. But sweet. Anyway, biscuits. We need a lot of biscuits. Maybe we should make a double batch? Can we have a half-birthday party for my teddy? He’s feeling a bit sad he didn't get a party on his real birthday. A half-birthday party for Bartholomew? That’s… actually a really good idea! We can have tiny biscuits for Bartholomew and his friends. Can I invite Rex? My dinosaur? Of course! Everyone’s invited to Bartholomew’s half-birthday. Right, back to biscuit logistics. I was at Morrisons earlier and I saw this amazing book – a pop-up dinosaur book! It was huge. You two would love it. Did you buy it? Not this time, it was a bit pricey. But I did get that Tomodachi Life guidebook I was looking for. Apparently, it tells you all the secret codes and how to get your Mii's to fall in love! Falling in love? In a game? Wow! It's all very complicated. Anyway, I also grabbed that book about space. The one with all the sparkly planets. Remember asking for that? Ooh, yes! The one with the black holes! Are black holes scary? They're a bit mysterious, aren't they? They suck everything in. But they're also really far away, so we don’t need to worry about being sucked into a black hole anytime soon. Good. I don’t want to be sucked into a black hole. I want to eat a monster biscuit!

Honestly, the state of Facebook these days. It's just… relentless. Every single person I knew from primary school is suddenly a life coach or selling protein powder. You've hit the nail on the head. It’s become a marketplace of aspiration, isn’t it? Everyone's presenting this hyper-curated version of their lives. I swear, if I see one more "manifest your dreams" post, I’m muting someone. It’s exhausting! And the arguments… remember when it was just for sharing photos of cats? Now it's full-blown political warfare in the comments. Dark days. I mostly use it now to keep an eye on Mum, to be honest. She's discovered groups dedicated to vintage china and spends hours debating the merits of different floral patterns. It's… endearing. Oh, that sounds perfectly Mum. Mine’s currently convinced she’s found a long-lost relative through one of those ancestry things. She's already planning a trip to Ireland. Oh, lovely! That's actually a good use of it, isn’t it? Connecting with family. Speaking of connections… did you see Old Man Hemmings’ car yesterday? Down by the bakery? Hemmings? The one with the ridiculously bright orange Rover? No! What was he doing with it? Still driving that thing, is he? Apparently. It was parked halfway up the pavement, hazard lights flashing. He was arguing with Mrs. Gable about having blocked her driveway. It was a glorious mess. The Rover looked… even more orange in the afternoon sun. Oh, that’s classic Hemmings. That car is a hazard to society. I genuinely thought he’d finally traded it in for something a bit more sensible. Maybe electric? Sensible and Hemmings don't really go hand in hand, do they? He reckons it’s a classic. Apparently, it’s appreciated in value. He showed me some online forum or other where people were offering him a fortune for it. Online forums? Oh dear. I bet those were the same people selling protein powder on Facebook. You can't trust anything you read on the internet, you know. It's all algorithms and bots and… …and orange Rovers. Don’t forget the orange Rovers. Honestly, sometimes I feel like we’re living in a simulation. Everything is just… heightened. Tell me about it. I spent an hour this morning trying to explain to a student why citing Wikipedia isn't acceptable academic practice.

Right, honestly, the day was  brutal . Old Mrs. Higgins was back, complaining about the price of the biscuits  again . Like, it’s printed on the packet! Ooooh! That was a big one! Do you think everyone's okay? Probably not, darling. It’s a cartoon. They bounce. Honestly, it’s the complaining that gets me. You’d think people had nothing better to worry about than 5p on a pack of Digestives. But she probably really likes Digestives. And 5p is like…a whole sweet! True, true. Speaking of which, are you actually eating those crisps or just… arranging them? You’ve barely touched them. I’m saving the ready salted for the end. These are cheese and onion. I’m building a city. See? This one’s the library, that one’s the…meatball factory. Brilliant. You've got a knack for that. Right, can you pass me the remote? I can’t reach it from here. Think I’ll flick through and see if there’s anything… less catastrophic on. Which button? There’s loads. The red one. No, the other red one. Top right. No, wait… the  silver  one, then red. It’s a nightmare this remote. Honestly, everything’s over-complicated these days. Got it! But I like it when it rains meatballs. It's so funny. Do you think the scientist should have stopped making them, though? Even if everyone liked them? That's… a really good question, actually. It's kind of like, what's more important, making people happy or being responsible? It’s a surprisingly deep film, for something about flying food. Is that what grown-ups talk about when they watch films? Like, the deep stuff? Sometimes. Although usually it's just… moaning about work. Which brings me back to Mrs. Higgins and the biscuits. And my boss breathing down my neck about sales targets. It's exhausting. She called me lazy... can you believe it? Lazy! That’s not fair! You work really hard. You’re studying  and  working. Thanks. It's just… draining. And I feel like I’m constantly having to justify myself. It’s like, if I don’t match some ideal of ‘productive’ then I’m worthless. That’s what Bethany was saying in feminism society. About how girls have to be seen as, like, always trying to achieve something, whereas boys can just  be . It’s rubbish.

So, another weekend gone, eh? Did you catch the match? Everton were… well, Everton. Catch it? Lad, I  live  for the match. Though living out here in Finland means a lot of dodgy streams and getting up at ungodly hours. They were shocking, weren’t they? Absolutely shocking. Looked like they hadn't bothered turning up in the first half. A recurring theme, sadly. Though, given the state of things generally, it hardly feels surprising to see a bit of listlessness, does it? I mean, look at the political landscape back home. Utter chaos. Chaos is an understatement, mate. It’s a right mess. Remember when Blair came in? Everyone was saying ‘New Labour, new hope!’ Real change, they promised. Look at it now. Seems like every politician's only in it for themselves. Exactly! And the hypocrisy is astounding. All that talk about the working class and then…well, look at the state of the country. The widening gap, the cuts... It’s disheartening, to say the least. Studied it for years, written papers on the rhetoric of New Labour, but even  I  underestimated how quickly it would all unravel. I remember voting for him, y’know. Thought he was the answer. He sounded alright, did Tony. Proper smooth talker. But then you see the wars, the dodgy dossiers… Started to smell a bit fishy, didn’t it? Incredibly fishy. And the way they spun it all! The language was masterful, deliberately ambiguous. Trying to appeal to everyone, meaning they appealed to no one effectively. It’s a fascinating subject for analysis, actually, that kind of political rhetoric. But as a citizen? It’s infuriating. Infuriating’s a good word for it. Makes you wonder what’s the point, y’know? I spend my days driving people around, listening to their gripes. Everyone’s feeling squeezed. The government’s obsessed with these… these ‘stakeholder’ initiatives. What even  is  a stakeholder? Sounds like something out of Dracula. A rather apt analogy, actually. It’s a buzzword designed to obscure accountability. It’s about shifting responsibility, distributing blame. "Oh, we consulted with all stakeholders." Meaning, they listened to everyone and did exactly what they wanted anyway. It's linguistic trickery. Trickery’s right. It's all trickery. And then they wonder why no one trusts them. They've lost touch with real people, the ones struggling to make ends meet. All these politicians in their fancy suits, talking about abstract concepts… They don't know a day in my life, driving around Liverpool in the rain.

Honestly, wading through those BNC recordings for the new project is  killing  me. It's just… so much beige. Like, conversation after conversation about the weather and what they had for tea. Oof, sounds grim. Still, at least you're getting paid to listen to people chat, right? Beats my Sunday, which is mostly staring at a Word document and aggressively editing semicolons. True, true. Though sometimes I fantasize about just chucking it all and becoming a professional dog walker. Specifically, pug walker. Imagine being surrounded by little wrinkly faces all day. You and your pugs! You’re obsessed. They're just so  comical . Anyway, have you updated your LinkedIn recently? I keep getting those "people you may know" suggestions, and half of them are people I actively avoided at uni. Briefly. Mostly to ignore the recruiters desperate for 'Content Creators' who apparently require a PhD in English Literature. It’s insulting, honestly. Social media just feels… exhausting these days. Everyone curating this perfect life. Tell me about it. I saw Amelia’s photos from the Maldives. Seriously? Turquoise water and cocktails at sunrise? Makes my rainy East London flat look particularly bleak. Oh, the Maldives. I was supposed to go there with… well, never mind. It’s a long story. But the thought of being on a tiny island surrounded by ocean just makes me panic. You and flying, eh? Still haven’t cracked that one? Nope. The idea of being suspended thousands of feet in the air in a metal tube… It’s my biggest fear. Honestly, I’d rather swim to Spain. That’s… ambitious. Though, if anyone could do it, it’d be you. You spent half your childhood swimming in the Welsh rivers, didn't you? She did! It’s true. Grew up practically amphibious. Speaking of Wales, are you still planning to visit your family soon? Next weekend, hopefully. Mum’s been going on about needing help with the garden. Which basically translates to 'sit and watch me prune roses while I complain about the neighbours.’ Sounds idyllic. I miss having a garden. Living in London, you forget what actual green spaces are like. Though, I’m thinking of trying to squeeze in a trip to Barcelona in the autumn. Oh, nice! Have you been before? No, never. Always wanted to go. A friend of mine lives there now, said it’s amazing. He’s trying to convince me to move.

Right, so I was thinking, maybe a fragrant rice with that? It’ll soak up all the sauce nicely. You’re chopping onions like a pro, by the way. Much faster than me. Years of practice, darling. Years of suppressing tears while chopping onions for demanding authors. It builds a certain…efficiency. How's the dissertation going? Still wrestling with post-structuralism? Wrestling is a good word for it. It feels less like active research and more like being pinned to the mat by Derrida. I had a breakthrough on Tuesday, though. Might actually finish the chapter by the end of the week. Excellent! See? You just need occasional breakthroughs. Speaking of breaks, have you thought any further about that tattoo? The one with the… constellations? Yeah, I did some more sketching. I think I want it to wrap around my forearm, instead of just being on the bicep. It feels…more subtle. Plus, I spoke to Ben, he knows a guy who does really good work, proper artist. Oh, Ben from the pub? Good. Don't go to one of those dodgy places with questionable hygiene. Seriously. Remember what happened to poor old Derek? Don’t remind me. Floral infection is  not  a good look. I’ve checked this guy’s portfolio, it’s solid. Anyway, what about you? Any news from the literary world? Still battling with interns who think ‘proofreading’ means running spellcheck? You know me too well. Honestly, the things I find. One of them suggested changing ‘metaphor’ to ‘similie’ because it "sounded more modern." I nearly had a stroke.  A door opens and another voice enters  Hello! Am I interrupting culinary artistry? Smells amazing in here. Liam! No, not at all. Just prepping dinner. Come on in, have a seat. Speaker_2 is telling me horror stories about her interns. Oh, the intern saga continues then. Classic. Honestly, you'd think universities taught basic grammar these days. Listen, I just wanted to quickly say hi, I’ve been completely swamped with Christmas lists. The publishers are demanding everything to be finalized by next week, it’s madness! Christmas already? It feels like October was five minutes ago. Are you surviving the festive push, Liam? Barely. Everyone's panicking about getting their books positioned for the Christmas market. It’s all “must-have gifts” and “perfect stocking fillers.” Honestly, sometimes I think I'm selling scented candles, not literature.

Right, so I think this needs a  bit  more chilli powder, don’t you? It's looking a little…pale. Mmm, yeah, definitely. Not enough kick. And maybe a squeeze of lime? It'll brighten the flavours up. Oh, and have you seen my new trainers? Lime, good shout. And  no , I haven't seen your trainers. Are they the bright orange ones you were eyeing up online? The very same. They arrived this morning. I wore them to pilates. Honestly, they’re a game changer. Apparently, they're supposed to help with your form. Pilates? Brave you. I tried it once. Ended up feeling like I’d been run over by a bus for three days. Oh, it’s intense, I won’t lie. But Gemma – you know, from book club – she’s a proper pilates convert. She says it’s done wonders for her back. Speaking of Gemma, she went to Morocco last month. Said it was incredible. Morocco! Oh, I've always wanted to go. Is it…safe? I keep hearing mixed things. She said it was fine, she went with a small group tour, which she’d recommend. Apparently, the markets are insane – like, a total sensory overload, but in the best way. And the food…she kept raving about the tagines. Tagines sound amazing. I tried making one once, but it was a complete disaster. The chicken was dry, and the spices were all wrong. Oh no! It’s a tricky one. You need to really let it simmer, don't you? Low and slow. I’ve got a recipe from my auntie, she used to live in Marrakech for a year. I could send it over? That would be amazing, actually! Thank you. I’m trying to broaden my repertoire, you know? I feel like I make the same five dinners on repeat. It’s so boring. I know the feeling. I'm stuck in a rut with pasta. It's just…easy. But I'm trying to be better. That’s why I signed up for the cookery class. Oh, how is that going? It’s fun! Last week we made sushi, which was…challenging. I'm pretty sure mine looked like a small, ricey explosion. But the instructor was really patient. It’s a good way to force yourself to learn new skills. Absolutely. You're always so good at picking up new things.

Honestly, the student feedback this year is… something else. I’m getting a real mixed bag. Some of them are genuinely engaging, asking insightful questions, and then you get the ones who clearly haven’t read a single assigned reading. Tell me about it. I had one student email me last week, asking for a summary of the entire module… two weeks before the exam. Two weeks! It's just… the entitlement, sometimes. Do you think it's a generational thing? Maybe. Or maybe it’s just the pressure they’re under. Everyone’s so focused on getting the ‘right’ qualifications to get the ‘right’ job. It’s all very… transactional. Remember when we were at uni, it felt a bit more about actually  learning ? Nostalgia’s a powerful thing, isn’t it? Though I do recall a lot of all-nighters fuelled by instant noodles and questionable life choices. Still, you're right. It feels different now. Speaking of different… did you see Sarah’s photos from her trip to Bali? Oh, yes! Absolutely stunning. She looks so relaxed. She really needed that break. She was completely frazzled after dealing with… well, everything. How  is  Mark, actually? She didn’t say much in her messages, just that things were ‘complicated’. Complicated is putting it mildly. Apparently, he's decided he needs to “find himself” which, as far as I can tell, involves learning to surf and documenting it all on Instagram. It’s… a bit much. She’s trying to be supportive, but I think she’s secretly furious. Oh, that’s dreadful. Poor Sarah. He always struck me as a bit… flighty. Remember that time he tried to start a kombucha business and then gave up after two weeks because “it smelled funny”? Oh god, yes! The Kombucha King. He’s brilliant at starting things, absolutely hopeless at finishing them. It’s exhausting just  being  around him. I feel terrible for Sarah. She deserves someone a bit more… grounded. Absolutely. And she's such a rock for everyone else. It's not fair. Oh! I nearly forgot. I ended up having to cut Amelia’s toenails for her yesterday. She’d bent over backwards trying to do them herself and couldn't reach! Oh,  no . That sounds… uncomfortable for everyone involved. Is she okay? Perfectly fine. She's surprisingly ticklish. It was a whole operation involving a magnifying glass and me pretending to be a professional podiatrist.

Honestly, I’m shattered. That spin class nearly killed me. I feel like my legs are going to fall off. You and me both. I thought I was fitter than I am. Old age creeping up, you know? Though, to be fair, I haven’t done a proper spin class in… well, ages. It's brutal. But good brutal, right? Clears the head. Speaking of clearing heads, did you catch that documentary about… well, it was a bit out there, but about the simulation theory? Oh,  that  one. My brother was going on about it for weeks. Something about us all living in a computer program? Sounds a bit… dramatic, doesn’t it? Dramatic, yes. But fascinating! He made some really interesting points about glitches in reality. Like, have you ever had that feeling of déjà vu, so strong it feels… wrong? Right, yeah, I have. But I just put that down to a lack of sleep or too much coffee. My wife, Sarah, thinks it’s all nonsense. She's much more grounded. She was watching one of those royal documentaries last night – the one about Charles and Diana. That was a drama of a different kind. Oh, I saw trailers for that. It looks intense. Sarah’s your wife… how’s the planning going for the anniversary? Is the big party still on? It’s… complicated. We were thinking a big bash, you know, invite everyone. But then Sarah started worrying it would be too much fuss, too stressful. She's rather low-key, my wife. I’m trying to convince her a small gathering with close friends and family is a good compromise. It's twenty years, you know? Should be celebrated. Definitely. Twenty years is a milestone. You’ve got to do something. You’re good together, though. I always think you two are really solid. Which is amazing, considering how hectic your job is. How's work going, anyway? Still juggling a million things at once? Always. We're launching a new product line next month, so it's all hands on deck. Endless meetings, presentations, the usual. It’s rewarding, but exhausting. Though, funnily enough, I had a conversation with one of the younger employees the other day, and he was saying how much he values flexible working. Made me think about how different things are now compared to when I started out. It's true.

Dad, are we nearly there yet? Seriously, my legs are going numb. Nearly, love, nearly. Cornwall’s a long way from Manchester, you know. We’ve still got a good few hours yet, mind. Look out the window, though. Isn't the countryside lovely? All those shades of green. It’s…green. Yeah. It all looks a bit samey after a while. Did you see that weird purple flower back near the motorway? What  was  that? Probably heather. Getting a bit early for full bloom, but you get patches. Yorkshire Moorland's covered in it. Reminds me of  Jamaica Inn , actually. Have you read that, by Daphne du Maurier? Isn't that the spooky one? With the smugglers? Mrs. Davies at school made us read bits in English. It was…okay. Bit slow. I prefer stuff like Sherlock Holmes. Sherlock Holmes is good. Your Grandma used to love Sherlock Holmes. She'd read them aloud, doing all the voices. Remember? She did a brilliant Mycroft. Vaguely. I was little. Did you ever try learning Morse Code, like in those old films? Sending messages with a torch? Oh, aye! Back when I was a lad, me and your Uncle Barry tried to. Couldn’t get past ‘dit dit dit, dah dah dah’ for SOS. It's a bit different to texting, eh? Imagine having to tap out a message in dots and dashes just to ask someone what they're having for tea! Imagine having to send a  telegram ! Like, paying someone to write a really short message and deliver it. So slow! Slower than the post! Before telegrams, you had to rely on letters. Took weeks to get a reply from Australia. And before that…well, birds with messages tied to their legs, I suppose. Seriously? Like in fairy tales? Well, not exactly. But people  did  use carrier pigeons. And they had signal fires, flashing messages across hills. It's all about communication, innit? Even these wind turbines, they're kind of like giant signals, telling us we're trying to use cleaner energy. Look at those ones over there. Massive things. They’re kind of creepy, though. Like giant, slow-moving robots. Are we stopping for petrol soon? I need chocolate. Urgently. We stop at the next services. Got a tenner for you for the sweet shop. Now, about directions… I think we take the A30 after Exeter, but I don’t want to rely on my memory.

Honestly, this Victoria sponge is  amazing , Gran. You’ve outdone yourself. Aye, well, a woman needs a hobby, doesn't she? Keeps the hands busy. Though back in my day, we didn't have all these fancy electric mixers. Everything was done by arm power, let me tell ya. Strong arms I had, mind. Used to shift coal, you see, during the war. Speaking of shifts, my project’s been absolutely mental this week. Had to rewrite half the code because of… well, let’s just say someone didn’t quite understand the brief. Oh, no. Not another one? Who was it this time? Mark. He’s a good lad, really, just… a bit enthusiastic. And occasionally skips reading the documentation. It’s infuriating. I swear, sometimes I feel like I’m back in primary school, explaining things to someone who’s deliberately trying not to understand. Primary school, eh? Mine was a right pickle. Miss Higgins, she was called. Kept threatening to cane us for the smallest thing. Though she was a kind soul underneath, I suppose. Different times, eh? During the war, we had air raid drills every day. Used to hide under our desks. Terrifying for a little lad. Crikey, that must have been scary. I can’t even imagine. It’s completely different now. My biggest worry is finding a decent petrol station on the way to Bristol. They’re all charging a fortune these days. Fifty quid to fill up a tank – it’s robbery! Robbery indeed! Back in my day, petrol was tuppence ha’penny. And you could get into the cinema for sixpence! Sixpence! Now they’re charging a tenner a ticket? It’s scandalous. It is. I haven’t been to the cinema in ages. Too expensive. Although, I did see a listing for a drive-in cinema near Yeovil. Thought that might be fun. A drive-in? That’s a bit retro, isn’t it? That’s the point! It’s different. Speaking of different, I was looking at swimming the Channel. Swimming the Channel?! You? Have you lost your marbles, lass? It’s freezing cold! And teeming with jellyfish! I know, I know. It's just a thought. It would be… a challenge. I’ve been doing a bit more running lately, trying to get fit. Good for you. I’ve been meaning to start exercising again. Lockdown really did a number on my routine.

Right, so I’ve made a start on the list for stuff you want taking to the new place. It’s… longer than I anticipated. Oh dear. I knew it would be, wouldn't I? Thirty years in a house… things accumulate. Did I put the good china on there? The Wedgewood? Yeah, it’s on here. Under ‘Fragile – Handle with Extreme Care’ which felt appropriate. It’s quite a hefty box, actually. I nearly dropped it just  looking  at it. Good. That needs looking after. Your grandmother gave me that, you know. She was so proud of it. Oh, and the silver? Did you put the silver cutlery down? Silver’s all accounted for. It's in a separate, padded box, labelled ‘Valuable - Do Not Bend’. I'm trying to be thorough. Though I’m already regretting offering to do this. My flat’s looking like a storage unit. Oh, don’t be like that. I’m terribly grateful. Honestly, I don’t know how I’d manage without you. Jet lag's still hitting me, you know? Even a short flight to Malaga knocks me for six these days. My memory isn’t what it used to be, either. I walked into the kitchen earlier and completely forgot why. Malaga sounds nice, though. Did you have a good time with Auntie Brenda? Oh, lovely. She’s getting on well, considering. Still talking about that man from the bowls club. Says he reminds her of your grandfather. Can you imagine? And she’s convinced he’s got a secret stash of weaver fish. Weaver fish? Seriously? That’s what she says! Apparently, they're a delicacy. She’s proper fixated. Anyway, back to the house. I was thinking, that little table in the hallway, the one with the marble top… you don't think it'd look right in your flat, do you? It's rather… ornate. I could probably squeeze it in. I've got that little alcove by the front door. It might actually look quite good. It's better than it just sitting in a storage unit somewhere, right? I was talking to Liam last week, by the way. He asked after you. Oh, lovely. Give him my love. Is he still…seeing that Sarah? The one who works at the library? Yeah, they're still going strong. Actually, they’re talking about getting married. Oh, how wonderful!

Right, honestly, that presenter is  awful . Just rambling. Is this about the A-Level reforms again? Yeah, they’re having another go at explaining it. It’s a mess, isn’t it? All this talk about de-coupling and making things more flexible… feels like they’re just making it harder for kids from state schools, if I’m honest. Completely. My cousin’s just started her A-Levels, and she’s already stressed about knowing which subjects are ‘facilitating’ and which aren’t. It’s ridiculous pressure at sixteen. It is. Remember when it was just… do your A-Levels, get the grades, go to uni? Simple. Now it’s a strategic game of subject selection. Speaking of stressful, have you seen the petrol queues? Oh, don't even  start . I drove past three stations on the way back from the library, and they were all rammed. People are panicking over nothing. It just shows how quickly things can unravel, doesn’t it? Like the NHS, honestly. Exactly. The NHS is constantly on the brink, and a little bit of disruption and everyone loses their minds. It’s terrifying. Speaking of things needing attention… look at that poor fern. It’s looking a bit peaky. Oh, the fern! I keep forgetting to mist it. I've been so busy with the research this week. It's just… endless data sets. You need to delegate more, babe. You’re going to burn out. I know you like being hands-on, but you’ve got a team, use them. I know, I know. It’s hard to let go sometimes, you know? Especially when you’re the one who understands all the nuances. Right, I'll give it a proper misting later. It's just… it was thriving when we first got it. Remember? All lush and green? I do. It matched your hair, actually. Speaking of hair… you thinking about changing it again? Saw a really cool layered bob on Instagram this morning. Oh, now you’re talking! Maybe. I was thinking something a bit shorter… but I don’t want to go  too  drastic. I liked having some length to tie back when I'm coding. True. Practicality is key with research. Although, a bit of a change might do you good. You've been looking a bit… academic lately. Oh, very funny. And you’ve been looking like you haven’t slept in days thanks to that PhD.

Right, so I genuinely think I’m gonna have to get a job this term. Like,  actually  get a job. Not just a few shifts here and there. Oof, that’s rough. Uni’s expensive, though, innit? What are you thinking of doing? Retail? God, probably. Or maybe a bar job. Anything where I can just…exist and get paid a tiny bit. I hate the thought of it, honestly. All my free time, gone. Though, thinking about it, more money  does  mean more nights out…it’s a vicious cycle. Tell me about it. I’m seriously considering picking up more hours at the library. It’s mind-numbingly boring, shelving books and dealing with weirdos, but it pays. And I need to save for that trip to Amsterdam next summer. Amsterdam! Oh my god, I’m so jealous. I’m currently subsisting on instant noodles and regret. I spent all my loan on, well, let's just say questionable choices. And too many textbooks I didn't actually need. Oh, classic. We’ve all been there. Remember that time Liam bought a textbook on the Black Plague thinking it’d be relevant to his History essay and then…didn’t even open it? Oh god yes! He was convinced it was gonna give him some kind of edge. “Think about the societal implications!” he said. Ended up writing about the Tudors. Speaking of societal implications… I was reading this article for my sociology essay, about the history of smoking and how it used to be seen as sophisticated and glamorous. Now it's like, practically illegal and totally frowned upon. It’s just fascinating how perspectives change. It's mad, isn’t it? Like, my grandma used to smoke  everywhere . Even in the hospital after I was born! Can you imagine? Now you can't even light up outside a pub without getting a lecture. It’s also really interesting when you look at it through a feminist lens. The tobacco companies actively targeted women with campaigns specifically designed to make smoking “liberating”. Like,  that's  empowerment? Selling you a deadly addiction? Totally. It's a really cynical exploitation of emerging ideas about female freedom. Which links back to so much advertising actually. Always playing on insecurities, you know? It's awful. It makes you question everything. Like, even when brands try to be ‘woke’ now, are they actually doing it because they care, or just because it's good for their image?

Honestly, this coastline is breathtaking. Makes you forget about all the… life admin, doesn't it? It really does. Though my brain keeps wandering back to Sarah, actually. I've been meaning to talk to you about it. Sarah? Oh, right. You mentioned things were a bit… strained last time we spoke. What's going on? It's just… I think I'm done. Properly done. With the friendship. But I have absolutely no idea how to navigate that without causing a massive explosion. We've been friends since uni, you know? It feels awful. I get it. That longevity makes it so much harder. It’s not like a work colleague you just gradually stop chatting to. It feels… intentional. Like a failure, almost. Exactly! And she’s one of those people who’s  really  good at making you feel guilty. Any tiny attempt at creating distance is met with a wounded ‘Oh, so you don’t want to see me anymore?’ Oh, the guilt trip specialist. I know that type. It's exhausting. Have you tried just… slowly reducing contact? The fade-out method? I've attempted it. But it doesn’t feel natural with her. She's not someone who just  lets  things be. She needs reasons, explanations, grand declarations. Honestly, I'd rather wrestle a bear. Okay, avoiding the dramatic confrontation is sensible. Maybe… focus on being genuinely busy? Say you've taken up a new hobby that takes up a lot of your evenings or weekends. A pottery class, a language exchange, anything. I’ve tried the busy excuse. She immediately offered to come  with  me to the pottery class. Said she’s always wanted to try it. Oh, no. The ultimate friendship cling. Right, okay. That’s… dedicated. Maybe you need a slightly firmer, but still kind, approach. Like, ‘Look, Sarah, I’m really enjoying focusing on some personal things right now and I need a little space. It doesn’t mean I don’t value our history, but I just need to recharge.’ Something along those lines. That sounds… calmer than anything I’ve managed to formulate in my head. But what if she asks  why ? That’s the killer. She’ll dissect it and find an issue with everything. You don't  have  to give her a fully itemized list of grievances. 'I'm just feeling a need for some space' is a complete sentence.

Honestly, this shepherd’s pie is amazing, Nana. You’ve really outdone yourself. Oh, pooh, it’s just a bit of lamb and potato, darling. Nothing fancy. Though, I did use a dash of nutmeg in the mash, that’s the secret. More flavour, you see. Secret’s safe with me. So, how was your week? Did you get much painting done? A little. I’ve been wrestling with this landscape. Trying to capture the light on the Tuscan hills. It’s proving difficult. It’s never quite  right . You know how it is. I can imagine. Sounds beautiful though. Still planning that trip back to Italy next spring? Oh, absolutely! I’ve already started looking at flights. Perhaps we could join me this time? It’s been far too long since you’ve been. That would be incredible, honestly. University’s been… demanding, to say the least. A bit of Italian sunshine sounds like exactly what I need. Though, I’ve got to finish this dissertation first. Of course, of course. School first. What are you writing about this time? Something to do with Shakespeare? Last I heard you were buried in  Hamlet . Actually, I switched focus. I’m doing it on the Pre-Raphaelites, specifically how their work was a reaction against Victorian industrialisation. Oh! Now  that  is interesting! Very interesting. They were a wonderful group. Rossetti, Millais… such romanticism, such detail. Have you been to the Tate Britain recently? They had a rather lovely collection on display. I haven’t, no. Been a bit tied up. But I’ll definitely add it to my list. Actually, Aunt Clara sent me a book on them, for my birthday. She knew I’d be into it. Your Aunt Clara always has good taste. She’s got that artistic eye, just like your grandfather. Speaking of, have you spoken to your cousin Leo recently? He called me last week, said he was applying for a grant to film a documentary in Peru. Leo! No way. That’s… classic Leo. Always chasing the next big adventure. I texted him a couple of days ago, just a quick check-in. He’s always so busy. He is. He gets that from his father, I think. Always had to be doing  something . Still, Peru! That’s quite a journey. Are you worried about him going so far? A little, yeah. But he’s prepared.

Honestly, I feel a bit silly even  thinking  about the gym after that pierogi feast last night. It’s going to be…a commitment. You’ll be fine. You always say that. And you always go. It's your coping mechanism, isn't it? Punishing yourself for enjoying food? No! That’s… harsh. It's not punishing. It’s… balancing. Maintaining. You know, the whole life thing. Right, balancing. And how’s the driving going? Still feeling okay? It’s a long stretch to Tarnow, even on these roads. Yeah, I’m alright. Bit tired, actually. I think I underestimated how draining all this is, even  with  you doing most of the navigating. Keeps looking at the time. Honestly, where does it go? Feels like we only just left Białka. Time is weird when you're travelling. Especially in a campervan. It's like it compresses and stretches all at once. Still, Tarnow’s a nice little town. Supposedly, it used to be a major centre for rose oil. Rose oil? Fancy that. So, you’ve been teaching all morning? How were the students? It was okay. A bit of the usual. One kid kept trying to explain Brexit to me, like  I  didn’t already know. Honestly, it's exhausting having to constantly…re-explain things. Especially to people who think being English automatically makes you a political expert. Oh, the burden of being British. I know that feeling. It’s always ‘So, what do  you  think about…?’ followed by a pre-judged expectation of what your answer will be. Exactly! And it’s always a loaded question. It's even worse when they ask about football. Oh god, don’t even get me started. It's just… a constant negotiation of national identity, isn't it? Pretty much. It’s funny, though. I was talking to one of my female students yesterday, and she was saying how surprised she was that I, as a woman, was so direct in my teaching style. Apparently, she's used to male teachers who are more... deferential. Deferential? Oh, that’s… interesting. Typical. She said it was refreshing, actually. But it got me thinking about how often women are expected to be agreeable, even when they’re the ones in charge. It's insidious, isn’t it? That subtle expectation of softness. It is. It’s everywhere. At work, in social situations… it’s tiring to constantly be aware of it, and to navigate around it.

This mug’s lovely, isn’t it? Properly hand-thrown, you can feel the difference. Not like those mass-produced ones. Aye, lovely. Though I still prefer a nice thin one, for me tea. These are a bit…substantial. Do you put milk in, dear? You always forget to ask. I do, a little. Just a splash. It’s still surprisingly warm for October, isn't it? Proper Indian summer. Keeps the spiders busy, I reckon. Saw a big one in the bathroom this morning. Nearly gave me heart failure. Oh, don't! I’m terrible with spiders. Though, I suppose they’re doing a good job, keeping the flies down. Speaking of which, the roses are still flowering – absolutely ridiculous for this time of year. I really should get the beds cleared before the frost hits. You and your gardening! Always something to do, isn't there? You’ll wear yourself to a frazzle. Remember old Mrs. Higgins? She used to say a garden is a mistress, and a demanding one at that. She did, didn’t she? She was a character. Still, it's a good distraction. Less time to fret. Though, I did nearly fret myself silly last Tuesday. What happened? Not another tumble in the garden? Worse, actually. The power went off, right in the middle of marking essays. Everything just…died. Computer, lights, the lot. Felt like going back to the Stone Age. Oh, those power cuts! Used to get them all the time when I were a lass, living out in the sticks. You'd have to light candles and tell stories. Though, nowadays, it's more inconvenient than romantic. Did you manage to salvage your work? Eventually. The laptop had some battery left, luckily. But it was touch and go for a bit. Reminded me of what happened to Brenda last month. Oh, Brenda and her kitchen? The one with the…the mishap? That's the one. Apparently, she tripped over the cat while carrying a kettle of boiling water. Dreadful! Burns to her arm. Poor thing. She’s recovering now, but she's still very shaken. Oh, dear me! Cats are a menace, really. Though, I do love watching the birds in your garden, they're lovely. That robin's been back again, hasn't he? He has. Little bold thing, comes right up to the window. I've been meaning to get some more birdseed, it’s nearly empty.

Right, so, like, are we  definitely  going to Cornwall this year? It's just… everyone else is going to Spain or Greece or somewhere, and Cornwall feels a bit… lame, doesn't it? Lame, darling? Cornwall is beautiful! You know your Dad’s always wanted to go back to St. Ives. And honestly, after the year we’ve had, I just want somewhere easy. No stressful airport queues, no worrying about passports… just the car and a cream tea. Easy’s good. I’m with your Mum on that one, Liv. I’ve had enough stress with trying to get gigs lately, the last thing I need is a fraught holiday. Plus, remember Mrs. Trevithick from next door last year? She went to Majorca and had her purse nicked. Cornwall’s far safer, I reckon. I know, I know, it's safer. It’s just… Chloe’s going to Zante with all her mates, and they’ll have like, boat parties and sunbeds and loads of stuff to post on Insta… I just don’t want to be stuck looking at grey skies and pasties. Oh, don't be silly. We’ll have lots of things to post! We can get you some nice pictures on the beach, maybe a surfing lesson? They do those around Newquay. And we'll be getting pasties, of course – you know you love a good Cornish pasty! Aye, and we can visit the Eden Project! I heard it’s quite impressive. It's a bit touristy, mind you, but it's good to see something different. Hmm. Is old man Hemmings going to be there? He always finds us when we go to Cornwall. It’s so embarrassing. Oh, Hemmings! He does have a knack for appearing. He always says he “just happens” to be in the same café as us. We'll just have to be strategic with our café choices this year. He's a good lad, Hemmings. Bit of a chatterbox, but harmless. He used to come to my gigs back in Widnes, you know. Always asking for requests… usually sea shanties. Sea shanties? Seriously? Aye! He’s a bit of a romantic, that one. Loves a good yarn about the sea. Well, hopefully, we won’t see  too  much of him. We need to catch up on some proper relaxing. Oh, I must remember to ask Sarah how her holiday with the girls went.

Oh my god, that film was  so  good! Heath Ledger, seriously… swoon. I know, right? Like, Patrick Verona is the blueprint. Though, I think Kat was a bit harsh, honestly. He wasn't  that  bad. Harsh? He literally paid her to go out with him! That's… questionable, to say the least. But yeah, he did redeem himself. Did you see the poem he wrote? Ugh, the poem! I rewound it like three times. Okay, but enough about dreamy fictional boys. We have actual school to complain about. Mr. Davies is  determined  to make us all fail history, I swear. Tell me about it! His tests are impossible. I studied for like, five hours last night and I still didn't recognise half the dates. It's just… remembering stuff. I’m terrible at just  remembering  stuff. I'm better at understanding the actual events, but just writing them down in the right order... ugh. It’s so stressful. Do you think we should try and form a study group? Maybe quiz each other? That’s actually a really good idea! We could meet at mine on Wednesday? My mum’s already nagging me about revising anyway, so it'd be a good excuse to actually  do  it. Perfect. Wednesday works. Oh! Speaking of excuses… have you thought any more about asking your parents about the London trip? I’ve been dropping hints, but they’re being super vague. Like, “We’ll see” and “Maybe if your grades are good.” It’s so frustrating! I really want to go to that exhibition at the V&A. The one on fashion through the ages? Ooh, that sounds amazing! My mum said she'd be happy to drive us, as long as we promise to behave. And maybe do some cultural stuff, not just shopping. Behave? We are  always  well-behaved!… Mostly. And yes, we can do cultural stuff. We could go to a museum, or a play… or even… wait for it… a  historical  site! To impress Mr. Davies. You are ridiculous. But a museum sounds good. Maybe the British Museum? They have everything there. And we  have  to go to a cute cafe, though. That's non-negotiable. Deal. Okay, operation ‘Convince Our Parents London Trip’ is officially a go. We need a plan. A detailed plan. Maybe a PowerPoint presentation? A PowerPoint presentation is… excessive. But I appreciate the enthusiasm. Let’s just start with lists.

Right mess you’ve made of this sugar bowl, Margaret. Looks like a bomb’s hit it. Oh, honestly, Arthur! Just a little spill. And you're the one who insisted on using Grandma’s best china for a Tuesday afternoon cuppa. It's a beautiful set, though, isn’t it? I always remember admiring it as a kid. It is lovely. A bit much for everyday, perhaps, but lovely. So, Mum, how’s Facebook going? Still getting bombarded with political arguments? Don’t even  mention  Facebook. It’s dreadful. Old school friends posting about everything, all the time. And the arguments… honestly, it’s like a digital shouting match. I nearly had a row with Brenda over Brexit again yesterday. Brexit! Still at it, are they? Bunch of nonsense, the lot of it. Waste of time. You’ve avoided it, haven’t you, Dad? You always said you weren’t one for getting involved. Sensible, I am. Sensible. Now, speaking of nonsense, did you see young Timothy’s post this morning? All about his ‘spiritual journey’. Honestly. He’s going through a phase, Arthur. Leave him be. He’s a good boy. Trying to find himself, that's all. It’s just… the way he’s talking about crystals and energy fields. It’s a bit much. It's a bit like when I had chickenpox as a kid. Mum was convinced it was a sign of something… divine. She was reading all sorts of things. Well, it  was  a particularly bad case of chickenpox! And Mrs. Higgins swore blind her auntie used lavender to ward off evil spirits. You take things seriously when your child is poorly. Lavender. Ha! Used to grow it in the garden. Smelled nice, though. Pointless, of course. Just a flower. Like all this 'energy' nonsense. I think sometimes people just need something to believe in, Dad. Something outside of… everything. I think with Timothy, it’s partly tied to his anxiety. He gets really fixated on things. He’s mentioned it’s getting worse, actually. Almost… obsessive. Obsessive? Like… how? Just little things. Checking the door’s locked repeatedly. Arranging things in a certain order. He thinks it’s just being organised, but he’s worried it's becoming… more than that. Sounds like my cousin Edgar. Had to have everything just so. Drove his wife mad. Terrible. Used to spend hours polishing the doorknobs.

Honestly, I’m still dreaming of that little bakery in Bruges. The smell of the chocolate… absolute heaven. Did anyone else manage to snag a box of those biscuits I told you about? Oh, the speculoos? Yes! I got a big box. They didn't last long, though, I warn you. Ben practically inhaled them. Bruges was lovely, wasn't it? A bit…chocolate-centric, perhaps? But nice. Though getting Ms. Eleanor to navigate those cobbled streets was a military operation. You're telling me. She was convinced we were going the wrong way half the time, even with the sat nav! She’s a force of nature, that woman. Speaking of navigation… remember Dad trying to drive in Germany? That was a sight. He insisted on trying to read the road signs in… well, whatever language that was. Oh, don’t even  start  with that. It wasn’t German, it was just Dad making noises that sounded vaguely Teutonic. He thought he was being helpful! We ended up going around in circles for an hour. I remember! And he kept saying “Jawohl!” to every single person, even the petrol station attendant who clearly hadn’t a clue what he was saying. He thought he was being incredibly polite. He’s always been… enthusiastic. Remember when he tried to learn Italian before our trip to Rome? He just learned how to order spaghetti and kept repeating it to everyone we met. "Spaghetti! Spaghetti!" It's amazing the things he remembers. He can't recall what he had for breakfast but he can flawlessly recite that phrase. Honestly, he’s a character. He always was. Do you remember when he tried to fix Mrs. Higgins' car? The whole bonnet was off and he had no idea what he was doing. Oh, bless him. He thought he was a mechanic for a week. Poor Mrs. Higgins nearly had a heart attack. She ended up calling a proper mechanic, who just stared at everything Dad had 'improved' and then quoted her an astronomical price. He’s got a good heart, though. Always willing to help, even if he makes a complete mess of things. Though I do think his attempts at DIY should be outlawed. Absolutely. Though I did hear him telling Mum last week he was thinking about taking up plumbing. Oh no. Please, no. We’ll be living in a flood zone if he does that.

So, have you been to any good gigs recently? Anything beyond the usual pub stuff? Not really, no. Been too busy slinging food, honestly. Though Old Man Hemmings was banging on about this band, ‘Static Bloom’, played down the Cavern last week. Said they were proper good, a bit like early Arctic Monkeys but with… more synth, apparently? You heard of ‘em? Static Bloom? Vaguely. I think I saw something on Spotify. They're alright, yeah. A bit overhyped, maybe. I’ve been properly obsessed with ‘The Static Waves’ new album, though. It’s a total shift from their last one. Much more… atmospheric. Oh yeah, seen the posters. Never really got into them, to be honest. Too polished for me. Give me something raw, you know?
