Like, I was watching some old footage of The Clash the other day and just… the energy. Properly inspiring. Definitely. They were incredible. I’ve been trying to get back into drumming, actually. My kit's been gathering dust in me nan's garage for ages. Oh, cool! Still got the chops? Haha, debatable. It’s mostly just remembering where everything  goes  at this point. Think I need to find a space to practice, though. Nan’s not exactly thrilled about the noise. Tell me about it. Mum nearly had a fit when I was learning guitar. Said it sounded like a strangled cat. It did, to be fair. Have you heard from Liam? Still trying to get that internship at the studio in Bristol? Yeah, spoke to him last week. He had an interview. Apparently, it went alright. He’s waiting to hear back. He’s pretty stressed about it, obviously. It’s a really competitive field. Yeah, it is. He's good though, really talented. He deserves it. What about you? Any luck with applications? Still aiming for that marketing placement in London? I’ve sent out a few more. Nothing concrete yet. It’s a bit daunting, to be honest. Everyone seems to want experience, but how do you  get  experience without someone giving you a chance in the first place? It’s a classic catch-22. Tell me about it. It's the same in the kitchen. Everyone wants a chef with five years' experience, but you have to start somewhere, don't you? Actually, old Mr. Peterson at the pub is looking for a kitchen porter. It’s not glamorous, but it’s a foot in the door.

Honestly, this place is  rammed . I didn’t realise it got so busy on a Tuesday afternoon. And the noise! It’s like a school dinner hall in here. It’s alright, Mam. Just a bit…much. Is this where you wanted to meet Mrs. Henderson, though? Seems a bit loud for a proper chat. I thought it was convenient. Right off the A1, easy for her coming from Durham. And I needed a coffee, desperately. Double espresso, I think. This marking is draining me. Did you remember to write down everything for the shopping list? We’re properly running out of milk. Yeah, it’s on my phone. Milk, bread, sausages, those weird posh biscuits you like…anything else? Ooh, good lad. And some more of that fruit squash. Your father drinks it like it’s going out of fashion. Honestly, the amount of sugar… it’s a wonder he’s still bouncing about. Speaking of bouncing about, did you see that clip of that lad falling off the inflatable obstacle course online? Hilarious. Yeah, Jacob sent it to me. Proper wiped out. He said it reminded him of Mr. Thompson trying to do the hurdles in PE. Oh, don’t you start! That man was a legend. Remember old domino drives at the community centre? He always tried to cheat. He did! And kept complaining about the people in the drive-through blocking up the car park. Every. Single. Week. He was a character, alright. I suppose it’s good to have a bit of excitement. Although, honestly, I’m just looking forward to a quiet week. What are your plans for the summer holiday, have you thought about it any more? I’m still trying to convince Ben and Liam to go camping. But they’re both saying it’s “uncool”. Camping is brilliant! Fresh air, stargazing… although, remembering last time, we  need  to get new sleeping bags. And maybe a proper airbed. Your back was killing you on that thin roll mat. It was awful. I felt every single stone. And it rained the whole time. Well, that’s camping! It builds character. Speaking of character, did you hear about Old Man Hemmings down the street? Apparently, he’s starting a business… selling refurbished garden furniture. Seriously? That’s… ambitious. It is, isn’t it? An entrepreneur at 70! Good for him. Although, knowing him, it’ll all fall apart after a week.

Right, so this place is… smaller than I imagined from the photos, but definitely cosier. It suits you, actually. Bit more… lived-in than your student digs were. Cheers. It's a bit of a project, to be honest. Still got boxes everywhere, as you can see. And the flat above, seems to be filled with a family of elephants, honestly. You can hear  everything . Ah, the joys of flat living. Remember old Mrs. Higgins banging on our ceiling because we were “disturbing the peace” playing The Strokes at 2 am? Oh god, don’t remind me! That woman was terrifying. Anyway, how are things? Last I heard, you were… entrenched in the world of teaching, correcting dangling participles and all that? Still am. It’s alright. It pays the bills, allows me to indulge in overpriced craft beer and, you know, pay for the privilege of having you visit. I’m actually doing some recording for a linguistics project at the moment, trying to catalogue regionalisms. It's fascinating, actually. Oh, really? What sort of stuff? You'll need to get me on tape, my Brummie is a dying art, you know. People think it’s all about saying ‘bah’ instead of ‘bath’, but there’s so much more to it. Exactly! That’s the surface level. I’m interested in the subtle shifts in grammar, the specific colloquialisms… It’s amazing how much variation there is, even within a relatively small area. Speaking of changes… massive news, mate. Sarah and I are expecting. No way! Seriously? Sarah’s pregnant? That’s brilliant! Congratulations! That’s… huge. Yeah, it’s a bit of a shock, to be honest. We found out a couple of weeks ago. We’re both a bit overwhelmed, but mostly excited. Wow. Wow. When's the due date? Are you… have you started thinking about names? Tiny humans and all that. October. It feels ages away, but I know it’ll fly by. Names… that's a battlefield right now. Sarah’s got a list a mile long, I’m mostly just trying to veto anything remotely ridiculous. We’re also having the whole conversation about finances, naturally. Honestly, the cost of everything is insane. Tell me about it. Even just getting groceries feels like a strategic operation these days. And kids… they’re not cheap. Have you been looking at maternity leave, stuff like that?

…and honestly, the guilt is awful, isn’t it? Just knowing she was pushing through for the grandkids, and now… well, you know. It is. Mum always did that. Put on a brave face for us all, even when… you remember that time with her knee? She refused to go to the doctor for months, said she just needed to ‘walk it off’ because she didn’t want to spoil Emily’s birthday party. Oh, God, yes! And she was hobbling! Emily was about five then, wasn’t she? Absolutely determined. It’s just… it feels different this time. It wasn't like she’d been ‘managing’ anything, this cancer just…took hold. It’s the speed of it, isn’t it? That’s what’s so shocking. You hear stories, people battling for years, and then with Dad… it was just a few months from diagnosis to…everything. It makes you feel helpless. Completely. And I keep thinking about Sarah. She’s taking it really badly. She’s always been so close to Gran. She is. She’s a sensitive soul, that one. Have you spoken to her today? She hasn’t replied to my texts. I tried calling, went to voicemail. I’m worried she’s just… shutting down. She was already struggling with her anxiety, and now this… I’m half tempted to just go round. That's probably a good idea. She needs someone, even if just to sit with in silence. Jamie’s been brilliant, hasn’t he? Stepping up and taking on so much with the funeral arrangements. He really has. He’s always been good in a crisis, level-headed. It’s a relief, honestly. I’m a mess, I’m not going to lie. I keep bursting into tears at random moments. Even over weeding the garden yesterday! That sounds about right. It’s okay to be a mess, you know. You're allowed to grieve. Don’t try to be strong for everyone else at the expense of yourself. Easier said than done. And then there’s Ben. He’s pretending he’s fine, all stoic and ‘it is what it is’. Which is so typical of him, but I know it’s eating him up inside. He adored Gran. He did. Remember when she taught him to knit? He was so proud of that wonky scarf he made her. Oh, bless him!

So, Leo, how was school today? Anything exciting happen? Besides the usual chaos, of course. It was alright, Mum. History was boring. Mr. Davies just read from the textbook  again . Sounds familiar. I remember those days. Though, our textbooks were probably older than you are, Leo. Mine was okay. We started tennis club. It's pretty good, actually. Bit cold though. Oh, that’s lovely, Finn! Are you enjoying it? Are you getting any coaching? Yeah, a bit. Old Mr. Henderson helps us out sometimes. He used to be proper good, apparently. He’s got loads of trophies in the clubhouse. Tennis is alright. I’d rather be playing football, though. Training’s tough this week, coach is really pushing us before the match on Saturday. Good. A bit of discipline is good for you. You need to be putting that effort in, you know. That match is important. Speaking of effort… have you two given any more thought to what you want to do after school? It's not tomorrow, but it’s creeping closer, isn't it? Leo, you were mentioning apprenticeships last week? Yeah, but I'm still not sure. Dad said maybe engineering? But that seems… boring. I don’t know what I’d actually  do . Engineering is a solid trade, Leo. Good money, good prospects. But it has to be something  you  want to do. Have you looked at any of the online careers advice sites? They have quizzes and stuff. And Finn, you’re still keen on sports science, aren't you? That tennis coaching might give you a good grounding, actually. Maybe. I was thinking about it, but it feels like everyone’s going to uni, and I don’t want to be the only one doing something different. Oh, darling, don’t worry about that. Everyone's path is different. It’s about finding what’s  right  for you. Remember old Mrs. Peterson down the road? She started her own bakery at 50! That’s true. Though I suspect she had a rather substantial inheritance to help her along! Speaking of which, I was reading an article today – apparently, more and more people are looking at investing in smaller businesses now. Before the referendum, it was pretty much all property. Now it’s… different. Oh, really? That’s interesting. I’ve been thinking about expanding my proofreading business, maybe taking on a junior partner.

Honestly, I’m already stressing about the dissertation. Just… the  thought  of it. It feels so far away, but also like it’s looming, you know? Oh, totally. I felt like that for ages. Honestly, the worst part is just starting. Once you’ve got a few thousand words down, it doesn’t feel so terrifying. What’s your topic again? It’s on the socio-linguistics of online gaming communities. Basically, how people use language to build identity and signal belonging. It  sounds  cool, but translating that into a coherent, 12,000-word argument… That actually sounds fascinating! A bit niche, maybe? But good niche. Is the data collection side going well? It’s…ongoing. I’m mostly doing forum analysis and some interviews. People are surprisingly willing to talk about their online personas. Though, a lot of it is just teenagers, which feels a bit limiting. Well, that’s your demographic, isn’t it? Still, good to get a range. Lancaster is going to be a nice change of scenery though, right? Not just staring at a screen all day. Absolutely. And seeing your family! I’m really looking forward to meeting your mum and dad properly. I feel like I’ve only met them briefly at Christmas and things. They're really excited to meet you. Mum’s already planning all sorts of things. Potentially a trip to the coast? If the weather holds up. Oh, that would be amazing! I haven’t been to the coast in ages. Not since… well, since that disastrous cockle-picking trip with my cousin.  Laughs  Oh god, don’t remind me. I’d almost forgotten about that. You ended up with sand  everywhere . Everywhere! And feeling incredibly guilty about potentially illegally harvesting cockles. Honestly, a really bleak day. We definitely earned our fish and chips after that. Speaking of earning things, have you thought any more about what you want to do after the Masters? Any career ideas? Honestly? Not really. I'm kind of hoping something will magically fall into place. I like the research side of things, obviously, but the academic job market is…grim. Maybe something in lexicography? Or content strategy? I’m throwing darts at a board. I get that. I’m toying with the idea of going into teaching, but it feels like a huge commitment. And the workload… Yeah, my aunt’s a secondary school teacher and she’s perpetually exhausted.

Right, so then Liam proper tripped over, didn't he? Right in front of everyone at the gig. No way! Liam? Seriously? He’s always going on about how coordinated he is. I know, right? Total showman. He went flying. Landed right near the speaker. Thought for a minute he’d broken something. Oh dear. Was the band any good at least? Who were they again? The… Static Waves? Yeah, Static Waves. They were alright. Not amazing, a bit loud, really. But the atmosphere was decent. Loads of people were there, mostly sixth formers though, predictable. Yeah, that’s the problem with gigs in Doncaster, isn’t it? Always a younger crowd. I’m starting to feel ancient at 22. Don’t be daft. You’re not ancient. Though, thinking about it, it feels like ages since we were all cramming into the back of Mrs. Higgins’ car to get to a band practice. Oh god, those were the days. The smell of damp dog and cheap air freshener. And the absolute terror of her driving. She was a menace. A lovely menace, but a menace nonetheless. Remember when she nearly took out a lamppost on Frenchgate? How could I forget? Everyone screamed. Anyway, what have  you  been up to? Apart from witnessing Liam’s spectacular fall? Still painting miniatures? Yeah, still at it. I’m working on a whole squad of Space Marines at the moment. It’s… therapeutic, actually. Gets me away from revision. What about you? Still obsessed with that guitar? Absolutely. Been trying to learn this new riff by IDLES. It's driving me mad, though. My fingers are killing me. It’s way harder than it sounds. IDLES are wicked. You’ll get there. You always do. Remember when you first started and couldn’t even hold a chord? Don't remind me. It was brutal. My housemates were threatening to evict me. Said it sounded like a dying cat. They weren’t far off, to be fair. Have you been practicing with Ben and Chloe lately? Are they still trying to form a band? They are. Actually, they’re sounding pretty good. Ben’s got some decent songwriting skills. Chloe’s drumming is…enthusiastic. Enthusiastic is a polite way of putting it. She hits those drums like she’s personally offended them. Exactly! But that’s Chloe. Speaking of bands, have you heard anything from The Northern Lights since they went to uni in Newcastle?

Right, okay, so I’m going to use my researcher to fly to Atlanta. And then… oh no, wait. The eradication counter is at two! We are  so  close to curing blue. Hold your horses, Sarah! Don’t get ahead of yourself. You need the three cubes to even  start  eradicating. You’ve got two in Atlanta, that’s it. Aye, and don’t forget about the outbreak in Santiago. That’s looking nasty. Honestly, this game is stressful. I’m a chef, not a global pandemic manager. I think it’s brilliant. Properly tense. Though I’m still trying to figure out this Operations Expert role… what exactly does ‘share knowledge’  mean  in practice? It means you get to be a bit of a busybody, Rhys! You go around telling everyone what to do, pretending you’re terribly clever. It’s the Welsh way. Oh, Glyn, you’re awful! But he’s not wrong, Rhys. You can give Sarah a card from your hand if it helps her research. Think of it as… strategic interference. Yes, please Rhys! Honestly, I'm flailing. I had a whole plan for tackling blue, thinking I was about to win, and then  bam  – another outbreak in Cairo. Okay, okay. Rhys, give Sarah the blue card. I'm going to build a research station in Essen. We need somewhere central for Europe. And keep an eye on that black disease, it’s creeping across Russia. Russia? Seriously? This is just like real life, isn’t it? Always something going on in Russia. Reminds me of the time I tried to cater a wedding for a Russian diplomat… Oh, do tell! Was it chaotic? Chaotic doesn’t even  begin  to cover it. They wanted caviar fountains, a live bear… I’m not joking! A  bear ! Luckily, health and safety intervened. A bear! I can just picture it, Huw. You looking horrified, trying to explain to a Russian dignitary why a bear isn’t conducive to a pleasant wedding reception. You always have the best stories, Huw. It truly is a gift. Okay, focus people! Bear stories later. Rhys, did you give me the card? I need to research… right. Atlanta, then hopefully eradicate. Given! Now, the problem with this game is the relentless pace. It feels like a proper sprint. Anyone fancy a cuppa? I’ll put the kettle on. Yes, please. Strong and sweet, if you don’t mind.

Right, so, the CBeebies panto is booked! Tickets secured for Saturday afternoon. Are you both excited? Yes! Is Mr. Tumble going to be there? I hope so! Will there be a dragon? I  love  dragons. I think there's a very silly dragon involved, yes. And Mr. Tumble is definitely making an appearance. It's all about getting into the Christmas spirit early, isn’t it? Though, it feels a bit strange booking Christmas things in November. It’s not Christmas yet! My birthday is  before  Christmas! You are absolutely right. We mustn’t skip over your birthday! We’re still figuring out what we're doing for that, aren’t we? Any more brilliant ideas than the zoo? Can we have a massive cake? With dinosaurs on it? A massive dinosaur cake is a  very  good suggestion. We can definitely do that. I was thinking maybe a small party too, just a few friends from school? I want Lily and Thomas to come! And Chloe! Okay, Lily, Thomas, and Chloe. Noted. We’ll have to check with their parents. It’s going to be a summer birthday, so hopefully, we can do something outdoors if the weather is nice. Maybe a picnic and games in the park? Can we have a bouncy castle? A bouncy castle is a bit ambitious for the park, darling. Maybe for a bigger birthday? Speaking of things outdoors, I saw on CBeebies this morning they were doing a story about a little robin who was lost. It was very sweet, but it made me think about winter already. I like ‘Bluey’ the best! Bluey is so funny! Bluey is brilliant, isn’t she? That show is so clever. It’s lovely seeing them try and teach kids about family life and emotions in such a fun way. Do you remember what Nana said last week? “Happy as Larry” she was, because we were all having a good time. What does ‘Happy as Larry’  mean ? It’s an old saying, sweetie. It just means very, very happy. Really content. Nana uses lots of old sayings. Like when she said, ‘Don’t count your chickens before they hatch!’ That was weird. That’s another one! It means don’t assume something good will happen until it actually  does . It's a bit of a warning. Anyway, back to important things! World Book Day is coming up soon, too.

Right, this sourdough is genuinely amazing. Where did you get it, Chloe? Not the usual place, is it? No, actually. Old mate Dave from down the road is doing a ‘micro-bakery’ thing from his kitchen. Apparently, he’s a retired chemist, which explains the obsession with hydration percentages and gluten development. A retired chemist making sourdough? That’s… oddly perfect. Sounds very ‘Great British Bake Off’ contestant backstory. Ha! It is good though. Seriously. So, any progress on the flat hunt, Sarah? Still looking at places in Bristol? Bit of a disaster, actually. Saw a place yesterday that looked amazing online – modern, city centre, all that jazz. Turned up and it smelled… damp. Like, properly damp. And the landlord kept referring to the ‘character’ of the mould. Oh,  no . "Character" is code for “structural issues and potential respiratory problems”. You deserve better than a mouldy character flat. Definitely. Bristol’s a nightmare for that, isn’t it? All those old buildings… Still, gotta stay positive. You’ll find something. Are you still keen on being closer to Liam? Is that driving the Bristol search? It’s part of it. It’s just… he seems so settled there. Proper Bristolian now, complaining about the tourists and the students. And I miss him, obviously. It feels a bit silly, commuting up to Manchester every other weekend. It  is  a long commute. But if it’s worth it, it’s worth it, right? Though, I can see how it would be nice to just… be there, without the travel. Have you considered the compromises? Maybe somewhere halfway? Yeah, a halfway point could work. Though then you’re not really close to  anyone . It's a tough one. Speaking of tough, how’s the teaching going, Amy? Any particularly… spirited students lately? Oh, you know. A mixed bag. I’ve got one lad who genuinely believes Shakespeare was a collective of AI robots from the future. Trying to argue linguistics with him is… an experience. Oh my god. That's amazing. And terrifying. AI robots! That’s a new one. I had a student once who insisted the Second World War was a hoax perpetrated by the pigeon fanciers’ association. Pigeon fanciers?! Seriously? Swore blind. Said they controlled the flow of information. Apparently, they needed to boost the market for homing pigeons. It's a long story. I’ve learned not to question it.

Honestly, this lemon drizzle is the best I’ve made. I think I finally got the balance right between the zest and the juice. It's a bit crumbly though, isn't it? It’s lovely, honestly, Sarah. Seriously good. And crumbly’s good! Gives it a rustic feel. Speaking of good, did anyone else spend their childhood trying to build a perfect tower with those wooden building blocks? The ones painted in really garish colours? Oh my god, yes! I had a set. Spent  hours  meticulously stacking them. They always fell down, though. It was incredibly frustrating. I think I was trying to engineer something structurally sound before I even knew what engineering  was . I remember those! Mine were mostly used as furniture for my Sindy dolls. Never really got the tower thing. Though I  did  have a very impressive collection of miniature teacups. My Nan bought them for me. She collected them herself. My Nan collected porcelain dolls. Absolutely terrifying things. They’d just… stare. I used to hide them in the airing cupboard. My mum had this weird phase where she tried to get me to learn French. Little cassette tapes, everything. Utterly useless. I can still remember a few phrases, mostly involving farm animals. Oh, I did French in school! Managed to scrape a C. I think I was more interested in dissecting the teacher's accent. Miss Dubois was from Normandy, and she’d get  so  frustrated with our pronunciation. It was almost a hobby of mine, subtly mimicking her. Naughty! I did German. Even worse. It feels like I’ve completely purged all knowledge of it from my brain. Though, funnily enough, I find I pick up bits and pieces of languages when I travel. Little phrases, just enough to be polite. It's odd. You’ve done a lot more travelling than us, haven't you? That account management role must keep you busy. How’s it going with the new client, the engineering firm? It's...challenging. They're very detail-oriented, naturally. And quite resistant to anything that deviates from their established processes. It's a lot of explaining, a lot of justifications. It requires a lot of patience, let me tell you. It reminds me a bit of dealing with my brother actually. Always had to have things his way. Sounds familiar. I had a similar issue with a supplier recently. Trying to convince them that their invoice was, shall we say,  optimistic .

So, how was it then? Honestly, spill the beans. Did you have a good time? Yeah, seriously! You two have been gone a week, practically radio silence. We needed updates! Was the hotel decent? Oh, it was lovely, honestly. A little… older than the pictures suggested, mind you. Bit of chintz, if you know what I mean. Floral wallpaper everywhere. But clean as a whistle, and the staff were absolutely wonderful. Aye, that’s the main thing, isn’t it? Staff. We had a cracking young lad on reception, name of Ben. Kept us right with directions and recommendations. He told us the best pub for a proper Sunday roast. A proper Sunday roast? Standards are high, Dad. And it  delivered , lass. It delivered. Yorkshire puddings the size of your head, proper gravy… I had two helpings. Nearly burst. Good to know your priorities haven’t changed, Dad. Mum, what about you? What did  you  think? Oh, I enjoyed it. The scenery was breathtaking, honestly. We did a lovely coastal walk, though my knees were complaining by the end of it. And the little villages were just gorgeous, all quaint and colourful. We bought a few bits and bobs in a little craft shop. Oh, nice! Anything good? Just little things. A knitted tea cosy, because why not? And a couple of little ceramic hedgehogs for the garden. Hedgehogs? Really? She’s got a thing for hedgehogs, lad. Always has. Remember that time she rescued that one with the tangled foot? Oh, yeah! The one you named Prickles? Don’t remind me! That was a whole ordeal. We had it in a box in the spare room for days. It kept trying to escape. Sounds chaotic. Did you manage to do any proper sightseeing? Besides the pub crawl, Dad? We went to that castle, Scarborough Castle, it was. Bit windy up there, nearly lost my hat. But the views were smashing. You can see for miles. And we went to Whitby, of course. Had to get some fish and chips. Whitby! Did you go to the Abbey? That’s supposed to be amazing. We did! It was beautiful, very atmospheric. Though a lot of steps, I'll tell you that. My legs were aching for days. And it was packed with tourists. Sounds busy. Did you take many photos? We want to see  everything . Oh, aye. Loads. I'll have to sort them out.

Morning, you two. Anyone else smell burnt toast? Pretty sure it wasn’t me. Morning, Mark! And yes, that was absolutely me. Tried a new rye bread, forgot it wasn’t white. It’s…rustic. Rustic is a polite word for carbonized, Sarah. You nearly set off the smoke alarm. Did you at least scrape off the worst of it? Of course! Though honestly, a little char adds flavour, doesn’t it? Anyway, how was your run, Mark? You were out early. Bracing. Absolutely freezing. The canal path was slick with ice in places. Almost lost my footing a couple of times. Thinking I might stick to the treadmill for a bit now, honestly. My knees aren’t getting any younger. Sensible. Though, risking life and limb for a Saturday morning run is very…you. Speaking of risking things, have you seen this article about that actor, what’s his name…the one from  Bridgerton ? Apparently, he’s investing heavily in crypto. Oh, Luke Newton? No, but that sounds spectacularly ill-advised. Celebrities and crypto, it’s a disaster waiting to happen. They get told what to do by…well, anyone. It’s the same principle as dodgy investments, really. People thinking they can get rich quick. It's all just applied engineering, really – leveraging risk and reward. Only in this case, the engineers are charlatans. You manage to bring everything back to engineering, don’t you? It’s admirable. Although, I suspect understanding stress tolerances in bridge design is slightly more useful than understanding meme coins. Absolutely. Anyway, are we still on for that pottery class next weekend? I booked us in, thought it would be a laugh. Pottery? Seriously? Last time you did anything remotely arts and crafts related, you ended up covered head to toe in glitter. It was a Christmas card making session! And it was…festive. Besides, it’ll be good to try something different. It's not like you’re swimming in exciting hobbies at the moment. Besides, I need a birthday present for my mum. It sounds wonderfully awful, actually. I’m in. I’m picturing a chaotic scene of flying clay and passive-aggressive shaping. Fine. But I’m warning you, if I end up with clay in my beard, I’m blaming both of you. Do you want me to pick up some pastries on the way back from work later? There’s that new bakery down the high street.

Honestly, Reg, you're going to miss us all terribly when you’re out in Saudi. It’s not just leaving Peterborough, it’s leaving  us . She’s right, you know. It won't be the same without you winding up Dad at Christmas. Or generally just…being here. Yeah, who am I gonna moan to about work now? You always understood the state of things down at the yard. Don’t you lot start gettin’ all sentimental on me now. I've seen lads shipped off to worse places than Saudi. At least you’ll be earnin’ proper money, eh? Not like some of the…jobs around here. It's a good opportunity, obviously. And the money is amazing. But it just feels…weird. You’ve lived here your whole life. Remember when you got absolutely lost trying to drive to Stamford? Even with the Sat Nav? Oh, God. That was a mess. You ended up in some farmer’s field, convinced you’d discovered a new shortcut. Google Maps was laughing at you too, wasn't it? Google Maps! Pah! Give me a proper map and a compass any day. These youngsters rely too much on their little screens. Couldn’t find their way out of a paper bag without one. That’s a bit harsh, Dad. It's just…convenient. Although, in Reg’s case, even the Sat Nav couldn't save him. He swore the Sat Nav was deliberately misleading him. Said it had a personal vendetta. I’ll tell you what’s misleading – estate agents. Your Mum and I were thinkin’ about down-sizing, a bit of decorating, and the fella tries to tell us a three-bedroom semi is 'charming and full of potential'. Potential for what? Collapse? You need my mate, Liam. He's a builder, does a good job, doesn’t rip you off. Actually, speaking of jobs… I think I might apply for that assistant manager role at the library. It’s a pay rise, and it's… quiet. Quiet? You? The woman who once accidentally set off the fire alarm during a book display competition? It was a rogue glitter cannon! And it was for charity. Honestly, I need less excitement in my life. Good on ya, lass. Sometimes a bit of peace and quiet is just what you need. It's easy to get caught up in all the madness.

Honestly, this air is doing wonders for my sinuses. Back in London, it feels like I'm constantly battling something. You two feeling alright? Any London-lung clinging on? I'm surprisingly good, actually. I think getting away from the… children… for a few days is medicinal in itself. Though, my feet are killing me. These shoes were a terrible idea for all this walking. Tell me about it! I’m regretting the stylish-over-practical choice intensely. Though, speaking of medicinal, I’ve been trying this new probiotic. Apparently, 70% of your immune system resides in your gut. Sounds… dramatic. Dramatic, but probably true. I’ve been meaning to look into those. I’m all for biohacking at this point. Though, honestly, I just need to be better at remembering to actually  drink  water. It’s so basic, but… Oh, you and water. It’s a long-running saga. Remember that time you tried that app that buzzed you every hour to remind you? Don’t remind me. I just ended up turning off all notifications. It became more stressful than the dehydration! But seriously, this garden is incredible. Look at the variety of ferns. It’s giving me ideas for the back garden, though I suspect it’ll all end in tears. You and gardening… another saga. I’m fairly certain you killed a cactus once. It was a particularly stubborn cactus! And the soil was… wrong. Okay, fine, I probably overwatered it. But look at these rhododendrons! They're enormous. How do they get them to flower like this? It’s all in the soil acidity, apparently. And a lot of careful pruning. You know, old Mr. Henderson – my neighbour – he's a horticultural wizard. He'd happily give you advice, but be prepared for a lecture lasting at least an hour. An hour? Worth it, potentially. I need all the help I can get. I'm considering hiring someone, actually. Just someone to advise, you know? I don't want to end up with a jungle. Good plan. Although, a jungle  could  be quite trendy. Very ‘Lost World’ aesthetic. Very appealing… until the slugs arrive. So, how are things back home, aside from the inevitable chaos? Any interesting news? Work is… work. The usual teenage dramas. Little Timmy is convinced he's a TikTok star. It's mortifying. He's filming dances in the kitchen. Oh, lord.

Honestly, Dad, you sound completely different on the phone these days. It’s like… less London. More… well, I don’t know  what  it is. It's like you’re deliberately softening everything. Softening? What are you on about, Chloe? I speak perfectly normal. Always have. It’s probably your phone. These newfangled devices, they do funny things to voices. Can't understand a word anyone says half the time. Oh, don’t start on the phones, Arthur. Mine keeps trying to text my shopping list to the vicar. Honestly! And Chloe’s right, your accent  has  changed. It’s…rounder? You used to have that proper East End edge. Yeah, I noticed it too. Remember when you used to wind up Grandma with your cockney rhyming slang? Proper brilliant that was. I was a young man! People change. Besides, what’s wrong with sounding a bit less… harsh? It’s tiring, innit? All that glottal stopping. It's just… it doesn't sound like  you . Speaking of things sounding different, how’s Mark doing? Still… not talking? Oh, dear. Don’t bring that up, love. He’s… well, he’s Mark. He’s been “busy” with work, apparently. Which means down the pub with Gary. He’s a proper mess, isn’t he? Always has been. Remember when he tried to build that shed and nearly took out next door’s prize-winning roses? That boy. Honestly, that boy. I told him, I said, “Mark, you’re not cut out for DIY.” And did he listen? No. Ended up owing Mrs. Henderson a new rose bush and a whole lot of apologies. It's just... I feel so bad for Liam. He deserves a dad who actually  shows up . It’s not fair. This whole custody thing is dragging on. It's awful for the little one. And you’re doing brilliantly, Chloe, keeping everything together. It’s just… Mark needs to sort himself out. It's the drinking, isn’t it? It always comes back to the drinking. Remember Uncle Barry? Same story. Lost everything to the bottle. Lost contact with Sarah and Ben. Proper sad. Don't go bringing up Barry. That's stirring up bad memories. We all had a rough time with that. Speaking of rough times… anyone remember trying to ride bikes down that hill by the old quarry? I nearly broke my arm. Oh my god, yes!

Honestly, the grating of cheese is the worst bit. Absolutely the worst. I’d rather wrestle a badger than grate a whole block of cheddar. Mmmhmm. Badger wrestling sounds fun. Is that a thing? Don’t talk with your mouth full, darling. And no, badger wrestling is emphatically  not  a thing. It’s a metaphor for something deeply unpleasant. Like this cheese. Although, it does smell nice. Are you enjoying the mac and cheese? It’s good. Can I have dessert first? Absolutely not. Dessert is after you’ve finished your vegetables. We agreed. But I  want  Baked Alaska. You promised you’d make it! It’s been ages. And I will. After dinner. It’s a bit of a palaver, you know. Torching the meringue… it requires concentration. Though, thinking about it, your Uncle David tried to make one once. It was… a disaster. Uncle David? What happened? Oh goodness. He set fire to the kitchen towel. Small fire, thankfully, swiftly extinguished, but the meringue ended up looking like a lunar landscape. And tasted faintly of smoke. Haha! He’s so clumsy. He is, isn’t he? He’s always been like that. Remember when he tried to help me decorate for Halloween last year? Oh yeah! He kept trying to hang the spider webs  inside  the house. Like, in the living room, instead of on the bushes. Precisely! And then he got tangled in them himself. It was chaos. We’re having the Halloween party here again this year, aren’t we? Should be good. Though I’m dreading the recruitment of volunteers. Getting people to help with the decorations is like pulling teeth. I can help. I'm good at hanging spider webs. Properly. You are, aren’t you? That’s excellent. Perhaps you can supervise Uncle David. Speaking of things that are… complicated… I had a really frustrating meeting at work today. Oh? What happened? Just… some resistance to a diversity initiative I'm trying to push through. A lot of subtle… well, frankly, discriminatory attitudes masquerading as ‘concerns’ about qualifications. Honestly, it's exhausting. It's 2024, you'd think people would be more enlightened. That’s rubbish. Everyone should have a chance. Exactly. You're absolutely right. It just… it reminds me of some of the things I encountered when I was starting out in my career. Being a woman in a predominantly male field.

Right, this toast is lovely, isn’t it? Proper Yorkshire butter makes all the difference, you know. Not like that…spreadable stuff. You and your Yorkshire butter. It  is  good, though, I'll give you that. Much better than anything I’ve found in Swansea. Though, to be fair, Swansea doesn’t really  do  butter properly. Aye, it’s a skill. So, New York… you never did tell me everything. Beyond the bagels and the Broadway shows. Was it as overwhelming as everyone says? Overwhelming is…a good word. It’s just  constant . Constant noise, constant people, constant… everything . But in a good way, mostly. I did manage to find a little quiet in Central Park, though. Sat and watched the world go by for a good hour. Felt almost…peaceful. Sounds lovely. Though, give me the Dales any day. Or even the Gower Peninsula, to be fair. Did you get up the Empire State, then? I did! Went up at sunset. Touristy as hell, naturally, but worth it. Bit chilly, mind. Reminded me of those windswept hills in Japan, actually. Remember trying to take a decent photo of Mount Fuji in November and nearly blowing away? Oh, I do! Honestly, you clung to that vending machine for dear life. Japan… good times, eh? Still can’t believe we ended up living there for five years. No, it’s bizarre isn’t it? Feels like a different lifetime. Speaking of different… did you ever actually book those flying lessons? You were going on about learning to fly last time I saw you. I did! Got a slot next Saturday. Terrified, naturally. Always been a bit of a scaredy-cat, me. But I thought, at my age, I ought to start ticking things off the bucket list, y’know? That’s brilliant! You absolutely should. Though, maybe don't tell your insurance company just yet. Good point. Right, what are we doing today? I'm at your mercy. I was thinking a wander down Mumbles? Perhaps a pasty? Mumbles sounds perfect. And yes to the pasty! We could walk along the promenade, have a look in the shops… it's supposed to be quite mild today. Though, speaking of mild, have you seen when the refuse collection is here? I haven't put the bins out, and I don’t want to miss it. I think it's Wednesday. But check the council website, don’t trust my memory.

Right, okay, my go. Ugh, seriously? Another vowel. This is hopeless. You’re just moaning, Leo. You’ve got loads of consonants. Play ‘quixotic’! ‘Quixotic’? With what?! I’ve got a Q, an I, an X, an O… and a bunch of vowels. It’s massively unfair. I swear, this board is rigged against me. Relax, mate. It’s just Scrabble. Though, honestly, you were always terrible at it. Remember that time at uni, you tried to play ‘zeitgeist’ and spelled it ‘zitegeist’? Oh,  shut up , Ben. I was tired! It was after that all-nighter for the history essay. And Professor Davies was droning on about… something. It all blurred into one. It's a good job you weren't trying to spell ‘onomatopoeia’ then, eh? That would've been a disaster. Still, I reckon ‘zeitgeist’ is a pretty impressive word to  attempt  when you're exhausted. Speaking of impressive words... did anyone else realize ‘cryws’ is a Welsh word? This road’s name? It means ‘crooked’ apparently. No way! That’s… surprisingly apt. The road  is  crooked. Always wondered why it was spelled like that. Interesting. Makes you think about where words come from, doesn’t it? Like, everything has a story. It's mad to think how language evolves. Remember in A-Levels, we had to do etymology? Torture. Oh god, the etymology essay. I wrote mine on the origins of 'sandwich'. Riveting stuff. My teacher thought I was joking. Ha! ‘Jazzy’! Twenty-two points. And it’s on a triple word score. Take that, Leo. Unbelievable! You’ve been saving those J and Z’s. That’s… that's strategic villainy. I'm bringing this up at our next house meeting. You're no match for my Scrabble skills, Leo. Though, I'm trying to think of a word... I need to use this ‘h’ before you get another go and dominate. You know, my grandma's really into the Chelsea Flower Show. She's always going on about hybridizing roses and the best method for pruning hydrangeas. It's... a lot. Sounds relaxing, actually. Better than being stuck in a library writing a dissertation on 18th-century land ownership. Which, incidentally, is what I  should  be doing. Don't feel guilty, Leo. A little Scrabble never hurt anyone. It’s a good break. Honestly, I think I'm starting to genuinely enjoy it. It's a lot more fun than reading about Victorian children's literature for my course.

Right then, love. Kettle’s just boiled. You want a cuppa? Earl Grey alright? Oh, that'd be lovely, George. Yes, Earl Grey’s perfect. Bit chilly in here, isn’t it? Thought it was supposed to warm up a bit today. Supposed to, according to that fancy forecast on the telly. Doesn’t always get it right, does it? Still, better to be prepared. Milk and sugar as usual? Please. Though, don’t go overboard with the sugar, mind. Doctor’s been on at me again about my levels. Said I need to be more careful. Always the doctor, isn't he? He'll be telling us to eat rabbit food next. Here you go, careful it's hot. So, anything interesting happen today? You had young Thomas and Lily, didn’t you? Yes, all day. Goodness me, they’re bundles of energy, those two. Thomas is obsessed with dinosaurs at the moment. Covered the entire living room in plastic ones. I spent half an hour picking them up before their mum came. Dinosaurs, eh? Always a popular choice. Remember when our Michael went through that phase? Had a whole bookshelf dedicated to them. He used to roar around the house, frightening the cat half to death. Oh, I remember! Poor old Whiskers. She’d just disappear under the sofa until the roaring stopped. It’s funny what they get interested in, isn't it? Little Lily, she's all about princesses and sparkly things. Everything has to be pink and glittery. They do their own thing, don't they? Makes life interesting. Speaking of interesting, old Mrs. Higgins was having a right go at the postman this morning. Said he delivered her pension book to number 42 by mistake. Oh, dear. Poor Mrs. Higgins. She gets so flustered. Probably just a simple mix-up. Happens all the time. That it does. She was convinced it was a conspiracy though. Said the postman was trying to steal her money. You wouldn’t believe the things people come up with. No, you wouldn't. I sometimes think people just  want  something to complain about. Keeps them occupied, I suppose. Oh, I did manage to finish knitting that scarf for Emily. Good for you! She'll appreciate that, especially with this weather. What colour is it? A nice deep burgundy. I think it suits her. She's always liked that color. I'm hoping to post it to her tomorrow.

Right, that was a lovely bit of cod, honestly. Your mum always did make the best batter. A little lighter than mine, I must admit. It  is  good, isn't it? She’s got a secret ingredient, she won’t tell anyone what it is. I think it’s just a really good dusting of flour, but she pretends it’s something exotic. Oh, she always has. It’s probably just a pinch of baking powder. Though, she does insist on using lard. Says it’s the only thing that gives it the right texture. Lard is key, absolutely key. None of this vegetable oil nonsense. Speaking of key things…have either of you downloaded that ‘StepTrack’ app I was telling you about? Oh, that fitness one? Not yet, I keep meaning to. Been a bit hectic getting back into the swing of school. What do you think of it? It’s good. It’s not brilliant, but it’s good. It’s motivating, you know? It’s got little goals you can set, and it syncs with my watch. I did a decent walk this morning, actually, before we all descended for lunch. Needed to work off some of this pudding later, naturally. I'm still using my old pedometer. Low tech, but it does the job. I did manage a good walk yesterday, though, down to Wellington station to have a look. Oh! Is it really looking like it’s going to open soon? I heard they’ve had so many delays. They’re saying November now. They’ve finally finished the platform extensions, apparently. It’s been such a saga, hasn’t it? We’ve been promised that station for… well, decades. Old man Hemmings was campaigning for it when I was a girl! Remarkable. It’ll make a difference though, won’t it? Especially for you, with commuting to Exeter. You won't have to rely on that awful bus service. It'll be amazing! Actually, thinking about getting to Exeter… I need to sort out ingredients for a science experiment I'm doing with the kids next week. We're making slime. Slime? Good grief. Is that still a thing? Oh, it’s  huge . Apparently, it’s all the rage on TikTok. Borax, PVA glue… it's surprisingly complex. Sounds… messy. You’ll need a good apron. And probably a dedicated slime-making zone. You remind me, I saw Mrs. Higgins in town earlier.

Honestly, that burger last night was…a choice. Like, aggressively mediocre. I think I've had better microwave meals. You’re too harsh, man. It was fuel. After that walk up the hill, you  needed  fuel. Though yeah, I wouldn’t write a poem about it, would I? Did you see that new Marvel film yet? Everyone’s banging on about it. Nah, not yet. I’m holding out. I heard it’s…long. Like, three hours long. I’d rather re-watch ‘The Thing’ for the tenth time, honestly. Plus, I’ve got that essay looming. Professor Davies is relentless. Three hours! Jesus. That  is  a commitment. ‘The Thing’ is a classic though, can’t argue with that. You’re lucky you've got essays. I’m still stuck in Sixth Form essay hell. Though, to be fair, History is… engaging. Most of the time. Davies is pushing us hard on the Shakespeare module too. He wants us to dissect every single soliloquy. It's exhausting. Speaking of Shakespeare, did you catch that production of ‘Hamlet’ on the Beeb last week? I flicked it on for a bit. Looked a bit… moody. I was more engrossed in trying to beat Level 7 on Elden Ring. Seriously, that Malenia boss is a nightmare. I’ve lost count of how many times I've died. Oh, Elden Ring. Don’t even get me started. Jamie’s been obsessed for weeks. He keeps trying to get me to co-op but I just don’t have the patience. I'm more of a FIFA guy, admittedly. Though the Premier League has been a bit all over the place this season, hasn't it? Totally. Arsenal looking strong, though. I’ve put a tenner on them to win the league. Probably a terrible idea, knowing my luck. Speaking of terrible ideas… Ben's stag do is coming up. He's talking paintballing. Paintballing! Oh god. Paintballing. That sounds… painful. And humiliating. I’m picturing a lot of welts and bruised egos. Have you started thinking about what you're doing after sixth form? University applications? It’s looming, yeah. I’m leaning towards Cardiff Met. A few mates are going there. Bit close to home, maybe, but the course seems good. What about you? Still set on Nottingham? Yeah, still Nottingham. I’ve already got the accommodation sorted, thankfully. The seminars looked really interesting when I went to the open day.

Honestly, this cake is  divine . You have to try a bite. They do the best carrot cake here, don’t they? Oh my god, you’re right! It’s… moist. That's the word. Everything seems to be dry these days, but this is properly moist. It’s good to be back in civilisation, I swear Oxford is just…beige. Beige! That’s perfect. It  is  beige. So good to see you, by the way. It feels like ages since we properly chatted, not just quick texts. How was the train? Dreadful. Delayed. Of course. Said it was signal failure. Honestly, the whole system needs a revamp. But it’s worth it to escape. And to see you! How’s work? Still battling the spreadsheets? You know it. Spreadsheet warfare is my daily life. It's alright, though. They've given me a new project, which is good. It’s coordinating the rollout of this new internal communications programme. Sounds boring when I say it like that… but it's actually quite interesting. Lots of stakeholder management. So,  people  stuff, not just data. Ooh, sounds more up your street. I’m drowning in marketing campaigns right now. Pearson are pushing this new online learning platform  hard . It’s… a lot. Honestly, I miss the days when we were just worried about passing our dissertations. Tell me about it! Remember Sarah’s meltdown the night before hand-in? She legitimately thought she’d failed and was convinced her life was over. Oh,  god  yes. She was inconsolable. Good old Sarah. Speaking of disasters… how’s, um… Mark? Any news? I saw him vaguely ‘liked’ a picture of some girl on Instagram. Ugh, don’t even. Yes, I saw that too. And then my sister, bless her, helpfully pointed out she also follows a pilates instructor who looks suspiciously like a model. It’s all very subtle. I officially consider us broken up. He just hasn’t officially  told  me. That’s awful! He’s such a…well. You deserve better. I always thought he was a bit of a commitment-phobe anyway. Definitely. Moving on. How’s your mum? She was flagging up needing a hand with her garden last time we spoke. She's good! The garden is…less good. It’s been a bit neglected, to be honest. I promised I’d go up and help next weekend, but I don’t know if I’ll manage.

Right, so I was on the phone to Mam earlier, and you will  not  believe what she's trying to grow now. Oh dear. Let me guess, something wildly impractical for a Sunderland garden? Is it olives again? She was talking about olives last time. Worse. Figs.  Figs , Ben! She's convinced she can get a fig tree to thrive in November in Sunderland. I tried to explain, gently, about the climate, but she just said old Mrs. Henderson down the street grew one "years ago". Old Mrs. Henderson probably had a microclimate powered by sheer northern grit and a greenhouse full of heating lamps. Your mam's a force of nature, you know that. She believes in the power of positive thinking…and probably a lot of horticultural fleece. Honestly, it's exhausting. She sent me a ten-minute video detailing the specific variety of fig she’s ordered, and the 'perfect' south-facing wall it’s going to live on. It’s a brick wall that gets about an hour of direct sunlight a day! Sounds… optimistic. Speaking of optimistic endeavours, how's your sourdough starter doing? Last I heard it was looking a bit… lifeless. Don't even  start  on the sourdough. It’s currently residing in the fridge, looking forlorn. I made one loaf, it was dense enough to sink a boat, and I haven’t had the heart to try again. I’m sticking to shop-bought for now, my skills are clearly better suited to data analysis than breadmaking. It's a skill, alright. A surprisingly demanding skill. I tried to make a proper Yorkshire pudding last week. It…didn’t puff. At all. Just a sad, flat disc of batter. Oh no! Yorkshire puddings are sacred. You’ve committed a culinary sin, Ben. I know, I know. My grandma would disown me. Though she'd probably just offer to make me some herself. She's a legend in the kitchen. She could probably get figs to grow in Antarctica. See? It's a family trait. Stubborn horticultural optimism. Speaking of families, how are your folks doing? You said your dad wasn’t feeling great last time we spoke? He’s a bit better, thankfully. Just a bad cold. He’s been stubbornly refusing to slow down, though. Still trying to re-tile the conservatory. Mum keeps telling him to stop, but he insists on doing everything himself.

Morning, Gareth. Dreadful weather out there, isn’t it? Though, I suppose it’s good for the garden. Morning, David. Ay, you’re right about that. Been battling with the slugs all weekend. They’ve got a taste for my hostas, the greedy little blighters. Spent a good couple of hours out there with the torch, picking them off. A never-ending war, that is. I’ve switched mostly to pots now, easier to control. Though, the tomatoes are doing remarkably well this year, despite everything. You growing any? A few. Though I’m more focused on the roses. Trying to get ready for the village show. Old Mrs. Davies always has a stunning display. Rigorous competition, that is. Sounds it. Speaking of competition, did you see young Bellingham scoring again last night? Absolutely phenomenal. Makes you wonder what the kids of these footballers  do  with their time, doesn’t it? All that opportunity. It does. My nephew's a teacher, primary school. Says some of the children are already completely spoiled rotten, expecting everything handed to them on a plate. It’s a shame, really. All this money… Indeed. Though, it’s not just footballers. I was reading an article about the sons of some of the snooker players. Apparently, Ronnie O'Sullivan's lad is trying to break into professional snooker. Massive pressure, I imagine. Huge. It's difficult enough carving out a career under your own steam, let alone with a famous father shadowing you. Speaking of pressure… I’m drowning in essays. The sheer volume is unbelievable. They all seem to think they're writing the next great novel! Tell me about it. I’m halfway through the dissertations. Some of them… well, let’s just say the referencing is creative. I had one chap cite Wikipedia as a primary source. Wikipedia! Oh, David! You can’t win. Still, keeps us employed, I suppose. I had a rather bizarre application for a research assistant position come through yesterday. Young lad, ex-military. Apparently, he’d spent five years in the Parachute Regiment and was now looking to… academia. Interesting. A complete career change. Though, discipline can’t hurt. We had a few ex-servicemen go through our Archaeology department. Excellent students, always organised. Aye, that's what I thought. Though he also mentioned he’d initially applied to join the police force, then the army, and been rejected by both for… …vision.

Right, so, the bunting… I’m thinking lilac and white? For the Christening, obviously. Do you think that’s a bit… much? Pink! Pink and sparkly! Oh, darling. Pink  is  lovely. But Auntie Maureen already bought a ton of pink decorations for your birthday next month. Maybe lilac will be a nice change? Lilac’s good, Mum. Keeps it a little different. And honestly, Auntie Maureen’s pink explosion last year was… intense. Remember the inflatable flamingos? Oh, don't remind me. The garden looked like a tropical bird sanctuary, and not in a good way. Speaking of which, have you finalised the guest list, love? I need to give the caterers a rough headcount. Pretty much. I sent out a reminder email this morning. Think we’re looking at around thirty, maybe thirty-five. Gran and Grandpa are definitely coming, obviously. Of course. And Sarah and David said they're trying to rearrange things to make it? Yep, they’re pushing meetings around. David’s boss is being a bit of a nightmare, apparently. He keeps asking him to do weekend work. Honestly, some people. He needs to learn some work-life balance. How are  you  holding up with uni? Still drowning in coursework? It’s… manageable. I handed in the linguistics essay yesterday, thank goodness. That was a beast. Professor Davies is obsessed with the National Corpus. Seriously, every lecture is based around analysing sentence structure from the 1990s. Linguistics, eh? Sounds… fascinating. Is that why you were quizzing your cousin on his pronunciation of “bath” last week? You’re turning into a right little dialect expert. Research, Mum! Purely academic research. It’s amazing how subtle the regional variations are. And the social implications! I want a bath! A pink bath! Later, sweetie. We’ll have a lovely pink bath tonight. After the party planning. Speaking of which, did you manage to book the photographer? Booked. Sorted. She’s lovely. Showed me some of her portfolio, and she’s really good with babies. Apparently, she has a secret stash of bubbles and silly noises. Perfect. Right. I need to call the cake lady. I’m still debating between a traditional tiered cake and something a little more… whimsical. Maybe with miniature sugar flowers? Flowers! For me? Yes, darling, pretty flowers for the cake. And for you, maybe afterwards, we can plant some in the garden. Do you remember when we planted those sunflower seeds last year?

Honestly, this weather is dreadful, isn’t it? Rain, rain, rain. Makes you just want to curl up with a book all weekend. Tell me about it! It’s been awful for footfall at the shop too. Everyone's avoiding getting wet, I guess. Had a really grumpy customer earlier complaining about the lack of sunshine. You try controlling the weather, you know? Can we build a fort in the living room if it rains all weekend? A really big one? Oh, darling, that's a brilliant idea! We absolutely can. We can use all the blankets and pillows. But first, let’s finish planning our New York trip. Have you looked at hotels, Chloe? Yeah, a bit. It's… expensive. Really expensive. Especially anything central. I found a couple of options in Long Island City, which are cheaper, and apparently only a quick subway ride into Manhattan. Long Island City? Hmmm. Is it nice? I want us to be somewhere with a bit of atmosphere, you know? Remember Barcelona? That little hotel in the Gothic Quarter… Oh god, Barcelona! That was… an experience. Remember getting utterly lost trying to find that tapas place? And then Dad trying to order in Spanish? Daddy said “Hola, I would like some… chicken!” Oh, he did! Bless him. He was so proud of himself. Anyway, New York needs a bit more…planning. Maybe a slightly bigger budget. I’ve been saving a little, but… work's been a bit hectic lately. What's been happening at work? Still dealing with that difficult client? Worse, actually. They’ve decided on a restructure. And naturally, I’m in a “potential redundancy” situation. It’s all a bit of a mess, to be honest. They say nothing’s confirmed yet, but… What's 'redundancy'? Does it mean you won't be able to take me to New York? Oh, sweetheart, no. It doesn’t mean that. It just means grown-up things are a bit complicated at the moment. We’ll still go to New York, I promise. We just need to figure things out. Look, Mum, don’t worry about it. You’re brilliant at what you do. They’d be mad to let you go. And if they do, well, that’s their loss. We’ll figure something out. Maybe you could finally start that pottery class you were talking about? It is tempting. I always did love pottery.

Right, so basically, this whole pile… it’s all for the methodology chapter. And honestly, it feels like it’s multiplying overnight. Methodology? Blimey. That sounds… intense. What exactly  is  the issue? Just the volume of stuff, or is there something specific you’re stuck on? It's both, innit? The volume is mental, yeah. But it's also trying to justify  why  I’m doing things the way I am. Like, Professor Davies was really drilling me in the last meeting about the representativeness of my sample. Oh, the Yorkshire Dales ramblers? Thought that was a pretty solid group, to be fair. Bit niche, maybe, but… She thinks it’s too niche! She says it doesn’t adequately reflect broader attitudes towards landscape preservation. Says I need to consider people who  don’t  actively go rambling. Which… yeah, okay, makes sense. But finding those people and getting their opinions is… a whole other kettle of fish. So you’re having to design a new part of your data collection? Like, surveys or interviews with non-ramblers? Yeah, essentially. And this… this monstrosity here is me trying to work out the best way to do that. I’ve got potential survey questions, interview scripts, ethical considerations… it's a nightmare. I’ve been looking at different sampling techniques, stratified random sampling, convenience sampling… it’s all blurring into one. Oof. Sounds stressful. Right, okay, break it down. What's the main problem with finding these non-ramblers? Is it access? Advertising the surveys? Access, definitely. I can’t exactly go into pubs and ask people if they  don’t  like walking in the countryside, can I? They’d think I’m mental. I need somewhere I can reach a broad spectrum of people, but without it being biased. What about online surveys? You could target people based on demographics and interests. Maybe run it through a couple of university mailing lists? I thought about that. But Davies is really pushing for qualitative data, in-depth interviews. She thinks surveys are too… superficial. Right, the academic quest for ‘authenticity’. Classic. So, interviews then. Have you considered approaching local community centres or libraries? They might have notice boards where you could advertise. Yeah, that's on the list. I've also emailed the Salford council to see if they have any mailing lists for residents. No joy so far, though. Keep badgering them.

Honestly, I had the strangest dream last night. I was presenting a sales pitch… to a room full of badgers. Badgers? Seriously? What were you selling them? Prospect Research software. Naturally. But they weren’t buying it. Kept sniffing at my shoes and then one of them started trying to build a set with the brochures. It was chaos. Badgers are silly! I want a badger! Can we get a badger? No, sweetie, we are not getting a badger. They… are wild animals. And probably wouldn't appreciate a sales pitch. Though, I suppose they are quite cute. Cute until they’re dismantling your carefully constructed Powerpoint presentation. It was so vivid. I woke up properly flustered. It makes you wonder what your brain gets up to while you're asleep, doesn't it? Definitely. I dreamt I was teaching a history class, but all the students were replaced with inflatable dinosaurs. And they kept deflating. It was… stressful. Like trying to maintain order in a bouncy castle. Oh god, dinosaurs! That sounds more terrifying than badgers, honestly. Though, imagine trying to take register with inflatable dinosaurs. Roar! I’m a dinosaur! I’m a T-Rex! Very good dinosaurs. You two are excellent at being extinct reptiles. You know, it's funny, sometimes I dream about things I really  want . Like what? A pay rise? World peace? Actually, last week I dreamt we had a dog. A big, fluffy golden retriever. It was running around the garden, and the kids were just… beaming. Oh. See, that’s nice. A dog… We’ve talked about it. I know. I just… It felt so right in the dream. So cozy. It’s just finding the time, isn’t it? And the right breed. And generally being responsible adults. Tell me about it. It’s a big commitment. Although, if I won the lottery… If  I  won the lottery, I would buy a dinosaur! A real one! A real dinosaur, huh? That's ambitious. I’d get a gardener. And a dog. Definitely a dog. And maybe a really sophisticated badger-proof presentation case. Just in case. You and your badgers! But seriously, the lottery… What would  you  do? Pay off the mortgage, obviously. Then set up a trust fund for the kids’ education. And, yeah, maybe a little something for us to travel. And the dog. A very pampered dog. And a big garden for the dog!

Honestly, the state of it. Absolute chaos. What? What’s happened now? You sound…stressed. A&E. I had to go to A&E last night. Woah, hold on. What for? Are you alright? What happened? I tripped. Over…nothing, basically. Just completely lost my footing coming down the stairs at Mum’s. Seriously? You okay? Did you break anything? I don’t  think  anything’s broken. I’ve really badly sprained my ankle, I reckon. It’s swollen up like a balloon and I couldn't put any weight on it. Mum was panicking, said we needed to go straight to A&E. Rightly so. That sounds awful. A&E is…well, you know what it’s like. A complete nightmare. Nightmare doesn’t even cover it. Four hours we waited. Four! And it was packed. People coughing, screaming babies, the whole shebang. Ugh. The joys of the NHS on a Saturday night. Did they at least give you some proper pain relief? Eventually. After about three hours of whimpering and trying not to cry, a lovely nurse finally gave me some paracetamol. Paracetamol! For a potentially sprained ankle. Honestly. Seriously? That’s…unacceptable. Did they x-ray it, at least? Yeah, they did an x-ray. Thankfully, nothing broken. Just a really bad sprain. They strapped it up, told me to rest, ice it, and come back if it doesn’t improve. Good, good. At least it’s not broken. Though a sprain can be just as bad, to be fair. You’ll be hobbling around for weeks. I know! And I have that conference next week in Bristol. How am I supposed to get around? I was hoping to do some sightseeing too. Oh, that’s a pain. Maybe you could hire one of those mobility scooters? Be a bit dramatic, but practical. You’re not wrong. Imagine me whizzing around Bristol on a scooter. I'd have to invest in a hat and sunglasses. You’d be a legend. Look, I’m really sorry this happened. It sounds properly awful. Mum must've been beside herself. She was. She kept saying I need to be more careful. As if I  wanted  to fall down the stairs! It's just… clumsy me, I guess. You’re not clumsy. Just… momentarily gravity-challenged. Seriously though, look after yourself. Don’t try to be a hero. Rest it up, ice it, and let it heal.

Honestly, the state of things… did you see that report on the BBC last night about the unrest in France? Absolute chaos. Did a bit, yes. Flicked through it while having my tea. Seems they’re really feeling the pinch with the pension changes, isn’t it? Similar sort of rumblings we had a while back, but on a much larger scale. Exactly. Though I still think Macron’s got a point. Something  has  to give with these pension systems. People are living longer, you know? Can’t keep supporting everyone indefinitely. Well, that’s all well and good in theory, Arthur. But when you’ve been working since you were sixteen, like a lot of those chaps, and they tell you you’ve got to work until sixty-four… it’s a bitter pill to swallow. Especially when the politicians seem to be doing alright for themselves. True enough. Hypocrisy is rife, isn’t it? Speaking of work, how’s the shop going? Still busy with the tourists? Relatively. It's been… slow. Honestly, I'm starting to think about maybe selling up. Bit drastic, I know. Selling up? Good heavens! After all these years? What brought that on? Just…tired, Arthur. Truly tired. The hours, the stock, the constant need to be ‘on’. And frankly, the competition’s getting fierce. That new gift shop down on Church Road is undercutting everyone. Plus, I've been tinkering with an idea. An idea? What sort of idea? Don't tell me you're taking up beekeeping. No, no beekeeping. Although, that does sound rather peaceful. No, I was thinking… a small tour company. Focusing on local history, specifically the Regency period. Brighton’s  full  of it, you know? People love that stuff. A tour company, eh? That's… actually a rather clever idea, George. You always were good at spinning a yarn. You know the town like the back of your hand. That's what I’m hoping. I’ve started doing a little research, looking into licensing and insurance. It’s a bit daunting, to be honest. I haven’t had to deal with that sort of thing in years. Well, you’ve always been a resourceful chap, George. You’ll figure it out. And I'm happy to lend an ear if you need to bounce ideas around. Though I wouldn’t pretend to know much about business these days, having spent my life surrounded by teenagers and grammar rules.

Right, so are we thinking pub grub, or shall we head somewhere else afterwards for something proper? I'm suddenly quite craving a curry. Hmm, curry sounds good, but it’s a bit of a trek from here, isn't it? And I'm quite liking the look of their burger. Bit predictable, I know. Predictable, but satisfying. It  is  a good burger joint apparently. Though, look at this place - it’s… cozy. A bit dated, though. That wallpaper. Honestly. Looks like my nan’s front room. You are brutal. It's got character! It’s a proper pub, isn’t it? Not one of these trendy gastropubs. Character meaning 'hasn't been decorated since the 70s'. Still, the beer seems alright. Have you started  Happy Valley  yet? Everyone at work is banging on about it. Not yet, it’s on the list! Been meaning to. Too much boxset overload recently, I think. Finished  Severance  last week, that was… something. Oh,  Severance  is fantastic! Seriously unsettling. But  Happy Valley  is supposed to be gripping. Apparently, Sarah Lancashire is incredible. She always is. Remember her in  Last Tango in Halifax ? Brilliant. This place is busy, isn't it? It’s a Friday, I suppose. It is. Feels like a proper local. Do you remember that awful student pub we used to go to in Leeds? The one with the sticky floors? Oh god,  The Beaver , was it? Don’t remind me. That place was a health hazard. Though, to be fair, we were young and didn't care. University… feels like a lifetime ago. It does, doesn't it? I was just thinking about old Professor Davies the other day. The one who always wore that tweed jacket. The one who smelled perpetually of pipe tobacco? Yes! He terrified me. Though, he was a brilliant lecturer. He was. Right, I’m going to brave the bar. Do you want another pint? I’m getting a diet coke, trying to be good. Yeah, another pint would be good. And maybe some peanuts if they have them. Oh, and have you seen my coat? I thought I left it by the door. No, haven't seen it. Maybe you left it in the car? I’ll keep an eye out. What are they playing now? Is that… The Smiths? It is! Good choice, whoever’s on the jukebox. Though maybe a little morose for a Friday night.

Right mess of a day, the weather’s been. Bucketing it down since I left the house. Nearly lost my favourite beanie! Aye, a proper dreich one. Glad I walked here with the waterproof. You should’ve texted, I’d have walked with ye, saved ye a soaking. So, how was the drive up to Skye last weekend, then? You were bangin’ on about the landscapes. Ach, it was unreal. Seriously. Worth every minute stuck behind that caravan on the A87. The Old Man of Storr… honestly, photos don’t do it justice. I took about two hundred, and I  still  feel like I didn’t capture it properly. Two hundred, eh? Sounds about right. You get obsessive about yer photography, don't ye? I remember when you were trying to get the perfect shot of Arthur's Seat at sunrise – dragged us all down there at the crack of dawn. Hey, that  was  a good shot! And the light was amazing that morning. But Skye… Skye was different. The scale of it all. I was trying to get some long exposures with the sea crashing against the cliffs, but the wind was playing havoc with the tripod. You need one of those wee weighted bags to hang on the legs to stabilise it. I saw one online the other day, wasn't too bad the price. Speaking of stabilisation, did you get any decent shots of the fairy pools? I've been meaning to go there for ages, but it always seems mobbed. Aye, managed a few. Got there early, thankfully, before the tour buses descended. The water was absolutely freezing though! A couple of Germans were braving it for a swim, looked like they regretted it almost immediately. I was concentrating on getting the water silky smooth with a slow shutter speed. That’s where the wind was a real pain, kept shaking the camera. See, that’s the thing with landscape photography, isn’t it? It’s never just about the scenery. It’s battling the elements and hoping for a fleeting moment of perfect light. I tried doing some astrophotography a few months back, up near Tinto Hill. Complete disaster. Too much light pollution, and my camera battery died halfway through. Oh, that’s rough. Tinto Hill's a good spot, though. I remember hiking up there as a wee lad. Did you at least get a decent view of the stars?

Right, so, the week ahead. Utter chaos, I foresee. You alright with picking Leo up from football on Tuesday? I’ve got that meeting with Mrs. Henderson about… well, you know. The funding. Tuesday’s good. Though honestly, football practice seems to be consuming his life. It’s every other night! Is he even enjoying it, or is it just… pressure? He loves it, honestly. He really does. It’s the social side as much as anything, I think. All those little boys running around, causing mayhem. Keeps him out of trouble, doesn’t it? True. Though I’m pretty sure the mayhem  is  the trouble. What about Wednesday? Is Dad still doing the supermarket run? He said he would. Though knowing your father, he'll probably forget the milk again. Honestly, it’s like pulling teeth getting him to remember a shopping list. You’re telling me. It’s been like that since I was little. Remember the time he came back with three tubs of pineapple chunks instead of peaches for my birthday crumble? Oh,  don't  remind me. The crumble was… interesting. Speaking of which, how’s planning for the nursery going? Have you had any luck with viewings? It’s a nightmare. Everything’s either booked up for months, or outrageously expensive. I went to see one yesterday, it was tiny! And smelled faintly of disinfectant and despair. Oh, bless. That doesn’t sound promising. You’re right to be picky though. It’s where little Noah will be spending a lot of time. You want somewhere happy and safe. Exactly! And somewhere they don’t just shove all the kids in front of Peppa Pig all day. I swear, some nurseries rely on television as a babysitter. Ugh, don’t even get me started on kids’ TV these days. It’s all flashing lights and relentless noise. Whatever happened to good old-fashioned storytelling? I know! I tried to watch something with my class today and it was just… overwhelming. Honestly, I need a cup of tea and a lie-down after five minutes of some of that stuff. I completely understand. Have you seen that new drama everyone’s talking about, ‘The Crimson Tide’? Apparently, it’s brilliant. Oh, I’ve heard of it! Sophie was going on about it at work. Said it's a bit slow-paced, but the acting is incredible. I might have to give it a go.

This pasta’s proper good, actually. You’ve outdone yourself, ANON. Aye, well, me nan always said a good ragu solves everything. Though, truth be told, I just followed a recipe I found online. Don’t want you thinkin’ I’m some culinary genius. Don't undersell yourself! It’s a vast improvement on my usual dinner of microwave meals. Honestly, work’s been  mental  lately. I barely have time to boil an egg, let alone cook a whole feast. Tell me about it. Been graftin’ twelve hour shifts on that building site, rain or shine. Back aching somethin’ fierce. The gaffer's been on me case all week too, says I’m not shiftin’ enough bricks. Like it's a competition! Oh, that’s rubbish! Some bosses just love a power trip, don’t they? I had a nightmare at work last week. This conference… absolute chaos. VIPs turnin’ up late, AV equipment malfunctionin’, the catering messed up the dietary requirements… It was a full-on disaster. Oof, sounds stressful. What kind of conference was it? Biotech. Loads of scientists and investors. All very important and very… particular. I swear, one woman nearly had a meltdown because her sparkling water wasn’t chilled  enough . Seriously? People are weird. I’d be more bothered if I had no water at all, sparklin’ or not! You're a man of simple pleasures, aren't you? I'm dealing with budget cuts at work, that’s my ‘sparkling water’ equivalent. They want me to streamline everything, basically do the job of two people for the same money. That’s awful! You should push back on that, shouldn't you? Easier said than done. Corporate life, innit? Everyone’s just tryin’ to survive. Speaking of surviving… how’s things with Liam? You two still… okay? It's… complicated. We had a bit of a row last weekend. Over clothes, of all things. Clothes? What, he doesn’t like your style? It's not that! It’s just… he’s always commentin’ on what I wear. Says I wear too much black, that I need to ‘brighten up’. Like me mood depends on the colour of my jumper! I like black! It’s practical. And comfortable. Men, honestly. Always thinkin’ they can redesign your entire personality. It’s control, isn’t it? Subtly tryin’ to change you. Maybe... I don’t know. It just feels like he doesn’t really  get  me, y’know?

Right then, this tea's brewed nicely, hasn’t it? Bit strong, maybe, but I like it like that. Reminds me of my Nan’s. She'd make a cuppa that could stand a spoon up in it. Oh, don’t I know that feeling! My mother was the same. Always said a proper brew needed to have some… backbone. None of this wishy-washy stuff. Though, honestly, sometimes it felt like drinking paint stripper. You two and your strong tea! I prefer mine a little gentler, myself. Years of marking essays, I suppose. Needed something soothing. Though, the staff room brew was legendary for its potency. Kept us all going through parents' evening. Speaking of potent brews, does anyone remember old Mrs. Higgins down the road? She used to add a pinch of salt to her tea. Said it brought out the flavour. I tried it once, out of politeness, and it was… an experience. Salt in tea! Good heavens! That’s a new one on me. Sounds like something a sailor would drink. Though, I did have a friend who swore by a drop of brandy in his tea when he had a cold. Said it cured everything. Brandy now, that’s more like it. A little tipple can certainly warm you up on a chilly day. Though, I draw the line at salt. Honestly! What will they think of next? It’s all these fancy teas, isn’t it? Earl Grey, Darjeeling, Jasmine… Give me a good strong builders’ tea any day. Tetley’s or PG Tips, you can’t go wrong. I rather like a bit of chamomile sometimes, especially before bed. Helps me relax. Though, you’re right, there’s something very comforting about a classic cuppa. It's the ritual, I think. The kettle boiling, the tea brewing, the quiet moment to yourself. That’s right. It's a good excuse for a sit down and a natter. Can't beat a good natter with friends. And a strong cuppa, naturally. More biscuits anyone? I’ve got digestives and ginger nuts. Oh, go on then, a digestive would be lovely. Though I'm trying to watch my weight, you know. Retirement doesn't mean you can eat everything in sight! Nonsense! You’ve earned it. After all those years looking after little ones, you deserve a biscuit or two. I’ll have a ginger nut, if you don’t mind.

Honestly, this roast is amazing, Mum. You’ve really outdone yourself. It’s lovely, isn’t it? Though, I think I’ve had about three Yorkshire puddings already. No self-control. These potatoes are  chefs kiss . Seriously, best roast I’ve had in ages. Though, to be fair, my cooking skills peak at beans on toast. You say that, but your curry last month was phenomenal, Rhys. Don’t undersell yourself. That was a lucky accident, powered by a pre-made paste and sheer desperation. Speaking of desperation, did you manage to book that hotel in London for the exhibition, Ben? Yeah, got a decent deal actually. Small place near Shoreditch, but it has good reviews. I was worried everything would be booked solid with… well, everything going on. Everything going on?
