You mean the protests? I saw snippets on the news. Sounded a bit chaotic. Chaotic is an understatement. Apparently, it's been building for weeks. The tube was completely disrupted last Tuesday. London always has something going on. Remember that time we ended up walking miles because of a tube strike? Felt like a proper adventure. An adventure involving blistered feet and a very expensive emergency kebab. Don't romanticize it, Rhys. Oh god, the kebab! I completely forgot about that. It cost a fortune. Worth it though. Saved our lives. Speaking of saved lives – are you still volunteering at the youth centre, Sarah? I am, yeah. It’s… rewarding. Although, the CRB check process was a nightmare. Endless forms and waiting. It’s just a lot of responsibility, you know? Especially with everything you hear. It’s the world we live in sadly. You’ve got to be careful. It’s awful. Mum, remember when Uncle Geoff was talking about… well, you know… about little Timmy and… Oh, let’s  not  go there, please. Honestly, that conversation gives me the creeps. The whole thing about circumcision is just… so sensitive. I can’t. Fair enough. Awkward topic. More gravy, anyone? Please. This gravy is a gift from the gods. Did you see old Mrs. Higgins at the pub last week? She was going on about the price of a pint again. Said it’s daylight robbery. She always says that. It’s her default setting. Though, she’s right, isn’t she? It’s getting ridiculous. It’s just corporate greed, plain and simple. They're rinsing us.

Right, spill. Holiday debrief. How was Greece? Honestly, don’t hold back. Was it as Instagrammable as it looked? Oh my god, it was… exhausting, actually. Beautiful, obviously, the photos don't lie, but  exhausting . Constant sunshine, constant crowds. I needed a holiday  from  the holiday when I got back. You wouldn’t believe the queues for breakfast. No way! I thought you were all about that relaxed vibe. Did you actually manage to, like, relax? Briefly. On a boat trip, for about half an hour. Then someone’s kid threw up over the side and I spent the rest of the time trying not to breathe through my mouth. Speaking of which, how was your weekend at your parents’? Did your mum make you eat three roast dinners? Almost. Two and a half. She was determined I needed “putting back together” after a stressful week at work. It was actually really nice though, honestly. Dad’s been getting really into gardening, and it’s… surprisingly captivating. Aww, that’s sweet. He's always been a bit of a hidden talent, your dad. So, work’s stressful then? Still dealing with the chaos of the Henderson project? You have  no  idea. Henderson is driving me insane. He changes his mind every five minutes. I swear, I spent half of Monday re-doing a presentation he’d already approved. It’s like talking to a brick wall. How are things with you? Still battling the world of mental health? Always. It's been a tough week, actually. We had a patient sectioned, really sad case. It always hits me hard, you know? It’s just… draining. I’m glad I had the holiday, even if it was chaotic, just to recharge a bit. I can imagine. You’re amazing at what you do, though. Seriously. It takes a special kind of person. Did you hear anything from… Liam while you were away? Oh god, don't even. He messaged me, naturally. Some rambling apology about “not being ready” and then proceeded to tag himself at a festival with some other girl. The audacity! Ugh, the absolute  nerve . I still can’t believe you dated him. He was… a choice, let's say. I know, I know. I was young and easily swayed by a six-pack and a vaguely artistic personality. Lesson learned. Anyway, enough about him. Are you free next Saturday?

Honestly, I’m still reeling from seeing Sarah yesterday. She looked… smaller. And just so tired. It’s brutal, isn’t it? The chemo must be really knocking her about. She put on a brave face, as always, but you could see it in her eyes. Exactly. She kept trying to talk about normal things, the kids, work… but then she’d drift off, talking about appointments and scans. It just makes you feel so helpless. Did she mention if they’ve decided on the next round of treatment yet? She said they’re reviewing the scans next week. Apparently, it’s not responding as well as they’d hoped. She wasn’t giving much away, but… well, you could read between the lines. It sounded pretty grim. Oh, that’s awful. I wish there was something,  anything  we could do. We need to make sure we keep checking in, even when she’s pushing us away. You know how she gets. Definitely. A regular phone call, a quick visit when she’s up to it. Even just knowing someone’s thinking of her will help. Right, changing the subject slightly – have you had a proper look at those houses on Rightmove again? The one on Willow Lane? I have, briefly. It’s… nice. Very chocolate-box village. But the garden's tiny, and the photos make it look a bit dark inside. True, the garden isn’t huge, but it gets the sun for most of the day. And think of the commute! We could walk the kids to school. Remember how stressed we were about that in Norwich? The traffic was insane. That’s true, the school run here is a dream. But I’m still worried about space. We'd need a dedicated office each, wouldn’t we? And what about a playroom for Leo? This house is just… cosy. We could convert the loft. I saw a company online that does really good loft conversions. It would add loads of space, and a decent view. Plus, it wouldn't eat into the garden. Loft conversions are expensive though, aren’t they? And disruptive. Remember Uncle George and his loft debacle? Took him six months and half his savings. Okay, point taken. But this company seemed reputable. Plus, you’d have to factor in the cost of getting the current house up to scratch anyway. The kitchen’s dated, the bathroom needs a complete overhaul… It does.

Right, I’ve had enough. Honestly, I’m starting a list. A proper, documented list of things I do not like about this job. Oh, go on then. I’m already halfway through my own mental one, so I’m happy to contribute. What’s number one? Don’t tell me it’s the fire alarms again. It’s  related  to the fire alarms, actually. It’s the students treating them like a game. Seriously, leaving toast burning just to set them off? It’s a waste of everyone's time. And mine especially when I’m halfway through a cuppa. Ugh, tell me about it. Last week, someone microwaved metal. Metal, Mark! I had to evacuate a whole floor because of someone’s apparent inability to operate a microwave. See! It’s just…thoughtless. They don’t think about the consequences. They don’t think about me having to stand outside in the freezing cold making sure nobody sneaks back in to grab their phones. And then apologize to everyone for the inconvenience. It’s always “sorry, didn’t mean to” as if burning toast is an accidental occurrence worthy of a Nobel Prize! Exactly! It’s not rocket science. Okay, number two on my list: the constant streams of lost keys. Honestly, five pairs a week. Where do they put them? Do they just…fling them into the ether? It's like they've never encountered a keyring before. I swear, half of them look at me like  I'm  the crazy one when I suggest they attach something to their keys so they don’t lose them. It’s just…basic life skills, isn’t it? And then they expect us to magically produce a spare. “Can you just let me in? It’s really important!” Important for what? Another Netflix binge? Don’t even get me started on the noise complaints. 3am drum solos, impromptu parties… I’ve had to knock on doors more times this month than I have in the last six combined. Oh yeah, the noise. That’s definitely going on the list. And the passive-aggressive notes left on reception complaining about…well, everything! “The bins were slightly overflowing.” Slightly! It was two extra bottles, Carol! They’re adults, Mark! Actual adults! Why can't they just talk to someone directly instead of writing a strongly-worded essay about the state of the recycling?

Honestly, seeing Mr. Henderson at that little tapas place in Malaga was  wild . Of all the places… didn’t realise he holidayed over there. He didn't recognise me at first, bless him. Malaga, eh? Fancy. Still, you get ‘em everywhere, don’t you? Used to work with a bloke who swore he saw his neighbour in bloody Buenos Aires. Probably just someone who looked like him. It’s the package tours, isn’t it? Makes it almost inevitable. Brenda and Derek went to Prague last year, said it was overrun with people from Basildon. Oh, the Essex contingent taking over Europe! Mum, you’d have loved the Christmas markets in Malaga though. They had all sorts of German sausages and glühwein… not quite the same as Germany, obviously. German sausages… reminds me of Antwerp. Went there with Margaret, years ago. Absolute nightmare getting around, traffic was horrendous. Tiny little streets, built for horse and cart, not these modern monstrosities. I’ve always wanted to go to Antwerp. Is it nice? Apart from the traffic, naturally. The city itself is beautiful, proper old buildings, lovely squares. But honestly, getting anywhere felt like a military operation. And everyone speaking Dutch… I tried a bit of French, didn’t get me very far. Honestly, I'm trying to pick up some Spanish on Duolingo. It's going…slowly. It's mainly just useful for ordering tapas, at this rate. Good for you, love. Always useful to have another language under your belt. Though I’ve never had the patience. Elsie at work’s doing an evening class. Says it’s exhausting! Speaking of exhausting, I’m dreading Christmas shopping. Herne Bay’s getting worse and worse. It was rammed last weekend. Tell me about it. I took little Tommy there on Saturday, trying to get him a new football. Chaos. Everyone pushing and shoving and the parking… don’t even get me started. Herne Bay… used to be a lovely little place. Used to take the boys down there when they were little. Built sandcastles, ate fish and chips. Simpler times. Remember when Leo got stung by a jellyfish on Brighton seafront? He screamed the place down! Oh, that was awful! Poor little man. He was convinced he was going to lose his arm. Leo’s birthday is coming up fast, isn't it? It is. He wants a puppy. A proper, fluffy one.

So, did you see about the equality vote in Ireland? Like, the one about expanding the definition of family? Oh yeah, I skimmed an article. Something about carers and… more than just traditional families, right? Honestly, it all feels a bit complicated. Complicated? It’s just about making things fairer, isn't it? Like, why should it  only  be a mum and dad? My mate Liam has two dads, and he’s totally normal. It's weird judging people just because their family isn’t… textbook. I’m not  judging , darling. It’s just… it's a big change. And sometimes these things have unintended consequences. I read a comment online saying it could mess up inheritance laws. Ugh, online comments. Don't even start. Everyone’s an expert all of a sudden. Inheritance laws sound boring anyway. It's about people being able to, like, legally recognise the people who actually care for them. True, true. Though, you know your Nana, she'd have a field day. She's still trying to figure out why people even  want  to get married these days. “Back in my day…” she’d start. Oh god, yeah. She thinks marriage is the only way to be proper. She keeps asking when I'm going to settle down, even though I'm fifteen! She’d probably faint if she heard about all this. Honestly. She’d probably blame it on the youth of today. Which, let’s be honest, she often does. Speaking of settling down… did Uncle Mark finally propose to Fiona? She was hinting rather heavily at your birthday. He did! He proposed at the bowling alley! It was SO embarrassing. She nearly knocked over a rack of shoes she was so excited. Then she started crying, and he didn’t know what to do. He just kept offering her a handkerchief. Oh, Fiona. She’s a drama queen. But sweet. That's lovely. So, a good birthday then? Yeah, it was good. A bit chaotic. Mum tried to make a fancy cake, and it… didn’t go well. It kind of collapsed. It looked like something exploded. She tried to blame the oven. Your mum and her oven. That’s a classic. Remember when she tried to bake biscuits for Christmas and they were basically charcoal? Oh my  god , yes! And she tried to pass them off as ‘rustic’! No one ate them.

Right then, lovely bit of bubble and squeak, isn’t it? Though your bubble and squeak, Margaret, always had a… a certain… firmness to it. Mine's a bit more, well, broken down, I suppose. Firmness is good, Arthur! Holds its shape, doesn't fall apart on the plate. Yours looks like it’s had a good weep, dear. It’s perfectly acceptable bubble and squeak, Dad. Relax. Though, I still maintain you overuse the nutmeg. It overpowers everything. Nutmeg? A touch of nutmeg brings it alive, Thomas! It’s a secret ingredient, passed down from my mother. Not like those modern kitchens, everything bland and tasteless. She’d have a fit if she saw what people call cooking these days. Speaking of mothers… did I ever tell you about young Timmy, the little terror I used to mind? He decided to put his hamster in the microwave. Oh, not this story again, Mum. It's a good story! Honestly. Little blighter thought it needed warming up. Luckily, I caught him just as he was pressing start. Poor Hammy was absolutely traumatized. Shaking like a leaf. A hamster in a microwave?! Good heavens alive! What will they think of next? It’s a wonder the world hasn't ended. Though, I suppose it's no stranger than some of the things they did during the war. The war again, Dad? We’ve covered the war. Many times. Well, it puts things in perspective, doesn’t it? A hamster in a microwave… trifling compared to what people faced back then. Though, needless to say, young Timmy received a very stern talking to about the welfare of small animals. Stern is an understatement. His mother nearly had a heart attack. Still, he grew up alright. Became a…a veterinarian, actually. Irony, isn't it? That  is  ironic. Right, changing the subject entirely – Dad, you were rummaging around in the shed yesterday. Find anything interesting? Oh, yes. Found me old lathe tools. Haven't touched them in years. Beautifully made, those were. Solid steel. Not like the plastic nonsense they sell now. Your lathe… you used to make such lovely things with that. Little wooden animals for the grandchildren. Remember Sophie's rocking horse? Aye, took me months that rocking horse. Polished it until you could see your face in it. Shame the woodworm got to it eventually. Still, the tools are all there.

Honestly, the state of things… did you see that story about the cat who accidentally ordered things online with its paws? No, I missed that! A cat ordering things online? What did it buy? Apparently, a whole load of cat food! And a scratching post. The owner’s bank flagged it as fraudulent activity, naturally. It’s a funny story, though, isn’t it? Highlights how easily everything is done digitally now. It is funny, but it also makes you wonder about security. I was on the phone to the bank  again  today. Still trying to sort out that…mess. Oh, that debt? Still dragging on? It feels like it! They’re not being very helpful, just sending letters and adding more fees. It's infuriating. Sometimes I wish we'd just stuck to cash. Cash! A quaint notion these days. Though, I do remember a time when everything  was  done with cash. Simpler, perhaps, but certainly not more efficient. You know, when we first got married, everything was so different. Mortgages were manageable, house prices were…well, reasonable. Reasonable is an understatement, Mum! Try telling that to anyone trying to get on the property ladder now. It’s just…impossible. We were looking at that little cottage near the high street, the one with the garden… And it went for almost double the asking price! It's ridiculous. People are just bidding against each other, fueled by desperation. It's a bubble, I tell you. A great big property bubble. It’ll burst eventually. Though, likely not before we’re all pushing daisies. Let’s not talk about daisies, shall we? It’s too depressing. I've been trying to get my head around this new update on the work system. It’s supposed to be streamlining things, but honestly, it’s just added another layer of complexity. Oh, technology. My nemesis. I’m still struggling with the new email layout. It’s like they deliberately make it difficult to find things. It’s a constant battle, isn’t it? They think younger generations will just adapt instantly, but even  they  struggle sometimes. I was reading an article about American politics, and the disinformation campaigns they're running… it’s frightening. Don’t even get me started on American politics. It's a circus. Thankfully, we have slightly less…drama over here. Though, I did see they’re considering charging for plastic bags again.

Right, okay. Lego Ninjago’s packed away. That was a  very  intense battle. Honestly, it felt like a war zone in here for a minute. But Mum! Kai was  about  to defeat the Overlord! I needed just one more piece! Yeah! It wasn't fair! He had all the Spinjitzu masters trapped! Well, it’s getting late, and we talked about having some quiet time before bed. Remember? We agreed that  after  Lego, we’d try and do a little reading? But…Minecraft world needs finishing! I was building a secret underwater base for my villagers. It has a redstone door and  everything . And I’m terraforming a whole mountain! It needs a minecart track and a lava fall! It's gonna be epic! Epic is good. But real books are epic too, you know. They take you to different worlds, but you get to  make  the pictures in your head. It’s…a different kind of building. But Minecraft  is  building! It’s just…digital building. And it's faster! That’s true. It is fast. But sometimes slowing down is nice. Remember how much you both enjoyed that story about the dragon riders last week? That was cool. The dragons breathed  actual  fire! Exactly! And you were both picturing what the dragons looked like, and imagining flying with them. You were building the world in your heads. But I can build faster in Minecraft. I can build a whole castle in like, five minutes. I bet you can. But can you build a castle that smells like old paper and feels warm in your hands? Can you share that castle with someone else just by reading the words to them? Hmm…no. Exactly. Look, how about this? Fifteen minutes of reading – one chapter each - and  then  you can both have another twenty minutes on your screens? Deal? Fifteen minutes…that’s a long time. Think of it as a challenge! See who can read the fastest…and understand the most. I can read really fast! I’m practically a speed reader. Oh really? Well then, let’s see it! Go on, get your books. I’ll get us comfy cushions. And no complaining about the fifteen minutes, understood? Speaker_2 & Okay… That’s the spirit! Now, let's find some adventures between the pages. Can I read the one about the ninja again? Absolutely. But maybe a different ninja story, okay?

Honestly, it’s so lovely to have you both here. It feels like ages since we’ve all just sat and had a proper chat. How was the drive down, Chloe? It was alright, Mum. A bit busy around Birmingham, as always, but nothing major. Tilly navigated perfectly, though, didn’t you, Tilly? Oh, I do try! Google Maps is my best friend. Though, I swear it tried to send us through a field at one point. Oh, goodness! That sounds about right. Those things aren’t always reliable are they? Did you two manage to get a decent breakfast before you left? Just a quick granola bar, I'm starving, actually. Smells amazing in here – is that coffee and… cinnamon rolls? Guilty as charged. I thought we deserved a treat. I made them fresh this morning. So, tell me everything about your holiday, Chloe. You barely mentioned it on the phone. How was Greece? Oh, Mum, it was incredible. Truly. The island was beautiful, the food was out of this world, and the weather was perfect. We spent most of our days just sunbathing and swimming. I did drag Lewis on a hike one day though, he wasn’t thrilled. He hates walking, doesn’t he? Honestly! He says it’s ‘unnecessary exertion.’ Honestly, he would have happily spent the whole week by the pool with a cocktail. It was relaxing, though. Exactly what I needed. Sounds like paradise. You deserve it, working as hard as you do in that shop. I worry about you being on your feet all day. It’s okay, Mum. Keeps me fit! Though, my feet were killing me by the end of the week in Greece, even with the sandals. Well, I’m glad  someone  was enjoying themselves. My ‘holiday’ was mostly spent in the library. Dissertation research isn’t exactly glamorous. Oh, Tilly, you poor thing. Are you making any progress? It sounds so stressful. It is, but I’m starting to see a light at the end of the tunnel, I think. I've managed to get most of the initial literature review done. That’s fantastic! See, you  are  making progress. Now, what about today? Any plans? I was thinking we could go into Lichfield later, maybe do a bit of window shopping, and then get some lunch? That sounds lovely, Mum. I'm happy with that. I need to buy a birthday present for Auntie Carol, anyway.

This sandwich is… underwhelming. Seriously, they call this chicken and bacon? It’s mostly lettuce. Tell me about it. Mine’s supposed to be tuna mayo, and it tastes suspiciously like just mayo. They really skimp on the filling here, don’t they? You guys are complaining about sandwiches? I had chips for lunch, and they were soggy. Soggy! It’s a culinary crime. At least chips  can  be good. A bad sandwich is just…sad. So, anyone actually do anything interesting over the weekend? Apart from suffer through mediocre lunchtime cuisine? I was trying to teach my little brother how to play Magic: The Gathering. He just kept trying to attack me with the discard pile. Oh my god, that sounds awful. He's only like, eight, right? Yeah, and convinced he's a master strategist. He keeps saying he's going to join the army when he’s older. The army? What even? Where did  that  come from? Apparently, he watched some documentary about WWII and now thinks it’s all really cool and heroic. I tried explaining the… less glorious parts, but he wasn’t having it. Kids and their obsessions. My cousin went through a phase of wanting to be a pilot after watching Top Gun. Drove my aunt mad. Speaking of mad, did you see Mr. Harrison yesterday? He was going off on one about someone talking in his history class. Oh, the usual. He’s so uptight. I heard it was Liam Peterson, again. That kid just lives to annoy him. He’s asking for it, though, isn’t he? Constantly questioning everything. Though, to be fair, Harrison  is  a bit…much. Always going on about ‘discipline’ and ‘respect’. It’s like, chill out, we're teenagers. Seriously! It’s not like we're launching a full-scale rebellion or something. Though, maybe that would spice things up. Have you guys seen the new season of ‘The Owl House’ yet? No, not yet. I was planning on binging it tonight. Heard it gets pretty intense. I started it last night. It’s good, really good. Luz is amazing. Though, I’m still trying to figure out what’s going on with that Belos guy… he's creepy. Oh, you haven't gotten to the really creepy bits then. Trust me. It gets wild. You know, my mum was telling me about this thing she read online about… well, it’s complicated, something about political tensions between France and Algeria.

Honestly, Mr. Davies is the  worst . He just… doesn’t explain anything. Like, he’ll write equations on the board and just expect us to  know  what’s happening. Tell me about it! He's so smug too, isn’t he? Like he thinks we’re all just, naturally gifted in physics. I swear, half the class is just pretending to understand. Exactly! And then when you ask him to go over it again, he sighs like you’ve personally offended him. I actually understood more from that YouTube video we watched last night. No way! Which one? The one with the animations? That was actually really helpful. I’m starting to think YouTube is a better teacher than half the staff at our school. Definitely. Oh, and did you hear Mrs. Evans is on sick leave?  Really ? No! What happened? Is she okay? Apparently, she’s got a bad chest infection. Miss Harding is covering for her, which is… interesting. Oh god, Miss Harding. The one who makes us read poetry aloud even when you  specifically  ask not to? Seriously? She’ll make my life a misery! I hate reading in front of everyone. I know, right? She’s so determined to turn us all into the next Shakespeare. Honestly, I'd rather do another physics lesson with Mr. Davies. And that's saying something. Totally. It's just… awkward. Especially when it’s, like, really flowery romantic poetry. Everyone just giggles. Remember when Liam had to read that bit from ‘Romeo and Juliet’ and he went bright red? Oh my gosh, yes! He completely stumbled over the words and then just started mumbling. Poor Liam. He’s such a sweetheart. Speaking of people, have you noticed how quiet Chloe’s been lately? Yeah, it’s weird. She usually has something to say about  everything . I saw her in the library yesterday, looking really down. I wonder what's up. Maybe something happened with Ben? They were arguing in the corridor last week, but she wouldn’t tell me what it was about. Ooh, good point. That was a proper shouting match. They’re so up and down, aren’t they? One minute they’re all loved up, the next they’re trying to kill each other with words. Drama central! Anyway, did you see that trailer for ‘17 Again’? It looks hilarious! Oh my  god , yes! I want to see that so bad!

Honestly, the thought of Monday… it’s actively making my Sunday worse. Like, just  knowing  it’s coming. Tell me about it. Though at least I have the bakery to look forward to. New sourdough starter is bubbling away nicely. It's called Brenda. Brenda the sourdough? You name  everything , don't you, Liv? She deserves a name! She's a living thing! And speaking of living things, did you guys hear Maisie’s finally going for the laser eye surgery? No way! Good on her. She's been talking about that for ages. Hope it works out well. I nearly went for it when I was back in Sydney, but chickened out. The thought of anyone poking around in my eyeballs… nah. Yeah, she's a bit nervous, apparently. But she’s fed up with contacts. She keeps losing them, you know? Found one in her dog’s fur last week. Oh,  god . That’s horrifying. Anyway, enough about lost contacts and eyeball poking. What’s the plan for summer, everyone? Any exciting trips on the horizon? I was thinking… Transylvania! Transylvania?! Seriously? You’re going full Dracula on us? I know, right? It’s a bit random. But apparently, there’s a really cool hiking trail through the Carpathian Mountains. And the castles! I’m a sucker for a good castle. Plus, it’s cheap as chips. Cheap as chips? What’s that even mean? Back home, we’d say “cheap as… well, nothing really. Chips aren’t particularly cheap.” It means it’s really affordable, mate. It's a British saying. You’ll pick it up. Transylvania sounds…intense. I’m leaning towards something a bit more beachy. Maybe try and get down to Cornwall again. Although, knowing my luck, it’ll rain the entire time. I'm hoping to get a few weekends away in the van. Maybe the New Forest. Somewhere I can take the dog. I’ve been slaving away at the café all spring, need some time to recharge. It's been mental. Speaking of mental, did anyone hear from Ben? He said he was going climbing in the Peak District this weekend. Actually, yeah. Sent me a picture. He’s currently dangling off a cliff face looking ridiculously smug. Said the weather was surprisingly good. Good for him. He's a bit of a thrill seeker, isn’t he? You know what we say back home?

Right, so, the playlist for Saturday… I was thinking a bit of everything? Some of those 80s songs your Dad loves, a bit of current stuff, maybe some Disney for the little ones? Can we have the  Frozen  songs? Please! And the one from  Moana ! Of course, sweetie. Definitely. Both of them. And maybe a little bit of ABBA? ABBA’s boring. Oh, come on! Your Grandma loves ABBA. And it’s good dancing music! We need good dancing music for a party. I want the loud music! Like… like rock music! We’ll have some of that too, don’t worry. Balance is key. Now, about the photos… I was thinking we could try and recreate some old family photos? You know, the ones from when  I  was little? Ooh! Like the one of you dressed as Alice in Wonderland? YES! Exactly like that! I think I still have the dress somewhere… though it might be a bit small now. We could do a mini photoshoot in the garden if the weather’s nice. Can I be the Mad Hatter? You could be  anything  you want to be. The Mad Hatter, the White Rabbit, the Cheshire Cat… whatever you like. We just need to find a hat! I want to be the Queen of Hearts! And I’ll shout “Off with their heads!” Okay, okay, we’ll definitely need to supervise the Queen of Hearts. Now, food-wise, I’m making a big lasagna, and your Dad’s doing the salads. Any requests? Pizza! Can we have pizza too? We could order a pizza, yes. But eat your lasagna first! Remember what happened last time you refused to eat your vegetables? You said no dessert! That's right! No dessert if you don’t eat your greens. Speaking of which… please, no swearing at the party. I know you both pick up words from… well, everywhere. But let's try and keep it polite, okay? Especially with Grandma around. But sometimes it just  comes  out! I know, I know, it's a habit. Just try to think before you speak. Okay? Good. Now, on a completely different note, have you two seen the video of Auntie Sarah doing the aerial hoop? The shiny circle thing? It looked scary! It is a bit scary! She’s very brave. She’s training for a show. It reminded me of that muddy obstacle course we did last summer… remember how covered in mud you both were?

Honestly, the roulade’s gone down a treat, hasn’t it? Little vultures, the pair of 'em! They’ve earned it, Arthur. Those exam results weren’t handed to them on a silver platter, you know. Though, Elsie, darling, you did look a bit pale when you opened yours. Rightly so, Mum. GCSEs are serious business. But honestly, both did brilliantly. Especially considering the disruption over the last few years. Proud of you two. It was a relief, honestly. I thought I’d failed Maths! Mr. Peterson makes it sound like the end of the world if you get anything less than a 7. He  does ! He’s so dramatic. I was just glad to be done with the exams. Now I can actually enjoy the summer. Enjoy the summer? What about thinking about what you want to  do  with yourselves? That’s what we were at your ages. I was just itching to get out and find a proper job, even if it was down the factory. Oh, Arthur, don’t start with the factory stories again. They've got options now, thank goodness. Elsie’s talking about A-Levels, and Maisie’s leaning towards a vocational course, isn’t she? Maisie’s showing a real aptitude for the creative arts. The photography course she's looking at is excellent. And Elsie, you’ve always been a bookworm. A-Levels seem a natural fit. I think I want to do English Lit, History and maybe Psychology. I like figuring people out. I want to do something practical. My friend Chloe’s doing a hair and beauty course, and it looks amazing! All the Instagram pictures are incredible. Though, Mum, you'd probably have a fit if I came home with bright pink hair. Well, let's not go  too  wild, dear. A subtle colour, perhaps. Speaking of pictures, I saw you tweeting photos from that football match last weekend, Maisie? Oh, yes! She managed to get some excellent shots of the winning goal. She’s got a good eye, that one. It was so exciting! The atmosphere was amazing. Although, Elsie and I had a play fight on the way home and nearly ended up in a ditch! It was your fault! You started it! And then you tripped over your own feet. Did not! Play fights, eh? Reminds me of your father and I, always scuffling about. Though we usually ended up arguing over the telly.

Right, your move, love. Don’t think too long, I haven’t got all day. Though, honestly, this is a much better morning than I anticipated. That rain last night really did the garden some good. Hmm. Okay, okay. Moving my horse… there. Bit of a defensive manoeuvre, I think. And yes, the garden  does  look good. Properly soaked through. Did you get the recording of the BBC Breakfast news this morning? I set it for you. Oh, good lad. I wanted to hear what they said about that new policy on… well, everything, really. Seems like things are getting more complicated by the minute. Though, I swear, they just repeat the same things, slightly differently. They do. It’s all just noise. Honestly, sometimes I wish I hadn’t bothered with a smart speaker. Used to just read the paper with my breakfast. Speaking of breakfast, did you two manage something decent? I just had toast. I had a proper full English. Felt like I deserved it after marking essays until late. One student’s attempt at analysing Keats was… optimistic, shall we say. Optimistic is one word for it. Ha! I had a bit of bacon and egg myself. And a proper mug of tea. Not one of those fancy herbal infusions your sister’s always on about. Oh, don’t get me started on Brenda and her ‘detox teas’. Honestly. She's convinced they’re the secret to eternal youth. Reminds me of old Mrs. Higgins, always swearing by cod liver oil. Anyway, back to the chess. You're letting me get ahead, you two. I wouldn’t say letting… more strategically yielding! Actually, Dad, I was reading about South Korea the other day, and they're huge on strategy games. Apparently, baduk – that’s like Go – is almost a national pastime. Baduk, is it? Sounds a bit like Chinese chess, doesn't it? Although, this is the proper game, mind. Learned it from old man Peterson down the road. He was a real stickler for the rules. Peterson? Oh, the one who used to smoke a pipe all day and smell of woodsmoke? I always thought he was a bit… eccentric. He used to lecture us all about Winston Churchill, too. Said he was a genius. Churchill's a controversial figure, isn’t he? Lots to unpack there. Did you hear anything more about what’s happening with university tuition fees?

Honestly, the level of English some of my online students have… it’s astonishing. And they  pay  me to tell them what a gerund is. Oh, tell me about it. I had one yesterday who genuinely thought ‘affect’ and ‘effect’ were interchangeable and argued with me for ten minutes. Ten minutes! They were prepping for IELTS, mind you. IELTS! Good grief. Well, at least you’re preparing them for something. I’m just…filling time, really. It pays for the occasional pierogi, which, let's be honest, are the main reason I’m here in Poland. Fair enough! Tarnow is a good choice for pierogi. Although, slightly terrifying politically at the moment, isn’t it? All that talk about… well, everything. It feels like Brexit all over again, but with more religious undertones. Precisely! It's unnerving. Reminds me of my aunt, constantly going on about… never mind. It's best not to go there. What about you? Any political debates with your students? Surprisingly, not much. Most are just desperate to pass their exams and get into uni. Although, I did have one student last year who spent the entire lesson trying to convince me that student loans were a capitalist conspiracy. Oh, bless him. He's not wrong, entirely, is he? I mean, the whole system is… predatory. It’s absolutely criminal what they charge young people these days. I’m quite glad I missed that boat. Though, admittedly, my 'boat' mostly involved inheriting enough to last rather than actually having a career. Lucky you! I’ll be paying mine off until I’m practically eligible for a pension. Speaking of, are you looking into yours at all? My mum's constantly going on about state pensions and how they're going to disappear by the time we need them. Honestly, it all feels so far off. And frankly, overwhelming. I delegate that sort of thing to professionals. It’s what they're  for , isn't it? Though I did get a letter about my MOT being due… that I need to sort. It's a slightly more pressing concern than my future financial security. Oh, right! You drove here, didn't you? How was the drive? Long! And quite stressful, actually. Honestly, Polish drivers are… enthusiastic. I was bracing myself for near-misses the whole way. They are a  little  direct, aren’t they? So, where shall we head after this?

Seriously though, Human Sciences at Oxford? That’s… ambitious. Not saying you can’t do it, but it’s a jump from GCSE Drama, innit? Hey, it’s interdisciplinary! I like the idea of, like, looking at things from loads of different angles. Sociology, psychology, anthropology… it seems way more useful than just, like, memorising formulas. What about you? Still dead set on Maths at Imperial? Pretty much. It’s just… the STEP papers are terrifying. I’ve been doing past papers and honestly, some of them look like they're written in another language. But yeah, Imperial’s the goal. It’s close enough to home I guess. Not wanting to be miles away. Fair enough. My mum’s already started looking at student accommodation around Oxford. It's mental. Expensive, obviously. She keeps saying about meal prepping, like I'm going to be a domestic god at uni. Meal prepping? Seriously? You’ll be living off Super Noodles and energy drinks like the rest of us. Remember last year when you tried to make that pasta bake? Okay, okay, that was a disaster. The cheese burned, the pasta was rock solid… let’s not revisit that. I can handle a microwave meal, alright? Still, if I  did  learn to cook, it’d be a good look, wouldn’t it? Impress the girls. You trying to impress girls already? We haven’t even got our A-Level results yet. Just thinking ahead, mate. Thinking ahead. Anyway, what are you having? I’m going for a mocktail, still on the no-alcohol train until after results day. Gotta keep the brain functioning at peak performance. I'm thinking a beer. Just one. Celebrating getting through the UCAS process, mainly. It's been stressful. Plus, Ben and Liam are coming over later to watch the rugby. Wales are playing Ireland, apparently. Oh yeah? You still obsessed with rugby? I thought you were getting into football. Rugby's just…different. It’s more tactical, more physical. And I've been playing again with the school team, you know. It's good to have something to look forward to. That's good. Keeps you busy. So Ben and Liam? Are they applying for uni as well? Ben's doing Engineering. He's got offers from a bunch of places. Liam’s taking a gap year, travelling around South America. Proper adventurous. Jealous! A gap year sounds amazing.

So, you were asking about National Insurance contributions, weren’t you? Bit of a fiddle, it is. People think it just goes towards their pension, but it's more than that, you see. Yeah, I was a bit confused. It feels like another tax, but… different? And what  does  it actually pay for? Well, it’s a contribution towards state benefits. Your pension, of course, but also things like unemployment benefits, sickness benefits, maternity allowance… things to help folks when they fall on hard times. It’s supposed to be a safety net, really. Right, a safety net. So, it’s not just  my  contributions that pay for  my  pension, it’s everyone’s? Exactly. It’s a collective pot. And that's where the arguments start, isn't it? People say, "I don't want my money going to those who don't work.” But that’s the idea of a society, isn’t it? We look after each other. Or, at least, we  should . It makes sense when you put it like that. But it seems like the government’s always changing the rules. I was reading about the new Health and Social Care Levy… is that part of National Insurance now? In effect, yes. They’ve increased the National Insurance contributions by 1.25% to fund social care and the NHS. Bit of a sneaky way to do it, if you ask me. They could’ve just raised taxes directly, but then people would’ve noticed more, wouldn't they? It does feel a bit… underhanded. And is it actually going to make a difference? The NHS is so stretched already. That’s the million-dollar question, isn't it? They say it will, but I’m skeptical. A lot of it gets swallowed up in administration, you see. And there’s always waste. It’s a massive organisation. It’s just… frustrating. I pay my taxes, and I want to know where my money's going, and if it's actually helping. It’s not like I'm earning a fortune, you know? No, of course not. And that's a fair point. Transparency is key. But governments rarely prioritize transparency, do they? They like to keep things complicated. Keeps people from asking too many questions, I reckon. Do you think it’s deliberate? Like, they  want  it to be confusing? Oh, absolutely deliberate. It's a way of controlling the narrative.

Honestly, this project is just… consuming my life. I feel like I’m living at work. Oh, darling, you always say that! But you're so good at it, aren’t you? Always taking on too much. What’s making it so awful this week? It’s the stakeholders, definitely. They all have  such  strong opinions, and none of them agree on anything! I spent three hours on a call yesterday just going around in circles. It's like herding cats. Ugh, stakeholders. The bane of everyone’s existence. Sounds exhausting. At least  my  days are fairly predictable. Exam season is over, thankfully, so it’s mostly just paperwork and dealing with the occasional parent query now. Though Mrs. Henderson phoned again today, convinced her son was marked down unfairly on his history paper. Honestly, some people… Oh, the parents! I can imagine. Do they not understand that marking isn’t subjective? You’d think so, wouldn't you? She was going on about ‘emotional impact’ and how the question ‘resonated’ with him. Resonated! It’s a GCSE, not a poetry slam! Oh, bless her. Sounds like you handled it though? I did. Politely, of course. Explained the marking scheme, showed her the paper again. She eventually backed down, but not without a dramatic sigh and a comment about ‘the youth of today’. It's always something. It really is. Speaking of things being something… Have you heard from Aunt Carol lately? I haven't managed to catch her on the phone for ages. She was fine when I last spoke to her, about a week ago. She said she’d been busy with the gardening club, getting ready for the village fete. Apparently, they’re trying to win the ‘best floral display’ award this year. She’s taking it very seriously. Oh, that sounds like Carol. Always competitive! Remember when she entered the jam-making competition and practically accused Mrs. Peterson of sabotage? Oh, I’d almost forgotten about that! She was convinced Mrs. Peterson had added too much pectin to her raspberry jam. It was a whole scandal! Good times. It's nice to know some things never change. Are you still going to Sarah’s birthday drinks on Friday? Yes, absolutely! I’ve already got a dress sorted. Though I might need a little help with my hair. I haven’t a clue what to do with it these days.

Right, so I was thinkin’ about Friday night, aye? We could get a takeaway, lass. Fancy Indian? Or Chinese? Ooh, Indian sounds good, Dad. Been ages. Not too spicy though, yeah? Remember last time… I do indeed. I think I spent the next hour searching for milk. It was… an experience. Though, honestly, worth it. Your Dad makes a mean Vindaloo when he’s in the mood. Aye, well, I won't be makin’ one on Friday, lad. I’m retired, remember? Takeaway’s the height of my culinary ambition these days. What about you, Liam? Anything in particular? Not really. Happy with whatever, honestly. Just good to be hangin’ out. Been a busy week with work. Had a right nightmare with a new client – completely unrealistic expectations. Oh, tell me about it. Applications are  killing  me. I’ve sent out, I don’t know, twenty this week. And mostly just… silence. One rejection email, very polite, but still. It's demoralising. Ah, that’s rough, pet. What sort of jobs are ye applyin’ for? Still stickin’ with the corpus linguistics stuff? Yeah, mostly. There’s a couple that are a bit more general admin, just to get something, anything. But I really want to use my degree, y’know? It feels… wasted otherwise. You're brilliant at what you do, Chloe. Someone will snap you up. It's a tough market, though, that's for sure. I mean, even  I  had to fight for this job. He’s right, lass. Don’t you fret. You're a clever girl. Reminds me of your Gran, always had her head in a book. Speaking of old memories, did I ever tell ye about the time your Gran tried to recycle glass bottles… in the cardboard bin? Oh, Dad! No, I don’t think so. Aye, she was convinced it was all the same. Nearly gave the bin men a heart attack. She was a character, that woman. Sounds like it. My Nan was the same - always tryin’ to fix things with duct tape. Anything and everything. They all have their quirks, don't they? Actually, talking about things needing fixin' – have you seen my iPod? I swear I left it on the coffee table but it’s vanished. Check behind the sofa, pet. That’s where everything goes to die in this house. Dust bunnies, remote controls, lost hopes and dreams… Sounds about right.

Honestly, I’m still recovering from that conference. My feet are  killing  me. Three days of standing and smiling… it’s exhausting. Tell me about it! I was starting to think I’d permanently fused to my sensible shoes. Though, yours were probably worse, weren't they? All that demonstrating phonetics with the little mirrors and tongue twisters… Don’t even  start  on the tongue twisters. Old Man McGregor’s mouthwash is going to haunt my dreams. And the mirrors! Honestly, I felt like a primary school teacher again, trying to get adults to understand the difference between a ‘th’ and an ‘f’. It’s the principle of it, isn't it? They’re all supposed to be qualified teachers, lecturing  other  teachers, and half of them can’t pronounce a simple vowel sound correctly. Exactly! And the worst part was the keynote speaker. Professor Armitage, remember? The one who supposedly revolutionized TEFL with his ‘immersive experiential learning’ method? Oh,  him . Yes. The one who spent forty-five minutes talking about the emotional connection he has with his rubber duck. You’re so brutal! But yes! Forty-five minutes. And then he showed us a PowerPoint presentation of photos of the duck… in different hats. I kid you not. Different. Hats. I thought I was going mad. I kept looking over at Sarah from the college, and we were exchanging these bewildered glances. I’m pretty sure she was sketching caricatures of the duck in her notebook. I wish I’d thought of that! It would have made the time go quicker. The only redeeming feature was the free biscuits at the coffee break, and even  those  tasted a bit stale. Honestly. And the workshops… I went to one on ‘Using TikTok for Classroom Engagement’ – apparently, I need to get my students making dance videos about conditional sentences. Oh god. No. Please tell me you didn’t sign up for that one. I lasted twenty minutes. The presenter was, like, seventeen and kept saying things like “It’s giving vibes” and “Let’s get this bread.” I just… couldn’t. I snuck out and found the room with the comfy chairs and pretended to read a journal. Good move. I’m starting to think these conferences are more about networking and showing off than actually providing useful professional development. It feels that way, doesn't it? I got so many business cards from people who are selling “revolutionary” online platforms.

Honestly, this Polish countryside is just… relentless green. It’s beautiful, but after a while, it all just blurs into one big emerald wash. You say that now, but you were waxing lyrical about the ‘rolling hills’ five minutes ago. Needed a photo for Instagram, didn’t you? Don't judge! It  was  a nice hill. And my feed needs updating. Speaking of needing things… my thighs are starting to adhere to the campervan seat. This sitting is killing me. I really should have committed to that Pilates class. You and a million other people. I keep meaning to get back into running, but then I remember how much I hate the feeling of my lungs burning. It’s a vicious cycle. At least we walked around Tarnow a bit yesterday. That cobbled street nearly finished me off, though. Seriously, my ankles are still complaining. And did you see that woman? She must have been eighty, hiking up that hill like she was on a leisurely stroll. I felt incredibly unfit. Polish grandmas are a force of nature, apparently. My students tell me they all garden and walk everywhere. It’s the secret to their longevity. Right. I need a Polish grandma. Or just a personal trainer. Although, realistically, I’ll probably just get another book. I’m halfway through this historical fiction thing. It’s… okay. A bit predictable, honestly. Oh yeah? What is it? I’m looking for something new. I’ve been bouncing between marking essays and trying to decipher Polish road signs, I could use a good escapist read. It’s called “The Shadow of the Birch.” It’s set in Lithuania during… some sort of uprising. Lots of brooding heroes and forbidden romance. It’s filling a hole, I suppose. Though, it’s making me feel culturally inadequate. You? Culturally inadequate? You spent a year living in Italy! That was mostly eating pasta and attempting to flirt with waiters. I didn’t exactly immerse myself in the art and literature. This feels… different. More demanding. Fair enough. Hey, Google Maps says we need to turn off this main road in about half a mile. Do you think we'll find somewhere to park easily in Rzeszow? That’s the million-dollar question, isn’t it? This thing is basically a small house, finding a spot big enough feels like an expedition sometimes. Hopefully, it won't be one of those ridiculously narrow streets.

…and the thing about the pyramids, you know, everyone’s obsessed with aliens, but honestly, the precision of the stonework, the sheer logistical feat of moving those blocks… it points to an incredibly sophisticated understanding of mathematics and engineering. And hydraulics, potentially. We underestimate ancient civilizations, I think. It  is  amazing, isn't it? I saw a documentary about how they think they used wet sand to reduce friction when moving the stones. Genius, really. Though, honestly, speaking of incredible feats, have you been following the research on telomeres? Telomeres? Ah, the little caps on the ends of chromosomes? I’ve skimmed a few articles. The anti-aging thing, is it? Not entirely convinced, to be fair. Sounds like a lot of hype. Maybe, but the science is getting pretty compelling. Apparently, maintaining telomere length seems to correlate with lifespan and overall health. They're even talking about therapies to lengthen them, effectively slowing down aging. Or at least, delaying age-related diseases. Slowing down aging… that’s a bold claim. Reminds me of the alchemists, searching for the elixir of life. Though, I suppose with our understanding of genetics now, it’s a slightly more informed search. Still sounds a bit… fantastical. I know, it does. But it ties into all the stuff we were talking about last week – global warming, resource depletion, the potential for a much longer lifespan. Imagine a world where people routinely live to 120, 150 years old. The implications are enormous. We’d need a completely different energy infrastructure, wouldn't we? Forget fossil fuels, we'd be looking at fusion, or maybe harnessing energy from comets. Comets? Now  that  is ambitious. Though, thinking about energy, Iceland's doing amazing things with geothermal. Should be looking at replicating that more widely. It’s far more sustainable. And speaking of ancient things… did you know the Vikings actually made it as far as North America centuries before Columbus? I did, yes. L'Anse aux Meadows in Newfoundland, wasn't it? It always strikes me as odd that they didn't establish a major settlement. Too far from their base, I suppose? And the local indigenous populations wouldn't have been too welcoming. Likely both. Though their seafaring skills were incredible. Considering the technology – or lack thereof – they were willing to take quite a risk. That reminds me… we still haven’t fully nailed down where we’re going for that weekend away.

Honestly, this coffee is amazing. You’ve really outdone yourself with this new machine, Mum. Thank you, darling. It was a bit of an investment, yes? But worth it, I think. Much better than instant, eh? Your Dad practically lived on that stuff. Aye, that I did. Anything to get me going in the morning. Still prefer a bit of sugar in mine, though. It’s a bit… strong. You and sugar, Dad. It's a love story. Speaking of investments, did you manage to get those vouchers redeemed at that Italian place in Lytham? The one I told you about? Oh, yes! Booked a table for Saturday. Seven o’clock. We should all go, yes? It’s supposed to be very good. They have a beautiful garden as well. Sounds alright. As long as they serve a decent portion of chips. I’m starving after gardening all morning. Those roses needed deadheading, you know. Always a gardener, you are. I was thinking about getting some new sunglasses, actually. Mine are scratched to bits. Do you think I should go to St Annes town centre, or is Southport better for shopping? Southport has more choice, definitely. But it’s a bit of a trek. St Annes has a few decent shops. And we need to pop to B&M anyway. They’re doing good deals on… oh, what was it? Baby things. The highchair! We need that new highchair. The old one’s falling apart. Little Leo's getting too big for it now, isn't he? It’s a miracle how quickly they grow. He is! He’ll be walking any day now. You two are going to be run ragged. Honestly, it’s proper cute though. It’s tiring, yes, but rewarding. We’re still trying to figure out the best way to manage expenses… it all adds up, doesn’t it? Especially with the garden. Your father wants a fruit tree! Well, I do! Imagine fresh apples…or pears…straight from the garden! It’d be lovely. Although, I’m not sure about the chickens. Your mother keeps threatening to get chickens. Oh god, no. We don't need chickens! That’s a whole other level of responsibility. Plus, the mess! They lay fresh eggs! It's very healthy. And it keeps the garden free from pests. That’s what  you  say. I reckon they’d just attract foxes. Speaking of messes, did you read about that referendum again?

Honestly, the state of Mrs. Higgins’ garden. You’d think someone was actively  trying  to grow weeds. It’s a jungle out there. She's always been a bit…relaxed with the gardening. Remember when her rose bush completely took over her shed? Oh, don't even remind me! Old Mr. Peterson was furious. Said it was encroaching on  his  prize-winning dahlias. Such a drama queen, that man. Speaking of which, have you seen how enormous Winston’s getting? Winston? Oh, the cat? Yeah, he’s basically a fluffy loaf now. He nearly knocked over the Christmas tree yesterday when he tried to jump on top of it. Oh no! Did it stay up? I’ve been worried it's a bit wobbly. Leo insisted on getting a real one this year, even though I told him the mess… It did! Just barely. He got a good smack on the head with a bauble for his efforts though. Serves him right. Real trees  are  better, though. Smell amazing, don’t they? They do. It just feels…more Christmassy. Speaking of Christmas, have you finished your shopping? I’m still struggling with a present for Dad. He always says he doesn’t want anything. Nearly. Just need to get something for Uncle George. He’s impossible to buy for. I was thinking maybe a book? He’s been on about wanting to learn more about…German history, I think? Oh clever! He did mention something about the Holy Roman Empire last time I saw him. He’s got a bit of a fascination with that period. Remember that trip we took to Germany with Gran? Vaguely! I was about ten? All I remember is eating an awful lot of sausages and being incredibly bored in castles. That sounds about right. Gran loved all those old places. She was convinced she was a princess in a past life. Anyway, how's work? Still drowning in copy? Pretty much. It's manic right now. Everyone wants everything  yesterday . I'm working on a campaign for a new nail varnish range at the moment. Honestly, the amount of money people spend on their nails... It’s mad, isn’t it? I had a patient come in with acrylics so long they were getting in the way of her being able to do simple things. They looked beautiful, but totally impractical. Speaking of nails, I really need a manicure.

Right, so… officially residents! Feels a bit weird, doesn’t it? Still smells very… new. And faintly of paint. It does! It's lovely though, isn't it? So much brighter than your old place. And bigger! I can actually  move  without bumping into things. Seriously. That studio was…cozy. This is… manageable. Okay, first things first: internet. Have you sorted that out with the letting agency yet? They said they had a preferred provider. I emailed them this morning. No reply yet. I’m a bit worried it’ll take ages. I need to upload that dissertation chapter, and you need to… well, exist as an English instructor seemingly requires constant online presence these days. You’re not wrong. I’ve got like, three online classes scheduled for tomorrow. I’m hoping the wifi is decent even before they connect it properly. Right, shopping list. We are dangerously low on… everything. We literally have three potatoes and a jar of pickles. And half a loaf of bread. We need  everything . I was thinking we could head to that farm shop just outside of town tomorrow? They have amazing seasonal stuff. Apparently, the plums are incredible right now. Ooh, yes! That sounds perfect. And we’ll need cleaning stuff, obviously. And… rubbish bins. Where do the bins go? I haven't spotted any sign of where to put the rubbish. I think there’s a communal area round the back? I saw some wheelie bins when we were unloading. I'll have a proper look later. It's rubbish collection day on Thursday, I think I saw it somewhere in the paperwork. Good. Organised chaos is the goal here. Speaking of organised, I need to ring the bank. Change of address, naturally. It’s such a hassle. Ugh, tell me about it. I’ve been meaning to do mine for weeks. It’s always the admin stuff that gets you. Oh! And we should definitely buy some plants. Brighten the place up a bit. Absolutely. Although… I'm slightly worried about the nursery next door. It's very… enthusiastic. I can already hear tiny voices. Oh, bless! It'll be good. A bit of life, a bit of noise. Beats the sound of traffic, anyway. Although, I did notice a few smokers hanging around the entrance to the nursery during pick-up. Hopefully, it won’t be too bad. Yeah, that’s a bit grim.

Honestly, this burger is  amazing . I’ve been craving a proper one all week. How’s your halloumi and roasted vegetable thing? It's good! Really tasty, actually. A bit healthier than what I initially wanted, seeing as I skipped breakfast, but good. It’s so nice to actually sit down and properly  chat  though, isn’t it? It feels like ages since uni. It really does! Uni feels like another lifetime. Everything was so… chaotic but fun. Remember that trip to Newquay? The one where we ended up sleeping on the beach? Oh my god, yes! That was insane. I think we genuinely thought we could just find a sheltered spot and be okay. And then the rain came. Mum was  furious  when I called her, begging for a lift. Furious is an understatement! My phone call was… terse. She just kept saying, “Why didn’t you book a hotel?!” Still makes me chuckle. So, how’s the placement going? You said you were at that marketing firm, right? Yeah, it’s…interesting. A lot more corporate than I expected, if that makes sense? Everyone’s really nice, but it’s very much ‘meetings about meetings’ kind of vibe. I’m mostly doing admin and social media scheduling at the moment, which is fine, but I was hoping for something a bit more creative. That’s a bit frustrating. Is there scope to get involved in more of the campaign stuff? I’m trying to. I volunteered to help with the new product launch, hoping to get some copy-writing in, but they’ve got a dedicated agency doing that. They said they’ll keep me in the loop, but… yeah. It’s okay. What about you? How's project coordinating treating you? Still wrangling spreadsheets? You know it. Spreadsheets are my nemesis. It’s actually pretty good though. It’s a small team, so I get to be involved in lots of different things, which is good for learning. It's just… demanding. Long hours sometimes. I’m seriously considering a holiday. Somewhere far away. Ooh, where were you thinking? I’ve been daydreaming about Thailand. Beaches, cheap food... pure bliss. Thailand sounds amazing! I’ve always wanted to go. I was thinking maybe Italy? Easier to get to, and I've been trying to practice my Italian on Duolingo. Pathetic, I know. No, that’s cool! Italy would be lovely.

Honestly, this pint is  exactly  what I needed. That commute from London was brutal. Tell me about it. Even getting  into  Cambridge feels like a commute sometimes. Though, at least you didn’t have to battle the M11… that was a car park this morning. How was London though? Any exciting research developments? Work was… work. You know. Endless meetings about meetings. But I did get some really interesting initial data back on the social mobility project. It's grim, honestly. Really grim. Reinforces everything I suspected about postcode lottery stuff. It makes you think about where you’re from, doesn’t it? It does. You get a bit detached here in the Cambridge bubble, surrounded by… well, privilege, let’s be honest. Reminds me why I keep going back to Birmingham. Family, yeah, but also just… reality. What’s the data saying specifically about the North East? Oh, it’s predictably awful. Sunderland’s right down there, unsurprisingly. It’s just… the systemic barriers are  so  entrenched. My mum still says there’s no opportunities up there for young people unless you leave. Bit depressing, really. She always wanted me to stay closer to home, but she also wanted me to have a better life. It’s a contradiction. That’s… rough. My dad always drilled into me the importance of education, specifically because he grew up in a really working-class area of Birmingham. He wanted to break that cycle. It’s good you’re looking into it, though. Actually making a difference. Trying to! It feels small sometimes, staring at spreadsheets. Speaking of small things, did you see what Sarah was wearing to that seminar yesterday? Oh,  that  dress? The floral one? Yes! It was… a choice. Honestly, it looked like something my gran would wear to a garden party. And she has  good  taste, but it just wasn’t right for a post-structuralist theory seminar. You are savage. She does have a… unique sense of style. Bless her. I think she gets most of her clothes from vintage shops. That explains it then. It’s brave, I'll give her that! It’s a lot more adventurous than my wardrobe of various shades of grey. I haven’t bought anything new in months. You always look good though. Simple and classic. I’m more of a t-shirt and jeans kind of guy myself. Functionality over fashion.

Gran, did you see what happened in Parliament today? Proper chaos, like. Oh, lad, don't get me started on Parliament. It’s always chaos. Always has been, always will be. Used to be proper gentlemen, you know, arguing with respect. Now it's just…shouting. But this was different. They were practically at each other's throats! Over, like, a new law about… something to do with the environment, I think? Mr. Henderson at school was explaining it, but it went right over my head. Environment, eh? They’re all talkin' about the environment now, aren’t they? Fancy that, after all these years, suddenly worryin' about the planet. It's all for show, you mark my words. Just tryin' to get votes. But isn’t it important to look after the planet? Everyone says it is, and with the weather being all weird lately… Aye, important it is. But they wouldn't be worryin’ if it didn’t get ‘em re-elected, would they? Back in my day, we didn’t have all this fuss. We just got on with things. Mind you, things  were  different. Less plastic, for a start. Everything came in glass bottles. Dad said you used to get milk delivered in glass bottles? That sounds cool. Cool? It was normal! Every mornin’, the milkman would leave ‘em on the doorstep. And proper cream on top, you could scoop it off with a spoon! Not like this watery stuff you get now. And the bottles were washed and used again, not thrown away like everything else. That’s a good idea. Maybe they should bring that back. Do you think… do you think politicians even  care  about stuff like that? Care? They care about power, lad. That’s all they care about. And money, of course. Don't you ever think they’re normal folk like you and me. They're a different breed altogether. Remember old Mr. Bailey down the street? He stood for Parliament once, a long time ago. Said he wanted to make a difference. Lasted about six months before he said it was all a load of…well, I won't repeat it. What did he say? Oh, never you mind. It wasn't very polite. Just that he realised they were more interested in lining their own pockets than helping people. He went back to fixin' clocks, which he was much better at, anyway.

Now, that was a fine stew, Mary. A  very  fine stew. Though, young master Leo here seemed to be… excavating for treasure with his spoon, rather than  eating  the stew. It’s just…the potatoes are kinda sticking to the roof of my mouth. Leo! Honestly. You're practically making a noise like a tractor. Remember what we talked about? Small bites, chewing with your mouth closed. It’s not a race. Oh, the manners of the young these days! Back in my day, a boy would be sent to bed without supper for that kind of behaviour. A good, firm telling-off was all that was needed. Now, now, Margaret. No need for tales of the old days to frighten the lad. He’s just enjoying his food. A vigorous enjoyment, admittedly. It’s just… good stew, Dad. Loads of it. That doesn't excuse shovelling it in, darling. It's disrespectful to Mary who spent ages making it. Speaking of ages, did you see that blood moon last night, Margaret? A right spectacle it was. All reddish and looming. I did indeed. Went out onto the back step with a wee cup of tea. Gave me the shivers, it did. Reminded me of old stories - bad omens and all that nonsense. Still, a beautiful sight. It was beautiful. Leo and I watched it from the window. He was asking all sorts of questions about space and why it was red. Little scientist in the making. It was cool. Kinda spooky though, right? Spooky is good. Keeps the imagination working. So, are we all agreed on a family outing this weekend? I was thinking Fitzgerald’s Park. We could feed the ducks, maybe get an ice cream… That sounds lovely. A nice, easy day out. Though, Leo will want to go on the swings for hours. Swings are awesome! And the slide! Fitzgerald's Park is a grand spot. I took a whole class of wee ones there for years. Always a bit of a scramble trying to keep them all together. We’ll keep a close eye on this one. Say, Margaret, would you be able to… possibly babysit Leo for a few hours next week? Mary and I have that dinner with the McAllisters, and we don’t really want to drag him along. Of course, I would. I adore that boy. He’s a right wee charmer.

Honestly, the whole Scottish referendum thing… still can’t quite believe it went the way it did. Thought it’d be a lot closer, you know? Did you? I always thought ‘No’ would win, but I confess, I underestimated the momentum. Proper nail-biter though, wasn’t it? Remember staying up all night watching the results come in? Vaguely. I was probably marking essays, if I’m honest. The life of a teacher, eh? Speaking of which, had that interview for the head of department role yesterday. Oh, good! How did it go? You seemed a bit apprehensive about it last week. It was… alright. Not spectacular. A lot of the usual questions, ‘where do you see yourself in five years?’ ‘What are your leadership qualities?’ The whole rigmarole. There was a particularly trying colleague on the panel – Brenda Higgins. You remember her, always a bit… frosty. Brenda Higgins. Oh,  her . Yes, I remember. Thought she’d retire years ago. Still causing trouble, is she? Still causing trouble. Kept interrupting, challenging everything I said. I think she fancies the job herself, probably. Made me feel like I was back in school, being grilled by the headmaster. Sounds awful. They can be right pains, some of those people. Don’t let it get you down, though. You’re a damn good teacher, Arthur. They’d be fools to pass you over. Thanks, Roger. I appreciate that. Trying not to dwell on it, really. Distracting myself. Speaking of distractions… how’s Sarah? Still enjoying university? She's doing well, thank you. Keeps herself busy. Just finished her first term, absolutely exhausted. She's thinking about doing a year abroad, possibly in Spain. Always loved the language. Spain, eh? Good for her. Getting out there, experiencing a different culture. That’s what it’s all about. My own daughter, Emily… well, she's settling into her new job. A bit of a whirlwind, this last year for her. Still with Mark? Still with Mark, yes. They’re talking about moving in together. It's… a big step. A bit nerve-wracking as a parent, you know? Want them to be happy, but also worry about the practicalities. Tell me about it. It feels like only yesterday I was trying to figure out how to get Sarah to eat her vegetables. Now she’s talking about Erasmus programs and gap years. Time flies, doesn’t it?

Right, so, are we actually heading to Mum’s now, or are we doing another supermarket sweep first? I’m starving. We said Mum’s, didn’t we, darling? I’ve got that potato salad to drop off, you know, the one with the dill? She loves it. Dill, really? Seems a bit… much. I’m with Aaron, though. Lunch is a serious priority right now. This journey’s taking ages. Aye, it is a bit of a trek. But it's good to get out of the house, innit? Least I think so. Been cooped up enough lately. Still, this sat nav is sending us round the houses. Honestly, you’d think it would know St Neots by now. Seriously! It's like it's actively  avoiding  the quickest route. And the voice…it's so condescending. "In 200 meters, prepare to turn left." Like I haven’t driven before! Oh, you're just like your father, always complaining about the technology. Remember when he refused to get a mobile phone for years? Said it was the devil’s work. I did not! I just…preferred a good map. And knowing where I was going without a robot telling me. Though, I have to admit, that new telly with the built-in streaming is pretty handy. Speaking of handy, has anyone looked into those student loan repayment plans properly? It’s a complete mess, honestly. I feel like I’m paying off a mortgage, not a degree. Don’t even get me started. I’m still trying to figure out if consolidating makes any sense. It’s a nightmare. All this financial stuff… I wish I’d just learned to become a master board game player. Heard someone broke a world record for the longest continuous Monopoly game recently. Monopoly? Oh, that game ends families, it does. My sister and I haven’t spoken properly since the Great Monopoly Incident of ‘87. '87, eh? Those were the days. I remember when a tenner could get you a decent shopping trip. Now? It barely covers the milk and bread. Tell me about it! I went to Tesco yesterday, and I practically needed a loan to buy a few bits for dinner. It's outrageous. I was thinking about trying to make pasta from scratch. It seems therapeutic, and probably cheaper in the long run. Although, my kitchen skills are… questionable. Oh, I'm a dab hand at pasta making!

Honestly, this road is mental. I didn’t realise quite  how  countryside-y we were getting. It’s like…single track at points. Aye, well, you’re in proper farming country now, lass. Used to be even worse, mind. They’d be tractors blocking the whole thing, farmers having a natter in the middle of the road. No bother now, most of ‘em respect the fact folk need to get about. It  is  quite narrow. Are we sure the satnav knows what it's doing? It feels like we're heading straight for…a field. It says this is the quickest route, apparently. And Gran said the farm shop is worth the detour. Proper local produce and everything. Worth it, aye. Old Man Hemmings has some cracking sausages. Proper pork, not that processed muck you get in the supermarkets. And his eggs…best you’ll ever taste. Free range, you see. The hens roam all over. Free range, excellent. I’m trying to cut down on…well, everything, really. Eating better, more exercise. It’s all a bit overwhelming. Tell me about it. I’ve started trying to meal prep, and it’s a disaster. I end up just ordering a takeaway anyway. Meal prep? What’s that, some sort of fancy cookery? Back in my day, you just  cooked . And you cooked what was in season. Didn’t have a choice, mind. No flying in mangoes in December then! It's basically just cooking a load of food on Sunday so you have lunches for the week. Theoretically. Exactly! Sounds good in theory. Look! Sheep! Loads of them. Wow, there really are. They’re just…everywhere. Those’ll be Hemmings’ sheep. He breeds them, sells the lambs. Good quality stock, he has. Proper North Country Cheviots, tough as old boots. They’re all staring at the car. It’s a bit unnerving. Probably wondering what these city slickers are doing invading their space. They’re used to it. They see tractors and lorries all day. A little car like this is probably a novelty. Though, they’re clever animals, sheep. More than people give ‘em credit for. Do they recognise you, Gran? Are you like…the Sheep Whisperer? Don't be daft, lass. But I've lived around farms my whole life, you pick things up. You can tell if they're content, if something's bothering them. They’re a lot like people, really.

Honestly, this shepherd’s pie is lovely, Margaret. You’ve outdone yourself. Though, a little more pepper wouldn’t go amiss, if you don’t mind me saying. It  is  good, isn't it? Seriously comforting. Proper winter food. And you’re right, Mum, a tiny pinch of pepper… just to lift it. Aye, it’s champion. Reminds me of your grandmother’s, Mary. She could knock up a shepherd’s pie that would solve world peace. Though, she’d always insist on adding a dash of Worcestershire sauce. Ruined it, if you ask me. Oh, your grandmother and her Worcestershire sauce! A woman of strong opinions. Speaking of strong opinions, did young Liam finally manage to drag himself out of bed for his swimming lesson this morning? Eventually. It was a battle. He claimed he was ‘too tired’ after staying up late building something with Lego. Honestly, you’d think he’d run a marathon. Kids these days. No stamina. When I was his age, I was building dens in the woods, not plastic bricks. Though, I suppose times change. Are you still going to choir, Mary? I am, though attendance is dwindling. Old Mrs. Higgins has a bad hip, and poor Father Michael has a terrible cold. It’s hard to keep the altos going, you know. Need some fresh blood. Maybe I should join? It sounds… nice. It wouldn't hurt to learn something new. Though my singing voice is probably best kept to the shower. You’ve got a lovely voice, love. Don’t sell yourself short. It'd be good for you, get you out and about. Keeps the brain ticking over too, remembering all those harmonies. Absolutely. It's good for the soul. Though, you’re always so busy with that transcription work, aren't you, dear? Do you ever take a break? I try to. I’ve started doing a bit of walking again. Just around the village, nothing strenuous. It clears my head. Though getting motivated… that’s the hard part. Motivation's a fickle thing. I used to motivate teams of engineers with promises of bonuses and promotions. Now I struggle to motivate myself to get off the sofa. Retirement is a strange beast. Tell me about it. I miss the structure, the children, even the paperwork. Though, not the parents' evenings. Goodness, the drama! Remember Mrs. Patterson complaining that little Timmy wasn’t getting enough attention because I praised his friend’s maths work?

Right, so Parent’s Evening was… interesting. Honestly, Mrs. Davies seems to think you’re a delightful little chatterbox, Leo, but a bit of a daydreamer. And Elsie, you’re lovely and polite, but your maths is… a sticking point. Maths is  boring . I like numbers! But sometimes I forget what they  mean . See, that’s what she said! You understand the process, Elsie, but applying it to real-world problems is tricky. We really need to work on that. Maybe some extra practice? Five minutes after dinner? Five minutes is a  long  time! Can I have dessert first if I do five minutes of maths? No dessert before dinner, Elsie. Absolutely not. But you can choose what we read tonight. How about a chapter of ‘The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe’? Ooh, yes! I like Aslan! He’s really strong. He is, isn’t he? Speaking of strong, and characters… World Book Day is next week. Have you two thought about what you want to dress up as? I want to be Hermione Granger! With the wand and everything! I wanna be… a pirate! A really scary pirate with an eye patch. Brilliant! We can definitely sort that out. Right, dinner’s nearly ready. It’s shepherd’s pie. YAY! Shepherd’s pie! Can I have lots of peas? Of course, you can. Now Leo, remember what we talked about? No playing with your food. Okay, Mum. And Elsie, please don’t talk with your mouth full. Oh, and… you won’t believe what little Timmy Nelson said to me at pick-up today. What? What? He asked me… he actually  asked  me… what cooked human flesh smells like. Ewww! I know! Honestly! I just stared at him. I said, “That’s a very morbid question, Timmy!” And he just shrugged and said his dad told him. Can you  imagine ? That’s horrible! What does it smell like? I have absolutely no idea, and I don't  want  to know! Honestly, some parents. Anyway, after dinner, Elsie, maths, then we can brainstorm World Book Day costumes a bit more properly. Leo, you can practice your pirate roar. And then can we talk about the circus? Grandma said she might take us on Saturday! Yes! The one with the elephants and the trapeze artists? Possibly. Let’s get through dinner and maths first. Then we can call Grandma and find out.

Right, so, the curtain shop… young Eamon and Ciara, working Saturdays. Honestly, it’s a good thing for them, getting a bit of pocket money, but the manager called me. Apparently, Eamon was trying to convince a woman she  needed  blackout curtains for her conservatory. In July. Oh, Eamon. Always the salesman. He gets that from your side of the family, definitely. Cuh! Curtain! Och, he’s a wee chatterbox, isn’t he? Sounds like he’s agreeing with your assessment of Eamon. He’s got a point, actually. Speaking of chatterboxes, Oisin’s vocabulary is… expanding. He called the cat a ‘fluffy monster’ this morning. A  fluffy monster . Where does he get these things? He’s picking up everything from Peppa Pig, I reckon. It’s a linguistic nightmare. Though, ‘fluffy monster’  is  rather good, I must admit. It’s terrifying. Anyway, birthday party. We need to solidify plans. Are we still thinking the community hall?
