Yes, I booked it for the Saturday after his birthday. It was the only slot left. I booked the bouncy castle too, the dinosaur one he loves. A bouncy castle! Oh, that’ll be lovely. He'll be bouncing off the walls for a week afterwards. Remember when your cousin Fergus had a bouncy castle at his fifth birthday? He ended up with a black eye. Don’t remind me. Fergus and chaos go hand-in-hand. Right, food… I was thinking pizza? Easy, everyone likes it. Pizza’s good. We’ll need to get a cake, of course. I was thinking maybe a superhero theme? He’s obsessed with Spider-Man at the moment. Man! Spideh-Man! He’s got his priorities straight, that boy. Now, are you going to that rugby match next weekend, Liam? I am, aye. Munster versus Leinster. Should be a good one. I managed to snag tickets, thankfully. It was a right scramble. Good, you deserve a bit of downtime. Although, knowing you, you’ll spend half the time discussing IT security with the bloke next to you. It's a curse, I tell you. So, you’re still being bombarded with calls from charities? It’s relentless. Three today alone. They’re getting clever, too. One of them pretended to be a local hospice. Disgraceful. Absolutely disgraceful. And this tax on rented houses... it's a terrible idea. My neighbour's daughter is a landlord and she’s beside herself.

Right, I’m telling you, it’s impossible. Absolutely impossible. I’ve been thinking about it for ten minutes and I can't get it. What’s impossible? You've been muttering to yourself for the last…well, a good five minutes now. Something to do with letters, wasn't it? It's this word game Liam set us. A word with seven letters, where you swap one letter at a time to get to another word, and each step  has  to be a valid word. He said it was 'fiendishly difficult'. Fiendishly difficult is an understatement. Oh, that one! He set that at uni, didn’t he? Drove poor old Sarah mental. What’s the start and end word? Start word is ‘LAUNCH’ and you have to get to ‘SAILOR’. I’ve tried everything. Launch to…lurch, to perch, to porch... it’s a dead end every single time. Hmm. ‘LAUNCH’ to ‘SAILOR’. Okay, let’s think… Don't jump to changing just one letter each time. Sometimes you need to rework a little more fundamentally. Is there a vowel change that might open things up? I’ve tried swapping the ‘A’ for an ‘E’ and an ‘I’, tried changing the ‘U’... Honestly, I'm starting to suspect Liam made it up. Like, it’s just a theoretical impossibility. Nah, Liam wouldn’t do that. He’s devious, but not a liar. Let's see… 'LAUNCH'…hmmm… what about changing the L to a S? Then you’d have ‘SAUNCH’… nope, doesn’t exist. Exactly! It’s all dead ends! It's infuriating. I'm usually pretty good at these things. Word puzzles are my  thing . Okay, okay, don’t get stressed. Let's try a different tack. What about focusing on getting the ‘S’ in early? Maybe a chain leading  to  a word  with  an ‘S’ in it? That’s a good shout. Launch… change the ‘U’ to an ‘S’… Lasch? No. Wait a minute... wait... change the ‘H’ to an ‘S’… LAUNCH becomes LASCNH? Still doesn’t look likely. Okay, clearly that's not working. Ok, think about the letters you  need  to keep. The ‘A’, the ‘I’, the ‘L’, the ‘O’, and the ‘R’. How can you subtly manipulate the others to fit? It’s almost like a little anagram within the larger puzzle. Right, anagram-adjacent. Okay… Hmmm. I’m officially stumped too now. Maybe we need a dictionary...or Google?

Honestly, I think I peaked at napping this afternoon. Like, Olympic-level napping. I was  out . You and your naps! You’ve always been able to fall asleep anywhere. Remember that time at Grandma’s, during Uncle Barry’s really long story about… whatever it was? Oh god, yes! The one about the pigeon? I face-planted into a cushion. He was so offended. Did he ever actually  catch  that pigeon? I don’t think so. It’s a blurry memory shrouded in Barry’s rambling. Speaking of blurry, has Liam replied about Saturday? I need to know if I need to mentally prepare for another one of his… interesting music choices. Nope, radio silence. He’s probably still trying to curate the ultimate ironic playlist. You know, full of Abba followed by death metal. Don’t even. Last time it was Celine Dion straight into Slipknot. My ears haven’t recovered. Honestly, I think he does it on purpose, just to wind us up. Absolutely. He thrives on chaos. Remember that photo I showed you, the one from high school, of him with the questionable hairstyle and the even more questionable shirt? Oh my god, yes! The one with the band t-shirt that clearly didn't belong to him? He looked like he’d raided his dad's wardrobe! Exactly! And he was so proud of it! I need to find that photo again. It needs to resurface. It's a public service, honestly. It genuinely does. It’s a reminder that everyone makes terrible decisions at 16. Though, thinking about it, are  we  making terrible decisions now? Just slightly more sophisticated ones? Debatable. Very debatable. Probably. Speaking of decisions, I saw Chloe at the library earlier. She was looking… stressed. Oh no, what’s up with her? Midterms getting to her? I think so. She said something about her dissertation supervisor being… particularly unhelpful. Apparently, he keeps changing his mind about what he wants. Oh, that’s awful. Professor Davies is a nightmare. I heard Sarah had similar issues with him last year. He just seems to enjoy making people miserable. Exactly! It’s like a power trip for him. Poor Chloe's been working so hard. We should probably go check on her later, maybe take her a coffee and a biscuit. Good idea. Although, knowing Chloe, she'll probably just want to rant for an hour.

Right, so I’ve been through the council planning committee minutes from last month, and honestly, it's a bit of a mess. A mess how? Specifically, because I’m trying to mentally prepare for having to actually  speak  at the meeting next week. The thought fills me with dread. Well, for starters, the notes are incredibly sparse. Apparently, there was a lot of back and forth about the access road, but it’s just written as ‘access concerns – further discussion needed.’ Doesn’t tell us  what  the concerns were. Fantastic. So, we’re walking in blind. And did old Mr. Henderson turn up and try to derail everything again? He was there. He didn’t actively derail it, but he asked about seventeen questions about the potential impact on badgers. Seventeen! Apparently, he’s a self-proclaimed badger expert. Of course, he is. Right. Okay. So, we need to assume they’re still worried about the access road. What did our traffic assessment say again? It said it’s perfectly adequate for the anticipated level of traffic. They’re worried about congestion during school drop-off and pick-up times, which is fair, but we addressed that in the revised plans with the staggered entry system. And the turning circle? That was another point they laboured over last time. Plenty big enough. We even included a visual showing a refuse lorry navigating it without issue. Honestly, I’m starting to think some of these councillors just enjoy arguing. It wouldn't surprise me. Okay, so we go in armed with the traffic assessment, the updated plans, and a firm but polite reiteration of the refusal reason rebuttal. We need to be concise. They get bored easily. Exactly. And we need to be prepared for Henderson and his badgers. I’ve found a report on local badger populations. Just in case we need to counter his claims. Good thinking. Speaking of being prepared, have you finalised the selling points for the house? I’ve been meaning to sit down and really flesh them out. I’ve got a draft. 'Charming period cottage, excellent school catchment area, quiet residential street, close to amenities...' You know the drill. I need to add something about the garden being south-facing. Definitely. That’s a big one. And the newly renovated kitchen. People love a renovated kitchen. We've put a lot of work in.

Honestly, this soup is… underwhelming. I followed the recipe  exactly . It just tastes like vaguely orange water. Oh dear. You and cooking, eh? Remember that time you tried to make a Victoria sponge and it resembled a pancake? Hey! That was one time! And the oven was faulty. Besides, I’ve improved. Sort of. Anyway, enough about my culinary failings. How was your shift? Dreadful, I presume? You know what, it wasn't  too  bad. Old Mr. Henderson was particularly chatty, regaling me with stories of his youth. Apparently, he was a ballroom dancer. No way! That's lovely. He always seems so… grumpy. Speaking of grumpy, have you seen Mrs. Peterson’s new garden gnome collection? It’s escalating. There are, I counted,  seven  now. Seven! Oh my god, really? She’s building an army of them! I swear, she just wants to wind up Mr. Davies next door. Remember when they had that epic feud over the hedge height? How could I forget? It was front-page news in the local newsletter! Anyway, did you manage to speak to Chloe? I haven’t seen her in ages. I did, actually! She’s doing really well. Apparently, she got promoted at work. She’s a bit stressed, though, said her boss is a nightmare. Sounds like some things never change. Haha, classic Chloe. Always landing the difficult jobs. We should all go out for drinks, the old gang. It feels like we never see each other anymore. That’s a brilliant idea! I’m free next Saturday. We could try that new tapas place on High Street - I've heard good things. Ooh, yes! Perfect. I need a proper night out. This week has been relentless at work. They keep piling on more projects. It’s exhausting. Tell me about it. It’s the same in my job. Always short-staffed, always under pressure. Oh, and I saw Liam from uni the other day.  Liam ? Oh wow. How is he? Still trying to be a rock star? Surprisingly not! He’s a solicitor now, can you believe it? Very sensible haircut, suit and everything. He asked after you, said he still remembers when you accidentally set off the fire alarm during fresher's week. Oh, don’t remind me! That was mortifying. He’s forgiven me, then? I was convinced I’d ruined his entire university experience. Apparently so. He seemed… settled, which is a change.

…and honestly, the advert was just  begging  to be taken down. That bloke trying to sell washing powder looking like he’d just lost a fight with a badger? I mean, come on. You’re still on about that? It was a bit…unconventional, yeah. But memorable. That’s what they want, isn’t it? Something that sticks in your head. Sticks in your head for all the wrong reasons, love. It's actively putting me  off  washing powder. Think I’d rather just live in a pile of clothes, to be honest. Speaking of which… have you seen the state of the bathroom? Don’t start, Liam. I was going to get to it. I've been at work all day dealing with… well, dealing with stuff. You know. 'Stuff'? Mysterious 'stuff'. Is 'stuff' involving people pretending they’re pigeons again? You told me about that last week. It was a metaphorical pigeon, alright? Used in a therapeutic exercise. Honestly. And no, today’s ‘stuff’ involved explaining to someone why they shouldn’t try and self-diagnose using WebMD. It’s a minefield. Sounds…intense. Right, bathroom then. I’ll tackle the shower. You do the sink? Deal. But seriously, we need to hit a car boot sale this weekend. I’m convinced we can find a decent bookcase for the living room. Everything’s just…piled up at the moment. A car boot sale? Haven’t been to one of those in ages! Remember that time your nan bought that ceramic cat with one eye missing? She swore it was ‘vintage’. Please don’t remind me. It haunted the hallway for years. It was terrifying. Still, you never know what treasures you might find. Maybe even a functioning telly. This one's starting to act up again. It’s just tired. Like us. I’ve been thinking though… I saw a course advertised online. NLP. Neuro-Linguistic Programming. Apparently, it’s good for… communicating better and stuff. NLP? Really? Sounds a bit… woo-woo. That's what I thought at first, but apparently loads of people use it. Even in journalism, for interviewing techniques. Makes you think, doesn’t it? Maybe. I'm more interested in finding out how to stop my phone auto-correcting everything I type to complete nonsense. It just changed "dyslexia" to "dandelion". No way! Seriously? Seriously! It’s driving me mad. I was writing a report on it for work, and it was just… dandelion, dandelion, dandelion.

Honestly, this weather is doing my head in. One minute it’s sunshine, the next it’s biblical rain. Makes planning anything impossible. Tell me about it. I was hoping to get the car washed this weekend, but looking at the forecast… forget it. It'll just be a waste of water, and time. Speaking of cars, anyone seen those new electric Mini Coopers? They look properly cool. Though, I suspect the price tag will be… substantial. Oh, I saw those! They’re gorgeous, but honestly, I'm still trying to wrap my head around the whole electric car thing. Where do you even  charge  them properly if you don’t have off-street parking? It's a nightmare in London. Yorkshire’s getting better with charging points, slowly. Though, it’s mostly in the bigger towns. Out in the Dales… you’re a bit stuck. Anyway, anyone actually  listening  to good music these days? I’ve been stuck in a 90s nostalgia loop. Oh god, me too! I rediscovered Spice Girls the other week. Don't judge. Reminded me of being twelve. But honestly, the algorithm is just feeding me the same things over and over. I tried a new music app, 'Flux', apparently it’s good for discovering stuff, but it’s just… cluttered. I've been using 'Tidal’ – lossless audio quality, apparently. Makes a difference, even if you're not a proper audiophile like Ben here. Hey! I appreciate good sound. And Tidal is alright, yeah. I’m more into podcasts at the moment, actually. Found this amazing investigative journalism one about… well, it’s a bit grim, actually. Never mind. Speaking of grim, the housing market is terrifying. I was seriously looking at places in Walthamstow, but even a tiny flat requires a mortgage the size of a small country. Don’t even get me started. My partner and I have been saving for ages, and it feels like we’re just running to stand still. It's… demoralising. It is. I’m renting at the minute, and honestly, it's freeing. But that freedom comes at a price, doesn’t it? You're just throwing money away. It's a tough one. We managed to get on the ladder a few years ago, but even then it felt like winning the lottery. And the interest rates now… scary. I’ve been meaning to ask, Amelia , how’s the new job going?

…and honestly, the houses around here were fields when we first came. Proper fields. You wouldn’t believe it now, all houses, all the way out to… well, where the M5 is now, practically. It's astonishing, isn't it? We came down in ‘68, and it was similar. Just on the edge, really. Lovely little detached, fairly modern for then, but surrounded by farmland. Finding it was a nightmare though. Tell me about it. Coming for that interview at the hospital… I remember thinking, ‘Good Lord, where am I?’ Everything looked so  green . I’m a Birmingham boy, you see. Used to the smog and the brick. And trying to find the dental hospital was a mission in itself! Eventually got there, though. And got the job, thank goodness. You were lucky. I was trailing around Bristol trying to find anywhere vaguely affordable. All the decent places were snapped up. Eventually, I ended up in a bedsit in Clifton. Tiny little thing, overlooking a car park. Not ideal, but it was a roof over my head. Oh, bedsits! We had a brief stint in one as well, while we were saving up. Dreadful things. Damp, drafty… and the landlady! She used to inspect the fridge.  The fridge , Arthur! Oh, the landlords. We were luckier, found a little semi, needed a lot of work. All floral wallpaper and avocado bathrooms. But it was ours, eventually. It took us years to get rid of that wallpaper, though. Floral wallpaper… that was the 60s, wasn’t it? I had to convince my wife to move from her perfectly respectable little flat. She was horrified by the state of the place. But, you know, potential. We ripped out everything - the avocado suite, the orange carpet – and started again. You’d need a strong constitution for that. I met my wife, Margaret, while marking papers at the college. She was teaching Geography. A lovely woman, always the sensible one. Kept me grounded, she did. I met Arthur at a teacher training course in… oh, Cardiff, was it? A dreadful course, actually. Awfully organised. But it did lead to Arthur, so I suppose it wasn't a complete waste of time. Mine, bless her, I met at a conference. A history conference. She was speaking, and I was… well, largely admiring her. She'd just finished her doctorate. Very clever woman. I was doing my postgraduate course then, actually.

…and honestly, the dust! You’d think being antiques, they’d be…preserved, wouldn’t you? But no, decades in attics, barns… it gets  everywhere . I used to find myself coughing up history, quite literally. Oh, I can imagine. Though my dust came with a different flavour. Schools, mostly. And hospitals. All that chalk and… disinfectant. A very specific scent combination, really. Schools and hospitals, eh? You were a teacher then? I always admired teachers. Such patience. I could never have done it. Too much… chaos. I needed things to stay still, to be beautiful, to have a story attached already. Not a teacher, exactly. A speech and language therapist. So, children mostly, yes, but with… different challenges. Helping them find their voices, you could say. It was incredibly rewarding, even on the frustrating days. And a lot less dust, thankfully. Oh, that’s lovely. Finding voices. That sounds… meaningful. I suppose dealing with objects, pretty things, it  felt  meaningful, but… it often felt a little shallow, if I’m honest. All that fuss over a Chippendale chair. Is it really vital? Vital? Perhaps not. But beauty has its own value, doesn’t it? And preserving a piece of history... that’s important too. Sometimes people need to be surrounded by things that remind them of better times, of craftsmanship, of… well, of  something  that isn’t just the everyday grind. You’re right, of course. I just sometimes wonder if I should have done something… more. When I was younger, I dreamed of being a proper artist, you know? Big canvases, bold colours. But then my father’s health failed, and the gallery needed looking after. It just… happened. Life often does, doesn’t it? Takes you down paths you hadn't anticipated. I always wanted to be a veterinarian, actually. Absolutely loved animals. But my parents… they had different ideas. “Too messy,” they said. “Not a suitable profession for a young lady.” So, I ended up with speech therapy. Not messy, certainly. And very  suitable . Oh, posh parents! Mine were… bohemian, in a way. Very encouraging of artistic pursuits, but equally hopeless at practical matters. Left me with a beautiful mess, really. Where did you grow up, in Australia? Was it very different to Somerset? Quite different. Sydney. A lot of sunshine, a lot of beach. My childhood was very outdoorsy. Swimming, surfing, exploring the bush. Nothing like the rolling hills and cider farms of Somerset.

Right, so onions are diced, garlic’s minced… think that’s the boring bit done. You’re a master with a knife though, honestly. It's therapeutic watching you chop. Years of practice, darling. Seriously, after a twelve-hour shift at the bakery, precisely chopping things is the only thing holding me together. It’s…meditative. So, how was uni today? Anything exciting happen in the world of academic brilliance? Nah, usual stuff. Professor Davies rambled on about post-structuralism for an hour. I think he just likes the sound of his own voice. Honestly, I spent most of the lecture sketching tattoos. Tattoos? Still obsessing over that sleeve, are you? What design today? I’m thinking…a Japanese wave, crashing over some koi carp. Very cliché, I know, but I really like it. Found a really good artist in Shoreditch, apparently they specialize in that style. Sounds amazing! Expensive, though, right? Good tattoos aren’t cheap. Yeah, it'll be a chunk of change. But it’s a long-term investment, you know? Art on my skin. Plus, it’ll give me something to work towards. Speaking of investments, how’s the café going? Still swamped with Christmas orders? Oh, you have  no  idea. It's chaos. Everyone and their mother wants gingerbread lattes and festive cupcakes. I’m basically living on coffee and sugar at the moment. Good chaos, though. Profitable chaos. It's mad, I've had to take on another part-timer just to cope. That’s brilliant! See? I told you going independent was the right move. You’re killing it.  A key turns in the lock and Speaker_3 enters, laden with shopping bags.  Hellooo! Am I interrupting culinary genius? Smells amazing in here. Izzy! No, just about to start the sauce. You’re a lifesaver though – I completely forgot the cranberries! Sorted! And I got the extra-large bag of candy canes. We  need  candy canes for gingerbread house building. It’s non-negotiable. Candy canes are vital. So, how was your Christmas market hunt? Find any amazing decorations? Oh my god, yes. Found this incredible hand-painted wooden snowman. It's huge. Absolutely hideous, but in the best way possible. It  screams  Christmas. You and your gaudy Christmas decorations… Hey! They’re festive! And don’t pretend you don’t secretly love them. Anyway, are we doing the traditional Christmas dinner this year, or are we branching out?

Honestly, Cambridge feels…small, you know? After London. It’s nice, obviously, beautiful even, but it’s a bit…contained. That’s Cambridge for you. It’s designed to be a little world unto itself. A bubble. Did you feel like you got everything you needed from it, though? For the thesis, I mean. Yeah, academically it was perfect. The library access was incredible, and Professor Davies was…brilliant. It’s just…living there. I missed the chaos, the options. The sheer  volume  of stuff happening in London. You are a London boy through and through, aren’t you? I always suspected you’d find it a bit restrictive. So, thesis… how are we looking? Officially finished, or still tweaking? Officially finished, submitted last week. Now it’s just… the waiting. The agonizing waiting. Feels weird handing in something you’ve spent two years pouring over and then just… letting it go. I remember that feeling well. Though mine wasn't quite as… existential, I suspect. More about commas and semi-colons, probably. But it's a necessary detachment. You need to be able to let the experts do their job. Easy for you to say, you’re a literary editor, you  are  the expert! But seriously, what happens next? Have you… thought much about after the viva? I have. And frankly, darling, we need to talk about housing. It’s all very well having a shiny new Masters, but you can’t live on accolades alone. Your father and I have been discussing it. Oh, here we go. The housing discussion. Is this going to involve me moving back in with you guys? Because, no offence, but… No, no, not permanently. Though the spare room is always here, of course. We were thinking…have you looked at those new developments near Tooting Bec? Quite reasonable, small flats, good transport links. Foot on the ladder and all that. Tooting Bec? That’s…not where I imagined myself living. I was thinking maybe Hackney, or even somewhere a bit further out, like Walthamstow. Hackney's terribly expensive, and Walthamstow…well, it’s a lovely area but a bit of a commute. Tooting is up-and-coming. And it's closer to us. Which, you know, we’d appreciate. I get it. Close to Mum and Dad. Always a priority. What about Oxford, though? Remember talking about maybe doing a DPhil there? That was a conversation  before  reality set in, darling.

Honestly, the train was absolutely packed. I barely got a seat, and it was standing room only for the last half hour from Peterborough. Worth it though, Cambridge is lovely, isn't it? Oh, tell me about it! I drove down from Lincoln, and the A1 was…an experience. So many slow lorries. But yes, it  is  lovely. It feels…important here, somehow. Especially in the Law Faculty. Important? Aye, it does have a certain weight to it, doesn't it? Been coming here on and off for nearly fifty years, you know. First as a student, then a lecturer. Feels like only yesterday I was trying to navigate these corridors myself, utterly lost. Fifty years! Wow. That’s incredible. I'm still pretty new to Cambridge, finished my Masters here last year. This is my first Alumni Day. I’m a Language Research Coordinator now, working with Professor Davies. That’s fascinating! I’m a Research Administrator, just down the hall from Professor Davies, actually. I graduated last year too. Didn’t realise we had so many new faces at this event. Are you enjoying it so far? Oh yes, very much so. It’s good to see the Faculty thriving. I’ve been spending a lot of time recently, well, since I officially ‘retired’ – although I'm still giving the odd lecture – on a bit of a personal project. Archeology, you see. Oh, really? That's so interesting! What sort of archeology? Mostly local stuff. Shropshire, where I grew up. We've been excavating a small village site, dating back to the early medieval period. Remarkable what you can learn from a few broken potsherds and the layout of a longhouse. It's almost…linguistic, in a way. Deciphering a past culture from fragments. I can see that connection. We deal with interpreting meaning from fragments all the time, just with different kinds of data! Are you finding anything particularly exciting at the dig site? We unearthed a rather unusual brooch, a few weeks ago. Definite Arab influence. Highly polished silver, intricate designs. Suggests trade links further afield than we previously thought. It’s sparked a whole new line of inquiry. Makes you wonder about the stories behind the object. That’s amazing. It’s incredible how things like that can completely rewrite what we thought we knew. I actually did a small project looking at the influence of Arabic on medieval Spanish during my undergrad.

Honestly, this marking is killing me. Three essays on post-structuralism due Friday. Three! It's like they think I have no life. Three essays? Oof. Sounds rough. At least you  have  a clear deadline. I was up ‘til midnight last night piping roses onto bloody cupcakes. A wedding order, naturally. Turns out ‘rustic chic’ involves a  lot  of precision. Tell me about it. Ran out of oat milk  again  this morning. Absolute chaos. Had a woman threaten to leave a one-star review because she couldn’t have a flat white with oat milk. A FLAT WHITE. People are wild. You lot sound stressed. I’m just wading through endless Zoom calls trying to convince someone that a colour grade is  essential  to a documentary about artisanal cheese making. Honestly. Artisanal cheese? That’s… specific. I was scrolling through TikTok earlier and saw this video of a bloke building a fully functional shed out of cardboard. Went viral. Millions of views. Makes you question everything, doesn’t it? Like,  I’m  working towards a Master's, and this guy is building sheds out of cardboard and becoming famous. Classic TikTok. All it takes is one weird skill and suddenly you’re an influencer. Remember that girl who just… organised things? Colour-coded her spice rack, rearranged her stationery. Millions. It's because everyone's feeling overwhelmed, innit? They want to watch someone else bring order to chaos. Makes them feel better. Speaking of chaos, I was having a chat with old Mr. Henderson today, the bloke who runs the bookshop, and he was going on about how young people don't have any work ethic anymore. Oh, here we go. The classic generational moan. Right? Like, he reckons everyone expects to be handed everything on a plate. I tried to explain to him that the job market’s completely different now. You need a degree just to apply for a barista job these days. Exactly! And the cost of living is insane. My student loan is bleeding me dry. How are people supposed to buy houses? It's all… rigged. It’s a class thing as well, isn’t it? My cousin, she’s brilliant – genuinely talented – but she left school with barely any qualifications. She’s got dyslexia, and the support just wasn’t there for her. Now she’s stuck in a dead-end job, and it's just… frustrating.

Honestly, this pint is  exactly  what I needed. That seminar this afternoon was… draining. Tell me about it. Third years are brutal this time of year. All the existential dread kicks in, and they take it out on you, questioning everything. Did you get the usual "Is this even relevant to the real world?" routine? Oh, relentlessly. And then someone tried to argue that post-structuralism was just a justification for laziness. Laziness! I nearly lost it. It's just… exhausting trying to explain complex ideas to people who’d rather watch Love Island. Speaking of which, are you still hooked on that awful show? I caught a glimpse of it at Mum's last weekend. It's… hypnotically bad. Don't judge! It's a guilty pleasure. A complete switch-off. It’s just… brainless. Which is sometimes necessary after a day dissecting Foucault. Though, honestly, it’s started to feel irresponsible. Like I’m actively lowering my IQ. You’re a lecturer, your IQ is safely secured. Though, speaking of responsibilities… have you looked at the energy bills again? They’ve gone up  another  fifty quid this month. Don’t even. I actively avoid looking at them. It’s like opening a Pandora’s Box of financial doom. Honestly, I'm starting to feel like we’re just working to pay for heating. It's ridiculous. It's the government, isn't it? All talk and no action. They promised to cap prices, and it's just… nonsense. They're too busy arguing amongst themselves to actually do anything useful. Exactly! And then they have the gall to talk about “fiscal responsibility”. It's just infuriating. I saw a headline today about another tax cut for the wealthy… honestly, it’s breathtaking. It's always the same, isn’t it? Trickle-down economics doesn't trickle, it just… evaporates into offshore accounts. I'm starting to think we should just move to a yurt and live off the land. A yurt in Norfolk? You'd be eaten alive by midges. And you’d complain about the lack of decent Wi-Fi. Fair point. Though, honestly, a week without emails wouldn't be the worst thing in the world. I was talking to Mark from History earlier, and he's been having trouble with his back. Apparently, he’s got a slipped disc from hunching over marking essays. Oh no, poor Mark!

Honestly, this quiche is lovely, Margaret. Much better than anything I could conjure up these days. My hands just aren’t what they used to be for pastry. It  is  really good, Gran. Did you get the recipe from one of your cookbooks? You always had the best ones. Oh, a little bit of here, a little bit of there, dear. Mostly Mrs. Higgins from next door, back in Bramhall. She was a champion quiche maker, she was. Though, she used far too much nutmeg, if you ask me. Nutmeg… she could practically  taste  the nutmeg before you did, that woman. Remember when she tried to convince us all that a dash in the gravy would cure all ills? I’ve never heard that story! You two have a wealth of anecdotes locked away. Oh, Stamford was quiet, but Bramhall... Bramhall was  full  of characters. Different entirely. Less… flat, if you know what I mean. More going on. More nosy neighbours too, let’s not forget that. Everyone knew everyone’s business. Still, it had a charm. Speaking of charm, I saw a trailer for a new David Attenborough documentary. It’s about deep-sea creatures. Looks incredible. Oh, David! I adore him. Always so calming. Though, some of those creatures… terrifying! I saw one on the television the other day that was bioluminescent – a sort of glowing fish. Utterly bizarre. The ocean depths are a whole other world, aren’t they? I used to tell my geography students about the pressure down there. They couldn’t quite grasp it, even with diagrams. It’s hard to imagine, isn't it? Everything we know is based on what  we  experience. I’ve been reading about some of the research they’re doing on exoplanets now – habitable zones, potential for life… it’s mind-blowing. That's your science publisher world coming out, isn't it, dear? Always thinking about outer space. I prefer the birds in the garden, honestly. Saw a little wren building a nest in the ivy just this morning. I saw a badger down by the river last week. Bold as brass. Just strolled across the path, didn’t even glance at me. Wow! You're lucky to see one. They're pretty elusive. Your Auntie Carol was talking on the phone the other day about Millie’s birthday. She’s turning… what is it now, Arthur? Five?

So, Leo, what were you up to all afternoon? Didn’t hear a peep out of you once you finished your homework. Just… gaming. Mostly. “Mostly”? That doesn’t sound very specific. Which game was occupying all your attention? Uh, ‘Realm of Warriors’. It’s… complicated. There's a new update, and I was trying to unlock this character. It took ages. Realm of Warriors, is it? Sounds… intense. Not much fresh air involved in that, I presume? Not really. Unless you count the virtual air in the game. Very funny. We were out with little Finn this afternoon. Tried to get him to appreciate the park. He mostly just wanted to eat leaves. Ah, the classic toddler experience! Finn's a little explorer, that one. Did you manage a proper walk, or was it just a series of stops to investigate interesting bits of foliage? It was… punctuated by foliage investigations. And attempts to throw pebbles. And a very strong desire to run towards any dog we encountered. He's a handful, but a lovely handful. He’s cute. He was trying to give me a cuddle earlier, but his hands were covered in… something. Probably biscuit crumbs and remnants of a rogue carrot. He's a messy eater, our Finn. Did you see him with his soft toys earlier? He was having a full-on conversation with Mr. Bear. Oh yes! He was giving Mr. Bear very serious instructions. I think he was telling him to guard the sofa from… well, I’m not sure what. He often assigns Mr. Bear important duties. He's always dragging Mr. Bear around. Poor Bear's looking a bit worse for wear, isn’t he? One of his eyes is hanging off. That's a repair job for tomorrow, I think. I’m handy with a needle and thread. Maybe we can get Finn involved. He might enjoy “helping”. That would be…chaotic. But sweet. He  loves  helping, even if his helping usually involves adding more mess to the situation. He tried to ‘help’ me build my Lego Star Wars ship last week. It ended up with random bricks stuck to everything. See? Proof. A little bundle of energy, that boy. And you, young man, might consider putting down the controller and joining us for a walk tomorrow. Fresh air will do you good. Maybe. Depends if there’s a double XP weekend on.

Right then, are we all set for the journey tomorrow? Didn’t realise it was Christmas Eve already, didn’t I? Time just… vanishes. Nearly! Just need to remember to pack those little Christmas crackers I got. And your good scarf, Arthur, it gets  bitter  up there. Bitter? You two are soft. I’ve faced worse in February in Birmingham. Though, I admit, Norfolk winds have a certain… bite. Are we  still  talking about the journey? It’s three hours! And I have to sit in the back with Lily. Hey! It’s not  that  bad. We can listen to music. And maybe Dad will tell us one of his awful jokes. Awful? My jokes are classics! Did you hear the one about the snowman? Oh, Arthur, not now. Let the girls have a peaceful journey. We just want to get to Bethany’s without any… incidents. Speaking of Bethany, how's young David getting on? Still glued to his horse, I presume? He's obsessed! He spends every weekend at the stables now. He’s already planning what he’s going to do with it when he’s old enough to compete properly. It's kind of sweet, actually. Though he does smell permanently of hay. Young love, eh? It’s lovely to see him having something he’s passionate about. Still, Bethany's art is lovely too, isn't it? Remember those watercolors she did of the beach last summer. Very good, very good. Though she always was a bit of a messy one, Bethany. Remember when she painted the dog? Old Buster was never the same. I do indeed. Poor Buster looked like a Jackson Pollock painting for weeks. Grandad, you are  so  mean! Mean? I'm just recalling facts! And speaking of facts, did you remember to get the car serviced, Michael? Don’t want a breakdown halfway up the A1. Already done, Arthur. Booked it in last week. New oil, filters, the whole shebang. Should be good as gold. Though, the mechanic did say something about the brake pads needing attention soon. Oh dear. Another expense. Still, it’s better safe than sorry. Christmas dinner won’t be much fun if we’re stranded on the motorway. Christmas dinner is the best bit anyway. Bethany’s mum makes the  best  roast potatoes. Seriously. And Bethany always gets those little cocktail sausages! They’re the best part.

Honestly, the shift was  mental . Old Mrs. Higgins decided she was a mermaid again, and insisted on being wheeled to the window to ‘call her pod’. A mermaid, you say? Sounds… invigorating. Still, beats a departmental meeting, I suppose. Had young Timmy trying to convince me TikTok is a vital business tool today. Oh god, Timmy. He’s… enthusiastic. Though, honestly, some of the marketing campaigns I’ve seen on TikTok are pretty clever. We really should be looking at it. TikTok? At the hospital? You’re joking. The patients would be filming everything! She has a point. We'd be trending for all the wrong reasons. Speaking of trending, have you heard back from Sarah about Saturday? She was on about a pottery class. She texted earlier, she’s in! Said she’s always wanted to try it. Apparently, it’s really therapeutic. Though knowing Sarah, it’ll end in competitive throwing and someone getting covered in clay. Oh, definitely. Remember her attempting watercolour painting? The kitchen looked like a Jackson Pollock had exploded. What are we doing for dinner, by the way? I’m starving. I only managed a biscuit and a coffee at work. I was thinking Shepherd's Pie. Comfort food after a day dealing with mermaids and over-enthusiastic millennials. Does that sound good? Sounds perfect! Though, are we having Aunt Carol over? She mentioned something about wanting to show off her new… hat. Please no. The last hat involved feathers and a miniature lighthouse. I still have nightmares. You’re terrible! But yes, Carol's confirmed. She said it’s “a statement piece.” I’m bracing myself. Right. Well, I’ll start prepping the veg then. Oh! And I need to get a gift for Dave. His birthday's next week, isn’t it? I’m completely clueless. He said he ‘doesn’t need anything’. Which, as we all know, is code for ‘I want something expensive and you have to guess what it is’. Classic Dave. Maybe something outdoorsy? He was going on about wanting a new barbeque last time I saw him. Good shout, Amelia. Or perhaps those fancy noise-cancelling headphones? He's always complaining about your mother’s… enthusiastic gardening. My mother's gardening is a passion! And he just needs to embrace a bit of birdsong. Although, the headphones might be a lifesaver. A barbeque  is  practical. Maybe a nice one, with all the fancy gadgets?

Honestly, Doreen, you wouldn’t believe the fuss old Margaret’s made. Apparently, Bernard’s been seen having a right cosy natter with that woman from the WI - Patricia, is it? Oh, not again. Bernard? He's always been a flirt, hasn't he? Margaret needs to get a grip, really. It’s probably just a bit of harmless village gossip blown all out of proportion. It  is  a bit much, isn’t it? People get so worked up over nothing. Though, I will say, Bernard does have a way of… engaging with the ladies. Remember that incident at the church fete? Oh, don’t remind me! He nearly auctioned off the vicar’s wife’s prize-winning marrow to the highest bidder, with himself offering increasingly ridiculous amounts. She was mortified! Mortified is putting it mildly! Anyway, Margaret’s convinced it’s a full-blown affair. She’s been practically living at the village shop, just to ‘accidentally’ bump into Patricia and give her the stink eye. Poor Patricia. She doesn’t deserve that. Still, it’s a good job we don’t have that sort of drama. Though, I did hear about young Tim and his… complicated situation. Apparently, his wife found messages on his phone. Oh, dear. That's a tricky one. Tim always struck me as a bit… flighty. And his wife, bless her, is a saint. Have you started thinking about the Christmas party arrangements yet? I was thinking we could have it here, as we did last year. That would be lovely. Are you sure you’re up to it, though, with the heating being so temperamental? Remember last year, we were all huddled in the dining room with blankets? The heating's a right state, I tell you. Still colder in here than outside some days. It’s all this new technology, I reckon. Give me a good old coal fire any day. At least you  felt  the warmth. I popped into town earlier for a bit of shopping. Honestly, the prices! It's a wonder anyone can afford Christmas these days. I ended up getting most of the presents from the charity shop. Found some lovely things, actually. That’s a good idea, Doreen. It’s more thoughtful, in a way, than buying something brand new. And it’s good to support the charity shops. Speaking of thoughtful, have you seen that new Big Brother series?

Right, so I reckon another ten minutes on these potatoes and they’ll be perfect. Honestly, I'm starving. This conference at work completely wiped me out, endless back-to-back meetings. Tell me about it. Production's been… manic. Honestly, I’m starting to think they intentionally overload us just to see how much we can take. Did you manage to actually  eat  anything at these meetings, or was it all just lukewarm coffee and stale biscuits? Oh, the biscuits were a highlight, I won't lie. But seriously, I had a granola bar shoved in my bag on Monday, that was it. Hence the ravenous hunger now. Speaking of highlights, did you ever get around to watching that film I told you about, ‘Past Lives’? Oh, 'Past Lives'! Oh my god, Elsie, it was  beautiful . Properly wrecked me, though. I was a mess for a good hour afterwards. The way they portrayed that sense of unspoken connection? Just… wow. See! I told you! It’s just… really gets you thinking, doesn't it? About paths not taken and what could have been. Definitely. It reminded me a bit of my Auntie Maureen and Uncle George, actually. She always said she regretted not being braver when she was younger and travelling more. She met him practically on her doorstep and they had a good life, but she often wondered… Oh, bless her. Auntie Maureen’s always been a bit of a romantic. Did she ever talk about a specific place she wished she’d gone? Italy, always Italy. She used to pore over travel brochures when I was little. Said she wanted to see the Amalfi Coast, eat all the pasta, learn some Italian. Uncle George wasn’t keen on flying though, so it never happened. He was a proper homebody. That's a shame. Still, they had each other, didn’t they? That's the main thing. It’s just sad when dreams get put on hold, isn’t it? It is. Hey, how’s your mum doing? I haven't spoken to her since Christmas. She’s good, she's good. Still relentlessly knitting, apparently. She's working on a blanket for my nephew, Leo. It's going to be huge, she reckons he’ll be able to build a fort out of it. Typical Mum. Oh, that's perfect! She’s the best. Tell her I said hello.

So, have you been following everything with the Scottish referendum then, lad? Seems to be getting quite heated. A bit. Mostly just what I see on TikTok, to be honest. Lots of people saying Scotland should be independent. TikTok, eh? Well, that’s a source, I suppose. It's a big decision, a really big one. More complicated than people realise, you know. It's not just about wanting to be separate. Why not? Seems pretty straightforward. They want to run their own country, they should be allowed to. It  sounds  straightforward, doesn’t it? But then you get into the money side of things. The currency. What happens to the borders, the oil… it’s a right mess, really. Remember when we went to that ceilidh near Edinburgh a few years back? Vaguely. The one where Dad tried to do the Strip the Willow and nearly took out Old Mrs. Higgins? That’s the one! Well, speaking to some folks up there, even then, years before this referendum, you could feel the tension. Lots of pride, obviously, but also a lot of worry about what leaving the UK would actually  mean . So, what do you reckon will happen? Will they vote yes or no? Honestly? I’m not sure. It's neck and neck, isn’t it? The last referendum, back in 2014, they voted no, but things have changed a lot since then. Brexit’s thrown a spanner in the works, hasn't it? Plenty of people who voted to leave the EU now feel differently about being part of a larger body. Yeah, I get that. It’s confusing. My history teacher said it's about more than just economics, it's about national identity. He’s right to say that. It’s about how people  feel  connected to their country. My nana, bless her, she was part Scottish – her mother was from just outside Glasgow. She always had a wee bit of a soft spot for Scotland, always said they were a proud people. But even she worried about the practicalities of it all. Did she ever talk about why they left? She didn't talk about it much, if I’m honest. Said it was a long time ago, and best left in the past. Something about opportunities down south, better prospects for work. That was common enough, back then. People moving around looking for a life.

Oh, honestly. Look at ‘im, thinkin’ he’s a proper hardman. Bet he cries when he gets ‘ome. Seriously! They're all the same on this show. “She cheated on me with me cousin!” Like, get a grip, lad. It's Jeremy Kyle, what did you expect? I don’t understand why we even  watch  this. It’s just… depressing. And the accents! Honestly, some of ‘em you can barely understand a word they’re saying. That’s ‘cos they drop all their ‘Hs! Makes it sound all slurred. Proper lazy speakin’, that is. Like, “’ow much is it?” instead of “How much is it?” Drives me mad. Yeah, it's the elision innit? Droppin’ letters left, right and centre. I was talkin’ to this bloke from down south the other day and I had to ask him to repeat himself like five times. He was sayin’ somethin’ about “goin’ to the pub” but it sounded more like “goyn’ t’ pub.” Goyn’ t’ pub! That’s brilliant! But yeah, it’s true. It's funny, though, isn't it? How much you can tell about someone just from where they’re from, from their accent. It is, yeah. I can spot a Scouser a mile off, even if they're tryin’ to hide it. It’s that distinctive nasal tone. My nan always said you could tell a true Liverpudlian by the way they say 'bath'. My Auntie Carol tried to do a posh accent once. It was awful. Sounded like she was choking on a biscuit. She kept saying “pahth” instead of “bath”, and trying to elongate all her vowels. Mortifying. Oh, don't even. People trying to sound like they're from somewhere they're not is the worst. It’s just…pretentious. Like they think it makes them sound cleverer. This fella on the telly... listen to ‘im. He's tryin' to sound all streetwise, but it just sounds like he’s swallowin’ marbles. You can tell he's not from around 'ere. It’s like they’re layering on the accent, you know? Trying to  perform  it. Just be yourself, mate! It's Jeremy Kyle, not an audition for a play. I reckon Jeremy Kyle probably encourages it, though. Gets more drama. He loves a good accent clash. It just reinforces stereotypes, doesn’t it? Like all people from certain areas are loud and aggressive.

Honestly, the refereeing in this game is absolutely shocking. Shocking! Did you  see  that foul? Completely let it go. Aye, it was a bit soft, wasn’t it? Though I think he’s been fairly consistent with letting things flow, you know? Doesn't want to kill the game with whistles every five seconds. Consistent in being  bad , maybe. They were practically taking chunks out of their ankles over there! It’s a derby, there’s going to be a bit of bite, but that was just… dangerous. Fair enough. It  is  a bit fiery, isn't it? Reminds me of that game between Villa and Blues a few years back… absolute chaos. Bottles thrown, pitch invasions, the whole shebang. Oh god, don’t even remind me. My auntie Doreen was down there! Said she thought she was going to be trampled. She’s a proper football fanatic, that woman. She's started knitting scarves for all the players, you know. No way! Doreen knitting? That’s a new one. So, is it all Sunderland colours, or is she branching out? Mostly red and white, naturally. Though she did attempt a Villa one for your mate, Liam. It… didn’t quite look like a Villa scarf, apparently. More like a vaguely claret and blue rectangle. Oh, bless her. Liam will appreciate the thought, though. He’s always going on about how much his nan supports him. He is. Remember when he tried to explain the offside rule to her? It took about an hour and a detailed diagram drawn in biscuit crumbs. Oh, that’s brilliant! She’s a character, your Auntie Doreen. Speaking of characters, have you been following the Olympics at all? A little bit. It’s hard to get distracted when there’s football on, admittedly. But I’ve seen some of the swimming. That young girl, Summer… what a talent. Absolutely phenomenal. And I’m loving the gymnastics. It's just… incredible what they can do with their bodies. Reminds me, we need to start thinking about baby names again. Oh god, not this again. We’ve been through like, twenty different lists. We'll never agree. I know, I know. But I saw this name, “Olympia”, and it just… stuck with me. It’s got a bit of that athletic vibe, doesn't it? Olympia? Hmm… It’s a bit grand, isn’t it? Sounds like a Greek goddess.

Honestly, the Bee Movie is… a cinematic masterpiece. Don’t look at me like that, Leo. It’s surprisingly philosophical! Bees talk! And they sue people! Is it like King Arthur? Does he fight bees? No, darling, it’s nothing like King Arthur. King Arthur fought knights and dragons. This is about bees and… the human exploitation of honey. It's heavier than it sounds. Can we watch it again tonight? Please? We'll see. Maybe. Right, before we get totally lost in animated insects, did you both see that article about the Royal Family? Apparently, Prince William is trying to modernize the whole fruit-growing operation at Highgrove. Fruit? Like… apples and stuff? Apparently. They’re boasting about new varieties of plums and peaches. "Royal Fruits," they're calling them. Honestly, the whole thing just feels… a bit much. Paying to walk around Buckingham Palace feels pretty ridiculous when you consider we could be a republic. What’s a republic? It’s… well, it’s a country where people choose the leader, instead of it being someone born into the job. Would  we  be the leaders? Eventually, maybe! Sometimes I think it would be easier to just  be  the Queen. No one would tell  me  what to do, and I could have all the fruit I wanted. Or, actually, maybe being a politician is better. You get to make the rules. You would make a rule that we have cake every day! I like the way you think. Though, being honest, sometimes I think I’d rather just be a dog walker like Auntie Margaret. Less pressure. Speaking of pressure, have you both been taking your vitamins? Yuck! They taste like orange sadness. They're good for you! We need to be strong and healthy for the Olympics. Remember we're going to see the diving? The jumping! Into the water! That’s right. But it’s a bit of a rule, isn’t it? These big events? You have to be completely silent during the actual diving. Imagine trying to keep  you  two quiet for an hour! I can be quiet! When I'm pretending to be a ninja. A ninja, right. And speaking of things that require a surprising amount of discipline, remember last week when we tried to take you both to that Italian restaurant? I wanted noodles! But they didn’t HAVE noodles! Exactly! It was a disaster.

Honestly, that tip was chaos. Absolute chaos. I haven’t seen so much discarded furniture since… well, since your Auntie Brenda downsized, actually. Brenda and her…collections. Still, good to get a clear out done, eh? Feels good to be rid of stuff. Though, my back's complaining now. All that lifting. It smelled really bad too. Like old socks and damp wood. You’re not wrong, lad. The things people just chuck away. I saw a perfectly good garden gnome. Perfectly good! Someone’s loss. Did you manage to get rid of all the boxes from the attic, Mum? Nearly. There's still a box of your grandfather’s old lecture notes. History of the North Riding, apparently. I’ve no idea what to do with them. They’re just…papers. Oh, those! Your father always said your grandfather was a bit of a local expert. Maybe a museum in Thirsk would be interested? They're always looking for local history bits and pieces. Good shout, Mum. Thirsk Museum would be ideal. They even have a section on Thomas Lord, you know, the founder of Lord’s Cricket Ground? He was born near Thirsk. Cricket’s boring. Oh, now that’s a controversial statement, young man! Your great-grandfather used to take me to watch Yorkshire play. It was a proper event, you know. Packed lunches, flat caps… a different world. Everything  was  different then, wasn't it? Remember when we went to that auction in Northallerton? The price people paid for old furniture was ridiculous. Aye, and half of it was probably just dumped from tips like that one! People getting carried away. Speaking of ridiculous prices, have you seen what they charge for a coffee these days? This is daylight robbery! Can I have another biscuit with mine? Of course, love. There you go. Though don’t fill yourself up before your dinner. This cafe’s alright, isn’t it? Better than that place near the market. Remember when they tried to serve us coffee in those tiny little cups? Oh, hideous! You could barely get a sip in. And the woman behind the counter acted like we were insulting her for asking for a larger size. They’re all the same these days. No customer service skills. It's all about efficiency, isn’t it? Speaking of efficiency, I’m still waiting for my new laptop. The delivery date keeps getting pushed back.

Right, so I was thinking, for your birthday, we could actually go to that new museum down by the docks. The one with all the…boats and stuff? Oh, the Maritime Museum? Yeah, that sounds good actually. I’ve been meaning to go. Is parking gonna be a nightmare though? Remember last time we tried to go anywhere near the docks, it cost us a fortune. Aye, it’s a right pain. We could get the train, easily enough. It’s only a ten minute walk from James Street station. Save loads on parking, and we can both have a pint without worrying about driving. Good shout. That sounds much better. How was work today? Any particularly…interesting students? You wouldn’t believe it. Had a lad trying to convince me that Shakespeare was an alien. Proper conspiracy theorist. Spent the entire lesson trying to rewrite  Hamlet  with spaceships. Oh, no way! You’re kidding. I wish I was. Honestly, sometimes I wonder if I’m teaching English or intergalactic diplomacy. What about you? How was the assessment centre? All go smoothly? Yeah, it wasn’t awful. The group exercise was… chaotic. Everyone trying to talk over each other. I think I managed to get a few good ideas across, though. And the interview was okay. They seemed really interested in my experience at the hospital. Brilliant! Fingers crossed then, yeah? Getting onto that Masters course would be amazing for you. I know, it would be. Although, thinking about it… if I get accepted, it means moving to Manchester. Oh. Right. Manchester. That’s… a bit of a trek. I know, I know. It’s just for a year, though. But it’s the flat as well, isn’t it? We’d have to find someone to take over the lease here. And all the hassle of moving… We can sort it. We always do. It’s just…I quite like it here. And I’m starting to get settled with the school. I know you are. It’s just… this course is a really big opportunity. And financially, it could open up so many doors. Have you started thinking about Christmas presents yet? That’s a distraction, right? Trying to be. My mum keeps dropping hints about wanting a fancy new vacuum cleaner. A vacuum cleaner! Honestly. Mine's already asked for a ridiculous spa day. She's a nightmare.

Honestly, this canteen food is…an experience. I think that’s supposed to be pasta. It's just… beige. Tell me about it! It’s like they actively  try  to make things look unappetising. At least we’ve got gossip to make up for it. Speaking of which, did you see what Liam posted on his Insta story last night? Ooh, spill! Liam’s usually pretty quiet online. Was it something scandalous? Not scandalous, exactly. Just…very enthusiastic about his FIFA game. He was livestreaming and yelling at the screen for like three hours. Apparently, he lost a really important match. It was actually quite funny watching the comments roll in, everyone roasting him. Oh, brilliant. He  does  take that game seriously. Remember when he refused to come out with us last Saturday because of a tournament? How could I forget? We ended up at that new cafe on Brick Lane, the one with the ridiculous milkshakes. Honestly, worth missing Liam for. Did you finally start watching 'Heartstopper' like I told you to? I did! And you were right, it's so good. Properly made me feel things. I’m completely obsessed with Charlie now, Darcy’s got good taste, I'll give her that. But honestly, the soundtrack is  chef’s kiss . Right?! Joe Locke is adorable too. It’s just… wholesome, isn’t it? Everything feels so stressful with uni, it’s nice to watch something sweet. I’ve been trying to get my brother to watch it, he’s obsessed with football and thinks anything remotely romantic is ‘silly’. Boys, honestly! What does  he  watch then? Just endless amounts of Gary Neville analysing set pieces? Pretty much! He's currently convinced Arsenal are going to win the league, despite all evidence to the contrary. He was going on about Bukayo Saka for a solid hour at dinner last night. Ugh, football chat. The bane of my existence. I’d rather re-watch ‘The Little Mermaid’ for the hundredth time. Honestly, Ariel is a mood. Oh my god, yes! Disney movies are actual perfection. I’m thinking of getting a small tattoo of a seashell, inspired by Ariel. Ooh, cute! Where? I was thinking behind my ear. What about you? Any tattoo plans? You've been talking about getting one for ages. I’m still waffling. I kind of want something with lyrics from a favourite song. But I can’t commit to a song!

Honestly, Mum, the Charizard card I got today is  insane . Like, seriously good. Old school, you know? Found it at a boot sale for a fiver. That’s nice, dear. A fiver? That  is  a bargain. Though honestly, all these Pokémon cards… they just end up scattered everywhere. Remember when Oisin was obsessed? The living room looked like a battlefield. ‘Zard! Fire! He still likes Pokémon, doesn’t he? He was pretending to be Pikachu earlier, running around making… electric noises. He does. He mimics everything now, it’s lovely and utterly exhausting. He was trying to say “helicopter” all afternoon, it came out as “heelo-copta.” It's adorable. Are you Skyping Gran tomorrow night? Yeah, around seven, I think. Unless I’m busy with… well, with battling. There’s a tournament thing going on online. Battling. Right. Listen, about Saturday… I was thinking, maybe we could go for Ramen? There’s that new place opened on Patrick Street, apparently it's amazing. And we haven’t been out properly just the three of us in ages. Ramen sounds good! As long as I can wear my new jeans. Your… skinny jeans? Honestly, they look painted on. Are you sure they’re comfortable? They  are  comfortable! Everyone wears them! It’s the style. Jeans! Slippers! Don’t be silly, darling, that’s a rather random pairing. He’s got you thinking about fashion now, hasn’t he? Speaking of which, where  are  your slippers? It’s freezing in here. Upstairs, probably. Look, the Ramen sounds great, but can we go after I’ve had a practice with my guitar? I’m trying to learn that solo from… you wouldn’t know it… it's a bit complicated. Of course, dear. We can work around it. Although, if you’re practicing that solo for too long, I might just confiscate the guitar and make you build a Lego castle with Oisin. Distraction tactics, you understand. Harsh! Mum, you wouldn’t. Try me. And, just a thought, maybe after Ramen we could get some ice cream? Little Oisin loves ice cream. Strawberry, specifically. He gets very vocal if it’s any other flavour. Stwawbewwy! ‘Ce cream! Okay, okay, you’ve convinced me. Ramen, guitar practice, ice cream… Sounds like a plan. Just, please, don’t mention the skinny jeans to Gran on Skype. She’ll have a field day. No promises. She loves a good fashion critique.

Honestly, this cupboard is a disaster. I’ve no idea how we accumulated so much… stuff. Look at this! Oh my goodness. Is that… is that the remains of the gardening set? The little plastic tools? It is! Heavens. I’d almost forgotten about that. We spent  hours  with that set, didn’t we? Digging in the flowerbeds, mostly destroying your mother’s petunias if I recall correctly. She was furious! Absolutely furious. Though she pretended to be because Grandad would always step in and say we were ‘helping’. He adored us, that man. Remember the tiny watering can? I always insisted on using the watering can, even if it only held about a thimbleful of water. And you’d spend ages meticulously watering each individual flower. Bless you. I was always more interested in the ‘digging’ part, creating absolute chaos. It’s funny the things you remember. Did we ever actually  grow  anything successfully with that set? I don't think so. Mostly just uprooted things. Speaking of things we never quite mastered, is that a box of Bako pieces lurking in the back? It is! Oh, wow. Bako. That was a challenge. Trying to make anything resemble the picture on the box was impossible. Everything always ended up wonky and collapsing. It did! And the instructions… utterly incomprehensible. We'd argue for ages about which piece went where. I remember being utterly convinced I was right, and you'd be equally certain  you  were. Well, I usually was! No, I’m joking. We were both hopeless, weren’t we? Still, it kept us occupied. It's a shame to just throw it all away though, isn't it? It feels a bit… disrespectful, somehow. Like discarding pieces of our childhood. But realistically, we’re never going to use it. And it's taking up a lot of space. It’s just… hard, isn't it? Letting go. It is. Everything feels imbued with memory. It's not just a plastic gardening set or a box of building blocks, it's summers in Margate, Grandad's smile, your mother’s exasperated sighs. Exactly. It’s all wrapped up in there. Oh, look at the weather now. Absolutely dreadful. Pouring with rain. Seems fitting for a day spent dredging up the past. It does, doesn’t it? Perhaps a cup of tea is in order. We can sort through this another day, when we’re feeling a bit less… sentimental.

Honestly, I think I've got about twenty mosquito bites. Twenty! And it’s only May. No way! Really? I haven't noticed any. Though, to be fair, I'm usually covered head to toe, even in this weather. Protecting the pale skin, you know. Fair enough. But little Leo’s getting munched. I swear I saw one hovering over his pram just now. I’m going to have to invest in one of those net things. A mosquito net for the pram? Is that a thing? Apparently! I was googling frantically last night. They do them on Amazon. A bit ridiculous, but I’d rather look ridiculous than watch him swell up like a balloon. Good plan. It’s just… mosquitoes weren’t this bad when we were kids, were they? No, definitely not. Climate change, probably. Everything's getting worse. Speaking of worse, the traffic getting here was  horrendous . Honestly, I aged ten years sitting in that queue. Tell me about it. I cycled, thankfully. Saw you stuck near the roundabout – looked pretty grim. I waved, but I doubt you saw me. I was in full survival mode. Just trying to merge without getting decimated by a bus. But hey, we made it. And Leo seems to be enjoying the park. Look at him gurgling at that tree. He is a happy little chap. He's a lot more chilled than I am at the moment. I'm still mentally preparing for marking all those dissertations. Oh god, don't even  start  on the marking. I’ve managed to put it off until Monday, but the dread is building. It’s like a dark cloud looming over the weekend. Exactly! I keep thinking about it. I need a distraction. Did you see that The National are doing a gig at the O2 next month? Ooh, really? I hadn’t heard. That's tempting. Very tempting. It’s been ages since we’ve been to a proper gig. I know! It could be a good escape from the dissertation abyss. Plus, it's a date night! We could get a babysitter. Hmm… We’d need to book tickets quickly, I’d imagine. They sell out fast. And find a babysitter that isn’t terrified of mosquitoes. A fair point! I’ll check on Ticketmaster tonight. Maybe we can rope in your mum? She loves a good excuse to spoil Leo.

Right, so I genuinely think I spent more time today trying to figure out why my phone decided to die at 7% than I did actually  playing  golf. It's infuriating, innit? Ugh, phones. Don't even get me started. Mine’s been glitching all day, randomly opening apps and sending gibberish texts. I’m convinced they’re designed to make us miserable. Did you manage to get a practice round in at least? Eventually. Had to borrow old man Hemmings’ phone to call the pro. He was…less than thrilled. Apparently, I’ve disrupted his routine now. He was in the middle of writing a strongly worded letter to the council about the state of the 15th green. Classic Hemmings. Still going on about the green then? Honestly, he writes more letters than my grandma. Speaking of writing, I spent hours today trying to tailor my cover letter  again . It's soul-destroying. Every single one just feels…wrong. What job is it for now? You've applied for like, a million. This one’s for a recruitment agency. Bit vague, but it’s a foot in the door, right? They said they’re looking for grads with “strong communication skills and a proactive attitude." I feel like I’m turning into a walking cliché. You’re overthinking it. You’re brilliant at communications, you aced that presentation at uni remember? The one on… what was it? Pidgins and Creoles? Don't remind me. I spent a month researching that. It feels like a lifetime ago. Manchester feels like a lifetime ago. I miss just…being a student. No pressure, no job hunting, just endless essays and questionable nights out. Tell me about it. I was thinking about that awful house party we went to near Oxford Road. Remember that guy who tried to convince everyone he was a ghost hunter? Oh god, yes! And the toilet was basically a biohazard zone. I honestly think I developed PTSD from that night. Good times. Seriously though, you’ll get something. You are qualified and you’ve got the brainpower. Don't let these agencies get you down. Have you seen what Gemma's doing? She's landed a job at that theatre in London. Yeah, I saw her post. Good for her. It's just… frustrating. I feel like I'm supposed to have a plan, you know? Everyone else seems to know what they’re doing.

Ah, stop that now, little man. You’ll be giving us all a headache with the ABCs this close to dinner. …L, M, N, O, P! He’s got a good voice, though, doesn’t he? Really going for it. He does. It’s…enthusiastic. Though I am starting to feel a bit peckish. Are we nearly ready, love? Almost. Just getting the potatoes on. Did you two have a good day out in the town? Yeah, it was alright. We went to that new games shop, the one near the square. They had a demo of that new racing game – it’s brilliant. Oh, the one you were telling me about? Did you manage to restrain yourself from spending all your pocket money? …Mostly. I got a small thing. A new controller grip. It helps with the steering. Good man. Now, listen, about tomorrow… I was thinking we could try and go see that film, the animated one? The little fella seems to be obsessed with the trailer. Oh, yes, the one with the talking animals? That sounds lovely. But are you sure you’re not working late? No, thankfully, it's a quiet week at the office. Although, ironically, I spent half the day today fixing someone’s printer. You wouldn’t believe the state of it! Printers are the worst. They’re designed to fail. …Q, R, S, T, U! Alright, superstar, maybe a little quieter while we’re talking? Look, there’s a lovely cloud shaped like a dinosaur outside the window. Dino-saw! Right, dinner’s ready. Potatoes, sausages, and a bit of broccoli. Don’t tell me you two are not fans of broccoli. Broccoli’s fine. It could be worse. I’ll eat some. It’s good for him, isn’t it? The best. So, tomorrow then, film and maybe a walk in the park if the weather holds up? Sounds good to me. Maybe we can grab an ice cream afterwards? We’ll see. Don’t get your hopes up too high. It's starting to look a bit grey out there. Ah, don’t be such a pessimist. We’ll have a grand day, whatever the weather. Come on, eat up. Before your sausages disappear. V, W, X, Y and ZZZZ! That’s enough ABCs for one night, son! Honestly, he’s relentless. He gets it from somewhere. I’m proud of him.

Honestly, I walked past his room and just… pants. Full-on pyjama top, but just pants. It’s a look. Oh, bless him. Is he cold? He’s always complaining about being chilly. Mummy? I need a drink! Coming, darling. He’s probably just supremely comfortable. It’s the school holidays, rules are slightly more…lax. Though pants? Really? Daddy! Can we build a fort in the garden? A really,  really  big one? A really big one, eh? That sounds ambitious. We’d need a lot of blankets. And probably the entire garden furniture set. It’d be a logistical nightmare. Speaking of logistical nightmares… I was thinking about the house again. Oh here we go. The grand plans commence. No, but seriously. If we knocked down the little utility room, and extended back into the garden… we could get a proper kitchen diner. A big island, the works. The utility room is vital, darling. Where would we put the washing machine? Honestly, you'd have soggy socks everywhere. We could put it in the garage! We barely use the garage. It’s mostly just…golf clubs and cobwebs. And your hoard of old electronics. Don't pretend that's not a thing. It’s a collection! And I might need those spare phone chargers someday. But think about it. The light! The space! We could even have bi-fold doors onto the patio. Mummy, more juice, please! One moment, sweetie. You and your bi-fold doors. It would cost a fortune. And we’d be living in a building site for months. Remember the bathroom reno? This would be different! We'd get a proper architect this time. Someone who understands the  vision . Can the fort have a roof? And a secret tunnel? A secret tunnel! Excellent idea. We could link it to the shed! That's the kind of thinking I like to see. Honestly, this extension idea is making me feel quite inspired. You're inspired by potential disruption and financial ruin. That's… concerning. It's  investing  in our future! And providing a magnificent space for family gatherings. And potentially, a secret tunnel entrance to the fort. Alright, alright. Let’s not get carried away with the tunnels just yet. Let’s finish our coffee, get the kids building their fort, and then we can casually browse Rightmove for inspiration. No promises though. Casual browsing... that's how it always starts, isn't it?

Right, that’s a bit better. Honestly, the coffee machine in here is a temperamental beast. One day it’s nectar of the gods, the next it tastes like dishwater. Tell me about it, Alistair. More unpredictable than a Welsh weather forecast, that machine. Speaking of unpredictable, I’ve finally finished painting the spare bedroom. Took me long enough. Oh? And what shade did you settle on? I remember you agonizing over greys for weeks. Agonizing is putting it mildly! Ended up with ‘Dove Grey’. Apparently, it’s calming. Though my wife says it just looks like a slightly depressing cloud. She wanted something bolder, a sort of terracotta, but I put my foot down. Too…Italian. Too Italian? You’ve been spending too much time reading travel brochures again, Gareth. Though, I must admit, Italy is calling my name. Been meaning to go back for years. Last time was a conference in Florence, beautiful city, dreadful plumbing. Reminded me of Cairo, actually. Oh, your Cairo days. You've told me stories… Always a contrast, isn't there? Ancient history versus… well, leaky pipes. Anyway, this room. I’m hoping it'll be a proper guest room, not just a dumping ground for Christmas decorations. Good plan. Though, ironically, I'm finding  I'm  the one doing a lot of dumping these days. Dumping grant applications, mostly. This funding round is a nightmare. Application after application, all for relatively small amounts, and the competition is fierce. You and me both. I’m applying for something to extend the simulations on the hadron collider data. It’s a long shot, granted, but if we get it, it’ll be genuinely transformative. The problem is, they want three years of data analysis for the cost of a small car. Exactly! It's utterly absurd. And then they wonder why so much research gets shelved. Have you seen the state of the water companies lately, as well? Absolutely scandalous, hiking up prices while simultaneously… well, you know. Don’t get me started. It’s daylight robbery. My sister lives in a village outside Newport, and they’ve had three burst mains in as many months. She's practically bathing in bottled water. Makes you wonder where all the money’s going. Certainly not into infrastructure. Precisely. It’s infuriating. It really is. I was thinking of writing a letter to the local MP, but what difference would it make?

Right, operation Lego sort is officially underway. Honestly, it looks like a bomb’s hit in here. Everything’s just…bricks. Everywhere. It’s not a bomb, Mummy! It's a castle! A really, really big castle! I’m building the Batmobile. It needs all the grey bits. Where are all the grey bits? Grey bits are in that tub, darling. Though judging by the amount of blue and red I’m seeing, you've raided all the other tubs already, haven't you? Maybe. A Batmobile needs  some  colour. It's a super-fast Batmobile. Batman’s good, but Harry Potter is  better . He has a wand! Can you make me a wand out of Lego, Mummy? We’ll see. After the castle and the Batmobile are sorted. We need to get this under control before Daddy gets home. He’ll have a fit. Remind me again why we bought so much Lego? Because I asked! And because it’s awesome! Can we watch the Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles later? The new one? We’ll see. We might go to the cinema actually. There's that new animated film everyone’s talking about. Ooooh, can we see it? With popcorn? And sweets? We'll see about the sweets. Okay, so, castle pieces go here, Batmobile pieces there… Right, what have you two been watching today? Besides Lego construction, obviously. The Simpsons! Bart is so funny. He always gets into trouble. I watched a Harry Potter one! The one with the dragon. It was scary but good. Good choices. You two have excellent taste in television. Better than some adults I know. Speaking of which, Grandma's house… did she say anything more about the builders coming to do the kitchen? She said they’re coming next week, but she’s worried they’ll make a mess. She said she’s hidden all her favourite ornaments. That sounds like Grandma. Very sensible! She’s always prepared for the worst. It's going to be lovely when it’s all finished, though, isn’t it? A shiny new kitchen for her. Can we go to Grandma's and help? I can help sort the Lego at her house too! That’s a lovely idea, sweetie. Maybe. Let's get this room sorted first, then we can think about visiting Grandma. Oh, and has anyone been sneaking into the Easter chocolate? I swear the bunny’s getting smaller...

Oh my god, you are back! How was Greece? Honestly, fill me in. Did you actually manage to switch off, or were you still mentally at work the whole time? Honestly? It was…needed. I think I genuinely forgot what sunshine  felt  like. And yes, mostly switched off. The first couple of days I was constantly checking my emails, preemptively stressing about things, but then I just…stopped. Forced myself to. How was your weekend with your mum? Did she interrogate potential suitors like she usually does? Oh, you  know  she did. It's a full-time hobby for her, honestly. She barely mentioned my actual life, it was all “Are you seeing anyone nice? Not one of those artists, are they? They never have any money!” It was exhausting. Though, she did bring back the most incredible lemon drizzle cake. Want a slice? It's on the counter. Lemon drizzle? Don’t mind if I do! God, mums are the same everywhere. Mine just subtly implies that I’m going to die alone surrounded by cats if I don’t find someone soon. It's…motivating. Work has been absolutely mental since I’ve been gone. We’re completely understaffed on my ward and everyone’s just running around like headless chickens. Oh no, that sounds awful. You practically saved lives all through the pandemic, you deserve a permanent holiday. Are they actually trying to recruit, or are they just expecting you to absorb all the extra workload? Just expecting me to absorb it, mostly. They’ve posted a job advert, but it’s been up for weeks. I think the pay is a bit low for the level of stress involved, to be honest. Speaking of stress, remember Ben?  Ugh . Ben. The one who thought emotional unavailability was a personality trait? What’s he up to now? Please tell me he hasn't reappeared on the scene. No, thankfully not. Sarah from work is dating him now. Apparently, he’s still the same old Ben. She’s convinced she can “fix” him. It’s painful to watch, honestly. I keep wanting to pull her aside and just say, “Run. Just run.” Oh, Sarah. That’s…a choice. You know what I did while you were basking in the Greek sun? I tried to learn how to make sourdough. You?! Sourdough is the most millennial, pretentious thing ever. And you're…not exactly known for your patience.

Now then, are you sure you’ve got everything you need for school tomorrow? Physics practical, wasn't it? Yeah, Mum, I’ve checked three times. Bunsen burner, goggles, the worksheet… all good. Honestly, you fuss more than Miss Harrison. Aye, she’s got a point, lad. Your mother always was a worrier. Even when you were tiny, she’d check your pockets for bogies before you went to playgroup. Mother! That’s a terrible thing to say! It was germs, not… never mind. It was a different time. And you were a handful. A right little rascal, he was. Always covered in mud. Used to bring the garden indoors, that one. Granddad, you’re exaggerating. Am I? I remember your grandma nearly having a fit when you decided her prize-winning roses needed “decorating” with earthworms. Oh, don't even  start  on the roses. It took me a week to get all the worms out! Honestly, the state of the garden after you two had been… Now, now, don’t get yourself all worked up, love. It's a good garden, still.
