And he was just a lad. Learning about nature, he was. Learning about destruction, more like! Anyway, have you seen the state of the kitchen? I asked you, Ethan, to put your plate away after tea. I was finishing my homework! It's due first thing. Homework can wait five minutes to avoid a mountain of dirty dishes. Honestly, sometimes I think you think the fairies come and do it all. Fairies? Now there's a thought. Wonder if they'd tackle the hoovering. You cheeky bugger, Arthur. Trying to get out of your chores again, are you? A man can dream, can't he? My back’s not what it used to be. Besides, I’ve got a joke for you. Why don’t skeletons ever go on holiday? Oh no, here we go… Oh dear. Go on, Arthur, tell us. Because they've got no  body  to go with! Oh, Arthur. That was dreadful. Absolutely dreadful. Oh, it were lovely! You always tell the best bad jokes, Arthur. Seriously. That was… wow. Right, that's enough silliness. I’m making a pot of tea. Would you like some, you two? And Ethan, honestly, the kitchen. Five minutes. Just five minutes. Tea would be lovely, pet. Strong, mind. And a biscuit, if you've got any of those ginger ones.

Right, so we’re all agreed, bath time first, then we can finish talking about Peter Pan? Honestly, you two have been buzzing about it all afternoon since we finished the film. But Mummy! Tinkerbell is  so  sparkly! And she’s really brave, even though she’s tiny. Yeah! And Captain Hook has a hook instead of a hand! That’s really silly. Did he lose it fighting Peter Pan? He did, actually. The story says he lost it in a fight with Peter Pan, and a crocodile ate the rest of his hand. That’s why he has the hook! A bit scary, isn’t it? Not scary, cool! He looks like a pirate! Is Great Ormond Street Hospital still getting money from Peter Pan? That’s a really good question, Lily. Yes, it is! J.M. Barrie, the man who wrote Peter Pan, he gave the copyright – that means the rights to make money from the story – to Great Ormond Street Hospital. So every time a new Peter Pan film is made, or a play, or even a book, the hospital gets money. Why did he do that? Well, his family had been helped by the hospital before, and he wanted to make sure other children could get better there too. It’s a very kind thing to do, isn’t it? It’s amazing how much money they’ve raised over the years because of Peter Pan. More than all our Christmas presents? Oh, definitely more than all our Christmas presents, clever clogs! It’s helped  lots  of children. You know, they made another film a few years ago, called  Pan ?  Pan ? Is that about Peter before he went to Neverland? Yes! It’s kind of a prequel, it tells the story of how he got there. It’s not quite as good as the original story, or even the Disney  Peter Pan  film, but it’s… interesting. I don't remember that one. Was it sparkly like Tinkerbell? Not  quite  as sparkly, no. It was a bit… darker. More about how Peter became Peter Pan. It tries to explain how he can fly and things. But everyone knows Peter Pan can fly! He has happy thoughts! Exactly! That's what makes his story so magical. Actually, there are loads of different films about Peter Pan. And lots about Tinkerbell too – she has her own adventures. I like the Tinkerbell ones best.

Honestly, this M5 is a nightmare already. Even at this time on a Sunday. Reminds me of the old A38, dodging tractors and holidaymakers all the way to… well, everywhere, really. You always find a way to bring it back to Devon, don’t you, Dad? It’s ingrained in you. Still, at least it’s not as bad as trying to get to Exeter from Taunton on a Friday. That was always a complete standstill. Oh, don’t even. I used to factor an extra hour onto that journey just in case. Remember that tiny cottage we had near Wiveliscombe? Lovely place, but getting anywhere was an ordeal. Wiveliscombe! Goodness, that feels like a lifetime ago. Before your mum… well, before everything. Did I ever tell you about the time I got completely lost trying to find a petrol station near there? Ended up on some farmer’s track, convinced I’d broken the car. You tell that story  every  time we drive through Somerset. It’s a classic. Are you getting enough sleep, by the way? You were yawning a lot at breakfast. Oh, I’m alright. It’s just… getting older, you know. Don’t sleep as soundly. Thinking about things. Mostly about making sure you two are alright. And the grand kids, of course. We’re fine, Dad. Honestly. A bit stressful with the end of term, but that’s normal. And you know how much we appreciate you worrying. Speaking of stressful, have we finalised Christmas at your place? Are we still doing the usual turkey and all the trimmings? That’s the plan. Though your Auntie Maureen keeps hinting she’s bringing a vegan nut roast. Oh, dear. That could be interesting. We can deal with a nut roast. More importantly, are you still up for a house-warming party once we’re settled into the new place? We were thinking maybe January, before it gets  too  bleak. Absolutely! A proper knees-up. We’ll invite everyone. Your mum would have loved that new house. It’s a shame she can't see it. She would have. It's got that lovely garden she always wanted for the grandchildren. We're hoping so. It is a bit of a project, though. That kitchen especially needs gutting. Well, you two are good at projects. Remember that disastrous attempt to repaint the bathroom at our old house in Torquay?

Goodness, it’s warm work, isn’t it? All that shifting of gravel… my hands are aching already. Tell me about it. I thought my days of heavy lifting were over when I retired from the Building Society. Though, dealing with some of the customers felt like moving mountains at times, mind you. You with the working party then? Yes, I am. Though ‘working’ feels a bit strong. More like… carefully rearranging. I used to be an artist, you see. Not much call for physical labour in that profession. Spent years running a little gallery in Wells. Wells, lovely part of the world. My daughter used to take the grandchildren down there. Said the little ones adored the Bishop’s Palace. I’m Arthur, by the way. Delighted to meet you, Arthur. I’m Margaret. And yes, Wells is rather special. Though I sold up a few years ago. Became… tiring. All the sourcing, the valuations. A Swedish massage is what I really need right now, not more gravel. Swedish massage, eh? My Brenda – my wife, God rest her – used to swear by those. Said it was the only thing that kept her back from seizing up altogether. She volunteered at the local hospice for years. A truly wonderful woman. Oh, that’s lovely. It’s so important, that kind of work. I did a bit of work with nursery education, years ago, helping with art classes. The little ones are just so… uncomplicated. It’s a world away from the art market, with all its pretensions. It is. Though, that reminds me. My granddaughter’s training to be a nursery teacher now. Says she finds the paperwork a nightmare. All these new directives. Still, she’s a strong girl. A bit too opinionated for her own good, if you ask me, but that’s the young generation for you. Expecting equality on a plate. Equality  on  a plate? It's rather a long time coming, isn’t it? I mean, I remember a time when a woman asking for a mortgage alone was practically a scandal. You’re not wrong there. Though I always treated everyone the same, I like to think. Brenda certainly didn't suffer fools gladly, and she made sure  I  didn’t either. Still, terminology’s all changed, hasn’t it? Can’t say ‘chairman’ anymore, it’s ‘chairperson’. Drives me mad. It’s a bit silly, yes.

Right, so I was looking at flights again, and honestly, Mum, it’s just… ridiculous. Everything has gone up so much since last time I checked. Oh dear. To Portugal, is it? Still set on the Algarve? Yeah, I think so. I mean, I’m open to suggestions, but it felt like a good compromise, you know? Sun, not  too  far to travel, relatively affordable… well, it  was  relatively affordable. Affordable is a relative term these days, isn’t it? Everything’s gone up. Petrol, the price of a loaf of bread… it's frightening. When your father and I went to Majorca in… oh, goodness, 1985, it was a song. We practically stole the holiday. You always tell me that story! But seriously, the flights are looking at nearly four hundred pounds each now. And that's just for the flights! Four hundred! Goodness me. Have you tried EasyJet or Ryanair? They’re usually the cheapest, even if they are a bit… basic. Of course, I’ve tried them! They’re the first places I looked. Ryanair wants me to pay extra for a carry-on bag now, can you believe it? It's getting beyond a joke. Honestly! They squeeze every penny out of you. Remember when baggage was included? Anyway, have you thought about going a bit earlier or later in the season? Maybe June instead of July? I did. June is a bit cheaper, but the weather’s a bit more unpredictable, isn’t it? I’d rather pay a bit more and guarantee some sunshine. I’m not keen on spending a week huddled in a cardigan. Fair enough. Sunshine is important. Have you looked at package holidays? Sometimes they can work out cheaper, especially if you include the hotel in the deal. I had a quick look, but most of them try and stick you in these awful, out-of-the-way places. I want to be near the beach, and somewhere with a bit of life. Not stuck in a concrete block miles from anywhere. Hmm. You are picky, you know. But you deserve a nice holiday. You work so hard. Have you checked Airbnb for apartments? Sometimes you can find lovely places for a good price. That's a good shout, actually. I hadn't really considered Airbnb. I always worry about it being a bit… dodgy, you know? But I suppose if you read the reviews carefully… Exactly.

Right, so I checked the bank again, and they’ve  still  only authorised eighty quid for the concert tickets. Eighty! Do they think I’m going to sneak into Wembley with eighty pounds? Eighty quid, eh? That’s a bit tight, even for standing room. Did you call them, explain the situation? Yeah, I spent half an hour on hold listening to that awful synthesized music, and then the bloke on the phone just kept repeating their standard security protocols. “Have you used your card abroad recently, sir?” No! “Have you noticed any unusual transactions?” No! It’s just… frustrating. It’s  my  money. I feel you. Banks are getting worse, honestly. They’re all about protecting themselves, not helping the customer. You should try writing a formal complaint, sometimes that gets things moving. Maybe. I just want to go and see Arctic Monkeys without having to remortgage the flat. Speaking of frustrating, did you catch the Forest game yesterday? Oh, don't even  start  me. Absolutely robbed! That penalty decision was unbelievable. The ref was clearly biased. Totally! I was shouting at the TV. My missus thought I’d lost it. Said I was acting like a proper hooligan. They don’t understand the passion, do they? It’s a different level. Reminds me of when I was back in Barbados, watching cricket with my grandfather. The atmosphere was electric. Every boundary was celebrated like a national holiday. Sounds amazing. I’ve never really been to a proper cricket match. It always seemed… slow. Slow? It’s strategic! It’s a chess match played with a ball and a bat. You just need to understand the nuances. Anyway, enough about sport – how’s work been? Still drowning in essays? Pretty much. I’ve got this dissertation on post-structuralism to finish, and I’m completely stuck. It’s like trying to explain fog. Sounds challenging. You always were a bright spark, though. You’ll figure it out. My work’s been… hectic. Had a major incident down at the warehouse last week. Forklift driver reversed into a stack of pallets. Luckily, no one was hurt, but the paperwork was a nightmare. Oh, blimey. That sounds stressful. You always take it all on your shoulders, don't you? It's the nature of the job, I suppose. Someone’s got to keep things running smoothly. Speaking of family, have you heard from Auntie Maureen lately?

…and then the whole thing just wobbled, you see? Right off its stand. Nearly took the telly with it. Oh, Arthur! Not the globe again? Honestly, you'd think after all these years you'd find a safer place for it. Is it still in one piece? Mostly. Bit of a crack across South America, but nothing a bit of glue won't fix. It’s a beautiful thing, that globe. Reminds me of holidays, you know? When we went to… oh, where was it? Not Spain, not Italy… Yorkshire? You two were always banging on about Yorkshire. That ridiculous little cottage? It wasn't  ridiculous , David. It was charming! And the walks were lovely. Though Arthur did nearly break his leg on that one hill… Now, that weren’t my leg, Beatrice. That was after the youth hostel trip. Remember that? In the Peak District? That stone staircase… Oh, God, yes. I remember you both recounting that tale for years. Apparently, a sprained ankle doesn’t stop Arthur from climbing mountains. I was a young man then! Full of beans. And Beatrice insisted on packing enough for a month in a rucksack barely big enough for a loaf of bread. Well, someone had to be prepared. You’d forget your head if it wasn’t screwed on, Arthur. Speaking of prepared… did young Emily manage to finish her school project? The one on underground systems? She did. Quite a good one, actually. She chose the London Underground, naturally. Spent ages researching it. Even made a miniature model with working lights. It was impressive. Though I did have to help her with the history bit – her knowledge before was… limited. Ah, London Underground. Now  that's  a proper system. Always a bit grubby, mind, but gets you where you need to go. Nothing like the tube we had planned in Norwich. Never happened, did it? Too much fuss. They talked about it for years. Remember Mr. Henderson at the council? Always going on about 'improving infrastructure.' All talk, that man. He was more interested in his prize-winning roses. Speaking of gardens… how's yours doing, Beatrice? Are the tomatoes coming along alright? Slowly. We had a terrible slug infestation. Lost half the seedlings. David’s been trying to build me some sort of barrier, but he’s a teacher, not a gardener. Not quite the same skillset. Hey! I'm a perfectly capable builder… of poorly constructed slug barriers.

Right, so I’ve been lookin’ at flights again, yeah? And honestly, they’re just… mental. For what, like, three days in Barcelona? You'd think you were goin' to the moon, the price of ‘em. Ugh, tell me about it. I was having a look at Lisbon last night, just a cheeky weekend away, and it’s practically the same price as flyin’ to New York. It’s ridiculous. Are you lookin’ at EasyJet, Ryanair, all the usual suspects? Aye, all of ‘em. And British Airways just to, like, make me feel properly poor. They’re all just rampin’ up the prices now summer's comin’. It's a conspiracy, I’m tellin’ ya. Probably is. They know everyone’s desperate for a bit of sun. Have you tried bein’ flexible with the dates at all? Sometimes shifting it by a day or two can make a difference. I have, a little. But work is… well, work. Hard to get time off. I was hopin’ for the bank holiday weekend, obviously, but everyone and their dog is thinkin’ the same thing. Yeah, that’s a no-go zone. Speaking of work, I had a proper nightmare today. The entire print run for the new brochure came back wrong. Wrong colours, missin’ pages, the whole shebang. Oh, no! Seriously? What happened? Did someone mess up the file or…? It’s a long story, involving a very stressed graphic designer and a printer who clearly needs to invest in a new colour calibration system. I had to spend three hours on the phone, basically yellin’ at people. It was not a good afternoon. Blimey. Sounds awful. You deserve a big glass of wine for that. And for havin’ to deal with printers in general. They're all cowboys, aren't they? You have  no  idea. I’m pretty sure they just make mistakes on purpose to see how much they can get away with. Actually, speaking of wine… is that lasagne smellin’ as good as I think it is? It is! My mum sent us over a massive one. Enough to feed a small army. Help yourself, y’know. Oh, you’re a star. I’m starvin’. Honestly, after that day, all I want is carbs and comfort. Do you fancy puttin’ somethin’ on after? I was thinkin’ maybe that new true crime doc on Netflix? Oh, yeah! The one about the art forgery?

Honestly, the price of a loaf of bread these days… it’s daylight robbery. Used to be you could get a decent white sliced for… what was it, 40p? Now it’s pushing a pound twenty! It’s ridiculous, isn't it? I was looking at the cost of pasta sauce yesterday, and even the basic own-brand stuff is almost £1.50. I'm starting to think growing my own tomatoes is the only way forward. Don’t even  start  me on the supermarkets. I went to Tesco last week and the self-checkout tried to charge me twice for a tin of beans. Twice! I had to get a member of staff involved. And you know what she said? “Oh, it happens all the time.” Happens all the time! They’re relying on people not checking. They are. It's a disgrace. And the banks… don't even get me started. Charging you for  having  your money with them! What is that about? Used to be they  paid  you interest. I switched providers last year, hoping for better rates, but honestly, it was more hassle than it was worth. Endless forms, security questions… and the difference in interest was barely noticeable. My nephew, bless him, he's always going on about these challenger banks, online ones. Claims they offer fantastic deals. Sounds dodgy to me. I like knowing there’s a branch I can go to if something goes wrong. Me too. Though the branch in Woburn closed years ago, of course. Everything’s moving online, isn't it? It's all well and good if you're tech savvy like yourself, dear, but what about those of us who struggle with these gadgets? It's a generational thing, isn’t it? I'm constantly explaining to my students how to do basic things on their phones. And then I complain about supermarket self-checkouts… hypocrisy, I suppose. Speaking of phones, I tried to call my daughter yesterday, and the signal was absolutely dreadful. I swear, these mobile companies just take your money and provide a rubbish service. I’m thinking of switching, but who to? They all sound the same. My hearing aid’s been playing up again. Keeps whistling. I took it back to the audiologist, and she said it needs adjusting. Another appointment, another wasted afternoon. They’re so booked up now, you have to wait weeks to get seen.

Right, so we’re doing favourites, yeah? Favourites of everything. I’ll start with holidays. Mine’s gotta be… South Africa, obviously. It just  feels  like home, even though I didn't grow up there. The light, the smells, the braais… perfect. Ooh, good choice! South Africa sounds amazing, I’ve never been. Mine’s gotta be Italy. Just… Italy. The food, the history, the people. I went interrailing after first year and spent a month just wandering around. I’d move there tomorrow if I could. Italy is brilliant! I was there last summer, Rome was incredible. But honestly? My favourite is Ireland. Not even Dublin, like, the west coast. Proper rugged beaches, sheep everywhere, the pubs with the trad music… it's just magic. You can’t beat a good Irish pub session. Oh, I’m a bit boring. I love Cornwall. Proper British seaside, you know? Rock pools, cream teas, walking the coastal path... It's just… calming. Plus, my Nan has a little cottage there, so it's always felt special. Cornwall sounds lovely, actually. I’m always up for a cream tea. My favourite’s probably… Tenerife. Total cliché, I know, but my family always went when I was a kid. It's just pure sunshine and relaxation. And really cheap cocktails, let's be honest. Tenerife  is  a good shout for a cheap getaway! Okay, next favourite. Animals. No thinking too hard, just the first one that pops into your head. Ooh, easy. Dogs. Specifically, golden retrievers. They’re just the best, aren’t they? Loyal, silly, fluffy… perfect companions. I'm definitely getting one when I have my own place. Cats, definitely cats. They're so independent and sassy. I have three back home, all rescue cats. They run the house, honestly. I miss them so much. Horses. Always horses. I used to ride all the time when I was younger, but haven't had the chance since starting nursing school. They're just… majestic. And powerful. Makes you feel small, in a good way. I'm gonna go with penguins! They’re so awkward and waddle-y, it just makes me laugh. I went to the aquarium last month and spent ages just watching them. Penguins are brilliant! Okay, final favourite… food. This is the important one. Pizza. No contest. Any pizza, really, but especially a really good Neapolitan one, with proper San Marzano tomatoes and buffalo mozzarella.

Right, honestly, this essay is killing me. “The socio-political implications of Pre-Raphaelite art…” Like, who  cares ? Everyone at Lancaster, apparently. Dr. Armitage lives for this stuff. Just tell her Rossetti was a bit of a creep and Millais liked painting really detailed flowers. You’re golden. Easier said than done, love. It needs analysis. Critical engagement. I’ve been staring at ‘Ophelia’ for three hours and I’m starting to feel like  I  want to drown in a river. Honestly? It’s beautiful, but a bit… morbid, isn’t it? All that floral symbolism for a girl who basically lost her marbles because her dad told her to stop seeing Hamlet. Exactly! It's depressing! And I'm supposed to write a coherent 2000 words on the symbolism of willow trees and poppies? I swear, sometimes I just want to drop out and become a professional gamer. Don’t tempt me. I've been neglecting  Stardew Valley  all week. Although, if you did, who’d make me tea when I inevitably fail my statistics module? Fair point. Besides, imagine us at 70, both rocking gamers tags, battling it out online. “GranNanners” versus “ScouseSniper”. Oh my god, stop! That’s brilliant! Though I reckon I'd be more of a "ScouseStrategist", thank you very much. Still, the thought of being 70…makes me feel…old already. Right? It’s terrifying. My nan is 85 and she’s basically just become a walking collection of complaints and Werther’s Originals. My grandma’s pretty good, actually. Still goes line dancing three times a week. Says it keeps her young. Although, she did try to explain TikTok to my uncle last week. That was…something. Oh, bless her. It’s just…I feel like everyone expects you to have your life planned out at our age. What you're doing in five years, ten years. And I’m just like, “I haven’t figured out what I’m having for dinner tonight.” Tell me about it! Everyone at home’s asking about grad schemes, and I’m here thinking, “Can I afford to live on instant noodles for another year?” I mean, I love art history, but realistically… What do you  want  to do, though? If money wasn't an issue. Forget the expectations for a sec. Honestly? I’d probably open a little gallery. Somewhere cozy, with lots of local artists, and maybe a little café inside.

Right, so I was thinking pasta tonight? I’ve got loads of pesto in the fridge that needs using up. Unless you’re vehemently opposed? Pasta sounds  amazing . Honestly, anything is better than attempting to decipher what's lurking in the back of the freezer again. You know that unidentified frozen lump? I’m genuinely scared to examine it. Oh god,  that . I think it was meant to be chicken, but it’s been there since… well, a long time. We should probably just bin it, honestly. It’s starting to haunt my dreams. Definitely bin it. It’s a health hazard waiting to happen. Speaking of hazards, how was your day at work? Still stuck in endless meetings about the, what was it, the “synergy initiative”? Don't even  start  me on the synergy initiative. It’s just corporate jargon for ‘make everyone work harder for the same pay’. Honestly, I spent three hours today debating the colour scheme for a flowchart. A  flowchart ! Oh my god, that's… spectacularly pointless. Some people just like making life difficult, don’t they? My day was… a rollercoaster. Old Mr. Henderson was convinced aliens were communicating through his hearing aid again. Took about an hour to gently redirect him. Oh, bless him. He's a character, isn't he? You're so good with them. I’d completely fall apart. I can barely handle coordinating office stationery, let alone existential crises. It’s just… listening, I think. And a lot of distraction. He did give me a very detailed drawing of the spaceship though. I might have to frame it. You absolutely have to! That’s brilliant. Right, pasta water’s boiling. Are you still on for drinks with Chloe and Liam on Friday? Yeah, definitely! I need a proper catch-up with Chloe. She’s been really quiet lately. I texted her earlier, she just said she’s been ‘busy’. Which, with Chloe, usually means she’s re-watching terrible reality TV and avoiding her responsibilities. Sounds about right. She’s a professional procrastinator. Speaking of avoiding responsibilities… have you talked to Ben lately? Ben? No, not really. Why? Is everything okay? He’s been a bit distant, hasn’t he? I saw his Instagram story, he was hiking in the Peak District all alone. Yeah, I think things are a bit rocky with Sarah. I overheard them having a really tense phone call yesterday.

Right then, shall we have another look at this speaker consent form? I’m still not entirely happy with the phrasing on section three, regarding image rights. It feels a bit… heavy-handed, doesn’t it? Hmm, I see what you mean, Brenda. “Irrevocably granting the university…” sounds a bit much when we’re just talking about taking a few photos for the intranet. Perhaps “allowing the university to…” would be softer? Aye, softer’s definitely better. Though, legally speaking, ‘irrevocably’ protects them. Still, for a seminar, ‘allowing’ is plenty. We’re not exactly selling their souls, are we? And it  is  standard university boilerplate, isn't it? It is, Jane, but that doesn’t mean we can’t nudge it towards being a bit more palatable. It's about making people feel comfortable, especially those who aren't used to public speaking. I had Old Man Hemmings in my Foundations class last year – he nearly had a heart attack at the thought of being photographed. Good point, Brenda. Comfort levels are key. Right, I’ll amend it to ‘allowing’ then. While I’m doing that, let's quickly run through the seminar structure again. I’ve drafted a rough timeline. I’ve got us starting with the cultural dimensions – Hofstede, Trompenaars, that sort of thing - for about 45 minutes. Sounds good. That gives a solid theoretical foundation. Are we sticking with the case study on the Japanese automotive industry for the practical application section? Yes, I think so. It’s a classic, and it highlights the pitfalls of assuming universal business practices brilliantly. The issues with  ringi-sho  and decision-making always get a good reaction. I’ve updated the slides with some more recent examples of Western companies stumbling in Japan. Excellent. I’ve prepared some role-playing scenarios based on a negotiation gone wrong between a British supplier and a Japanese manufacturer. Should get them thinking on their feet. I’m allocating about an hour to that. An hour sounds about right. Those case studies can run away with themselves if you’re not careful. Folks get bogged down in details. We need to keep a firm hand on the time. And what about the Q&A? I was thinking half an hour at the end. That should give everyone a chance to ask questions, and hopefully, we'll still have enough energy to answer them coherently. Honestly, these seminars always drain me.

Honestly, that seminar was… a lot. Old Man Hemmings really went off on one about post-structuralism again. You’d think, after twenty years, he’d have a slightly more concise way of explaining it. Concise is not in his vocabulary, is it? I swear, he enjoys watching the students’ eyes glaze over. Mine certainly were. I spent most of it mentally planning the grocery shopping. At least you were being practical. I was just desperately trying to remember what Derrida actually  said  before Hemmings started… embellishing. Did you manage to get that email sorted with the department head about the funding? Nearly. I drafted it, but I need to read it over again. I’m worried about sounding too… demanding. It’s just, the promised equipment hasn't materialized, and I can’t really run the experiments without it. They keep saying ‘supply chain issues’ but it feels like a convenient excuse. Oh, the classic supply chain excuse. It’s the university’s favourite at the moment. Is it the specialist sensors you need? Yeah, those. And the calibration software. Apparently, everything is ‘on order’ but ‘dates are uncertain’. I’m starting to think I’ll be teaching undergrads how to use prisms and lenses for the foreseeable future. That sounds… fun. Not for you, obviously. It’s frustrating, though. You deserve to have the resources to do proper research. It’s what they  pay  us for, isn’t it? Exactly! It’s the principle of it. And it makes me think about the house again. I was looking at properties online again last night… don't judge. No judgement, I’m guilty of the same crime. Anything catch your eye? A little cottage just outside of Oxford. It had a garden, a proper fireplace… and a price tag that was approximately three times our combined annual income. Oxford, huh? Always optimistic. That's a lovely area though. It’s just… insane how expensive everything is now. Remember when we were first talking about buying a place, and we thought a two-bedroom flat in Zone 3 was ambitious? Vaguely. Now a garden shed in Zone 3 costs a fortune. I saw one advertised as a ‘charming compact living space’ the other day. Seriously. Oh, that's brilliant. The estate agents are truly masters of spin. I’m starting to think we'll be renting forever. Don't say that!

Honestly, this shepherd’s pie is…fine. It’s just a bit bland, isn’t it? Gran always put a dash of Worcester sauce in hers. Changed everything. Worcester sauce? Really? I never would have thought. Hers was always amazing though, wasn’t it? That kitchen… always smelled of something baking or simmering. Remember that floral wallpaper? Dreadful. Hideous! Mum tried to get rid of it for years, but Gran was having  none  of it. Said it reminded her of her mother. It’s funny, the things we inherit, isn’t it? Not just furniture, but…attachments. It is. Speaking of furniture, what are you thinking about doing with that awful sideboard when you finally clear out the attic? It's a monstrosity. Honestly, I don’t know. I feel bad just…binning it. But it doesn't fit anywhere and no one wants it. It feels wrong, though. All that solid wood. It just feels like such  waste . Like everything these days. Look at the amount of food we throw away. Tell me about it. Work canteen is horrific. Mountains of perfectly good pasta salad chucked at the end of lunch. Makes you feel guilty just eating it. We’re generating so much waste it’s ridiculous. And then everyone’s talking about robots taking over jobs…it's all linked, isn’t it? Industrialisation, overproduction, waste…it's terrifying. I was talking to a Year 10 student yesterday, and he wants to be an engineer, like you, but he was asking about job security. What do you even  say ? Tough. I try to be realistic. I say engineering’s always going to be needed, someone’s got to fix the robots when they break down, right? But it’s changing so fast. More automation, more reliance on AI…It’s not like my grandad’s engineering, building things with his hands. No. And the career advice in school is…lacklustre, to say the least. It’s all ‘think about university, get a degree’. Nobody talks about apprenticeships, the closed industries, the ones where it’s impossible to get a foot in the door without knowing someone. It’s so unfair. Completely. It's all about who you know, especially in some of the more established companies. Honestly, sometimes I think private industry is the only way to get anywhere. More adaptable, more willing to take risks. Maybe. Although, even there, it feels like a bit of a boys’ club sometimes.

Right, so onions are softening nicely. You okay to chop the peppers while I deal with this garlic? My hands are already smelling like an Italian kitchen. Yep, peppers are under control. Honestly, this week has just  flown  by. It feels like Monday was yesterday, and now it’s Thursday evening already. Tell me about it. I spent the entire day battling with statistical software. Honestly, sometimes I think it’s deliberately designed to be infuriating. It’s like it enjoys throwing errors at me just to watch me squirm. Ugh, sounds stressful. Work was…interesting. Had a safeguarding meeting this morning that went on forever. Honestly, some of the cases just break your heart. Makes you feel so helpless. That sounds incredibly draining. You’re amazing for doing what you do, putting up with all that. It must be emotionally exhausting. It is. But someone has to, right? Though I swear, every time I think I’ve got my head around the new assessment guidelines, they change them. It’s a perpetual cycle of learning and unlearning. Bureaucracy, eh? Reminds me of grant applications. Endless revisions, tiny font sizes, and the constant fear of rejection. It’s soul-crushing. Did you hear back about your sister's house sale yet? Yes! Finally. They’ve accepted an offer. It’s a relief, honestly. She was starting to worry it would be stuck on the market forever. It's good timing, she's hoping to move closer to Mum. Oh, that’s brilliant news! Mum will be thrilled, won't she? It’ll be so much easier for you both to visit. Definitely. And it’ll give your sister a bit more support, she's been needing it. She’s really taken on a lot with Dad’s health. Speaking of which, have you managed to chat to him this week? I did, on Tuesday. He sounded…okay. He’s still complaining about the physio, says it’s “torture,” but he’s actually going to the sessions, which is the main thing. He was mostly talking about the cricket. That’s good. Distraction is a good thing. He always gets so wrapped up in the cricket. He lives for it, really. Honestly, it's his lifeline. It gives him something to focus on. Okay, peppers are looking good? Just chuck them in. This is going to be a pretty fiery curry, I think.

…and honestly, Doreen, I’ve not felt this low in years. Just…a grayness, you know? Like someone’s turned the colour down on everything. Oh, Arthur, dear. That sounds awful. It's no good bottling things up, is it? You’ve always been a bit of a stoic, but even stoics need a chat. What’s brought it on, love? Is it the weather again? You do get poorly when the damp sets in. If you don’t mind me jumping in…it sounds a bit more than just the weather, doesn’t it? I mean, the damp’s miserable, but… a ‘grayness’? That sounds like a proper dip. It’s not  just  the weather, Michael. Though it doesn't help staring at the rain day in, day out. It’s… well, Maureen’s been on at me again, about the house. Your daughter? Still fussing over you selling up, is she? Honestly, that girl. You’ve lived in that bungalow for forty years, Arthur! It’s full of memories. She says it’s too much for me now. Too big. Too much garden. Says I’d be better off in one of those retirement flats. “Low maintenance,” she calls it. Low  life , more like. Retirement flats aren’t all bad, you know. Some of them are quite nice, with communal gardens and activities. Activities! Bridge and bingo? I’d rather stare at a brick wall. And frankly, I can’t afford to move. Even downsizing, there’s stamp duty and estate agent fees… it’s a fortune. Precisely! And where would all your treasures go? That model railway collection, your wartime medals… you've got a lifetime of things, Arthur. You can't just shove them in a cupboard. It’s the feeling of losing control, I think. When family start making decisions  for  you, it's easy to feel… helpless. It’s a common thing, actually. I see it a lot with the parents of my students. Worrying about their independence. It’s not just the house, either. Old Mr. Henderson passed away last week. We used to meet down the seafront every Tuesday, rain or shine. Just to watch the waves. Keeps you grounded, you see? Now… just feels empty. Oh, dear Arthur. That  is  sad. Losing a friend like that… it leaves a hole. Did you go to the funeral? Couldn't manage it. Too choked up, to be honest.

Honestly, this new moisturiser is a game changer. You  have  to try it. My skin feels…plump. Which is a word I never thought I’d use to describe my face, ever. Ooh, really? What is it? I'm still battling this dry patch on my chin, it’s driving me mad. Feels like sandpaper, honestly. It’s the Nivea Hyaluron + Vitamin C thing. Sounds basic, I know, but honestly, it’s brilliant. It was on offer in Boots, three for two, so I grabbed it. Thought ‘what have I got to lose?’ Boots is a dangerous place, isn't it? Especially when they have offers on. I always end up spending a fortune. Last week I went in for toothpaste and came out with four lipsticks and a new eyeshadow palette. Oh, I know the feeling! It's the layout, I swear. They  want  you to impulse buy. Speaking of makeup, have you seen Sarah’s new hair? She went completely platinum blonde! No way! Sarah? Really? She always said she wouldn’t go blonde, said it washes her out. Is it nice? It’s…different. It’s very bright. I think she’s having a bit of a mid-life crisis, honestly. She’s also started getting her nails done – those really long, acrylic ones. Bright red. It's a lot. Oh, bless her. She’s always been a bit of a follower, hasn't she? Remember when we all had to wear those chunky platform trainers in Year Ten? She had to have them, even though she tripped over them constantly. Oh god, yeah! And the butterfly clips! The horror! I'm thinking of getting my nails done again, though. I had a gel manicure for my birthday, and it lasted  ages . What colour were you thinking? I don't know… Something autumnal, maybe? A deep burgundy or a burnt orange? I was browsing Instagram earlier and saw someone with a really nice navy blue, though. Navy’s nice! Sophisticated. I'm leaning towards a really dark green, like a forest green. I saw a shade in Superdrug the other day that was gorgeous. We should go shopping next weekend, we haven’t done a proper shopping trip in ages. Ooh, yes! That sounds amazing. We could hit up the market first, see if there are any bargains. And then Boots, obviously. For more ‘essentials’. Of course. Essentials.

Right, so the interview… honestly, I’m bricking it. A Masters in Applied Linguistics? It feels… huge. You’ll be sound, Liam. You’ve always been brilliant with the language stuff. Remember when you used to correct our nan’s grammar? Only because she kept saying “an’ all” instead of “and all”. It was driving me mad! But this is different, this is academic. Proper essays and research and… funding. That’s the killer, isn’t it? Aye, the money’s always the killer. How much are you looking at needing, roughly? Best case, about seven grand. Worst case… ten. I’ve a bit saved, obviously, but not  that  much. I’m thinking another part-time job, maybe. Teaching English to tourists in the summer, like I did at uni. That’s not a bad shout. Or maybe a few extra shifts at the pub? Though you’d be wrecked. Speaking of wrecked, I spent half of yesterday trying to find parking near the Maritime Museum. Absolute nightmare. Oh, tell me about it. Trying to get anywhere central is a joke. They’re building something new near the Albert Dock again, aren’t they? More apartments, I think. Yeah, more overpriced flats for students. Speaking of students, how are things at the school? Still dealing with teenage existential crises over Shakespeare? You have no idea. It’s amazing how much angst can be packed into a discussion about Romeo and Juliet. I had one lad yesterday who was convinced the whole play was a metaphor for Brexit. No way! What did you say? I just… nodded. Sometimes it’s easier to just let them have their moment. It's draining though, honestly. Social work must be even more intense. It has its days. Yesterday was mostly safeguarding meetings. Endless paperwork. But then you get the small wins, you know? Helped a family sort out some housing issues, stuff like that. Makes it worthwhile. Good. It’s good to hear that. Right, speaking of worthwhile… I need to start thinking about Christmas presents. My Auntie Maureen keeps hinting she wants a fancy new vase. Oh god, Maureen and her vases. She’s got enough to open a pottery shop. Have you been thinking about moving closer to your mum, by the way? You were saying something about it last week. Yeah, I am. There’s a little flat going in Allerton, near her.

Honestly, it’s just…exhausting, you know? The constant negotiation. It's not even  with  Leo half the time, it's with his mother. Tell me about it. It never really ends, does it? Even when they’re teenagers, there's still a…dynamic. A history. Exactly! And she's…well, she’s convinced I’m trying to replace her. Which I'm absolutely not. I just want a bit of peace sometimes, a bit of time to actually connect with Leo without feeling like I’m being assessed. It’s that protective instinct, I think. And it's incredibly hard to navigate when you're trying to build a relationship with a child who’s already got a deeply ingrained one with someone else. Especially when that someone is…difficult. Difficult is putting it mildly. She'll agree to something one day, then completely backtrack the next. Like the football camp. She said he could go, I paid for it, booked it… then she sent me a text this morning saying she’d “thought better of it” and he’s spending the week with her sister. Oh, that’s infuriating! You’re right to be frustrated. It's not about Leo, it's about control. It feels like it. And I'm trying so hard to be the ‘cool’ step-mum, the one who doesn't interfere, the one who supports their relationship… but it's so draining when you’re constantly undermined. You're a good person, Sarah. Leo's lucky to have you. Truly. It’s just…she needs to understand that you’re not trying to erase her, you’re trying to  add  to his life. You sound like my therapist. It’s just…I miss having a relationship that doesn't involve navigating landmines. Remember when we were younger and relationships were just…simpler? Simpler? We thought they were simpler. We were probably both just oblivious! But yes, there was definitely less…complexity. Less history. I envy you sometimes, just being…you. You're so independent. You’ve always been so clear about what you want. It's wonderful to see you thriving, even with the chaos that little Leo brings! Oh, don’t romanticise it! It's chaos, pure and simple. And I'm not thriving, I’m surviving on caffeine and the goodwill of my mum. But… It is good, isn’t it? And honestly, after years of feeling…lost, maybe a little bit lost myself, having him has given me a sense of purpose.

Honestly, I’ve been down a rabbit hole on Pinterest all week. It’s dangerous, you know? Especially this close to birthdays. Pinterest? What’ve you been pinning, extravagant hand-knitted sweaters for everyone? You know my mum hates anything remotely crafty. No, not sweaters! Though, that's a good idea, actually. No, I’ve been looking at…experiences. Like weekend breaks, pottery classes, that sort of thing. It’s a slippery slope though. One minute you’re looking at a weekend in the Lake District, the next you’re budgeting for a hot air balloon ride. Sounds about right. You always go big. Remember when you organised that murder mystery night for Sarah’s 25th? Oh god, don't remind me. The costumes! And poor Kevin nearly broke his ankle trying to ‘dramatically’ fall off the sofa during the reveal. He did look rather committed to the role of the disgruntled butler, though. Speaking of Sarah, have you heard from her recently? She's been awfully quiet. She texted me yesterday. She's completely obsessed with that new show, “The Gilded Age.” Apparently, she’s already re-watched the first three episodes. Says it's exactly her kind of thing - lots of drama and fancy dresses. Sounds…intense. I tried to get into it, but it felt a bit slow. I’m still ploughing through “Severance” on Apple TV. Have you seen that? No, is it good? Everyone keeps talking about it. What’s it about? It’s hard to explain without spoiling it. Basically, these people have had a procedure to separate their work memories from their personal lives. So, when they’re at work, they have no recollection of who they are outside, and vice versa. It's brilliantly unsettling. That sounds… bleak. Which is probably why I'm gravitating towards pretty pictures of cottages and baking recipes on Pinterest. It's escapism, purely escapism. Fair enough. Actually, speaking of escapism, I’ve started teaching myself Italian on Duolingo. Extremely slowly. Mostly I just learn how to order coffee. Salute! Very important skill. Though if you ever find yourself in Sunderland, you’re better off just asking for a “propper brewt.” They’ll know what you mean. A “propper brewt?” I'm already anticipating a culture shock. My Italian will be useless. You’ll be fine. You’re a quick learner. Oh! I almost forgot. I saw Liam at the library the other day.

Right, okay, so this one… it’s a bit much, isn’t it? All that glass. Looks like something out of a ballroom. Mmm. A bit ostentatious for the hallway, definitely. Though, I did like the one we saw earlier, the brushed steel, the rectangular one? Oh, yes! That was much more  us . Not too fussy. How much was it again? Let me just scroll back… Ah, here we are. £85. Not bad. Though, postage is a killer. Always is. Did you manage to filter Rightmove for anything with a garden bigger than a postage stamp? I swear, everything in our price range comes with a yard the size of my kitchen. I tried. I really did. But the filters are useless. You set it to “garden” and it throws up anything with even a patch of grass. It's deceptive. This one  looks  promising… Four bedrooms, semi-detached… oh. No garden. Just a patio. A patio is better than nothing, I suppose. But I was really hoping for somewhere we could, you know, actually  do  something outside. Maybe a little vegetable patch? Me too. And somewhere the dog can properly run around without knocking over everything. Though, realistically, with your gardening skills, a vegetable patch would be more weeds than vegetables. Hey! I grew some pretty impressive sunflowers last year. You mean the ones the slugs ate? They were  working  on the sunflowers! It's a process. Anyway, look at this one, in Melton Mowbray. Three beds, decent sized garden… but it needs a lot of work. Oh dear. Look at those photos. That wallpaper is… alarming. And the kitchen. It’s like a time warp back to the seventies. It's 'retro'! And it’s reflected in the price. We could get a good deal and just rip it all out. New kitchen, fresh paint… Rip it all out? That sounds… expensive. And time-consuming. Remember the bathroom fiasco last time? That was a learning experience! We know better now. We'd get a proper tradesman this time. Promise. Oh, I’m sure you would. Alright, alright. Let’s save it to our shortlist. But I’m warning you, if we end up living in a building site again, I’m blaming you. Deal. Just promise me we can at least  look  at houses with gardens, even if they’re slightly… challenging. I’m starting to feel like a hermit cooped up in this flat.

Honestly, this coffee is a lifesaver. Night shift was  brutal  last night. Old Mr. Henderson was convinced aliens were stealing his slippers again. Oh, bless him. He’s a character, isn’t he? Still, you’d think after all these years they’d just…accept the slipper situation. I’m just glad I don't have night shifts! Early mornings with Mrs. Davies are bad enough. She insists on telling me about every single one of her cats. All five of them. Oh, the cats! Right. I heard about those. Apparently, Percy’s been on a diet. Diet? Percy's a fluffy tub of a thing! She gives him cream with his biscuits, for goodness sake. She's a soft touch, is Brenda. She’d let those cats run the house if she could. Speaking of running things, how’s the house hunt going, Carol? Still looking? Still looking. It’s a nightmare. Everything’s either a shoebox or costs the earth. David's convinced we need a bigger garden for the dogs, but honestly, I just want somewhere with a functioning kitchen! This one’s…well, it’s seen better days. I saw a place advertised in Ashford, near the park. It looked alright on Rightmove, wasn't huge, but had a little garden. I can send you the link if you like? Oh, that would be lovely, darling, thank you. Anything’s worth a look at this point. It’s just so demoralising, isn’t it? David keeps saying, “Just be patient,” but patience wears thin after six months of searching! Tell me about it. My sister’s been looking for ages too. She's started looking further afield, even considering villages I've never heard of! It’s getting to that point, isn’t it? I might have to start broadening my horizons. Although, leaving Kent feels…wrong, somehow. I understand that. It's home, isn't it? How are things at the hospital, by the way, Carol? Still short-staffed? Massively. It’s getting ridiculous. I worked with a new agency nurse last night, lovely girl, but she was completely overwhelmed. Said she’d never seen anything like it. We’re all just running on fumes, to be honest. It’s the same at the home. We’ve had two carers off sick with the flu this week. Makes everything so much harder when you’re trying to give everyone the care they deserve.

Honestly, this research I was reading during my lunch break… fascinating stuff about sleep. Apparently, the temperature of your bedroom is  critical . Like, down to a specific degree. Really? I just pull the duvet higher or lower. Is it one of those things where it’s different for everyone? They said ideally 16.8 degrees Celsius. Apparently, your core body temperature needs to drop to initiate sleep. Too warm, and you toss and turn. Too cold, and your body uses energy to warm up instead of relaxing. 16.8! That sounds… chilly. We barely get our bedroom below 18 in the summer. Right? I’m skeptical, but seemingly, it makes a massive difference. They also talked about light exposure—obviously—but the temperature thing was the big takeaway. It made me think of that disastrous camping trip last year. Oh god, don't remind me. That field was freezing. I think I spent the entire night shivering despite being layered like an onion. Exactly! No wonder neither of us slept. We were battling the elements instead of letting our bodies relax. Speaking of battles with navigation… I was trying to drive into Cambridge yesterday, and the ring road is a menace. Tell me about it. It's deliberately confusing, isn’t it? They want you to use the Park and Ride. I suspect so. I ended up going round and round, ending up back at the same Tesco petrol station three times. It was ridiculous. I should have just stuck to the A10. You know, you always try to be clever and find a ‘shortcut’. It rarely works, does it? Remember that time in Florence? Oh, don’t even start. We were hopelessly lost for about three hours, wandering down tiny alleyways that smelled strongly of fish. And you were convinced you knew where you were going, confidently striding ahead while I trailed behind, muttering about maps. In my defence, Florence is a maze! Anyway, I finally managed to get into Cambridge, and I was watching a small plane taking off from the airfield. It was a bit… wobbly. Wobbly? What do you mean? Just… not a particularly smooth ascent. It didn't look entirely comfortable. I was thinking, you know, you’re putting your life in someone’s hands. It makes you wonder about their training and experience. Oh, you’re sounding like my dad now. He’s obsessed with analyzing any form of transport.

Right, so then Hammy, he’s just… he’s a menace, honestly. A tiny, fluffy menace. Still escaping? I thought you hamster-proofed the whole room. I  tried . He's wedged himself behind the wardrobe. Like, how?! It’s a solid piece of furniture! I had to get me dad to move it. Oh, bless him. Little Houdini. What’s he been getting up to once he’s out? Eating all your textbooks? Worse! He found a bag of crisps. A full bag! There were crumbs  everywhere . And he looked so smug about it. Like he’d won the lottery. Oh, he sounds brilliant. My nan’s hamster used to sleep in her bra. True story. No way! Swear on my life. Apparently, it was warm and smelled of lavender. She was convinced he preferred it to his little house. That’s… surprisingly wholesome. Though, a crisp-loving ninja hamster is pretty good competition. So, anyone else notice how many gingers there are in our uni lectures this year? Like, a disproportionate amount. Hmm, you’re right actually. I think there are at least three in my History seminar. It's a conspiracy, I tell ya. A ginger takeover! Don't be ridiculous, Liv. It's just a random coincidence. Though, they  are  known for their fiery personalities, aren't they? No, but seriously. It feels like every other person I see has red hair. And they all seem to have freckles, too. It's a bit unsettling. Maybe it's just because you’re noticing them more? Like when you buy a new car, you suddenly see that car everywhere? Could be. It’s just… striking. Do you think it's genetic or something? Are gingers breeding faster than the rest of us? Don’t even start. That’s just… stereotypical. It's a recessive gene, isn't it? That's why they're rarer. So, probably not breeding faster. Just… popping up. Like daisies. I always thought gingers were special. Like, they're supposed to be more creative or something. Oh, don’t tell me you believe in that rubbish! No, not really! It’s just what I heard when I was little. My friend Sarah, she  was  amazing at art, and she was a proper redhead. Correlation doesn't equal causation, babe. She’s just talented. And probably a bit eccentric. Speaking of eccentric… anyone seen the guy who wears the full Victorian outfit to the library?

Right, so if I move three armies from Siam into Indonesia… that completely cuts off your supply line, doesn’t it? Cuts off  my  supply line? You’re dreaming, lad. I’ve got Kamchatka reinforced. You’re relying on a gamble, pushing into Southeast Asia that early. You always do this, preemptive strikes, all flash and no substance. Honestly, you two. It’s just Risk. It’s not a declaration of war. Though, knowing you two, it feels like it sometimes. Mum! It’s strategy! Dad’s just… defensively minded. He likes to turtle up. Defensively minded is a polite way of saying I don’t waste troops on pointless offensives. Unlike some people who charge in like Genghis Khan. You know, he probably had better logistics, actually. Genghis Khan didn't have Australia, Dad. That’s the key difference. This map is fundamentally different. Speaking of maps, did you ever get around to downloading the updated version, dear? The one with the corrected place names? You were butchering Queensland last time. It sounded like you were summoning a demon. “Queeeensland!” It’s a difficult name! And I got it eventually. Though, I still maintain that the original was more… aesthetically pleasing. Aesthetically pleasing isn't helpful when you’re trying to formulate a coherent military plan. Oh, and a gentle reminder, you’re leaving North America completely unguarded. I'm waiting for  you  to attack. Lure you into a false sense of security. It's a classic tactic. You’re both so competitive. It’s exhausting. Anyone want more chocolate? I’ve got those salted caramels Aaron brought over. Yes, please! Salted caramel is the fuel of champions. Speaking of Aaron, how's he getting on with that recording project? He said he was trying to capture some traditional folk songs? He sent me a little snippet. Actually quite good. Captures the…atmosphere. Though, the instructions he gave me for sending feedback were utterly baffling. Five pages long! Bless him. He's a bit of a perfectionist. Which is good, I suppose. It means he takes pride in his work. Honestly, it reminds me of when the children were learning instruments. The sheer fuss! Mum, we’re not six years old anymore. No, but you still have that same…intensity. Remember when you were convinced you could beat Dad at chess at age eight? Ah, those were the days. He was a formidable opponent, even then.

Right, so I genuinely spent the last hour scrolling through TikTok watching videos of people renovating campervans. Like, full-on converting them. It's… a vibe. But also reinforces the fact I have  zero  clue what I’m doing with my life. Oh, you and your existential spirals. Campervan life sounds… ambitious. And slightly impractical when you consider you get seasick on the ferry to Heysham. Hey! It’s a  sensitivity to motion , okay? And it’s not about  living  in a campervan forever, it’s the idea of… freedom. Doing something different. Unlike this English Lit degree that feels increasingly like a very expensive way to learn how to read. Don’t knock it ‘til you’ve finished the dissertation, yeah? Plus, you're good at it. Remember that essay on Virginia Woolf? Professor Davies practically swooned. Davies swoons at everything slightly pretentious. Honestly. But you’re right, it just doesn’t feel…  useful . What about you? Still dead set on being a vet? That seems like a solid plan. Mostly. It’s the practical side of things that’s starting to worry me. I shadowed a vet last week, and honestly, it was way more… emotional than I thought. One minute you’re cuddling a fluffy kitten, the next you’re explaining euthanasia to a sobbing owner. Oh, blimey. That sounds rough. It is. And the student debt is terrifying. I saw a post online saying vets are statistically one of the most stressed professions. I'm starting to wonder if I should just become a dog walker. Less responsibility, more puppy cuddles. You’d be brilliant at dog walking! You’ve got that… patience thing down. I’d pay you to walk Barnaby. He needs someone who can withstand his relentless enthusiasm. Speaking of relentless enthusiasm, did you see that Tom Holland is going to be a dad? No way! With Zendaya? That’s amazing! They actually look like they genuinely like each other, unlike half of Hollywood. Although… imagine the paparazzi. Poor little thing’s gonna grow up with a camera in its face 24/7. I know, right? It’s awful. Makes you wonder who even  wants  to have kids these days. It just seems like so much… effort. And expensive. And terrifying. My mum keeps dropping hints. “Wouldn’t it be lovely to have little feet running around?” No, Mum, not right now. Maybe never.

Honestly, this Geography project is killing me. “The Impact of Socioeconomic Factors on Urban Development.” Like, who even  cares  about urban development? Seriously! Mr. Davies is obsessed. But it's kinda interesting when you think about it. Slough is… well, Slough. You can  see  the difference between the Trading Estate side and, like, Langley. Yeah, but writing a 2000-word essay about it? It’s just loads of statistics and depressing stuff. I was reading about poverty rates and… it’s grim. It is, isn’t it? My cousin Liam, he lives over near the station, right? Their mum works two jobs just to keep a roof over their heads. He doesn’t get much, like new stuff, or even go on holiday. That’s rough. Makes you think, doesn’t it? We moan about having to do homework, but at least we  have  a warm house to do it in. And decent food. Exactly. And new phones. My mate, Josh, he’s got one of those really old iPhones, the one with the home button. He's super embarrassed about it. But what can he do? His dad’s always saying they can’t afford a new one. It's messed up how much everyone expects you to have the latest things. Like, if you don't have the new trainers, you're automatically out. It’s just consumerism gone mad. Totally! It's like you're being judged on what you  own , not who you  are . Remember Miss Henderson going on about ‘responsible consumerism’ in PSHE? What a joke. Oh, she’s the worst. All talk, no action. Still rocking the designer handbags, I bet. Speaking of stuff we shouldn’t be thinking about, did you see the article about that scientific research into extending lifespan? The one where they slowed down aging in worms? Yeah. It’s kinda scary, isn’t it? Imagine if they figured it out for humans. Only rich people would be able to afford it. Exactly! It'd just make the inequality even worse. Like, the already posh people living to 150 while the rest of us… well. It's just… a lot to think about, you know? School, friends, money, the planet ending… Tell me about it. Did Leo finally apologize to Maya? I heard they had a massive blow-up last week. Apparently. He sent her a TikTok with one of those sad dog filter things.

Honestly, the recording session yesterday was a  nightmare . Absolutely dreadful. I thought I’d prepped enough, but the sound engineer kept saying my diction was… well, he didn’t say  bad , exactly. More that it wasn’t consistent. Apparently, fluctuating vowel sounds are a real problem for audiobooks. Who knew? Oh, really? You’d think after all those years teaching English Lit, your diction would be spot on! You’d think, wouldn't you? But apparently reading aloud to a room of teenagers and reading into a sensitive microphone are two entirely different beasts. He made me do the first chapter  five  times. Five! My mouth felt like sandpaper by the end of it. Ouch. Sounds stressful. Did you get a biscuit break at least? A biscuit break! That’s rich. No, he kept offering me herbal tea. Herbal tea! As if a peppermint infusion is going to magically restore vocal cord lubrication. Speaking of neighbours, have you seen old Mr. Henderson lately? Not for a couple of days. He was pottering about in his garden last I saw, muttering to his roses as usual. Well, he was banging around yesterday afternoon, sounded like he was dismantling his shed. I popped over to check if he was alright, and he just waved me away, said he was “reorganising”. I suspect he’s just having one of his moods. He’s a bit…eccentric, isn’t he? A bit. He offered me a prune and a lecture on the importance of composting last week. I politely declined both. Oh, he’s a character. Anyway, I finally managed to book that physiotherapy appointment. My knee is absolutely killing me. It’s this weather, I swear. Damp air just seizes everything up. You and your joints! You're turning into your mother. She always said the barometer dictated her pain levels. Don't remind me! And my hips aren’t much better. Walking is becoming…an adventure. Though, honestly, I suspect it’s also the extra weight. I really need to get back on a diet. You say that every week. I  know  I do. But it’s so tempting to just have another slice of cake, isn’t it? It’s comfort eating, pure and simple. I was looking at some clothes online last night, and nothing fits properly. Everything feels… constricting. Maybe you just need to go up a size? No, no.

Right, so I reckon another splash of wine is needed for both of us, yeah? This sauce  needs  it, honestly. It’s… lacking a certain  oomph . Absolutely. Though I’m blaming the tomatoes, not your cooking, love. They just don’t have the same flavour as the ones you get in Italy. It’s a scientific fact. Scientific fact? You and your ‘facts’. Honestly, you could convince anyone of anything with that posh degree of yours. Hey! It’s a Masters in Production Control, it’s very useful. Someone’s gotta make sure things run smoothly, even when it’s just pasta sauce. Speaking of smooth running… my boss is driving me up the wall. Oh, go on. What’s he done now? Is it the constant re-scheduling? I thought you said he was getting better at that. He’s not better at re-scheduling, he’s decided we need to implement a whole new ‘synergy initiative’. Apparently, our department isn’t ‘collaborative’ enough. He wants us to have mandatory team-building exercises. Team-building? What, trust falls? Awful. God, I did one of those at a conference last month. Nearly broke my nose. See? Exactly! It's humiliating and unproductive. He’s also fixated on ‘key performance indicators’ – apparently, I'm not hitting my KPI for ‘proactive problem solving’. Proactive problem solving? Is that even a thing? Sounds like something made up in a management textbook. Just tell him you’re proactively solving problems  in your head  before they even happen. I might actually try that. He’d hate it. It’s just… exhausting, you know? Constantly justifying everything. What about you? Anything exciting happening in Doncaster-land? Not really. Mum's still trying to set me up with every eligible bachelor within a fifty-mile radius. Last week it was the butcher’s son. Apparently, he’s “a good provider”. Oh, no. The pressure! Is he at least… reasonably attractive? He owns a lot of sausages. That's about all I can tell you. I politely declined. I swear, sometimes I think she'd be happy if I just married the postman. Maybe you should just move to Spain and open a tapas bar. You always talked about that. Tempting, very tempting. Although I’d probably just end up arguing with tourists about the proper way to make paella. It's a curse, I tell you. A Yorkshire curse.

Right, okay, so we’re doing film night next week, yeah? What are we thinking? I’m open to suggestions, honestly, I’ve been watching so much coursework-adjacent stuff I just need… escapism. Ooh, escapism is good. I was thinking something properly cheesy. Like, a 90s rom-com. I’m in the mood for  You’ve Got Mail  levels of fluff. Cheesy? Ah, now there’s an idea. But I'm thinkin’ we should push the boat out a bit. I’ve been meaning to get ye all to watch  Derry Girls . It’s not a film, I know, but the extended Christmas special is basically one, right? And it’s brilliant.  Derry Girls  is amazing! But we’ve all seen it, haven’t we? Multiple times? Yeah, Mum’s made us watch it loads. It's funny though, I’ll give it that. I was thinking something scary? Like, a proper jump-scare type film? I’m feeling brave. Oh god, no. Absolutely not. Scary films are not a vibe right now. I’ve already had enough stress this week. I’m voting against anything with a ghost or a masked killer. Honestly, I'm with Chloe. Need something light and fluffy. I saw this advert for a new one on Netflix,  Anyone But You , it looks really terrible… in a good way? Like, peak rom-com ridiculousness?  Anyone But You … oh yeah, I saw trailers for that! Sydney Sweeney and Glen Powell, right? It looks… aggressively average. Which, honestly, is perfect for a student film night. Aggressively average, eh? That’s a new one. But I’ll admit, a bit of mindless entertainment does sound appealing. Although, I still think ye all need to appreciate the genius of Michelle and Erin. Look, maybe we can do  Derry Girls  another time. It's just… been done. Has anyone seen… um… what was that one with Timothée Chalamet?  Dune ? Is that too long?  Dune  is three hours long, Hannah. We're trying to  relax , not commit to a second degree. Plus, all that sand is depressing. I'd rather watch something with, like, pretty dresses.  Anyone But You  it is then? Unless anyone has a truly compelling argument against aggressively average rom-coms? I’ll make popcorn. Extra butter. Alright, alright.  Anyone But You  it is. But I’m makin’ a list for next week.  Derry Girls  will be screened, I promise ye.

Honestly, my feet are  killing  me. I didn’t realise how much walking we’d actually do in Paris. Oh dear, you poor thing! Paris is lovely, isn't it? But it is a walking city, that's for sure. Did you manage to see everything you wanted to? Most of it, I think. The Louvre was… overwhelming. So many people. And Mum, you wouldn’t  believe  the queue for the Mona Lisa. It wasn’t even worth it, honestly. Just a tiny painting behind glass, surrounded by a sea of phone cameras. Sounds hectic! How was it overall though? Worth the blisters? Definitely worth the blisters. The food was amazing, obviously. And wandering around Montmartre was just… lovely. Properly picturesque. I did almost get pickpocketed though, which was a bit scary. Oh, goodness! Pickpocketed? Where were you? On the Metro. This guy bumped into me, really aggressively, and I felt someone trying to get into my bag. Luckily, I’d zipped it up tight and he gave up pretty quickly. Still, it shook me up a bit. That’s awful! You have to be so careful. It's good you were prepared. Did you report it? No, he ran off. And honestly, I just wanted to get out of there. It happened near that really crowded station, Châtelet–Les Halles, I think. Dreadful place, that station. A warren! I can see why you’d be upset. Are you sure your bag was okay? Yeah, everything seemed to be there. I just checked like, five times. It’s more the principle of it, you know? And the fact that it completely ruined the vibe for a bit. I can imagine. So, apart from almost being robbed, French food and picturesque streets? Pretty much! Oh, and Lisa – you know, from work? – she’s going through a really messy breakup. Apparently, he left her for his Pilates instructor. Oh, the  nerve ! Pilates instructor, honestly? What's wrong with people? Poor Lisa. That's terrible! She always seemed so happy. She was telling me last week about planning a weekend away with him. Yeah, well, that's off the cards now, obviously. I felt so bad for her. I tried to offer some advice, but honestly, what  can  you say? Just be a good listener, dear. Sometimes that’s all people need. Speaking of needing things, I’m starving. What are we having for dinner?

Morning, Chloe! Chaos as usual before a Monday lecture, huh? Tell me about it! I swear, the students are actively  more  tired on Mondays than I am. And you? Ready to wrestle with passive voice again? Sadly, yes. Though I’ve started thinking about framing it as a stylistic choice rather than a grammatical error. Makes it less… soul-crushing. You’ve been quiet about your weekend – anything exciting happen? Not particularly. Went down to Chichester to see my Nan. She’s… well, she’s Nan. Complaining about everything, but secretly thrilled I visited. She keeps asking when I’m getting engaged, it’s exhausting. Oh, gosh. The pressure! Speaking of, Liam—from the English department—proposed to Sarah last week. It’s all anyone’s been talking about. Very public, down on one knee in the library.  Really ? Liam? Wow. They seem…nice. But the library? Bit much, isn’t it? My ex, Mark, tried to propose at a West End musical. It was mortifying. Oh no! Which one?  Wicked . I swear, half the audience knew it was coming. And he’d booked the worst seats in the house. Long story short, we didn’t last. Divorced now, thankfully. Oh, Chloe, I'm so sorry to hear that. That sounds… a lot. It's good you got out of it. Anyway, back to less stressful topics – Nan and Chichester. Did you get any decent coffee down there? Brighton's spoiling me. The coffee was… functional. Honestly, going to Nan’s is more about the obligation than the enjoyment. It’s a two-hour train ride each way, though, so I tried to make the most of it. She’s been going on about how much my hair has changed. Apparently, ‘a proper young lady’ doesn’t dye it purple. Tell her it’s a statement about the evolving nature of linguistic structures! She wouldn't understand, but… it’s the principle of the thing. Speaking of principle, I'm counting down to payday. Student loan repayments are looming. Ugh, don’t even  mention  student loans. I still owe a fortune from my Masters, and this supervisor job barely covers rent and, well, coffee. It's ironic, isn't it? A Masters degree and I’m basically telling people where the biscuits are. Hey, don't downplay it! Supervising is a skill. You’re a people person, you handle everything. It’s more than I could do.

Right, so how much water did you say? Like, for the rice? Just enough to cover it, love. See? About an inch above the rice. And then a good pinch of salt. Don’t be shy with the salt, it makes all the difference. An inch… okay. So, like… that much?  gestures vaguely with a measuring cup  Yep, perfect. See, I always use this pan. It’s got a really thick base, so it doesn’t stick. You remember last time when it all stuck to the bottom and we had to scrape it off? Ugh, yeah. That was… not good. It tasted burnt. Exactly! So thick base, good heat, and don't stir it once it's boiling. Just leave it to do its thing. While that’s simmering, we can get the curry going. Are you still up for trying to make it spicy? Yeah! I want to try with the jalapenos. Like, not  too  spicy, but enough to… you know. Enough to feel alive?  laughs  Okay, okay. We’ll start with half a jalapeno then, finely chopped. And remember what I said about handling them? Don’t touch your eyes! Yeah, you said it burns. Like, really bad. It does! Learned that the hard way. Now, are you wanting to go out for food  ever  again or are we sticking to cooking? I found those vouchers for ‘Spice Paradise’ – remember, the one with all the pictures of really colourful curries? Spice Paradise? Oh yeah! The one where that guy had, like, a really noticeable… thing with his face?  Sighs  You and your observations. Yes, that's the one. He has a facial difference, darling. It’s not something to point out. He makes a brilliant vindaloo, though. Sorry. I just… noticed. It was kinda… different. It's okay, you're learning. It's just important to be respectful. Anyway, the vouchers are for 20% off, but honestly, I’m kind of enjoying cooking again. Especially with you helping. Me too. It's better than getting pizza all the time, I guess. Though, pizza’s good. Pizza  is  good. But too much isn't. Did you see what they put in some of that ready-made pizza? The amount of salt is shocking! And the fats… Ew. Is that why the chicken looked a bit… grey yesterday? I thought it might be going off. Exactly! It was. It’s all the preservatives and stuff.

Right, so then Miss Harrison, you remember her, the one with the perm that never moved, she goes, “Daniel, you’ve not handed in your coursework!” And I’m like, “Coursework? What coursework?” Oh, God, Miss Harrison. She was terrifying. Absolutely terrifying. You always knew when she was coming because you could  smell  the hairspray. Honestly, school was just… a blur of anxiety. Did anyone actually  enjoy  it? I had good teachers, mostly. Mrs. Davies in English Lit, she really got me into wanting to go to uni. But yeah, the stress. It was relentless. How’s uni going anyway, Chloe? It’s… okay. It’s a lot. More reading than I anticipated, honestly. And trying to balance it with, you know, actually  living . Rent’s a killer though. Seriously. Rent’s always a killer. You should see the prices round here, even for a shoebox. Still, better than being stuck here, eh? No offense. None taken, Daniel. Whitehaven’s… comfortable. But a bit stagnant, isn’t it? It can be. That’s why I wanted to get out, get a job where I’m actually helping people. It’s exhausting, the support work, but it's worth it. Long shifts though. I’m knackered most of the time. Knackered? You wouldn’t know the meaning of the word. You’re  working . I haven't had a proper job since… well, since ever, really. Don’t start, Daniel. We’ve been over this. There were opportunities. Opportunities? What opportunities? A shelf stacker at Tesco? That’s not an opportunity, that’s…existing. Maybe you need to think a bit outside the box. Have you looked at online stuff? Freelancing? Freelancing? I’m not exactly brimming with marketable skills, am I? It’s not like I can code or design websites. You’re a history graduate, Daniel. You could tutor. Write articles. There’s stuff you can do. You just need to build a portfolio. Easier said than done. Portfolio, schmortfolio. Plus, you need a computer that doesn’t take five minutes to load a single webpage. You could use mine. Whenever you want. Seriously. Cheers, Chloe. I might take you up on that. What’s for pudding? I’m starving after all this intellectual debate. I made that chocolate brownie thing. Remember? The one with the raspberries? Ooh, yes please! That was amazing last time. I’m stuffed from the pasta, but I think I can  always  find room for chocolate brownie.

This pasta’s lovely, honestly. You’ve really outdone yourself, Geoff. Proper comforting after a day of wrangling conference calls and demanding speakers. Mmmph. It’s just a simple tomato and basil, lass. Nothing fancy. Glad you like it though. Needed something to do, y’know? Gets a bit… quiet, just bein’ ‘round here all day. I can imagine. It must be a big change, retiring. Mum says you’re driving her mad with all your projects though – rebuilding birdhouses, learning to knit… She exaggerates. A man needs hobbies. Keeps the brain ticking over. Though that knitting… that was a disaster. Ended up with a wonky scarf that only a very forgiving dog could wear. Oh, I’d love to see a picture! Seriously though, are you enjoying it? Being retired, I mean? It’s… odd. It’s lovely not having to get up at six every morning, that’s for sure. But I miss the… the buzz. The routine. The people. Even Old Man Hemmings from accounts, as much as he grated on me. You’d think you’d be thrilled to escape Hemmings! I’ve got enough “Hemmings” types at work, constantly questioning every single decision. Honestly, sometimes I feel like I spend more time justifying things than actually  doing  them. Sounds familiar. Though I wouldn't have been justifying things, just… doing. That was the role, eh? Anyway, you sound stressed. Long day? You have no idea. We’ve got that tech conference next month, and the main speaker – some Silicon Valley guru – has just requested a specific brand of sparkling water that’s apparently ‘infused with moonlight’. Moonlight?! What in tarnation?! I kid you not. Apparently, it enhances his creativity. My boss just emailed back saying “Consider it done.” I’m the one who has to  find  this stuff, Geoff! I've spent the last hour scouring the internet for 'moonlight-infused water'. Well, that’s… something. People are strange, aren’t they? Though, maybe you could just get regular sparkling water and shine a torch on it? Genius! I’m writing that down. Actually, I'm starting a list of all the ridiculous requests I get. It’ll be a book one day. "Confessions of a Conference Coordinator." You should! You’d make a fortune. Speaking of fortunes, are you still going to that fitness class? The one you were saying was tiring you out? Ugh, don't remind me.

Right, who’s doing the dishes tonight? Don’t all look at me at once. It's your turn, Leo. Ugh, Mum! But I did them last time! Well… sort of. I stacked the dishwasher. “Sort of” doesn’t count, mate. Stacking is the easy bit. The actual washing up, the scraping… that’s the test. I’ll help Leo. But only if you promise to watch some of the tennis with me later. Wimbledon’s on. Deal. But you two are a team. No half-hearted loading, got it? And no arguments. Honestly, sometimes I think I’m running a creche. It’s not  that  bad, is it? Remember that time your grandad tried to teach you to load a dishwasher properly? He went on for a good half hour about plate angles. Oh god, don’t remind me. He was obsessed. He used to say it was like building a fortress. He was a bit…particular. Like when he wouldn’t let anyone touch his model trains. He was a man of routines, your grandad. A product of his time, I suppose. Speaking of… I was reading something the other day about how Hitler was apparently a terrible painter. That's a pretty well-known fact, actually.
