Rejected from art school twice, if I remember rightly. It's a strange thought isn't it? How different things might have been if he’d been a successful artist. Woah, that's…dark. Can we not talk about Hitler after dinner? It ruins my appetite. Sorry, love. Just a random thought. Right, let’s move swiftly on. Leo, is that a… moustache you’re attempting to grow? No! It’s… stubble. It’s cool. All the guys at school are doing it. It looks like you've drawn it on with a marker pen. Shut up, Jamie! It's evolving! It needs time to… mature. Careful you don’t end up looking like a Bond villain. He’s got a point. Maybe stick to clean-shaven for now. Oh, and Leo, your girlfriend Sarah, is she still posting all those pictures on Instagram? Yeah. Why? Just… be mindful of what’s on there, okay? Once it’s out there, it’s out there. And maybe don’t comment on  every  single photo she posts. It can come across a bit… keen. But I like her photos! There’s a balance, son. A delicate art to social media engagement.

Honestly, the sofa situation is stressing me out. I just… I don’t know  where  to start looking. Everything’s either hideous, or costs a fortune, or both. Have you checked Facebook Marketplace? There's always good stuff on there, people just wanting rid. You might get a bargain. Aye, Marketplace is alright, but you gotta be careful. Loads of time-wasters, and things aren’t always as they seem when you get there. Remember that dresser I went to look at? Advert said ‘excellent condition’… it was falling apart! Oh, bless you, Mum. I can see it now. You getting all excited then finding a disaster. I’m just picturing it. Did you take all the stuff to the tip yesterday, Mum? The garden stuff? I did, yeah. Queue was mental, though. Absolutely rammed. Everyone’s having a clearout, I think. And that lad on the gate was a right misery guts. Didn't crack a smile all day. Some people just  are  like that, aren’t they? It’s a job, but you can still be polite. Speaking of misery… have you heard anything more about Sarah’s sister, Jen? How’s her little lad doing with his asthma? Not a lot, actually. Sarah mentioned briefly the other day he’d had a bit of a flare-up, but she’s been so busy with… well, you know, with Mark being poorly. Oh, poor Mark. How  is  he? Still really bad then? Yeah, pretty rough. She says he’s got all sorts of tests coming up, they’re trying to figure out what’s going on. It’s scary, isn’t it? He’s not even sixty. It’s awful. Things like that. My Auntie Elsie, she went downhill so quickly. One minute she was perfectly fine, the next… well, you know. The dementia just took her. That's terrifying. It's a horrible disease. Makes you appreciate your own health, doesn't it? Definitely. It's a bit weird though, isn’t it? Seeing people you knew as solid as a rock... changing. Remember old Mr. Henderson from down the road? Always swearing like a trooper in the garden? Proper character. His daughter said he doesn’t even  remember  swearing anymore. Just… blank. Oh, stop it, you’re making me well up! Speaking of changes… did you see they’re building another huge housing estate just past the library?

Honestly, Mum, this whole week at work has been… draining. It feels like everyone's walking on eggshells since the redundancy announcements. Oh, dear. Still? I thought they'd made the decisions by now. Is anyone you’re close to affected? Not directly, thankfully. But the atmosphere is awful. Old Mr. Henderson in accounts, he’s absolutely gutted. Been there thirty years, apparently. And the whispers are endless – who’s next, what departments are safe… it’s just stressful. Poor man. Thirty years is a long time. It’s a rotten thing to do, really, announcing redundancies right before Christmas. They could have waited, surely? You’d think so. Anyway, enough about work. It's ruining my evening just thinking about it. What have  you  been up to? Anything exciting happening at school? Just the usual Christmas chaos, really. Mock exams are looming, so the kids are all stressed. And I’m trying to get everything organised for the Ofsted visit in January. It’s a nightmare, honestly. Still, keeps me busy. Did you manage to get to the gym this week? You were saying you wanted to try that new spin class. I did! Tuesday and Thursday. It’s… intense. I thought I was reasonably fit, but wow. My legs were screaming. I might need a lie down just  talking  about it. Good for you though, sticking with it. It's good to have something for yourself. Speaking of which, your Grandad's been asking after you. He's been a bit down since the weather turned. Says his arthritis is playing up. Oh, bless him. I should really call him. I keep meaning to, but then work… you know how it is. I’ll do it tonight, promise. Has he been eating properly? He always skips meals when he’s feeling a bit low. Honestly, it's a battle. I keep sending him soups and casseroles. He says he's not hungry, then I catch him sneaking biscuits! Men, honestly. Anyway, what about this weekend? Any plans? Not really. I was thinking of just having a chill weekend, maybe do some Christmas shopping. You? Well, your Dad and I were talking, and we're starting to seriously look at getting that extension done on the back. We’ve been putting it off for years, haven't we? Getting quotes, looking at designs… it's a big project. Oh wow!

Right, Leo, eat your broccoli. It’s good for you, makes you strong like Mick! Mum, Mick doesn’t  need  to be stronger! He’s already, like, super strong. He can build anything with sticks. And broccoli is… yuck. Boooo! Leo! Don’t throw your food. And yes, Mick is strong, but even Mick needs his greens. Now, what did you want to do today? You’ve been glued to that screen all morning. But there’s nothing to  do ! Everyone’s at their grandparents or on holiday. Ben’s in Spain with his family, and Chloe’s with her aunties in Devon. Oh, poor you. Well, maybe we could go swimming? The pool’s not too busy during the week. Swimming’s okay… But I went yesterday. And it’s boring on my own. I wish Finn was here. I know, darling. Finn’s family are busy this week, remember? He’s probably building amazing stick structures himself, just like Mick! Maybe we could invite Leo’s friend, little Patrick, over? His mum’s always asking if we’re free. Patrick? He’s… a bit little, isn’t he? He just likes smashing things. Remember when he broke your plant pot? Yes, I remember the plant pot. But he’s growing up fast. And it would be nice for Leo to have a playmate. What about you practising your guitar? You promised me you’d do at least half an hour today. Ugh,  guitar . It’s so hard! My fingers hurt. And I don’t even know what to play. Mr. Henderson just keeps saying “practise your scales,” but scales are boring. I want to learn, like, a real song. Well, maybe you could look up some easy songs online? There are loads of tutorials. Or I could try to help – I used to play a bit of piano, ages ago. It’s all the same sort of principle, isn't it? You played piano? Really? I didn’t know that! Can you still play anything? Oh, goodness no. Honestly, it was decades ago, and I was never very good. More like… plinking. Leo, darling, are you finished? Da-da! Da-da! He wants me to play with him. Can I just… quickly show him something on my tablet? There’s this really cool manga I found. It’s all in Japanese, but it has pictures… Japanese? Where did you learn about manga?

Oh, for crying out loud,  now  he decides to reveal his tragic backstory? Bit convenient, innit? Shush, you. It's building tension. Though, you're right, it  is  a bit… textbook. Like they ticked ‘tragic past’ off a checklist somewhere. Textbook is putting it mildly. It’s like someone’s watched every action film ever made and just… mashed ‘em together. Still, the explosions are decent. Explosions always are. Reminds me of that time I went to see that fireworks display over the Mersey. Proper biblical, that was. Oh, aye! The one where it started raining halfway through and everyone just stayed put anyway? Mental. Speaking of mental, I need to book a dentist appointment. Been putting it off for ages.  Ugh . Don’t even. The dentist is my personal nemesis. That little scraping noise… sends shivers down me spine. Dr. Bell’s alright though, isn't he? Proper Scouser, too. Bit of a chat, but you can't fault his bedside manner. Yeah, he's decent. Good accent, too. It's important, a good accent. Adds character. Yours is, obviously, the best. Oh, you flatterer. Though I  do  get asked if I’m from Liverpool about five times a day, even just ordering a coffee. You think my accent’s gotten worse since I moved back? Nah, it’s strong as ever. It’s just… distinctive. Like a musical instrument. Mine, apparently, is ‘Midlands twang’. Doesn’t exactly roll off the tongue, does it? ‘Midlands twang’ sounds… quaint. Like a character in a Victorian novel. Anyway, are we still on for that gig next week? The one at the O2? Absolutely. Can't wait. Heard the support band are pretty good. Post-punk, apparently. A bit shouty, but I’m into it. Excellent. I’ve been trying to get back into reading, too. Found this old book in a charity shop. Some proper gritty Northern Realism. Really pulls you in. Ooh, what is it? I’m still slogging through that sci-fi novel everyone's raving about. It’s alright, but it feels a bit…cold. Lacking in heart, y’know? It's called 'Stone Walls', by a bloke called Alan Sillitoe. Factory life in Nottingham in the sixties. Proper bleak. Makes you appreciate central heating and Netflix. Speaking of, fancy ordering a takeaway? I’m starving. Now  you’re  talking. Chinese? Indian? I’m open to suggestions. Though I’m still vaguely regretting that dodgy kebab I had last week.

Honestly, this coffee is a lifesaver. Been chasing after little Leo all morning. He's a whirlwind, that one. Oh, I can imagine! Three year olds have endless energy, don’t they? How was the Easter cake making? Did you manage to avoid a complete kitchen disaster? Mostly. There was a slight… incident with the sprinkles. Ended up everywhere. Leo thought it was snowing indoors. But the cakes turned out alright. Sent one over to your Auntie Maureen, she was thrilled. Said it reminded her of your Grandma. Oh, that’s lovely. She always loved a good bake. I’m glad it cheered her up. I haven’t seen her in ages, I really must make more of an effort. It's just… school's been  manic . Still enjoying teaching then? You seemed a bit down about it last time we spoke. It’s… complicated. The kids are wonderful, truly. But the workload is just relentless. And now there’s all this talk of curriculum changes, new assessment methods… it's exhausting trying to keep up with it all. That sounds stressful. You always were a conscientious one. Do you think you’ll stick it out long-term? I’m not sure, honestly. I’ve been looking at a few training courses, actually. Thinking maybe I could move into special educational needs. It feels like it would be more… rewarding, you know? More focused on really helping individual children. That sounds interesting. You'd be brilliant at that, you always have a knack for understanding people. Have you told David about it? Yeah, I mentioned it. He’s supportive, as always. Though he does worry about the pay cut if I retrain. We're saving for a holiday, you know? We're thinking of going back to Greece this year, remember how much we loved it last time? Oh, Greece! Yes! That was amazing. Definitely a good idea to go back. It's good you're talking about it with David. He’s a sensible lad. Speaking of big plans, are you still sorting out the Christening for little Elsie? Mostly. The church is booked, and we’ve got the photographer sorted. I’m stressing about the guest list though! Everyone wants to be involved, it’s turned into a bit of a nightmare. Your side of the family are… extensive to say the least. You're not wrong there! Don't worry, I’ll handle it.

Honestly, the parents this year… it’s a different breed, isn’t it? I’m battling with three sets who seem to think my lesson plans are open to suggestions - and by suggestions, I mean complete rewrites! Oh, don’t even get me  started . It’s the instant access to information, I think. Suddenly, every parent’s a pedagogical expert because they read an article on Facebook. I had one emailing me about ‘growth mindset’ last week, telling me I wasn't fostering it enough! Oh, bless. It's exhausting. Still, at least the kids are lovely. How are things with you? Still navigating the joys of year six SATs prep? Don’t remind me! It’s looming. Honestly, I feel like all we do is test, test, test. Little Leo keeps asking me if a bad score means he’s ‘stupid’. Breaks your heart, doesn't it? Oh, absolutely. I try to tell them it’s just one snapshot, one way of measuring things, but it's hard to get through. Speaking of little ones, how’s Winston doing? Still terrorizing the neighbourhood? Oh, you know Winston. He’s a whirlwind. He’s discovered the joy of digging in the garden, which is lovely... except he’s currently excavated a substantial portion of my rose bushes. My husband, Arthur, is furious. Oh dear! Is Arthur still…embroiled in that online pottery business? He is. Slowly but surely. It’s mostly a labour of love at this point, to be honest. He's getting some lovely reviews, but profit margins are…minimal. He spends more on the kiln electricity than he makes in sales, I suspect. It’s his retirement plan, apparently. Bless him. It's good he has something he enjoys. I’ve been trying a new skincare regime, actually. Remember I said my skin was feeling a bit blah? Oh yes! What have you gone for? I’m forever on the lookout for something that actually works. I'm starting to feel like I need scaffolding just to hold my face up! You and me both! I found this little independent brand online, all natural ingredients. It's early days, but it  feels  nicer than everything else I've tried. And the smell is divine - lavender and chamomile. Ooh, that sounds lovely. Anything lavender-scented reduces my stress levels by at least thirty percent. How are your parents doing?

Honestly, this charoset is incredible, Maya. You’ve outdone yourself. It's not too sweet, is it? My Grandma Rose always made hers like pure apple sauce with, like, a mountain of sugar. Oh, God, no. Definitely not like Grandma Rose’s. I actually used dates this year, which makes it a bit stickier, and a  tiny  bit of orange juice. It’s a secret. Don’t tell anyone. Dates are a good shout. Makes it feel… ancient, somehow. You know, really connecting to the story. Speaking of which, Leo, are you following along with the Haggadah, or are you just enjoying the food? Both! Multi-tasking. I’m absorbing the historical significance through osmosis… and through the matzah ball soup. Seriously, is this from a packet, or did you  make  the matzah balls? Made, obviously! Though I did contemplate just getting the Streit’s ones just to save time. But honestly, after attempting croissants last week… I needed a win in the kitchen. Croissants, huh? Ambitious. I tried making sourdough once. It resembled a hockey puck. Took three days to get that right. Oh, sourdough is a beast. Completely unforgiving. You need practically a PhD in fermentation. Which reminds me, David, you were saying you were thinking about a trip to Italy? Yeah, potentially. My sister’s been banging on about Florence for ages. Wants to drag me around all the art galleries. It would be a nice break from… well, from everything. Thinking maybe May? Florence is amazing. Food’s incredible. Though, obviously, not kosher. Speaking of which, remember that time Uncle Ben tried to order a pork sandwich in Rome? Oh, don’t remind me. The waiter was  so  confused. He kept trying to explain it was "prosciutto di Parma," like that made it better. Ben just kept saying, "No pig!" He truly is a force of nature. Reminds me of that story my mother told me… about her grandfather trying to explain to a Parisian chef in the 1930s why he couldn’t eat ortolan. Apparently, the chef just burst out laughing. Ortolan?! That’s…that’s the bird you eat with the napkin over your head, right? To catch the juices? Seriously barbaric. Absolutely barbaric. Though, I read somewhere it’s making a comeback on some posh French menus. Which is just… appalling. Right, appalling. So, Maya, any other secret ingredients in this charoset? Seriously, it's incredible.

Right, so, who actually finished “The Seven Husbands of Evelyn Hugo”? Because honestly, I started it and just… couldn’t get into it. All the hype and it felt really, really… soapy. I did! I blazed through it on the train last week. It  is  soapy, absolutely, but in a good way! Like a guilty pleasure soapy. And I thought the twist was actually quite clever. You’ve got to give it a few chapters, honestly. I’m about halfway through. I’m finding it a bit slow, though. I keep getting distracted by… well, everything. I’ve started knitting another scarf. This one’s for my nephew, a ridiculous bright orange. Oh, a knitter! I’ve tried. Honestly, I just end up with a tangled mess. My mum tried to teach me, years ago, but I’m all thumbs. Crochet is marginally less terrifying, I think. My aunt’s a crochet queen. She makes these incredible blankets. Sent us one for little Leo last Christmas, it’s enormous. He practically lives under it. It’s very mindful, isn’t it? Just the rhythm of the needles. Keeps my brain quiet. Speaking of quiet, how was your weekend with your sister, Sarah? Did she finally manage to wrestle those garden gnomes from next door? Oh, don’t even  start  on the garden gnomes. It’s escalated. Apparently, they've now got tiny little fishing rods. She's threatening legal action. It’s ridiculous. She sent me photos; it looks like a miniature, aggressively cheerful militia has taken over their front lawn. Honestly, some people! It sounds like something out of a sitcom. Did you see that new series, “After Life”? Ricky Gervais is just brilliant, isn’t he? A bit bleak, obviously, but also really funny. I’ve heard good things, but I’m trying to limit my screen time. I’ve been trying to get back into reading proper books, you know, the paper kind. I bought a Kindle a few years ago, and it mostly gathers dust. I’m the same. I  love  the feel of a book in my hands, the smell of the paper. Ebooks just feel… cold. Although, I will admit, they’re useful for holidays when you need to pack light. That’s true. And for those really embarrassing cover books, you know when you're on the train and you really don’t want everyone to know you’re reading a bodice-ripper.

Right, so… the box feels suspiciously light, doesn’t it? For a flagship phone. You'd think they’d at least  pretend  to give you some heft for the price. Don't be dramatic. Everything's going smaller and lighter these days. Oh, good, screen protector's included, at least. Always forgetting those. And… yep, there it is. Beautiful, isn't it? The Arctic White is a good shout. It is. Very minimalist. Though I still miss the days when Nokia phones were basically indestructible bricks. Remember those? You could use one as a hammer and it’d probably still make a call. Dad! You and your Nokia nostalgia. They were solid, yes, but functionally… limited. This thing's got more processing power than the computers we had in uni. Though speaking of, I feel a bit silly setting up a brand new phone  here , in Finland of all places. The irony isn't lost on me. Well, you needed a new phone  before  we came, love. Your old one was on its last legs, threatening to spontaneously combust every time you opened Instagram. And this seemed like a good time, with the new international SIM and everything. So, let’s get it sorted. Do you want me to walk you through the initial setup, or are you feeling confident? A quick walkthrough would be good, actually. I'm fairly tech-savvy, but I always get tripped up on the data privacy stuff. They bury it in the small print, don’t they? Like, “By continuing, you agree to have your location tracked, your browsing history analysed, and your soul sold to the highest bidder.” Pretty much. Okay, first things first. Language selection. Let’s stick with English, unless you fancy testing your Finnish? Then, connect to the hotel Wi-Fi– thankfully they’ve given us the password this time. Right. Now, it’s asking about restoring from a backup. Are you using iCloud or Google Drive? Google Drive. I'm a bit of an Android ecosystem person, remember? Though this is… it’s the first  proper  Android phone I’ve had in years. Always been a OnePlus girl, but you convinced me to try this Pixel. And you won’t regret it. The camera is phenomenal, seriously. Plus, you benefit from all those Google AI features. Now, it’s asking to transfer apps… This'll take a while. Fancy another  lonkero ?

Right, so Leo’s birthday is getting closer, isn’t it? We need to actually  make  plans this time, not just talk about them. Yeah, Mum. I know. I was thinking... maybe a laser quest thing? All my mates are up for that. Hmm, laser quest. That sounds… loud. And expensive. What about something at home? We could do a movie night, get pizza? Doggie! Doggie! Yes, sweetie, doggie. Leo loves doggies, don’t you? Speaking of which, remember Malamooche? Old Mrs. Higgins’ dog? The fluffiest thing ever. She was a bit weird, Mrs. Higgins. Always offering me biscuits. And Malamooche shed  everywhere . She was a kind lady. And Malamooche was a lovely dog. Though I always preferred cats, myself. What about you, Leo? Do you like cats? No! Doggie! He's a dog person, definitely. I’m more of an animal person generally. Like, have you seen Red Pandas? They’re amazing. They’re practically real-life Pokemon. Red Pandas? No, I haven't. What are they like? They're like, little fluffy bears, but with ringed tails. They live in the mountains and eat bamboo. Honestly, look them up when you have a minute. They’re way cooler than cats, even. I’ll try to. Now, back to the birthday... have you thought about who you want to invite? A list, darling. We need a list. I’ve got a rough one in my head. Sam, Ben, Josh, maybe Ethan... and definitely Tom. Tom, right. And what about Lily? You two are friends now, aren't you? Uh, yeah. I guess. She's okay. Okay? Just okay? You were building Lego with her last week. Yeah, but… she’s kind of bossy. Well, some people are. Anyway, we need to get her an invite if she’s a friend, even a “kind of” friend. Have you thought about a present for Jamie? His birthday’s next week, isn’t it? Ugh, Jamie. I don't know. He already has everything. That’s not true. He needs a friend who remembers his birthday. Have you thought about that new Japanese animated film everyone’s talking about? The one about the robot? Spirited Away? Yeah, but he’s seen it. He’s really into anime. I was thinking maybe one of those board games? The new one with the dragons? Oh, that does sound good! We could all play that. Though I’m terrible at strategy games.

Honestly, Christmas at Nana and Grandad’s was… intense. Not bad, just… a  lot . Like, a full-on assault on the senses. Intense how? Was it the sheer number of people crammed into that little bungalow? Because I remember it being like sardines in a tin. Oh, don’t I know it! Your Grandad always insisted on having  every  cousin, aunt, uncle, and their dog. And the decorations! He’d start putting them up in November. November! He did love his Christmas, Arthur did. Wouldn’t let anyone near the fairy lights though, convinced they were a fire hazard. “Hazardous festive cheer,” he’d call it. It was the combination of everything. The people, the lights, the music… and the sherry. Oh, the sherry. Nana always had a sneaky glass, or three, before even starting on the cooking. Classic Nana! My Lola – that’s my grandma, from the Philippines – she’s the same with San Miguel. Christmas isn't Christmas without her slightly tipsy stories. Though hers are usually about dodging Japanese soldiers during the war, which is… a bit heavier than Nana’s tales of burnt Yorkshire puddings. Oh my goodness, that’s a world away from Yorkshire puddings, isn’t it? It’s fascinating how different cultures celebrate. We’re so steeped in our own traditions, you forget others even exist. It is. I remember travelling through Italy once, just before Christmas. They don’t have the same build-up as we do. It's much more focused on the religious aspect, and the feasting on Christmas Eve. And the  panettone ! Beautiful stuff. See, I’d never even  heard  of panettone before last year when Sarah – you know, from uni – brought some in. She’s Italian, and she was horrified when I asked if it was some kind of fancy bread pudding. Apparently, it’s a whole  thing . It's good stuff, yeah. Lola makes a similar thing called bibingka – rice cake cooked in banana leaves. It’s… an acquired taste, honestly. Kind of salty, kind of sweet. Sounds interesting. It's funny, isn't it, how food is so tied to culture and memories? I can smell my mother’s Christmas cake baking from here, even though she’s been gone for twenty years. Absolutely. It’s a sensory trigger. And not just food. Accents, too. I can hear someone from Barrow – like yourself, dear – and immediately think of the seaside and a certain… robustness.

Honestly, this shepherd’s pie is a lifesaver. Just needed something… comforting, you know? After the day I’ve had. It smells fantastic, actually. You’ve outdone yourself, love. Though anything’s good after a day of spreadsheets, let’s be real. How was transcription today? Anything juicy? Oh, you would  not  believe. A police interview. About… competitive vegetable growing. Apparently, it gets  fierce . Accusations of sabotage, prize-winning marrow theft… honestly. Competitive vegetable growing? Is that a real thing? Apparently! I’m transcribing the whole thing. It’s a side-splittingly dull, yet oddly fascinating, saga. Though my ears are starting to bleed from the technical terms. “Bolt resistance” and “leaf blight prevention” are now permanently lodged in my brain. Sounds… intense. Reminds me of that documentary we watched about sheep shearing. Equally bizarre. Speaking of intense, have you started the new Vera? The one set in Northumberland? Not yet, no. Been buried in edits. The publishers are pushing for a revised ending. They think it needs… more oomph. More of a twist. Honestly, I think they just want me to rewrite the whole thing! Oh, darling. That sounds exhausting. They always do that, don’t they? "Just a little tweak…" which turns into a complete overhaul. Exactly! It’s infuriating. Anyway, Vera. I’m hoping to have a quiet evening on Saturday and binge-watch it. Ken Stott is just…  chefs kiss . He’s brilliant. And Northumberland looks stunning, even when someone’s being murdered. I’ve been meaning to book a weekend away up there. Maybe coincide with a new series? Ooh, good idea! We could all go. Though I’d need a solid week of non-vegetable related transcripts beforehand to recover. That sounds lovely. We haven't had a proper weekend away in ages. Has anyone heard from Fiona? She said she was going to try and get tickets for that theatre production. I texted her yesterday. She was still on the waiting list. Apparently, it's sold out for weeks. She said she might try her luck on the day, but it's a long shot. She’ll manage. She always does. She’s remarkably resourceful. Speaking of resourceful, anyone using Kindles these days? I’m thinking of finally getting one. My bookshelves are threatening to collapse under the weight of hardbacks. Oh, I switched years ago. Best decision ever. Particularly for holidays. And you can download samples before you buy.

Now, you’re sure about this, Eileen? You’ve thought it through proper? Oh, Arthur, I've been thinking about it for weeks! Honestly, it’s the only sensible thing to do. The house is just… too much for me now. Too much garden, too much cleaning. She’s right, you know. It’s a big place for one person. A lovely place, mind, but a big place. I know, I know. It just feels… hasty. You’ve lived there nearly forty years. And it’s a nice area, Harrow. Not like some places. Hasty? Arthur, I’m seventy! My knees ache when I bend down to deadhead the roses, and the loft needs doing, and frankly, I’m tired of climbing all those stairs. A bungalow is what I need. One level. Everything within reach. Sensible. Very sensible. Have you looked at places in Middlesex at all? Closer to us? A few. There’s a lovely little one in Pinner. Two bedrooms, a small garden, and a conservatory. It’s all on one level, thankfully. And it’s near a bus route so I can still pop over and see you both. Pinner, eh? That’s… alright. Still a bit busy for my liking, but alright. Have you got someone to help with the move? It’s a lot of stuff you’ve accumulated over the years. David’s offered, of course. He’s been wonderful. And I’ve asked Margaret and Susan to help pack the kitchen. Good, good. David’s a strong lad. And Margaret’s always been organised, she’ll get that kitchen sorted in a jiffy. Still, you’ll want a proper removal company for the big furniture. Don’t skimp on that, Eileen. Back problems aren’t worth saving a few quid. He's right there. A proper removal company. And make sure they’re insured. You don’t want anything broken. Those china dolls your mother gave you… I’ve thought of that, Arthur! I’ve already got quotes from three companies. One’s even got specialist packing for fragile items. Honestly, I’m not completely helpless, you know. Didn’t say you were, dear. Just… worried about you. It’s a big change. It's a positive change, though, isn’t it? Less stress, more freedom. You can take up your painting again properly. That’s what I’m hoping for. And maybe join a book club.

Right, so, Friday. Is everyone still good for the Black Duck? I’ve put a tentative reservation down for eight thirty. Yeah, sounds good to me. Though, honestly, after today, I’m just looking forward to  sitting  more than anything. This data cleaning is brutal. Agreed. My eyes are definitely crossing. Eight thirty works, though. I’ll need a large wine to recover. Aye, Black Duck’s decent. Eight thirty’s grand. I’ve been meaning to ask, did anyone else see that massive moth clinging to the window in the archive this afternoon? Honestly, it was the size of my hand. Oh my goodness, yes! I nearly walked into it! It was absolutely enormous. I tried to shoo it outside, but it just kept flapping around like it was lost. Classic moth behaviour. They get disoriented by the lights. You were being a good Samaritan though, trying to help it. Good Samaritan? You were screaming, Eleanor. Let’s be real. I was  expressing concern ! It was a very large insect! And possibly prehistoric. I think you’re exaggerating slightly. But it  was  big. Reminded me of the ones my grandma used to get in her garden, always attracted to the lavender. Lavender, aye. My nana used to say lavender kept the bad spirits away. And moths. Apparently, they're both drawn to the scent. That’s a lovely bit of folklore. It's interesting to see how those beliefs persist. Speaking of which, anyone hear anything more about the funding application? I’m starting to get a little twitchy. I chased Professor Armitage earlier. He said he’s expecting an answer by the end of the week. Apparently, they’re having some internal debates about the scope of the project. Sounds promisingly vague. ‘Internal debates’ usually means they’re considering it seriously. Fingers crossed, eh? It’ll be a nightmare if it falls through. All that work for nothing. Tell me about it. I've already started mentally spending my portion on a new microphone. This one’s starting to cut out mid-sentence, and it's deeply unprofessional. A new microphone is always a good investment. Honestly, it's the unseen things that make all the difference in this job. Like decent coffee. And functioning computers. And colleagues who rescue moths! Seriously, though, any dietary requirements for Friday? Just want to make sure I can mention it when I confirm the booking.

Ugh, I genuinely think Mr. Davies is actively trying to make our lives miserable. Tell me about it! That history homework was  brutal . Three essays on the Tudors? Seriously? It's like he thinks we have nothing else going on. Exactly! And the way he phrased the questions… it wasn't even about understanding the history, it was about using specific, obscure vocabulary. Like, who even  says  “heretofore” in normal conversation? Oh my god, you’re right. He loves “heretofore” and “aforementioned.” It’s a competition for him, I swear. Did you manage to finish it all? I was still writing the last paragraph when I had to go to bed. Managed to scrape through, yeah. Mum helped me with a couple of the vocab bits, but I felt so stupid even  needing  help. I think I just threw enough historical facts at it to make it sound intelligent. That’s my strategy too. Fact vomit. It usually gets you a B, at least. Though, I’m starting to worry about Geography. Mrs. Peterson keeps hinting at a surprise test next week. Oh no! On what? I’m actually enjoying Geography at the moment, surprisingly. Learning about plate tectonics is… kinda cool? Don’t encourage me! I’m terrible at remembering all the different types of rock formations. And the capital cities… it’s a lost cause. I spent ten minutes yesterday trying to remember the capital of Botswana. Is it… Gaborone? Yes! Okay, you’re a genius. See, I knew I had friends for a reason. You remember all the random facts. I’m more of a literature person, remember? Yeah, you're brilliant at English. You always get amazing marks on the poetry analyses. I still can’t wrap my head around symbolism half the time. Mrs. Albright just expects us to  feel  it, and I’m like, “I feel confused!” She’s the worst. Although, I did actually enjoy reading ‘Ozymandias’ this week. It's a bit depressing, but the imagery is incredible. Did you notice how…? Oh, speaking of depressing, have you seen the canteen menu for next week? They’re serving that grey sludge they call “Shepherd's Pie” again. Don't even. I think I’m going to start bringing packed lunches every day. It’s a sacrifice, but my stomach will thank me. Plus, Mum makes a really good pasta salad. You're so lucky!

Honestly, this pasta is amazing. Like, seriously good. You were right to pick this place, Mum. Told ya! I saw a review online, said their carbonara was the best in town. And it seems they weren't lying. Dig in, both of you. Aye, it’s good stuff. Not like that place we went to last month, all flash and no flavour. Remember that, Liam? The one near the theatre? Oh god,  that  place. Overpriced and the portions were tiny. I was still hungry afterwards. Felt robbed, I did. Seriously. And the waiter kept trying to upsell us on expensive wine. I just wanted a glass of Pinot Grigio, not a lecture on vintages! They think just because you’re young you don't know anything about wine, do they? I’ve been drinking the stuff longer than you two have been alive, young 'uns! Fair enough, Mum. Speaking of work, how’s everything going with the new department at the shop? Still dealing with endless complaints? Oh, you have no idea. It’s been a nightmare. They decided to re-organize everything just before Christmas, naturally. And now everyone’s blaming  me  because they can't find anything. Honestly, some people. That sounds stressful. Is there, like, a proper system in place yet, or is it just chaos? Chaos, mainly. It’s slowly getting there, but it’s like herding cats. I’ve suggested a colour-coding system for the files, but Janice keeps insisting her old method is ‘perfectly adequate.’ The woman’s been there twenty years and refuses to change a thing. Sounds about right. Change is scary for some people. How are things at work for you, Chloe? Still drowning in admin? Pretty much. It’s busy, though, which is good. I’m helping out with a new project now, data migration from one system to another. It's surprisingly… riveting. Okay, maybe not riveting, but it’s a change of pace. Data migration? Sounds intensely dull. It has its moments. Actually, the worst part is dealing with people who haven't backed up their files. Cue panic stations when the cutover happens. Honestly, it's like no one learned anything about data security. People are daft, all of 'em. Absolutely daft. Now, about your Aunt Carol… she’s been on the phone again. Oh dear. What now? Is it about the Christmas presents again? No, no.

Honestly, the week has been… hectic. Mum’s operation went okay, thankfully. They said it was pretty routine, but you know how she worries. Oh, bless her. I'm glad it went alright. Is she recovering okay? She was so nervous beforehand, wasn’t she? She is, slowly. Mostly just exhausted, and a bit sore. I’m trying to get her to take it easy, but you know Mum – she’s already planning what she’s going to bake next week! It’s just… well, it's made me think, you know? About everything. About…? Just… health, I suppose. It’s silly, isn't it? She's had a scare, and it makes  me  think about everything. And then there's Leo. Oh, Leo. What’s he been up to now? Still getting detentions? Worse, actually. He’s been suspended. For two days. Apparently, he and a mate were messing about in the science lab. Something with… I don't even know, chemicals and a lighter. Honestly, I nearly choked when the headteacher called. Oh, no! That’s dreadful! A lighter?! He’s a bright lad, Leo, but he can be a right handful, can’t he? That's putting it mildly. I’ve grounded him, obviously. No phone, no computer, nothing. He's furious, but honestly, I couldn’t just let that slide. It’s just… it’s so stressful, trying to navigate all this teenage angst. It is. They test you, don’t they? My Sarah was just the same, though obviously, she's a bit older now and thankfully a bit more sensible. She’s been wanting to visit her friend Chloe in Bristol, but I'm a bit worried about letting her go on her own. Bristol is a long way. Is Chloe a good friend? Oh, yeah, they've known each other since primary school. She’s a good girl, Chloe. It's just… things are happening, you know? Things you read about. Makes you wonder. It does. It’s scary. Listen, I need to sort something out with the building society. We need to adjust Mum’s direct debits now she’s retired. I was hoping to pop in on Friday afternoon, but I’ve got that conference call. I could do it for you if you like. If you tell me which ones to adjust. Really? Would you? That would be amazing, actually! I would be so grateful.

Right, honestly, I'm shattered. Double shift last night. My feet are killin' me. Oh no, really? What was it like? Busy? Busy doesn't even  begin  to cover it. It was the student night, see. Every single fresher decided to descend on The Lion at once. It was just… bodies everywhere. And requests. So many requests for ridiculously complicated cocktails they’d seen on TikTok. Ugh, sounds awful. I can imagine. I’m just trying to get through these readings for Political Theory. It's drier than a nun’s… well, you get the picture. At least  I  get to sit down. That's the dream, innit? Sitting down. Or, like, just not having someone yell “Another Jägerbomb!” every thirty seconds. Did you see that new lad, Liam, started at the bar down the road? The one near the train station? Vaguely. Tall, bit scruffy looking? Saw him through the window once. Apparently he’s a student too. Doing… something. Can’t remember what. Yeah, that’s him. Apparently he lasted one shift and nearly had a breakdown. Said he didn’t realise how much  running  bartending involved. I said to him, “Welcome to the club, love.” Honestly, people think it’s all shaking fancy drinks and having a laugh. It’s mostly cleaning up spilt vodka and avoiding eye contact with aggressively flirtatious people. Oh god, sounds horrific. It's tempting to get a part-time job, money's a bit tight. But I don't think I could cope with customer service. I’m terrible with confrontation. You’d be alright. You’re good at just… being firm. Like when you're arguing about philosophy, you don't back down, do you? You could do that with someone asking for a free drink. "Actually, no. The socio-economic implications of free alcohol distribution are deeply problematic." Okay, maybe not. I think I’d just end up crying in the stockroom. Are you still planning on doing a Christmas temp job somewhere? Yeah, thinking about it. My aunty's trying to get me a job at the garden centre. Which, honestly, is miles better than another bar shift. Just potting plants and telling people what fertilizer to use. Sounds blissful. Though, knowing my luck, it'll be during a blizzard. Well, at least you wouldn't be dealing with drunk students. Maybe you could get free plants? Fingers crossed.

Right, so, anyone actually  doing  anything exciting this summer? Or is it just going to be a repeat performance of binge-watching boxsets and complaining about the rain? Speak for yourself, Mark. I'm off to Majorca! All-inclusive, sun, sea, and a distinct lack of Salford drizzle. First proper holiday in… oh, goodness, I’ve lost count. Majorca, is it? Lovely spot. Though a bit… rowdy, if you get near the strip. I spent a week in County Clare myself. Quiet, peaceful, mostly sheep for company. Bliss, I tell you. Bliss. Sheep? Sounds… relaxing, Eileen. I’m attempting to teach my kids the concept of ‘doing nothing’ in Cornwall. It’s proving challenging. They’ve already planned a rigorous schedule of beach volleyball, bodyboarding, and badger watching. Badger watching? Seriously? Apparently, it's 'a thing'. My daughter read about it in some wildlife magazine. I suspect it’ll involve a lot of sitting in the dark, waiting for something that probably won’t show up. Ha! Sounds delightful, David. Reminds me of a ‘wildlife’ holiday I went on once. Ended up staring at a damp patch of grass for three hours, convinced a rare beetle was about to appear. Oh, the disappointments of nature! Though, you know, sometimes the quiet is reward enough. Last week I saw a robin build a nest right outside my window. Nearly cried, I did. That  is  sweet, Eileen. I'm contemplating a weekend in the Lake District. Just… walking. Avoiding people. Possibly taking a flask of tea. Sounds a bit… solitary, Mark? That's the point, Brenda. After a year of shelving books and politely asking students to be quiet, I need solitary. I need nature. I need a significant amount of tea. You're preaching to the choir. I’m hoping the sea air will restore some semblance of sanity before September hits. This last semester has been…intense. University students, eh? Always a handful. Though, I do get a kick out of helping them find that obscure text they need. It's like being a literary detective. More like a literary shepherd, herding them towards the Dewey Decimal System! Honestly, some of them look utterly lost. Remember that lad last year who asked where the 'internet books' were? Oh, don't remind me! I nearly choked on my coffee. The youth of today! Though don’t be too hard on them. They're just trying to navigate a complicated world.

Honestly, the refereeing in this game is absolutely shocking. Shocking! That was a clear foul, clear as day. Mmm? Oh aye, bit soft maybe. He's letting them get away with murder, isn't he? Still, good game though, proper end-to-end stuff. Good game? They're getting completely overrun in midfield! And don't even get me started on their defensive shape. It's like watching a school team. Relax, lass. It's just a football match. Besides, you're getting all worked up over it. Want another chip? I got a mega box from that new place on Mill Road. 'Crispy Heaven', they call it. No thanks. I'm trying to be good. Though… Crispy Heaven, you say? Is it actually any good? I've been craving something proper greasy. Proper greasy is an understatement. It's... transcendent. Salt and chilli chicken wings are  life-changing . They do a decent burger too, though it's the wings you need to focus on. Seriously. You’re tempting me. I had a salad for lunch, which feels like a monumental error in judgement now. This game is just stressing me out and I need comfort food. See? The football gods are telling you something. They’re saying, “Lay down your virtuous salad, and embrace the crispy goodness!” Okay, okay, you've convinced me. But if I regret it tomorrow, it's your fault. No regrets! Just pure, unadulterated fried potato bliss. I’ll even get you some of those onion rings. They're massive. Onion rings  and  wings? You're enabling my bad habits. I'm supporting your emotional wellbeing, there's a difference. Plus, we both know you can't resist a good onion ring. Remember that time we went to that American diner in Brighton? Don't remind me! I think I ate my weight in onion rings that day. And then regretted it for a week. Worth it. Everything's worth it for a good onion ring. Now, watch this, they're building up an attack… Oh, and I’ll get the dips sorted, which ones do you fancy? Garlic mayo or sweet chilli? Sweet chilli, definitely. And stop analysing the game and focus on Crispy Heaven logistics! We need a plan of attack for those wings. Right you are. Operation Crispy Heaven is a go. Seriously though, they need to sub that midfielder. He's running around like a headless chicken.

Right, this tea’s proper good, Mum. You’ve outdone yourself. And Grandma, are you alright with your biscuit? Need me to crumble it a bit? Crumble it? Lad, I've been crumbling biscuits myself for ninety-odd years, I think I can manage. Though, a bit of dunking never hurt anyone, did it? Don't encourage her, Michael! She'll have the whole thing swimming. Honestly, Mum, you know what happens when you dunk. Oh, hush you. A little soggy biscuit never killed anyone. It reminds me of when your Grandad…He loved a good dunk, your Grandad did. Always said it was the only way to get a proper flavour release. He sounds like a man of discerning taste. Did he like films, Grandma? I was telling Mum about that new Scorsese,  Killers of the Flower Moon . Proper long, mind you, three and a half hours. Scorsese? Never heard of him. Back in my day, it was all Bogart and Gable.  Casablanca , that was a good film. Made you weep, it did. And  Gone With The Wind . Oh, Scarlett O’Hara! A beautiful woman. Though a bit dramatic, if you ask me. She’s more of a Morecambe and Wise woman, honestly. She’ll watch anything with Eric and Ernie on. They were funny lads, those two. Always made me laugh. And they didn't go on for three and a half hours! What’s wrong with a bit of brevity these days? Fair enough. I’m just…work’s been hectic, you know? Big project at the moment, trying to get everything signed off. It’s all deadlines and meetings. Needed something long and immersive to switch off afterwards. Sounds stressful. You’re always working, Michael. You need a holiday. Maybe cycle down to Wales, you used to love that. I’ve been thinking about it, actually. My bike's been gathering dust in the garage. I might just dust it off next weekend. I saw old Mr. Henderson down the road, polishing his classic car again. Makes me feel like I should use mine, or at least the bike, more. Cars. Horrible things. Always making a racket. I remember when we didn’t  have  cars. Everyone walked, or got on the tram. Much nicer. Though, your Grandad did have a little Austin Seven. Called her Bessie. He was very proud of Bessie. He was proud of anything that had an engine, bless him.

Right, Leo, one more bite of pancake, please. Honestly, it’s delicious. Poppy, you’ve barely touched yours! What's wrong? It's...sticky. Sticky? It's just a little syrup, darling. It makes it nice. Leo, are you enjoying yours? Yes! It’s the best pancake  ever ! Can I have more syrup, please? You can have a tiny bit more, alright? Poppy, honestly. You love pancakes usually. Are you feeling okay? I just… don’t want it right now. Okay. Well, we’ll put it to one side. It's Pancake Day, you should at least  try  to eat some. It reminds me of being little, my mum always made us pancakes. Though, she wasn't very good at flipping them! They always ended up a bit wonky. Wonky pancakes! That’s funny! It was! She'd laugh and say they were 'characterful'. Speaking of school, how was assembly today, Poppy? Mrs. Davies said you both were very well behaved. It was boring. They talked about...counting. Counting? Oh dear. Well, that  is  a bit dull, isn't it? Leo, what about you? Did you enjoy assembly? We sang a song! About…plants! Oh, lovely! Mrs. Davies is trying to get everyone thinking about Spring. I had a tricky one in my class today. Little Alfie didn’t eat his lunch  at all . Just pushed it around his plate. It breaks your heart, you know? To think some children don’t even  have  lunch to look forward to. Sad. It is very sad. It makes you appreciate what we have, doesn’t it? Right, after pancakes, we need a big teeth-brushing session. And hand washing! You two are like magnets for germs. But I brushed my teeth this morning! That's good, but you need to do it after breakfast too. It’s important. You wouldn't want those pancake sugars sticking to your teeth all day. It makes me think of when  I  was little. We didn’t have electric toothbrushes, you know. Just a boring old brush and some toothpaste. Feels like a lifetime ago. Did you live in Norwich then? No, I grew up in Dartford, in Kent. It's near London. A very different place to Comberton! When I was your age, my biggest dream was to go to Paris. It seemed so exotic and far away. Paris! With the Eiffel Tower? Exactly! We eventually went when I was at university, and it  was  amazing.

This egg fried rice is… surprisingly good. I was bracing myself for it being a bit oily, but it’s actually really fluffy. Right? I think we’ve found  the  Chinese. Old Man Wong’s has been consistently solid for, what, a year now? Easily. Remember when we tried that new place, Golden Dragon, down by the station? That was an absolute disaster. Everything tasted vaguely of dish soap. Oh god, don’t remind me. I spent the next day regretting my life choices. Anyway, anyone catch the news today? Apparently, old Mr. Henderson passed away. Oh no! Old Mr. Henderson from number 14? The one with the prize-winning roses? The very same. Apparently a heart attack. He was a lovely bloke, always had a wave and a chat. That’s awful. He always used to complain about my cricket practice in the garden, but he did it with a smile. Said it reminded him of his youth. It’s just… it feels like everyone’s funerals are piling up lately. Old Mrs. Davies last month, and now Mr. Henderson. Makes you think, doesn’t it? It does. It’s grim. Speaking of grim, have you guys heard from Sarah lately? I haven’t seen her post anything on Facebook in ages. I messaged her a couple of days ago, just checking in. She’s… dealing with stuff. Apparently, her flatmate, Liam, just up and left. Vanished. No way! Leaving without a word? What a jerk. She sounded really upset when I spoke to her last week. Said she felt totally betrayed. He apparently owed a lot of money, and just… ran. That’s terrible. Poor Sarah. We need to do something for her. Maybe a movie night? Distraction is key. Although, what  is  good at the moment? Everything feels a bit heavy. I saw the new Wes Anderson film is out. Seems suitably quirky and escapist. Ooh, good shout. Wes Anderson always delivers. Although, honestly, I’m in the mood for something brainless. Like, aggressively brainless. You mean like… Bob the Builder? Don’t mock! Sometimes you just need “Can we fix it?” to soothe the soul. Seriously though, a silly action film would be good. I’m up for anything, as long as it doesn’t involve existential dread. Oh! And we should definitely get more prawn crackers. These are going fast. I’ll order another portion. Anyone fancy a dessert menu?

Honestly, remembering Auntie Mabel trying to navigate the self-checkout at Sainsbury’s was a highlight. She insisted on scanning  every  item three times. Said she didn’t trust the machine. Mabel was a character. Stubborn as a mule, that one. Reminded me of old Mr. Henderson next door, back in Wolverhampton. He’d argue with the postman if a letter was delivered five minutes late. Five minutes! It's funny, isn't it? How people cling to the old ways. Mum's still convinced everything's better done by hand. Tried to explain the Scan As You Go to her last week… she looked at me like I’d suggested she learn Mandarin. Oh, the Scan As You Go! Don't even get me started. It's supposed to be quicker, right? But half the time it doesn’t recognise something, or accuses you of stealing a pineapple. A pineapple? Good heavens. When I was a boy, you were lucky if you  saw  a pineapple! We mostly ate… well, sensible things. Potatoes, mostly. And my mother made a lovely rice pudding. Not these pre-packaged things you get now. Speaking of sensible, have you seen the price of rice lately? It’s gone up again. I swear, they’re going to price us all out of a decent risotto. It’s ridiculous. And don't even get me started on new builds and the insurance. We're still battling with the builders over everything at the new house. They say we have to have specific insurance for the underfloor heating because… well, because it’s new. Apparently it’s incredibly sensitive. Insurance! Back in my day, insurance was simple. Car insurance, house insurance… that was about it. Now you need insurance for your toaster, I wager. Virtually! I read an article about someone trying to insure their bicycle against accidental damage while learning to ride. Apparently, it was a genuine request. That  is  a new one. Though honestly, I’m starting to think we’ll need insurance against driverless cars. I saw a report about a test drive where it just… stopped. In the middle of a roundabout. Driverless cars? Nonsense. Absolute nonsense. People need to drive! Gets the blood flowing, keeps the mind sharp. Though, I suppose air travel’s safer these days. I always worried about flying, you know. All those metal birds… Statistically, yes, it’s incredibly safe.

Right, so, Dragon heads need  massive  jaws, don’t they? Yours is looking a little… polite, Leo. It’s supposed to be a friendly dragon. Not a scary one. Mine is going to breathe  fire ! I’m drawing sparkly bits, look! Ooh, very effective. Very fiery. Just try not to get glitter  everywhere , Elsie, please. Remember last time? It was in my hair for a week. Sorry, Mummy. But dragons  need  sparkles. It's Chinese New Year! Chinese New Year is about red envelopes with money in, isn’t it? It is, but it’s also about dragons and celebrating new beginnings. And delicious food! We’re having noodles tonight, you know, for long life. Can we have prawn crackers? Of course. And spring rolls. And maybe a little bit of that sweet and sour chicken you both like. Though not  too  much, we don't want sugar rushes before bedtime. I don’t really like sweet and sour chicken. Oh? What  do  you like best, Leo? Noodles. And… dumplings. And are we still doing drum lessons on Wednesday? Yes, drum lessons are still on. Though Mr. Davies said you were a little distracted last week. Something about planets? Uranus is really far away. And it’s blue. Teacher said so. And it has rings, but they're not as good as Saturn’s. I know Saturn! It has  lots  of rings! Like a princess’s crown! I’m learning a new song on the piano, it sounds like twinkling stars! That’s lovely, Elsie. You’re getting so good. It was really nice of Mrs. Henderson to say how much you've improved. She said I play with ‘expression’ now. What does that mean? It means you put feeling into it! You're not just hitting the notes, you're  telling a story  with the music. Like when you were pretending to be a ballerina when you were playing. I wish I could learn the drums faster. It’s hard to keep the rhythm. It takes practice, darling. It's like learning anything new. Remember how hard it was to learn to ride your bike? I fell over a lot. You did! But you kept trying, and now look at you, zooming around the park! Elsie, are you still excited about your aerial hoop class this weekend? YES! I’m going to be a fairy! And I’m going to learn a new trick!

Honestly, this Aperol Spritz is hitting the spot. Needed that after lugging our bags halfway across Rome to this AirBnB. Tell me about it! That little cobbled street was  not  designed for suitcases with wheels. Though, the AirBnB is gorgeous, isn’t it? That balcony…worth the struggle, I reckon. Absolutely. And the host left us Prosecco! Which, let’s be honest, has already been partially sampled. Though speaking of struggle, has anyone tried ordering a coffee yet? My Italian’s… rusty, to say the least. I just pointed and hoped for the best. You’re telling me! I walked into a place this morning, tried to ask for a flat white, and the barista looked at me like I’d grown another head. Had to mime a milky coffee, eventually. Apparently, flat whites are a mythical creature here. Haha, classic. I managed a ‘caffè latte’ reasonably well, but I’m pretty sure they overcharged me. My GCSE Italian is failing me spectacularly. Mine’s even worse. I spent a year in Spain, so I keep accidentally throwing in Spanish words. It’s a disaster. I asked for ‘agua’ instead of ‘acqua’ and got a very confused look. Oh, bless you. I’m just sticking to pointing. It's safer. So, dinner plans? I’m starving again already. Saw a tiny trattoria down that alleyway - looked proper authentic. That sounds good. I’m up for proper authentic. Anything but another pizza, as amazing as they are. Leo, you in? Yeah, sounds good to me. As long as they have wine. Actually, thinking about it, anyone know what the weather’s doing tomorrow? I was hoping for a bit of sunshine to wander around the Forum. I checked earlier. Apparently, it’s going to be scorcher. Mid-thirties. Perfect for gelato and avoiding all strenuous activity. Excellent. I'm packing a giant hat then. It’s a necessity. Speaking of packing, Mum keeps texting me asking if I’ve remembered my scarf. Honestly, it’s Rome in July! Mothers, eh? Always worrying. Mine’s convinced I’ll get pickpocketed if I so much as look at a souvenir shop. Mine's on a mission to find me a suitable Italian husband. Sent me a link to a dating app specifically for expats. Seriously. Oh, that’s brilliant! So, you’re on husband-hunting duty then? I thought you were happy being a free spirit, baking all those incredible cakes.

Honestly, the planning for Chloe’s hen do is  stressful . I feel like I'm her mum, not a friend! Oh, tell me about it! Whose bright idea was it to make friendship bracelets for everyone? My fingers are killing me. It was Sarah, wasn’t it? She seems to think everyone secretly wants to spend their weekend crafting. Classic Sarah! She's all about the ‘experiences’ but forgets that some of us just want a good night out. Have you actually got anywhere with booking the cocktail making class? I’ve emailed like, five different places. Either they’re fully booked or they want a ridiculous deposit. It’s a nightmare. And then Aunt Carol keeps sending me Pinterest boards labelled “Hen Do Inspiration” – mostly involving elaborate themed costumes. Oh no. Aunt Carol… the woman who suggested we all dress as princesses? Please don’t remind me. I’m still having flashbacks. Right, deposit situation. I called "Mixology Magic" last week. They had a cancellation for the Saturday afternoon, but it's £100 non-refundable deposit. I could potentially put it on my credit card and you guys can reimburse me? Oh, you'd do that? You’re a lifesaver, honestly. I’m already over budget after accidentally ordering glitter cannons. Glitter cannons?! You are brave. Chloe will  love  that. My flat, however, won't. Seriously, glitter gets  everywhere . I found some in my coffee last month, just from a birthday card. I figured it was worth it for the photos. Speaking of photos, Jess said she’s happy to be designated official photographer but she's worried about needing extra batteries. We could all chip in for a portable charger for her? And actually, I’ve been meaning to ask – is anyone good at baking? I was thinking of attempting a cake, but my last attempt resembled something closer to a brick. Oh gosh, baking isn't my strong suit. I once tried making macarons and they… disintegrated. I can do a reasonable victoria sponge, but nothing fancy. Maybe a sheet cake with some icing? That would be amazing! Even just a plain cake with some nice decorations would be perfect. I’m happy to grab the decorations if you’re up for baking. Maybe we could make it a little hen-themed? Perfect! And then we just need to finalize the guest list and confirm with the restaurant for Saturday night.

Right, so you reckon this much chilli is enough? Seems… ambitious. Ambitious is good, mate. It's a flavour bomb, innit? Besides, you were complaining about my last pasta sauce being a bit bland. Bland is a strong word. Subtly seasoned. And I was mostly just trying to be polite, knowing you spent like, an hour on it. But yeah, alright, lay on the heat. You alright though? You look a bit peaky. Just a bit tired, honestly. I think I'm fighting something off. Had a dodgy stomach all day. Probably something one of my students brought in from their travels. They're all coming back from their gap yahs now, full of exotic germs. Lovely. So you're basically a human petri dish. No wonder you're looking a bit green. You should have stayed in bed. Nah, needed to distract myself. Plus, I promised I’d cook tonight, and you’ve been working on that commission all week, you deserve a proper meal. How's the artwork going, by the way? It's… slow. The client is being incredibly picky. Keeps asking for ‘more texture’. Like, what  is  more texture? I’ve practically sculpted the thing. Honestly, I’m tempted to just send him a photo of sandpaper. Don’t do that! You’ll lose the commission. Just… nod and smile and add a bit more gesso. Speaking of picky, remember that hotel we stayed in in Barcelona? The one with the ‘view’ of a brick wall? Oh god, don’t remind me. That was a disaster. “City view,” they said. It was a view  of  the city’s backside. And the breakfast was just… sadness on a plate. Stale croissants and lukewarm coffee. And that weird, processed cheese that smelled faintly of feet. I swear. I think I survived on churros for the entire trip. You live for churros. This sauce is smelling pretty good though, even if it  is  likely to melt my face off. Are you sure about those peppers? Positive. Although, thinking about it, maybe I should've gone for slightly milder chillies... My throat feels a bit scratchy. Perhaps this sickness is just me preemptively reacting to my own cooking. You are a menace to your own digestive system. Maybe we should have a backup plan. Like, some yoghurt or something. Or a fire extinguisher. Good thinking. You grab the yoghurt from the fridge, I'll just… test the heat level.

Right, shopping list. We’re definitely out of milk, aren’t we? And I think we’re down to the last of the teabags. Yorkshire Tea, obviously. Though I saw some of that Earl Grey stuff on offer… Oh, don't you dare! Earl Grey is just… perfumed dust. Stick with Yorkshire. And did you remember to get stamps? I need to post Brenda’s birthday card. Stamps. Yes. Are you sure she’s 75? It feels like only yesterday we were stealing sweets from her mum’s shop. She’s definitely 75. She reminded  me  just yesterday! It’s funny the ages people put on the cards now, isn’t it? Used to be just a simple ‘Happy Birthday’, now it’s ‘Wonderful 75th!’ as if it’s a massive achievement just for getting there. Everything’s so… celebratory. And a lot more expensive. I was just looking at calendar fobs – those little ones you can hang from your bag – and they’re nearly ten pounds! For a tiny picture of a sunflower. Ten pounds! Goodness me. When we were little, calendars were things Mrs. Henderson made us do in art and craft. Remember? Awful, glue-covered things with bits of cotton wool stuck on them. And glitter. Always glitter. It got  everywhere . Do you remember those felt tip pens that smelled of fruit? I used to try and eat the green one. Honestly, you were a menace! Mrs. Davies used to threaten to call your mother every other day. It wasn’t just the pens, was it? It was the clay. You always managed to get clay in your hair. It was a good clay, though! Proper modelling clay. Speaking of school... I was thinking about old Mr. Peterson, the hockey teacher. He always made me wear those ridiculous hockey boots, even though they were three sizes too big. Said it was protection. More like torture. Oh, the boots! Designed by Satan himself, I think. Although, I always thought he favoured you. You were rather good at hockey, weren't you? I was hopeless. Utterly hopeless. Favoured? I think he just felt sorry for me. I was always the last one picked. Anyway, it made me think about what everyone did after school. What did you initially want to study at university? Oh, I was all set on History. Social History, specifically. I was fascinated by the lives of ordinary people.

Right, so Old Man Hemmings next door… he’s a character, isn’t he? Apparently, he’s been here since before the war, or so he claims. Keeps telling me stories about rationing and evacuees. Sounds delightful. Though I imagine after a bit, it gets a bit… repetitive? You know how some people are. Oh, absolutely. Old Hemmings is a fixture. Everyone knows him. He’s got a prize-winning marrow, apparently. Massive thing. He’s always showing it off. A marrow? Good Lord. I’m more concerned about his chickens. They’re wandering all over the lane! Nearly tripped over one yesterday carrying the groceries in. Oh dear! Have you spoken to him about it? Briefly. He just waved a hand and said, “They’ve got freedom, they do!” Honestly. Freedom to cause a hazard, more like. He’s hopeless. But harmless, I think. You’ll get used to him. This village is full of characters. That Mrs. Featherstone down the road collects gnomes. Hundreds of them. In her garden. It’s…a sight. Hundreds?! Oh, I need to see this. It sounds wonderfully eccentric. Is it a particularly… well-maintained garden otherwise? Or is it just a gnome explosion? More of an explosion. Though she does try. It’s just… overwhelmed. She’s very proud of them. It’s just everything is so  different  from Southend, isn't it? Used to the constant noise, the crowds. Here, it's…peaceful. Too peaceful sometimes. That’s what you wanted though, wasn’t it? A quieter life? I did, I did. It's just… adjusting. And trying to figure out where everything  is . Getting to the village shop feels like a major expedition. It does at first. You get your bearings. The lanes are confusing. You'll learn the shortcuts. And the shop, well, it's a lifeline. Old Mrs. Trellis runs it. She knows everyone's business. Sounds… cosy. Have you managed to start that little herb garden you were planning? I’ve made a start. Dug over a patch. It’s looking rather sad at the moment, to be honest. Mostly mud. The soil's heavier than I expected. You need to get some of Farmer Giles' compost. He delivers. It's fantastic stuff. Really rich. Giles, you say? I’ll look into that. I’m hopeless at this gardening business. Always was. Your mother, though – she had a proper green thumb.

Right, so I was proper scrolling through Amazon last night, yeah? Not even looking for anything specific, just…scrolling. You and Amazon. It’s a dangerous combination, Liam. You know you shouldn’t. I know, I know. But they just  know  what I want, don’t they? It’s creepy. Found these noise-cancelling headphones though, dead cheap. Like, seriously cheap. Cheap as in…likely to break after a week cheap? Nah, reviews were decent. Apparently good for gaming. I was thinking, maybe if I actually  started  applying for jobs, I could use ‘em for online interviews. You know, block out the sound of Mam yelling at the telly. Fair enough. You’d need some serious noise cancelling for that. She was going mental at  Gardeners’ World  last night. Shouting advice at Monty Don like he could actually hear her. It’s a skill, honestly. Still, £30 for headphones. It’s a bargain. Ordered ‘em anyway. You didn’t. Honestly, Liam. You're supposed to be saving for… well, for something. Anything! Look, it’s not like I’m spending a fortune. It’s practically an investment. In my future employability! Think about it. Professional headset, confident interview, job secured… chain reaction, innit? You’re good at that, you know. Justifying things. I’m still trying to understand why you need a gaming keyboard when you haven't touched a computer in a month. That was different! That was for… precision. You need precision for certain games. And sometimes I do use the computer. I’m watching YouTube, aren’t I? For three hours straight, yesterday, watching videos of blokes building Lego. It’s an art form! Seriously. And they’re really good at it. Anyway, what about you? Still stressing about those college applications? Yeah, a bit. I’m trying to decide between Lancaster and Newcastle. Lancaster’s closer, obviously. And cheaper to get to… but Newcastle has a better reputation for my course, I think. Lancaster’s good, though. Proper campus vibe. Loads of students, you’d make loads of mates. Yeah, but it feels a bit…isolated. Newcastle's a proper city. Proper nightlife. Nightlife is overrated. Trust me. It's mostly sticky floors and overpriced drinks. You're better off finding a decent Netflix series. Have you seen that new one, ‘Squid Game’? Everyone's talking about it. Oh yeah, I started it. Bit…intense, though.

Right, so the heating's still playing up, isn't it? I swear, this ancient system is going to be the death of me. I spent all morning fiddling with the thermostat again. Oh no, Dad. Still? Thought you’d cracked it last week with all that… well, whatever it was you did with the spanner. He  thinks  he cracked it. It’s a temporary stay of execution, more like. You need a proper engineer, honestly. It’s a miracle the house hasn’t spontaneously combusted. Now, now, don't exaggerate, Margaret. It’s perfectly safe. Just… temperamental. And expensive to get someone out here, that’s the problem. Speaking of expensive, what about lunch? I’m starving. Did you two bring anything, or am I on sandwich duty? I grabbed some pasties from the bakery in Holsworthy, thinking they might be good for a picnic if the weather holds up for your walk tomorrow. Oh, lovely! Pasties are perfect. And I’ve got some fruit, and a flask of tea. We can easily make do. So, about this coastal path… are you sticking to the stretch around Hartland Quay? That’s the plan. I’ve got the Ordnance Survey map spread out, planning the route. Thinking I can do about six miles, maybe seven, depending on how I’m feeling. It’s been ages since I’ve had a proper walk. Sounds good. Just be careful, will you? It can get pretty treacherous near the cliffs. Remember Auntie Brenda slipping on that muddy path last year? Oh, dear Brenda. She’s remarkably resilient, that woman. Still going strong at 88, can you believe it? She’s outliving everything, even the furniture! Speaking of which, you need a new sofa for here, don’t you? That one looks like it’s seen better decades. It  has  seen better decades! It came with the house, and I suspect it's older than I am. I was thinking of venturing into Okehampton next week. I saw a furniture shop there, looked reasonably priced. Okehampton’s good. We could come with you? Two extra pairs of eyes might help you avoid anything too… questionable. You have a tendency to fall for things just because they’re ‘a bargain.’ I do not! I am a discerning shopper. Though, I admit, I did get conned into buying a ‘vintage’ record player on eBay that didn’t work.

Right, that was a good lasagne. Seriously, you’ve outdone yourself. Oh, stop it! It's just a recipe I found online, really. Though, I did add a bit more garlic than it said. You know me. More garlic is  always  the answer. So, how was your day? Beyond the lasagne mastery, I mean. Ugh. Honestly? Exhausting. Parent’s evening. Three hours of slightly awkward small talk and trying to gently let parents know their darling child is… enthusiastic, but needs to focus. Sounds rough. I’ve always been slightly terrified of those. It feels like walking a tightrope. It is! Mrs. Henderson practically interrogated me about Timmy’s handwriting. Apparently, it’s ‘a creative interpretation of legible writing.’ I bit my tongue so hard, I nearly drew blood. Oh, bless her. They all have their battles. I had a student today who genuinely believed he’d solved climate change. He wanted to present his ‘solution’ to the UN. No way! What was his solution? Giant fans. He was convinced strategically placed giant fans could just blow all the pollution away. He’d even done a PowerPoint. It was… ambitious. Kids are the best. Speaking of ambitious, I’m starting to think this new project at work is going to be a disaster. They want me to overhaul the entire Year 6 assessment process in three months. Three months! That  is  ambitious. Sounds like a lot to take on. What’s the biggest issue? The sheer volume of it. And the fact that everyone has a different opinion on what ‘good’ assessment looks like. Old school teachers want back to traditional tests, the younger ones are all about continuous assessment and portfolios… it’s a minefield. Sounds like a classic change management nightmare. Have you spoken to Sarah about it? She’s pretty good at navigating that kind of stuff. I have, briefly. She suggested I ‘facilitate a collaborative discussion to reach a consensus.’ Which is code for ‘good luck herding cats.’ That’s Sarah in a nutshell. Look, I know you're stressed, but you’re brilliant at what you do. You’ll figure it out. Don’t let them heap everything on you at once. Prioritise, delegate where you can, and remember to breathe. Easy for you to say, Mr. ‘I spend my days pondering the mysteries of the human mind’! You don't have parents breathing down your neck about spelling tests.

Honestly, the price of everything is just… ridiculous now, isn’t it? Even cat food. Jasper’s demanding the salmon pate, the little tyrant. He knows a good life, that cat. Still, you’ve got to admit, he’s worth it. Keeps us on our toes. Speaking of demanding, your mother was on about needing new curtains again. Oh, no. Not the floral ones? Please tell me she’s moved on from the floral ones. Apparently, they’re “looking tired.” Tired! They were only up three years! And she wants me to get Derek – you know, her friend’s son – to do it. He charges a fortune. Derek? Oh, he’s a good decorator, alright. Bit pricey, yeah, but you get what you pay for. Properly preps the surfaces, he does. I’ve used him a couple of times myself. He did my hall, last year. Lovely job, but… definitely not a budget option. Though, to be fair, it  still  looks fantastic. See? Value for money. Reminds me of old man Hemmings, the carpenter. Charged an arm and a leg, but his work lasted a lifetime. Used proper dovetail joints, he did. None of this chipboard nonsense. It’s like everything’s disposable now, isn't it? Built to break. I was reading an article about planned obsolescence… Don't start, darling. I’ve had a long day on the ward. Let's talk about something cheerful. Like…remember when Dad tried to build that chicken coop? Oh, lord yes! That was a disaster. It looked like something out of a cartoon. All wonky and leaning. The chickens wouldn't go near it. He was convinced he could do it all himself, wasn’t he? Despite having zero carpentry skills. And Mum just stood there, trying not to laugh. He was a stubborn man, your father. Refused to ask for help. Said he could figure it out. Eventually, he had to admit defeat and call Mr. Peterson. Mr. Peterson, with the enormous moustache? I remember him vaguely. The very same. He fixed it in an afternoon, shaking his head and muttering about “amateur hour.” It was brilliant. Though Dad pretended to be insulted. Speaking of fixing things, I found something odd the other day. My right-hand man, Geoff, completely butchered a skirting board - couldn't get a straight line to save his life. Then I realised…he’s left-handed!

Honestly, Grandad, you wouldn’t  believe  the queues at the airport. Absolute chaos. Everyone trying to get away for half term, I think. Half term, eh? Back in my day, you were lucky to get a week off for your holidays. More likely a long weekend, if you were fortunate. We didn't all go gallivanting off to Spain and Greece like you youngsters do now. It’s a bit different now, isn’t it? Accessibility and all that. Though, honestly, the airport experience itself isn’t exactly relaxing. Security felt like an interrogation! Tell me about it! They practically strip-searched my toiletries bag. And then the flight was delayed by two hours. Two hours! I was fuming. I had plans, you know? Proper plans for exploring. Two hours? Pah. I remember a flight being cancelled altogether once, back in '68. Stranded in Amsterdam for three days. Had to sleep on a bench in the airport! Now  that’s  a holiday story. Though not a very comfortable one. Wow, that’s rough. Did you at least manage to see any of Amsterdam? A little bit. Managed to wander into a little cafe and get a decent coffee and a stroopwafel. They were newfangled things back then, you know. Quite the treat. But mostly, it was just… waiting. And trying to avoid pickpockets. See, that’s what worries me! I heard stories about Barcelona, especially around the tourist hotspots. People getting their phones snatched. I was clutching my bag for dear life. I did manage to try Paella though. Honestly, the best thing I ate the whole trip. Paella’s good. I had a surprisingly good Thai green curry in a tiny cafe near the beach. It was ridiculously cheap, too. Sometimes the best food is found in the most unexpected places. Aye, that's true. I remember when travelling meant proper adventure. No package holidays, no all-inclusive resorts. You just… went. Found a room somewhere, ate what was available, and made it up as you went along. Built character, it did. It sounds…intimidating. I do like knowing I’ve got a hotel booked and some things planned. Though, maybe I should be a bit more spontaneous. There's a balance to be struck, I think. Planning ensures you don't miss out on the big things, but leaving some room for improvisation is definitely worthwhile. You stumble across the best experiences that way.

Right, so I was thinking for the first year undergrads… we really need to hit them hard with the primary sources. They get so bogged down in secondary criticism, they forget to actually  read  the texts. I agree. It's a problem. I've noticed the same thing. Though, ‘hit them hard’ seems a little… aggressive, doesn’t it? Maybe ‘encourage engagement with’? It’s a stylistic choice. It’s meant to convey urgency! They need to understand that the interpretations  come  from the texts, not the other way around. I was thinking three core texts for the whole year. ‘Frankenstein’, ‘Jane Eyre’, and… maybe ‘Wuthering Heights’? ‘Wuthering Heights’ is solid. It’ll give them something to wrestle with. But aren't we doing Victorian lit in the second semester? Might be a bit of overlap. What about ‘The Picture of Dorian Gray’? It’s got the Gothic elements, the societal commentary… it fits the themes we’re pushing. Hmm. You’re right about the overlap with the Victorian stuff. ‘Dorian Gray’ is a good shout. Bit more accessible, too, which might be kinder to them initially. Okay, ‘Frankenstein’, ‘Jane Eyre’, ‘Dorian Gray’… I’m feeling that. How about the seminar structure? I was thinking group presentations, but… Group presentations can be a disaster. Honestly, you always get one person doing all the work, and the others just ride on their coat tails.
