Maybe individual close reading exercises? Short, focused essays based on passages we analyse in class? I like that. Keeps them accountable. It forces them to engage directly. We could give them a list of critical lenses to apply, you know - feminist, Marxist, post-colonial… just to give them a framework. Exactly. Introduce the theory  after  they’ve formed their own interpretations. Otherwise, they just regurgitate jargon. Speaking of frameworks, are you hungry? I was thinking of trying that new Sichuan place down the street tonight. The one everyone's raving about. Sichuan? Oh my god, yes. I've been craving spice. I’ve been living on congee and fruit for the last few days, trying to be ‘healthy’. It’s depressing. Congee is lovely, but yeah, a bit… beige. We deserve some ma po tofu and dan dan noodles. Plus, I think I need to de-stress. Marking those dissertations is turning my brain to mush. Tell me about it. I swear half of them didn’t even  read  the reading list.

Honestly, this coffee machine is driving me round the bend. It makes a lovely cup, when it  feels  like it, but half the time it just gurgles and spits and then refuses to cooperate. It’s possessed, I tell you. Possessed. Is it the descaling again? You mentioned it needed doing a couple of weeks ago. Descaling, cleaning, praying to the coffee gods… I’ve tried everything! It’s just… temperamental. Like someone we know. Oh, are we naming names now, Mary? Don’t even  start  with the naming names, Arthur. I’ve had a day. Quotes for the storage came back – absolutely extortionate! They want a fortune just to keep the furniture for a few months while we sort the house. Ouch. That’s rough. Did you get quotes from a lot of places? Maybe try a smaller, local company? I got five. Five! And they’re all roughly the same. Apparently, demand is huge since… well, you know. Everything going on. Everyone downsizing or moving. It’s the market, Mary. Simple as that. Supply and demand. Though, I do agree, it’s a bit of a daylight robbery. Speaking of robberies… did you see what Keir Starmer said yesterday? Honestly, I’m starting to think the Conservatives are the lesser of two evils at this point. Oh,  don’t  bring politics into it, Arthur. Please. I’ve spent the morning wrestling with a coffee machine and storage costs, I haven’t the energy for political despair. He’s just voicing an opinion, Mary. It’s allowed. Although, I must admit, Starmer’s been a bit… underwhelming, hasn't he? He lacks that spark, that… belief. Exactly! It’s all so… calculated. No passion. Remember Kinnock? Now  he  had fire in his belly. A bit naive maybe, but genuine. Genuine naivety… that’s the problem with idealism, isn’t it? You start with the best intentions, a vision of a better world, and then reality kicks in and…well, you end up with Starmer. It’s a tough one. It feels like everyone's lost faith in the system. No one trusts politicians. And frankly, can you blame them? It's not just politicians. It’s everything. The banks, the media… it's all rigged. Oh, don’t go down that rabbit hole, Arthur. We’ll be here all day. Honestly, I just want a nice cup of coffee, a reasonably priced storage unit, and a bit of peace and quiet.

Right, so we’ve established I’m calling you ‘Sparks’ for the week. It suits your chaotic energy. Chaotic? Rude! I’m perfectly organised… around baking. And you’re ‘Rhyme’ because you insist on dropping little lyrical bombs every five minutes. Oh god, don't encourage him. I’m sticking with calling Liam ‘London’ – it’s geographically appropriate and delightfully unoriginal. And you, Darcy? Just Darcy’s fine. No need for a nickname, honestly. Though ‘Aussie’ feels… predictable? I’m happy being Darcy. Predictable is good! Keeps things simple. Speaking of simple, did anyone actually manage to figure out why they call that little stream the Fleet? It’s barely a trickle these days. Ooh, good question. I read something about it being an ancient name, pre-Roman even, meaning like, “fast-flowing.” Which is hilarious considering its current state. It’s depressing, isn’t it? You see those canal boats chugging along, all idyllic, and then you remember half the rivers in London are basically glorified drains. Back home, we don’t really  do  canals like that. Mostly just huge rivers. Murray, Darling… names that actually sound… substantial. Substantial! Like a good sourdough. Speaking of which, Sparks, your baking smells amazing, even through the lingering scent of yesterday’s questionable Italian. Thanks! It’s just a focaccia. But I did use proper olive oil, so it  is  a step up from the last place. That restaurant had… interesting ideas about what constitutes ‘authentic’ Italian. Interesting being code for “violently incorrect,” I presume? I swear they put ketchup on the pasta.  Ketchup . The horror! You know, my Nan was really strict about kosher laws, even though we weren’t particularly religious. She’d have a fit if she knew what they were doing. No mixing of meat and dairy, right? Yep, that's the gist of it. It's… a whole thing. My cousin married a Jewish guy, and I learned a surprising amount about it. It’s fascinating. It's a lot of rules! Makes baking a challah braid seem intensely stressful. Although, I do love a good challah. Don't even get me started on food rules. Trying to cater for everyone at the café is a nightmare. Gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free… sometimes I just want to microwave everything and be done with it. Microwave everything?! Sparks would have a meltdown. You’re a  baker , you can’t just advocate for microwave meals!

Right, so I swiped right on this lad on Tinder, yeah? Proper fit, looked like a model. Turns out his bio said he ‘enjoys long walks… to the fridge’. Honestly. No way! You're joking! That’s… brutally honest, innit? More lads should be like that, saves time. Honestly, Tinder is a minefield. I matched with someone who just sent me a picture of his feet.  Feet , I ask you. Oh. My. God. That's… disturbing. I’ve had a couple of weird opening lines, like, “Do you believe in love at first swipe?” It's just…cringey. I deleted Tinder after a week. It was just endless scrolling and disappointment. Plus, you always recognise someone from lectures. Makes it awkward. Tell me about it! I matched with Ben from my History seminar. He messaged me asking if I understood the Carolingian Renaissance. Like, seriously? We're on a dating app, not in a lecture hall. Ben? Oh, he's a bit of a… know-it-all, isn’t he? I avoid eye contact in seminars. Anyway, speaking of awkward, have you heard anything back from Liam about moving into the house next year? Not yet. I texted him yesterday, but he just left me on read. I’m starting to think he's going to bail and we'll be stuck with another year of Fiona's questionable cooking. Oh, please no. Fiona’s pasta bake is a weapon of mass destruction. And her ‘cleaning’ involves just moving things from one pile to another. Remember last month when she tried to fix the leaky tap with duct tape? It flooded the kitchen! Honestly, we need someone reliable to live with. Liam would be perfect, he's actually tidy. He just seems… indecisive. Maybe he found somewhere else? Or maybe he got a girlfriend. Remember Chloe from the library? He was proper chatting her up last week. She's alright, bit quiet though. Ooh, good point! That would explain the silence. I wonder if she knows about the state of the house. She'd probably run a mile. We need to up our housemate game. Like, seriously impress anyone who views it. Fairy lights, scented candles, strategically placed houseplants… the full works. And deep clean Fiona's room. That's a biohazard zone. Honestly, it looks like a bomb went off in there. Right, Operation Rescue-the-Housemate is a go.

Honestly, Doreen, this latest nonsense from the government… they’re talking about tightening up the benefit rules  again . As if it isn't hard enough already. Aye, I read something about that in the paper. Saying they want to get more people into work, don’t they? Like everyone’s just sitting at home  wanting  to claim, instead of trying to earn a living. It’s just rhetoric, isn’t it? Appealing to the voters who think everyone on benefits is a scrounger. It’s easy to say 'get a job’ when you’ve had a job your whole life. Difficult when there  are  no jobs, or when your health isn’t up to it. Precisely! I was a civil engineer, a perfectly good one, for forty years. Retired, fair enough. But now, if I wanted to… well, realistically, who’s going to hire a man of my age, even for consultancy? They want young blood, don’t they? And the pension barely covers everything. It’s the same with me. I was a builder, hands-on all my life. Knees are shot now, back gives me grief. Can't swing a hammer, let alone climb scaffolding. They don’t account for that, do they? Just assume you're fit as a fiddle and capable of anything. And the forms! Don't even get me started on the forms. I used to help some of the younger mums I minded with their benefit claims. Absolute nightmare. Endless paperwork, needing proof of everything. It’s deliberately designed to be confusing, I think. To put people off. It’s dehumanizing, that’s what it is. They treat you like you’re a number, a statistic. And then they wonder why people get depressed. It’s a vicious cycle. Speaking of depressing, did you see that new drama on ITV last night? ‘The Long Shadow’? About the Yorkshire Ripper. Gave me the shivers. Oh, yes! Awful. So well acted, though, wasn’t it? Dreadfully upsetting, of course, but important to remember. I remember at the time, it was terrifying. I agree. It was a brave piece of television. Though I do wish they’d stop making so much crime drama. There’s enough misery in the real world without having it pumped into our living rooms. Fair point. I’d rather watch something lighter. Have you seen that show with the antiques? ‘Bargain Hunt’ or something?

Right, honestly, that was… a day. I need a glass of wine. Did you have a good one, love? Not bad, not bad. A bit of a slog, actually. Mrs. Henderson was  particularly  resistant to the idea of a direct debit for her monthly donation. You’d think after twenty years, she’d just… let it happen. Oh, bless her. She's a character, isn't she? Still, you’re brilliant at winning people over. That's why they pay you the big bucks… well, relatively big bucks. How much did you manage to raise today, actually? Managed to get another £300 pledged for the new hospice wing. It adds up, you know? Every little helps. It's just… draining sometimes, constantly asking for money. Feels a bit grubby, if I'm honest. I can imagine. It's a good cause though, and you  do  make a difference. Anyway, enough about work. What did  you  do all day? Still battling the spreadsheet demons? Worse. I tried to fix the leak in the bathroom. Oh, no. Seriously? Is it still leaking? It’s… contained. For now. I think I may have made it slightly worse, actually. I tightened something, and now there’s a drip that wasn't there before. It's a rhythmic drip, ironically. Keeps time beautifully. A rhythmic drip? You are doomed. Honestly, leave plumbing to the professionals. You’ll end up flooding the whole house. I know, I know. It’s just… principle. I hate having to call someone out for something so silly. It feels like admitting defeat. Well, you've admitted defeat to a drip, haven’t you? It's not worth the stress. We can afford it. Remember what happened last time you tried ‘a quick fix’? The kitchen ceiling… Don’t remind me. Okay, okay, I’ll call someone tomorrow. Promise. Speaking of tomorrow, did you remember to remind Leo about the dentist? Oh, crikey no! I completely forgot. He’ll be furious with me. He’s been putting it off for months. He's a stubborn one, that boy. Just like his mother. You’d better message him now before he settles in for an evening of video games. You’re right. Teenagers. Honestly. What did you think of that new cooking show we watched last night? The one with the ridiculously enthusiastic Italian chef? It was… loud. Very loud. And his recipes looked incredibly complicated.

Honestly, this weather is just… relentless. Grey, grey, grey. I feel like I haven’t seen the sun properly in weeks. It’s not even  cold  cold, just damp. It seeps into your bones, you know? Tell me about it. Manchester was exactly the same when I left. Mum was going on about needing to get the heating on, even though it’s practically September. It’s depressing, isn’t it? Makes you want to hibernate. Exactly! And then I started feeling a bit… off yesterday. Just a scratchy throat and a bit achy. I’m trying to tell myself it’s just the damp, but realistically, it’s probably a bug. Oh no, not good. You’ve got to be careful. Especially with everything going around. Did you remember to pack your Lemsip? I did, thankfully. Though I’m not sure even Lemsip can combat Polish gloom. It’s funny, isn’t it? I’m supposed to be embracing this new life, learning the language, exploring… and yet I spend half my time wishing I was back in Cambridge, even with the Cambridge drizzle. I get that. It’s…disorienting, isn’t it? Moving somewhere new. It’s not like in the pictures, all romantic and exciting. Real life is…sorting out plumbing and trying to find decent tea. Exactly! And then my Auntie Margaret died. So, I have to go back. Oh, Sarah, I’m so sorry. I didn’t know. It was quick. She just…stopped. A heart thing. It’s a relief, in a way, she didn’t suffer. But the funeral… it’s going to be awful. And it just makes me feel so… rootless. Always going back, always leaving. I don’t really feel like I  belong  anywhere anymore. That’s rough. It sounds like you’re really struggling with that. I’m glad you're going back, though. You need to be with family. But I totally understand what you mean about feeling unmoored. I think that’s why I keep finding myself scrolling through old photos on Instagram. Seeing everyone I grew up with… it’s a strange comfort. Oh, I do that too! It’s awful, isn’t it? Just endlessly comparing your life to everyone else’s curated highlight reel. I saw Emily’s holiday snaps – Santorini, gorgeous hotel, perfect sunset… I was momentarily consumed with envy. Then I remembered she’s constantly complaining about her job.

Honestly, this tea is a lifesaver. I swear, copywriting is draining all the moisture from my soul. Tell me about it. Staring at a screen all day, trying to make “innovative synergy” sound… not completely awful. What are you working on at the moment anyway? Still the dog food campaign? Sadly, yes. Still dogs. Still trying to convince people their furry friends  need  gourmet kibble. I pitched a whole concept around dogs having tiny existential crises and needing superior nutrition to cope, and they said it was “too niche.” Oh my god, that’s brilliant! Too niche?! They’re dogs, they literally eat anything off the floor. Exactly! I know! Apparently, “emotional resonance” doesn’t sell biscuits. It’s infuriating. How’s the survey programming going? Any insight into the minds of the British public gleaned from endless multiple-choice questions? It’s…monotonous. Mostly just confirming everyone loves a good cup of tea and is vaguely worried about the price of petrol. Though, I did stumble across one fascinating response where someone claimed their spirit animal was a bin bag. A bin bag? Okay, that’s…specific. Maybe  that  should be a copywriting campaign. “Embrace your inner receptacle.” I’ll pitch it to your dog food clients. They’d probably love it. Seriously though, I’m starting to think I need to be more strategic about my part-time work. It’s paying the bills, obviously, but it's not exactly creatively stimulating. I feel you. I’m constantly battling the urge to just quit and open a little bakery. Imagine, no more “brand messaging,” just perfectly laminated pastries and the scent of cinnamon. Oh, don’t even. I’d be a regular. Though, honestly, I can barely boil an egg, let alone create a perfect pain au chocolat. I went to Borough Market yesterday, though. It was chaos, but the cheese…the cheese was a revelation. Borough Market is amazing, but you need to go early. I tried going on a Saturday afternoon once. It was shoulder-to-shoulder tourists and ridiculously overpriced olives. Oh, definitely. I went during the week. Managed to snag some incredible cheddar and a loaf of sourdough. Speaking of food, you need to come to that Ethiopian place with me next week. It's near King's Cross. Apparently, you eat with your hands. Ooh, yes! I’m in. Eating with your hands is inherently more satisfying.

Ugh, morning everyone. Did anyone else have a ridiculously early start this morning? I dreamt a dinosaur was tickling my feet. That's why I woke up. I woke up because Lily was talking in her sleep! She was saying something about sparkly unicorns. Sparkly unicorns, huh? Sounds about right. Well, I was jolted awake by the bin men at half six. Honestly, the racket! Right, plans for today. It's Saturday, which means… freedom! Sort of. Can we go to the park? Please? And can I take my scooter? Park is a definite. Scooter, yes, but helmets on, okay? We can aim to get there before it gets  too  busy. I was also thinking… remember I booked those circus skills workshop for this afternoon? CIRCUS SKILLS?! Really?! Will we get to juggle? Juggling, plate spinning, maybe even a bit of tightrope walking – well, a  low  tightrope, obviously! It's at the community centre, starts at two. Before that, though, we need to tackle breakfast. What are we having? Pancakes! With sprinkles! And bananas! And chocolate sauce! Okay, okay, we'll aim for a balanced pancake situation. Sprinkles are definitely happening. Oh! I was talking to Auntie Carol on the phone yesterday. She’s been travelling in Australia. She said something really weird. What? She told me to “chuck a U-ey” when I got lost. Apparently, it means to do a U-turn! Isn’t that bizarre? Chuck a what-ey? It means turn around! It’s just an Australian thing, apparently. She’s picked up all sorts of strange phrases. Australians are funny. They certainly are. Right, pancakes. Then park. Then circus skills. And… oh! I almost forgot. Remember Neon Moon said they're doing a little pop-up event at the farm shop tonight? Live music and stuff? Can we go? It’s late though… It starts fairly early, like seven. We could go after dinner, just for a little while. We'd have to be quick, getting you both to bed. What do you think? Yes! Neon Moon is really cool! If I can have ice cream. We'll see about the ice cream. First, pancakes. Come on, let’s get cooking before these two little circus performers demand more sprinkles! I hope this meets your requirements! Let me know if you'd like any adjustments or further conversation. Is there anything else I can help you with?

Honestly, the state of things… it’s just exhausting, isn’t it? All this back and forth. You’d think after all this time they’d have  something  concrete to offer, instead of just… noise. Exhausting is a polite word for it, Carys. It's a performance, that's all it is. A carefully choreographed performance designed to keep people arguing amongst themselves instead of looking at  who  is really benefiting. It feels so performative, yeah. Like they  want  us to be angry at each other. My lecturer was saying in our politics module that it’s classic divide and conquer. Keeps the focus off their own… questionable decisions. Exactly! And the rhetoric! It’s become so polarized. You’re either ‘with’ them or ‘against’ them. There’s no room for nuance anymore. Remember when debates actually  were  debates? Now it’s just shouting matches. Oh, I remember. Back in the days of Kinnock, there was genuine…robustness. Disagreement, certainly, but a respect for the opposing view. Now? It's just… personal. And frankly, lacking in any real substance. It’s all soundbites and slogans. My Nan always says politics used to be about local issues, you know? Proper stuff that affected people’s lives directly. Now it’s all this global stuff and… I don’t know, it feels distant. Like they’re talking  at  us, not  to  us. Your Nan’s right, you know. My grandfather, he was a councillor in Lambeth for years. Completely different world. It was all about pot holes and libraries and making sure the bins were collected. Grounded, practical stuff. He said the biggest complaint he ever got was about a particularly unruly rose bush blocking the pavement. A rose bush! That’s brilliant. My father, now  he  was a firebrand. Involved in all sorts of… demonstrations. Always challenging the authority. He’d be apoplectic if he were alive today. He’d see right through this charade. He came from a mining family, you see. Nantyglo, actually. Right where we're headed. Nana's side was also mining. Abertyswyth. Apparently, Great-Grandad Thomas was a bit of a union man. Always getting into trouble for sticking up for the other miners. Mum's told me stories. Said he'd bring home black eyes and bruises, but he was a legend among them. It’s funny isn’t it, how strongly those roots run. That sense of collective struggle.

Right, so the brave knight, Sir Reginald, he rode his slightly wobbly horse… what was his horse’s name again? Sparkles! Yes, Sparkles, he rode Sparkles towards the… the Grumble Mountain! But it wasn’t actually a mountain of grumbling, it was a mountain made of… Broccoli! A mountain of broccoli! Yes! A very large, very green mountain of broccoli. And guarding the broccoli was… A dragon! But a friendly dragon! A friendly dragon, exactly! Though he  did  have rather bad breath. It smelled of… Old socks! Old socks and… and cheese! A very powerful combination. And Sir Reginald needed to get to the top of the broccoli mountain to… Rescue the princess! Rescue the princess! Princess Penelope, who was very good at building Lego. But the dragon wouldn’t just let him pass. He said… “You must tell me a story! A  really  good story!” Tell him about Helen Moss! Oh! That’s a good idea! Should we tell the dragon about Helen Moss? You know, the author who writes all those adventure stories? She wrote about the explorers! And the lost city! She did! She wrote about the explorers finding the lost city of… what was it called? Er… Zargoth? Zargoth! That's right! And it was full of secret passages and amazing treasures. Do you think the dragon would like that story? Yes! He’d like the treasures! Especially if they were shiny! Definitely shiny. Maybe Sir Reginald could tell the dragon about all the shiny things in Zargoth, and then the dragon would let him pass to rescue Princess Penelope. How does that sound? Good! Then he can fight the broccoli with a sword! He can certainly  attempt  to fight the broccoli with a sword. It’s a very tough vegetable, you know. Although… maybe he could just eat his way to the top? Ew! No! Alright, alright, no eating the broccoli mountain. We’ll stick with the sword. Speaking of stories, did you both see the flyer for the Linton Book Festival? It's next weekend. Book festival? Are there books? Lots and lots of books! And maybe even some authors who write stories like Helen Moss. We could go and see if we can meet one! Can we get new books? We can certainly look! Let's see what they have. But for now, let’s finish our story about Sir Reginald and the broccoli mountain.

Right, so I was reading this article, and they’re saying lab-grown meat, like, proper ‘shmeat’ as they call it, is getting  so  close to being commercially viable. Apparently, they’ve managed to get the texture really good now. Oh, really? I’ve been a bit dubious, honestly. It just… feels weird, doesn’t it? Like, meat without the animal, but still  made  of animal cells? It’s a bit unsettling. I think it’s brilliant. Seriously. If it means we can drastically reduce the number of animals being farmed, I’m all for it. I mean, the conditions they keep them in… it’s horrific. I was watching a documentary last night about factory farming, and I honestly couldn’t eat my dinner afterwards. It  is  awful. I’ve been trying to cut down on meat for ages, but I love a good roast dinner. That’s where I always fail. Switching to fully vegetarian feels… restrictive, somehow. I get that. It’s a cultural thing as well, isn't it? My nan would be absolutely horrified if I told her I’d gone veggie. She thinks a proper meal  has  to have a bit of meat on the plate. Though even she admitted the sausages nowadays don’t taste like they used to. Yeah, ‘cause they’re mostly filler! That's the problem. Animals deserve better than to be turned into… pink sludge. Honestly, I don’t even understand how people can compartmentalise it. Like, you pet a dog, you love a dog, but you happily eat a pig? It's mental. It’s the disconnect, I think. We don’t see where our food comes from. It’s all neatly packaged in plastic. Though, to be fair, hunting your own food isn't exactly ethical either, is it? It’s still taking a life. True. It feels… more personal though, somehow. Like, you're acknowledging the sacrifice. Abattoirs… that’s just industrialised cruelty. And the environmental impact of animal agriculture is insane, isn't it? All the methane… Massive. It's a huge contributor to climate change. And don’t even get me started on the land clearing to grow feed for livestock. It's madness. So, shmeat, failing that, good quality vegetarian options – that’s the way forward. Are you taking your vitamin D tablets, by the way, Liv? You were looking a bit peaky yesterday.

Honestly, this washing machine is driving me round the bend. It sounds like a jet engine taking off every time it spins. It’s getting on a bit, isn't it? We’ve had it… what, ten years now? Probably time to start thinking about a replacement, love. You said that last year, Dad. And the year before. It’s still churning out clean clothes, albeit with a dramatic soundtrack. It's not just the noise, it’s the vibrations! I swear the whole house shakes. And it’s left the kitchen floor soaking again. Honestly, I feel like I'm constantly mopping. Right, I'll have a look at the levelling feet tomorrow. Might just need adjusting. Though I suspect it’s beyond salvation. Remember Auntie Brenda’s washing machine? That thing smelled of mildew for five years after a single sock got stuck behind the drum. Oh god, don’t remind me. The whole house reeked whenever you visited. Mum, you were brilliant at strategically placing scented candles. I was! It was a full-time job masking that smell. Speaking of smells, are you two peckish? I’m thinking of getting the casserole on. Sounds lovely. I’ve got a glass of that Merlot chilling, should go perfectly. Did you see that new baking show on Channel 4 last night? The one with the ridiculously complicated cakes? Oh, ‘Extreme Baking’? It was bonkers! That woman built a functioning carousel out of gingerbread. It was both terrifying and impressive. I missed it. Was watching ‘Call the Midwife’ again. Comfort viewing, you know? All those lovely babies and heartwarming stories. Though sometimes it reminds me too much of the ward… Don’t dwell, love. You do a fantastic job. Though, you know, your sister called earlier. Apparently, she’s decided to learn Italian. Auntie Carol? Italian? That’s… unexpected. I know! She can barely manage a polite ‘bonjour’ on our holidays to France. Says it’s for ‘cultural enrichment’. I suspect it’s because she’s met a rather dashing Italian man online. Oh really? Now that’s a story. She never did get over Geoffrey, did she? No, definitely not. She still talks about his stamp collection. Speaking of Geoffrey, remember when he tried to fix the internet and accidentally deleted the entire family photo album? Oh, don’t even! I was furious. Years of memories,  poof , gone. Thankfully, Dad backed everything up.

Honestly, the things they send me at work… I had a meeting this morning solely to discuss whether we should be using butterfly forks for the gala dinner. Butterfly forks! Butterfly forks? What  are  butterfly forks? Is that like, tiny ones? No! They’re… decorative. The tines are shaped like butterfly wings. Apparently, they’re ‘more elegant.’ I nearly choked on my coffee. Elegant? It's a buffet, people will be piling their plates high with sausage rolls! Sounds a bit… fussy, doesn’t it? I’d just use a normal fork. Exactly! I pointed that out, of course. But apparently, aesthetics are very important to Brenda in marketing. Brenda sounds… intense. Oh, you have  no  idea. Anyway, it got me thinking about Remembrance Day. Two minutes silence. That's proper respect, isn't it? Not fiddling about with butterfly forks. Yeah, definitely. We had it at school today. It’s always a bit weird, though, isn't it? Everyone just…stops. It is. Bit spooky. Mr. Harris always tells this really long story before though, about his grandad. It’s sad, but good. They do a good job at your school. It’s important to remember. It feels…distant, somehow. Like it happened ages ago, but it really didn’t. It's like with Russia, isn't it? What's happening there feels like something from a history book, but it's  now . It is. Truly frightening. And it’s so difficult to know what’s real and what’s propaganda. We were talking about it in history. It's really confusing. Our teacher said... I can’t remember exactly, something about misinformation. That’s a good way to put it. Misinformation. It's everywhere. Hey, is it nearly my birthday? I’m trying to work it out. You  always  start thinking about your birthday about three months early. It’s the 17th of December, darling. Still a while to go. He wants the new Lego Star Wars set. The really big one. Oh, really? That's… ambitious. It’s not  that  ambitious. It’s only… … £600. £600?! For Lego? Right. Clearly, we need to revisit the whole concept of birthdays. Maybe butterfly forks are a more reasonable expense. Hey! Don't joke about the forks. Sorry, sorry. But seriously, we'll talk about presents closer to the time. Now, finish your supper. It's getting cold. Okay, but just saying...

Right, so, Cornwall is officially on the cards then? Everyone happy with that? Cornwall! Yay! Can we go to the beach  every  day? And build a massive sandcastle? And can I bring Rex? Rex, the dinosaur? Absolutely, buddy. He'd love Cornwall, I’m sure. Though he might scare the seagulls. As for beach time, we’ll  try  for every day, sweetheart. Though Mummy has to do a bit of exam marking, remember? Oh. Right. Exams. Boring. Not boring for the children who need to pass them! Anyway, Cornwall. I was looking at a little cottage near Porthleven. It’s not right  on  the beach, but it's a short walk. And it has a garden! A garden for Rex to explore! Will there be mud? Probably. Definitely. Cornish mud is the best kind. Have you two been reading your ‘Adventure Island’ books? YES! We’re on book four! Flora’s really brave, isn’t she? She climbed all the way up the scary cliff! And sailed the boat all by herself! It was awesome. It is a brilliant series, isn’t it? Makes me wish I was off on an adventure rather than marking Year Six SPaG tests. Speaking of adventures, remember last year when we went to that V&A exhibition? The one about pirates? Ooh, yes! With the real treasure chest! And the maps! And the scary pirate ship! It was so big. Exactly. Cornwall has a bit of a pirate history too, you know. We could visit some old smuggler’s caves. Cool! Can we look for treasure? We can certainly  look  for treasure. Although, I wouldn’t put too much hope in finding any gold doubloons. Right, logistics. I was thinking we go next Saturday? That gives me a week to finish marking these dreadful tests. Can we take the picnic blanket? Of course. And the buckets and spades. And Rex. And… oh dear. I’ve completely forgotten about Grandma’s dietary requirements. She’s still having trouble with… everything, isn’t she? She doesn't like gluten or dairy or… anything tasty? It’s a bit more complex than that, darling. We need to be really careful about what we pack for snacks. And when we go to a restaurant. Last time, she spent the whole holiday feeling poorly. Can we make her a special cake? A gluten-free, dairy-free, everything-free cake? That’s a lovely thought, sweetheart.

Honestly, Mr. Davies is  out  to get me. I swear. What’d he do this time? Don’t tell me it was the phone again? Worse. He said I was “disruptive” during the lesson. Disruptive! I asked a question, a legitimate question about the causes of the First World War, and he called  me  disruptive. Seriously? He’s always picking on someone. Remember when he gave Ben a detention for… breathing too loudly? Yeah! That was ridiculous. I think he just likes the power trip. Honestly, I’m starting to think about emailing the head of year. Woah, hold on, that’s serious. You sure? It might make things worse. I dunno. It's just infuriating. And it's affecting my coursework. I can't concentrate properly in that class when I'm worrying about getting pulled up for existing. Speaking of coursework, have you even  started  the English essay? Uh… loosely. I’ve got a mind map. It's very vibrant. Mostly just arrows pointing at “Shakespeare” and “misery.” Brilliant. That’s… helpful. I’ve already written the intro and a bit of the first argument. It’s about Lady Macbeth, obviously. She’s a proper villain. I’m going for Othello. Seems easier to pull apart. Less… scheming. True. Hey, did you hear about Liam’s party next weekend? Yeah! Massive one, right? Apparently he’s hired a DJ. Should be good. Hopefully. Last time he threw a party it ended with Mrs. Henderson calling all our parents. Remember? Because someone let loose a ferret in the kitchen? Don’t remind me. My mum lectured me for a week about responsible party behaviour, even though I wasn't even  there . Classic. Are you riding your bike to the cinema on Friday? They’re showing the new Marvel film. I was planning to. But my back brake is a bit dodgy. I need to get it fixed. Plus, knowing my luck, it'll rain. I hate cycling in the rain. We could both go on my bike. It’s got pretty good mudguards. Though you’d have to sit on the crossbar… Actually, no, bad idea. You're too tall. Definitely a bad idea. My knees would be in my face. Oh, and speaking of allergies, don't let Sam near the snacks at Liam’s. He touched some peanuts last week and nearly ended up in hospital. Right, noted.

Honestly, this road is dreadful. I didn’t realise quite  how  bumpy it was going to be. Every time I come down here I forget. It’s… agricultural, isn’t it? They really haven't invested in the infrastructure around here. Potholes the size of small craters. More suited to a tractor than a… well, than anything, really. Exactly! I’m half expecting to see a combine harvester coming the other way. It’s a miracle the suspension on this car still works. You’d think, being so close to… well, everything, really, they’d prioritise it. They probably don’t get much council tax revenue out here. Not many big houses, is there? Mostly farms and fields. Speaking of which, have you seen the cricket scores? England are getting properly thrashed. Ugh, don’t even. I tried to catch a bit on the radio earlier but I switched off. It was too depressing. They seem to be falling apart again. What’s the score now? About 80 for 6. It’s not pretty. Root’s out, Stokes is struggling… it's looking like a quick finish. Oh, brilliant. Another Saturday ruined. I was hoping for a good match. It's always more entertaining when it's close. Honestly, I'm starting to think I should just stick to watching cycling. At least it doesn’t rely on eleven people all having a good day at the same time. You and your bikes. Still obsessed, are you? Always. It’s just… pure effort, you know? It’s down to you. No relying on anyone else. Plus, the scenery’s usually a bit better than a cricket ground in Manchester. Fair enough. Although, you’re used to those nice, flat cycle paths around Harpenden. Try cycling up the hills around here. It’s a whole different ball game. I’m aware. That’s why I generally avoid coming this far west with the bike. Although… I did consider bringing it this weekend. Thought maybe a little off-road adventure. Oh, don't you dare. These roads are bad enough in a car. On a bike you'd be rattled to pieces. And the farmers won’t be pleased if you’re bouncing across their fields. Noted. Perhaps I'll stick to walking. Or just watching cycling on the telly. Safer option all round, I think. This road is making me reconsider my entire life choices, honestly.

Right, okay. Anyone got strong opinions on which Chinese we’re going for? I’m feeling indecisive. Honestly? Not particularly. Happy with whatever. Though, last time we had Golden Wok, the chow mein was a bit… sad. Like, all noodles, no flavour. Oh, God, yes! It was offensively bland. I think I spent the entire evening adding soy sauce. I vote against Golden Wok. Noted. No Golden Wok. Okay, what about Dragon Palace? They do that salt and chilli chicken that's ridiculously good. Dragon Palace is decent. A bit pricey, though. Remember when I tried to order a massive spread for my birthday and they told me they couldn't handle the order? Said it would throw their kitchen into chaos. Oh my god, I'd forgotten about that! You just wanted  all  the things. I wanted a feast! A glorious, greasy feast! They treated me like I was trying to bankrupt them. Okay, okay, Dragon Palace is on the maybe list. How about New City? They’re usually pretty quick. New City is… reliable. A little bit greasy, but reliably tasty. And they always throw in extra prawn crackers, which is a win. Prawn crackers are vital. It’s not a Chinese takeaway without a mountain of prawn crackers. Right, I'm thinking New City then? Unless anyone’s got a compelling argument for something else? Actually, wait. There's that new place, Lucky Star, that opened up on Friday. I saw a picture of their Peking Duck online, and it looked incredible. Oh! I hadn't heard about that one. Peking duck  is  tempting… but new places are always a gamble, aren't they? Could be amazing, could be disastrous. True. Remember that Italian place that opened up near the market? Promised authentic Neapolitan pizza and it tasted like cardboard. A painful memory. Okay, maybe we play it safe with New City. Unless… anyone feeling adventurous? I'm willing to risk it for the Peking duck. Hmm. Okay, you know what? Let’s be bold. Lucky Star it is! But if it's terrible, you’re buying the next takeaway, deal? Deal! Honestly, I'm willing to take that risk. I've been craving good Peking duck all week. Right. I'm in. But I'm calling dibs on most of the prawn crackers, regardless of where they come from. Fair enough. Okay, I’ll go on Just Eat and see what the delivery time is looking like.

…and honestly, the paperwork alone is enough to send you round the bend. They’re asking us to justify  everything  now, even why we’re teaching Keats. It's like they think students just wander in craving sonnets for the sheer joy of it. Sounds about right, doesn’t it? Everything's a metric, everything's an audit. It’s the same in the NHS, you wouldn't believe. They want data on  everything  – how long you spend with each patient, the colour of their socks, probably. The socks bit sounds about right, actually. It’s the constant demonstrating of ‘value’ that gets me. Like we’re all just churning out widgets. You dealing with a lot of pressure at the hospital then? Oh, you have no idea. It’s relentless. Staff shortages are getting worse, the waiting lists are… well, don’t even get me started. I had a woman in yesterday, been waiting six months for a knee replacement, practically in tears. You try explaining to someone that it’s not  personal , it's systemic. It's awful. Reminds me a bit of what they’re trying to do with education – squeeze every last drop out of everyone, with no thought for the actual human being involved. I’ve been reading about the Finnish system, actually. They seem to have a much more… holistic approach. Finland, eh? I've heard good things. Loads of outdoor learning, smaller class sizes… wouldn't that be the dream? Though I imagine getting the NHS to adopt their model would be like pulling teeth. It would be. I was over there a few years ago, visiting a friend. They really value teachers, you know? It’s a respected profession. Here, it feels like we’re constantly being undermined. It’s the same with nursing. Everyone appreciates what we  do , but no one wants to pay for it, or actually acknowledge the toll it takes. Speaking of tolls… have you had any trouble with Old Man Hemmings lately? Oh, Hemmings. Don't even… He was at it again this morning, complaining about my recycling bin being “half an inch” over the line. Honestly, he’s a menace. He spends all day looking out the window, judging everyone. Poor Mrs. Davies next door practically lives in fear of him. Apparently, he reported her for having a slightly overgrown rose bush. A rose bush! Seriously? The man needs a hobby.

Right mess, isn’t it? This weather. Proper biblical. Been like it all week. Aye, biblical is right. Reminds me of ‘63, the winter of ‘63. Couldnae get out for weeks. Everything frozen solid. Had to chop ice off the windows just to see daylight. Blimey. I remember reading about that. I wasn’t about then, of course. Lived in Germany ‘til I was about ten. They get snow, but not usually like that. More…organised, you know? Less chaos. Organised snow? Now there’s a thing. Sounds a bit German, that does. Everything in its place. You hear about them trying to get all these folk in now, though. From all over. Aye, it’s… complicated, isn't it? I was reading a report the other day, at the uni, about the rhetoric around immigration. A lot of it, frankly, is nonsense. Or at best, massively oversimplified. Nonsense, you say? I saw young Kevin down the shops, getting a telling-off from PC Davies just last week. Apparently, he was having a go at a lad who looked foreign. Said he was ‘taking our jobs’. That’s…unfortunate. Kevin's a bit of a lad, though, isn't he? Always something. But honestly, the ‘taking our jobs’ thing… statistically, it barely holds up. They generally fill positions that people  aren’t  wanting to do. Or create their own. Aye, well, easy for you to say. You’re a lecturer. Secure job. Not many of those around anymore. My Arthur, God rest his soul, worked down the docks all his life. Hard graft, that was. Lost his job when they closed it down, you know. Thatcher’s doing. I know, I know. It was brutal. My wife’s father was a shipbuilder. Same story. But even before that…the decline was coming. Things change. It’s just… how we manage that change is the important thing. Welfare's stretched so thin though. It's… it’s a worry. Welfare. Hah! When I were a lad, welfare meant your neighbours helping you out. A cup of sugar, a bit of coal. Now it’s forms and meetings and patronizing social workers. There's some truth in that. It’s lost some of its…community spirit. Though, there are some good people working in social care, you know? Properly dedicated. Dedicated, are they? I saw one driving a fancy car the other day. Belongs to  them , does it?

Right, so I genuinely spent half of yesterday evening trying to explain to my mam what a corpus actually  is . She thinks I just… file things. Like a really fancy filing cabinet. Oh god, the parents. Mine still thinks I’m translating Shakespeare. I mean, it’s technically language, but it’s not quite the First Folio, is it? Mine just nods and says “Sounds… important, love.” Which is helpful. Honestly, I think she thinks I work at a library. It's the same with me. My mom envisions me surrounded by books, dispensing wisdom. The reality is a lot more spreadsheets and statistical analysis. Though I  do  love the books part, admittedly. Tell me about it. My dad keeps asking when I’m going to “write a proper novel.” Like, publishing isn't writing?! He thinks I just…proofread things. And even when I try to explain editorial, it just goes over his head. It’s the vocabulary, isn’t it? “Corpus linguistics” sounds like something out of sci-fi. “Annotation schemes”... it’s a minefield. She asked if I had to wear gloves. Gloves?! Oh, that’s brilliant. My mum asked if I got free books. Which... sometimes, yes, but that's not the point! It’s the intellectual challenge, the… the insights into language! Though free books  are  a perk, let’s be honest. I’ve snagged some good ones through the department. It justifies the explanations to my nan, at least. "It's research, Nan. I need the source material." The perks are good. But I find myself explaining data privacy regulations more than the actual research these days. You realize how little people understand about how their information is used online? It’s a bit terrifying. Oh, definitely. My little brother asked me if I could ‘hack’ his ex-girlfriend’s phone to see what she was saying about him. I nearly choked on my tea. "No, Liam! Absolutely not! That’s…illegal and deeply problematic!" Oh, Liam. Sounds about right. Speaking of problematic, anyone see that article about the AI writing poetry? It was... unsettlingly good. I saw! It's impressive, technically. But it’s missing  something , isn’t it? That… spark. That human messiness. It’s like it understands the  form  of poetry, but not the  feeling . It’s grammatically perfect but emotionally flat. Exactly. It highlights the thing that makes human language so fascinating – it’s not just about the rules.

…and honestly, the sheer volume of content is just overwhelming. It’s not like when we were kids, flicking through four channels and being grateful for whatever was on. Tell me about it. I spent half an hour last night scrolling through Netflix, ended up re-watching an episode of  Taskmaster . Pure escapism, you know? Though, it does make me wonder if all this choice actually  reduces  enjoyment. Paradox of choice and all that. Exactly! You spend more time deciding what to watch than actually watching. It’s ridiculous. My parents, they’re still perfectly happy with terrestrial TV. “It’s free!” they say, as if that’s the only metric that matters. Fair enough. My Nan’s the same. She’s just discovered YouTube tutorials on how to knit, though. Apparently, there’s a whole community. It’s brilliant. Makes you realise the internet isn't all doom and gloom. That  is  lovely. It's amazing how it connects people. Though, you do get those comment sections… sometimes I worry about the anonymity. I was reading about how different cultures approach online interaction – some are much more direct and confrontational than others. Oh, that’s fascinating. I came across something similar when I was doing some research on language learning apps. Apparently, some apps designed for learners are inadvertently reinforcing negative stereotypes because of the way they portray different cultures in their examples. Wow. That’s… concerning. It’s so easy to fall into those traps without even realising. Speaking of language learning, are you still doing the Japanese classes? I am, yeah. It's slow progress, admittedly. The kanji is brutal. Honestly, sometimes I feel like I’m back in primary school, struggling with the alphabet. You were saying you considered learning Mandarin? I did. Briefly. Then I remembered how terrible I was at tones in French and thought better of it. My brain just doesn’t seem wired for tonal languages. I'd probably end up accidentally ordering a live chicken instead of a cup of tea. That  would  be awkward. I'm thinking of trying to incorporate more teaching into my research next year. I really enjoyed the bit of lecturing I did during my Masters. It's a completely different skillset than research, isn't it? It absolutely is. It’s about distilling complex ideas down into something understandable, which is… challenging. I’ve observed a few lectures for my academic skills module.

Right then, love, can you get your granddad a brew? He’s been complaining about his knees since we left Hull. Alright, Gran. Black coffee, yeah? Like always? Aye, lad. Black as the ace of spades. And a biscuit if you’re offering. One of them ginger nuts, if you’ve got ‘em. Don’t encourage him, Arthur! He’ll eat all the biscuits before tea time. Honestly, you’d think he hadn’t had a decent meal in weeks, the way he goes on. Now, now, Elsie. A man needs his sustenance. Especially a man of my vintage. These knees don’t oil themselves, you know. Speaking of needing things oiled, I’ve been meaning to ask you, Arthur, if you could have a look at that wonky cupboard door in the kitchen? It’s driving me daft. Keeps catching, and I swear it’s going to fall off its hinges one of these days. A cupboard door, eh? That’s a job for a master craftsman, that is. Though my hands aren’t what they used to be. Still, I can have a look. Might need a bit of wood glue, and maybe a screwdriver. Do you have a decent screwdriver, lass? Not one of those flimsy things they sell nowadays. There’s a whole toolbox under the sink, Arthur. You’re welcome to rummage. Though I suspect your granddaughter’s probably ‘borrowed’ half the bits for some school project. It’s not borrowing if I’m going to put it back! I needed some screws for my physics project, and yours were the only ones strong enough. Physics, eh? Fancy that. All these modern gizmos. When your grandfather and I were young, we made do with a bit of string and a good imagination. Aye, and we were happy enough. Though I wouldn't mind a bit of one of them fancy tellys now. The one with all the channels. Elsie keeps watching them programmes about baking. Makes my teeth ache just looking at ‘em. She enjoys a good bake-off, Arthur. It’s harmless. Although, she did try to make a croquembouche last week. Nearly set the kitchen on fire. A croquembouche? What even  is  that? Sounds dangerous. It's French, darling. A tower of cream puffs. Disaster waiting to happen, if you ask me. Elsie's a good cook, but sometimes she gets a bit ambitious.

Oh, look at this one! Remember Sarah’s hen do? Honestly, the outfits… Oh god, the inflatable flamingoes. That was… a weekend. I think I still have sand in my shoes from Brighton. Did anyone actually manage to keep theirs intact for the whole time? I don’t think so. Mine popped within about five minutes. It was a disaster, but a hilarious disaster. Speaking of disasters, have you seen what Mark’s done with his kitchen? No! What’s he up to now? He was talking about tiling it himself, wasn’t he? Tiling it himself, yes. And apparently, he’s gone for a mosaic. A full mosaic. He sent me a photo – it looks like a toddler’s been let loose with a glue stick and a box of brightly coloured ceramics. No way! That sounds… ambitious. Bless him. He always does go a bit overboard. Remember when he tried to build that garden pond? And flooded the neighbour’s shed! Oh, that was brilliant. I felt terrible for Mrs. Davies, but it was so Mark. He’s just full of enthusiasm, and occasionally, a complete lack of practical skill. It’s endearing, though, isn’t it? He means well. It’s good to see him being creative, even if it does end in chaos. These photos are making me miss everyone though. Especially with us being so far away. I know. It feels like ages since we’ve had a proper catch-up with everyone back home. Remember that pub quiz we all did last summer? We absolutely smashed it. We did! I still maintain that our general knowledge round was unfairly brilliant. We’d spent the whole week prepping, hadn't we? Googling obscure facts about Victorian plumbing. Worth it! It’s just… it feels a bit surreal sometimes, being here. It’s amazing, don’t get me wrong, and I absolutely love living in China, but sometimes I just miss the familiarity of… everything. A proper Sunday roast, a walk in Norfolk… I completely get it. It's a big change. But look at it this way – we're having adventures! We’re seeing things and doing things that most people only dream of. And we're doing it  together . You're right, of course. And it's been incredible being able to travel around so easily. That train journey to Guilin was just breathtaking. Absolutely stunning.

Honestly, my feet are  killing  me. I swear those shoes were designed by someone who's never actually walked anywhere. Tell me about it! I think I’ve permanently ruined my blisters. Did you see Liam trying to dance? It was… a choice. Oh my god, Liam! He thinks he's John Travolta, but it’s more like a malfunctioning scarecrow. Did you see him nearly take out old Mrs. Henderson with a rogue arm swing? I did! I actually had to physically restrain myself from laughing. She gave him the  look . You know the one. Like she was debating reporting him to the university authorities. The one that says "I've seen things, young man"? Yeah, classic. Honestly, the whole night was a bit of a mess. I only had like, two sips of that weird blue drink Chloe was raving about. It tasted like melted gummy bears. Oh no, don’t even. I fell for that one too! Thought it’d be all sweet and fruity. It was just… artificial. I stayed on vodka lemon all night. Safer option. Definitely. Speaking of safer options… did you hear back from your aunt about getting a kitten? You were saying you wanted one. Yeah! She said if I can promise to actually look after it and not just leave it to my mum, she’ll consider it. Which basically means proving I'm responsible. It’s a whole interrogation process. Ugh, family. They just  love  testing you, don’t they? My nan keeps asking when I’m going to ‘settle down’ and find a nice boy. Like it’s something you can just… order online. Right? It’s so annoying. My mum’s been showing me pictures of her friend’s son. Apparently, he's a 'very eligible bachelor'. He works in accounting.  Accounting . Oh, the horror! No offense to accountants, but… that just doesn't scream exciting weekend plans. Remember Ben from our history class? He was actually kinda cute. Ben? The one who’s obsessed with football? I think he spent the entire lecture talking about the offside rule. Okay, fair point. Maybe not. It's just… everyone seems to be coupled up. It's like a competition to see who can find a boyfriend first. They're all posting loads online, aren’t they? Every picture is like, “Look at us, we’re so in love!” It’s exhausting.

Honestly, the peas are lovely tonight. They’ve a proper sweetness to them, haven't they? Not like those frozen ones that taste of nothing. They are good, aren’t they? Proper mushy peas. Makes a change. How was your call with your sister, Ma? About Gran coming up? Oh, the usual. She’s convinced Gran’s already packed seven suitcases. I told her, “Mary, Gran is 92, not embarking on a Himalayan expedition!” She’s worried about the journey. I said the train is perfectly comfortable, and we’ll meet her at Penrith, make a fuss, and get her settled. Penrith’s a bit of a trek from Hunsonby, isn’t it? Should we offer to pick her up from the station, Eileen? Save her a taxi fare. That's kind of you, Arthur, but she insists on the taxi. Says she likes 'having her own space’ after a long journey. Stubborn as a mule, that woman. Still, she’ll be delighted to see us all. She keeps asking about young Leo. He’s been obsessed with FIFA again all week. Honestly, you’d think he was preparing for the World Cup. He’s been shouting at the television relentlessly. FIFA, eh? Always a trial. Remember young Jamie next door? He was glued to it, barely came out of his room. Missed a whole summer playing that game. It's a bit addictive, I’ll grant you. Leo’s not  quite  that bad, thankfully. Though his commentary is… colourful. Apparently, I’m a "terrible defender" when I try to have a game with him. Oh, I can imagine! He takes it seriously, doesn’t he? It's always someone else’s fault when he loses. It’s the nature of the beast, isn’t it? No one wants to accept culpability these days. Always an excuse. Back in my day… though, I suppose I was a bit like that myself when playing cricket. Blamed the pitch, the sun, the umpire… anything but my own batting. You were always a bit of a charmer, Arthur, getting away with murder! Still, I think it's good he's got something he enjoys. Better than getting into mischief. True. Speaking of mischief, did you manage to fix that dodgy tap in the bathroom, Arthur? It’s been dripping for days. Almost. It needs a new washer. Ordered one online. Should be here tomorrow.

Right, well, that was a lovely spread, wasn’t it? Bit of a sugar rush now though. Definitely! Mum really outdid herself with the scones. Though I think I ate about three… maybe four. Don't judge. Four scones? That’s nothing. Your grandmother could put away a whole Victoria sponge on her own. Good woman, your grandmother. Speaking of putting things away, has anyone seen my glasses? I swear I had them on a minute ago. Check on top of the TV, love. You were watching that nature documentary earlier, weren’t you? You often leave them there. Oh, you're right! There they are. Falling asleep with the telly on again, I suppose. It's a terrible habit. You and Dad are both guilty of that. Honestly, I wake up to the news at 3 am sometimes. Well, it’s better than nothing to listen to, eh? All this talk about the bin strikes is depressing enough as it is. Honestly, this council! It's ridiculous. The whole city's starting to smell. And the seagulls are having a field day. Makes a walk around Brighton less appealing, doesn’t it? Less appealing than usual, you mean! They're always circling, those things. Honestly, they're like feathered bandits. I was thinking of going down to the pier tomorrow, if the weather holds up. Thinking of trying to get some sea air. Sea air’s good for you. Clears the head. Speaking of clear… I’m still trying to get my head around this new phone. Sarah tried to set up my Blackberry, but it’s all voice recognition and things. I just want to make a phone call! Oh, those things can be a nightmare. I had the same problem with my laptop last week. Kept freezing, so I ended up having to basically rebuild it. Took all day. Oh dear, that doesn't sound fun. I’m still using my old one, it's slow but it does the job. I don’t need all the fancy stuff. Speaking of jobs, how's everything with the patients, Carol? Still hectic? You have no idea. Understaffed as usual. It’s draining, but someone’s gotta do it. At least the weather's been… reasonably okay. Though it threatened rain all morning. It’s funny, isn't it? How people talk about water these days. Filtered, sparkling, alkaline… Back in my day, it just  was  water!

Honestly, this coffee is  lovely . They’ve really got it right here at The Tram. It's a world away from that instant stuff I was attempting back home. Did you check the football scores yet? Any hope for United? Just glanced, actually. Proper thrashing, unfortunately. Three-nil down at half time. I didn’t even bother looking after that. It’s just… demoralizing, isn’t it? Speaking of demoralizing, I’m having a proper homesick moment. It’s this grey weather, I think. It’s starting to feel very November-y even though it’s only October. Think it’s the SAD creeping in. Oh, darling, I know the feeling. It’s the light, isn’t it? Or lack of it. Cambridge gets it too, you know. Damp, grey, and endless. It's why I semi-retired to avoid it, and here I am, chasing the gloom across Europe! Did you hear back from that student, Anya? The one who was struggling with the conditional clauses? I did, yes. She’s…well, she’s completely overwhelmed with preparing for the FCE. She sent me a really long message last night, basically a panic attack in text form. I feel so awful. I try to be supportive, but I also feel responsible for her success, you know? Like, if she fails, it’s somehow  my  fault. Oh, bless her. And you. That’s the trouble with teaching, isn’t it? Especially when you actually care. Remember old Mr. Henderson, my history teacher? Utterly terrifying man, didn't give a fig if anyone passed or failed. It was rather refreshing, actually. Although, probably not conducive to good learning. Definitely not! I wish I could be more like that, but I just get so invested. It’s probably because I enjoy the subject so much. You wouldn't believe the things I’ve been trying to explain about reported speech. It’s like their brains just…short circuit. Speaking of things that short-circuit, I keep thinking about Gran and her attempts at farming when she moved to Norfolk. Oh, goodness, yes! The chickens! And the disastrous vegetable patch! She thought she could just  will  the tomatoes to grow. It was hilarious, looking back. Though she was incredibly frustrated at the time. She swore the slugs were personally attacking her. Exactly! And she insisted on getting a huge Labrador to ‘protect’ everything, which promptly trampled all over it.

Right, who wants more of this chilli? I made way too much, as usual. Honestly, I could feed the whole of Cambridge with it. Go on then, yeah. It’s proper good, this. Beats a Pot Noodle any day. Though, to be fair, most things beat a Pot Noodle, don't they? You and your Pot Noodles, Liam. You’re a man of simple pleasures. Thanks, Chloe. It  is  really good. Though, my stomach might hate me later. Spicy food and me aren’t the best of friends. Think of it as character building! So, how was work today, Amelia? Still battling the spreadsheets? You have  no  idea. The new production line is a disaster waiting to happen. Everything's delayed, components are missing, and my manager seems to think shouting at people will fix it. Honestly, it's like stepping back into secondary school. Sounds stressful. At least building sites aren't full of spreadsheets. Just bricks, mud, and the occasional dodgy foreman. Speaking of stressful, my boss decided  today  – two weeks before Christmas – is the perfect time to revamp the entire conference schedule for next year. Like, every single one. It’s going to be a long night. Ugh, bosses. They do seem to thrive on chaos, don't they? You should’ve said no, Chloe! I tried! He just gave me that look. You know the one. The "you’re lucky to have a job" look. Yeah, I know the look. My gaffer’s got that down to a fine art. Right, enough work talk. Let’s talk about something more fun. Liam, how’s the dating scene treating you? Any luck finding someone who doesn’t think wearing tracksuits to a pub is acceptable attire? Don’t even. I went on a date last night, and she spent the entire time talking about her ex. Like,  every  detail. And then tried to pay for me! I felt like saying, “Love, I can handle a pint, honestly.” Oh, that’s rough. You deserve better. Someone who can at least hold a conversation that isn't about their past relationships. Absolutely! What about you, Amelia? Still seeing that architect guy? The one with the questionable taste in jumpers? Thankfully, no. That was a short-lived disaster. Turns out his ‘artistic vision’ translated to expecting me to decorate his flat in shades of beige. Beige! I think I politely excused myself after he suggested I wear matching beige outfits.

Honestly, the layout of this square is just…odd. It feels like they tried to cram too much into too little space. All these paths crisscrossing. Yeah, it’s not terribly intuitive. Though I do like the lime trees, they smell amazing this time of year. Reminds me a bit of Devon, actually. Devon! God, haven't been back there in ages. My sister’s still down there, though. She was saying she had a group of Chinese guests staying with her, doing a walking tour. Apparently, one of them was  obsessed  with pandas. Pandas? Of course. Everyone loves pandas. They’re basically the ambassadors of China. I remember reading something about the incredibly strict breeding programmes they have to keep the population going. She said he kept asking if you could just…find one in the wild. Like they just wandered around the countryside. She had to explain about the bamboo forests and the whole conservation thing. It made me think, though, about how different the wildlife is over there. Bears, for instance. Proper, big bears. Yeah, vastly different. Though I’ve seen photos of bears in zoos, obviously. Bit sad, really. Apparently, the landscapes in some parts of China are incredible. Rugged mountains, vast plains... she was talking about Tibet, too. Tibet…that’s a whole other kettle of fish, isn't it? Politically, I mean. Anyway, she said these guests were obsessed with taking pictures of  everything . Even a kid catching a pigeon just now. Right. Gotta document the whole experience for WeChat. Everything goes on WeChat, doesn’t it? It’s like the Facebook of China, but ten times more pervasive. Apparently. Speaking of China, are you still getting requests to teach TEFL over there? I know you were looking into that a while back. A couple. Mostly through agencies. The money’s good, but…I’m still a little hesitant. You hear stories. And the death penalty and the drug laws…it's a bit unsettling. It’s definitely not a walk in the park. Remember old Martin from the department? He spent a year teaching in Shanghai. He said it was amazing, culturally, but the bureaucracy was a nightmare. And he said the food was…an experience. Too much salt, apparently. Salt’s a common complaint. I’d be worried about the supervision aspect, too. Trying to get feedback on my research remotely would be a pain.

Right, so if we take the A19, it’ll be… about an hour and forty-five, yeah? Depending on traffic ‘round the Tyne Tunnel, obviously. An hour and forty-five? Blimey. I was thinking more like an hour and a half if we stuck to the motorways. Aye, but the A1 is always chocka. Especially on a Friday. Remember that time we tried to go to York? Took us three hours to get past Leeds. Oh God, don’t remind me. That was… a learning experience. Still, I’m aiming for a reasonably civilised arrival. Mum will have my head if I turn up too late for Sunday lunch. She’s already side-eyeing my workload this week. Oh, she's always side-eyeing your workload. She thinks being a ‘Consultant Engineer’ means you spend your days doing sums in a shed, and then spend every evening at a gala dinner. Exactly! And if I dare to mention ‘site visits’ she just assumes I'm off gallivanting. Speaking of, did you get my email about the, uh, the data sets? For the corpus project? Aye, saw it this morning. Just hadn’t had a chance to properly look through ‘em. Been a bit hectic with Professor Davies wanting everything re-formatted five minutes before the deadline. You know how he is. All too well. He’s a lovely man, genuinely, but… relentlessly precise. Is everything alright though? You sounded a bit stressed on the phone yesterday. Just the usual work stuff, really. And Gran's been a bit poorly. Nothing major, just a bad chest. She’s being stubborn and refusing to go to the doctor, naturally. Thinks doctors are ‘all quacks’. Oh, bugger. Gran’s a force of nature, but she really does need to listen to people sometimes. Should we… pop round and see her on the way back from your Mum's on Monday? That'd be lovely, actually. She’d appreciate that. She always said you were the only one who could make sense of her telly when it packed in. It was a single cable, Gran! A very obvious single cable. But she insisted it was some kind of sophisticated electromagnetic malfunction. That's her alright. Right, so, A19 it is then? We’ll leave after I finish this coffee, yeah? Gives us time to stop for petrol somewhere near Durham. Sounds like a plan. Just promise me no detours down ridiculously narrow country lanes.

Honestly, this shepherd’s pie is proper good, ANON. You’ve outdone yourself. It's a world away from student cooking, isn't it? Aye, it is. Proper comforting. Beats a Pot Noodle any day. Though, I did live on them for a good six months after leaving home, didn't I? Don't tell me mum. You and half the student population, Finn. Though, speaking of needing comfort… how are you actually feeling, Liam? You’ve been a bit quiet since you arrived. Still battling that awful cold? It's hanging on, that's for sure. Just a proper bug, it is. Not the Covid, thankfully, tested negative twice. Just feels like my head's going to explode most of the time. And my throat's all scratchy. Oh, you poor thing. You should be resting up, not being dragged out to Cambridge for a fancy shepherd’s pie! Though, I am glad you came, obviously. I needed getting out, to be fair. Staying in all day just makes it worse. Moping around, feeling sorry for myself. Plus, you two are good company. That’s what friends are for. So, anything exciting happening work-wise, Liam? Still doing the same site? Yeah, same site. Honestly, it's draining. Same faces, same slog. The foreman's been riding everyone hard lately, trying to get the project finished ahead of schedule. It's just… relentless. Sounds awful. Is it physically demanding or just mentally draining? A bit of both, really. It’s shifting stuff all day, but it’s also the constant pressure. If you slow down, you get a telling off. I’m knackered by the end of the day, and then I come home and just collapse. And how’s Chloe coping with you being poorly and stressed? Is she looking after you? That’s… complicated. We had a bit of a row last week. She said I wasn’t putting enough effort into… well, into  us . Said I was always at work or too tired to do anything when I was home. Oh, no. That sounds rough. Especially when you're already feeling rough physically. Yeah, and I get it, I suppose. I haven't been the best company lately. But it's hard when she doesn't  see  how much I’m doing, or how tired I am. It feels like she just expects me to be… on, all the time.

Honestly, this week has been  wild  at work. You will not believe who’s finally admitted they’re leaving. Oh, no way! Let me guess… Gary from accounts? He’s been talking about it for six months. Worse. Bethany. Bethany from marketing. The one who thinks she’s Anna Wintour, but mostly just sends passive-aggressive emails about font choices.  Bethany ? Seriously? She’s the queen of unnecessary meetings. Good riddance, honestly. Where’s she off to? Apparently, some start-up in Shoreditch. Says she wants to “be more creative” and “disrupt the industry”. I nearly choked on my coffee when she told me. Oh, Bethany, never change. So, less meetings for you then? Hopefully! Though knowing our luck, they’ll just replace her with someone even more… intense. And the handover? Oh god, the handover. It’s going to be a nightmare. All her meticulously organised spreadsheets and colour-coded files. It’ll take me a month to decipher it all. Sounds delightful. Work drama is the absolute best, isn’t it? Speaking of drama, how are things with Liam? Still radio silence? Utter silence. I texted him, like, a really simple “Hey, how are you?” on Tuesday. No reply. I’m trying to be all dignified and not look desperate, but it’s hard. Ugh, that’s rubbish. Men are the worst. Just… the  worst . Seriously, the lack of communication is infuriating. Are you sure he’s not just… ignoring you? I think he is. My friend, Chloe, bumped into him at the pub on Wednesday. She said he looked… fine. Like, genuinely cheerful. Apparently, he was with some girl from his old university. Oh, wow. Okay, that’s…direct. Chloe could have maybe kept that to herself, but… at least you know. That's awful though. Yeah, well. Chloe means well. I think. It just…stings. I was starting to think maybe I’d overreacted, you know? But cheerful with another girl? That pretty much confirms it. You didn’t overreact. It sounds like he was already checking out. Honestly, you deserve someone who actually communicates with you, and isn’t out flirting with uni girls. You’re right. It just feels… embarrassing, doesn’t it? Like I misread everything. Don't be silly. You're amazing! And Liam is clearly clueless. Look, why don't we order a takeaway tonight, watch terrible reality TV, and completely forget about him?

Right, so the story goes, Old Man Hemlock lived in the woods, and he wasn't a  bad  man exactly, but he definitely wasn’t…nice. He hoarded all the best berries and wouldn't share with anyone. Was he a witch? Some people said he was. More of a wise man, really. Knew all the secrets of the forest. But he used those secrets to keep things for himself. He’d cast little…what would you call them? Not spells, exactly. More like…tricks. Like what? Did he turn people into frogs? No, not frogs. He’d make you lose your way if you were rude to the trees. Or make your apples fall off the branch before they were ripe. Small things. Annoying things. That  is  mean. It was. And that's where the good part comes in. There was a little girl, Elara, who lived nearby. Her mum was really sick and needed special berries to get better, berries Old Man Hemlock had all to himself. Did Elara ask him nicely? She did. She went to his little hut and asked  very  politely. But he just said no, those berries were for him. Oh! That’s awful. It was. But Elara didn't give up. She knew the forest really well, better than Old Man Hemlock even. She figured out that he wasn’t protecting the berries, he was…distracting something. What was he distracting? A monster? Not a monster. Something older. There was this creature, called the Gloomwing, that lived in the caves behind his hut. It fed on happiness, and it would drain the colour from everything if it got loose. Old Man Hemlock kept the Gloomwing busy by keeping all the best things for himself - the berries, the shiniest stones, the prettiest flowers. He thought if it was focused on  his  treasures, it wouldn’t bother anyone else. But that didn't work, did it? Not really. It just made him a bit grumpy and lonely. Elara realised that if she could give the Gloomwing something  better  than Old Man Hemlock's treasures… something it really liked… she could distract it long enough to gather the berries. What did she give it? Chocolate? Even better. Stories. The Gloomwing loved stories. Not scary ones, but stories about kindness and bravery and friendship. She sat outside the cave and told it stories for hours, and the Gloomwing was so captivated, it didn't even notice her sneaking around and collecting the berries.

Right, so the filming went okay then? Did they actually get usable footage of everything? I think so. Mrs. Davies seemed pretty pleased when I picked Elsie up. She said Elsie was brilliant, really engaged, and asked loads of questions. Apparently, they got some great shots of the Roman ruins. Elsie’s already planning what she wants to be when she grows up – a historian, naturally. I want to dig up bones! Like a real archaeologist! Bones are yucky. And dusty. They’re also fascinating, Leo. That’s why Elsie wants to dig them up. Anyway, it sounded like a really good day. She was buzzing when she got in the car. Good, good. It’s always nice when they enjoy those trips. Seems mild enough outside, doesn't it? Do you think we’ll need the extra duvet on tonight? I don’t know. It  feels  warmer, but it gets chilly later. Maybe just check before bed. Elsie’s been complaining her leg’s hurting again. Oh, not again. What happened this time? Another tumble in the park? No, apparently, she tripped over Leo in the kitchen yesterday. Said he left his cars everywhere. They were defending the castle! It needed a strong defense! Right, of course. Castle defense. Elsie says it’s just a niggle, but I’m keeping an eye on it. She’s a drama queen, though, so it’s hard to tell. They all are at that age. Speaking of drama, I’m thinking I should finally get back to the gym. I’ve been saying that for weeks. Oh, good! You’ve been looking a bit peaky lately. You need to get some stamina back. It’s just… I really hate the running machines. They’re so boring. I feel like a hamster. Well, you don’t have to use the running machines. They’ve got loads of other stuff. Weights, classes… Yeah, but I always end up back on the running machine. It feels like the most efficient way to get it over with. Plus, I can watch terrible daytime TV while I’m doing it. Can we go to the gym, Daddy? Can we see the weights? No, sweetie, the gym is for grown-ups. You can build castles with Leo. They need more soldiers! We need to build more soldiers! Have you seen the new doughnut shop that opened on Mill Road?

Honestly, Arthur, this sciatica is a right nuisance. Woke me up three times last night. Felt like someone was stabbing me in the hip. Oh, you poor thing, Bernard. It’s the damp, I reckon. Brighton air, lovely for the tourists, dreadful for the joints. I’ve been getting a twinge in my knee myself, though nothing like what you describe. Probably from all that bending down at the boot sales. Boot sales are the only thing keeping me sane, to be fair. Brenda keeps telling me I need to “downsize,” but where's the fun in that? Besides, I found a lovely first edition of P.G. Wodehouse last week for two quid. Two quid, Arthur! Not bad, not bad at all. I mostly sell off bits and bobs from the workshop. Old tools, bits of wood… a surprising amount of people want reclaimed timber these days. Keeps me busy, though. Retirement isn't quite the sit-down-with-a-pipe affair everyone promised, is it? No, it’s not. Keeps you  out  of trouble, mostly. Though Brenda says I create more trouble  at  the boot sales, bartering aggressively over chipped teacups. Speaking of trouble, did you see that article about the Green Party proposals for the seafront? Oh, that business with the pedestrianisation? Yes, I skimmed it. Absolute madness, if you ask me. They want to completely restrict access to Madeira Drive. What about the tourists? And where will people park? It’ll kill businesses. That's what I thought. All well and good wanting to be eco-friendly, but they need to think about the practicalities. I tried explaining that to young Sarah at the school, she’s a passionate Green supporter. She just rolled her eyes and told me I was “part of the problem.” Ah, the youth of today. Full of righteous indignation. Still, you’ve always been good with the youngsters, Bernard. Remember old Mr. Henderson’s boy? The one who was heading down the wrong path? You turned him around, you did. That was a long time ago. He’s a solicitor now, apparently. Sends me a Christmas card every year. It’s rewarding, teaching. Though with the cutbacks… I tell you, Arthur, the stress of it all is probably contributing to this sciatica. That’s a fair point. They’re making it harder and harder to do the job properly. Brenda's sister, Margaret, she was a primary school teacher, had to take early retirement.

Honestly, I’m convinced my fiddle-leaf fig is actively plotting my demise. It just  drops  a leaf a day, like a passive-aggressive protest. Oh, the fiddle-leaf fig. The plant world's equivalent of a drama queen. I think everyone has a love-hate relationship with those. Mine's currently sulking because I dared to repot it. Sulking is a good word for it. It’s just… judgment. Pure leafy judgment. Speaking of things judging me, I saw Bethany wearing  that  jumpsuit again today. The one with the questionable cut-outs. Oh, Bethany. Bless her. She commits to a look. Remind me, which jumpsuit is the offender? Is it the… leopard print one? Worse. It's bright orange. And strategically placed holes. I swear, she’s trying to single-handedly revive the 80s, and not in a good way. Right, the orange one. That’s… bold. Fashion choices. Anyway, on a more serious note, I had a slightly terrifying meeting with my supervisor today about funding. Oh no. Is it more cuts? They’re always finding ways to make things harder, aren’t they? Potentially. They’re talking about restructuring some of the grant allocations. Apparently, everything's getting funnelled into AI research now. Which, ironically, feels a bit terrifying in its own right, considering… everything. Don't even get me started on AI. It's all a bit Black Mirror, isn't it? And funding… Ugh.
