It feels like all research is perpetually on the brink of collapse. Did you hear anything about that new policy regarding interest rates? Vaguely. Something about trying to tackle inflation? Honestly, I switch off after the first sentence of anything political these days. It’s just… exhausting. Remember when Donald Trump was all anyone talked about? Feels like a lifetime ago, but also yesterday. Too true. A weird, orange-tinted fever dream. Although, honestly, sometimes I miss the sheer entertainment value. At least it was  interesting . This current lot… they just seem to exist to be beige. Beige is a good description. Speaking of beige… I’m craving a proper Cornish pasty. I haven't had one since I left the Midlands. Honestly, Cambridge is lovely, but their pasty game is weak. Oh, you've come to the wrong place, love. This is definitely a punnet of strawberries and scones kind of town. Though, now you've mentioned it, a proper pasty  does  sound amazing.

Honestly, the student feedback this year has been… interesting. Mostly good, thankfully, but one of them said my lectures were “a bit enthusiastic.” A bit enthusiastic! What does that even  mean ? It means you’re passionate, darling. They’re probably intimidated by anyone who actually cares. You know, the generation raised on TikTok and instant gratification. Maybe. But another one said I talk too fast when I get excited about, of all things, Baroque art. Apparently, I become “a whirlwind of Rococo rambling.” Rococo rambling! That’s brilliant. You  do  get a bit carried away. Remember when we went to that exhibition in London, and you spent twenty minutes analysing the cherubs’ expressions? They were conveying such profound sadness! It was obvious! Anyway, it’s a relief to be here, away from marking. Your mum’s roast is exactly what I needed. She does a good roast. Speaking of needing things, I saw a documentary last night about killer whales… absolutely incredible. The way they hunt, their social structures… it's like watching a complex, aquatic society. Oh, really? I love documentaries. Anything but true crime, though. I’m officially saturated with true crime. This wasn’t true crime. It was… awe-inspiring. But it did make me think about the ethics of keeping them in captivity. It's just… wrong. Completely agree. It’s the same with all the debate around animal documentaries – are we exploiting them for our entertainment? And it then feels linked to other things, doesn’t it? Like, the amount of violence on TV. I was watching something with my niece the other day, a cartoon, and it was just relentless aggression. It’s awful, isn’t it? Glorifying conflict from a really young age. Remember being obsessed with  Blue Peter  as kids? All we did was try and collect badges and make things out of cardboard boxes. Relatively harmless. Oh, the badges! I had a silver one! I think I swapped about twenty bronze ones for it. And I remember trying to build a spaceship out of a washing-up liquid bottle. It didn't fly. Mine was a gold badge! I sent in a poem about… I have no idea what it was about, probably a cat. But it got me a gold badge. Actually, talking of things people occupy… did you see that article about the squatters taking over that luxury apartment block in London?

…and honestly, running that hostel was harder work than anything I ever did down the factory. People think it’s just handing over keys, don’t they? But it’s  dealing  with people. All sorts. You get your quiet ones, your trouble makers… you get ones who just need a bit of a chat. It sounds exhausting, Arthur. You always were a soft touch though, which wouldn’t have helped. Letting everyone off with everything. Now, that's not fair, Margaret! I had to be reasonable. A firm but fair hand, that’s what I tried for. Remember old Mr. Henderson? Used to sneak sausages from the kitchen? Sausages? A hostel, Arthur? Sounds…interesting. I’m used to dealing with teenagers trying to sneak phones into exams, but sausages are a new one. Oh, it wasn’t just sausages. He liked a bit of everything. He said it reminded him of his wife’s cooking. Lovely woman, she was. We had a picture of her on the fridge, didn’t we? Found it going through some old boxes last week. Oh, yes! With the little hat? Such a sweet face. We had so many photos pinned up there, it looked like a proper gallery. Speaking of photos, I’ve got some from little Emily’s birthday. I’ll bring ‘em next week. She's growing like a weed. That’s lovely. My mum keeps trying to send me photos via WhatsApp. I’m hopeless with the technology. She sends ten in a row, all blurry, then rings me up to ask if I’ve seen them! Technology. Humph. Give me a good old-fashioned photograph any day. You can  hold  it, you can  feel  it. This digital stuff…it's all smoke and mirrors. Heard poor old Mrs. Peterson's in hospital again. Pneumonia, apparently. Oh, dear, not again. She's a fighter, that one. Remember her husband, George? He was a brilliant engineer. Always tinkering with something. Designed a contraption to peel potatoes, I swear! Engineering’s fascinating, actually. I’ve got a few pupils who are really gifted with it. We're trying to get more girls into STEM subjects, though. It's still very male-dominated. My dad, he was a hard worker. Had that little shop in Costessey for years. Selling everything from nails to…well, everything. Mum worked alongside him. They didn’t have anything easy, not then.

So, you were a recruiter before this, right? That’s quite a jump to lecturing, isn't it? Yeah, a pretty massive one, actually. Six years in recruitment, corporate stuff mostly. Headhunting for finance roles, mostly. It paid well, honestly, but… it wasn’t  fulfilling . I can imagine. Dealing with people’s careers is a big responsibility. A lot of pressure, I suppose? Huge. And a lot of…spin. Let’s just say. You’re essentially selling people, and companies. I got really good at spotting BS, which, surprisingly, doesn't translate  directly  to academia. Though it helps with grant proposals. I bet! Though we have plenty of spin here too, just of a different sort. It's more… carefully worded nuance, perhaps? Definitely a different flavour. It's less about hitting targets and more about… academic integrity. Or at least, pretending to. Speaking of integrity... how are you finding the students’ academic literacy this semester? I'm marking essays for my first years, and it’s… a mixed bag. Oh, don't even get me started. It’s honestly shocking. I’m running a module designed to  improve  it, ironically, and half the students struggle with basic paragraph structure. Like, seriously. Topic sentences seem to be a mythical concept. Exactly! I had one essay that was basically a stream of consciousness. No clear argument, no supporting evidence, just… ideas. Floating. It’s partly the school system, I think. They’re not being taught how to  construct  an argument anymore. It’s all just ‘express yourself’ and ‘be creative.’ Which is fine, up to a point, but it doesn’t prepare them for university-level critical thinking. I agree. And the reliance on Wikipedia… it’s relentless. I’ve seen entire essays effectively paraphrased from Wikipedia with no original thought whatsoever. It's infuriating, isn’t it? I try to gently guide them towards proper academic databases but they seem so… resistant. Like it’s harder work than just googling. It’s a skills gap, that’s what it is. And we're expected to fill it  and  assess their subject knowledge. It’s exhausting. Honestly, sometimes I feel like I'm teaching remedial writing more than my actual subject. Tell me about it. I spent a good hour yesterday explaining the difference between ‘its’ and ‘it’s’. An hour! You’d think that would be something they’d have picked up by, I don’t know, year seven?

Right, honestly, this place is rammed. I swear it gets worse every week closer to deadlines. Tell me about it. I was circling for ten minutes just to find a plug socket. Needed to charge my phone 'cause my boss keeps texting me about shifts. It's relentless, this job. You work as well as studying, then? That’s dedication. I just leech off my student loan and hope for the best. Gotta eat, eh? Plus, being able to afford nights out is a bonus. I’m Liam, by the way. I don’t think we’ve actually properly met. I’m Aisha. And this is Chloe. We’re both doing English Lit. Chloe’s the brains of the operation. Oi! I just read a lot. I’m Sarah. What about you, Liam? What are you studying? I'm doing History. Though, honestly, most of my time is spent stacking shelves at Sports Direct. It's…educational, in its own way. You learn a lot about people’s footwear choices. Hello. Sorry to interrupt. I’m Priya. I’m new here, just starting my Masters in Computer Science. I was looking for a quiet space, but… Oh, hi Priya! Honestly, quiet is a rare find in here. We’re probably making enough noise ourselves. Welcome! Don't worry, we don’t bite. Much. No, not at all! It’s nice to meet you. Computer Science, that’s impressive. I can barely work my laptop. Truly. I once emailed my lecturer a picture of my cat instead of my essay. You did  what ?! That's brilliant. Did you get away with it? No! He sent it back with a little note saying, "Whilst Mittens is adorable, I require an analysis of Virginia Woolf." Oh, Sarah. You are a disaster. A loveable disaster, but a disaster nonetheless. That’s a good story. It's reassuring to hear things like that. I was worried everyone here would be super serious and focused. I come from a smaller university... it's all very different. Nah, everyone’s stressed. Underneath the pretending-to-be-organised facade, we're all just winging it. Trust me. I’ve seen some things in this library. People crying over Shakespeare, arguing about footnotes… It's a circus. He's not wrong. Last week, I saw someone trying to dismantle a printer with a stapler. Okay, now  that  I need to witness.

Right, so then Uncle Barry starts going on about his time in the Falklands, again. Honestly, you’d think he single-handedly won the war, the way he carries on. Oh, bless him. They all get like that, don’t they? My grandad was in the Royal Marines and he’d launch into these incredibly detailed, and frankly, terrifying stories at the most inappropriate moments. Christmas dinner was never dull. It was at Auntie Carol’s birthday! And she hates anything remotely military. She said it ruined her soufflé. Apparently, thinking about torpedoes isn’t conducive to a light, airy bake. Oh, that’s brilliant. Seriously though, it's… a lot. Is he still reading those war magazines? The ones with the incredibly dramatic covers? Oh god, yeah. “Combat Chronicles” or something like that. Honestly, they look like they're from the 1950s. All grainy photos and sensationalised headlines. I tried to subtly suggest a subscription to, like, a gardening magazine once, but he looked at me like I'd insulted his mother. You’re brave. My mum tried to get my grandad interested in “Homes & Gardens” and he just started explaining how you could fortify a shed to withstand a siege. See! They're a lost cause. Speaking of magazines, have you seen that article in “Sight & Sound” about the new Villeneuve film? Apparently, it's three hours long and entirely dialogue-free. No way! Seriously? Villeneuve is amazing, but three hours of silence? That's… ambitious. Is it sci-fi? He does do sci-fi well. Yeah, apparently it's some kind of space opera. All visuals and atmosphere. I’m a bit worried, to be honest. I love a good think piece, but sometimes I just want people to  talk  in a film. I get that. Although, thinking about it, my flatmate got really into this Japanese silent film the other week. “Rashomon” I think it was called. Apparently, it's groundbreaking. Oh, I’ve heard of that! Isn't it all about different people recounting the same event from their own perspectives? That’s the one. She was raving about it. Said it totally shifted her thinking. It's made me wonder if I should give silent films another go. I tried watching Buster Keaton once and just… fell asleep. Keaton’s a bit intense for a casual viewing. It's like trying to run a marathon before you've learned to walk.

Honestly, the state of dating apps right now is… a disaster. It’s just endless scrolling and everyone’s photos are clearly five years old. You’re telling me. I matched with someone last week who claimed to be 6’2”. Met him, and he was generously 5’8” in boots. Boots! Oh my god, that’s awful. It's the lying that gets me. Like, just be honest about your height, your hobbies, whether or not you still live with your mum… Exactly! I had a date the other day who spent the entire time talking about crypto. I’m an architect, I design buildings, I don’t need a lecture on Bitcoin! See, this is why I’m starting to think I’ll just meet someone properly, you know? Like… in the wild. Though where  is  ‘the wild’ these days? Apparently, it’s not pubs anymore. Or basketball courts. Well, you  were  glued to your phone half the basketball game, checking Tinder. Not exactly radiating ‘approachable’. Hey! I was strategizing. It's research! Seriously though, did you see that article about the rise in right-wing extremism amongst young men? It’s…scary. I did. It is. And the stuff happening in the US…it's creeping over here, isn’t it? Saw some awful comments online yesterday about that MP, that Asian woman. Disgusting. It’s infuriating. I think we’re all becoming desensitized to it, which is the worst part. It's just constant noise now. Mum and Dad are coming up next weekend, by the way. They want to see the flat and… interrogate you, Leo, about your ‘career trajectory’. Oh, lovely. Another round of “so, what  exactly  does a filmmaker do?” and “are you sure that’s a viable profession?” I’ll need fortifying. Lots of fortifying. They mean well. They just…worry. I know, I know. It’s just… draining. I’ve got a potential project lined up, actually. A small documentary for a local art collective. It’s not exactly Hollywood, but it’s something. That sounds amazing! See? You’re smashing it. You just need to tell my parents that. They understand ‘portfolio’ if it involves bricks and mortar, not… lenses and lights. Speaking of smashing it, are we still on for that weekend trip to the Peak District in a couple of weeks? I need to get out of the city. Absolutely! I’ve found a tiny little cottage, proper remote.

So, Dad, you were saying about the boiler needing a service? Is that still ongoing? Yeah, still a right palaver. They sent a bloke round, looked at it, said it needed a part. Then I chased them for a week, got another bloke, different bloke, he said it didn’t need a part, just a tweak! Honestly, you pay good money for these people and… Don’t get yourself worked up, love. It's done now, isn't it? That’s the main thing. Aye, done now. But the principle of it! And the waiting! I’d have fixed it myself if I could’ve gotten up the loft. You definitely shouldn’t be up in the loft, Dad. Remember what the doctor said. Oh, the doctor says a lot of things. Mostly telling me to eat less cheese. Which, frankly, is a bit rich coming from a man who looks like he’s been  living  on cheese. Alright, alright. Anyone fancy another cuppa? I can put the kettle back on. Oh, yes please, dear. Lovely tea. And this flat is so nice and warm, isn’t it? So much brighter than your old place. We’re glad you like it, Mum. It took us ages to get everything sorted. Remember all those trips to Ikea? Ikea… nightmare. Flatpack furniture is the devil’s work. I swear, half the screws are missing in everything we’ve got from there. We’ve learned to just buy extra screws now. It’s cheaper in the long run. Speaking of cheaper, are you two still managing alright with the bills? Everything's gone up, hasn't it? Electric, gas… it's frightening. It’s…tight. My student loan hasn’t come through yet, and Liam’s been covering most of it. I feel terrible. Don’t worry about it. I’ve got a bit saved up. And I picked up a couple of extra shifts teaching English online. It’s not glamorous, but it helps. Teaching English online? To who? Foreigners? Yeah, mostly. A few from China, a couple from Spain… It’s interesting, actually. Trying to explain the pronunciation of ‘scone’ is always a laugh. Some say it rhymes with ‘gone’, some with ‘cone’… Oh, that  is  tricky. We always say it with ‘cone’ down in Essex. And proper cream tea  has  to be clotted cream first, then the jam. It's the only way.

Honestly, this latte is saving my life. Been staring at spreadsheets all morning, feel like my brain’s turned to mush. Tell me about it. I spent the last two hours arguing with a software program that insists drains  don't  need to slope downwards. Like, seriously? It’s basic physics, mate. Oh, the joys of engineering. My job is basically making sure academics haven’t accidentally submitted their life’s work as a Word document instead of a PDF. Thrilling stuff. Sounds… meticulous. At least you're not battling the elements. It's chucking it down outside, isn’t it? Proper Cambridge weather. Aye, typical. Rain one minute, sunshine the next. Makes you wonder if the weather forecast is just someone throwing darts at a board. Speaking of which, have you seen what's happening with the council tax again? They're raising it  again . Don’t even get me started. Trying to save for a deposit on a house in this city is a joke. My mum keeps sending me Rightmove links, but everything's either a shoebox or costs a million quid. A million quid for a terraced house with a garden the size of a postage stamp! It’s mental. Remember when we were kids and houses seemed… affordable? Vaguely. Mostly I remember worrying about getting good grades. Which, ironically, is now making it harder to afford a house. The whole system's backwards. It really is. I saw this article online about the government’s new housing scheme… complete waste of time, honestly. It’ll just line the pockets of developers. That’s usually how it goes, isn’t it? I try not to read too much political stuff, it just stresses me out. Although, saw something about that by-election the other day… Oh, yeah? The one in… Blackpool, wasn’t it? Another chance for everyone to shout at each other on Twitter. Pretty much. Anyway, enough doom and gloom. How’s your health kick going? Still avoiding biscuits? It’s a struggle. Had a particularly stressful morning with a professor who’d forgotten his password  again , so I may have stress-eaten a digestive. But I’m back on the wagon now! What about you? Still doing that weird yoga thing? It's not weird! It's restorative. And yes, still contorting myself into increasingly awkward positions. My flatmate keeps catching me mid-pose and openly laughing.

Honestly, this shift was  chaos . Old Mrs. Higgins decided she absolutely needed a full facial, mid-medication round. Can you imagine? No way! Seriously? Did you manage to talk her down? Oh, bless her. She’s a character, that one. Always wanting to look her best, even when she’s convinced she’s talking to her sister who passed twenty years ago. My nan’s the same. Yesterday she tried to pay for her shopping with buttons. Buttons! The poor shop assistant looked terrified. It’s… draining. And then young Ben, the new agency nurse, tried to explain to her that a facial wasn’t in the care plan. She just glared at him and said, “You’re telling  me  what I need?” Oh, Ben. He’s a bit… earnest, isn’t he? He means well, but he hasn’t got the patience for the residents. I overheard him complaining about Mr. Davies’ poetry readings to Sarah the other day. Mr. Davies and his epic poems about pigeons. He’s harmless, but yeah, they go on a bit. I actually quite enjoy them, in a weird way. He always dedicates one to Margaret Thatcher. That’s mental! Speaking of mental, old man Hemmings keeps trying to sneak biscuits to the dog. Even though he’s diabetic! I had to confiscate a whole packet of digestives yesterday. Honestly, it's like herding cats. And my manager, Janice, is no help. She just says we need to ‘engage’ with the residents more. Like it’s that simple! ‘Engage’. That’s Janice’s favourite word. It’s corporate speak for “do more with less resources.” How is anyone supposed to ‘engage’ when they’re already run off their feet? Exactly! I had a neighbour round yesterday, Carol from number 23. She was saying her daughter’s thinking of doing care work. I tried to steer her towards something else. It’s not glamorous, you know? It's hard work. It is. But it's also… rewarding, sometimes. When you actually connect with someone, and make their day a little bit better... it's nice. True. Old Mrs. Peterson smiled at me genuinely today, and that made my whole shift. She hadn't really smiled since her son moved to Australia. Aw, that  is  lovely. So, anyone got plans for this weekend? I’m thinking of finally tackling that wardrobe clear-out. It’s been looming over me for months.
